passages.title: Increase in female suicides in Japan
passages.passage: Japan reports suicide faster and more accurately than any other country in the world, and the country ’ s suicide figures are compiled at the end of each month, unlike most other parts of the world, but during the coronavirus epidemic, suicide in Japan has been a very worrying statistic.  Japan ’ s suicide rate rose for the first time in 11 years in 2020, but even more remarkable is that despite a slight decrease in male suicides, the rate of female suicides has increased by about 15%.  The suicide rate of women in the country in October 2020 experienced an increase of more than 70% compared to the same month of the previous year.  The report, published on the BBC's website, interviewed a Japanese woman who has repeatedly attempted suicide, detailing the following from the interviewer: "It is not a pleasant experience to meet a young woman face to face with a young woman who has committed suicide many times.  This has given me a lot of respect for those who work in suicide prevention.  I'm sitting in a clinic in the Red Light neighborhood of Yokohama.  The clinic is run by Bond Project, a charity active in suicide prevention.  On the other side of the table, a 19-year-old woman with short, bangs is sitting motionless.  Slowly and without emotion, he begins to tell the story of his life.  He says it started when he was 15.  Having been regularly harassed by his older brother since then, he eventually ran away from home.  But it was not the end of his suffering and loneliness.  He had no choice but to commit suicide.  He said: “I ’ ve been in the hospital so many times since last year.  I tried to commit suicide several times but failed.  So I think I ’ ve stopped trying to end my life.  But Bond Projekt ’ s contributions played an important role in preventing his suicide.  They found a safe place for her to live and gave her intensive counseling sessions.  Joan Tachibana, founder of the charity Bond Project, said: “When girls are in serious trouble and suffering, they don ’ t know what to do.  We are here to listen to them and tell them that we are on their side.  Tachibana says COVID-19 disease appears to have brought vulnerable people closer to the edge of the cliff.  He talks about the heartbreaking phone calls his firm has received in recent months.  Like, “I want to die and I have nowhere to go ” is a phrase we hear a lot.  They say, “It ’ s so painful, I feel so lonely that I want to disappear. ”  But the coronavirus epidemic has made things much harder for those who are physically and sexually abused.  A ‘ very unusual ’ pattern in Japan ’ s previous crises, including the 2008 banking crisis and the stock market crash and housing bubble of the early 1990s, was largely traumatized by middle-aged men.  During this period, suicide rates among men increased dramatically.  But COVID-19 is different and mostly affects young people, especially young women.  There are also complex reasons for this.  Japan had the highest suicide rate of any developed country in the past, but over the past few decades it has managed to reduce the number by about a third.  Michiko Ueda, a university professor and one of the leading experts on suicide, said: “The reversal in suicide rates over the past few months has been so shocking.  She said: “The current pattern of suicide among women is very unusual.  As a researcher in this field, throughout my career, I have never seen such an increase.  The point is that the coronavirus epidemic has hit industries where most of the employees are women, including tourism, the food industry and shops.  Japan has seen a rise in the number of single women who prefer to live alone rather than marriages where traditional stereotypes still exist.  Professor Ueda says that women are also more likely to work in jobs that are less secure.  She said: “A lot of women are single now.  They have to live their own lives where they don ’ t have a stable job.  It ’ s obvious that when something happens, these people get hurt.  Over the past eight months, the unemployment rate among temporary workers has been very high.  One month of the year gets more attention than the rest.  Over the past year, 879 women have committed suicide.  This means that women ’ s suicide rates increased by more than 70% this month compared to the same period in 2019.  On September 27, the body of a famous Japanese actress was found at her home, and she was later reported to have committed suicide.  Yasuyuki Shimizu, a former journalist, is now the director of a non-profit organization called NPO, which works on suicide in Japan.  He said: “From the day the news of a celebrity ’ s suicide is published, the suicide rate goes up, and the trend continues for 10 days.  Within 10 days of the actress ’ s suicide on September 27, 207 other women had ended their lives.  But according to the data, the suicide rate among women around the same age is even more alarming.  Shimizu says women in their 40s are more affected than other age groups.  The suicide rate in this age group is more than twice that of other groups.  Other experts agree that there is a direct link between celebrity suicides and the rapid rise in suicide rates in the days that follow.  The phenomenon isn ’ t unique to Japan, which is one of the reasons why it ’ s so hard to report suicide.  Immediately after a famous person ’ s suicide, the more discussed in the media and social media, the greater the impact on other vulnerable people.  Mai Soganuma, a researcher at NPO, lost her father to suicide when she was a teenager.  He is now helping the families of people who have committed suicide.  The COVID-19 epidemic has made the lives of the families of suicide victims even more difficult because they, like the relatives of the deceased, do not have the opportunity to mourn their loved ones.  “When I talk to family members of suicide victims, the feeling of not being able to save a loved one ’ s life is so powerful that it often makes them feel guilty.  I blamed myself for not being able to save my father ’ s life.  He added: “Now they are told to stay at home.  I ’ m worried that the guilt will get stronger.  Japanese people don ’ t talk about death.  Talking about suicide is not common in our culture.  Following the outbreak of the third coronavirus in Japan in early January and the second declaration of a state of emergency, more and more restaurants, hotels and cafes are closing and more people are losing their jobs.  But there is one more question that haunts the mind of Dr. Oda.  When such things are happening in Japan, which has not imposed severe quarantine and has relatively low corona fatalities, what about the rest of the world, where the epidemic is worse?  End of message.

passages.title: The epidemic has increased the suicide rate, and the appointment of a "minister of loneliness" is urgent.
passages.passage: Japan suffered from COVID-19 in 2020, forcing people to work remotely and reducing social interaction, which led to the suicide rate breaking the previous 11 years ’ record. (AP) Japan ’ s suicide rate in 2020 broke the previous 11 years ’ record, and increased for the first time in the past 11 years, especially among women and young people.  To this end, Prime Minister Yoshihide Suga has appointed a “Minister for Solitude ” to address the worsening suicide problem.  According to data from the Ministry of Health, Labor and Welfare, the number of suicides in 2020 reached 20,919, the first increase since the financial crisis in 2009, with 6,976 women accounting for nearly 15% more than in 2019.  The Japanese government blamed the outbreak on social dysfunction and economic pressures such as unemployment.  For this reason, the Japanese government decided to follow the British example and set up the post of "Minister of Solitude".  On the 12th, Suga appointed the current cabinet as the first minister of loneliness, Tetsuji Sakamoto. On the 16th, he established the “Office of Solitude and Isolation Measures ” to deal with the serious problem of loneliness and isolation.  In announcing her appointment in January 2018, Prime Minister Theresa May described loneliness as a “sad reality of modern life ” and looked forward to helping those who had no way of expressing their grief.  Japan ’ s Nikkei Shimbun commented that since Suga decided to follow the British example, he should also send a stronger and stronger message to the people, like May, to encourage the people to work together to solve their psychological pain.  Japanese media reported that because of the strong reaction of public opinion, the Japanese government tends to continue to lock the country. (European News Agency) Japanese media: lifting the state of emergency will still lock the country In addition, the Korean news reported that the Japanese government has basically decided on the 24th, even if the state of emergency is lifted across the country, it will continue to maintain the state of lock, and the business bubble in 11 countries / regions will not reopen temporarily.  On the other hand, the International Olympic Committee said that the decision on whether to allow foreign tourists to enter Japan at the Tokyo Olympics is expected to be made at the end of April.  The epidemic in Japan has slowed down, and the state of emergency was originally issued by the prefectural governments of the ten prefectures until March 7, but now the rest of the region is expected to be lifted by the end of February.

Why among women victims more Rupert Wingfield-Hayes BBC News, Tokyo Suicides in Japan are recorded faster and more accurately than anywhere else in the world.  Unlike most countries, reporting is done on a monthly basis.  And during the Covid-19 pandemic, these statistics turned out to be more alarming than before.  In 2020, for the first time in 11 years, the number of suicides in Japan increased.  However, although the number of suicides among men decreased slightly, the increase among women was almost 15%.  In October alone, the suicide rate among women in Japan jumped more than 70% compared to the same month last year.  What's going on?  And why does the pandemic seem to affect women far more than men?  A young woman (her BBC identity unknown) met Rupert Wingfield-Hayes in Yokohama A face-to-face meeting with a young woman who repeatedly tried to commit suicide is not a pleasant experience.  I have a deep respect for people who work on suicide prevention.  I'm sitting in Yokohama's red light district in a center run by a suicide prevention charity called the Bond Project.  Anyone can enter here, no pre-registration is required.  At the table opposite, a 19-year-old woman with a short haircut is sitting motionless.  Quietly, without any emotion in her voice, she begins to tell me her story.  She said it all started when she was 15.  Her older brother began to harass her.  She eventually ran away from home, but the pain and loneliness didn ’ t go away.  Suicide seemed like the only way out.  “I ’ ve been to the hospital many times since that time last year, ” she tells me.“ I tried to kill myself many times, but I didn ’ t succeed.  It seems that attempts to die will have to be abandoned. ”  The Bond Project intervened in her life.  His staff found her a safe place to live and began intensive psychotherapy.  June Tachibana is the founder of the Bond Project, a tough woman in her 40s and a tireless optimist.  Joon Tachibana hopes the Bond Project will provide women with the help they need "When girls are in big trouble and hurt, they really don't know what to do," she says.  "We are ready to listen to them, to tell them - we are with you."  Tachibana says Covid-19 seems to be pushing vulnerable people to make a fateful decision.  She describes some of the calls her employees have received in recent months.  “We often hear ‘ I want to die ’ and ‘ I have nowhere to go, ’ ” she says.  They say, "It's so painful, I'm so lonely, I want to disappear."  The pandemic has made life much more difficult for those who are physically or sexually abused.  “The girl I spoke to the other day said her father was sexually harassing her, ” Tachibana tells me.“ But because of the covid, her father doesn ’ t work much and spends a lot of time at home, and she manages to escape from him. ”  If you look at previous crisis moments in Japan, for example, the banking crisis of 2008 or the collapse of the Japanese stock market and the real estate bubble in the early 1990s, the effect was felt mainly by middle-aged men.  During these periods, there were sharp spikes in the number of suicides among men.  A pandemic is a different story.  It affects young people, especially young women.  The reasons for this are very multifaceted.  At one time, Japan had the highest suicide rate among developed countries.  Over the past decade, it has been reduced by about a third.  Professor Michiko Ueda is one of Japan ’ s leading experts on suicide.  It tells me how alarming the growth dynamics have become over the past few months.  “This scenario leading to female suicide is very, very unusual, ” she says.  “In all the time I ’ ve been doing research on this topic, I ’ ve never seen such significant growth.  The peculiarity of the pandemic is that the industries in which many women are employed - tourism, retail trade and the food industry - have suffered the most. "  In Japan, there are more and more unmarried women living on their own.  Many of them prefer such a life to marriage, which still assumes quite traditional gender roles.  Professor Ueda says that young women are much more likely to find themselves in a state of so-called "casual employment."  Professor Michiko Ueda said: “Many women are no longer married, they have to earn a living, but they don ’ t have a regular job.  So when something happens, of course, they suffer a lot.  The number of lost jobs among non-permanent workers has increased significantly over the past eight months. ”  One month stands out.  In October last year, 879 women committed suicide.  This is more than 70% higher than in October 2019.  Newspapers are alarmed.  Some even compare the total number of suicides (both men and women) in October - 2,199 - with the total number of deaths in Japan from the coronavirus at that time - 2,087.  Something strange has happened.  On September 27 last year, a very famous and popular actress named Yuko Takeuchi was found dead in her home.  It was later reported that she had committed suicide. "Of all age groups, Takeuchi's death has had the greatest impact on women in their 40s and 50s," says Yasuyuki Shimizu. "Suicide rates have more than doubled in this age group."  Other experts also agree that there is a link between celebrity suicides and the spike in suicides in the days that followed. Her father killed himself when she was a teenager.  Now it helps to support the families of those who have voluntarily passed away.  The pandemic makes the lives of suicide families much more difficult.  “Members of the suicide family often blame themselves for what happened, ” says Mai Suganuma. – I also blamed myself for not being able to save my father.  And now they say, "Stay at home."  I fear that this will increase the sense of guilt.  The Japanese don ’ t usually talk about death. passages.title: The second wave of the COVID-19 epidemic increased the suicide rate in Japan by 16%
passages.passage: January 15, Minsk / Corr.  BELTA /.  The first wave of the COVID-19 epidemic reduced the number of suicides in Japan by 14%, and the second wave, which began in the fall, on the contrary, increased by 16%.  Such data scientists published in the scientific journal Nature Human Behaviour, reports TASS.  Sociologists led by Tokyo City Institute of Gerontology researcher Shohei Okamoto traced how the COVID-19 pandemic affected suicide rates in Japan.  This country ranks seventh in the world ranking of sad statistics.  The Japanese government monitors suicidal attitudes and tries to prevent them.  The researchers analyzed data from Japanese social services collected during the first and second waves of the pandemic, as well as for similar time periods between 2016 and 2019.  Particular attention was paid to the reaction of the most vulnerable segments of the population, including middle-aged men, as well as the categories that previously committed the least suicide.  "The COVID-19 epidemic has affected all aspects of Japanese society.  Within nine months of the official start of the pandemic, unemployment rose, and fear and anxiety became part of everyday life for all Japanese.  These factors may explain why there were more suicides during the second wave of the pandemic, "the researchers write.  This mainly affected residents of small settlements, women and adolescents who previously committed suicide very rarely.  The exact reasons are not yet known.  But the researchers suggest that these trends have both social and economic causes: rising unemployment, as well as school closures and social distancing.  Okamoto and his colleagues hope that they will be able to find out these reasons in the future and figure out how to prevent the number of suicides from increasing in the future.

Title: Increase in female suicides in Japan
Content: Japan reports suicide faster and more accurately than any other country in the world, and the country ’ s suicide figures are compiled at the end of each month, unlike most other parts of the world, but during the coronavirus epidemic, suicide in Japan has been a very worrying statistic.  Japan ’ s suicide rate rose for the first time in 11 years in 2020, but even more remarkable is that despite a slight decrease in male suicides, the rate of female suicides has increased by about 15%.  The suicide rate of women in the country in October 2020 experienced an increase of more than 70% compared to the same month of the previous year.  The report, published on the BBC's website, interviewed a Japanese woman who has repeatedly attempted suicide, detailing the following from the interviewer: "It is not a pleasant experience to meet a young woman face to face with a young woman who has committed suicide many times.  This has given me a lot of respect for those who work in suicide prevention.  I'm sitting in a clinic in the Red Light neighborhood of Yokohama.  The clinic is run by Bond Project, a charity active in suicide prevention.  On the other side of the table, a 19-year-old woman with short, bangs is sitting motionless.  Slowly and without emotion, he begins to tell the story of his life.  He says it started when he was 15.  Having been regularly harassed by his older brother since then, he eventually ran away from home.  But it was not the end of his suffering and loneliness.  He had no choice but to commit suicide.  He said: “I ’ ve been in the hospital so many times since last year.  I tried to commit suicide several times but failed.  So I think I ’ ve stopped trying to end my life.  But Bond Projekt ’ s contributions played an important role in preventing his suicide.  They found a safe place for her to live and gave her intensive counseling sessions.  Joan Tachibana, founder of the charity Bond Project, said: “When girls are in serious trouble and suffering, they don ’ t know what to do.  We are here to listen to them and tell them that we are on their side.  Tachibana says COVID-19 disease appears to have brought vulnerable people closer to the edge of the cliff.  He talks about the heartbreaking phone calls his firm has received in recent months.  Like, “I want to die and I have nowhere to go ” is a phrase we hear a lot.  They say, “It ’ s so painful, I feel so lonely that I want to disappear. ”  But the coronavirus epidemic has made things much harder for those who are physically and sexually abused.  A ‘ very unusual ’ pattern in Japan ’ s previous crises, including the 2008 banking crisis and the stock market crash and housing bubble of the early 1990s, was largely traumatized by middle-aged men.  During this period, suicide rates among men increased dramatically.  But COVID-19 is different and mostly affects young people, especially young women.  There are also complex reasons for this.  Japan had the highest suicide rate of any developed country in the past, but over the past few decades it has managed to reduce the number by about a third.  Michiko Ueda, a university professor and one of the leading experts on suicide, said: “The reversal in suicide rates over the past few months has been so shocking.  She said: “The current pattern of suicide among women is very unusual.  As a researcher in this field, throughout my career, I have never seen such an increase.  The point is that the coronavirus epidemic has hit industries where most of the employees are women, including tourism, the food industry and shops.  Japan has seen a rise in the number of single women who prefer to live alone rather than marriages where traditional stereotypes still exist.  Professor Ueda says that women are also more likely to work in jobs that are less secure.  She said: “A lot of women are single now.  They have to live their own lives where they don ’ t have a stable job.  It ’ s obvious that when something happens, these people get hurt.  Over the past eight months, the unemployment rate among temporary workers has been very high.  One month of the year gets more attention than the rest.  Over the past year, 879 women have committed suicide.  This means that women ’ s suicide rates increased by more than 70% this month compared to the same period in 2019.  On September 27, the body of a famous Japanese actress was found at her home, and she was later reported to have committed suicide.  Yasuyuki Shimizu, a former journalist, is now the director of a non-profit organization called NPO, which works on suicide in Japan.  He said: “From the day the news of a celebrity ’ s suicide is published, the suicide rate goes up, and the trend continues for 10 days.  Within 10 days of the actress ’ s suicide on September 27, 207 other women had ended their lives.  But according to the data, the suicide rate among women around the same age is even more alarming.  Shimizu says women in their 40s are more affected than other age groups.  The suicide rate in this age group is more than twice that of other groups.  Other experts agree that there is a direct link between celebrity suicides and the rapid rise in suicide rates in the days that follow.  The phenomenon isn ’ t unique to Japan, which is one of the reasons why it ’ s so hard to report suicide.  Immediately after a famous person ’ s suicide, the more discussed in the media and social media, the greater the impact on other vulnerable people.  Mai Soganuma, a researcher at NPO, lost her father to suicide when she was a teenager.  He is now helping the families of people who have committed suicide.  The COVID-19 epidemic has made the lives of the families of suicide victims even more difficult because they, like the relatives of the deceased, do not have the opportunity to mourn their loved ones.  “When I talk to family members of suicide victims, the feeling of not being able to save a loved one ’ s life is so powerful that it often makes them feel guilty.  I blamed myself for not being able to save my father ’ s life.  He added: “Now they are told to stay at home.  I ’ m worried that the guilt will get stronger.  Japanese people don ’ t talk about death.  Talking about suicide is not common in our culture.  Following the outbreak of the third coronavirus in Japan in early January and the second declaration of a state of emergency, more and more restaurants, hotels and cafes are closing and more people are losing their jobs.  But there is one more question that haunts the mind of Dr. Oda.  When such things are happening in Japan, which has not imposed severe quarantine and has relatively low corona fatalities, what about the rest of the world, where the epidemic is worse? The first wave of the COVID-19 epidemic reduced the number of suicides in Japan by 14%, and the second wave, which began in the fall, on the contrary, increased it by 16%. Within nine months of the official start of the pandemic, unemployment rose, and fear and anxiety became part of everyday life for all Japanese.  These factors may explain why suicides increased during the second wave of the pandemic, ” the researchers write.  In a new study, sociologists led by Tokyo City Institute of Gerontology researcher Shohei Okamoto traced how the COVID-19 pandemic affected suicide rates in Japan.  The country has the seventh highest suicide rate in the world.  The Japanese government constantly monitors suicidal sentiments and tries to prevent them.  The researchers used data collected by Japanese social services during the first and second waves of the pandemic, as well as for similar time periods between 2016 and 2019.  They were interested in how the most vulnerable sectors of the population, including middle-aged men, as well as those who had previously committed the least suicide, responded to the pandemic and its associated restrictions and unemployment.  The analysis showed that in the first wave, Japanese society reacted to the pandemic in a completely different way than in the second.  Surprisingly for scientists, in the spring of 2020, suicides in Japan became less: their number compared to the average of the past four years decreased by 14%. passages.title: NEWSru.co.il:: The Palestinian Authority is restoring relations with Israel
passages.passage: PA Civil Administration Minister Hussein al-Sheikh said the Palestinian Authority was restoring full relations with Israel.  According to the Wafa news agency, the Palestinian side will return to compliance with all the agreements that existed on May 19, 2020.  The minister said that Israel, through international mediators, had conveyed to PA President Mahmoud Abbas both written and oral commitments to abide by all agreements signed with the Palestinians.  Hamas issued a statement condemning the Palestinian Authority ’ s decision to restore relations with Israel.  The statement said that by his decision Ramallah legalizes the process of normalization of relations with Israel.  The PA chairman announced the rupture of relations with Israel after the publication of the US-prepared plan for a Palestinian-Israeli settlement - the so-called "deal of the century".  The plan provided for the extension of Israeli sovereignty to part of the territory of Judea and Samaria.  “Our rupture of agreements with the occupiers, undertaken after consultations with the leadership of the Palestinian factions, does not mean that we do not want peace.  We extend our hand and propose to hold an international conference under the auspices of the Quartet to work out a settlement mechanism, "Abbas said on June 24.  Israel has reported renouncing the annexation of Palestinian territories in normalization agreements with the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain.  The leaders of these countries declared their support for the principle of “two states ”, but noted that they do not intend to wait forever until the Palestinians agree to peace with Israel.  The Abraham Accords were perceived by the Palestinian side as a stab in the back.  Attempts to confront them have demonstrated the growing isolation of the Palestinians.  Even the Arab League refused to support them.  The rupture of relations with Israel led to the deterioration of the economic situation in the PA.  On the eve of the US presidential election, it was suggested that in the event of the victory of Democratic candidate Joe Biden, the Palestinian leadership would hurry to declare the restoration of relations, since the Palestinians themselves suffer from the rupture.

passages.title: Trump said about the possible desire of Palestine to normalize ties with Israel
passages.passage: US President Donald Trump believes that the state of Palestine would also like to take some steps to normalize relations with Israel.  He said this on Friday, October 23, in the presence of journalists during a telephone conversation with the leaders of Israel and Sudan.  Earlier, it was officially announced that the two countries had reached an agreement on normalizing ties through the mediation of the United States.  Thus, Sudan became another country to join the “Abrahamic Agreements ”.  “By the way, the Palestinians, if you ask about the Palestinians, want to do something about it.  They've never seen anything like it.  They want to do something.  I am sure that this will also be done, "TASS quoted the head of the White House as saying.  According to the American leader, now “at least five ” Muslim countries want to sign agreements on the normalization of relations with Israel.  And as Trump added, there will soon be many more.  Earlier in October, the Knesset of Israel approved an agreement on the normalization of relations between the Jewish state and the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain.  The agreements on normalization of relations were signed on September 15 at the White House by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, UAE Foreign Minister Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan and Bahraini Foreign Minister Abdel Latif al-Zayani.  The event was held at the White House in the presence of US President Donald Trump, his wife Melania and invited guests.  One of the points of the “Abraham accords ” implies a suspension by Israel of the extension of its sovereignty to Jewish settlements in the West Bank.  This condition is spelled out in Washington ’ s plan to resolve the Palestinian-Israeli conflict.  The signing of the agreements was condemned in Palestine.  They recalled their ambassador to the UAE and called Abu Dhabi ’ s actions an aggression against its people and a disregard for their rights and shrines.  The Arab Peace Initiative adopted in 2002, on which Palestine is based, provides for the possibility of concluding peace agreements and establishing good-neighbourly relations between the Arabs and Israel, but only if the Jewish State withdraws from the territories it occupied in 1967, including the Golan Heights and the Shab'a farms, and recognizes the State of Palestine in the West Bank and Gaza Strip, with East Jerusalem as its capital.

passages.title: Israel, the UAE and Bahrain reach peace deals: five things that are stirring up the Middle East landscape
passages.passage: Image copyright Reuters Image caption Israel's national security adviser flew to the United Arab Emirates on September 1.  A high-level delegation from Israel and the United Arab Emirates will sign a historic peace agreement led by the United States at the White House on Tuesday, September 15, when the UAE and Israel will formally establish diplomatic relations.  U.S. President Donald Trump announced last week that Bahrain ’ s foreign minister would attend the event and sign a comprehensive normalization agreement with Israel alone.  The signing of these agreements will change the landscape in the Middle East. BBC explains why these agreements are important.  Gulf countries see more trade opportunities This agreement will help ambitious UAE.  They built up their own military forces and developed the UAE into a place of business and holiday.  The Americans used the promise of advanced weapons to help reach this agreement.  In the past, the UAE was barely able to buy weapons including the F-35 stealth fighter and the EA-18G Growler electronic fighter.  The UAE has deployed well-equipped armed forces in Libya and Yemen.  But its greatest potential enemy is Iran on the other side of the Gulf.  Israel, like the United States and the United Arab Emirates, is skeptical of Iran.  The same goes for Bahrain.  Until 1969, Iran claimed Bahrain as part of its territory.  Bahrain ’ s Sunni rulers also believe that members of its unstable Shia majority could become Iran ’ s fifth pillar.  The two Gulf states are no longer hiding ties with Israel.  They expect open trade because Israel has the most advanced high-tech industrial chain in the world.  In the non-Covid-19 era, Israelis are avid vacationers who are passionate about exploring the deserts, beaches and shopping centers around the Gulf.  There are business opportunities everywhere.  For Israel, normalization of relations with the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain is a real achievement.  In the 1920s, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu firmly believed in the strategy of building an “iron wall ” between the Jewish state and the Arab states.  The idea is that Israel ’ s strength will eventually make the Arab states realize that their only option is to acknowledge Israel ’ s existence.  Israelis don ’ t like being isolated in the Middle East.  Peace efforts with Egypt and Jordan have never been so enthusiastic.  They may be more looking forward to a better future relationship with the Gulf states far away from Jerusalem and the occupied territories.  Strengthening the anti-Iran coalition is another major advantage.  Netanyahu views Iran as Israel ’ s number one enemy, sometimes comparing its leaders to the Nazis.  He has dropped his previous complaints about the UAE arms deal.  Netanyahu is also troubled, and he is facing a possible jail term for corruption.  His handling of the COVID-19 pandemic went well in the early stages, and badly in the later stages.  Opponents gather weekly outside his Jerusalem residence.  The ceremony at the White House was appropriate.  Image copyright Reuters Image caption Trump announced the so-called Abraham Accord at the White House in August. 3.  Trump celebrated the foreign policy coup, an agreement that has implications for the president of the United States on multiple levels.  This is conducive to Trump ’ s “maximum pressure ” strategy on Iran.  In the year of the election, this helps to support his claim that he is the best trader in the world.  Anything he does that is good for Israel, or more specifically for Netanyahu ’ s government, is good for maintaining good relations with Christian evangelical voters in the United States.  These are important parts of his constituency.  If the Arab states in the Gulf can handle their relations with Israel openly, rather than secretly, then the anti-Iran “Friends of America ” coalition should work more smoothly.  Trump ’ s so-called “deal of the century ” has made peace between Israel and the Palestinians impossible.  But the Abraham Accords between Israel and the UAE are known to have led to a major shift in the Middle East landscape, which the Trump administration has called a major foreign policy coup.  Image copyright Reuters Image caption Palestinian leaders have condemned the actions of the two Gulf states to restore relations with Israel.  The Palestinians felt betrayed that they were once again the last of the tournament.  The Palestinians condemned the Abrahamic Agreement as a betrayal.  The new agreement breaks the long-standing Arab consensus that the price of establishing diplomatic relations with Israel is recognition of Palestinian independence.  But now, Israel is consolidating new public relations with the Arab states, while the Palestinians remain occupied in East Jerusalem, the West Bank, and an area the size of an open prison in Gaza.  Mohammed Al Nahyan, the de facto ruler of the UAE, said his price for the deal was Israel ’ s agreement to stop annexing large parts of the West Bank.  At least because of the current international pressure, Netanyahu seems to have abandoned the idea.  The UAE offered him a way out of the embarrassing political deadlock.  Bahrain joined the agreement and Palestinian tensions increased.  Without Saudi Arabia ’ s approval, that would never have happened.  Saudi Arabia is the leader of the Arab Peace Plan for Palestinian independence.  King Kal Salman was the administrator of two temples in Islam, which gave him great authority.  He is unlikely to suddenly recognize Israel's independence.  His son and successor, Mohammed bin Salman, may also be reluctant to do so.  Image copyright EPA Image caption An agreement between the United Arab Emirates and Israel sparked protests in Iran  Iran Has New Strategic Trouble The deal has been roundly condemned by Iran's leaders.  It ’ s not just about words, the Abrahamic Agreement puts them under even more pressure.  Trump ’ s sanctions have caused real economic pain in Iran.  Now they also have strategic problems.  Israel ’ s home air base is far from Iran, but the UAE ’ s air base is opposite the Gulf waters.  It is very important if we talk again about air strikes on Iranian nuclear bases.  Israel, the United States, Bahrain and the United Arab Emirates have a bunch of new options.  Iran has found that their room for manoeuvre has been reduced.

passages.title: Human Rights Watch reports on Israeli crimes against Palestinians
passages.passage: In its 204-page report, titled “Rape of Limits: Israeli Authorities and the Crimes of Apartheid and Persecution, ” Human Rights Watch argues that Israel ’ s apartheid policy is based on its policy of perpetuating Jewish domination of the Palestinians and the grave human rights violations committed against Palestinians living in the occupied territories, including East Jerusalem.  The report highlights the current reality of a “unified Israeli power ” that controls the area between the Jordan River and the Mediterranean Sea, with a population of two groups of roughly equal size, systematically giving Jews concessions to suppress Palestinians, something that is happening more intensely in the occupied territories.  Kenneth Roth, executive director of Human Rights Watch, said: “Clear voices have been warning for years that if the Israeli regime ’ s approach to the Palestinians does not change, it is not far from apartheid.  This detailed study shows that the Israeli authorities have crossed this line and today are committing crimes against humanity, apartheid and persecution against the Palestinian people.  The results of Israel ’ s policy of apartheid and persecution against Palestinians do not change the legal status of the occupied territories, including the West Bank, East Jerusalem and Gaza, or the actual reality of the occupation.  The term apartheid was coined in reference to South Africa and is today a universal legal term.  Prohibition against severe institutional oppression and discrimination, or apartheid and racial discrimination, is a fundamental principle in international law.  The 1973 International Convention on the Prohibition and Punishment of the Crime of Apartheid and the 1998 Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court against Apartheid are defined as crimes against humanity, which includes three main elements: 1) intent to maintain the dominion of one ethnic group over another; 2) a background of systematic repression by the dominant group; 3) inhumane practices are emphasized in the Human Rights Watch report, which today referred to as defined in the International Convention on the International Convention for the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination. And race beyond behavior is based not only on genetic and hereditary traits, but also on ancestry or national and ethnic origin.  Human Rights Watch considers this broader concept of race.  Crimes against humanity and persecution defined by the Rome Statute and customary international law include severe deprivation of fundamental rights for a racial, ethnic, or otherwise group for discriminatory purposes.  Human Rights Watch has concluded that elements of these crimes are present in the occupied territories as part of a single Israeli policy.  This policy is in line with the continuation of Zionist Jewish domination over the Palestinians throughout the occupied territories.  This policy has been accompanied by systematic repression and inhumane actions against Palestinians living in these areas.  Based on years of legal reporting, case study and document review, Human Rights Watch compared planning, statements by Israeli officials and other sources, policies and approaches on Palestinians in the occupied territories to those of Zionist Jews living in the same areas.  In January 2020, Human Rights Watch sent a letter to Zionist officials demanding that Tel Aviv express its views on these issues, but received no response.  Human Rights Watch said Israeli authorities in various areas of the occupied territories have sought to make maximum available to Jewish communities and to concentrate more Palestinians in population centers.  Israeli officials have adopted policies to reduce what they have publicly called a demographic “threat ” from the Palestinians.  In Jerusalem, for example, a plan for a municipality, including the occupied western as well as eastern parts of the city, aims to “preserve the Jewish majority in the city, ” and even specifies desired demographic ratios.  Human Rights Watch, a New York-based international NGO, added that in order to maintain hegemony, Israeli authorities systematically discriminate against Palestinians.  Institutional discrimination faced by Palestinians in the occupied territories includes laws that allow hundreds of small Jewish settlements to evict Palestinians.  In the occupied territories, intensification of repression and systematic repressive measures are necessary for apartheid.  Repression includes a harsh and brutal military regime against the Palestinians, so that Jews living separately in the same region enjoy civil rights.  The organization said Israeli authorities have committed a wide range of violations against Palestinians.  Many of these violations in the occupied territories are grave violations of the fundamental rights and inhumane practices necessary for apartheid, such as the severe restriction of movement by Israel with the closure of the Gaza border, the confiscation of more than a third of the land in the West Bank, the imposition of harsh conditions in parts of the Bank that have displaced thousands of Palestinians, the deprivation of housing rights for hundreds of thousands of Palestinians, and the suspension of basic civil rights for millions of Palestinians.  The report stressed that many of the violations at the heart of these crimes, such as the near-absolute prohibition of building permits for Palestinians and the demolition of thousands of homes under the pretext of not having a permit, have no security justification.  Other cases, such as Israel ’ s de facto suspension of registration in the occupied territories, make it virtually impossible for Palestinians to form a family and prevent residents of Gaza from living in the West Bank.  Security is used as an excuse by the Zionist regime to advance demographic goals.  Human Rights Watch added that even when security is part of the Israeli regime ’ s motivation, it cannot justify apartheid and the persecution of Palestinians any more than it can justify excessive force or torture.  Roth, the executive director of Human Rights Watch, said that depriving millions of Palestinians of their basic rights, without a legitimate security justification and simply because they are Palestinians, not Jews, is not the only issue with occupiers who violate human rights.  These policies, which give Jews in the occupied territories the same rights and privileges, and to varying degrees of discrimination against Palestinians wherever they live, represent a policy of preferring one group to the detriment of another.  Human Rights Watch called on Israeli authorities to eliminate all forms of oppression and discrimination in the interests of Jews and at the expense of Palestinians, including freedom of movement, the allocation of land and resources, access to water, electricity and other services, and the granting of construction permits.  The organization, which has been working on human rights issues since 1978, called for the boycott of the Zionist authorities, adding that the Prosecutor of the International Criminal Court (The Hague) should investigate and prosecute those who have been involved in crimes against humanity, apartheid and persecution.  Other countries should do so, in accordance with their national laws and under the principle of international jurisdiction, and impose individual sanctions, including travel bans and asset freezes, against officials responsible for these crimes in the Occupied Palestinian Territory.  The report argues that the consequences of crimes against humanity should prompt the international community to reassess the nature of its relationship with Israel and Palestine and to adopt a human-rights and accountability approach rather than a “stalled peace process. ”  States should establish a UN Commission of Inquiry to investigate systematic repression and discrimination in the Occupied Palestinian Territory, and appoint a UN Global Representative with the authority to mobilize international action to end persecution and apartheid around the world.  Roth said that while much of the world sees Israel ’ s 50-year occupation as a temporary situation that the decades-long peace process will soon resolve, Israel ’ s repression of Palestinians has reached a limit that fulfills the conditions for apartheid crimes and persecution.  Those who seek Israeli-Palestinian peace, whether one or two states or confederally, must first recognize the reality of what it is and use the human rights tools necessary to end it.

passages.title: The Russian Jewish Congress commented on the accusations of human rights defenders against Israel
passages.passage: The human rights organization Human Rights Watch released a report in which it claims that the Israeli authorities commit crimes of apartheid in order to preserve the dominance of Jewish Israelis over the Palestinians.  This position is shared by the Israeli NGO B ’ Tselem, which collects information on human rights violations in the disputed territories.  These include the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, and the Gaza Strip, calling them Israeli-occupied territories.  HRW ’ s report is based on years of human rights monitoring, government planning documents, official statements, and other sources.  The experts compared the policy and real actions in the disputed territories and in Israel itself against the Palestinians and the Jewish population.  According to the organization, in July last year, a letter was sent to the Israeli authorities in which they were invited to present their vision of the situation, but a response has not yet been received.  German Zakharyaev, vice president of the Russian Jewish Congress (RJC) and president of the STMEGI Mountain Jews Foundation, called the entire HRW report not a serious study, but a damning pamphlet aimed at stigmatizing Israel as an apartheid state.  “The report is based on the false image of Israel as the country controlling the entire West Bank and Gaza Strip, but in reality it is not, only a few dozen Jewish settlements and a number of highways leading to them are under Israeli control.  The rest of the population is under the control of Mahmoud Abbas's Palestinian Authority and the Hamas movement in the Gaza Strip, "he said.  According to Zakharyaev, on the territory of Israel proper, Arab citizens are absolutely equal.  At the same time, he recognized the persistence of a significant difference in the social status and material situation of the Jewish and Arab populations.  At the same time, the vice-president of the RJC recalled that the same difference exists within the Jewish population - between immigrants from Europe and the countries of the East.  What does the report say?  Allocation of land.  It follows from the report that the authorities, both in Israel itself and in the disputed territories, mainly seek to provide land for Jewish communities.  Most Palestinians are driven into densely populated areas.  The organization also claims the existence of a certain policy of neutralization: for example, the state plan for the development of Jerusalem proceeds from the need for “confident preservation of the Jewish majority ” and even provides for desirable demographic proportions.  German Zakharyaev explained to Gazeta.ru that the Arab population prefers to live in large families and so-called hamuls, build houses near their loved ones in the territories of their towns and cities.  Moreover, he said, these structures are often illegal, allowing Palestinians to bypass the long and costly process of buying and registering property.  Cut off from the local community.  According to HRW, Israel has laws that allow hundreds of small Jewish municipalities to effectively cut off Palestinians from the local community.  In addition, according to the document, only a small part of the budget is allocated to Palestinian schools compared to the financing of schools where Jewish Israeli children study.  The report points out that in the disputed territories, the intensity of repression against Palestinians reaches the level of “systematic oppression ” as one of the hallmarks of apartheid.  The document refers to a draconian military administration for Palestinians in these territories, while Jewish Israelis living separately there are provided with the full range of rights under Israel ’ s model civil code.  Israeli political scientist, former adviser to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu Benny Briskin, said in a comment to Gazeta.ru that Israel ’ s judicial system is built in such a way that every real violation of human rights that occurs either in the disputed territories of the Palestinian Authority, or in the territory of Israel itself in relation to the Arabs, is checked and the guilty is always punished.  “Of course, there are exaggerations, but the Israeli judicial system is recognized by the whole world as serious, independent, which deals with all cases, ” he said.  Freedom of movement.  The authors of the report cite as serious violations of the fundamental rights of the Palestinians and the “inhumane actions ” against their freedom of movement in the form of the closure of the Gaza Strip and the imposition of a permit regime, the confiscation of more than a third of land in the West Bank with the forced eviction of thousands of Palestinians, the denial of housing rights, and the suspension of basic civil rights for millions of Palestinians.  Many of the violations underlying these crimes, according to the authors of the report, cannot be justified in the interests of security, including the almost complete ban on the issuance of building permits to Palestinians and the demolition of thousands of houses on the pretext of lack of such a permit.  There are also cases, according to human rights activists, when demographic goals are covered by security interests, as in the situation with the de facto freezing by the Israeli authorities of the registration of residents in the disputed territories.  The organization noted that this almost completely blocks the reunification of families of Palestinians living there and deprives residents of the Gaza Strip of the opportunity to get to the West Bank.  According to the RJC vice-president, the Gaza Strip is an independent administrative unit, from where Israel completely withdrew its army and settlements in 2005, and where today Hamas, recognized in Israel as a terrorist organization, is in power.  “Any interaction with it should be confirmed at the state and legislative level.  To date, based on security needs, some kind of restrictions are imposed.  It seems to me that it is difficult to interact with the administration, which for any reason or for no reason fires missiles at civilians, ” he said.  In addition, HRW recalled the constitutional law adopted in 2018, according to which Israel was declared the “national state of the Jewish people ”.  The authors of the document are convinced that the growing body of legislation increasingly favors Jewish settlers in the West Bank and does not extend to Palestinians living there.  As explained by German Zakharyaev, this law is designed to strengthen the status of Israel as a Jewish state.  According to the seventh paragraph of this law, the state of Israel sees the development of Jewish settlements as a national value for the entire Jewish people, he noted.  In addition, the expert drew attention to the fact that this law does not say anything about Jewish settlers in the West Bank, but only about the nature of the State of Israel.  Benny Briskin called such reports not new to Israel.  According to him, in Israel there are two points of view on this: either it is ordinary anti-Semitism, or it is left-wing liberalism.  But in any case, the result is the same - the attitude towards Israel is based on double standards, he stated.  “The approach of human rights organizations is that everything that happens in the territories they call occupied is already a crime.  It does not matter how the Jewish population behaves.  In Israel, they are already accustomed to this, ” the political scientist said.  He argues that the facts do not fit into these allegations.  The facts that lead human rights organizations, Briskin called slanderous fabrications of one side.  “That is, they find a Palestinian who tells a story that he was told to tell by the Palestinian secret services.  This is not verified in any way and is exposed as an unquestionable fact, ” he said.  “The claims of apartheid seem particularly absurd today, when Mansour Abbas — leader of the Joint Arab List in the Knesset — holds Israel ’ s political future in the wake of the March elections.  His voice is key in determining who will form the next governing coalition in Israel: Benjamin Netanyahu and his far-right supporters or the camp of his opponents.  Both sides are courting Abbas, which is hardly a sign of apartheid, ” said German Zakharyaev, president of the STMEGI Mountain Jews Foundation.

passages.title: Zionists' actions in support of civil wars
passages.passage: A report published by the Al-Zaitouneh Research Center shows that the Zionist regime is leading the way in selling weapons to dictatorial regimes and spy equipment to Arab countries to spy on human rights activists along with money laundering.  The Al-Zaitouneh Research Center is an independent center in Beirut, founded in 2004, that conducts research on issues related to the Arab and Islamic world, particularly the Palestinian issue.  Unfortunately, some Arab countries and Arab political institutions are buying weapons from the Zionist regime.  This makes dialogue between Palestinian resistance groups and Arab political parties more necessary to counter such actions.  According to the report, Israel has been arming separatist movements in South Sudan, and the Sudanese have not reacted very seriously.  Referring to the nuclear actions of the Zionist regime, the report said that it is necessary to resume Arab studies on the dangers of the Zionist regime ’ s nuclear program against the Middle East.  These studies should be focused on the efforts of the Zionists in the production of chemical and biological weapons.  NSO Group Technologies is an Israeli spy company that uses its programs to spy on human rights activists and journalists around the world.  The company ’ s spy programs have also been used to assassinate Saudi activist Jamal Khashoggi, a critic of the Saudi regime, according to the report, the Zionist regime has not signed any of the agreements on the non-proliferation of nuclear, biological or chemical weapons.  Interestingly, these weapons end up in the hands of dictatorial regimes that violate human rights.  In addition, the Zionist regime is trying to support civil wars and power struggles by sending these weapons.  We are witnessing a process of money laundering and espionage along with the sale of these weapons in general, which is confirmed by the reports of international delegations and academic research.  Israel did not even sign the arms trade agreement, which was ratified by 82 countries in 2012, as it considers humanitarian and human rights issues an obstacle to its arms deals.  According to the report, the Zionist regime is working secretly with security companies in order to transfer weapons.  Spying-related technologies are another area of concern: NSO Group Technologies is one of the Zionist spy companies whose programs are used to spy on human rights activists and journalists around the world.  The company ’ s spy programs have also been used to assassinate Saudi activist Jamal Khashoggi, a critic of the Saudi regime.  According to the report, the Israeli company ’ s plans have been sold to the UAE, Morocco, Bahrain and Saudi Arabia.

Title: NEWSru.co.il:: The Palestinian Authority is restoring relations with Israel
Content: PA Civil Administration Minister Hussein al-Sheikh said the Palestinian Authority was restoring full relations with Israel.  According to the Wafa news agency, the Palestinian side will return to compliance with all the agreements that existed on May 19, 2020.  The minister said that Israel, through international mediators, had conveyed to PA President Mahmoud Abbas both written and oral commitments to abide by all agreements signed with the Palestinians.  Hamas issued a statement condemning the Palestinian Authority ’ s decision to restore relations with Israel.  The statement said that by his decision Ramallah legalizes the process of normalization of relations with Israel.  The PA chairman announced the rupture of relations with Israel after the publication of the US-prepared plan for a Palestinian-Israeli settlement - the so-called "deal of the century".  The plan provided for the extension of Israeli sovereignty to part of the territory of Judea and Samaria.  “Our rupture of agreements with the occupiers, undertaken after consultations with the leadership of the Palestinian factions, does not mean that we do not want peace.  We extend our hand and propose to hold an international conference under the auspices of the Quartet to work out a settlement mechanism, "Abbas said on June 24.  Israel has reported renouncing the annexation of Palestinian territories in normalization agreements with the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain.  The leaders of these countries declared their support for the principle of “two states ”, but noted that they do not intend to wait forever until the Palestinians agree to peace with Israel.  The Abraham Accords were perceived by the Palestinian side as a stab in the back.  Attempts to confront them have demonstrated the growing isolation of the Palestinians.  Even the Arab League refused to support them.  The rupture of relations with Israel led to the deterioration of the economic situation in the PA.  On the eve of the US presidential election, it was suggested that in the event of the victory of Democratic candidate Joe Biden, the Palestinian leadership would hurry to declare the restoration of relations, since the Palestinians themselves suffer from the rupture.

Source: 2
Title: Trump said about the possible desire of Palestine to normalize ties with Israel
Content: US President Donald Trump believes that the state of Palestine would also like to take some steps to normalize relations with Israel.  He said this on Friday, October 23, in the presence of journalists during a telephone conversation with the leaders of Israel and Sudan.  Earlier, it was officially announced that the two countries had reached an agreement on normalizing ties through the mediation of the United States.  Thus, Sudan became another country to join the “Abrahamic Agreements ”.  “By the way, the Palestinians, if you ask about the Palestinians, want to do something about it.  They've never seen anything like it.  They want to do something.  I am sure that this will also be done, "TASS quoted the head of the White House as saying.  According to the American leader, now “at least five ” Muslim countries want to sign agreements on the normalization of relations with Israel.  And as Trump added, there will soon be many more.  Earlier in October, the Knesset of Israel approved an agreement on the normalization of relations between the Jewish state and the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain.  The agreements on normalization of relations were signed on September 15 at the White House by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, UAE Foreign Minister Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan and Bahraini Foreign Minister Abdel Latif al-Zayani.  The event was held at the White House in the presence of US President Donald Trump, his wife Melania and invited guests.  One of the points of the “Abraham accords ” implies a suspension by Israel of the extension of its sovereignty to Jewish settlements in the West Bank.  This condition is spelled out in Washington ’ s plan to resolve the Palestinian-Israeli conflict.  The signing of the agreements was condemned in Palestine.  They recalled their ambassador to the UAE and called Abu Dhabi ’ s actions an aggression against its people and a disregard for their rights and shrines.  The Arab Peace Initiative adopted in 2002, on which Palestine is based, provides for the possibility of concluding peace agreements and establishing good-neighbourly relations between the Arabs and Israel, but only if the Jewish State withdraws from the territories it occupied in 1967, including the Golan Heights and the Shab'a farms, and recognizes the State of Palestine in the West Bank and Gaza Strip, with East Jerusalem as its capital.

Title: Israel, the UAE and Bahrain reach peace deals: five things that are stirring up the Middle East landscape
Content: Image copyright Reuters Image caption Israel's national security adviser flew to the United Arab Emirates on September 1.  A high-level delegation from Israel and the United Arab Emirates will sign a historic peace agreement led by the United States at the White House on Tuesday, September 15, when the UAE and Israel will formally establish diplomatic relations.  U.S. President Donald Trump announced last week that Bahrain ’ s foreign minister would attend the event and sign a comprehensive normalization agreement with Israel alone.  The signing of these agreements will change the landscape in the Middle East. BBC explains why these agreements are important.  Gulf countries see more trade opportunities This agreement will help ambitious UAE.  They built up their own military forces and developed the UAE into a place of business and holiday.  The Americans used the promise of advanced weapons to help reach this agreement.  In the past, the UAE was barely able to buy weapons including the F-35 stealth fighter and the EA-18G Growler electronic fighter.  The UAE has deployed well-equipped armed forces in Libya and Yemen.  But its greatest potential enemy is Iran on the other side of the Gulf.  Israel, like the United States and the United Arab Emirates, is skeptical of Iran.  The same goes for Bahrain.  Until 1969, Iran claimed Bahrain as part of its territory.  Bahrain ’ s Sunni rulers also believe that members of its unstable Shia majority could become Iran ’ s fifth pillar.  The two Gulf states are no longer hiding ties with Israel.  They expect open trade because Israel has the most advanced high-tech industrial chain in the world.  In the non-Covid-19 era, Israelis are avid vacationers who are passionate about exploring the deserts, beaches and shopping centers around the Gulf.  There are business opportunities everywhere.  For Israel, normalization of relations with the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain is a real achievement.  In the 1920s, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu firmly believed in the strategy of building an “iron wall ” between the Jewish state and the Arab states.  The idea is that Israel ’ s strength will eventually make the Arab states realize that their only option is to acknowledge Israel ’ s existence.  Israelis don ’ t like being isolated in the Middle East.  Peace efforts with Egypt and Jordan have never been so enthusiastic.  They may be more looking forward to a better future relationship with the Gulf states far away from Jerusalem and the occupied territories.  Strengthening the anti-Iran coalition is another major advantage.  Netanyahu views Iran as Israel ’ s number one enemy, sometimes comparing its leaders to the Nazis.  He has dropped his previous complaints about the UAE arms deal.  Netanyahu is also troubled, and he is facing a possible jail term for corruption.  His handling of the COVID-19 pandemic went well in the early stages, and badly in the later stages.  Opponents gather weekly outside his Jerusalem residence.  The ceremony at the White House was appropriate.  Image copyright Reuters Image caption Trump announced the so-called Abraham Accord at the White House in August. 3.  Trump celebrated the foreign policy coup, an agreement that has implications for the president of the United States on multiple levels.  This is conducive to Trump ’ s “maximum pressure ” strategy on Iran.  In the year of the election, this helps to support his claim that he is the best trader in the world.  Anything he does that is good for Israel, or more specifically for Netanyahu ’ s government, is good for maintaining good relations with Christian evangelical voters in the United States.  These are important parts of his constituency.  If the Arab states in the Gulf can handle their relations with Israel openly, rather than secretly, then the anti-Iran “Friends of America ” coalition should work more smoothly.  Trump ’ s so-called “deal of the century ” has made peace between Israel and the Palestinians impossible.  But the Abraham Accords between Israel and the UAE are known to have led to a major shift in the Middle East landscape, which the Trump administration has called a major foreign policy coup.  Image copyright Reuters Image caption Palestinian leaders have condemned the actions of the two Gulf states to restore relations with Israel.  The Palestinians felt betrayed that they were once again the last of the tournament.  The Palestinians condemned the Abrahamic Agreement as a betrayal.  The new agreement breaks the long-standing Arab consensus that the price of establishing diplomatic relations with Israel is recognition of Palestinian independence.  But now, Israel is consolidating new public relations with the Arab states, while the Palestinians remain occupied in East Jerusalem, the West Bank, and an area the size of an open prison in Gaza.  Mohammed Al Nahyan, the de facto ruler of the UAE, said his price for the deal was Israel ’ s agreement to stop annexing large parts of the West Bank.  At least because of the current international pressure, Netanyahu seems to have abandoned the idea.  The UAE offered him a way out of the embarrassing political deadlock.  Bahrain joined the agreement and Palestinian tensions increased.  Without Saudi Arabia ’ s approval, that would never have happened.  Saudi Arabia is the leader of the Arab Peace Plan for Palestinian independence.  King Kal Salman was the administrator of two temples in Islam, which gave him great authority.  He is unlikely to suddenly recognize Israel's independence.  His son and successor, Mohammed bin Salman, may also be reluctant to do so.  Image copyright EPA Image caption An agreement between the United Arab Emirates and Israel sparked protests in Iran  Iran Has New Strategic Trouble The deal has been roundly condemned by Iran's leaders.  It ’ s not just about words, the Abrahamic Agreement puts them under even more pressure.  Trump ’ s sanctions have caused real economic pain in Iran.  Now they also have strategic problems.  Israel ’ s home air base is far from Iran, but the UAE ’ s air base is opposite the Gulf waters.  It is very important if we talk again about air strikes on Iranian nuclear bases.  Israel, the United States, Bahrain and the United Arab Emirates have a bunch of new options.  Iran has found that their room for manoeuvre has been reduced.

Title: Palestinian opposition to Israeli peace deal! 'Treason 'calls for Arab League emergency meeting
Content: ▲ Trump brokered the peace agreement, right Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. (Photo / Reuters) - Israel and the United Arab Emirates, which have no diplomatic relations, reached a historic peace agreement on the 13th, and Palestinian President Mahmud Abbas today expressed "strong opposition and condemnation" and demanded an emergency meeting of the Arab League.  According to the Associated Press, Reuters, the agreement signed by Israel and the United Arab Emirates, known as the Abraham Accords, is the first such agreement between Israel and Jordan since the signing of a peace treaty in 1994.  Palestinian Authority President Mahmud Abbas said in a statement today that the agreement was a "provocation" to the Palestinians and a total "treason" for the Palestinians to see Jerusalem as their future capital.  A senior White House official revealed yesterday that the peace agreement is the result of lengthy negotiations between the United States, Israel and the United Arab Emirates. President Trump signed it on the phone with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and UAE Crown Prince Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed.  Since Israel ’ s independence in 1948, it has been regarded as an old enemy in the Arab world. It only established diplomatic relations with Egypt in 1979 and Jordan in 1994. Today, the United Arab Emirates will be the first Persian Gulf Arab country to normalize diplomatic relations with Israel.

Title: Human Rights Watch reports on Israeli crimes against Palestinians
Content: In its 204-page report, titled “Rape of Limits: Israeli Authorities and the Crimes of Apartheid and Persecution, ” Human Rights Watch argues that Israel ’ s apartheid policy is based on its policy of perpetuating Jewish domination of the Palestinians and the grave human rights violations committed against Palestinians living in the occupied territories, including East Jerusalem.  The report highlights the current reality of a “unified Israeli power ” that controls the area between the Jordan River and the Mediterranean Sea, with a population of two groups of roughly equal size, systematically giving Jews concessions to suppress Palestinians, something that is happening more intensely in the occupied territories.  Kenneth Roth, executive director of Human Rights Watch, said: “Clear voices have been warning for years that if the Israeli regime ’ s approach to the Palestinians does not change, it is not far from apartheid.  This detailed study shows that the Israeli authorities have crossed this line and today are committing crimes against humanity, apartheid and persecution against the Palestinian people.  The results of Israel ’ s policy of apartheid and persecution against Palestinians do not change the legal status of the occupied territories, including the West Bank, East Jerusalem and Gaza, or the actual reality of the occupation.  The term apartheid was coined in reference to South Africa and is today a universal legal term.  Prohibition against severe institutional oppression and discrimination, or apartheid and racial discrimination, is a fundamental principle in international law.  The 1973 International Convention on the Prohibition and Punishment of the Crime of Apartheid and the 1998 Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court against Apartheid are defined as crimes against humanity, which includes three main elements: 1) intent to maintain the dominion of one ethnic group over another; 2) a background of systematic repression by the dominant group; 3) inhumane practices are emphasized in the Human Rights Watch report, which today referred to as defined in the International Convention on the International Convention for the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination. And race beyond behavior is based not only on genetic and hereditary traits, but also on ancestry or national and ethnic origin.  Human Rights Watch considers this broader concept of race.  Crimes against humanity and persecution defined by the Rome Statute and customary international law include severe deprivation of fundamental rights for a racial, ethnic, or otherwise group for discriminatory purposes.  Human Rights Watch has concluded that elements of these crimes are present in the occupied territories as part of a single Israeli policy.  This policy is in line with the continuation of Zionist Jewish domination over the Palestinians throughout the occupied territories.  This policy has been accompanied by systematic repression and inhumane actions against Palestinians living in these areas.  Based on years of legal reporting, case study and document review, Human Rights Watch compared planning, statements by Israeli officials and other sources, policies and approaches on Palestinians in the occupied territories to those of Zionist Jews living in the same areas.  In January 2020, Human Rights Watch sent a letter to Zionist officials demanding that Tel Aviv express its views on these issues, but received no response.  Human Rights Watch said Israeli authorities in various areas of the occupied territories have sought to make maximum available to Jewish communities and to concentrate more Palestinians in population centers.  Israeli officials have adopted policies to reduce what they have publicly called a demographic “threat ” from the Palestinians.  In Jerusalem, for example, a plan for a municipality, including the occupied western as well as eastern parts of the city, aims to “preserve the Jewish majority in the city, ” and even specifies desired demographic ratios.  Human Rights Watch, a New York-based international NGO, added that in order to maintain hegemony, Israeli authorities systematically discriminate against Palestinians.  Institutional discrimination faced by Palestinians in the occupied territories includes laws that allow hundreds of small Jewish settlements to evict Palestinians.  In the occupied territories, intensification of repression and systematic repressive measures are necessary for apartheid.  Repression includes a harsh and brutal military regime against the Palestinians, so that Jews living separately in the same region enjoy civil rights.  The organization said Israeli authorities have committed a wide range of violations against Palestinians. Israeli political scientist, former adviser to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu Benny Briskin, said in a comment to Gazeta.ru that Israel ’ s judicial system is built in such a way that every real violation of human rights that occurs either in the disputed territories of the Palestinian Authority, or in the territory of Israel itself in relation to the Arabs, is checked and the guilty is always punished.  “Of course, there are exaggerations, but the Israeli judicial system is recognized by the whole world as serious, independent, which deals with all cases, ” he said.  Freedom of movement.  The authors of the report cite as serious violations of the fundamental rights of the Palestinians and the “inhumane actions ” against their freedom of movement in the form of the closure of the Gaza Strip and the imposition of a permit regime, the confiscation of more than a third of land in the West Bank with the forced eviction of thousands of Palestinians, the denial of housing rights, and the suspension of basic civil rights for millions of Palestinians.  Many of the violations underlying these crimes, according to the authors of the report, cannot be justified in the interests of security, including the almost complete ban on the issuance of building permits to Palestinians and the demolition of thousands of houses on the pretext of lack of such a permit.  There are also cases, according to human rights activists, when demographic goals are covered by security interests, as in the situation with the de facto freezing by the Israeli authorities of the registration of residents in the disputed territories.  The organization noted that this almost completely blocks the reunification of families of Palestinians living there and deprives residents of the Gaza Strip of the opportunity to get to the West Bank.  According to the RJC vice-president, the Gaza Strip is an independent administrative unit, from where Israel completely withdrew its army and settlements in 2005, and where today Hamas, recognized in Israel as a terrorist organization, is in power.  “Any interaction with it should be confirmed at the state and legislative level.  To date, based on security needs, some kind of restrictions are imposed.  It seems to me that it is difficult to interact with the administration, which for any reason or for no reason fires missiles at civilians, ” he said.  In addition, HRW recalled the constitutional law adopted in 2018, according to which Israel was declared the “national state of the Jewish people ”.  The authors of the document are convinced that the growing body of legislation increasingly favors Jewish settlers in the West Bank and does not extend to Palestinians living there.  As explained by German Zakharyaev, this law is designed to strengthen the status of Israel as a Jewish state.  According to the seventh paragraph of this law, the state of Israel sees the development of Jewish settlements as a national value for the entire Jewish people, he noted.  In addition, the expert drew attention to the fact that this law does not say anything about Jewish settlers in the West Bank, but only about the nature of the State of Israel.  Benny Briskin called such reports not new to Israel.  According to him, in Israel there are two points of view on this: either it is ordinary anti-Semitism, or it is left-wing liberalism.  But in any case, the result is the same - the attitude towards Israel is based on double standards, he stated.  “The approach of human rights organizations is that everything that happens in the territories they call occupied is already a crime.  It does not matter how the Jewish population behaves.  In Israel, they are already accustomed to this, ” the political scientist said.  He argues that the facts do not fit into these allegations.  The facts that lead human rights organizations, Briskin called slanderous fabrications of one side.  “That is, they find a Palestinian who tells a story that he was told to tell by the Palestinian secret services.  This is not verified in any way and is exposed as an unquestionable fact, ” he said.  “The claims of apartheid seem particularly absurd today, when Mansour Abbas — leader of the Joint Arab List in the Knesset — holds Israel ’ s political future in the wake of the March elections.  His voice is key in determining who will form the next governing coalition in Israel: Benjamin Netanyahu and his far-right supporters or the camp of his opponents.  Both sides are courting Abbas, which is hardly a sign of apartheid, ” said German Zakharyaev, president of the STMEGI Mountain Jews Foundation.
