passages.passage: Morning Post reporter Yu Wenyan at the corner of Fuxing East Road and Zhonghua Road, there is a small green space of only 500 square meters, which has installed three leisure seats and some small outdoor fitness equipment, which has become a "Cao Jia Street small garden" in the eyes of nearby residents. A number of pocket parks, which are often referred to as street gardens in the past, their presence not only allows nearby residents to walk, chat, fitness, and enjoy the green, but also lights up the environmental face of the block.  It is reported that the city built 47 pocket parks last year, and this year will build or upgrade 50.  Last year, 47 pocket parks were built at the corner of Fuxing East Road and Zhonghua Road, with a small green space of only 500 square meters.  Once, it was a green space, and now, it has become a "small garden in Cao Jia Street" in the eyes of nearby residents.  In Hongkou District, after a number of illegal buildings were demolished, a pocket park was built.  For example, the Huishan Garden at 207 Lintong Road, do not look at it with an area of only 408 square meters, but "five dirty", not only has exquisite and small green products, but also fitness trails.  In order to coordinate with the surrounding architectural style, the entrance to the park has also been designed in the style of Shikumen.  More than 2,300 square meters of public green space has been built in the area of 1501 North Xinshi Road, Jiangwan Town.  If there are no pavilions and seats for rest, it is also a little larger than the green space of Cao Jia Street.  But with activities and rest facilities, it becomes a simple little park.  According to incomplete statistics, 47 pocket parks were built in the city last year.  Pocket Park is not clearly defined Pocket Park, which originated from the proposal of the New York Parks Association in 1963, originally refers to small parks scattered in high-density urban centers and distributed in plaques.  Since the beginning of just over half a century, the United States, Britain, Japan and China and other countries have begun to have their own unique "pocket park plan".  Today's pocket parks refer to small green open spaces scattered in plaques in the city.  At present, there is no clear definition of pocket parks, and various small green spaces, small parks, street gardens, and small community sports venues in the city are common pocket parks.  Liu Yuelai, a scholar at Tongji University's School of Architecture and Urban Planning, said that there is currently no clear definition of the size of the pocket park.  In terms of area, he personally feels that it can be counted as small as tens of square meters and as large as thousands of square meters.  Unlike the comprehensive park, it offers simple and short breaks, such as a walk after a meal, a small sitting or children's play.  The city's greening department said that at present, their definition of the street garden from the area generally refers to the area of 300-3000 square meters of green space.  The municipal greening and cityscape administration bureau recently introduced that this year Shencheng plans to build or upgrade 50 pocket parks.  The actual number may be more than that.  Among the 79 colorful community projects recently released in Pudong, nearly 40 projects are defined as pocket parks. The pocket park in Hongkou District is planning to build the second phase of Yongnian Li, so that the pocket park function is becoming more and more perfect.  This year, Putuo plans to build a new 10,000 li community green space with a total area of 14,930 square meters, consisting of forests, wetlands and pocket parks.  The first part covers an area of about 10,970 square meters, and is designed to be an accessible urban forest and wetland.  The second part is located at the northwest corner of Wanquan Road and Fu Ping Road, covering an area of about 3960 square meters, and is designed to be positioned as a pocket park.  Fang Yan, deputy director of the municipal greening and cityscape administration bureau, said that the greening department is trying to make more parks around the citizens, even some street gardens and pocket parks, so that people can walk in parks not far from their homes.  According to the relevant person in charge of the municipal greening and cityscape administration bureau, the goal of allowing citizens to go out 500 meters to see a 3,000 square meter park green space has been basically achieved.  However, some residents feel that the greening of Shanghai is not enough.  Shanghai is still far behind Beijing, Hangzhou, Guangzhou and other cities, as well as New York, London and Paris.  For example, according to the area of public green space in the city and the base ratio of the resident population of more than 24 million, the per capita public green space is only about 8%, while some cities in China are generally more than 10%.  Therefore, in the case of limited land resources, Shanghai can only build more "pocket parks" and make dojo in snail shells.  It is understood that there are 243 urban parks in Shanghai, and by 2020, the number of urban parks will reach 300, forming a three-level system of "pocket parks - community parks - regional parks", and basically realizing that citizens go out 500 meters to have parks.

Small "pocket parks" in high-density urban settings have been found to have numerous benefits for fostering more sustainable and resilient cities [93e05d05-4e27-428b-ad4d-dbe50339cb48].

One of the primary benefits of pocket parks is their ability to provide citizens with easy access to green spaces, even in densely populated areas [93e05d05-4e27-428b-ad4d-dbe50339cb48]. 
According to Liu Yuelai, a scholar at Tongji University's School of Architecture and Urban Planning, there is currently no clear definition of the size of a pocket park, but they can be as small as tens of square meters or as large as thousands of square meters [93e05d05-4e27-428b-ad4d-dbe50339cb48].

Pocket parks can also serve as a refuge against the stresses of urban living, providing a peaceful oasis for citizens to relax and recharge [93e05d05-4e27-428b-ad4d-dbe50339cb48]. 
For example, the pocket park in Hongkou District, built after the demolition of illegal buildings, has become a popular spot for residents to take a break from the hustle and bustle of city life [93e05d05-4e27-428b-ad4d-dbe50339cb48].

In addition to providing citizens with access to green spaces, pocket parks can also play a role in promoting physical activity and healthy lifestyles [93e05d05-4e27-428b-ad4d-dbe50339cb48]. 
According to Fang Yan, deputy director of the municipal greening and cityscape administration bureau, the goal of allowing citizens to go out 500 meters to see a 3,000 square meter park green space has been basically achieved [93e05d05-4e27-428b-ad4d-dbe50339cb48].

Pocket parks can also serve as a catalyst for community engagement and social interaction [74bf07ff-54f6-4b1b-a956-8f5c4fe1739c]. 
In the Luhansk region, the creation of a network of sports grounds is part of a larger effort to promote socialization and community involvement [74bf07ff-54f6-4b1b-a956-8f5c4fe1739c]. 
The Luhansk region's innovative portal aims to promote the region and encourage citizens to participate in outdoor activities [74bf07ff-54f6-4b1b-a956-8f5c4fe1739c].

Furthermore, pocket parks can help to mitigate the negative impacts of urbanization on the environment [ee368122-879d-43ed-98ca-293ce65ddf38]. 
According to Yahya Sotoudeh Nia, the creation of small parks in urban areas can help to offset the lack of green spaces and provide a refuge for citizens [ee368122-879d-43ed-98ca-293ce65ddf38].

In terms of design, pocket parks can be tailored to meet the needs of local communities and provide a range of features and amenities [93e05d05-4e27-428b-ad4d-dbe50339cb48]. 
For example, the pocket park in Cao Jia Street, built in Shanghai, features three leisure seats and small outdoor fitness equipment [93e05d05-4e27-428b-ad4d-dbe50339cb48].

Overall, small "pocket parks" in high-density urban settings offer a range of benefits for fostering more sustainable and resilient cities [93e05d05-4e27-428b-ad4d-dbe50339cb48]. 
By providing citizens with access to green spaces, promoting physical activity and healthy lifestyles, and serving as a catalyst for community engagement and social interaction, pocket parks can play a key role in creating more livable and sustainable urban environments [93e05d05-4e27-428b-ad4d-dbe50339cb48].

The greening of cities is also an important aspect of creating more sustainable and resilient urban environments [93e05d05-4e27-428b-ad4d-dbe50339cb48]. 
According to Fang Yan, the greening department is trying to make more parks around the citizens, even some street gardens and pocket parks, so that people can walk in parks not far from their homes [93e05d05-4e27-428b-ad4d-dbe50339cb48].

In Shanghai, the goal is to create a three-level system of "pocket parks - community parks - regional parks" to provide citizens with access to green spaces [93e05d05-4e27-428b-ad4d-dbe50339cb48]. 
However, the city still has a long way to go in terms of providing adequate green spaces for its residents, with only about 8% of the population having access to public green space [93e05d05-4e27-428b-ad4d-dbe50339cb48].

Overall, the benefits of small "pocket parks" in high-density urban settings are clear, and their design and implementation can play a key role in creating more sustainable and resilient cities [93e05d05-4e27-428b-ad4d-dbe50339cb48].

Organized space simulates the behavior of people, and outsiders do not go there, ” the architect explained.  He also noted that concentrated areas of green areas are much more useful than a large area with bushes and trees scattered randomly around the area.  According to Sergey Kuznetsov, in densely built-up areas of the city, air movement is more calm, there are no strong winds, and trees do not fall as often. Title: Luhansk region and the values of European parks
Content: I remember the ambivalent feelings when I saw how in Prague or Warsaw locals play football in parks, organize exhibitions or sports competitions.  Ukraine still lives on the Soviet imperative: "do not walk on the lawns", with all the ensuing consequences.  The essence of the European "park" paradigm is that such territories are not considered only as places for green spaces.  These are full-fledged public spaces open to people coming with different goals and interests.  Including for physical education and sports.  In the Luhansk region launched an innovative portal that will promote the region Based on this, the requirements for the park as a place of socialization are applicable.  It should be interesting for a teenager on a skateboard, and for a mother with a stroller.  It seems to me that our people are already ready to perceive a new park culture, with a synthesis of environmental and utilitarian functions.  Finding for yourself an opportunity to retire, and a space for communication, and – involvement in the cultural landscape.  In this context, we are trying to fit the program of creating a network of sports grounds in the Luhansk region within the framework of the national project of the President "Healthy Country".  Its essence is in the creation of new public spaces on the territory of local communities.  Not just sports, but universal, for interesting pastime of different social groups.  We have already received funds for 52 sites, and in two years we expect to build 215.  80% of the cost will be provided by the state, subject to 20% co-financing by the community and the region.  The most effective and initiative communities will receive the right to participate in the project. We will install information stands and QR codes on the simulators to watch video instructions of the exercises through a smartphone.  We will provide a unified concept and design of sites.  We will make the highest environmental and safety requirements to minimize the risk of accidents.  Attracting public investment in the construction of health infrastructure is not just a mechanism for updating existing simulators.  This is an attempt to instill in the Luhansk region the European trends of public park spaces.  A significant part of the sports grounds will be placed in areas with green spaces or in places where they will be equipped in the future.  It can be small squares or front gardens, which will appear thanks to new sports locations.  This format, by the way, corresponds to the modern trend of leaving one central park.  European urbanists believe that for the balanced development of territories in the context of decentralization, in addition to the main, the so-called pocket parks in different parts of the community are important.  This provides aesthetic pleasure and stimulates the physical activity of local residents.  At the same time, natural ecosystems are comprehensively protected and local communities are economically strengthened.  The weak point of park zones in Ukraine is their actual availability at certain hours.  The downside of this phenomenon is their attraction to anti-social elements.  The presence of sports infrastructure will increase their public value and eliminate security risks.  And over time, it will instill life there and help attract investments.

Title: Luhansk region and the values of European parks
Content: I remember the ambivalent feelings when I saw how in Prague or Warsaw locals play football in parks, organize exhibitions or sports competitions.  Ukraine still lives on the Soviet imperative: "do not walk on the lawns", with all the ensuing consequences.  The essence of the European "park" paradigm is that such territories are not considered only as places for green spaces.  These are full-fledged public spaces open to people coming with different goals and interests.  Including for physical education and sports.  In the Luhansk region launched an innovative portal that will promote the region Based on this, the requirements for the park as a place of socialization are applicable.  It should be interesting for a teenager on a skateboard, and for a mother with a stroller.  It seems to me that our people are already ready to perceive a new park culture, with a synthesis of environmental and utilitarian functions.  Finding for yourself an opportunity to retire, and a space for communication, and – involvement in the cultural landscape.  In this context, we are trying to fit the program of creating a network of sports grounds in the Luhansk region within the framework of the national project of the President "Healthy Country".  Its essence is in the creation of new public spaces on the territory of local communities.  Not just sports, but universal, for interesting pastime of different social groups.  We have already received funds for 52 sites, and in two years we expect to build 215.  80% of the cost will be provided by the state, subject to 20% co-financing by the community and the region.  The most effective and initiative communities will receive the right to participate in the project.  See also See Paris and the Maldives without going abroad: 5 places in Ukraine, where you have not been yet Provide for the creation of a navigation map for the active involvement of different age groups.  We will install information stands and QR codes on the simulators to watch video instructions of the exercises through a smartphone.  We will provide a unified concept and design of sites.  We will make the highest environmental and safety requirements to minimize the risk of accidents.  Attracting public investment in the construction of health infrastructure is not just a mechanism for updating existing simulators.  This is an attempt to instill in the Luhansk region the European trends of public park spaces.  A significant part of the sports grounds will be placed in areas with green spaces or in places where they will be equipped in the future.  It can be small squares or front gardens, which will appear thanks to new sports locations.  This format, by the way, corresponds to the modern trend of leaving one central park.  European urbanists believe that for the balanced development of territories in the context of decentralization, in addition to the main, the so-called pocket parks in different parts of the community are important.  This provides aesthetic pleasure and stimulates the physical activity of local residents.  At the same time, natural ecosystems are comprehensively protected and local communities are economically strengthened.  The weak point of park zones in Ukraine is their actual availability at certain hours.  The downside of this phenomenon is their attraction to anti-social elements.  The presence of sports infrastructure will increase their public value and eliminate security risks.  And over time, it will instill life there and help attract investments.

passages.title: Middle East drama: Saudi Arabia, Turkey fight for TV audience
passages.passage: By Paul Law Last updated: 2021-06-03 13: 00 Turkey has been a soft power powerhouse in the Middle East for more than a decade, and its TV series have swept the entire Arab region.  Last year, local dramas became the annual hit in the Arab region, including “The Ambassador ’ s Daughter ” in Saudi Arabia,“ You Knock on My Door, ” which was popular with Arab audiences, and “Miracle Doctor, ” which was adapted from a Korean drama. It is also a good word.  In the face of the threat of domestic drama, Saudi Arabia, another big brother in the Arab world, naturally does not dare to ignore it. In recent years, it has actively developed the film and television industry, and even cooperated with the United Arab Emirates in order to “fight ” with Turkey in the field of television.  Is it face, interest, or a struggle for cultural soft power?  With its huge budget, excellent scenes and excellent acting skills, Turkey has produced a high level of drama in recent years.  The Capital: Abdul Hamid is pictured. (Getty) The history of Turkish television goes back almost half a century.  Forbidden Love, the first original drama, was produced in 1974, but its popularity began in 2006, when Turkey established its first satellite television station, and the series began to gain global exposure.  Two years later, Waleed bin Ibrahim Al Ibrahim, owner of the Middle East Broadcasting Center (MBC) in Saudi Arabia, bought the show and made it popular in the Arab region.  Among them, “Noor ”, a Turkish love story that aired between 2005 and 2007, reached an unprecedented audience of 92 million people; in early 2010,“ One Thousand and One Nights ” was exported to about 80 countries around the world; and in 2013, “Magnificent Century ”, an epic drama about Sulaiman, the Ottoman monarch, attracted more than 500 million viewers worldwide.  Each episode is usually about 60 minutes long on weekdays, and each episode is about 160 minutes long on weekdays.  These high cost productions featuring handsome male and female actors, with gorgeous scenes and catchy songs, plus romantic and Middle Eastern TV plots such as Noor, 1001 Nights, Ertugrul, which depict love, arranged marriage, extended family, patriarchy, and righteous struggle. The series has fascinated television viewers in the Arab world.  (Getty) Turkish dramas easily surpass foreign dramas in Mexico, the United States and South Korea in the Middle East, capturing the hearts of 200 million television viewers in the region, not only because there are no other strong competitors in the region, but also because Turkish producers re-dubbed the series with Arabic names and characters. In addition, the plot of the same Islamic culture makes the local drama more suitable to the tastes of Middle Eastern people than other overseas works.  However, in recent years, the development of Turkish and Saudi Arabia has been involved in the development of Turkish drama. In March 2018, the Saudi government and MBC stopped buying Turkish drama, when Sheikh Abdulaziz al-Sheikh, the Grand Chief of Saudi Arabia, described “Noor ” as“ anti-Islamic ” and “subversive ”, and said that the TV channel that broadcast the drama was“ God ”. and the enemies of its prophets ", and many of the region's major buyers went on strike to buy local dramas.  Egypt, another major market for Turkish dramas, has also banned Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan for “revenge ” after he backed then-President Mohamed Morsi during Egypt ’ s 2013 military coup, culminating in Abdel Fattah el-Sisi ’ s coming to power.  The development of Turkish dramas in the Middle East has been affected in recent years. (Getty) At present, support for the Muslim Brotherhood and other Islamic movements remains a major controversy in both countries, and is why Turkish dramas have not been shown in the region.  As a result, local dramas in the Middle East dropped from US $80 million (about HK $621 million) per year to US $15 million (about HK $116 million) last year.  Due to the severe restrictions on development in the Arab region, local dramas have begun to look around the world in recent years. In 2018, they were released for the first time in Spain, which immediately set off a wave of drama in the region, and later expanded to several European countries, including Italy.  Jose Antonio Anton, Vice President of the Atresmedia Group, a Spanish media group that introduced local dramas, believes that Turkey is a country that combines modern and traditional aspects, and these elements are fully reflected in the local dramas, so that the world can know the country.  “Turkish dramas are generally of high quality, and the plot is also very avant-garde, containing all kinds of drama elements, such as drama, horror, crime, history, etc. ” In addition, Turkish TV has a huge budget, excellent scenes, excellent acting and outdoor video studios, which have been able to produce high quality TV series in the past two decades.  (Getty) In recent years, local dramas have also turned to the Internet, testing the water on video streaming platforms such as YouTube, Starzplay, Netflix, etc., in order to export to the world.  At the same time, the change of local dramas is not only the target of export, but also the variety of drama tends to be diversified.  The current COVID-19 pandemic has also unexpectedly provided more support for local dramas. With many countries suspending filming due to the epidemic, and stopping purchasing expensive Korean dramas in Europe and the United States, affordable local dramas will continue to attract the attention of the world.  To date, Turkey has surpassed Mexico and Brazil as the world ’ s second largest exporter of television series, after the United States, with exports in Europe, the Arab region, Central Asia and the Americas. To date, the country has contributed more than 150 TV series to an estimated 500 million viewers in 146 countries around the world.  It is estimated that the total value of domestic drama exports reached US $500 million (about HK $3.9 billion) last year, and it is expected that by 2023, TV drama exports will generate as much as US $1 billion (about HK $7.8 billion) for Turkey.  Turkish dramas successfully export soft power, bringing many tourists to Turkey, and domestic products are also popular. (Reuters) The Turkish television industry plays a major role in increasing the popularity of the country in Asia, Europe, Latin America and North Africa.  In recent years, there has been an increase in interest in local dramas around the world. This has also played a positive role in promoting Turkey ’ s national image and its manufactured goods, and the number of foreign tourists visiting Istanbul has increased, especially from countries that broadcast local dramas.  All of this suggests that Turkey ’ s soft power is being infiltrated through television dramas.  Saudi Arabia ’ s Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman announced in 2018 that he would invest US $64 billion (HK $496.8 billion) over the next decade to develop the country ’ s entertainment industry.  The National Economic Reform Roadmap “Vision 2030 ” has“ loosened ” some socially conservative policies, such as the lifting of the 35-year commercial theater operating order in 2018.  Saudi Arabia expects to expand into other cultural areas in the future, encouraging arts, musical performances and other types of entertainment.  Saudi Arabia has loosened a 35-year ban on commercial cinemas. (Getty) In addition, the country will expand its film and television industry by building infrastructure, producing localized entertainment content and creating more than 30,000 jobs.  The authorities estimate that the country will have about 350 cinemas and 2,500 movie screens by 2030, with an industry value of about US $1 billion (about HK $7.8 billion).  The country also plans to double household entertainment spending, from 3% of GDP in 2018-2019 to 6% by 2030.  On the other hand, Saudi Arabia is also cooperating with the UAE to develop the film and television industry.  Among them, the US $40 million (HK $310 million) series Kingdoms of Fire, jointly funded by the two governments, was broadcast in 2019, highlighting the Ottoman Empire as the tyrant who has ravaged the Arab world for centuries.  In addition to co-productions, long-term cooperation programs between the two media companies also include training of production and acting personnel.  Kingdoms of Fire, a collaboration between Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates, was launched in 2019. (Getty) Saudi film and television professionals are mostly young people under the age of 30, 34% of whom are women.  Many people see that the film and television development in countries and regions is becoming more and more vigorous, and they no longer oppose their children to enroll in relevant courses, believing that they can find the ideal job after graduation.  According to Mohamed Ghazala, dean of the Faculty of Film and Television Arts at Effat University, Saudi Arabia, “The demand for local talent and capabilities will continue to increase due to increased production and the opening of more cinema-related departments and institutes in Saudi universities. ” However, the Saudi film and television industry is also facing many difficulties, with 43% of the industry believing that it is mainly lack of funding, 13 A further 11% said there was a lack of training and education related to film and television

passages.title: What is Turkey looking for with the ‘ establishment ’ security series?
passages.passage: What is Turkey looking for with the ‘ establishment ’ security series?  Turkish affairs expert Beryl Akmal, BBC monitoring 57 minutes ago image source, TRT Description of the picture, the organization is broadcast from the Turkish state television network Tarti, a television series that aired in Turkey in March and praised the Turkish intelligence and security agency, has become a popular program.  The series has attracted attention due to its many parallels with Turkey ’ s sharp foreign policy and nationalist rhetoric.  The series "The Establishment", broadcast on the state television network TRT, focuses on the missions of the National Intelligence and Security Agency (MITT) forces who want to return the security documents related to the stolen drone program to the country.  The series reportedly shows pictures of the new headquarters and has received positive feedback among the public.  However, critics say the series has an "informational" function.  The establishment is the latest in a popular series that opens a window into the world within Turkey ’ s ruling circles, as Ankara tries to strengthen its international power.  What is the story?  The series revolves around the operation to protect Turkey from a shadowy global network that tries to turn the world against Turkey ’ s ambitions.  A group of agents is responsible for returning documents related to the drone program to the country.  Image source, TRT1 Image Description, is the villainous Fadi in the series, whose plan is to curb Turkey ’ s ambitions; Zayed Fadi is the villainous and villainous character who is a member of the “Company ” group.  The pro-government Yeni Shafagh newspaper wrote that Fadi was an allusion to Mohammed Dahlan, the ouster and former leader of the Palestinian Fatah movement.  Fadi ’ s background is reminiscent of Dahlan, both Palestinians who grew up in refugee camps.  It is said that Dahlan was known as Abu Fadi.  Dahlan has long been on the Turkish government ’ s hate list.  The Turkish government has placed him on the "Most Wanted Terrorist List", which includes those accused of involvement in the July 2016 coup.  Images of Turkish drones appear throughout the series.  Turkey-made drones have attracted global attention in recent years and have been used in Libya, Iraq and Nagorno-Karabakh.  Image source, TRT Image caption, Turkish-made UAVs are frequently shown in the series, showing UAVs flying over northern Iraq, and emphasizing their use in operations against Kurdish forces.  In one episode of the show, Fadi said, “I can ’ t wait to see [the faces of the Turkish forces] being shocked by the drone crash. ”  The series also advertises Turkey ’ s efforts to build military hardware.  On March 23, Ismail Demir, head of defense industries, posted a video showing the conversation, talking about Turkish-made military technology that has developed despite foreign sanctions and promised that Turkey will build domestic fighters.  He said, “Don ’ t hesitate for a moment, we ’ ll do it. ”  The “terrorism ” of Turkey ’ s overseas operations is a central theme in the series, with“ terrorists ” among the evil forces working with Fadi.  The sixth episode shows a clash between "terrorists" and Turkish forces in northern Iraq, and the seventh episode shows a militant who vows to avenge his friend who was killed by Turkish forces.  The final episode of the series is an allusion to Eren Belbel, a boy who was said to have been killed in northern Turkey in 2017 by the "illegal" Kurdish Workers' Party (PKK).  See: Turkey 's booming TV series industry. To play this file please enable JavaScript or use another browser.  Turkish TV series are popular around the world, and this episode shows agents sitting next to a young boy named Eren on a plane.  He said: “The Yankees have always been very brave.  You are always very brave.  Thank you for being with us, Erin. "  The PKK has been fighting the government for decades for greater autonomy for the Kurdish minority in Turkey.  The party is on the list of terrorist organizations in Turkey, the United States and the European Union.  Turkey has carried out several operations against the group in northern Iraq.  In January, the Turkish Interior Ministry announced the start of "Operation Ern" against the PKK "in memory of Ern Nightingale, who was martyred by the separatists of the terrorist organization."  The foreign policy of Mitt ’ s characters repeatedly underscore the importance of patriotism as they fight the opposition.  In the opening scene of the first episode, neo-Nazis in Germany lead the attack on a house owned by Turkish immigrants, leaving Mitt's future agent Sardar orphaned.  The source of the image, TRT explaining the picture, the attack on Turkish immigrants in a scene from the series apparently refers to the Salingen attack.  The incident probably refers to the 1993 Salingen attack when a group of extremists set fire to a house and killed five Turks.  A diplomat promised to bring Sardar to Turkey after the raid.  When Sardar says he has no one, the diplomat replies, “You have your country. ”  The camera then focuses on the diplomatic ring, which has an image of the Turkish flag engraved on it.  The series ’ tenth episode, after a character asks about Turkey ’ s presence in Syria, focuses on Turkey ’ s military policies in the region.  “What are Italy, France, the United States and Russia doing there?  What is China doing there? ”  Another officer, referring to the Ottoman period, added: “The place we call Syria has been a part of the motherland for the last 100 years. ”  The comments echoed what Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan said in March 2020: “They ask what Turkey is doing in Syria.  But they don ’ t ask other countries that question. ”  The ninth episode shows a conversation between two agents and a local man in the Greek city of Kozani, reflecting the Turkish government ’ s criticism of the Greek government.  The man says, “They [the Greeks] don ’ t want us to have the rights of minorities.  Everyone is working to take children away from their own language, religion and culture. ”  Western Thrace Muslims in Greece are the cause of tensions between Turkey and Greece, and Ankara often accuses Athens of violating minority rights.  The impact of the series has attracted attention on social media and social media.  Image source, TRT Image Explanation, Artoghrol Uprising, is a historical representation of the T.R.T. network, which gained worldwide fame, the hashtag series Enterprise often trended on Twitter and drew significant reactions on Facebook.  According to an analysis by social media outlet Khuros, more than 620,000 tweets with the hashtag were posted between the first episode of the series in March and the last episode in June.  Each episode had more than three million viewers on YouTube, and people made passionate comments about it.  One of the comments at the bottom of the last part reads: "[This message] was sent throughout the whole series: Don't go head-to-head with the Turkish government."  High-ranking security expert Mathew Yarar praised the series for showcasing the “advances ” of the Turkish intelligence agency, the technology used in warfare and covert operations.  But some critics discredited the series as a "propaganda" series.  One user wrote, “This series is entirely a propaganda series for the ruling Justice and Development Party. ”  TV critic Sina Kluoğlu in the Milliat newspaper added: “Advertising in this type of series is natural.  The point is that it should be done cautiously. ”  Internationally Benefit?  Formation is one of several T.R.T. series that deal with national and religious issues in parallel with the government ’ s vision.  The series, centering on its story, the founder of the Ottoman Empire, gained international fame with its religious flavour and heroic stories.  The recently released “Bir Zamanlar Kibris ” depicts attacks on the island ’ s Gravey-Turkish family in 1963 before Turkey ’ s controversial intervention.  The upcoming series of Barbaros (named after the Ottoman admirals Barbaros Kheiruddin Pasha) is a narrative to highlight the heroes of the Ottoman Navy, which coincides with Ankara ’ s naval and war policy as “The Blue Homeland ”.  Tarti General Manager Ibrahim Ehren said: “We always put our finger on scripts and products that support the country ’ s history, culture, ethics and human values and we will continue to play that role.  Many of our products have attracted the attention of international viewers in recent years.

passages.title: Turkish operation in Syria; sense of nationalism rises in Turks
passages.passage: Getty Images Image caption The military salute of the Turkish national team was greeted by fans, as Turkish national football players cheered for their goals in their match against Albania, which was repeated in front of the French national team.  They were warned not to make political moves in the stadium, but they have already done so twice.  Following this move, the fans of the team, who were present at the Stade de France in Paris, began waving their country ’ s flags with great excitement.  These actions were a tribute to Turkey ’ s military operation in northern Syria and a “symbol of indifference ” to the international condemnation of Turkey ’ s operation in Syria.  In Turkey, when it comes to international competitions, football has succeeded in evoking a sense of nationalism, and when it is mixed with anti-West, it has become even more intense.  This spirit of “victory ” quickly pervaded all social networks.  One Twitter user wrote: “France, know us.  You condemn us, but we salute you on your soil.  Long live Turkey, we are making history.  In addition, many people have used the hashtag # ConquestofEurope.  Another social media user wrote: “A small reminder to Western and UEFA media that the salute is a political or racist message: it is not a political message but a way of expressing respect for the soldiers of a country made with the blood of its soldiers. ”  AFP Image caption Many Turks see Turkey's operation in northern Syria as a broader form of its fight against Kurdish militants on their soil, and why the Turks are defending their army in the Turkish border town of Agça Qala.  A resident of the city, waving the country's flag, told the BBC: "We are ready to go to the front line and fight.  We are waiting for Erdogan ’ s order. ”  Turkey has been at war with the PKK on its territory for more than three decades.  That ’ s why supporters of Turkey ’ s military intervention in northern Syria see the move as a broader struggle.  The popular support for the Turkish military shows a sense of nationalism in the country, which is louder than the wave of criticism, mostly because those who dare to oppose the national discourse of military operations face criminal charges.  Nearly 80 social media users who criticized the operation were prosecuted for "inciting hatred and engaging in propaganda to intimidate" and a large number of Twitter accounts belonging to Kurdish activists and journalists in Turkey have been closed.  The main tool of Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan to use his power to shape public opinion has been the media, which has always been criticized for misusing them as propaganda machines.  The bulk of Turkey ’ s mainstream media belong to Erdogan ’ s corporate conglomerates.  So it ’ s no surprise that the voices of the opposition are not being heard.  Media that mainly reflect the thinking of the government.  Turkey ’ s prominent TV anchors who have gone to the border, dressed in military uniforms, portray Turkey ’ s military intervention in northern Syria in an epic and passionate way.  Playback of this file on your device is not supported.  Why is Turkey now fighting the Kurds in northern Syria?  The nationalist narrative is also very popular in the Turkish press.  They don ’ t give much space to criticism, and if they do, they will attack it.  David Lamy, Labour MP in the UK, was no exception.  LeMay posted a video of a child who died, writing: “The human face of Trump ’ s decision to give free tickets to Turkey to attack Kurdish allies in northeastern Syria.  CNN Turk, the pro-government network on Twitter, along with an image of Mr. Lami, in which his skin was darkened by manipulation, accused him of "black propaganda" about Turkey's military intervention.  It was a reaction that was accepted by many racially minded people.  @ DavidLammy Why have @ cnnturk darkened my image in this picture to accuse me of spreading propaganda?  I am raising important issues about Trump's decision to abandon the Kurds to Erdogan's forces in north eastern Syria.  pic.twitter.com / k2907GqCck — David Lammy (@ DavidLammy) October 12, 2019 What do Turkish Kurds think is the official policy of Turkey in this operation to clear its borders from the SDF, which consists mainly of Syrian Kurdish militias as well as Arab and Christian fighters?  Kurds make up nearly 20 percent of Turkey ’ s population, but their voices are barely heard.  Most residents of the Kurdish city of Diyarbakir have decided to remain silent because of fear of legal action against them.  Among them is the owner of a spice shop in the city ’ s busiest market, who told the BBC: “We are all hurt but we suppress our emotions.  When you ’ re surrounded by cops in civilian clothes, no one will talk to you.  “The political parties in Turkey largely follow the line of the ruling Justice and Development Party: the secular Republican People ’ s Party, the Good Nationalist Party, and the Nationalist National Action Party all support this military operation.  With regard to opposition parties, there is only one exception: the Peoples ’ Democratic Party (HDP), which is pro-Kurdish.  Its leaders are in prison and its members face ongoing prosecution, threats and online violence.  A large number of HDP members who protested in the southeastern region of Turkey against the country ’ s military intervention were either arrested or forced to leave by police.  Police have raided several municipal buildings in the predominantly Kurdish cities of Hakkari, Mardin and Van, arresting a number of Kurdish executives.  When voices opposing military intervention are silenced or suppressed, a sense of nationalism is all that remains, a sense that pro-government media plays a central role in creating.

passages.title: Armenia is among the countries that pose a threat to Turkey, and the United States is in the first place: a survey
passages.passage: Recently, the results of a poll entitled “Studies of the perception of Turkish foreign policy in public opinion ” were published, conducted under the leadership of the university professor Kadir Has Cinema Akgül Achikmeshe.  The survey best reveals the attitude of the citizens of Turkey, which has been experiencing turbulent foreign policy and domestic political events in the past few years, to the problems of foreign policy of this country.  Changes in public sentiment can be seen by comparing the data that are given for 2013, 2015, 2016.  The survey was conducted in the form of personal interviews among thousands of people over 18 years of age in 26 ili (administrative unit of Turkey), representing the demographic structure of the country.  In particular, they were asked questions about various aspects of Turkish foreign policy.  Noteworthy is the fact that the majority of respondents in the neighboring country consider television to be the source of information about Ankara ’ s foreign policy (86.5%), 37.5% consider the Internet to be the source of information, and 30.7% consider the print press to be the source of information.  Judging by these indicators, it can be concluded that public opinion about Turkey ’ s foreign policy is formed through the interpretation of the media of this country.  The majority of Turkish citizens consider their country to be Islamic (39.9%).  It is interesting that during the presidency of Erdogan, in parallel with the increase in the component of Islam in the political life of the country, as well as in the conditions of tension in relations with the European Union, 32.7% of respondents consider Turkey a European country, while this indicator has grown over time (2013 - 24.3%, 2015 - 26.4%, 2016 - 31.8%).  The efforts of President Erdogan and the ruling party of Turkey, the attempted military coup in 2016, the constitutional amendments in 2017 formed an opinion in Turkish society about who exactly implements Turkey ’ s foreign policy.  So in 2016, 76.4% of respondents said that Turkey ’ s foreign policy is implemented by the President of Turkey, in 2017 this percentage was 69.2%.  24.3% of respondents believe that the foreign policy of Turkey is carried out by the Armed Forces of this country, 13.4% of respondents said that the National Intelligence Organization.  Even after last year ’ s July coup attempt, when the country began to persecute law enforcement officers, as well as after constitutional amendments in April this year, the Turkish authorities made the work of these structures more controlled.  A significant segment of Turkish society in 2017 expressed the opinion that the foreign policy of their country is carried out by law enforcement agencies, while 3.8% of respondents thought so in 2016, and in 2013 there was no such answer at all.  People living in Turkey are of the opinion that the foreign policy priority of their country is to strengthen relations with other countries - 61.2% of respondents, and 14.5% of respondents said that the mission of Turkish diplomatic missions in other countries is to collect information about these countries.  Turkish citizens were also asked which country is Turkey ’ s closest friend.  The overwhelming majority of respondents (71.3%) named Azerbaijan, last year 59.3% spoke in favor of this point of view.  Among friends, Pakistan ranks second, but only 2.2% of respondents think so.  About 1% of respondents consider several other countries as friends of Turkey, and 17.2% of respondents believe that Turkey has no friends at all.  At the same time, the number of those who believe that “Turkey has no friends ” decreased to 17.2% (against 23.1% last year).  In 2016, the Middle East came to the fore in the list of countries considered a threat to Turkey.  However, this year the first place went to the United States, and compared with last year, the United States is considered the largest threat by 22.4% of respondents more.  It is interesting that 19.1% of respondents consider the Armenian issue to be the main problem in US-Turkey relations.  The second biggest threat to Turkey was identified by 37.4% of respondents as Israel.  The EU countries, which last year were a threat according to 10.4% of respondents, this year ranked third in the ranking of countries posing a threat to Turkey, at a rate of 24%.  The level of perception of Russia as a threat fell from 34.9%.  After the normalization of Russian-Turkish relations this year, this figure fell to 18.5%.  It is noteworthy that Armenia ranks fifth in this list: 18% of respondents consider our country a threat.  Another point that draws attention to itself: from year to year, the inhabitants of Turkey provide less and less support for the process of accession of the country to the EU.  At the moment, support for Turkey ’ s membership in the EU is at 48.4%.  In 2015, the number of those who said: “Turkey will never be able to become a full member of the EU ” was 47.6%.  Last year, this figure rose to 66.7%, and this year to 81.3%.  At the same time, the number of those who support the creation of a different model in relations between Turkey and the EU – instead of full membership, remained at the level of 30.4%.  There is an increase in the number of supporters of the view that Turkey should build strategic cooperation with Russia as an alternative to EU membership (27.6% vs 14.8%).  17.6% consider the Organization of Islamic Cooperation as an alternative, 13.1% – the Shanghai Cooperation Organization.  The initiators of the survey also touched upon the topic of the unrecognized Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus.  78.4% of respondents believe that North Cyprus is a friendly country that cannot be turned away under any circumstances.  Turkish citizens were also asked about their attitude to the foreign policy pursued by their country.  38.5% of respondents expressed confidence that Turkey pursues a successful foreign policy, 37.8% believe that this policy is partially successful, 23.7% believe that Turkey ’ s foreign policy is unsuccessful.

passages.title: Home show, competitor or second branch of Turkish networks?
passages.passage: According to the Cinema Zone, the cultural group of the Young Journalists Club, with the increasing influence of satellite networks among Iranian families, one of the most significant damage that was mentioned for these networks was the cultural impact of the works broadcast by these networks, especially the Turkish series dubbed.  The series, based on the family as the central subject, provided sexist, pornographic, aristocratic and corrupt narratives of Turkish families, which due to the visual and sexual attractions, these series were able to tell stories of love triangles, betrayal, class divisions, anti-family, mere pleasure and corruption in the context of melodrama to many audiences with their own.  The increase in the activity of satellite networks and the distribution of Turkish works in Iranian satellite networks coincided with the increase of activities in Iran ’ s home theater network; at that time, some cultural analysts considered the home theater network as a reasonable response to satellite networks and an opportunity to overcome their works, a network that had less audits on its works and could attract the audience of Turkish TV series.  But that ’ s where the mistake started.  Many of the programmers and artists who were born and raised by the IRIB moved from television to the home theater network in order to gain more profit and freedom.  This, more than ever, left the hands of the cultural authorities of the IRIB empty to produce attractive and popular works and caused the TV audience to collapse.  On the other hand, less monitoring of the home screen network caused the creators active in this network, instead of presenting a new form and production of a cultural product, to resort to repetitive and sexual formulas of Turkish series and, with a glance from the rival, produced works that even in some cases, had lower quality and content than their Turkish rivals, and even caused some Iranian families to protest against some of these works.  Works that were only economical and did not spare any effort to sell more, from unnecessarily stretching the story, music-based video clips and creating triangular and square love nodes to the inclusion of erotic sequences.  Content works that, as a cultural commodity, had a countercultural function and only filled the pockets of its creators.  This is something that even the creators of these works are aware of.  From Manouchehr Hadi, the director of the love and romance series, who himself has confessed to modeling the Turkish series, to the writer of the series Dell, who says that the reason for the increase in the series' episodes is more money.  Now, some time after increasing the activity of VOD and attracting the audience through free subscription services and attractive plans to sell the works of the home theater network at a lower price than physical broadcasters and strengthening their position among the families as a multimedia and video broadcaster, in their latest action, they have dubbed and broadcast exclusive Turkish series.  The home theater network and VOD, which were supposed to rival Turkish satellite and TV channels, have now become their second branch.  Their cultural and content performance shows that the lack of proper supervision of the production of cultural works and the transfer of the field to individuals who are concerned only with financial interests, not cultural ones, provides the way for cultural influence and the destruction of the cultural foundations of the country and Iranian families.  Now that we are living in the era of the soft cultural war, the abandonment and lack of supervision in the field of cultural production can cause irreparable damage to our country; therefore, it is recommended that we not leave the field of culture to the enemy, by increasing the controls on the production of cultural works in the home theater network, and by producing great cultural works, such as Mokhtarnameh, the lost innocence, Hazrat Yusuf, English Kiev, Imam Ali, zero degree Hats off and...  We ourselves become the issuer of TV series, not the importer of Turkish serials, which can leave Iranian families with many cultural problems.  Author: The End of the Message

passages.title: Turkey's hot markets in South America
passages.passage: Turkish television series now reached South America after capturing the film market of the Indian subcontinent, the Middle East, the Caucasus, Central Asia and the Balkans.  In South America, Chile, Argentina and Mexico are among the biggest customers of Turkish TV series.  The popularity of Turkish series in the Middle East or the Caucasus may be due to cultural and historical commonalities, but what could be the reason for the booming Turkish series market on the other side of the Atlantic in South America?  Tuggs Shaw, a German broadcaster, has been trying to answer this question in a report on the popularity of Turkish shows in South America.  Yamaj Okur, producer of the Çukur story series, which has been translated into Persian as “Gut ”, says that a 140-minute episode will be produced every week, which will be broadcast on Turkish television five days later.  The Trench series is currently one of Turkey ’ s most successful series.  It tells the story of a family who controls one of Istanbul ’ s most dangerous neighborhoods, the Pit.  The neighborhood has long been in the hands of small families, whose most important rule is to be strict about the distribution of drugs in the neighborhood.  If someone spreads drugs, they have to leave the neighborhood.  The first episode of the series premiered on October 23, 2017 on TV and is still ongoing.  Correspondents from Istanbul and Rio de Janeiro say the demand for Turkish TV shows has increased.  Diazis, or series, forms a separate genre on Turkish television that is more comparable to the well-known South American telenovelas.  Araya Kisternas, a Chilean couple who have been married for almost 50 years, has just discovered their love for Turkish TV shows.  They say they show love with respect in this series.  The looks are romantic and traditional families are portrayed as important and valuable.  The Chilean couple have a herd that "in modern South American nostalgia traps shows a lot of bare limbs, men kiss men, and violence is part of the film."  Juan Vicente, director of the Chilean TV channel Mega, brought the first Turkish series to South America seven years ago.  He recalls that when the show “Binbir gece ” was broadcast on the mega network, he enthralled people and saved the mega network from bankruptcy at the time.  Juwan goes on to say that since many South Americans are conservative and dream of an ideal world, Turkish TV shows are in their best interest.  Family structures in Turkey are comparable to those in South America.  The patriarchal structures with a strong grandfather or father who determines and leads everything in the family are similar to the Chilean family structure.  The traditional family structure is also popular in Turkey, thanks to Erdoğan ’ s conservative and Islamist government.  Thousands took to the streets in recent days to protest Turkey ’ s withdrawal from the Convention against Violence against Women, but the protests have not been successful so far.  Yamaj Okor, producer of The Pit, says sex, swearing, alcohol in movies and TV shows are as taboo as they were in the '90s.  Okor added, “We have to tell our stories more gently, otherwise the TV won ’ t play it. ”  The series as Turkey ’ s “soft power ” is different from most Turkish series that depict the glamorous life of the middle and upper classes.  In this series, usually luxury cars, expensive clothes are displayed.  But the hole has a different atmosphere.  The series is filmed in the Balat district of Istanbul.  In the Balat district of Istanbul, which used to be home to Jewish, Armenian and Greek communities, it is now a simple working-class area, but thanks to the series, the neighborhood has now flourished and many cafes have opened in its corners over the past few years.  Tagus Shaw reports that at any given time during filming, about 200 fans of the Pit series gather at the scene.  On the other hand, vendors are trying to sell their goods, and in the future, visitors to South America are likely to be seen in the narrow alleys of Balat.  The series was recently sold to Chile.  The Chilean couple who are fascinated by the film are also planning a trip to Turkey.  Hector said: “A trip to Turkey would be a dream for us. ”  His wife, Patricia, interrupts him: “In the past, we never had any idea of Turkey.  We knew a Turkey full of violence with terrorist attacks.  But now it seems to be getting better. ”  Turkey ’ s $1 billion in revenue has become the world ’ s second-largest TV series exporter after Hollywood.  Recent research by Turkish state television shows that Turkish dramas are a “soft power, ” often trying to convey a specific image in the form of a romantic historical drama from the Ottoman period, which is usually reflected in the politics of the current Turkish government.  Follow Deutsche Welle on Instagram: “We are exporting Turkish culture, language and products.  Many of them just became popular abroad through our series.  Take, for example, Turkish music, which is now popular in South America. ”  According to estimates by the Turkish film industry, the revenue of the series could reach $1 billion by 2023.  At the end of his report on the Turkish series, Tagus Shaw has written that the next goal of the Turkish series is to capture the film market in Spain and Italy.

Title: Middle East drama: Saudi Arabia, Turkey fight for TV audience
Content: By Paul Law Last updated: 2021-06-03 13: 00 Turkey has been a soft power powerhouse in the Middle East for more than a decade, and its TV series have swept the entire Arab region.  Last year, local dramas became the annual hit in the Arab region, including “The Ambassador ’ s Daughter ” in Saudi Arabia,“ You Knock on My Door, ” which was popular with Arab audiences, and “Miracle Doctor, ” which was adapted from a Korean drama. It is also a good word.  In the face of the threat of domestic drama, Saudi Arabia, another big brother in the Arab world, naturally does not dare to ignore it. In recent years, it has actively developed the film and television industry, and even cooperated with the United Arab Emirates in order to “fight ” with Turkey in the field of television.  Is it face, interest, or a struggle for cultural soft power?  With its huge budget, excellent scenes and excellent acting skills, Turkey has produced a high level of drama in recent years.  The Capital: Abdul Hamid is pictured. (Getty) The history of Turkish television goes back almost half a century.  Forbidden Love, the first original drama, was produced in 1974, but its popularity began in 2006, when Turkey established its first satellite television station, and the series began to gain global exposure.  Two years later, Waleed bin Ibrahim Al Ibrahim, owner of the Middle East Broadcasting Center (MBC) in Saudi Arabia, bought the show and made it popular in the Arab region.  Among them, “Noor ”, a Turkish love story that aired between 2005 and 2007, reached an unprecedented audience of 92 million people; in early 2010,“ One Thousand and One Nights ” was exported to about 80 countries around the world; and in 2013, “Magnificent Century ”, an epic drama about Sulaiman, the Ottoman monarch, attracted more than 500 million viewers worldwide.  Each episode is usually about 60 minutes long on weekdays, and each episode is about 160 minutes long on weekdays.  These high cost productions featuring handsome male and female actors, with gorgeous scenes and catchy songs, plus romantic and Middle Eastern TV plots such as Noor, 1001 Nights, Ertugrul, which depict love, arranged marriage, extended family, patriarchy, and righteous struggle. The series has fascinated television viewers in the Arab world.  (Getty) Turkish dramas easily surpass foreign dramas in Mexico, the United States and South Korea in the Middle East, capturing the hearts of 200 million television viewers in the region, not only because there are no other strong competitors in the region, but also because Turkish producers re-dubbed the series with Arabic names and characters. In addition, the plot of the same Islamic culture makes the local drama more suitable to the tastes of Middle Eastern people than other overseas works.  However, in recent years, the development of Turkish and Saudi Arabia has been involved in the development of Turkish drama. In March 2018, the Saudi government and MBC stopped buying Turkish drama, when Sheikh Abdulaziz al-Sheikh, the Grand Chief of Saudi Arabia, described “Noor ” as“ anti-Islamic ” and “subversive ”, and said that the TV channel that broadcast the drama was“ God ”. and the enemies of its prophets ", and many of the region's major buyers went on strike to buy local dramas.  Egypt, another major market for Turkish dramas, has also banned Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan for “revenge ” after he backed then-President Mohamed Morsi during Egypt ’ s 2013 military coup, culminating in Abdel Fattah el-Sisi ’ s coming to power.  The development of Turkish dramas in the Middle East has been affected in recent years. (Getty) At present, support for the Muslim Brotherhood and other Islamic movements remains a major controversy in both countries, and is why Turkish dramas have not been shown in the region.  As a result, local dramas in the Middle East dropped from US $80 million (about HK $621 million) per year to US $15 million (about HK $116 million) last year.  Due to the severe restrictions on development in the Arab region, local dramas have begun to look around the world in recent years. In 2018, they were released for the first time in Spain, which immediately set off a wave of drama in the region, and later expanded to several European countries, including Italy.  Jose Antonio Anton, Vice President of the Atresmedia Group, a Spanish media group that introduced local dramas, believes that Turkey is a country that combines modern and traditional aspects, and these elements are fully reflected in the local dramas, so that the world can know the country.  “Turkish dramas are generally of high quality, and the plot is also very avant-garde, containing all kinds of drama elements, such as drama, horror, crime, history, etc. ” In addition, Turkish TV has a huge budget, excellent scenes, excellent acting and outdoor video studios, which have been able to produce high quality TV series in the past two decades.  (Getty) In recent years, local dramas have also turned to the Internet, testing the water on video streaming platforms such as YouTube, Starzplay, Netflix, etc., in order to export to the world.  At the same time, the change of local dramas is not only the target of export, but also the variety of drama tends to be diversified.  The current COVID-19 pandemic has also unexpectedly provided more support for local dramas. With many countries suspending filming due to the epidemic, and stopping purchasing expensive Korean dramas in Europe and the United States, affordable local dramas will continue to attract the attention of the world.  To date, Turkey has surpassed Mexico and Brazil as the world ’ s second largest exporter of television series, after the United States, with exports in Europe, the Arab region, Central Asia and the Americas. To date, the country has contributed more than 150 TV series to an estimated 500 million viewers in 146 countries around the world.  It is estimated that the total value of domestic drama exports reached US $500 million (about HK $3.9 billion) last year, and it is expected that by 2023, TV drama exports will generate as much as US $1 billion (about HK $7.8 billion) for Turkey.  Turkish dramas successfully export soft power, bringing many tourists to Turkey, and domestic products are also popular. (Reuters) The Turkish television industry plays a major role in increasing the popularity of the country in Asia, Europe, Latin America and North Africa.  In recent years, there has been an increase in interest in local dramas around the world. This has also played a positive role in promoting Turkey ’ s national image and its manufactured goods, and the number of foreign tourists visiting Istanbul has increased, especially from countries that broadcast local dramas.  All of this suggests that Turkey ’ s soft power is being infiltrated through television dramas.  Saudi Arabia ’ s Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman announced in 2018 that he would invest US $64 billion (HK $496.8 billion) over the next decade to develop the country ’ s entertainment industry.  The National Economic Reform Roadmap “Vision 2030 ” has“ loosened ” some socially conservative policies, such as the lifting of the 35-year commercial theater operating order in 2018.  Saudi Arabia expects to expand into other cultural areas in the future, encouraging arts, musical performances and other types of entertainment.  Saudi Arabia has loosened a 35-year ban on commercial cinemas. (Getty) In addition, the country will expand its film and television industry by building infrastructure, producing localized entertainment content and creating more than 30,000 jobs.  The authorities estimate that the country will have about 350 cinemas and 2,500 movie screens by 2030, with an industry value of about US $1 billion (about HK $7.8 billion).  The country also plans to double household entertainment spending, from 3% of GDP in 2018-2019 to 6% by 2030.  On the other hand, Saudi Arabia is also cooperating with the UAE to develop the film and television industry.  Among them, the US $40 million (HK $310 million) series Kingdoms of Fire, jointly funded by the two governments, was broadcast in 2019, highlighting the Ottoman Empire as the tyrant who has ravaged the Arab world for centuries.  In addition to co-productions, long-term cooperation programs between the two media companies also include training of production and acting personnel.  Kingdoms of Fire, a collaboration between Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates, was launched in 2019. (Getty) Saudi film and television professionals are mostly young people under the age of 30, 34% of whom are women.  Many people see that the film and television development in countries and regions is becoming more and more vigorous, and they no longer oppose their children to enroll in relevant courses, believing that they can find the ideal job after graduation.  According to Mohamed Ghazala, dean of the Faculty of Film and Television Arts at Effat University, Saudi Arabia, “The demand for local talent and capabilities will continue to increase due to increased production and the opening of more cinema-related departments and institutes in Saudi universities. ” However, the Saudi film and television industry is also facing many difficulties, with 43% of the industry believing that it is mainly lack of funding, 13 A further 11% said there was a lack of training and education related to film and television

Title: What is Turkey looking for with the ‘ establishment ’ security series?
Content: What is Turkey looking for with the ‘ establishment ’ security series?  Turkish affairs expert Beryl Akmal, BBC monitoring 57 minutes ago image source, TRT Description of the picture, the organization is broadcast from the Turkish state television network Tarti, a television series that aired in Turkey in March and praised the Turkish intelligence and security agency, has become a popular program.  The series has attracted attention due to its many parallels with Turkey ’ s sharp foreign policy and nationalist rhetoric.  The series "The Establishment", broadcast on the state television network TRT, focuses on the missions of the National Intelligence and Security Agency (MITT) forces who want to return the security documents related to the stolen drone program to the country.  The series reportedly shows pictures of the new headquarters and has received positive feedback among the public.  However, critics say the series has an "informational" function.  The establishment is the latest in a popular series that opens a window into the world within Turkey ’ s ruling circles, as Ankara tries to strengthen its international power.  What is the story?  The series revolves around the operation to protect Turkey from a shadowy global network that tries to turn the world against Turkey ’ s ambitions.  A group of agents is responsible for returning documents related to the drone program to the country.  Image source, TRT1 Image Description, is the villainous Fadi in the series, whose plan is to curb Turkey ’ s ambitions; Zayed Fadi is the villainous and villainous character who is a member of the “Company ” group.  The pro-government Yeni Shafagh newspaper wrote that Fadi was an allusion to Mohammed Dahlan, the ouster and former leader of the Palestinian Fatah movement.  Fadi ’ s background is reminiscent of Dahlan, both Palestinians who grew up in refugee camps.  It is said that Dahlan was known as Abu Fadi.  Dahlan has long been on the Turkish government ’ s hate list.  The Turkish government has placed him on the "Most Wanted Terrorist List", which includes those accused of involvement in the July 2016 coup.  Images of Turkish drones appear throughout the series.  Turkey-made drones have attracted global attention in recent years and have been used in Libya, Iraq and Nagorno-Karabakh.  Image source, TRT Image caption, Turkish-made UAVs are frequently shown in the series, showing UAVs flying over northern Iraq, and emphasizing their use in operations against Kurdish forces.  In one episode of the show, Fadi said, “I can ’ t wait to see [the faces of the Turkish forces] being shocked by the drone crash. ”  The series also advertises Turkey ’ s efforts to build military hardware.  On March 23, Ismail Demir, head of defense industries, posted a video showing the conversation, talking about Turkish-made military technology that has developed despite foreign sanctions and promised that Turkey will build domestic fighters.  He said, “Don ’ t hesitate for a moment, we ’ ll do it. ”  The “terrorism ” of Turkey ’ s overseas operations is a central theme in the series, with“ terrorists ” among the evil forces working with Fadi.  The sixth episode shows a clash between "terrorists" and Turkish forces in northern Iraq, and the seventh episode shows a militant who vows to avenge his friend who was killed by Turkish forces.  The final episode of the series is an allusion to Eren Belbel, a boy who was said to have been killed in northern Turkey in 2017 by the "illegal" Kurdish Workers' Party (PKK).  See: Turkey 's booming TV series industry. To play this file please enable JavaScript or use another browser.  Turkish TV series are popular around the world, and this episode shows agents sitting next to a young boy named Eren on a plane.  He said: “The Yankees have always been very brave.  You are always very brave.  Thank you for being with us, Erin. "  The PKK has been fighting the government for decades for greater autonomy for the Kurdish minority in Turkey.  The party is on the list of terrorist organizations in Turkey, the United States and the European Union.  Turkey has carried out several operations against the group in northern Iraq.  In January, the Turkish Interior Ministry announced the start of "Operation Ern" against the PKK "in memory of Ern Nightingale, who was martyred by the separatists of the terrorist organization."  The foreign policy of Mitt ’ s characters repeatedly underscore the importance of patriotism as they fight the opposition.  In the opening scene of the first episode, neo-Nazis in Germany lead the attack on a house owned by Turkish immigrants, leaving Mitt's future agent Sardar orphaned.  The source of the image, TRT explaining the picture, the attack on Turkish immigrants in a scene from the series apparently refers to the Salingen attack.  The incident probably refers to the 1993 Salingen attack when a group of extremists set fire to a house and killed five Turks.  A diplomat promised to bring Sardar to Turkey after the raid.  When Sardar says he has no one, the diplomat replies, “You have your country. ”  The camera then focuses on the diplomatic ring, which has an image of the Turkish flag engraved on it.  The series ’ tenth episode, after a character asks about Turkey ’ s presence in Syria, focuses on Turkey ’ s military policies in the region.  “What are Italy, France, the United States and Russia doing there?  What is China doing there? ”  Another officer, referring to the Ottoman period, added: “The place we call Syria has been a part of the motherland for the last 100 years. ”  The comments echoed what Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan said in March 2020: “They ask what Turkey is doing in Syria.  But they don ’ t ask other countries that question. ”  The ninth episode shows a conversation between two agents and a local man in the Greek city of Kozani, reflecting the Turkish government ’ s criticism of the Greek government.  The man says, “They [the Greeks] don ’ t want us to have the rights of minorities.  Everyone is working to take children away from their own language, religion and culture. ”  Western Thrace Muslims in Greece are the cause of tensions between Turkey and Greece, and Ankara often accuses Athens of violating minority rights.  The impact of the series has attracted attention on social media and social media.  Image source, TRT Image Explanation, Artoghrol Uprising, is a historical representation of the T.R.T. network, which gained worldwide fame, the hashtag series Enterprise often trended on Twitter and drew significant reactions on Facebook.  According to an analysis by social media outlet Khuros, more than 620,000 tweets with the hashtag were posted between the first episode of the series in March and the last episode in June.  Each episode had more than three million viewers on YouTube, and people made passionate comments about it.  One of the comments at the bottom of the last part reads: "[This message] was sent throughout the whole series: Don't go head-to-head with the Turkish government."  High-ranking security expert Mathew Yarar praised the series for showcasing the “advances ” of the Turkish intelligence agency, the technology used in warfare and covert operations.  But some critics discredited the series as a "propaganda" series.  One user wrote, “This series is entirely a propaganda series for the ruling Justice and Development Party. ”  TV critic Sina Kluoğlu in the Milliat newspaper added: “Advertising in this type of series is natural.  The point is that it should be done cautiously. ”  Internationally Benefit?  Formation is one of several T.R.T. series that deal with national and religious issues in parallel with the government ’ s vision.  The series, centering on its story, the founder of the Ottoman Empire, gained international fame with its religious flavour and heroic stories.  The recently released “Bir Zamanlar Kibris ” depicts attacks on the island ’ s Gravey-Turkish family in 1963 before Turkey ’ s controversial intervention.  The upcoming series of Barbaros (named after the Ottoman admirals Barbaros Kheiruddin Pasha) is a narrative to highlight the heroes of the Ottoman Navy, which coincides with Ankara ’ s naval and war policy as “The Blue Homeland ”.  Tarti General Manager Ibrahim Ehren said: “We always put our finger on scripts and products that support the country ’ s history, culture, ethics and human values and we will continue to play that role.  Many of our products have attracted the attention of international viewers in recent years.
