Title: Turkish operation in Syria; sense of nationalism rises in Turks
Content: Getty Images Image caption The military salute of the Turkish national team was greeted by fans, as Turkish national football players cheered for their goals in their match against Albania, which was repeated in front of the French national team.  They were warned not to make political moves in the stadium, but they have already done so twice.  Following this move, the fans of the team, who were present at the Stade de France in Paris, began waving their country ’ s flags with great excitement.  These actions were a tribute to Turkey ’ s military operation in northern Syria and a “symbol of indifference ” to the international condemnation of Turkey ’ s operation in Syria.  In Turkey, when it comes to international competitions, football has succeeded in evoking a sense of nationalism, and when it is mixed with anti-West, it has become even more intense.  This spirit of “victory ” quickly pervaded all social networks.  One Twitter user wrote: “France, know us.  You condemn us, but we salute you on your soil.  Long live Turkey, we are making history.  In addition, many people have used the hashtag # ConquestofEurope.  Another social media user wrote: “A small reminder to Western and UEFA media that the salute is a political or racist message: it is not a political message but a way of expressing respect for the soldiers of a country made with the blood of its soldiers. ”  AFP Image caption Many Turks see Turkey's operation in northern Syria as a broader form of its fight against Kurdish militants on their soil, and why the Turks are defending their army in the Turkish border town of Agça Qala.  A resident of the city, waving the country's flag, told the BBC: "We are ready to go to the front line and fight.  We are waiting for Erdogan ’ s order. ”  Turkey has been at war with the PKK on its territory for more than three decades.  That ’ s why supporters of Turkey ’ s military intervention in northern Syria see the move as a broader struggle.  The popular support for the Turkish military shows a sense of nationalism in the country, which is louder than the wave of criticism, mostly because those who dare to oppose the national discourse of military operations face criminal charges.  Nearly 80 social media users who criticized the operation were prosecuted for "inciting hatred and engaging in propaganda to intimidate" and a large number of Twitter accounts belonging to Kurdish activists and journalists in Turkey have been closed.  The main tool of Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan to use his power to shape public opinion has been the media, which has always been criticized for misusing them as propaganda machines.  The bulk of Turkey ’ s mainstream media belong to Erdogan ’ s corporate conglomerates.  So it ’ s no surprise that the voices of the opposition are not being heard.  Media that mainly reflect the thinking of the government.  Turkey ’ s prominent TV anchors who have gone to the border, dressed in military uniforms, portray Turkey ’ s military intervention in northern Syria in an epic and passionate way.  Playback of this file on your device is not supported.  Why is Turkey now fighting the Kurds in northern Syria?  The nationalist narrative is also very popular in the Turkish press.  They don ’ t give much space to criticism, and if they do, they will attack it.  David Lamy, Labour MP in the UK, was no exception.  LeMay posted a video of a child who died, writing: “The human face of Trump ’ s decision to give free tickets to Turkey to attack Kurdish allies in northeastern Syria.  CNN Turk, the pro-government network on Twitter, along with an image of Mr. Lami, in which his skin was darkened by manipulation, accused him of "black propaganda" about Turkey's military intervention.  It was a reaction that was accepted by many racially minded people.  @ DavidLammy Why have @ cnnturk darkened my image in this picture to accuse me of spreading propaganda?  I am raising important issues about Trump's decision to abandon the Kurds to Erdogan's forces in north eastern Syria.  pic.twitter.com / k2907GqCck — David Lammy (@ DavidLammy) October 12, 2019 What do Turkish Kurds think is the official policy of Turkey in this operation to clear its borders from the SDF, which consists mainly of Syrian Kurdish militias as well as Arab and Christian fighters?  Kurds make up nearly 20 percent of Turkey ’ s population, but their voices are barely heard.  Most residents of the Kurdish city of Diyarbakir have decided to remain silent because of fear of legal action against them.  Among them is the owner of a spice shop in the city ’ s busiest market, who told the BBC: “We are all hurt but we suppress our emotions.  When you ’ re surrounded by cops in civilian clothes, no one will talk to you.  “The political parties in Turkey largely follow the line of the ruling Justice and Development Party: the secular Republican People ’ s Party, the Good Nationalist Party, and the Nationalist National Action Party all support this military operation.  With regard to opposition parties, there is only one exception: the Peoples ’ Democratic Party (HDP), which is pro-Kurdish.  Its leaders are in prison and its members face ongoing prosecution, threats and online violence.  A large number of HDP members who protested in the southeastern region of Turkey against the country ’ s military intervention were either arrested or forced to leave by police.  Police have raided several municipal buildings in the predominantly Kurdish cities of Hakkari, Mardin and Van, arresting a number of Kurdish executives.  When voices opposing military intervention are silenced or suppressed, a sense of nationalism is all that remains, a sense that pro-government media plays a central role in creating.

Title: Armenia is among the countries that pose a threat to Turkey, and the United States is in the first place: a survey
Content: Recently, the results of a poll entitled “Studies of the perception of Turkish foreign policy in public opinion ” were published, conducted under the leadership of the university professor Kadir Has Cinema Akgül Achikmeshe.  The survey best reveals the attitude of the citizens of Turkey, which has been experiencing turbulent foreign policy and domestic political events in the past few years, to the problems of foreign policy of this country.  Changes in public sentiment can be seen by comparing the data that are given for 2013, 2015, 2016.  The survey was conducted in the form of personal interviews among thousands of people over 18 years of age in 26 ili (administrative unit of Turkey), representing the demographic structure of the country.  In particular, they were asked questions about various aspects of Turkish foreign policy.  Noteworthy is the fact that the majority of respondents in the neighboring country consider television to be the source of information about Ankara ’ s foreign policy (86.5%), 37.5% consider the Internet to be the source of information, and 30.7% consider the print press to be the source of information.  Judging by these indicators, it can be concluded that public opinion about Turkey ’ s foreign policy is formed through the interpretation of the media of this country.  The majority of Turkish citizens consider their country to be Islamic (39.9%).  It is interesting that during the presidency of Erdogan, in parallel with the increase in the component of Islam in the political life of the country, as well as in the conditions of tension in relations with the European Union, 32.7% of respondents consider Turkey a European country, while this indicator has grown over time (2013 - 24.3%, 2015 - 26.4%, 2016 - 31.8%).  The efforts of President Erdogan and the ruling party of Turkey, the attempted military coup in 2016, the constitutional amendments in 2017 formed an opinion in Turkish society about who exactly implements Turkey ’ s foreign policy.  So in 2016, 76.4% of respondents said that Turkey ’ s foreign policy is implemented by the President of Turkey, in 2017 this percentage was 69.2%.  24.3% of respondents believe that the foreign policy of Turkey is carried out by the Armed Forces of this country, 13.4% of respondents said that the National Intelligence Organization.  Even after last year ’ s July coup attempt, when the country began to persecute law enforcement officers, as well as after constitutional amendments in April this year, the Turkish authorities made the work of these structures more controlled.  A significant segment of Turkish society in 2017 expressed the opinion that the foreign policy of their country is carried out by law enforcement agencies, while 3.8% of respondents thought so in 2016, and in 2013 there was no such answer at all.  People living in Turkey are of the opinion that the foreign policy priority of their country is to strengthen relations with other countries - 61.2% of respondents, and 14.5% of respondents said that the mission of Turkish diplomatic missions in other countries is to collect information about these countries.  Turkish citizens were also asked which country is Turkey ’ s closest friend.  The overwhelming majority of respondents (71.3%) named Azerbaijan, last year 59.3% spoke in favor of this point of view.  Among friends, Pakistan ranks second, but only 2.2% of respondents think so.  About 1% of respondents consider several other countries as friends of Turkey, and 17.2% of respondents believe that Turkey has no friends at all.  At the same time, the number of those who believe that “Turkey has no friends ” decreased to 17.2% (against 23.1% last year).  In 2016, the Middle East came to the fore in the list of countries considered a threat to Turkey.  However, this year the first place went to the United States, and compared with last year, the United States is considered the largest threat by 22.4% of respondents more.  It is interesting that 19.1% of respondents consider the Armenian issue to be the main problem in US-Turkey relations.  The second biggest threat to Turkey was identified by 37.4% of respondents as Israel.  The EU countries, which last year were a threat according to 10.4% of respondents, this year ranked third in the ranking of countries posing a threat to Turkey, at a rate of 24%.  The level of perception of Russia as a threat fell from 34.9%.  After the normalization of Russian-Turkish relations this year, this figure fell to 18.5%.  It is noteworthy that Armenia ranks fifth in this list: 18% of respondents consider our country a threat.  Another point that draws attention to itself: from year to year, the inhabitants of Turkey provide less and less support for the process of accession of the country to the EU.  At the moment, support for Turkey ’ s membership in the EU is at 48.4%.  In 2015, the number of those who said: “Turkey will never be able to become a full member of the EU ” was 47.6%.  Last year, this figure rose to 66.7%, and this year to 81.3%.  At the same time, the number of those who support the creation of a different model in relations between Turkey and the EU – instead of full membership, remained at the level of 30.4%.  There is an increase in the number of supporters of the view that Turkey should build strategic cooperation with Russia as an alternative to EU membership (27.6% vs 14.8%).  17.6% consider the Organization of Islamic Cooperation as an alternative, 13.1% – the Shanghai Cooperation Organization.  The initiators of the survey also touched upon the topic of the unrecognized Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus.  78.4% of respondents believe that North Cyprus is a friendly country that cannot be turned away under any circumstances.  Turkish citizens were also asked about their attitude to the foreign policy pursued by their country.  38.5% of respondents expressed confidence that Turkey pursues a successful foreign policy, 37.8% believe that this policy is partially successful, 23.7% believe that Turkey ’ s foreign policy is unsuccessful.

Title: Home show, competitor or second branch of Turkish networks?
Content: According to the Cinema Zone, the cultural group of the Young Journalists Club, with the increasing influence of satellite networks among Iranian families, one of the most significant damage that was mentioned for these networks was the cultural impact of the works broadcast by these networks, especially the Turkish series dubbed.  The series, based on the family as the central subject, provided sexist, pornographic, aristocratic and corrupt narratives of Turkish families, which due to the visual and sexual attractions, these series were able to tell stories of love triangles, betrayal, class divisions, anti-family, mere pleasure and corruption in the context of melodrama to many audiences with their own.  The increase in the activity of satellite networks and the distribution of Turkish works in Iranian satellite networks coincided with the increase of activities in Iran ’ s home theater network; at that time, some cultural analysts considered the home theater network as a reasonable response to satellite networks and an opportunity to overcome their works, a network that had less audits on its works and could attract the audience of Turkish TV series.  But that ’ s where the mistake started.  Many of the programmers and artists who were born and raised by the IRIB moved from television to the home theater network in order to gain more profit and freedom.  This, more than ever, left the hands of the cultural authorities of the IRIB empty to produce attractive and popular works and caused the TV audience to collapse.  On the other hand, less monitoring of the home screen network caused the creators active in this network, instead of presenting a new form and production of a cultural product, to resort to repetitive and sexual formulas of Turkish series and, with a glance from the rival, produced works that even in some cases, had lower quality and content than their Turkish rivals, and even caused some Iranian families to protest against some of these works.  Works that were only economical and did not spare any effort to sell more, from unnecessarily stretching the story, music-based video clips and creating triangular and square love nodes to the inclusion of erotic sequences.  Content works that, as a cultural commodity, had a countercultural function and only filled the pockets of its creators.  This is something that even the creators of these works are aware of.  From Manouchehr Hadi, the director of the love and romance series, who himself has confessed to modeling the Turkish series, to the writer of the series Dell, who says that the reason for the increase in the series' episodes is more money.  Now, some time after increasing the activity of VOD and attracting the audience through free subscription services and attractive plans to sell the works of the home theater network at a lower price than physical broadcasters and strengthening their position among the families as a multimedia and video broadcaster, in their latest action, they have dubbed and broadcast exclusive Turkish series.  The home theater network and VOD, which were supposed to rival Turkish satellite and TV channels, have now become their second branch.  Their cultural and content performance shows that the lack of proper supervision of the production of cultural works and the transfer of the field to individuals who are concerned only with financial interests, not cultural ones, provides the way for cultural influence and the destruction of the cultural foundations of the country and Iranian families.  Now that we are living in the era of the soft cultural war, the abandonment and lack of supervision in the field of cultural production can cause irreparable damage to our country; therefore, it is recommended that we not leave the field of culture to the enemy, by increasing the controls on the production of cultural works in the home theater network, and by producing great cultural works, such as Mokhtarnameh, the lost innocence, Hazrat Yusuf, English Kiev, Imam Ali, zero degree Hats off and... Title: Middle East drama: Saudi Arabia, Turkey fight for TV audience
Content: By Paul Law Last updated: 2021-06-03 13: 00 Turkey has been a soft power powerhouse in the Middle East for more than a decade, and its TV series have swept the entire Arab region.  Last year, local dramas became the annual hit in the Arab region, including “The Ambassador ’ s Daughter ” in Saudi Arabia,“ You Knock on My Door, ” which was popular with Arab audiences, and “Miracle Doctor, ” which was adapted from a Korean drama. It is also a good word.  In the face of the threat of domestic drama, Saudi Arabia, another big brother in the Arab world, naturally does not dare to ignore it. In recent years, it has actively developed the film and television industry, and even cooperated with the United Arab Emirates in order to “fight ” with Turkey in the field of television.  Is it face, interest, or a struggle for cultural soft power?  With its huge budget, excellent scenes and excellent acting skills, Turkey has produced a high level of drama in recent years.  The Capital: Abdul Hamid is pictured. (Getty) The history of Turkish television goes back almost half a century.  Forbidden Love, the first original drama, was produced in 1974, but its popularity began in 2006, when Turkey established its first satellite television station, and the series began to gain global exposure.  Two years later, Waleed bin Ibrahim Al Ibrahim, owner of the Middle East Broadcasting Center (MBC) in Saudi Arabia, bought the show and made it popular in the Arab region.  Among them, “Noor ”, a Turkish love story that aired between 2005 and 2007, reached an unprecedented audience of 92 million people; in early 2010,“ One Thousand and One Nights ” was exported to about 80 countries around the world; and in 2013, “Magnificent Century ”, an epic drama about Sulaiman, the Ottoman monarch, attracted more than 500 million viewers worldwide.  Each episode is usually about 60 minutes long on weekdays, and each episode is about 160 minutes long on weekdays.  These high cost productions featuring handsome male and female actors, with gorgeous scenes and catchy songs, plus romantic and Middle Eastern TV plots such as Noor, 1001 Nights, Ertugrul, which depict love, arranged marriage, extended family, patriarchy, and righteous struggle. The series has fascinated television viewers in the Arab world.  (Getty) Turkish dramas easily surpass foreign dramas in Mexico, the United States and South Korea in the Middle East, capturing the hearts of 200 million television viewers in the region, not only because there are no other strong competitors in the region, but also because Turkish producers re-dubbed the series with Arabic names and characters. In addition, the plot of the same Islamic culture makes the local drama more suitable to the tastes of Middle Eastern people than other overseas works.  However, in recent years, the development of Turkish and Saudi Arabia has been involved in the development of Turkish drama. In March 2018, the Saudi government and MBC stopped buying Turkish drama, when Sheikh Abdulaziz al-Sheikh, the Grand Chief of Saudi Arabia, described “Noor ” as“ anti-Islamic ” and “subversive ”, and said that the TV channel that broadcast the drama was“ God ”. and the enemies of its prophets ", and many of the region's major buyers went on strike to buy local dramas.  Egypt, another major market for Turkish dramas, has also banned Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan for “revenge ” after he backed then-President Mohamed Morsi during Egypt ’ s 2013 military coup, culminating in Abdel Fattah el-Sisi ’ s coming to power.  The development of Turkish dramas in the Middle East has been affected in recent years. (Getty) At present, support for the Muslim Brotherhood and other Islamic movements remains a major controversy in both countries, and is why Turkish dramas have not been shown in the region.  As a result, local dramas in the Middle East dropped from US $80 million (about HK $621 million) per year to US $15 million (about HK $116 million) last year.  Due to the severe restrictions on development in the Arab region, local dramas have begun to look around the world in recent years. In 2018, they were released for the first time in Spain, which immediately set off a wave of drama in the region, and later expanded to several European countries, including Italy.  Jose Antonio Anton, Vice President of the Atresmedia Group, a Spanish media group that introduced local dramas, believes that Turkey is a country that combines modern and traditional aspects, and these elements are fully reflected in the local dramas, so that the world can know the country.  “Turkish dramas are generally of high quality, and the plot is also very avant-garde, containing all kinds of drama elements, such as drama, horror, crime, history, etc. ” In addition, Turkish TV has a huge budget, excellent scenes, excellent acting and outdoor video studios, which have been able to produce high quality TV series in the past two decades.  (Getty) In recent years, local dramas have also turned to the Internet, testing the water on video streaming platforms such as YouTube, Starzplay, Netflix, etc., in order to export to the world.  At the same time, the change of local dramas is not only the target of export, but also the variety of drama tends to be diversified.  The current COVID-19 pandemic has also unexpectedly provided more support for local dramas. With many countries suspending filming due to the epidemic, and stopping purchasing expensive Korean dramas in Europe and the United States, affordable local dramas will continue to attract the attention of the world.  To date, Turkey has surpassed Mexico and Brazil as the world ’ s second largest exporter of television series, after the United States, with exports in Europe, the Arab region, Central Asia and the Americas. To date, the country has contributed more than 150 TV series to an estimated 500 million viewers in 146 countries around the world.  It is estimated that the total value of domestic drama exports reached US $500 million (about HK $3.9 billion) last year, and it is expected that by 2023, TV drama exports will generate as much as US $1 billion (about HK $7.8 billion) for Turkey.  Turkish dramas successfully export soft power, bringing many tourists to Turkey, and domestic products are also popular. (Reuters) The Turkish television industry plays a major role in increasing the popularity of the country in Asia, Europe, Latin America and North Africa.  In recent years, there has been an increase in interest in local dramas around the world. This has also played a positive role in promoting Turkey ’ s national image and its manufactured goods, and the number of foreign tourists visiting Istanbul has increased, especially from countries that broadcast local dramas.  All of this suggests that Turkey ’ s soft power is being infiltrated through television dramas.  Saudi Arabia ’ s Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman announced in 2018 that he would invest US $64 billion (HK $496.8 billion) over the next decade to develop the country ’ s entertainment industry.  The National Economic Reform Roadmap “Vision 2030 ” has“ loosened ” some socially conservative policies, such as the lifting of the 35-year commercial theater operating order in 2018.  Saudi Arabia expects to expand into other cultural areas in the future, encouraging arts, musical performances and other types of entertainment.  Saudi Arabia has loosened a 35-year ban on commercial cinemas. (Getty) In addition, the country will expand its film and television industry by building infrastructure, producing localized entertainment content and creating more than 30,000 jobs.  The authorities estimate that the country will have about 350 cinemas and 2,500 movie screens by 2030, with an industry value of about US $1 billion (about HK $7.8 billion).  The country also plans to double household entertainment spending, from 3% of GDP in 2018-2019 to 6% by 2030.  On the other hand, Saudi Arabia is also cooperating with the UAE to develop the film and television industry.  Among them, the US $40 million (HK $310 million) series Kingdoms of Fire, jointly funded by the two governments, was broadcast in 2019, highlighting the Ottoman Empire as the tyrant who has ravaged the Arab world for centuries.  In addition to co-productions, long-term cooperation programs between the two media companies also include training of production and acting personnel.  Kingdoms of Fire, a collaboration between Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates, was launched in 2019. (Getty) Saudi film and television professionals are mostly young people under the age of 30, 34% of whom are women.  Many people see that the film and television development in countries and regions is becoming more and more vigorous, and they no longer oppose their children to enroll in relevant courses, believing that they can find the ideal job after graduation.  According to Mohamed Ghazala, dean of the Faculty of Film and Television Arts at Effat University, Saudi Arabia, “The demand for local talent and capabilities will continue to increase due to increased production and the opening of more cinema-related departments and institutes in Saudi universities. ” However, the Saudi film and television industry is also facing many difficulties, with 43% of the industry believing that it is mainly lack of funding, 13 A further 11% said there was a lack of training and education related to film and television

Title: Turkish operation in Syria; sense of nationalism rises in Turks
Content: Getty Images Image caption The military salute of the Turkish national team was greeted by fans, as Turkish national football players cheered for their goals in their match against Albania, which was repeated in front of the French national team.  They were warned not to make political moves in the stadium, but they have already done so twice.  Following this move, the fans of the team, who were present at the Stade de France in Paris, began waving their country ’ s flags with great excitement.  These actions were a tribute to Turkey ’ s military operation in northern Syria and a “symbol of indifference ” to the international condemnation of Turkey ’ s operation in Syria.  In Turkey, when it comes to international competitions, football has succeeded in evoking a sense of nationalism, and when it is mixed with anti-West, it has become even more intense.  This spirit of “victory ” quickly pervaded all social networks.  One Twitter user wrote: “France, know us.  You condemn us, but we salute you on your soil.  Long live Turkey, we are making history.  In addition, many people have used the hashtag # ConquestofEurope.  Another social media user wrote: “A small reminder to Western and UEFA media that the salute is a political or racist message: it is not a political message but a way of expressing respect for the soldiers of a country made with the blood of its soldiers. ”  AFP Image caption Many Turks see Turkey's operation in northern Syria as a broader form of its fight against Kurdish militants on their soil, and why the Turks are defending their army in the Turkish border town of Agça Qala.  A resident of the city, waving the country's flag, told the BBC: "We are ready to go to the front line and fight.  We are waiting for Erdogan ’ s order. ”  Turkey has been at war with the PKK on its territory for more than three decades.  That ’ s why supporters of Turkey ’ s military intervention in northern Syria see the move as a broader struggle.  The popular support for the Turkish military shows a sense of nationalism in the country, which is louder than the wave of criticism, mostly because those who dare to oppose the national discourse of military operations face criminal charges.  Nearly 80 social media users who criticized the operation were prosecuted for "inciting hatred and engaging in propaganda to intimidate" and a large number of Twitter accounts belonging to Kurdish activists and journalists in Turkey have been closed.  The main tool of Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan to use his power to shape public opinion has been the media, which has always been criticized for misusing them as propaganda machines.  The bulk of Turkey ’ s mainstream media belong to Erdogan ’ s corporate conglomerates.  So it ’ s no surprise that the voices of the opposition are not being heard.  Media that mainly reflect the thinking of the government.  Turkey ’ s prominent TV anchors who have gone to the border, dressed in military uniforms, portray Turkey ’ s military intervention in northern Syria in an epic and passionate way.  Playback of this file on your device is not supported.  Why is Turkey now fighting the Kurds in northern Syria?  The nationalist narrative is also very popular in the Turkish press.  They don ’ t give much space to criticism, and if they do, they will attack it.  David Lamy, Labour MP in the UK, was no exception.  LeMay posted a video of a child who died, writing: “The human face of Trump ’ s decision to give free tickets to Turkey to attack Kurdish allies in northeastern Syria.  CNN Turk, the pro-government network on Twitter, along with an image of Mr. Lami, in which his skin was darkened by manipulation, accused him of "black propaganda" about Turkey's military intervention.  It was a reaction that was accepted by many racially minded people.  @ DavidLammy Why have @ cnnturk darkened my image in this picture to accuse me of spreading propaganda?  I am raising important issues about Trump's decision to abandon the Kurds to Erdogan's forces in north eastern Syria.  pic.twitter.com / k2907GqCck — David Lammy (@ DavidLammy) October 12, 2019 What do Turkish Kurds think is the official policy of Turkey in this operation to clear its borders from the SDF, which consists mainly of Syrian Kurdish militias as well as Arab and Christian fighters?  Kurds make up nearly 20 percent of Turkey ’ s population, but their voices are barely heard.  Most residents of the Kurdish city of Diyarbakir have decided to remain silent because of fear of legal action against them.  Among them is the owner of a spice shop in the city ’ s busiest market, who told the BBC: “We are all hurt but we suppress our emotions.  When you ’ re surrounded by cops in civilian clothes, no one will talk to you.  “The political parties in Turkey largely follow the line of the ruling Justice and Development Party: the secular Republican People ’ s Party, the Good Nationalist Party, and the Nationalist National Action Party all support this military operation.  With regard to opposition parties, there is only one exception: the Peoples ’ Democratic Party (HDP), which is pro-Kurdish.  Its leaders are in prison and its members face ongoing prosecution, threats and online violence.  A large number of HDP members who protested in the southeastern region of Turkey against the country ’ s military intervention were either arrested or forced to leave by police.  Police have raided several municipal buildings in the predominantly Kurdish cities of Hakkari, Mardin and Van, arresting a number of Kurdish executives.  When voices opposing military intervention are silenced or suppressed, a sense of nationalism is all that remains, a sense that pro-government media plays a central role in creating.

Title: Armenia is among the countries that pose a threat to Turkey, and the United States is in the first place: a survey
Content: Recently, the results of a poll entitled “Studies of the perception of Turkish foreign policy in public opinion ” were published, conducted under the leadership of the university professor Kadir Has Cinema Akgül Achikmeshe.  The survey best reveals the attitude of the citizens of Turkey, which has been experiencing turbulent foreign policy and domestic political events in the past few years, to the problems of foreign policy of this country.  Changes in public sentiment can be seen by comparing the data that are given for 2013, 2015, 2016.  The survey was conducted in the form of personal interviews among thousands of people over 18 years of age in 26 ili (administrative unit of Turkey), representing the demographic structure of the country.  In particular, they were asked questions about various aspects of Turkish foreign policy.  Noteworthy is the fact that the majority of respondents in the neighboring country consider television to be the source of information about Ankara ’ s foreign policy (86.5%), 37.5% consider the Internet to be the source of information, and 30.7% consider the print press to be the source of information.  Judging by these indicators, it can be concluded that public opinion about Turkey ’ s foreign policy is formed through the interpretation of the media of this country.  The majority of Turkish citizens consider their country to be Islamic (39.9%).  It is interesting that during the presidency of Erdogan, in parallel with the increase in the component of Islam in the political life of the country, as well as in the conditions of tension in relations with the European Union, 32.7% of respondents consider Turkey a European country, while this indicator has grown over time (2013 - 24.3%, 2015 - 26.4%, 2016 - 31.8%).  The efforts of President Erdogan and the ruling party of Turkey, the attempted military coup in 2016, the constitutional amendments in 2017 formed an opinion in Turkish society about who exactly implements Turkey ’ s foreign policy.  So in 2016, 76.4% of respondents said that Turkey ’ s foreign policy is implemented by the President of Turkey, in 2017 this percentage was 69.2%.  24.3% of respondents believe that the foreign policy of Turkey is carried out by the Armed Forces of this country, 13.4% of respondents said that the National Intelligence Organization.  Even after last year ’ s July coup attempt, when the country began to persecute law enforcement officers, as well as after constitutional amendments in April this year, the Turkish authorities made the work of these structures more controlled.  A significant segment of Turkish society in 2017 expressed the opinion that the foreign policy of their country is carried out by law enforcement agencies, while 3.8% of respondents thought so in 2016, and in 2013 there was no such answer at all.  People living in Turkey are of the opinion that the foreign policy priority of their country is to strengthen relations with other countries - 61.2% of respondents, and 14.5% of respondents said that the mission of Turkish diplomatic missions in other countries is to collect information about these countries.  Turkish citizens were also asked which country is Turkey ’ s closest friend.  The overwhelming majority of respondents (71.3%) named Azerbaijan, last year 59.3% spoke in favor of this point of view.  Among friends, Pakistan ranks second, but only 2.2% of respondents think so.  About 1% of respondents consider several other countries as friends of Turkey, and 17.2% of respondents believe that Turkey has no friends at all.  At the same time, the number of those who believe that “Turkey has no friends ” decreased to 17.2% (against 23.1% last year).  In 2016, the Middle East came to the fore in the list of countries considered a threat to Turkey.  However, this year the first place went to the United States, and compared with last year, the United States is considered the largest threat by 22.4% of respondents more.  It is interesting that 19.1% of respondents consider the Armenian issue to be the main problem in US-Turkey relations.  The second biggest threat to Turkey was identified by 37.4% of respondents as Israel.  The EU countries, which last year were a threat according to 10.4% of respondents, this year ranked third in the ranking of countries posing a threat to Turkey, at a rate of 24%.  The level of perception of Russia as a threat fell from 34.9%.  After the normalization of Russian-Turkish relations this year, this figure fell to 18.5%.  It is noteworthy that Armenia ranks fifth in this list: 18% of respondents consider our country a threat.  Another point that draws attention to itself: from year to year, the inhabitants of Turkey provide less and less support for the process of accession of the country to the EU.  At the moment, support for Turkey ’ s membership in the EU is at 48.4%.  In 2015, the number of those who said: “Turkey will never be able to become a full member of the EU ” was 47.6%.  Last year, this figure rose to 66.7%, and this year to 81.3%.  At the same time, the number of those who support the creation of a different model in relations between Turkey and the EU – instead of full membership, remained at the level of 30.4%.  There is an increase in the number of supporters of the view that Turkey should build strategic cooperation with Russia as an alternative to EU membership (27.6% vs 14.8%).  17.6% consider the Organization of Islamic Cooperation as an alternative, 13.1% – the Shanghai Cooperation Organization.  The initiators of the survey also touched upon the topic of the unrecognized Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus.  78.4% of respondents believe that North Cyprus is a friendly country that cannot be turned away under any circumstances.  Turkish citizens were also asked about their attitude to the foreign policy pursued by their country.  38.5% of respondents expressed confidence that Turkey pursues a successful foreign policy, 37.8% believe that this policy is partially successful, 23.7% believe that Turkey ’ s foreign policy is unsuccessful.

Title: Home show, competitor or second branch of Turkish networks?
Content: According to the Cinema Zone, the cultural group of the Young Journalists Club, with the increasing influence of satellite networks among Iranian families, one of the most significant damage that was mentioned for these networks was the cultural impact of the works broadcast by these networks, especially the Turkish series dubbed.  The series, based on the family as the central subject, provided sexist, pornographic, aristocratic and corrupt narratives of Turkish families, which due to the visual and sexual attractions, these series were able to tell stories of love triangles, betrayal, class divisions, anti-family, mere pleasure and corruption in the context of melodrama to many audiences with their own.  The increase in the activity of satellite networks and the distribution of Turkish works in Iranian satellite networks coincided with the increase of activities in Iran ’ s home theater network; at that time, some cultural analysts considered the home theater network as a reasonable response to satellite networks and an opportunity to overcome their works, a network that had less audits on its works and could attract the audience of Turkish TV series.  But that ’ s where the mistake started. From Manouchehr Hadi, the director of the love and romance series, who himself has confessed to modeling the Turkish series, to the writer of the series Dell, who says that the reason for the increase in the series' episodes is more money.  Now, some time after increasing the activity of VOD and attracting the audience through free subscription services and attractive plans to sell the works of the home theater network at a lower price than physical broadcasters and strengthening their position among the families as a multimedia and video broadcaster, in their latest action, they have dubbed and broadcast exclusive Turkish series.  The home theater network and VOD, which were supposed to rival Turkish satellite and TV channels, have now become their second branch.  Their cultural and content performance shows that the lack of proper supervision of the production of cultural works and the transfer of the field to individuals who are concerned only with financial interests, not cultural ones, provides the way for cultural influence and the destruction of the cultural foundations of the country and Iranian families. Title: Turkey's hot markets in South America
Content: Turkish television series now reached South America after capturing the film market of the Indian subcontinent, the Middle East, the Caucasus, Central Asia and the Balkans.  In South America, Chile, Argentina and Mexico are among the biggest customers of Turkish TV series.  The popularity of Turkish series in the Middle East or the Caucasus may be due to cultural and historical commonalities, but what could be the reason for the booming Turkish series market on the other side of the Atlantic in South America?  Tuggs Shaw, a German broadcaster, has been trying to answer this question in a report on the popularity of Turkish shows in South America.  Yamaj Okur, producer of the Çukur story series, which has been translated into Persian as “Gut ”, says that a 140-minute episode will be produced every week, which will be broadcast on Turkish television five days later.  The Trench series is currently one of Turkey ’ s most successful series.  It tells the story of a family who controls one of Istanbul ’ s most dangerous neighborhoods, the Pit.  The neighborhood has long been in the hands of small families, whose most important rule is to be strict about the distribution of drugs in the neighborhood.  If someone spreads drugs, they have to leave the neighborhood.  The first episode of the series premiered on October 23, 2017 on TV and is still ongoing.  Correspondents from Istanbul and Rio de Janeiro say the demand for Turkish TV shows has increased.  Diazis, or series, forms a separate genre on Turkish television that is more comparable to the well-known South American telenovelas.  Araya Kisternas, a Chilean couple who have been married for almost 50 years, has just discovered their love for Turkish TV shows.  They say they show love with respect in this series.  The looks are romantic and traditional families are portrayed as important and valuable.  The Chilean couple have a herd that "in modern South American nostalgia traps shows a lot of bare limbs, men kiss men, and violence is part of the film."  Juan Vicente, director of the Chilean TV channel Mega, brought the first Turkish series to South America seven years ago.  He recalls that when the show “Binbir gece ” was broadcast on the mega network, he enthralled people and saved the mega network from bankruptcy at the time.  Juwan goes on to say that since many South Americans are conservative and dream of an ideal world, Turkish TV shows are in their best interest.  Family structures in Turkey are comparable to those in South America.  The patriarchal structures with a strong grandfather or father who determines and leads everything in the family are similar to the Chilean family structure.  The traditional family structure is also popular in Turkey, thanks to Erdoğan ’ s conservative and Islamist government.  Thousands took to the streets in recent days to protest Turkey ’ s withdrawal from the Convention against Violence against Women, but the protests have not been successful so far.  Yamaj Okor, producer of The Pit, says sex, swearing, alcohol in movies and TV shows are as taboo as they were in the '90s.  Okor added, “We have to tell our stories more gently, otherwise the TV won ’ t play it. ”  The series as Turkey ’ s “soft power ” is different from most Turkish series that depict the glamorous life of the middle and upper classes.  In this series, usually luxury cars, expensive clothes are displayed.  But the hole has a different atmosphere.  The series is filmed in the Balat district of Istanbul.  In the Balat district of Istanbul, which used to be home to Jewish, Armenian and Greek communities, it is now a simple working-class area, but thanks to the series, the neighborhood has now flourished and many cafes have opened in its corners over the past few years.  Tagus Shaw reports that at any given time during filming, about 200 fans of the Pit series gather at the scene.  On the other hand, vendors are trying to sell their goods, and in the future, visitors to South America are likely to be seen in the narrow alleys of Balat.  The series was recently sold to Chile.  The Chilean couple who are fascinated by the film are also planning a trip to Turkey.  Hector said: “A trip to Turkey would be a dream for us. ”  His wife, Patricia, interrupts him: “In the past, we never had any idea of Turkey.  We knew a Turkey full of violence with terrorist attacks.  But now it seems to be getting better. ”  Turkey ’ s $1 billion in revenue has become the world ’ s second-largest TV series exporter after Hollywood.  Recent research by Turkish state television shows that Turkish dramas are a “soft power, ” often trying to convey a specific image in the form of a romantic historical drama from the Ottoman period, which is usually reflected in the politics of the current Turkish government.  Follow Deutsche Welle on Instagram: “We are exporting Turkish culture, language and products.  Many of them just became popular abroad through our series.  Take, for example, Turkish music, which is now popular in South America. ”  According to estimates by the Turkish film industry, the revenue of the series could reach $1 billion by 2023.  At the end of his report on the Turkish series, Tagus Shaw has written that the next goal of the Turkish series is to capture the film market in Spain and Italy.

background: I work for a tech company that may be involved in future expeditions to Mars. Our task is to determine whether it is possible to create a sustainable atmosphere for Mars expeditions.
title: Oxygen-generating experiment on Mars

passages.title: NASA's Mars rover receives oxygen from Mars' atmosphere for the first time
passages.passage: Mars Rover Perseverance for the first time was able to get oxygen from the atmosphere of Mars.  NASA launched it to the Red Planet in July 2020. — A growing number of discoveries of Perseverance, NASA ’ s newest six-wheeled work on the Martian surface, including the conversion of part of the thin, carbon-rich atmosphere into oxygen, — said in a statement of the space Agency.  The rover conducted the corresponding test on April 20, the 60th day since the landing of the mission to Mars.  The mission was carried out by a toaster-sized instrument aboard Perseverance called the Mars Oxygen In-situ Resource Utilization Experiment (MOXIE).  NASA explained that this discovery will help in the future to provide astronauts with air suitable for breathing.  Despite the fact that the atmosphere of the red planet is 96% carbon dioxide.  Also, the transformation of the local atmosphere with oxygen may allow in the future to produce fuel on Mars.  The agency noted that such achievements bring a person closer to landing on this planet.  The Perseverance rover was launched to Mars in July 2020 on the Atlas V rocket. The purpose of the mission is to search for traces of life in the Jezero crater, collect samples of rocks and sediments, and study the planet ’ s climate.  On February 22, the rocket landed on the surface of Mars.  In early March, the rover held its first test drive after landing.  The appearance of the “rainbow ” in the picture from Mars As part of the NASA Mars 2020 mission, the Mars Rover Perseverance took an unusual picture.  His lens got a rainbow, the appearance of which is impossible on Mars.  However, NASA has already officially denied the rainbow in the photo.  Its experts said that this is only a reflection of the sun, caught in the mechanism of the lens Hazcam Rover Perseverance.

passages.title: The expert assessed the prospects of creating a habitable atmosphere on Mars
passages.passage: Creating a habitable atmosphere on Mars will not work, but it is possible to produce oxygen there for a small team of researchers, scientists or colonists, said Vladimir Surdin, a senior researcher at the Sternberg State Astronomical Institute, commenting on the NASA report on the successful extraction of oxygen from the atmosphere of this planet.  NASA reported that the Mars Rover Perseverance for the first time extracted oxygen from the atmosphere of Mars.  It is expected that this technology in the future will help astronauts produce rocket fuel on this planet, as well as create a breathable atmosphere for them.  “Creating a habitable atmosphere on Mars, of course, will not work.  There are no resources for that.  But creating oxygen, for a small team of researchers, scientists or colonists on Mars, of course, is necessary.  Carrying oxygen from Earth is too expensive, you need to get it on Mars, ” says Surdin.  To get a small amount of oxygen on Mars has all the resources, the expert is sure.  The atmosphere of the planet is made up of carbon dioxide, which is carbon and oxygen associated with CO2.  In addition, Mars has water consisting of hydrogen and oxygen.  That is, in fact, oxygen on the planet is already there, but it is in a related form.  "Of course, it would be possible to break down water molecules - this is a process of hydrolysis, which in chemical terms, maybe, would be easier.  But there is very little water on Mars, and it lies in the polar caps, so it still needs to be reached.  And the atmosphere is everywhere, so humanity went a more difficult way, but so that at any point on the planet it would be possible to provide astronauts with oxygen.  That is, they decided to break down carbon dioxide molecules, ” the source said.  He emphasizes that the device that stands on the rover, rather cunning.  Nevertheless, it has proven its efficiency, which means it can be scaled - to send to Mars already larger vehicles of the same type.  They will be able to provide not only astronauts with oxygen for breathing, but also rockets that will be refueled with fuel - they need liquid oxygen as an oxidizer for the operation of engines.  Naturally, all this is quite expensive pleasure, as well as astronautics in general.  For example, the last rover that arrived on Mars in February is worth $3 billion.  This is a small car that weighs about a ton.  It is clear that any space flight is very expensive, but if there is a desire to explore a new planet, then you have to spend a lot, ” Surdin concluded.  Earlier, American scientists found that most of the water that previously covered the surface of Mars, did not escape into space, as it was believed until now, and is in the minerals that make up the rocks of the planet.

passages.title: Oxygen and hydrogen on Mars proposed to get from brine
passages.passage: Scientists have developed a method for producing oxygen and hydrogen from a liquid saline solution in Martian lakes using electrolysis.  A feature of the experiment was the use of lead-ruthenium oxide as an electrocatalyst for oxygen production.  The production of oxygen using such an installation was 25 times more energy efficient than in the case of MOXIE, launched to the Red Planet as part of the Mars 2020 mission, and the size and weight of the device for life support based on the described technology will be less than that of analogues.  The article was published in the journal PNAS.  Conditions on Mars are far from favorable for humans: the atmosphere is rarefied and 95 percent consists of carbon dioxide, and temperature changes exceed 100 degrees Celsius with an average temperature of minus 63 degrees.  Therefore, colonization of the Red Planet is impossible without the creation of a life support system that would be able to provide people with oxygen for breathing and fuel (for example, hydrogen) for energy supply and, ideally, return flight.  To solve the first problem, NASA created MOXIE (Mars Oxygen ISRU Experiment) - an experimental installation for obtaining oxygen from atmospheric carbon dioxide by electrolysis.  To test the effectiveness of such a method in the field, the installation became part of the Mars Rover Perseverance, which was launched on July 30, 2020 as part of the Mars 2020 mission.  An alternative source of not only oxygen, but also hydrogen on Mars can be water, the first direct evidence of the existence of which on the red planet was obtained in 1971.  Particularly attractive for use in applications, however, would be the reserves of salt water, impurities in which would allow it to remain in a liquid state even at low temperature and pressure.  The first traces of such brine (liquid salt solution) with magnesium perchlorate as the main component were found on Mars in 2015, and in 2018, a reservoir with a diameter of about 20 kilometers was found under the polar ice of the planet, which could have been formed due to volcanic activity.  Later, planetary scientists confirmed that such lakes on Mars really exist and can be numerous.  Now Pralay Gayen (Pralay Gayen) from the University of Washington in St. Louis together with colleagues created an installation for obtaining oxygen and hydrogen from a saline solution close in composition and temperature to that in Martian lakes.  As a brine in the experiment, a solution of magnesium perchlorate in water with a concentration of 2.8 mol per liter was used, cooled to minus 36 degrees Celsius and blown by carbon dioxide (the latter played the role of the Martian atmosphere).  As an electrocatalyst for the production of oxygen, the scientists used lead-ruthenium oxide Pb2Ru2O7-δ, the effectiveness of which they previously showed for alkaline solutions.  The electrocatalyst for hydrogen production was platinum on activated carbon - the standard catalyst in this case, and a commercially produced anion-exchange membrane was used as a separator.  Installation diagram.  In the red region, oxygen is produced, in the blue - hydrogen.  Image source: Pralay Gayen et al. / PNAS In the course of the study, scientists showed that lead-ruthenium oxide as an electrocatalyst is indeed several times more effective than the ruthenium oxide commonly used in such installations.  After the behavior of the created installation was studied in a wide range of temperatures from − 36 to 21 degrees Celsius and saw no radical fluctuations in the efficiency and rate of production.  The current output of the experimental installation was 70 percent, and the energy efficiency was in the range between 36 and 70 percent (depending on the voltage applied to the plates).  In addition, the installation was resistant to degradation of the catalyst: scientists were not able to find traces of ruthenium in the solution after 300-minute operation of the device.  The rate of production of oxygen (blue dots) and hydrogen (red dots), depending on the density of the cathode current.  Image source: Pralay Gayen et al. / PNAS Also, the researchers compared the achieved rate of oxygen production with MOXIE values of 10-22 grams per hour: it turned out that with the same energy supply, the created installation produces 25 times more oxygen than the experiment on the Mars Rover “Perseverance ”.  To have the same rate of oxygen production as MOXIE, the device would have to have electrodes with an area of ​ ​ 28-62 square centimeters, and to ensure the vital activity of a sleeping and actively moving person, this parameter would have to be 375 and 1235 square centimeters, respectively.  At the same time, the mass and volume of the installation will be less than if you use the technology inherent in MOXIE.  Moreover, the developed method of obtaining oxygen does not require its subsequent purification, while during electrolysis in MOXIE, carbon monoxide is also produced, which must be filtered.  Dependence on the power consumption of the rate of oxygen production of the installation (blue line), as well as its capes and volume to ensure various modes of human life (black lines).  The blue dot is the power and rate of oxygen production at MOXIE.  Image source: Pralay Gayen et al. / PNAS Previously, we talked about another method of obtaining oxygen from carbon dioxide in the Martian atmosphere (like MOXIE): scientists proposed to do this using low-temperature plasma.  And what is the role of the Mars Rover “Perseverance ” in addition to checking the method of oxygen production, you can read in our material“ Mars, there and back ”.  Nikita Kozyrev

passages.title: New technology will be able to produce hydrogen and oxygen from salty Martian water
passages.passage: In space launches, weight matters a lot, so the less we have to take with us, the better.  Now engineers at St. Louis University have developed a new electrolysis device that can convert very salty Martian water into breathable oxygen and hydrogen for fuel.  As you may remember from school, water electrolysis is the process of using electricity to break down water into its constituent hydrogen and oxygen atoms.  These gases can then be collected for use, so in theory electrolysis could be a way for astronauts to produce their own oxygen and hydrogen on the Red Planet.  The problem is that it doesn ’ t work well with brackish water, and that ’ s all you can find on Mars.  First, it is necessary to reduce the high salt content, which is a complex process in this inhospitable alien environment.  Therefore, for the new study, scientists have developed a new electrolysis system that can work with salt water in the extreme cold of the Martian atmosphere.  The key change is in two electrodes: the team created an anode from lead ruthenate pyrochlor and a cathode from platinum on the coal.  To test the new electrolyzer design, scientists modeled the Martian atmosphere, which required cooling to -36 ° C — and it worked.  The researchers say that at the same input power, the new electrolyzer produces 25 times more oxygen than MOXIE, the instrument aboard the Mars Rover Perseverance, which squeezes oxygen from carbon dioxide in the air.  While this technology has intriguing potential uses for astronauts, it ’ s worth remembering that water on Mars is a fairly rare commodity, so it ’ s probably better to use for drinking, although it also requires removing salt first.  Instead, the technology could first find application here on Earth.  "By demonstrating these electrolyzers in challenging Martian conditions, we also intend to deploy them in much milder conditions on Earth to use salt water to produce hydrogen and oxygen, for example by electrolysis of seawater," Pralai Gayen, a co-author of the study, said in a statement.  The study was published in the journal Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.

passages.title: Mars Rover Perseverance successfully tested the device to extract oxygen from the Martian atmosphere
passages.passage: An experimental device called MOXIE (Mars Oxygen In-Situ Resource Utilization Experiment) was first tested on April 20, and this test was recognized as successful: for an hour of operation, the installation the size of a conventional toaster was able to produce more than 5 grams of oxygen, writes Newsru.  The atmosphere of Mars is almost 96% carbon dioxide (CO2).  The MOXIE unit is capable of converting this carbon dioxide into oxygen and carbon monoxide (CO, carbon monoxide), which is a by-product of the processing and is released back into the atmosphere.  The process of processing carbon dioxide occurs by electrolysis of solid oxides at a temperature of 800 degrees Celsius.  During operation, the device captures carbon dioxide, passes through a filter to remove dust and compresses it, providing pressure at ground level.  The gas then passes through a heated electrolysis cell, which consists of several layers of nickel alloy and ceramics.  Ceramic elements of the cell are able to conduct current at high temperature - they pass oxygen ions and trap carbon monoxide.  The outer surface of MOXIE is covered with a thin layer of gold.  This coating protects the MOXIE surface from heating, protecting the rover electronics located next to the instrument.  Future astronauts: breathe easier.  The MOXIE technology demonstration aboard @ NASAPersevere successfully extracted oxygen from the thin Martian atmosphere — a critical component for life support on the Red Planet and rocket fuel for the trip home. https: / / t.co / HOsguer. hYgkP pic.twitter.com / SwL0etf9Uu — NASA JPL (@ NASAJPL) April 21, 2021 The maximum estimated performance of MOXIE is up to 10 grams of oxygen per hour.  The test program includes at least nine more tests over two years.  These tests will be carried out under different conditions to assess the performance of the plant.  In the future, more large-scale oxygen production on Mars may come in handy for practical purposes.  First, oxygen is used as an oxidizing agent for rocket fuel.  For example, to launch a rocket with four astronauts from Mars to Earth requires about 7 tons of fuel and 25 tons of oxygen.  The ability to produce this amount of oxygen during the astronauts ’ stay on Mars will prevent this oxygen from being delivered from Earth – delivering a large and productive oxygen generator modeled on MOXIE would be a more practical solution.  Secondly, oxygen, which makes up 21% of the Earth's atmosphere, is needed for breathing - four astronauts will be enough one ton of oxygen for a year on Mars.  We will remind, the Rover Perseverance landed in the area of 45-kilometer crater Jezero, named after the village in Bosnia and Herzegovina.  This crater is located on the western edge of the Isis Plain (a giant impact crater north of the equator of Mars).  As scientists suggest, in ancient times in the area of ​ ​ the crater Ezero was a river delta, where organic matter and other potential traces of microorganisms that could have lived on Mars about 3 billion years ago could have been collected.  The crater itself was then filled with water and was a lake.

passages.title: How does NASA build a base with breathable air on Mars?
passages.passage: The purpose of writing this article is to understand how we can now prepare for human life on an alien planet, and to do so, Digital Trends spoke to two experts.  Michael Hackett, a professor at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, and Assad Abu Bakr, a NASA engineer, talk about how to keep astronauts alive on a planet that wants to take their lives.  The window of opportunity to send humans to the Red Planet has to pass some kind of necessary timeframe.  Because of the structure of the orbits of Earth and Mars, the easiest way to get from one planet to another is to use the Hohmann Transport Orbit, in which the spacecraft moves in an elliptical orbit and slowly and steadily pushes out.  Hackett explains, “It ’ s because of the way the planets move.  Earth is in orbit around Mars and is moving faster than Mars, so every once in a while they collide.  A year on Mars equals about two years on Earth. ”  So you have to go with the exact timing to launch astronauts to Mars.  Every Martian year, or every 26 months on Earth, is given a window of opportunity at which Mars is closest to Earth.  "So you have an optimal opportunity every 26 months to send a spacecraft to Mars through this orbit.  “So the plans for Mars are to send the infrastructure first, and then after 26 months, we ’ ll send the crew. ”  Sending infrastructure doesn ’ t just mean ensuring astronauts have access to air to breathe and food to eat.  It also means sending and building power plants, a habitat, rovers, and vehicles that will allow astronauts to leave Mars once the mission is complete.  Why is oxygen so important?  The first major problem to deal with when building a Martian base is the production of oxygen.  When you hear about producing oxygen on Mars, you ’ re probably thinking about the simplest human need: having air to breathe, and certainly not finding a way to produce a breathable atmosphere inside a confined habitat on Mars.  But the habitat will require, at least compared to other components of the project, very small amounts of oxygen.  By other components, we mean things like rocket propellants that lift astronauts off the surface of the planet.  Hackett explains, “We are trying to manufacture the drive prerequisites.  "We're not trying to make fuel, we're trying to get some of the necessary chemical reactions that we never think about on Earth."  On the ground, when you burn gasoline in your car ’ s engine, you use oxygen that weighs several times more than your fuel to cause that reaction.  The same is true of pieces of wood burning in the fireplace.  “But if you go somewhere where there is no free oxygen, you have to take oxygen with you. ”  Modern missiles have several liquid oxygen tanks that provide the final fuel and add a lot of weight to the entire payload.  “We ’ ll need about 30 tons of oxygen to get those astronauts off the surface and into orbit, and if we have to take those 30 tons of oxygen with us to Mars, the whole mission will be delayed for about a decade.  A much easier solution would be to send an empty tank there and fill it with oxygen. ”  Using what is available to produce oxygen on Mars, Hackett and his colleagues are working on a concept called In-situ Resource Utilization (ISRU).  Basically, it means using whatever is already found on Mars to build what we need.  They will have to experiment with a device called MOXIE, which, along with NASA's Endurance rover, successfully landed on Mars in February 2021.  MOXIE is essentially a miniature version of a much larger device that picks up carbon dioxide, which is found abundantly in the Martian atmosphere, and produces oxygen.  This device may seem complicated at first glance, but it ’ s actually similar to a very well-known technology on the planet.  According to Hackett, “MOXIE is very much like a fuel cell.  There is basically no difference between the two.  If you take a fuel cell and you reverse the two wires that have been wired into it, you have an electrification system.  This means that if the device is a fuel cell, you have a fuel and an oxidizer that deliver a stable molecule.  If you have carbon monoxide as fuel and oxygen, carbon dioxide is produced.  You also get electricity. ”  “Now, if you reverse that, you have to let in carbon dioxide and electricity, and what you get is carbon monoxide and oxygen.  That ’ s how we ’ ll solve the problem. ”  This seemingly simple idea is radical in that it addresses a problem that no one outside the aerospace community sees as a challenge: producing oxygen.  Hackett said, “Nobody wants to produce oxygen on Earth.  No one has a reason to do that.  Oxygen is everywhere. ”  How to build an oxygen machine?  Understanding the chemical rules of making an oxygen machine is one thing, and designing and implementing a version of it that fits inside a rover is another.  Abu Bakr, the MOXIE thermal engineer at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory and who has been involved in the development of the MOXIE project from the beginning, explains how the experimental device was built and what obstacles the NASA lab team had to overcome.  He said: “The biggest challenge we ’ ve ever had is a little bit of energy.  The rover has a radioisotope thermoelectric generator, which is a nuclear source of electricity, so people think the rover relies on nuclear power, but that's not the case.  The rover is powered by batteries and has an atomic charger next to it. ”  This means that researchers need to be very careful about how much energy is being used to keep the battery from draining.  The entire Mars Endurance operates at only 110 watts, which is just a little more energy than it takes to light a light-bulb bulb.  As a result, a device like MOXIE has to operate with very small amounts of energy.  Simple knowledge but equipment design is only one aspect of trial and error – the other is to see if the idea works at all on Mars.  Even with concepts that work well on Earth, an alien environment can have unforeseen consequences, from the impact of the planet ’ s thin atmosphere on how heat is transferred to the depreciation of equipment in unexpected ways due to weaker gravity and unknown dust.  That ’ s why NASA engineers will soon be collecting MOXIE data to test its performance in Mars ’ true environment.  “In many ways, ” says Abu Bakr,“ MOXIE doesn ’ t really collect scientific data. ”  Compared to scientific equipment such as telescopes and spectrometers used to analyze rock samples, the data collected by MOXIE is relatively simple.  “What we get is almost like telemetry data in engineering.  We measure voltages and currents and temperatures, things like that.  This is our data, and the data is very small.  You can almost fit all of them in a floppy disk. ”  This means the team can get very quick feedback on whether the system is working properly – in just a few days.  Unlike other instruments on the endurance rover, which require weeks, months, or even years to analyze the data, MOXIE is a demonstration of practical performance rather than trial and error.  Abu Bakr said, “What we ’ re doing is not science, it ’ s technology.  We want to know whether the system works, and if we want to increase the scale in the future, what we need to do to make our goal work. ”  If MOXIE is successful, it will show how practical the ISRU principle is on Mars.  Then expanding the scale of the project and building a version of the machine on a real scale that produces oxygen at a much higher rate will be relatively easy; and the good news is that a larger version will appear more efficient and produce significant amounts of oxygen without requiring much energy.  With the oxygen challenge solved, we could move on to other resources humans need to survive on Mars.  Another essential resource that we need to establish in order to produce it on the Red Planet is water.  Water isn ’ t just necessary for humans to drink, but it ’ s also important because of the hydrogen and carbon dioxide compounds that can bring a plethora of efficient chemical compounds.  Hackett said: “The idea in the short term is to automate certain amounts of ISRU to make our mission possible.  “Once we build our base on Mars — a base like the McMurdo Station in Antarctica or the International Space Station — we can move on to more sophisticated ISRU methods like ice extraction. ”  “A lot of people feel like we need to extract ice automatically.  But I say no, it ’ s not worth the effort.  Ice is a mineral, which means you have to look for it underground, dig it out of the ground, and purify it.  It would be easier to take ice with us to Mars.  It's like a moxie, but it's a mechanical tree.  It breathes carbon dioxide and exhales oxygen. ”  Hackett argues that MOXIE is much easier to find resources through mining.  “It doesn ’ t have to go anywhere, it doesn ’ t have to look for anything.  These are methods in IRSU that appear to be really practical in the short term.  “You ’ re doing things as simple as possible, and one day you ’ ll have access to enough people

passages.title: Earth ’ s microbes should be sent to Mars.
passages.passage: Space agencies have taken a lot of precautions not to contaminate celestial bodies with terrestrial microbes, but some researchers believe sending Earth microbes to Mars could be beneficial because doing so could transform the Martian environment into a habitat for humans.  Researchers have recently said that Earth ’ s microbes should be sent to Mars for colonization so that the Red Planet becomes a suitable place for humans to live.  A recent study has shown that the spread of Earth ’ s microbes could trigger a change in the structure of the Red Planet and create an environment where humans can live.  Scientists have developed a process that involves screening promising microbes and leaving the most important on Mars.  The researchers' new paper shows that the release of human microbes is the beginning of the process of restructuring the Red Planet and creating an environment in which humans can inhabit.  Jose Lopez, a microbiologist and professor at Nova Southeastern University in Florida, USA, conducted the study with his colleagues.  They asked NASA and other space agencies to send microbes to Mars so they could change the planet ’ s unpredictable environment and create a habitable environment on Mars.  The main argument of the researchers is that preventing pollution is nearly impossible, but it can be done by doing some things, such as sending human microbes there.  According to the researchers, microorganisms are what made our planet habitable.  As we know, without beneficial microorganisms, life cannot exist.  More than four billion years ago, Earth was not a habitable place, but microbial life arose and evolved over time.  The findings were published in the FEMS Journal of Microbiology Ecology.

passages.title: Scientists have found organisms that can give rise to life on Mars
passages.passage: Scientists have found organisms that can give rise to life on Mars 16.02.2021, 14: 58 They are able to grow and multiply in the conditions of the red planet.  New experiments have shown that cyanobacteria, also known as blue-green algae, can successfully grow in Martian atmospheric conditions.  Of course, a few more ingredients will be needed, but when humans get to Mars, they will be able to create life support systems based on cyanobacteria for the human habitat, writes nv.ua.  "Here we show that cyanobacteria can use the gases available in the Martian atmosphere, at low overall pressure, as a source of carbon and nitrogen," said astrobiologist Cyprien Verso from the University of Bremen in Germany.  "Under these conditions, cyanobacteria retained their ability to grow in water containing only Martian dust, and they could be used to feed other microbes.  This can help make long-term missions to Mars sustainable, ” the authors of the study believe.  All types of cyanobacteria produce oxygen as a byproduct of photosynthesis, and even today they are an invaluable source of it.  For several years, scientists have speculated whether we could use the ability of cyanobacteria to produce oxygen to live on Mars.  This will bring additional benefits.  The atmosphere of Mars consists mainly of carbon dioxide (95 percent) and nitrogen (3 percent), which are fixed by cyanobacteria, turning them into organic compounds and nutrients, respectively.  However, atmospheric pressure on Mars is a big problem.  The total pressure there is less than 1% of Earth ’ s — from 6 to 11 GPa: this is too small for the presence of liquid water, while the partial pressure of gaseous nitrogen — from 0.2 to 0.3 GPa — is not enough for their metabolism.  But recreating the atmosphere, like on Earth, would be too expensive: gases would have to be imported.  So the researchers were looking for a middle ground: an atmosphere close to Martian, which allows cyanobacteria to grow well.  The authors have developed a bioreactor called Atmos, which has an atmospheric pressure of about 10 percent of Earth ’ s, but uses only what can be found on Mars, albeit in inverted proportions: 96 percent nitrogen and 4 percent carbon dioxide.  The bioreactor also included water that can be obtained on Mars from melting ice, which in some places is abundant on the surface, and a simulator of Martian regolith, a mixture of minerals created here on Earth using only what can be found on Mars.  The team chose the type of nitrogen-fixing cyanobacteria that preliminary trials showed was most likely to thrive under these conditions, Anabaena sp.  PCC 7938, and tested it in a variety of conditions.  The researchers concluded that nitrogen-fixing, oxygen-producing cyanobacteria can be grown on Mars at low pressure under controlled conditions using exclusively local ingredients.  From cyanobacteria, sugar, amino acids and other nutrients can be obtained to feed other crops, which can then be used for other purposes, such as the production of medicines.  Atmos was designed to test whether cyanobacteria can be grown under certain atmospheric conditions rather than for maximum efficiency, and the parameters of the bioreactor will depend on many factors in the mission to Mars, including the payload and mission architecture.  However, now that the concept has been proven, the team can begin work on optimizing the bioreactor system that could one day save us life on Mars. report:
Creating a sustainable atmosphere on Mars is a complex task that requires careful planning and execution. 
One of the key components of a sustainable atmosphere is the production of oxygen, which is essential for human life support [f23d0347-2a7a-42e3-92ae-041c694da975].

NASA's Mars rover, Perseverance, has successfully demonstrated the ability to extract oxygen from the Martian atmosphere using the Mars Oxygen In-situ Resource Utilization Experiment (MOXIE) [f23d0347-2a7a-42e3-92ae-041c694da975]. 
MOXIE is a toaster-sized instrument that converts carbon dioxide into oxygen and carbon monoxide [a9b637ed-3450-48ea-b997-51a387d2ede1]. 
The experiment was conducted on April 20, the 60th day since the landing of the mission to Mars [f23d0347-2a7a-42e3-92ae-041c694da975].

The MOXIE device uses electrolysis to break down carbon dioxide into oxygen and carbon monoxide [a9b637ed-3450-48ea-b997-51a387d2ede1]. 
The process involves capturing carbon dioxide, passing it through a filter to remove dust, and then compressing it to provide pressure at ground level [a9b637ed-3450-48ea-b997-51a387d2ede1]. 
The gas then passes through a heated electrolysis cell, which consists of several layers of nickel alloy and ceramics [a9b637ed-3450-48ea-b997-51a387d2ede1].

The MOXIE technology has the potential to provide astronauts with oxygen for breathing and fuel for rocket propulsion [a9b637ed-3450-48ea-b997-51a387d2ede1]. 
The device is capable of producing up to 10 grams of oxygen per hour, which is a significant improvement over previous oxygen-generating experiments [a9b637ed-3450-48ea-b997-51a387d2ede1].

Title: NASA's Mars rover receives oxygen from Mars' atmosphere for the first time
Content: Mars Rover Perseverance for the first time was able to get oxygen from the atmosphere of Mars.  NASA launched it to the Red Planet in July 2020. — A growing number of discoveries of Perseverance, NASA ’ s newest six-wheeled work on the Martian surface, including the conversion of part of the thin, carbon-rich atmosphere into oxygen, — said in a statement of the space Agency.  The rover conducted the corresponding test on April 20, the 60th day since the landing of the mission to Mars.  The mission was carried out by a toaster-sized instrument aboard Perseverance called the Mars Oxygen In-situ Resource Utilization Experiment (MOXIE).  NASA explained that this discovery will help in the future to provide astronauts with air suitable for breathing.  Despite the fact that the atmosphere of the red planet is 96% carbon dioxide.  Also, the transformation of the local atmosphere with oxygen may allow in the future to produce fuel on Mars.  The agency noted that such achievements bring a person closer to landing on this planet.  The Perseverance rover was launched to Mars in July 2020 on the Atlas V rocket. The purpose of the mission is to search for traces of life in the Jezero crater, collect samples of rocks and sediments, and study the planet ’ s climate.  On February 22, the rocket landed on the surface of Mars.  In early March, the rover held its first test drive after landing.  The appearance of the “rainbow ” in the picture from Mars As part of the NASA Mars 2020 mission, the Mars Rover Perseverance took an unusual picture.  His lens got a rainbow, the appearance of which is impossible on Mars.  However, NASA has already officially denied the rainbow in the photo.  Its experts said that this is only a reflection of the sun, caught in the mechanism of the lens Hazcam Rover Perseverance.
