passages.passage: Polizia di Stato / Reuters / Scanpix / LETA In the Italian city of Piacenza found a painting by Austrian artist Gustav Klimt “Portrait of a woman ”, the cost of which is estimated at 60 million euros.  The painting was stolen in 1997 and was included in the list of the most wanted art objects in Italy.  The painting was found in the wall of the Ricci Oddy gallery, from where it was taken 22 years ago.  Examination has not yet confirmed the authenticity of the painting, but the gallery staff believe that it is the original.  Gustav Klimt painted Portrait of a Woman in 1916 or 1917.  In 1925, the painting was bought by the aristocrat from Piacenza Giuseppe Ricci Oddi.  The collector bequeathed his collection of art to the city, and after his death they were exhibited in the gallery, which received his name.  “Portrait of a Woman ” was the most valuable exhibit of the Ricci Oddi Gallery.  In 1996, 18-year-old art student Claudia Maga noticed that Portrait of a Woman was similar to another female portrait of Klimt that no one had seen since 1912.  The magician made photocopies of both works of the artist from the album on art and with the help of tracing paper superimposed on each other.  Contours and sizes matched.  She told about her find to the then director of the gallery Ricci Oddi Ferdinando Arisi.  He took the Portrait of a Woman to the hospital to check the canvas on an X-ray machine.  It turned out that under the top layer of paint is really hidden another.  “Portrait of a Woman ” was the only“ double picture ” of Klimt.  Who is depicted on it is not known exactly.  It is assumed that it is the muse of Klimt Alma Mahler or another lover of the artist Ria Munch, who posed for him for several portraits.  According to a 2016 BBC story, Klimt fell in love with a young girl from Vienna and painted her portrait in a wide-brimmed hat and fur boa.  When the girl died suddenly, Klimt rewrote the painting so that it did not remind him of the loss.  In honor of the opening of the "double picture" of Klimt, the Ricci Oddi Gallery decided to organize an exhibition in the palace of the XIII century in Piacenza.  At the same time, the gallery building was closed for reconstruction.  There were workers, paintings were taken to storage, and the alarm was turned off.  In February 1997, the “Portrait of a Woman ” disappeared, and the disappearance was not immediately noticed: the curators did not see the canvas since Tuesday, but reported to the police only on Saturday.  Later, a frame was found on the roof of the museum.  This gave rise to the version that the picture was pulled out with a fishing rod through a window in the ceiling (it was quickly abandoned because the frame was larger than the window opening).  In April 1997, Italian customs reported that the "Portrait of a Woman" had been found on the Italian-French border.  The canvas was planned to be sent to the former Prime Minister of Italy Bettino Craxi, who at home was accused of corruption and fled to Tunisia.  Employees of the gallery rushed to the border - they were in such a hurry that they received a fine for speeding by 240 thousand liras (about $140 at the exchange rate of 1997).  However, on the spot, it quickly became clear that the picture was a fake: it smelled fresh paint.  Portrait of a Woman, which was one of two paintings by Klimt in Italy, became the second most valuable painting sought in the country (the first was Caravaggio ’ s “Christmas with St. Lawrence and St. Francis ”, stolen from Palermo in 1969).  It was suggested that it might have been a contract theft because the fame of the painting would have prevented it from being sold; but the police were unable to find the alleged customers and perpetrators.  In 2014, the case was reopened, as the police found a match fingerprint on the frame with some other prints.  However, this lead did not lead to the disclosure of the crime.  In November 2015, a man claiming to be an art thief offered to reveal the location of the Portrait of a Woman in exchange for 150,000 euros.  The police refused to pay.  A year later, the BBC published an interview with an unnamed resident of Piacenza, who in the past allegedly stole art, and later began to help the police in exchange for immunity from criminal prosecution.  The man claimed that he stole the “Portrait of a Woman ”.  He claimed that at first, with the help of one of the employees of the gallery, he replaced the original with a fake, and a few months later he took it out to cover his tracks.  A BBC interviewee said he sold the painting for cash and cocaine.  He added that the canvas will return to the gallery for the 20th anniversary of the theft, that is, by February 2017.  The forecast came true almost three years late.  On December 10, 2019, “Portrait of a Woman ” was discovered by an employee of one of the municipal enterprises of Piacenza, who was cleaning the walls of Ricci Oddi ’ s gallery from ivy.  He saw a cavity in the wall closed by an iron door; inside lay a painting wrapped in a black plastic garbage bag.  Employees of the gallery identified it as “Portrait of a woman ” Klimt.  They examined the seals and stamps on the back of the canvas and suggested that the find was the original (about six or seven fakes of the Portrait of a Woman had previously surfaced).  However, its authenticity will be determined by the examination. The head of the Department of Culture of the City of Piacenza, Jonathan Papamareng, questioned this version.  First, according to him, after the theft, the territory of the gallery was thoroughly inspected.  Secondly, the canvas is too well preserved.  “It is in excellent condition.  It is hard to believe that it has been hidden in a wall for 22 years, close to the ground and plants, ” Papamareng told Reuters.  Olga Korelina

Title: 23 year old Klimt painting accidentally found in stolen museum
Content: A painting by Austrian painter Klimt was stolen from an Italian art museum nearly 23 years ago, but it was accidentally recovered when a gardener cleaned the ivy on the exterior of the museum.  But exactly why this painting is hidden in the alcove of the outer wall of the museum is still a mystery.  Italian authorities have confirmed that the painting found last December at the Ricci Oddi Gallery of Modern Art in the northern Italian city of Piacenza is indeed the “Portrait of a Lady ” by Gustav Klimt, which was stolen from the gallery in 1997.  The painting was painted by Klimt in 1916-1917, bought by Italian collector Giuseppe Ricci Oddi in 1925, and kept in his own museum of the same name until it was stolen in preparation for a special exhibition on February 22, 1997.  The painting is valued at at least 60 million euros.  Just when everyone thought that the "lady portrait" will always evaporate, in December last year, the gardener cleaned the ivy of the outer wall of the Richie Odie Museum of Modern Art, but accidentally found a metal door panel, opened to find an alcove, there is a black bag in the wall, which is suspected of the painting.  In order to determine whether the paintings found were genuine, the experts irradiated them with infrared and ultraviolet light and compared them with the images taken during the examination of the original paintings in 1996.  "I can tell you with emotion that this work is genuine," said Italian prosecutor Ornella Chicca.  As for whether the painting has been placed in this niche after it has been stolen, or only after it has been placed, more tests are still needed to clarify.  According to the museum ’ s official statement, the exterior wall of the painting has not been trimmed for nearly 10 years.  Zika said that once the relevant tests are completed, the works will be displayed again in the museum.

Title: In the wall of the Italian Museum found a painting by Gustav Klimt “Portrait of a woman ” stolen 22 years ago – and he was one of the most wanted art objects – Meduza
Content: Polizia di Stato / Reuters / Scanpix / LETA In the Italian city of Piacenza found a painting by Austrian artist Gustav Klimt “Portrait of a woman ”, the cost of which is estimated at 60 million euros.  The painting was stolen in 1997 and was included in the list of the most wanted art objects in Italy.  The painting was found in the wall of the Ricci Oddy gallery, from where it was taken 22 years ago.  Examination has not yet confirmed the authenticity of the painting, but the gallery staff believe that it is the original.  Gustav Klimt painted Portrait of a Woman in 1916 or 1917.  In 1925, the painting was bought by the aristocrat from Piacenza Giuseppe Ricci Oddi.  The collector bequeathed his collection of art to the city, and after his death they were exhibited in the gallery, which received his name.  “Portrait of a Woman ” was the most valuable exhibit of the Ricci Oddi Gallery.  In 1996, 18-year-old art student Claudia Maga noticed that Portrait of a Woman was similar to another female portrait of Klimt that no one had seen since 1912.  The magician made photocopies of both works of the artist from the album on art and with the help of tracing paper superimposed on each other.  Contours and sizes matched.  She told about her find to the then director of the gallery Ricci Oddi Ferdinando Arisi.  He took the Portrait of a Woman to the hospital to check the canvas on an X-ray machine.  It turned out that under the top layer of paint is really hidden another.  “Portrait of a Woman ” was the only“ double picture ” of Klimt.  Who is depicted on it is not known exactly.  It is assumed that it is the muse of Klimt Alma Mahler or another lover of the artist Ria Munch, who posed for him for several portraits.  According to a 2016 BBC story, Klimt fell in love with a young girl from Vienna and painted her portrait in a wide-brimmed hat and fur boa.  When the girl died suddenly, Klimt rewrote the painting so that it did not remind him of the loss.  In honor of the opening of the "double picture" of Klimt, the Ricci Oddi Gallery decided to organize an exhibition in the palace of the XIII century in Piacenza.  At the same time, the gallery building was closed for reconstruction.  There were workers, paintings were taken to storage, and the alarm was turned off.  In February 1997, the “Portrait of a Woman ” disappeared, and the disappearance was not immediately noticed: the curators did not see the canvas since Tuesday, but reported to the police only on Saturday.  Later, a frame was found on the roof of the museum.  This gave rise to the version that the picture was pulled out with a fishing rod through a window in the ceiling (it was quickly abandoned because the frame was larger than the window opening).  In April 1997, Italian customs reported that the "Portrait of a Woman" had been found on the Italian-French border.  The canvas was planned to be sent to the former Prime Minister of Italy Bettino Craxi, who at home was accused of corruption and fled to Tunisia.  Employees of the gallery rushed to the border - they were in such a hurry that they received a fine for speeding by 240 thousand liras (about $140 at the exchange rate of 1997).  However, on the spot, it quickly became clear that the picture was a fake: it smelled fresh paint.  Portrait of a Woman, which was one of two paintings by Klimt in Italy, became the second most valuable painting sought in the country (the first was Caravaggio ’ s “Christmas with St. Lawrence and St. Francis ”, stolen from Palermo in 1969).  It was suggested that it might have been a contract theft because the fame of the painting would have prevented it from being sold; but the police were unable to find the alleged customers and perpetrators.  In 2014, the case was reopened, as the police found a match fingerprint on the frame with some other prints.  However, this lead did not lead to the disclosure of the crime.  In November 2015, a man claiming to be an art thief offered to reveal the location of the Portrait of a Woman in exchange for 150,000 euros.  The police refused to pay.  A year later, the BBC published an interview with an unnamed resident of Piacenza, who in the past allegedly stole art, and later began to help the police in exchange for immunity from criminal prosecution.  The man claimed that he stole the “Portrait of a Woman ”.  He claimed that at first, with the help of one of the employees of the gallery, he replaced the original with a fake, and a few months later he took it out to cover his tracks.  A BBC interviewee said he sold the painting for cash and cocaine.  He added that the canvas will return to the gallery for the 20th anniversary of the theft, that is, by February 2017.  The forecast came true almost three years late.  On December 10, 2019, “Portrait of a Woman ” was discovered by an employee of one of the municipal enterprises of Piacenza, who was cleaning the walls of Ricci Oddi ’ s gallery from ivy.  He saw a cavity in the wall closed by an iron door; inside lay a painting wrapped in a black plastic garbage bag.  Employees of the gallery identified it as “Portrait of a woman ” Klimt.  They examined the seals and stamps on the back of the canvas and suggested that the find was the original (about six or seven fakes of the Portrait of a Woman had previously surfaced).  However, its authenticity will be determined by the examination.  Klimt il giorno dopo Telelibertà Piacenza It is assumed that the thieves planned to return for the canvas of Klimt, but failed to do so due to increased security measures in the gallery of Ricci Oddi.  The head of the Department of Culture of the City of Piacenza, Jonathan Papamareng, questioned this version.  First, according to him, after the theft, the territory of the gallery was thoroughly inspected.  Secondly, the canvas is too well preserved.  “It is in excellent condition.  It is hard to believe that it has been hidden in a wall for 22 years, close to the ground and plants, ” Papamareng told Reuters.  Olga Korelina

Title: 23 year old Klimt painting accidentally found in stolen museum
Content: A painting by Austrian painter Klimt was stolen from an Italian art museum nearly 23 years ago, but it was accidentally recovered when a gardener cleaned the ivy on the exterior of the museum. Just when everyone thought that the "lady portrait" will always evaporate, in December last year, the gardener cleaned the ivy of the outer wall of the Richie Odie Museum of Modern Art, but accidentally found a metal door panel, opened to find an alcove, there is a black bag in the wall, which is suspected of the painting. Title: In the wall of the Italian Museum found a painting by Gustav Klimt “Portrait of a woman ” stolen 22 years ago – and he was one of the most wanted art objects – Meduza
Content: Polizia di Stato / Reuters / Scanpix / LETA In the Italian city of Piacenza found a painting by Austrian artist Gustav Klimt “Portrait of a woman ”, the cost of which is estimated at 60 million euros.  The painting was stolen in 1997 and was included in the list of the most wanted art objects in Italy.  The painting was found in the wall of the Ricci Oddy gallery, from where it was taken 22 years ago.  Examination has not yet confirmed the authenticity of the painting, but the gallery staff believe that it is the original.  Gustav Klimt painted Portrait of a Woman in 1916 or 1917.  In 1925, the painting was bought by the aristocrat from Piacenza Giuseppe Ricci Oddi.  The collector bequeathed his collection of art to the city, and after his death they were exhibited in the gallery, which received his name.  “Portrait of a Woman ” was the most valuable exhibit of the Ricci Oddi Gallery.  In 1996, 18-year-old art student Claudia Maga noticed that Portrait of a Woman was similar to another female portrait of Klimt that no one had seen since 1912.  The magician made photocopies of both works of the artist from the album on art and with the help of tracing paper superimposed on each other.  Contours and sizes matched.  She told about her find to the then director of the gallery Ricci Oddi Ferdinando Arisi.  He took the Portrait of a Woman to the hospital to check the canvas on an X-ray machine.  It turned out that under the top layer of paint is really hidden another.  “Portrait of a Woman ” was the only“ double picture ” of Klimt.  Who is depicted on it is not known exactly.  It is assumed that it is the muse of Klimt Alma Mahler or another lover of the artist Ria Munch, who posed for him for several portraits.  According to a 2016 BBC story, Klimt fell in love with a young girl from Vienna and painted her portrait in a wide-brimmed hat and fur boa.  When the girl died suddenly, Klimt rewrote the painting so that it did not remind him of the loss.  In honor of the opening of the "double picture" of Klimt, the Ricci Oddi Gallery decided to organize an exhibition in the palace of the XIII century in Piacenza.  At the same time, the gallery building was closed for reconstruction.  There were workers, paintings were taken to storage, and the alarm was turned off.  In February 1997, the “Portrait of a Woman ” disappeared, and the disappearance was not immediately noticed: the curators did not see the canvas since Tuesday, but reported to the police only on Saturday.  Later, a frame was found on the roof of the museum.  This gave rise to the version that the picture was pulled out with a fishing rod through a window in the ceiling (it was quickly abandoned because the frame was larger than the window opening).  In April 1997, Italian customs reported that the "Portrait of a Woman" had been found on the Italian-French border.  The canvas was planned to be sent to the former Prime Minister of Italy Bettino Craxi, who at home was accused of corruption and fled to Tunisia.  Employees of the gallery rushed to the border - they were in such a hurry that they received a fine for speeding by 240 thousand liras (about $140 at the exchange rate of 1997).  However, on the spot, it quickly became clear that the picture was a fake: it smelled fresh paint.  Portrait of a Woman, which was one of two paintings by Klimt in Italy, became the second most valuable painting sought in the country (the first was Caravaggio ’ s “Christmas with St. Lawrence and St. Francis ”, stolen from Palermo in 1969).  It was suggested that it might have been a contract theft because the fame of the painting would have prevented it from being sold; but the police were unable to find the alleged customers and perpetrators.  In 2014, the case was reopened, as the police found a match fingerprint on the frame with some other prints.  However, this lead did not lead to the disclosure of the crime.  In November 2015, a man claiming to be an art thief offered to reveal the location of the Portrait of a Woman in exchange for 150,000 euros.  The police refused to pay.  A year later, the BBC published an interview with an unnamed resident of Piacenza, who in the past allegedly stole art, and later began to help the police in exchange for immunity from criminal prosecution.  The man claimed that he stole the “Portrait of a Woman ”.  He claimed that at first, with the help of one of the employees of the gallery, he replaced the original with a fake, and a few months later he took it out to cover his tracks.  A BBC interviewee said he sold the painting for cash and cocaine.  He added that the canvas will return to the gallery for the 20th anniversary of the theft, that is, by February 2017.  The forecast came true almost three years late.  On December 10, 2019, “Portrait of a Woman ” was discovered by an employee of one of the municipal enterprises of Piacenza, who was cleaning the walls of Ricci Oddi ’ s gallery from ivy.  He saw a cavity in the wall closed by an iron door; inside lay a painting wrapped in a black plastic garbage bag.  Employees of the gallery identified it as “Portrait of a woman ” Klimt.  They examined the seals and stamps on the back of the canvas and suggested that the find was the original (about six or seven fakes of the Portrait of a Woman had previously surfaced).  However, its authenticity will be determined by the examination.  Klimt il giorno dopo Telelibertà Piacenza It is assumed that the thieves planned to return for the canvas of Klimt, but failed to do so due to increased security measures in the gallery of Ricci Oddi.  The head of the Department of Culture of the City of Piacenza, Jonathan Papamareng, questioned this version.  First, according to him, after the theft, the territory of the gallery was thoroughly inspected.  Secondly, the canvas is too well preserved.  “It is in excellent condition.  It is hard to believe that it has been hidden in a wall for 22 years, close to the ground and plants, ” Papamareng told Reuters.  Olga Korelina

passages.title: UN Climate Report: Warming Causes Drought, Hunger Threatens Human Health - Technology
passages.passage: A warming planet has a major impact on human health, with hunger, drought and disease afflicting tens of millions of people over decades, according to a draft report released by the United Nations today.  After more than a year of pandemics that have completely turned the world upside down, the forthcoming report of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) offers even more dire predictions of malnutrition, water scarcity and plague in the coming decades.  Policy choices such as the promotion of plant-based diets can limit these health consequences, but many will remain unavoidable in the short term, the report said.  Babies born today may face a variety of climate-related health threats before they reach the age of 30, depending on how well humans handle carbon emissions and rising temperatures, according to the report.  The 4,000-page draft report, expected to be released next year, is the most complete report yet on the impact of climate change on the planet and species.  The report estimates that 80 million more people are at risk of hunger by 2050 than today.  The report estimates that disruptions to the water cycle will reduce harvests of rain-fed staple crops in sub-Saharan Africa.  As many as 40% of India ’ s rice-producing areas are unsuitable for farming.  Rising temperatures not only affect crop yields, but also reduce nutritional values, such as rice, wheat, barley and potatoes, by 6% to 14%, the report said, adding that the number of people at risk of protein deficiency is nearly 150 million more than today.  Food prices are expected to rise by as much as a third in 2050 as climate change reduces crop yields and increases demand for biofuel crops and carbon dioxide-absorbing forests, increasing the number of low-income households facing chronic hunger by 183 million.  Across Asia and Africa, the number of undernourished and stunted children by the middle of the century will increase by 10 million, creating a new generation of better socioeconomic development, but lifelong health problems.  As with most climate change impacts, the impact on human health varies from place to place, with 80% of the population at risk of hunger living in Africa and Southeast Asia, according to the report.  According to the report, studies on freshwater supply, agriculture and sea level rise show that between 30 million and 140 million people will be displaced in Africa, Southeast Asia and Latin America by 2050.

passages.title: Reduction of water resources of Kazakhstan by 25% is predicted by 2030
passages.passage: Astana.  7 November.  KazTAG – The reduction of water resources in Kazakhstan by 25% is predicted by 2030, the press service of the UN Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) reports.  “Among the threats posed by climate change to Kazakhstan ’ s agricultural sector is water scarcity, which is projected to be reduced by 25% by 2030, putting additional strain on the sector and leading to even greater aridity, especially in the southern and central regions of Kazakhstan, ” FAO said on Wednesday.  Another expected impact of climate change in the organization called the drying of pastures and reduced access of livestock to water sources.  “Changes in weather cycles can also cause spring floods, torrential autumn rains and early frosts, leading to crop losses.  That is, strengthening the resilience of the agricultural sector to such phenomena through targeted investments that contribute to reducing vulnerability both within the country and in individual regions is an urgent task, ” the UN agricultural organization stressed.  FAO stressed that now the task of adapting to a changing climate is one of the key priorities in the world.  Climate change, including disruption of rain cycles, droughts, floods, and the spread of pests and diseases, according to the organization, both directly and indirectly affect agricultural productivity.  “Accelerating the adoption of climate technologies is a significant step towards addressing these challenges.  The use of modern climate technologies is a key element in the transition to more sustainable food production systems, ” said Nuno Santos, economist at the FAO Investment Centre.  In close cooperation with local governments, FAO and the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) organized the workshop to serve as a platform for dialogue among all stakeholders – the private sector, government agencies, research institutions, international organizations and civil society.  “All of them can play a role in supporting the implementation of climate technologies in Kazakhstan, ” the report said.  The participants of the seminar, according to FAO, noted the key trends in the implementation of climate technologies in the agri-food sector of Kazakhstan and focused on identifying problems and opportunities for private sector investment in modern agri-food technologies.  “The participants also shared their experience and made proposals to overcome difficulties and create a favorable climate for private investment.  The workshop also discussed possible areas for public support and collaboration with donors and international financial institutions to accelerate technology adoption, as strategic alliances and close collaboration among stakeholders are key to achieving the UN Sustainable Development Goals by 2030.

passages.title: Infographic Understanding Climate Change: Warmer weather not only harms human health, but agriculture and the economy have also paid the price
passages.passage: David Nelles and Christian Serrer: Climate change has now directly or indirectly affected the lives of 7.5 billion people on the planet.  However, the impact of global warming varies from place to place, which means that people and people living together in different regions will also be affected to varying degrees.  In any case, one thing is certain: the continued warming of the climate will continue to bring all kinds of adverse effects to mankind.  Climate change can have many effects on human health, such as heat stress caused by high temperature, operating environment factors (including air temperature, humidity, wind speed and radiation heat) and clothing, and high temperature events, which can worsen heart, blood circulation and respiratory related diseases. Increase the mortality rate of these diseases.  On the other hand, high temperatures are conducive to the formation of ozone close to the ground, which has adverse effects on human health, such as may lead to decreased lung function.  Extreme weather events such as floods or storms are more frequent and can also bring more hidden risks to human health, such as injuries and even death in serious cases.  In addition, already polluted waters may increase the risk of infectious disease outbreaks due to heavy rainfall and flooding.  Another effect of climate change in Germany is the lengthening of the pollen season, which exacerbates the symptoms of respiratory diseases such as asthma or allergic rhinitis.  And such climatic conditions are more conducive to the growth and reproduction of allergenic plants, such as Ambrosia is a good example.  Photo Credit: Businessweek / Lisa Schwegler, Stefan Kraiss, and Janna Geisse Produced The 2010 increase in global deaths due to climate change A spreading vector of disease caused by climate change refers to organisms that can transmit pathogens from infected animals or humans to other animals or humans, such as ticks commonly known as ticks, or mosquitoes.  Climate change is changing the current environmental conditions in which pathogens are spread by vectors.  In recent decades, due to globalization and favorable climatic conditions, the Asian-native Aedes albopictus (also known as the Asian tiger mosquito) has reached parts of southern Europe.  In the near future, other areas of higher latitudes in Europe should also become suitable for mosquito activity due to climate change.  It is important to note that the white line mosquito spreads dengue fever and Chikungunya virus.  On the other hand, the high temperature must be maintained for a period of time before the virus can be spread through the infected mosquitoes, because the warm temperature allows the virus to successfully reproduce in the mosquitoes and then transmit the virus to humans when the mosquitoes bite.  Rising temperatures create favorable conditions for the spread of Aedes albopictus and shorten the propagation time of the virus in Aedes albopictus.  Combining globalization with the risks that come with it, such as the importation of foreign goods that could trap Aedes albopictus, or returning travelers infected with the virus, increases the risk of disease transmission.  Photo Credit: Businessweek / Lisa Schwegler, Stefan Kraiss, and Janna Geisse produce Climate change impacts on agriculture High temperatures, high levels of carbon dioxide in the air, changes in rainfall patterns, and associated changing weather parameters can affect plant growth.  When the temperature rises to the most appropriate growth temperature, the yield of a particular crop can be increased, but once the temperature exceeds this optimum value, the crop yield begins to decrease.  In the case of corn and soybeans, as long as the growth period is more than 30 ° C, it is not conducive to the development of these crops.  In addition, extreme weather, especially drought and high temperatures, as well as heavy rain, can negatively affect yields. Between 2000 and 2007 alone, droughts and high temperatures have reduced global cereal crops by about 6.2%.  When the concentration of carbon dioxide in the air increases, many plants respond quickly by reducing the amount of water released from the leaves and increasing photosynthesis.  In this way, there is enough water and nutrients to promote plant growth, which is known as the "CO2 fertilization effect" (CO2-Düngungseffekt).  There is debate as to how much this fertilization effect can offset the reduction in production in some areas due to changes in temperature and rainfall patterns.  In addition, increased carbon dioxide concentration in the air can promote plant growth, but it also means that the nutrient concentration in the plant will be relatively reduced.  If higher average temperatures lead to longer tillage periods, less cold damage and higher crop yields, then climate change has positive implications for higher latitudes, such as northern Europe.  In contrast, climate change is not necessarily a good thing for crop yields in tropical and subtropical regions.  Climate change comes with three different types of costs: First, the cost of damage, such as direct damage to real estate or public infrastructure caused by extreme weather events.  This is followed by adaptation costs, such as levees or ponds for flood control.  The third is the so-called avoidance costs, such as the costs of switching from fossil to renewable energy to limit future global warming.  Because it is not possible to have a clear and comprehensive picture of all the costs incurred, it is actually very difficult to calculate precise figures for the economic costs of climate change.  Therefore, the calculated cost can only depend on the assumptions made, and it is very difficult to accurately grasp the costs of such things, such as melted permafrost, so it is extremely difficult to analyze the chart below.  Photo Credit: Business Week Publishing / Produced by Lisa Schwegler, Stefan Kraiss, and Janna Geisse Because of these high levels of uncertainty, it is very difficult to know exactly what climate protection measures should be taken and how much it should be interfered with from a purely economic point of view.  If people want to limit warming to 1.5 ° C, they will have to pay a very high investment cost.  Compared to setting the temperature rise range at a maximum of 3.5 ° C, the investment cost, although significantly reduced, will result in higher damage costs.  Overall, the cost of limiting global warming should be much less than the cost of damage caused by an unrestricted rise in global temperatures.  It is worth noting that as the temperature rises, the risk of irreversible damage is also increased.  Photo Credit: Businessweek / Lisa Schwegler, Stefan Kraiss, and Janna Geisse conclude that climate change is not a distant vision of the future, and that it represents more than just melting icebergs and rising sea levels, which are already threatening many people and their livelihoods.  In addition, it also shows that the temperature rise observed since the beginning of the industrial era is mainly due to man-made greenhouse gas emissions.  Fortunately, there ’ s also some ironic good news: we have the opportunity to influence the future of the climate, and we ’ re not completely powerless against climate change!  Climate model simulations show that as long as humans reduce greenhouse gas emissions, it is expected to limit the development of global warming.  Photo Credit: Businessweek / Lisa Schwegler, Stefan Kraiss, and Janna Geisse produced a global average temperature forecast for greenhouse gas emissions, but since the United Nations Climate Conference (UN-Klimakonferenz) was first held in Berlin in 1995, global greenhouse gas emissions have risen by 50%, reaching a record high.  If human beings continue to produce large quantities of greenhouse gases, it is not impossible to imagine that global temperatures will rise by another 5 ° C by the end of the century.  Therefore, we must all be aware of our responsibility: how the future of the climate, and the extent to which the impact of global warming will worsen, is entirely in our hands! passages.title: Biologist has estimated the possibility of the disappearance of habitual products due to climate change
passages.passage: Climate change can undoubtedly affect the crops and products of various crops.  However, this trend is likely to mean short-term problems.  Alexander Markov, Doctor of Biological Sciences, Head of the Department of Biological Evolution of the Biological Faculty of Lomonosov Moscow State University, told Zvezda.  According to him, despite the information that appeared in the media that climate change threatens the disappearance of most of the familiar products, this situation is not entirely true.  The reason is that in the case of a change in the usual climate, manufacturers will simply have to rebuild, which will take a certain time.  However, everyone ’ s favorite products will not disappear because of this.  “Climate change can affect the crops and products of various crops, plants, animals and so on.  If it gets warmer or colder, it will affect the productivity of the system.  In some regions it can be a positive impact, in others it can be negative.  In general, any climate change will cause short-term problems: something is changing, agricultural producers have adapted to certain conditions, but those have changed.  You will have to grow crops in other places.  These will be short-term problems for sure, ” Markov said.  The expert added that climate change could cause local problems with agricultural productivity in all regions.  But we can adapt to the changes.  “These are not fatal processes, ” he concluded.  Earlier in the media there was information that, according to scientists, climate change can supposedly lead to the disappearance of most of the usual human products - from potatoes to olive oil.  At the same time, British researchers are convinced that coffee can disappear, and by 2050 the territory suitable for its cultivation will be halved.  And after another 30 years, the plant will completely disappear.

passages.title: Sustainable development: why young people choose companies that work under this credo
passages.passage: Sustainable development as a concept in its current form started 50 years ago.  It was in the 1970s that global structures such as the United Nations or the Club of Rome realized that man was actively influencing the planet.  In the 21st century, this resulted in the UN ’ s 17 Sustainable Development Goals.  What are these goals, why are they needed, what is the situation of humanity on Earth now and why we all should somehow become conscious and responsible for the future - in the material Delo.ua in the framework of the special project "Leaders of sustainable development".  As of 2019, there were 7.674 billion people living on planet Earth.  Today, according to TheWorldCount, there are 7.85 billion people.  The good news is that the rate of population growth is still decreasing, in the 1970s it was 2%, in 2019 it was 1.1%.  But it's still a lot.  According to the UN Department of Economic and Social Affairs, 8.323 billion people will live in the world in 2030, and 9.3 billion by 2050.  In 2100, there will be 11 billion people in the world.  The gross domestic product of the planet in 2019 amounted to 87.8 trillion US dollars.  Faceless numbers behind which lies human interaction with the physical world.  Remember the year 2019?  You ate, drank, traveled, bought things, lost things.  They left a carbon footprint.  According to the constantly updated consumption calculator, at the current level, we need 1.8 planet Earth.  Yes, almost twice as much as there is at the moment.  And that ’ s the average cut.  At the same time, we have one Earth.  It is a small, unremarkable planet in a galactic backwater.  We are trying to go into space and even think about going to Mars, but in reality there is only one hole in the orbit of the International Space Station.  And if anything happens on the planet, we really have nowhere to run.  For example, if you travel by car, at least twice a year fly to conditional Egypt, live in an apartment building, buy food brought by plane, you need 4.5 Earth.  At the same time, we have one Earth.  It is a small, unremarkable planet in a galactic backwater.  We are trying to go into space and even think about going to Mars, but in reality there is only one hole in the orbit of the International Space Station.  And if anything happens on the planet, we really have nowhere to run.  And it can happen.  Because behind every dollar of global GDP is energy and industry that meets the needs of the population.  We plow the land, destroy the forests, warm up the permafrost - and out comes the same carbon, which, in turn, leads to the greenhouse effect.  Which, in turn, causes climate change.  And this is not warming, as many people think, but an increase in the number of extremes.  Last year, Ukraine experienced fires in the Chernobyl zone, in the Zhytomyr region, in the Luhansk region.  It is seriously affected by desertification.  Kiev and Kiev region were covered by dust storms.  Already in 2021, the Ministry of Ecology said that pesticides, pharmaceuticals and heavy metals were detected in Dnipro.  Studies show that Ukrainian lands may lose their fertility.  Half of the country was flooded with rains and floods, in the second half the harvest was scorched by the summer heat.  Abnormally low rainfall drained the land.  All these are consequences of global climate change.  According to a study conducted by an international team of scientists from Switzerland, Germany and the Netherlands, since 2008 disasters caused by natural phenomena have led to the displacement of 288 million people (including evacuations).  Three times as many people have left as have been the result of wars, conflicts and violence.  About half of people are forced to leave their homes due to flooding.  Agricultural productivity is declining.  The University of Maryland, in collaboration with Cornell University and Stanford University, has for the first time quantified the anthropogenic impact of climate change on global agricultural productivity growth.  In a new study published in the journal Nature Climate Change, researchers show that global agricultural productivity has declined by 21% since 1961, which the researchers believe is equivalent to a total loss of productivity growth over the past 7 years.  "Our study suggests that climate and weather-related factors have already had a major impact on agricultural productivity," said Robert Chambers, a professor of agricultural economics and resources at the University of Maryland.  Thus, since 1961, regions such as Africa, Latin America and the Caribbean, which are in regions with warmer climates, have already experienced a slowdown of 26-34%.  The United States suffered less, with growth slowing by about 5-15%.  “Some people think of climate change as a distant issue that should concern future generations first.  But this does not take into account the fact that people have already changed the climate, — says Ariel Ortiz-Bobea, lead author of the study from Cornell University. — In general, our study shows that anthropogenic climate change already has a disproportionate impact on poorer countries that depend primarily on agriculture.  It seems that technological progress has not yet led to greater resilience to climate change. "  At the same time, regions suffering from water shortages, such as Jordan, are facing an exacerbation of this problem.  According to a Stanford University study, water depletion and population growth will halve Jordan ’ s per capita water consumption by the end of this century.  Low-income areas will be hardest hit: by 2100, 91% of households will receive less than 40 liters of water per day for 11 consecutive months of the year.  If society has strong levers of influence - guilds, fraternities, unions, cooperatives, associations - it is more stable.  If ordinary people are unable to influence what is happening, crises exacerbate inequality.  Has the Covid-19 pandemic helped the world?  Reduced inequality, reduced production?  Did humanity think about the future?  Perhaps, but a recent study by historian Bas van Bavel of the University of Utrecht and ecologist Martin Schaeffer of the University of Wageningent says that so far everything is not too good.  They looked at the impact of catastrophes — like the plague — on humanity as a whole and concluded that they could exacerbate inequality.  “In times of crisis, the rules are usually rewritten.  The most influential social groups and organizations can use this window of opportunity to adapt institutional rules, thereby shaping the long-term distribution of wealth.  Because most societies have historically been unequal, in most cases the result has been a further increase in imbalances, ” van Bavel says.  At the same time, if society has strong levers of influence - guilds, fraternities, trade unions, cooperatives, associations - it is more stable.  If ordinary people are unable to influence what is happening, crises exacerbate inequality.  In 2015, the UN, as the largest unifying structure of mankind, collected 17 goals that must be fulfilled by 2030.  This is not just a declaration, each has a clear roadmap and KPI indicators.  Here are the goals: 1.  Eradication of poverty 2.  Ending hunger 3.  Good health and well-being 4.  Quality education 5.  Gender equality 6.  Clean water and sanitation 7.  Cheap and clean energy 8.  Decent work and economic growth 9.  Industrialization, innovation and infrastructure 10.  Reducing inequality 11.  Sustainable cities and human settlements 12.  Responsible consumption and production 13.  Combating climate change 14.  Conservation of marine ecosystems 15.  Conservation of terrestrial ecosystems 16.  Peace, justice and effective institutions 17.  The answer to this question is quite obvious: so that as many people as possible on planet Earth a) survive b) can lead a comfortable life.  More and more people are becoming conscious consumers who care where the product they consume comes from, how it was made and whether environmental norms or human rights were violated in its production or in its advertising.  “Everyone has realized that sustainable development is not just a buzzword.  Everyone realized that society — especially the new generation — wants business to embody universal values.  It doesn't matter how much you make.  It is important what you do for the world, for me, for my children, for our common future, ” says Elena Zubareva, head of the Association of Sustainable Development Leaders.  Science confirms these words.  The University of Hiroshima conducted a study and found that young people are ready to sacrifice their salaries for the sake of saving humanity and the planet.  The results were published on January 31 in a special issue of the journal Clean Production, dedicated specifically to the achievement of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).  “Many people in the popular media or even in everyday conversations say that the younger generation is more socially conscious and has behaviors focused on achieving sustainable development goals, but the scientific evidence is limited, ” said Tomomi Yamane, a researcher at Hiroshima University.  And young people are willing to give their income to work in companies striving to achieve the SDGs. ”

passages.title: Climate change and water scarcity are top priorities.
passages.passage: Assistant Professor of Water Engineering at the Faculty of Agriculture of Shahrekord University said: “The main priority of the authorities should be water shortage and climate change, so that water factories are moved to the seaside and agriculture in areas that are facing water shortage is limited. ”  He said: “It ’ s been a long time, it ’ s been a long time, it ’ s been a long time, it ’ s been a long time.  “When we talk about climate change, we mean meteorological parameters that have been measured over long periods of time, and these changes manifest themselves in either natural or artificial forms, which are caused by humans.  Nasr Esfahani said: “Various factors such as sunspots, changes in the earth ’ s crust, changes in vegetation or the movement of continents, or changes in ocean temperature naturally cause climate change.  “What has happened in the past year is that humans have caused an imbalance in meteorological parameters due to excessive consumption of natural resources, including oil, gas and fossil fuels, and by destroying natural resources such as forests and expanding factories and cities.  The university professor pointed out that the country is climatally located in a dry region, saying: "We should not expect the climate to change from dry to wet, because this is a very wrong expectation that some in the society suggest this."  He said: "Climate change has become very clear in the last 40 years, so we have to adapt to this situation that has been fluctuating and know that drought or drought fluctuations are part of the nature of the region's climate."  Nasr Isfahani said: "In this situation, climate change is occurring and extreme phenomena such as severe droughts, drought, heat and cold are increasing, there is no alternative but to adapt to them, for example, agricultural products can be used to prevent frostbite, to use resistant products.  Regarding water resources, he said: “At the same time as the climate change, the consumption of water resources has greatly expanded, especially in the last 50 years, when agriculture has been the center of development in the country. ”  The university professor said: "If we examine the rainfall parameter in more detail, we see that the average rainfall has not changed, but the extremes have changed a lot and these changes are significant, on the other hand, the effective rainfall has not changed and the ineffective rainfall has increased, which means that there is a shortage of water resources."  He said: "What has been observed is that, contrary to the rainfall parameter, changes in the temperature parameter, especially the minimum temperature, are highly effective and the trend of increasing the minimum temperature is observed in many stations in the country."  Nasr Esfahani pointed out that in mountainous areas the precipitation has changed from solid to liquid state, adding: "When there is snow in the region, because the snow is slowly melting and sinking into underground sources, it feeds them, on the other hand, the occurrence of rain brings water runoff, which feeds surface water instead of feeding groundwater resources."  He added that excessive consumption of water resources, expansion of the area under cultivation, non-observance of the cultivation pattern and the use of traditional methods for irrigation have led to the reduction of groundwater.  Assistant Professor of Water Engineering at Shahrekord University emphasized: "The authorities were aware of the current situation, but they did not think that the effects of climate change would be egregious and misrepresented, and today we face a fundamental problem, for example, if there was a shortage of water, it was solved by harvesting from underground water resources and we assigned this problem to the future."  He continued: “We have reached a point where groundwater resources are not the answer to the shortage of water, and this problem has become such that measures must be taken.  Nasr Esfahani said that for short-term purposes, water resources have not been considered because steel and water mills have been built in the country, which if this decision process continues, despite the lack of water resources, will still be built in the future.  “We should not expect that one day our country will be as abundant as Europe, because the lack of rainfall in our region has been caused by the rotation of the earth and the circulation of the atmosphere, so in addition to adapting to climate change, if there is to be a cost to this, it should be done today and we should not postpone those costs to the future, because we may face more limitations in the future. ”  The university professor noted that the main priority of the authorities should be water scarcity and climate change, so that water factories are moved to the seaside and agriculture is limited in areas with water scarcity.  End of message.

passages.title: In the North Caucasus and southern Russia will increase snowfall and droughts
passages.passage: Climatologists predict that in the 21st century, the amount and intensity of snowfall will increase throughout Russia, and in some regions, arid conditions are expected to worsen.  This is reported by RIA Novosti with reference to the national report “Global climate and soil cover of Russia: assessment of risks and environmental and economic consequences of land degradation ”.  The study was conducted with the aim of developing measures for adapting agricultural and forest management systems and technologies to climate change.  Discussion of the report, analyzing the forecast scenarios of climate change and their impact on agriculture and forestry, was held at the Vasily Dokuchaev Soil Institute.  According to scientists, if at the beginning of the XXI century in Russia there was a small increase in precipitation, then by the middle of the century it will increase, especially in the eastern and northern regions of the country.  “The increase in summer precipitation is most significant, mainly in the north and east of Russia.  In the south of the European part of Russia - in the Southern and North Caucasus Federal Districts - the worsening of arid (on average per year) conditions is expected, "the study says.  At the same time, more "sharp" precipitation will probably occur in the form of separate showers or snowfalls.  There will also be more floods and floods.  Note that recently, scientists said that in 30 years the climate of the Rostov region in 30 years may change to subtropical, and the weather on the coast of the Sea of Azov will be close to the climate of Abkhazia and Sochi.  So far, we are lagging behind in temperatures: in the subtropics, the annual is + 11, we have + 9.95, - said Lyudmila Bespalova, Doctor of Geographical Sciences.  In her opinion, the summer shallowing of the Don in 2017, when the water left the coast by ten meters, is one of the brightest examples of climate change.  Changes in climatic conditions can lead not only to a change in flora and fauna, but also to a change in the economy of the region.  For example, Don farmers will have to breed new varieties of wheat and shift the timing of crops.

passages.title: World Environment Day without a national plan
passages.passage: This year ’ s World Environment Day was named as the restoration and restoration of the ecosystem.  The world ’ s environmental problems, from plastic waste production to unprecedented waste and waste of water resources, have multiplied in the aftermath of global pandemics.  In addition, the spread of poverty and the increase in economic and social discrimination have made many individuals, organizations and countries unable to spend money to deal with problems related to natural resources and conservation.  To stop and repair the problems facing nature (at least that resilient part of the world), more than $530 billion per year will be required from today to 2050, the World Environment Organization reports.  It becomes even more important to recognize that natural resources have a significant contribution to the development and growth of countries, a path that will lead to access for all the inhabitants of the earth to health services, education, health and housing.  Without the restoration and protection of nature, sustainable development will not be possible, and the consumption of the earth ’ s natural resources cannot continue indefinitely without protecting it.  The destruction of the environment from one border to the other is both accelerating and becoming irreversible in many places.  The most important way to protect the world ’ s environment is to agree and engage all countries in stopping and mitigating the effects of consumer-driven mismanagement in countries around the world, invest in the preservation of natural reserves, and strive to remain committed to global agreements on water and waste and climate change.  The event is hosted by the World Environment Day conference in Pakistan.  Asia ’ s most populous countries such as India, Pakistan and Indonesia are among the first countries affected by climate change, global warming and its resulting phenomena, given their country ’ s climate and population. According to the Information Center of the Ministry of Energy (Pawn), in the year 1400 – 1399, of the total capacity of 50.5 billion cubic meters of dam reservoirs, about 28 billion and 810 million cubic meters, equivalent to 57 percent of the reservoirs have been filled.  Accordingly, due to the decreasing trend of precipitation and increasing air heat, the volume of water inlet from the beginning of the 1400-1399 year has been equal to 25 billion and 290 million cubic meters, which compared to the same period of the previous year (47 billion and 580 million cubic meters), represents a 47% decrease in water inlet to the country ’ s dams.  The report says that the latest status of the country ’ s dams shows that the early increase in temperature has done its job and the amount of water reserves in the reservoir of the dams has reached 28,810 million cubic meters, which is 27 percent lower compared to the 99-98 year (39,680 million cubic meters).  According to these statistics, due to the amount of input to the country ’ s dams, water output from the dams has decreased, and up to this time, 23 billion and 630 million cubic meters of water output from the country ’ s dams has been made, so that compared to the same period of the previous year, there has been a 35% reduction.  In the last two years, planting rice in Fars province, Isfahan, even southern Khorasan in the desert was one of the worst decisions in the field of agriculture and a symbol of water mismanagement in this field.  They are still planting rice with the immersion method, while the same Gilan and Mazandaran have water problems, let alone central and eastern Iran.  Why no planning or training has been done to replace other crops for farmers to change their cultivation pattern.  The first methods of adaptation to water scarcity and water management should also be considered in the field of agriculture.  New research shows that climate change and global warming have shown their impact even on short-term crops such as agricultural land and horticulture.  Apart from rain showers and short periods outside the growing season and the need for plants, sudden changes in temperature and the reduction of the duration of the middle seasons (spring and autumn), other problems have also occurred for farmers in this area.  Pests are becoming more and more diverse, and weeds are also growing in the winter.  The number of bees has decreased, and the fertility of the blossoms and the size of the fruit has changed significantly over the last half century.  Also, the possibility of fresh cultivation in areas with cooler temperatures has made it difficult for tropical countries to trade and compete.  For some crops, such as coffee and some types of rice, the land suitable for cultivation is declining globally, and many farmers do not consider it economical to continue cultivating it.  In Iran, the set of variables such as the reduction of rain and the change in the type of precipitation and its seasons, the increase in the average air temperature and the increase in the rate of evaporation, and climatic variables such as this are also changing under the influence of climate change.  Do we have a plan to adapt to the situation we face for agriculture and animal husbandry that is directly linked to Iran ’ s food security?  How to meet the basic needs of villagers, farmers and ranchers in applying the latest technology in the field of agriculture and irrigation?  The national plan and vision is very important to solve this problem.  Do presidential candidates really have a plan for this?

Title: UN Climate Report: Warming Causes Drought, Hunger Threatens Human Health - Technology
Content: A warming planet has a major impact on human health, with hunger, drought and disease afflicting tens of millions of people over decades, according to a draft report released by the United Nations today.  After more than a year of pandemics that have completely turned the world upside down, the forthcoming report of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) offers even more dire predictions of malnutrition, water scarcity and plague in the coming decades.  Policy choices such as the promotion of plant-based diets can limit these health consequences, but many will remain unavoidable in the short term, the report said.  Babies born today may face a variety of climate-related health threats before they reach the age of 30, depending on how well humans handle carbon emissions and rising temperatures, according to the report.  The 4,000-page draft report, expected to be released next year, is the most complete report yet on the impact of climate change on the planet and species.  The report estimates that 80 million more people are at risk of hunger by 2050 than today.  The report estimates that disruptions to the water cycle will reduce harvests of rain-fed staple crops in sub-Saharan Africa.  As many as 40% of India ’ s rice-producing areas are unsuitable for farming.  Rising temperatures not only affect crop yields, but also reduce nutritional values, such as rice, wheat, barley and potatoes, by 6% to 14%, the report said, adding that the number of people at risk of protein deficiency is nearly 150 million more than today.  Food prices are expected to rise by as much as a third in 2050 as climate change reduces crop yields and increases demand for biofuel crops and carbon dioxide-absorbing forests, increasing the number of low-income households facing chronic hunger by 183 million.  Across Asia and Africa, the number of undernourished and stunted children by the middle of the century will increase by 10 million, creating a new generation of better socioeconomic development, but lifelong health problems.  As with most climate change impacts, the impact on human health varies from place to place, with 80% of the population at risk of hunger living in Africa and Southeast Asia, according to the report. Title: UN Report: Drought, Hunger Threatens Human Health – Radio France Internationale
Content: PARIS (AFP) The United Nations has released a draft report that says a warming planet will have a major impact on human health, with hunger, drought and disease afflicting tens of millions of people for decades.  After more than a year of pandemics that have completely turned the world upside down, the forthcoming report of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) offers even more dire predictions of malnutrition, water scarcity and plague in the coming decades.  The report said that policy options such as the promotion of plant-based diets can limit these health consequences, but many things are still unavoidable in the short term.  Babies born today may face a variety of climate-related health threats before the age of 30, depending on how well humans manage carbon emissions and rising temperatures.  The 4,000 page draft, expected to be published next year, is the most complete report yet on the impact of climate change on the planet and species.  The report estimates that 80 million more people will be at risk of hunger by 2050 than today.  The report estimates that disruptions to the water cycle will reduce harvests of rain-fed staple crops in sub-Saharan Africa.  Up to 40% of India ’ s rice-producing areas are feared to be unsuitable for farming.  The report said that rising temperatures will not only affect crop yields, but also reduce nutritional value, such as rice, wheat, barley and potato protein content is expected to be reduced by 6% to 14%, which will increase the number of people at risk of protein deficiency by nearly 150 million.  Food prices are expected to rise by as much as a third in 2050 as climate change reduces crop yields and increases demand for biofuel crops and carbon dioxide-absorbing forests, increasing the number of low-income households facing chronic hunger by 183 million.  Across Asia and Africa, the number of undernourished and stunted children by the middle of this century will increase by 10 million, creating a new generation with better socio-economic development and lifelong health problems.  As with most of the impacts of climate change, the impact on human health varies from place to place, with 80 percent of the population at risk of hunger living in Africa and Southeast Asia, the report said.  Studies of freshwater supply, agriculture and sea-level rise suggest that between 30 and 140 million people will be displaced in Africa, Southeast Asia and Latin America by 2050.  © 2021 AFP

Title: Reduction of water resources of Kazakhstan by 25% is predicted by 2030
Content: Astana.  7 November.  KazTAG – The reduction of water resources in Kazakhstan by 25% is predicted by 2030, the press service of the UN Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) reports.  “Among the threats posed by climate change to Kazakhstan ’ s agricultural sector is water scarcity, which is projected to be reduced by 25% by 2030, putting additional strain on the sector and leading to even greater aridity, especially in the southern and central regions of Kazakhstan, ” FAO said on Wednesday.  Another expected impact of climate change in the organization called the drying of pastures and reduced access of livestock to water sources.  “Changes in weather cycles can also cause spring floods, torrential autumn rains and early frosts, leading to crop losses.  That is, strengthening the resilience of the agricultural sector to such phenomena through targeted investments that contribute to reducing vulnerability both within the country and in individual regions is an urgent task, ” the UN agricultural organization stressed.  FAO stressed that now the task of adapting to a changing climate is one of the key priorities in the world.  Climate change, including disruption of rain cycles, droughts, floods, and the spread of pests and diseases, according to the organization, both directly and indirectly affect agricultural productivity.  “Accelerating the adoption of climate technologies is a significant step towards addressing these challenges.  The use of modern climate technologies is a key element in the transition to more sustainable food production systems, ” said Nuno Santos, economist at the FAO Investment Centre.  In close cooperation with local governments, FAO and the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) organized the workshop to serve as a platform for dialogue among all stakeholders – the private sector, government agencies, research institutions, international organizations and civil society.  “All of them can play a role in supporting the implementation of climate technologies in Kazakhstan, ” the report said.  The participants of the seminar, according to FAO, noted the key trends in the implementation of climate technologies in the agri-food sector of Kazakhstan and focused on identifying problems and opportunities for private sector investment in modern agri-food technologies.  “The participants also shared their experience and made proposals to overcome difficulties and create a favorable climate for private investment.  The workshop also discussed possible areas for public support and collaboration with donors and international financial institutions to accelerate technology adoption, as strategic alliances and close collaboration among stakeholders are key to achieving the UN Sustainable Development Goals by 2030.

Title: Infographic Understanding Climate Change: Warmer weather not only harms human health, but agriculture and the economy have also paid the price
Content: David Nelles and Christian Serrer: Climate change has now directly or indirectly affected the lives of 7.5 billion people on the planet.  However, the impact of global warming varies from place to place, which means that people and people living together in different regions will also be affected to varying degrees.  In any case, one thing is certain: the continued warming of the climate will continue to bring all kinds of adverse effects to mankind.  Climate change can have many effects on human health, such as heat stress caused by high temperature, operating environment factors (including air temperature, humidity, wind speed and radiation heat) and clothing, and high temperature events, which can worsen heart, blood circulation and respiratory related diseases. Increase the mortality rate of these diseases.  On the other hand, high temperatures are conducive to the formation of ozone close to the ground, which has adverse effects on human health, such as may lead to decreased lung function.  Extreme weather events such as floods or storms are more frequent and can also bring more hidden risks to human health, such as injuries and even death in serious cases.  In addition, already polluted waters may increase the risk of infectious disease outbreaks due to heavy rainfall and flooding.  Another effect of climate change in Germany is the lengthening of the pollen season, which exacerbates the symptoms of respiratory diseases such as asthma or allergic rhinitis.  And such climatic conditions are more conducive to the growth and reproduction of allergenic plants, such as Ambrosia is a good example.  Photo Credit: Businessweek / Lisa Schwegler, Stefan Kraiss, and Janna Geisse Produced The 2010 increase in global deaths due to climate change A spreading vector of disease caused by climate change refers to organisms that can transmit pathogens from infected animals or humans to other animals or humans, such as ticks commonly known as ticks, or mosquitoes.  Climate change is changing the current environmental conditions in which pathogens are spread by vectors.  In recent decades, due to globalization and favorable climatic conditions, the Asian-native Aedes albopictus (also known as the Asian tiger mosquito) has reached parts of southern Europe.  In the near future, other areas of higher latitudes in Europe should also become suitable for mosquito activity due to climate change.  It is important to note that the white line mosquito spreads dengue fever and Chikungunya virus.  On the other hand, the high temperature must be maintained for a period of time before the virus can be spread through the infected mosquitoes, because the warm temperature allows the virus to successfully reproduce in the mosquitoes and then transmit the virus to humans when the mosquitoes bite.  Rising temperatures create favorable conditions for the spread of Aedes albopictus and shorten the propagation time of the virus in Aedes albopictus.  Combining globalization with the risks that come with it, such as the importation of foreign goods that could trap Aedes albopictus, or returning travelers infected with the virus, increases the risk of disease transmission.  Photo Credit: Businessweek / Lisa Schwegler, Stefan Kraiss, and Janna Geisse produce Climate change impacts on agriculture High temperatures, high levels of carbon dioxide in the air, changes in rainfall patterns, and associated changing weather parameters can affect plant growth.  When the temperature rises to the most appropriate growth temperature, the yield of a particular crop can be increased, but once the temperature exceeds this optimum value, the crop yield begins to decrease.  In the case of corn and soybeans, as long as the growth period is more than 30 ° C, it is not conducive to the development of these crops.  In addition, extreme weather, especially drought and high temperatures, as well as heavy rain, can negatively affect yields. Between 2000 and 2007 alone, droughts and high temperatures have reduced global cereal crops by about 6.2%.  When the concentration of carbon dioxide in the air increases, many plants respond quickly by reducing the amount of water released from the leaves and increasing photosynthesis.  In this way, there is enough water and nutrients to promote plant growth, which is known as the "CO2 fertilization effect" (CO2-Düngungseffekt).  There is debate as to how much this fertilization effect can offset the reduction in production in some areas due to changes in temperature and rainfall patterns.  In addition, increased carbon dioxide concentration in the air can promote plant growth, but it also means that the nutrient concentration in the plant will be relatively reduced.  If higher average temperatures lead to longer tillage periods, less cold damage and higher crop yields, then climate change has positive implications for higher latitudes, such as northern Europe.  In contrast, climate change is not necessarily a good thing for crop yields in tropical and subtropical regions.  Climate change comes with three different types of costs: First, the cost of damage, such as direct damage to real estate or public infrastructure caused by extreme weather events.  This is followed by adaptation costs, such as levees or ponds for flood control.  The third is the so-called avoidance costs, such as the costs of switching from fossil to renewable energy to limit future global warming.  Because it is not possible to have a clear and comprehensive picture of all the costs incurred, it is actually very difficult to calculate precise figures for the economic costs of climate change.  Therefore, the calculated cost can only depend on the assumptions made, and it is very difficult to accurately grasp the costs of such things, such as melted permafrost, so it is extremely difficult to analyze the chart below.  Photo Credit: Business Week Publishing / Produced by Lisa Schwegler, Stefan Kraiss, and Janna Geisse Because of these high levels of uncertainty, it is very difficult to know exactly what climate protection measures should be taken and how much it should be interfered with from a purely economic point of view.  If people want to limit warming to 1.5 ° C, they will have to pay a very high investment cost.  Compared to setting the temperature rise range at a maximum of 3.5 ° C, the investment cost, although significantly reduced, will result in higher damage costs.  Overall, the cost of limiting global warming should be much less than the cost of damage caused by an unrestricted rise in global temperatures.  It is worth noting that as the temperature rises, the risk of irreversible damage is also increased.  Photo Credit: Businessweek / Lisa Schwegler, Stefan Kraiss, and Janna Geisse conclude that climate change is not a distant vision of the future, and that it represents more than just melting icebergs and rising sea levels, which are already threatening many people and their livelihoods.  In addition, it also shows that the temperature rise observed since the beginning of the industrial era is mainly due to man-made greenhouse gas emissions.  Fortunately, there ’ s also some ironic good news: we have the opportunity to influence the future of the climate, and we ’ re not completely powerless against climate change!  Climate model simulations show that as long as humans reduce greenhouse gas emissions, it is expected to limit the development of global warming.  Photo Credit: Businessweek / Lisa Schwegler, Stefan Kraiss, and Janna Geisse produced a global average temperature forecast for greenhouse gas emissions, but since the United Nations Climate Conference (UN-Klimakonferenz) was first held in Berlin in 1995, global greenhouse gas emissions have risen by 50%, reaching a record high.  If human beings continue to produce large quantities of greenhouse gases, it is not impossible to imagine that global temperatures will rise by another 5 ° C by the end of the century.  Therefore, we must all be aware of our responsibility: how the future of the climate, and the extent to which the impact of global warming will worsen, is entirely in our hands! Title: Biologist has estimated the possibility of the disappearance of habitual products due to climate change
Content: Climate change can undoubtedly affect the crops and products of various crops.  However, this trend is likely to mean short-term problems.  Alexander Markov, Doctor of Biological Sciences, Head of the Department of Biological Evolution of the Biological Faculty of Lomonosov Moscow State University, told Zvezda.  According to him, despite the information that appeared in the media that climate change threatens the disappearance of most of the familiar products, this situation is not entirely true.  The reason is that in the case of a change in the usual climate, manufacturers will simply have to rebuild, which will take a certain time.  However, everyone ’ s favorite products will not disappear because of this.  “Climate change can affect the crops and products of various crops, plants, animals and so on.  If it gets warmer or colder, it will affect the productivity of the system.  In some regions it can be a positive impact, in others it can be negative.  In general, any climate change will cause short-term problems: something is changing, agricultural producers have adapted to certain conditions, but those have changed.  You will have to grow crops in other places.  These will be short-term problems for sure, ” Markov said.  The expert added that climate change could cause local problems with agricultural productivity in all regions.  But we can adapt to the changes.  “These are not fatal processes, ” he concluded.  Earlier in the media there was information that, according to scientists, climate change can supposedly lead to the disappearance of most of the usual human products - from potatoes to olive oil.  At the same time, British researchers are convinced that coffee can disappear, and by 2050 the territory suitable for its cultivation will be halved.
