Title: Sustainable development: why young people choose companies that work under this credo
Content: Sustainable development as a concept in its current form started 50 years ago.  It was in the 1970s that global structures such as the United Nations or the Club of Rome realized that man was actively influencing the planet.  In the 21st century, this resulted in the UN ’ s 17 Sustainable Development Goals.  What are these goals, why are they needed, what is the situation of humanity on Earth now and why we all should somehow become conscious and responsible for the future - in the material Delo.ua in the framework of the special project "Leaders of sustainable development".  As of 2019, there were 7.674 billion people living on planet Earth.  Today, according to TheWorldCount, there are 7.85 billion people.  The good news is that the rate of population growth is still decreasing, in the 1970s it was 2%, in 2019 it was 1.1%.  But it's still a lot.  According to the UN Department of Economic and Social Affairs, 8.323 billion people will live in the world in 2030, and 9.3 billion by 2050.  In 2100, there will be 11 billion people in the world.  The gross domestic product of the planet in 2019 amounted to 87.8 trillion US dollars.  Faceless numbers behind which lies human interaction with the physical world.  Remember the year 2019?  You ate, drank, traveled, bought things, lost things.  They left a carbon footprint.  According to the constantly updated consumption calculator, at the current level, we need 1.8 planet Earth.  Yes, almost twice as much as there is at the moment.  And that ’ s the average cut.  At the same time, we have one Earth.  It is a small, unremarkable planet in a galactic backwater.  We are trying to go into space and even think about going to Mars, but in reality there is only one hole in the orbit of the International Space Station.  And if anything happens on the planet, we really have nowhere to run.  For example, if you travel by car, at least twice a year fly to conditional Egypt, live in an apartment building, buy food brought by plane, you need 4.5 Earth.  At the same time, we have one Earth.  It is a small, unremarkable planet in a galactic backwater.  We are trying to go into space and even think about going to Mars, but in reality there is only one hole in the orbit of the International Space Station.  And if anything happens on the planet, we really have nowhere to run.  And it can happen.  Because behind every dollar of global GDP is energy and industry that meets the needs of the population.  We plow the land, destroy the forests, warm up the permafrost - and out comes the same carbon, which, in turn, leads to the greenhouse effect.  Which, in turn, causes climate change.  And this is not warming, as many people think, but an increase in the number of extremes.  Last year, Ukraine experienced fires in the Chernobyl zone, in the Zhytomyr region, in the Luhansk region.  It is seriously affected by desertification.  Kiev and Kiev region were covered by dust storms.  Already in 2021, the Ministry of Ecology said that pesticides, pharmaceuticals and heavy metals were detected in Dnipro.  Studies show that Ukrainian lands may lose their fertility.  Half of the country was flooded with rains and floods, in the second half the harvest was scorched by the summer heat.  Abnormally low rainfall drained the land.  All these are consequences of global climate change.  According to a study conducted by an international team of scientists from Switzerland, Germany and the Netherlands, since 2008 disasters caused by natural phenomena have led to the displacement of 288 million people (including evacuations).  Three times as many people have left as have been the result of wars, conflicts and violence.  About half of people are forced to leave their homes due to flooding.  Agricultural productivity is declining.  The University of Maryland, in collaboration with Cornell University and Stanford University, has for the first time quantified the anthropogenic impact of climate change on global agricultural productivity growth.  In a new study published in the journal Nature Climate Change, researchers show that global agricultural productivity has declined by 21% since 1961, which the researchers believe is equivalent to a total loss of productivity growth over the past 7 years.  "Our study suggests that climate and weather-related factors have already had a major impact on agricultural productivity," said Robert Chambers, a professor of agricultural economics and resources at the University of Maryland.  Thus, since 1961, regions such as Africa, Latin America and the Caribbean, which are in regions with warmer climates, have already experienced a slowdown of 26-34%.  The United States suffered less, with growth slowing by about 5-15%.  “Some people think of climate change as a distant issue that should concern future generations first.  But this does not take into account the fact that people have already changed the climate, — says Ariel Ortiz-Bobea, lead author of the study from Cornell University. — In general, our study shows that anthropogenic climate change already has a disproportionate impact on poorer countries that depend primarily on agriculture.  It seems that technological progress has not yet led to greater resilience to climate change. "  At the same time, regions suffering from water shortages, such as Jordan, are facing an exacerbation of this problem.  According to a Stanford University study, water depletion and population growth will halve Jordan ’ s per capita water consumption by the end of this century.  Low-income areas will be hardest hit: by 2100, 91% of households will receive less than 40 liters of water per day for 11 consecutive months of the year.  If society has strong levers of influence - guilds, fraternities, unions, cooperatives, associations - it is more stable.  If ordinary people are unable to influence what is happening, crises exacerbate inequality.  Has the Covid-19 pandemic helped the world?  Reduced inequality, reduced production?  Did humanity think about the future?  Perhaps, but a recent study by historian Bas van Bavel of the University of Utrecht and ecologist Martin Schaeffer of the University of Wageningent says that so far everything is not too good.  They looked at the impact of catastrophes — like the plague — on humanity as a whole and concluded that they could exacerbate inequality.  “In times of crisis, the rules are usually rewritten.  The most influential social groups and organizations can use this window of opportunity to adapt institutional rules, thereby shaping the long-term distribution of wealth.  Because most societies have historically been unequal, in most cases the result has been a further increase in imbalances, ” van Bavel says.  At the same time, if society has strong levers of influence - guilds, fraternities, trade unions, cooperatives, associations - it is more stable.  If ordinary people are unable to influence what is happening, crises exacerbate inequality.  In 2015, the UN, as the largest unifying structure of mankind, collected 17 goals that must be fulfilled by 2030.  This is not just a declaration, each has a clear roadmap and KPI indicators.  Here are the goals: 1.  Eradication of poverty 2.  Ending hunger 3.  Good health and well-being 4.  Quality education 5.  Gender equality 6.  Clean water and sanitation 7.  Cheap and clean energy 8.  Decent work and economic growth 9.  Industrialization, innovation and infrastructure 10.  Reducing inequality 11.  Sustainable cities and human settlements 12.  Responsible consumption and production 13.  Combating climate change 14.  Conservation of marine ecosystems 15.  Conservation of terrestrial ecosystems 16.  Peace, justice and effective institutions 17.  The answer to this question is quite obvious: so that as many people as possible on planet Earth a) survive b) can lead a comfortable life.  More and more people are becoming conscious consumers who care where the product they consume comes from, how it was made and whether environmental norms or human rights were violated in its production or in its advertising.  “Everyone has realized that sustainable development is not just a buzzword.  Everyone realized that society — especially the new generation — wants business to embody universal values.  It doesn't matter how much you make.  It is important what you do for the world, for me, for my children, for our common future, ” says Elena Zubareva, head of the Association of Sustainable Development Leaders.  Science confirms these words.  The University of Hiroshima conducted a study and found that young people are ready to sacrifice their salaries for the sake of saving humanity and the planet.  The results were published on January 31 in a special issue of the journal Clean Production, dedicated specifically to the achievement of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).  “Many people in the popular media or even in everyday conversations say that the younger generation is more socially conscious and has behaviors focused on achieving sustainable development goals, but the scientific evidence is limited, ” said Tomomi Yamane, a researcher at Hiroshima University.  And young people are willing to give their income to work in companies striving to achieve the SDGs. ”

Title: Climate change and water scarcity are top priorities.
Content: Assistant Professor of Water Engineering at the Faculty of Agriculture of Shahrekord University said: “The main priority of the authorities should be water shortage and climate change, so that water factories are moved to the seaside and agriculture in areas that are facing water shortage is limited. ”  He said: “It ’ s been a long time, it ’ s been a long time, it ’ s been a long time, it ’ s been a long time.  “When we talk about climate change, we mean meteorological parameters that have been measured over long periods of time, and these changes manifest themselves in either natural or artificial forms, which are caused by humans.  Nasr Esfahani said: “Various factors such as sunspots, changes in the earth ’ s crust, changes in vegetation or the movement of continents, or changes in ocean temperature naturally cause climate change.  “What has happened in the past year is that humans have caused an imbalance in meteorological parameters due to excessive consumption of natural resources, including oil, gas and fossil fuels, and by destroying natural resources such as forests and expanding factories and cities.  The university professor pointed out that the country is climatally located in a dry region, saying: "We should not expect the climate to change from dry to wet, because this is a very wrong expectation that some in the society suggest this."  He said: "Climate change has become very clear in the last 40 years, so we have to adapt to this situation that has been fluctuating and know that drought or drought fluctuations are part of the nature of the region's climate."  Nasr Isfahani said: "In this situation, climate change is occurring and extreme phenomena such as severe droughts, drought, heat and cold are increasing, there is no alternative but to adapt to them, for example, agricultural products can be used to prevent frostbite, to use resistant products.  Regarding water resources, he said: “At the same time as the climate change, the consumption of water resources has greatly expanded, especially in the last 50 years, when agriculture has been the center of development in the country. ”  The university professor said: "If we examine the rainfall parameter in more detail, we see that the average rainfall has not changed, but the extremes have changed a lot and these changes are significant, on the other hand, the effective rainfall has not changed and the ineffective rainfall has increased, which means that there is a shortage of water resources."  He said: "What has been observed is that, contrary to the rainfall parameter, changes in the temperature parameter, especially the minimum temperature, are highly effective and the trend of increasing the minimum temperature is observed in many stations in the country."  Nasr Esfahani pointed out that in mountainous areas the precipitation has changed from solid to liquid state, adding: "When there is snow in the region, because the snow is slowly melting and sinking into underground sources, it feeds them, on the other hand, the occurrence of rain brings water runoff, which feeds surface water instead of feeding groundwater resources."  He added that excessive consumption of water resources, expansion of the area under cultivation, non-observance of the cultivation pattern and the use of traditional methods for irrigation have led to the reduction of groundwater.  Assistant Professor of Water Engineering at Shahrekord University emphasized: "The authorities were aware of the current situation, but they did not think that the effects of climate change would be egregious and misrepresented, and today we face a fundamental problem, for example, if there was a shortage of water, it was solved by harvesting from underground water resources and we assigned this problem to the future."  He continued: “We have reached a point where groundwater resources are not the answer to the shortage of water, and this problem has become such that measures must be taken.  Nasr Esfahani said that for short-term purposes, water resources have not been considered because steel and water mills have been built in the country, which if this decision process continues, despite the lack of water resources, will still be built in the future.  “We should not expect that one day our country will be as abundant as Europe, because the lack of rainfall in our region has been caused by the rotation of the earth and the circulation of the atmosphere, so in addition to adapting to climate change, if there is to be a cost to this, it should be done today and we should not postpone those costs to the future, because we may face more limitations in the future. ”  The university professor noted that the main priority of the authorities should be water scarcity and climate change, so that water factories are moved to the seaside and agriculture is limited in areas with water scarcity.  End of message.

Title: UN Climate Report: Warming Causes Drought, Hunger Threatens Human Health - Technology
Content: A warming planet has a major impact on human health, with hunger, drought and disease afflicting tens of millions of people over decades, according to a draft report released by the United Nations today.  After more than a year of pandemics that have completely turned the world upside down, the forthcoming report of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) offers even more dire predictions of malnutrition, water scarcity and plague in the coming decades.  Policy choices such as the promotion of plant-based diets can limit these health consequences, but many will remain unavoidable in the short term, the report said.  Babies born today may face a variety of climate-related health threats before they reach the age of 30, depending on how well humans handle carbon emissions and rising temperatures, according to the report.  The 4,000-page draft report, expected to be released next year, is the most complete report yet on the impact of climate change on the planet and species.  The report estimates that 80 million more people are at risk of hunger by 2050 than today.  The report estimates that disruptions to the water cycle will reduce harvests of rain-fed staple crops in sub-Saharan Africa.  As many as 40% of India ’ s rice-producing areas are unsuitable for farming.  Rising temperatures not only affect crop yields, but also reduce nutritional values, such as rice, wheat, barley and potatoes, by 6% to 14%, the report said, adding that the number of people at risk of protein deficiency is nearly 150 million more than today.  Food prices are expected to rise by as much as a third in 2050 as climate change reduces crop yields and increases demand for biofuel crops and carbon dioxide-absorbing forests, increasing the number of low-income households facing chronic hunger by 183 million.  Across Asia and Africa, the number of undernourished and stunted children by the middle of the century will increase by 10 million, creating a new generation of better socioeconomic development, but lifelong health problems.  As with most climate change impacts, the impact on human health varies from place to place, with 80% of the population at risk of hunger living in Africa and Southeast Asia, according to the report.  According to the report, studies on freshwater supply, agriculture and sea level rise show that between 30 million and 140 million people will be displaced in Africa, Southeast Asia and Latin America by 2050.

Title: Reduction of water resources of Kazakhstan by 25% is predicted by 2030
Content: Astana.  7 November.  KazTAG – The reduction of water resources in Kazakhstan by 25% is predicted by 2030, the press service of the UN Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) reports.  “Among the threats posed by climate change to Kazakhstan ’ s agricultural sector is water scarcity, which is projected to be reduced by 25% by 2030, putting additional strain on the sector and leading to even greater aridity, especially in the southern and central regions of Kazakhstan, ” FAO said on Wednesday.  Another expected impact of climate change in the organization called the drying of pastures and reduced access of livestock to water sources.  “Changes in weather cycles can also cause spring floods, torrential autumn rains and early frosts, leading to crop losses.  That is, strengthening the resilience of the agricultural sector to such phenomena through targeted investments that contribute to reducing vulnerability both within the country and in individual regions is an urgent task, ” the UN agricultural organization stressed.  FAO stressed that now the task of adapting to a changing climate is one of the key priorities in the world.  Climate change, including disruption of rain cycles, droughts, floods, and the spread of pests and diseases, according to the organization, both directly and indirectly affect agricultural productivity.  “Accelerating the adoption of climate technologies is a significant step towards addressing these challenges.  The use of modern climate technologies is a key element in the transition to more sustainable food production systems, ” said Nuno Santos, economist at the FAO Investment Centre.  In close cooperation with local governments, FAO and the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) organized the workshop to serve as a platform for dialogue among all stakeholders – the private sector, government agencies, research institutions, international organizations and civil society.  “All of them can play a role in supporting the implementation of climate technologies in Kazakhstan, ” the report said.  The participants of the seminar, according to FAO, noted the key trends in the implementation of climate technologies in the agri-food sector of Kazakhstan and focused on identifying problems and opportunities for private sector investment in modern agri-food technologies.  “The participants also shared their experience and made proposals to overcome difficulties and create a favorable climate for private investment.  The workshop also discussed possible areas for public support and collaboration with donors and international financial institutions to accelerate technology adoption, as strategic alliances and close collaboration among stakeholders are key to achieving the UN Sustainable Development Goals by 2030.

Title: Infographic Understanding Climate Change: Warmer weather not only harms human health, but agriculture and the economy have also paid the price
Content: David Nelles and Christian Serrer: Climate change has now directly or indirectly affected the lives of 7.5 billion people on the planet.  However, the impact of global warming varies from place to place, which means that people and people living together in different regions will also be affected to varying degrees.  In any case, one thing is certain: the continued warming of the climate will continue to bring all kinds of adverse effects to mankind.  Climate change can have many effects on human health, such as heat stress caused by high temperature, operating environment factors (including air temperature, humidity, wind speed and radiation heat) and clothing, and high temperature events, which can worsen heart, blood circulation and respiratory related diseases. Increase the mortality rate of these diseases.  On the other hand, high temperatures are conducive to the formation of ozone close to the ground, which has adverse effects on human health, such as may lead to decreased lung function.  Extreme weather events such as floods or storms are more frequent and can also bring more hidden risks to human health, such as injuries and even death in serious cases.  In addition, already polluted waters may increase the risk of infectious disease outbreaks due to heavy rainfall and flooding.  Another effect of climate change in Germany is the lengthening of the pollen season, which exacerbates the symptoms of respiratory diseases such as asthma or allergic rhinitis.  And such climatic conditions are more conducive to the growth and reproduction of allergenic plants, such as Ambrosia is a good example.  Photo Credit: Businessweek / Lisa Schwegler, Stefan Kraiss, and Janna Geisse Produced The 2010 increase in global deaths due to climate change A spreading vector of disease caused by climate change refers to organisms that can transmit pathogens from infected animals or humans to other animals or humans, such as ticks commonly known as ticks, or mosquitoes.  Climate change is changing the current environmental conditions in which pathogens are spread by vectors.  In recent decades, due to globalization and favorable climatic conditions, the Asian-native Aedes albopictus (also known as the Asian tiger mosquito) has reached parts of southern Europe.  In the near future, other areas of higher latitudes in Europe should also become suitable for mosquito activity due to climate change.  It is important to note that the white line mosquito spreads dengue fever and Chikungunya virus.  On the other hand, the high temperature must be maintained for a period of time before the virus can be spread through the infected mosquitoes, because the warm temperature allows the virus to successfully reproduce in the mosquitoes and then transmit the virus to humans when the mosquitoes bite.  Rising temperatures create favorable conditions for the spread of Aedes albopictus and shorten the propagation time of the virus in Aedes albopictus.  Combining globalization with the risks that come with it, such as the importation of foreign goods that could trap Aedes albopictus, or returning travelers infected with the virus, increases the risk of disease transmission.  Photo Credit: Businessweek / Lisa Schwegler, Stefan Kraiss, and Janna Geisse produce Climate change impacts on agriculture High temperatures, high levels of carbon dioxide in the air, changes in rainfall patterns, and associated changing weather parameters can affect plant growth.  When the temperature rises to the most appropriate growth temperature, the yield of a particular crop can be increased, but once the temperature exceeds this optimum value, the crop yield begins to decrease.  In the case of corn and soybeans, as long as the growth period is more than 30 ° C, it is not conducive to the development of these crops.  In addition, extreme weather, especially drought and high temperatures, as well as heavy rain, can negatively affect yields. Between 2000 and 2007 alone, droughts and high temperatures have reduced global cereal crops by about 6.2%.  When the concentration of carbon dioxide in the air increases, many plants respond quickly by reducing the amount of water released from the leaves and increasing photosynthesis.  In this way, there is enough water and nutrients to promote plant growth, which is known as the "CO2 fertilization effect" (CO2-Düngungseffekt).  There is debate as to how much this fertilization effect can offset the reduction in production in some areas due to changes in temperature and rainfall patterns.  In addition, increased carbon dioxide concentration in the air can promote plant growth, but it also means that the nutrient concentration in the plant will be relatively reduced.  If higher average temperatures lead to longer tillage periods, less cold damage and higher crop yields, then climate change has positive implications for higher latitudes, such as northern Europe.  In contrast, climate change is not necessarily a good thing for crop yields in tropical and subtropical regions.  Climate change comes with three different types of costs: First, the cost of damage, such as direct damage to real estate or public infrastructure caused by extreme weather events.  This is followed by adaptation costs, such as levees or ponds for flood control.  The third is the so-called avoidance costs, such as the costs of switching from fossil to renewable energy to limit future global warming.  Because it is not possible to have a clear and comprehensive picture of all the costs incurred, it is actually very difficult to calculate precise figures for the economic costs of climate change. If people want to limit warming to 1.5 ° C, they will have to pay a very high investment cost.  Compared to setting the temperature rise range at a maximum of 3.5 ° C, the investment cost, although significantly reduced, will result in higher damage costs.  Overall, the cost of limiting global warming should be much less than the cost of damage caused by an unrestricted rise in global temperatures.  It is worth noting that as the temperature rises, the risk of irreversible damage is also increased. Title: Sustainable development: why young people choose companies that work under this credo
Content: Sustainable development as a concept in its current form started 50 years ago.  It was in the 1970s that global structures such as the United Nations or the Club of Rome realized that man was actively influencing the planet.  In the 21st century, this resulted in the UN ’ s 17 Sustainable Development Goals.  What are these goals, why are they needed, what is the situation of humanity on Earth now and why we all should somehow become conscious and responsible for the future - in the material Delo.ua in the framework of the special project "Leaders of sustainable development".  As of 2019, there were 7.674 billion people living on planet Earth.  Today, according to TheWorldCount, there are 7.85 billion people.  The good news is that the rate of population growth is still decreasing, in the 1970s it was 2%, in 2019 it was 1.1%.  But it's still a lot.  According to the UN Department of Economic and Social Affairs, 8.323 billion people will live in the world in 2030, and 9.3 billion by 2050.  In 2100, there will be 11 billion people in the world.  The gross domestic product of the planet in 2019 amounted to 87.8 trillion US dollars.  Faceless numbers behind which lies human interaction with the physical world.  Remember the year 2019?  You ate, drank, traveled, bought things, lost things.  They left a carbon footprint.  According to the constantly updated consumption calculator, at the current level, we need 1.8 planet Earth.  Yes, almost twice as much as there is at the moment.  And that ’ s the average cut.  At the same time, we have one Earth.  It is a small, unremarkable planet in a galactic backwater.  We are trying to go into space and even think about going to Mars, but in reality there is only one hole in the orbit of the International Space Station.  And if anything happens on the planet, we really have nowhere to run.  For example, if you travel by car, at least twice a year fly to conditional Egypt, live in an apartment building, buy food brought by plane, you need 4.5 Earth.  At the same time, we have one Earth.  It is a small, unremarkable planet in a galactic backwater.  We are trying to go into space and even think about going to Mars, but in reality there is only one hole in the orbit of the International Space Station.  And if anything happens on the planet, we really have nowhere to run.  And it can happen.  Because behind every dollar of global GDP is energy and industry that meets the needs of the population.  We plow the land, destroy the forests, warm up the permafrost - and out comes the same carbon, which, in turn, leads to the greenhouse effect.  Which, in turn, causes climate change.  And this is not warming, as many people think, but an increase in the number of extremes.  Last year, Ukraine experienced fires in the Chernobyl zone, in the Zhytomyr region, in the Luhansk region.  It is seriously affected by desertification.  Kiev and Kiev region were covered by dust storms.  Already in 2021, the Ministry of Ecology said that pesticides, pharmaceuticals and heavy metals were detected in Dnipro.  Studies show that Ukrainian lands may lose their fertility.  Half of the country was flooded with rains and floods, in the second half the harvest was scorched by the summer heat.  Abnormally low rainfall drained the land.  All these are consequences of global climate change.  According to a study conducted by an international team of scientists from Switzerland, Germany and the Netherlands, since 2008 disasters caused by natural phenomena have led to the displacement of 288 million people (including evacuations).  Three times as many people have left as have been the result of wars, conflicts and violence.  About half of people are forced to leave their homes due to flooding.  Agricultural productivity is declining.  The University of Maryland, in collaboration with Cornell University and Stanford University, has for the first time quantified the anthropogenic impact of climate change on global agricultural productivity growth.  In a new study published in the journal Nature Climate Change, researchers show that global agricultural productivity has declined by 21% since 1961, which the researchers believe is equivalent to a total loss of productivity growth over the past 7 years.  "Our study suggests that climate and weather-related factors have already had a major impact on agricultural productivity," said Robert Chambers, a professor of agricultural economics and resources at the University of Maryland.  Thus, since 1961, regions such as Africa, Latin America and the Caribbean, which are in regions with warmer climates, have already experienced a slowdown of 26-34%.  The United States suffered less, with growth slowing by about 5-15%.  “Some people think of climate change as a distant issue that should concern future generations first.  But this does not take into account the fact that people have already changed the climate, — says Ariel Ortiz-Bobea, lead author of the study from Cornell University. — In general, our study shows that anthropogenic climate change already has a disproportionate impact on poorer countries that depend primarily on agriculture.  It seems that technological progress has not yet led to greater resilience to climate change. "  At the same time, regions suffering from water shortages, such as Jordan, are facing an exacerbation of this problem.  According to a Stanford University study, water depletion and population growth will halve Jordan ’ s per capita water consumption by the end of this century.  Low-income areas will be hardest hit: by 2100, 91% of households will receive less than 40 liters of water per day for 11 consecutive months of the year. Title: Climate change and water scarcity are top priorities.
Content: Assistant Professor of Water Engineering at the Faculty of Agriculture of Shahrekord University said: “The main priority of the authorities should be water shortage and climate change, so that water factories are moved to the seaside and agriculture in areas that are facing water shortage is limited. ”  He said: “It ’ s been a long time, it ’ s been a long time, it ’ s been a long time, it ’ s been a long time.  “When we talk about climate change, we mean meteorological parameters that have been measured over long periods of time, and these changes manifest themselves in either natural or artificial forms, which are caused by humans.  Nasr Esfahani said: “Various factors such as sunspots, changes in the earth ’ s crust, changes in vegetation or the movement of continents, or changes in ocean temperature naturally cause climate change.  “What has happened in the past year is that humans have caused an imbalance in meteorological parameters due to excessive consumption of natural resources, including oil, gas and fossil fuels, and by destroying natural resources such as forests and expanding factories and cities.  The university professor pointed out that the country is climatally located in a dry region, saying: "We should not expect the climate to change from dry to wet, because this is a very wrong expectation that some in the society suggest this."  He said: "Climate change has become very clear in the last 40 years, so we have to adapt to this situation that has been fluctuating and know that drought or drought fluctuations are part of the nature of the region's climate."  Nasr Isfahani said: "In this situation, climate change is occurring and extreme phenomena such as severe droughts, drought, heat and cold are increasing, there is no alternative but to adapt to them, for example, agricultural products can be used to prevent frostbite, to use resistant products.  Regarding water resources, he said: “At the same time as the climate change, the consumption of water resources has greatly expanded, especially in the last 50 years, when agriculture has been the center of development in the country. ”  The university professor said: "If we examine the rainfall parameter in more detail, we see that the average rainfall has not changed, but the extremes have changed a lot and these changes are significant, on the other hand, the effective rainfall has not changed and the ineffective rainfall has increased, which means that there is a shortage of water resources."  He said: "What has been observed is that, contrary to the rainfall parameter, changes in the temperature parameter, especially the minimum temperature, are highly effective and the trend of increasing the minimum temperature is observed in many stations in the country."  Nasr Esfahani pointed out that in mountainous areas the precipitation has changed from solid to liquid state, adding: "When there is snow in the region, because the snow is slowly melting and sinking into underground sources, it feeds them, on the other hand, the occurrence of rain brings water runoff, which feeds surface water instead of feeding groundwater resources."  He added that excessive consumption of water resources, expansion of the area under cultivation, non-observance of the cultivation pattern and the use of traditional methods for irrigation have led to the reduction of groundwater.  Assistant Professor of Water Engineering at Shahrekord University emphasized: "The authorities were aware of the current situation, but they did not think that the effects of climate change would be egregious and misrepresented, and today we face a fundamental problem, for example, if there was a shortage of water, it was solved by harvesting from underground water resources and we assigned this problem to the future."  He continued: “We have reached a point where groundwater resources are not the answer to the shortage of water, and this problem has become such that measures must be taken.  Nasr Esfahani said that for short-term purposes, water resources have not been considered because steel and water mills have been built in the country, which if this decision process continues, despite the lack of water resources, will still be built in the future.  “We should not expect that one day our country will be as abundant as Europe, because the lack of rainfall in our region has been caused by the rotation of the earth and the circulation of the atmosphere, so in addition to adapting to climate change, if there is to be a cost to this, it should be done today and we should not postpone those costs to the future, because we may face more limitations in the future. ”  The university professor noted that the main priority of the authorities should be water scarcity and climate change, so that water factories are moved to the seaside and agriculture is limited in areas with water scarcity. background: I work for The United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR). I have been tasked to find ways to stop refugees from moving from France to England through the English Channel by small unsafe boats.
title: English Channel Refugees Drowning

passages.title: Drowned refugees in the Channel are Iranians.
passages.passage: A woman and a man who died with their three children while trying to reach Britain are from the village of Glynne.  The website also published the names and photos of the deceased.  French authorities on Tuesday confirmed the capsizing of a small boat carrying asylum seekers and the death of four people on board in the English Channel.  The third child of the Kurdish family is missing.  A total of 27 people were on the way.  A number of survivors are being treated in the hospital.  The rescue operation involved several coast guard boats and a Belgian army helicopter.  British Prime Minister Boris Johnson offered his condolences to the survivors.  British Home Secretary Priti Patel expressed sympathy for the victims and said she was very sorry to hear the news.  Patel said the incident once again highlighted the dangers of crossing the canal.  He promised to do everything in his power to stop traffickers from exploiting refugees in need.  The English Channel (English Channel) is a canal in northern France and southern Britain that connects the Atlantic Ocean to the North Sea.  According to data from PA Media, more than 7,400 people reached the UK via the English Channel in small boats this year, nearly four times more than in 2019.  This year ’ s “record ” was set with the arrival of 416 refugees on September 2.  Official statistics show that from June 2019 to June 2020, more than 3,400 people who applied for asylum are under the age of 17.  Of these, nearly 2,800 were unaccompanied children.  The British government can return refugees arriving from France under the Dublin Accords.  According to the treaty, asylum seekers who have entered Europe are only allowed to apply for asylum at their place of entry on European soil.

passages.title: A repeat of the nightmare of 2015. Europe is facing a new migration crisis
passages.passage: https: / / ria.ru / 20210525 / migratsiya-1733716124.html A repeat of the nightmare of 2015.  Europe is facing a new migration crisis, a repeat of the nightmare of 2015.  Europe is waiting for a new migration crisis - RIA Novosti, 25.05.2021 A repeat of the nightmare of 2015.  Europe is once again on the brink of a migration crisis.  And this is not yet the summer, which traditionally accounts for the peak of the wave of illegal migration from countries...  RIA Novosti, 25.05.2021 2021-05-25T08: 00 2021-05-25T08: 00 2021-05-25T08: 02 migrants refugees europe authors / html / head / meta [@ name = 'og: title'] / @ content / html / head / meta [@ name = 'og: description'] / @ content https: / / cdn.com 24.img.ria.ru / images / 07e5 / 05 / 18 / 1733713287 _ 0: 153: 1920: 1233 _ 1920x0 _ 80 _ 0 _ 85ca65dc729db44d8073637ad5013c74.jpg Europe is again on the verge of a migration crisis.  And this is not yet the summer, which traditionally accounts for the peak of the wave of illegal migration from Asia and Africa.Now in the center of attention is Ceuta, a Spanish enclave in North Africa, where thousands of illegal refugees from Morocco rushed.  The refugee crisis in Ceuta and Melilla (another Spanish port in Africa) is largely the result of the artificial escalation of relations between Spain and Morocco.  According to many observers, Rabat decided to take revenge on Madrid for the assistance recently provided to the Polisario Front (which for many years has been fighting for the independence of Western Sahara from Morocco).  The revenge was the actual inaction of the border guards of this country, who turned a blind eye to the crowds of migrants breaking into Ceuta.  According to The Economist magazine, in this way King Mohammed VI of Morocco “made migration a weapon ” .But in fact, the sharp influx of refugees from Africa began not only in the Spanish enclaves.  Again, a series of flimsy ships illegally transporting Africans (mainly Libyans) from Tunisia to the Italian island of Lampedusa.  Last week, 1,200 people were transferred there during 12 hours of good weather alone.  And even despite the weather, accidents were recorded: 73 refugees from Bangladesh almost drowned trying to reach the cherished island.  How long it took, no one can say.  According to the Italian Interior Ministry, 4,290 migrants reached the country ’ s shores in the first three weeks of May.  While for the whole of May last year, their number was 1654 people.  The flow of illegal refugees is also increasing between the EU and Britain.  Since January, more than three thousand people have crossed the English Channel.  And over the same period last year, this figure was 1,400 refugees – more than double the growth.  Just the other day, the Belgian coast guard rescued a sinking ship on which 49 migrants, mostly Vietnamese, tried to cross the strait.  Based on the above facts and statistics, we can safely assume that the migration crisis will return to the European agenda in the foreseeable future.  However, the numbers are not as catastrophic as they were in 2015, when Europe was literally drowned by a flood of refugees.  And the increase compared to last year is easily explained by the fact that in 2020, many people in Asia and Africa gave up their intentions to go to pandemics in Europe.  In addition, the result of the shift of public attention from the problem of migration to the fight against the covid was a noticeable decrease in the ratings of a number of parties advocating strict measures to limit the influx of immigrants (in the Western media, these political organizations are usually indiscriminately called ultra-right, even despite the rather liberal economic program of many of them).  It is quite logical that now, with the rapid return of migration problems to the agenda, many publications have sounded the alarm in connection with the imminent growth of the popularity of these political forces.  Almost all analysts agree that the crisis around Ceuta, which has not descended from the front pages of the Spanish press for several days, will significantly strengthen the anti-Islamic party Vox (Voice).  Even before the current crisis, it actively dispersed the fears of the enclave residents in connection with the influx of poor Africans.  And in the end, it won the first place in the parliamentary elections of 2019, receiving more than 35 percent of the vote – and this is in a city where 40 percent of the population is Muslim.  It would be strange if the Vox party did not now take advantage of the crisis to increase its popularity in Ceuta.  For example, a local cell of the party is publicizing protests against the fact that African migrants entering the Spanish enclave receive coronavirus vaccinations, while Spanish citizens living there wait months for their turn.  This is confirmed by events in the regional parliament of Andalusia, where after the 2018 elections, for the first time in history, the People ’ s Party took the first place and was able to form a minority government.  Until last week, it relied solely on the informal support of Vox MPs.  However, on Thursday, they announced the termination of cooperation with the senior partner in connection with the fact that the authorities of the region agreed to accept 13 minor refugees who infiltrated Ceuta.  This could lead to the fall of the regional government and early elections.  That is why the People ’ s Party is forced to show more and more rigidity in the migration issue, causing panic in the European liberal media.Even more worrying in the mainstream is the electoral situation in Italy.  After the 2015 crisis, the League party, led by Matteo Salvini, has been the consistent leader of the polls there.  Having proved himself a tough fighter against illegal migration as the Minister of Internal Affairs, he increased the leadership of his party to record levels.  At the peak of popularity in the summer of 2019, the League ’ s figures were approaching 40 percent, which gave it hope even for the formation of its government.  Based on these calculations, Salvini provoked a government crisis in order to hold early elections, but was outplayed by opponents.  Since last year, there has been a drop in the ratings of this political force, whose supporters cannot forgive the support it expressed for the technocratic government of Mario Draghi.  Liberals can breathe freely.  But the fact is that the ratings of the League, which is still in the first place in the polls, are moving on opposite courses with the rapidly growing indicators of the even more right-wing and even more anti-migrant party “Brothers of Italy ”.  According to some polls, she already came in second place after the League, behind that couple of percent.  Three years ago, its ratings fluctuated around three to four percent, and now confidently approaching 20.  If elections were held now, these two forces, with the support of Silvio Berlusconi ’ s Forward Italy party, could well form a majority government.  They do not hide their ideological continuity from the far-right Italian social movement, which was created in 1946 by former supporters of Benito Mussolini.  This legacy is clearly indicated by the logo of the party, which includes the former symbol of ISD.The growth of the popularity of the "Brothers" will contribute to the charisma of the head of the party Georgia Meloni ("Sisters of Italy", as it was nicknamed by the press) - she last year surpassed in the approval ratings of the leader of the "League", becoming the second most popular politician in the country after the current prime minister.  There is no doubt that in the event of an aggravation of the migration crisis, the League and Brothers will be able to get additional votes to their already serious ratings.  Trends in the first months of the year show that the threat of the covid is no longer deterring refugees seeking to Europe.  And this means that the nightmare of 2015 may repeat itself — and the popularity of far-right, anti-migrant, anti-Islamic, Eurosceptic parties will again sharply rise. passages.title: Four refugees, including two children, drowned in the English Channel.
passages.passage: Four asylum-seekers, including two children, drowned in the English Channel (Reuters) Photo source: A rescue operation has been going on for hours by French boats since French authorities announced the deaths of two children and a man and woman who were trying to cross the English Channel to reach Britain.  A boat carrying refugees has sunk across the English Channel between France and Britain.  The prosecutor of the French city of Dunkirk has opened an investigation into the cause of the sinking of the ship.  These people are said to be Iranian.  A massive rescue operation has been under way for hours, which crashed near the northern French city of Dunkirk.  According to French authorities, two children aged 5 and 8 and a man and woman died.  The other 14 were taken to hospitals in the port of Calais and the French city of Dunkirk.  The English Channel, between France and Britain, is one of the world ’ s busiest waterways, and it can be dangerous to cross by small vessels, especially in winter when the sea is stormy.  Another disaster came after the British Meteorological Office warned of bad weather and strong winds in the Channel region.  Natalie Alpeik, MP for the Dover region in the British Parliament, said: “It ’ s terrible that there ’ s been another disaster on the canal.  Human traffickers have no respect for human life: "A sailboat accidentally encountered a ship and alerted French authorities of the incident.  Four French ships, a Belgian helicopter and a French fishing vessel were involved in the rescue.  Since the beginning of the year, more than 7,400 asylum seekers have arrived in Britain by sea in small boats.  While there are still two months left until the end of 2020, that number is 1,825 more than in 2019.  The survivors were taken by helicopter to hospitals in the port of Calais and the northern French city of Dunkirk on Thursday, August 6, and a total of 235 migrants, including several pregnant women, crossed the English Channel from Europe to the southern coast of Britain.  This is the highest recorded number of illegal immigrants arriving in the region in a single day.  About ten days ago, Home Secretary Priti Patel announced the “most significant revision ” of the country ’ s asylum system in a decade.

passages.passage: As part of an investigation conducted by local prosecutors, the provincial gendarmerie command, the Turkish Coast Guard team and the national intelligence service initiated a joint operation and caught the boat just as it was about to leave Merdivenli Bay in the Urla area.  Turkish security forces rescued 109 Afghan and Iranian asylum seekers on the boat, including a pregnant woman and children.  Four people were arrested on suspicion of organizing illegal transportation.  Asylum seekers were taken to the Provincial Directorate of Migration after medical checks and routine procedures.  According to the agency ’ s sources, a malfunction of the boat ’ s engine was discovered, which jeopardized the “journey ” in case of bad weather conditions. passages.title: Iranian Refugees Steal Fishing Boat to British Coast
passages.passage: Reports say 17 Iranian migrants made their way to British shores early Tuesday after hijacking a French fishing boat and crossing the English Channel, but were stopped by coast guard forces.  British officials have confirmed that the 17 migrants, including three children, were able to reach British shores by hijacking a 12-meter fishing boat near the French port of Calais early Tuesday.  French naval officials described the migrants ’ actions as “unprecedented ” and said they had previously tried to reach Britain in small boats, but in most cases failed.  The Home Office said in a statement that the group of migrants stopped arriving in Dover.  "They are 14 men and three children and all have declared themselves Iranian."  A Home Office spokeswoman said their asylum applications were being investigated and that three children had been handed over to the social services.  The report also said that three other small boats were stopped at Kent by the British Coast Guard on Wednesday, possibly from Iran.  According to the BBC, the passengers of one of the small boats were "seven men, a woman and a small child" and 10 other men were found in another boat.  According to the report, the British Coast Guard first noticed at 4: 30 that the passengers of a boat in the southwest of the shipping lane were in trouble and had gone to the aid of the refugees.  The second boat was found at 9: 00.  The report said five people on another boat were rescued a few miles off the coast of Ramsgate.  AFP says thousands of migrants from the Middle East and Africa are trying to reach Britain's shores.  The coastal city of Calais has the shortest water route between France and Britain, and since the destruction of the so-called "Jungle" camp, many Calais refugees have stepped up their efforts to reach Britain.

passages.title: Is it going to be harder for Britain to get asylum?
passages.passage: Will it be harder to get asylum in Britain?  Journalist Kianoosh Bustani An hour ago image source, Getty Images, a refugee boat in the south of the United Kingdom On Thursday, April 25, British Interior Minister Priti Patel unveiled in the House of Commons a plan that will soon be implemented and the future of asylum in the United Kingdom will undergo a serious and irreversible transformation.  Ms Patel said: “For the first time, asylum claims in the UK will be processed based on the route migrants took to reach the country.  Boris Johnson ’ s interior minister refers to migrants who reach northern France via the Central European or Spanish route and then arrive on small boats off the southern coast of England.  Last year, 8,000 refugees arrived in the UK via smugglers' boats, crossing the dangerous waters of the English Channel or English Channel.  Iranians are at the forefront of these travelers in terms of the number of refugees.  A journey that is not safe and in some cases ends up costing the lives of refugees.  Ms Patel, referring to international gangs of human trafficking, said: "Sufficient tolerance".  The Home Secretary pointed to the determination of the British government to destroy these gangs.  "The British government believes that human trafficking gangs are the same gangs that are involved in the trafficking of arms and drugs."  Ms Patel called them "organised and dangerous gangs" that take advantage of refugees trying to reach the UK.  The UK government considers its new asylum application process “fairer and quicker ”.  The Labour Party, the official government opposition in the British parliament, has called the plan lacking human sentiment and unable to resolve the issue.  Under the new scheme, people who enter the UK via routes deemed illegal by the UK government will not be given the same rights as those who enter the UK via ‘ authorised ’ routes.  The British government says the new plan will create “safe and legal pathways ” to seek asylum in the country.  The Home Office accuses many migrants arriving in the UK of using EU territory to reach the UK ’ s shores.  Interior Minister Preeti Patel made it clear in Parliament on Thursday that “if you ’ re going to enter the UK illegally through a safe country where you can apply for asylum, it ’ s clear that you ’ re not trying to escape danger.  “Contrary to the international community ’ s stated goals for asylum, you have only chosen the UK as your preferred destination. ”  Last year, news that refugees arriving by sea on the UK coast could be transferred to Ascension Island, a remote location in the South Atlantic, drew criticism from British charities and human rights organisations.  The plan, which his critics said was reminiscent of the relocation of refugees to remote Australian islands and "difficult living conditions" for asylum seekers in those areas.  The possibility of such a return to the Home Office has drawn criticism from the Conservative government.  Mike Anderson, executive director of the British Red Cross, said sending refugees to remote locations was “ineffective in solving the refugee problem. ”  Anderson says, “Such a plan ignores the root cause of the refugee influx. ”  He added: “The government ’ s plan will undoubtedly lead to unfortunate human consequences. ”  The source, Getty Images, has also faced criticism from political parties.  Nick Thomas Simond, Labour ’ s shadow cabinet interior minister, called Priti Patel ’ s remarks “absurd ” and a sign of“ the government ’ s lack of control over the refugee situation and lack any compassion. ”  In addition to the official opposition, the Liberal Democratic parliamentary party has joined the ranks of opponents of the new asylum plan.  Elder Carmichael, the party's spokesman for state affairs, called the plan ineffective and inhumane.  Mr Carmichael said: "The government should instead think of a plan for refugees who have been waiting more than six months to process their application."  In the face of all this criticism, the government considers changing the asylum procedure as the only way to avoid risking the lives of people who consider the sea route to be the best way to reach Britain.  With the end of the Brexit transition period in December 2020, the British government lost the right to access the EU ’ s integrated asylum rules, known as the Dublin Regulation.  According to these rules, the state that is obliged to process the asylum application is determined.  These rules allow union governments to ask another member to take responsibility for handling an asylum application or, in some cases, repatriation of an asylum seeker.  The general purpose of these regulations is to ease the burden of some countries and prevent rework at the EU level.  With the end of Britain ’ s membership in the European Union, the Conservative government sought to replace it with a similar deal, which was strongly opposed by the European Union.  The plan was to return all refugees arriving in the UK from a third country to EU countries.  The plan, which Brussels has called “unbalanced and unprofitable ” for the EU, has been rejected.  Is Britain a good destination for refugees?  According to the United Nations Refugee Agency, 79 million people are currently displaced from their homes.  Of these, 26 million are refugees.  Asylum seekers are people who leave their country in the hope of finding a safe environment for themselves and their families.  According to data from the Office of National Statistics, nearly 29,000 people applied for asylum in the UK last year, including more than 5,000 children.  More than 2,000 children arrived in the UK alone and without their parents.  Among them, Iran, with 4,000 refugees, is at the top of the countries seeking asylum.  This makes up 12% of all asylum seekers in the UK.  On average, more than half of Iranian asylum seekers received asylum in the first stage.  In addition to those seeking asylum on UK soil for the first time, nearly 6,000 asylum seekers who arrived in the UK years before Iran are still waiting to be resettled.  According to available information, 21% of the applicants received a negative response from the Home Office.  Iraq, Albania, Eritrea, Sudan and Syria are next in the rankings.  According to previous Home Office regulations, those entering the UK via water can apply for asylum on British soil.  In order to receive the right to asylum, people had to prove that they would be persecuted if they returned to their home country.  Racial, religious, sexual and gender discrimination or suppression of freedom of expression and opinion are the main reasons why asylum seekers seek asylum in the UK.

passages.title: 39 'Iranian' refugees detained on Britain's southeast coast
passages.passage: Sean Gallup / Getty Images Image caption One of the boats normally used by asylum seekers to cross the Channel to the UK, four boats carrying 39 Iranian refugees were taken off Sunday, November 17, at separate events off Britain's southeast coast.  The British Interior Ministry confirmed that all of the asylum seekers identified themselves as “Iranian ”.  The first boat, which had nine people on board, took off at 4: 40 a.m. yesterday, while the second, with five people on board, reached the British coast at around 6 a.m.  According to the Coast Guard and Kent County Police, a boat with 11 people on board was seized at around 7 a.m. and a half hour later another boat with 14 people was taken off the coast of the UK.  As soon as they received a message of help from the boats, rescue helicopters, as well as rescue boats from the ports of Dover, Dunness and Hastings, as well as two coast guard vessels, took action to rescue the passengers.  A Home Office spokesman said: "Crossing the canal by these small boats is extremely dangerous.  For those who have gone through such a journey, their lives and their loved ones are at risk. ”  According to the British Home Office, over the past two years Iranian citizens have applied for asylum more than any other country in the UK.  In 2017, about 9% of all 26,350 asylum applications were submitted by Iranians.  In November last year there was a significant increase in the number of asylum seekers trying to cross the English Channel to Britain, with the Home Secretary calling the issue a "serious incident" and calling for the French government to work together to resolve the issue.  Due to the increasing number of migrants and asylum seekers arriving on the east coast of the UK via the sea and the English Channel, the British Coast Guard has announced an increase in staff.

passages.title: Brexit is on the verge of a surge in the number of people crossing the sea to test British border controls
passages.passage: Image copyright Susan Pilcher Image caption On New Year's Eve 2019, 12 stowaways arrived in the UK on a small rubber dinghy, including a 10-year-old child.  British Border Agency agents inspect what they have discarded.  Soon after Brexit, a large number of stowaways in small rubber dinghies flooded from the European continent to England.  At the request of the Home Secretary, the Royal Navy and the Air Force sent aircraft and warships to help resolve the crisis.  Once the formal Brexit, both Britain and the EU will no longer be bound by the Dublin Agreement, which originally defined refugee ownership, but the UK may find it difficult to repatriate any influx of migrants to the EU.  The 2019 New Year holiday has been a rough ride for Home Secretary David Javid: he ended his holiday in South Africa early and rushed back to London to discuss the crisis of stowaways arriving on British shores by boat from the sea.  The UK plans to leave the EU by the end of March 2019.  The BBC ’ s investigation found that the group tricked refugees who had arrived in the Calais region of France to “sell tickets for the last chance to sneak into the UK in front of the UK ’ s closed border gates ”.  Stowaways who board a small rubber dinghy to get to Britain pay a fee of £6,000.  They rode in small rubber dinghies that the British border radar could not see.  The shortest distance from Calais, France, to the British coast in the English Channel is only 33.3 kilometers, so how many people come by boat from mainland Europe?  No one knows the exact number.  However, on New Year ’ s Eve 2019, the number of illegal immigrants suddenly increased significantly.  Why in the coldest, the English Channel wind and high waves when risking life and death to smuggle people? The reason is still related to Brexit!  Image copyright @ premarmanche Image caption Britain and France have stepped up efforts to crack down on smuggling across the Channel.  A small boat was stopped off the coast of France.  Under the Dublin Agreement, refugees arriving in the EU must be registered in the country they first arrive in.  Although they are all under the EU agreement, the treatment and even development prospects of refugees vary from country to country.  Britain has begun to worry that once Britain leaves the EU, there will be no reason for Britain to return refugees from the continent to their original EU countries, whether France, Spain, the Netherlands or other EU countries, according to the principle of first arrival.  After urgent consultations, the British Home Secretary ordered that the two ships involved in the search and rescue project in the Mediterranean Sea be sent back to the English Channel to intercept the smugglers along with the border ships already patrolling the Channel.  But the Home Office is feeling overwhelmed.  Home Secretary David Javid said the deployment of the Royal Navy and Air Force was the only way to avoid the tragedy of the sudden death of so many refugees at sea.  The British defense secretary immediately sent the Mersey coastal patrol ship, the Royal Air Force aircraft to help solve the problem of refugee smuggling.  Javid said Britain would continue to deliver on its promise to give asylum to those in genuine need, but would not allow criminals to exploit the system to exploit the most vulnerable.  Who are the stowaways?  According to the BBC, from November to December 2018, more than 239 people successfully crossed the English Channel in rubber boats from coastal locations such as Calais, France, where refugees are concentrated.  This includes women and children.  Most of those arriving in Britain by rubber boats are from the Middle East, such as Iran.  Javid said the reasons for the sudden increase in the number of people trying to sneak into Britain by dinghy were complex, including the turmoil in the Middle East, organized crime operations and Britain's efforts to prevent stowaways from travelling to Britain by truck, train and ferry.  Many of them will come to the police and ask the British government for asylum.  Although these people will be detained by the police, the British side will always need to provide basic humanitarian guarantees to these refugees, especially the children among them.  Although France has promised to help strengthen the fight against illegal immigration in the English Channel, the departure of illegal immigrants from France does not appear to have caused any pressure on French society.  How many people are currently applying for asylum in the UK?  The United Kingdom grants "refugee status" to those who are unable to live in their country because of fear of persecution on various grounds, such as race, religion, nationality, political opinion or sexual orientation, and provides the basic necessities of living, food, shelter and welfare, as well as cash assistance.  Successful applications usually allow applicants to stay in the UK legally for five years, after which they can apply for permanent residence in the UK as long as they meet the conditions such as no criminal record.  The applicants include those who arrived in Britain by rubber boats, but also stowaways who arrived in Britain by ferry, truck and other means.  According to the Home Office, in 2017, the Home Office received more than 26,000 asylum applications.  This is a small number compared to the number of asylum applications received by other large countries in Western Europe during the same period: 198,000 in Germany, 126,000 in Italy and 91,000 in France.  The EU has been critical of Britain over the number of refugees it has received.  In the same period, the Home Office issued more than 21,000 applications, and granted 31.8% of them asylum needs.  At the end of 2018, more than 24,500 people in the UK were waiting for the Home Office to approve their asylum applications, of which 42% had been waiting for more than six months.  Most asylum seekers rejected by the Home Office go to court. In 2017, out of more than 14,000 asylum applications rejected by the Home Office, more than 5,000 were approved by court decisions, meaning that the Home Office ’ s initial refusal to approve was overturned.  Image copyright Lewis Morris Image caption A large number of migrants, many of them Iranians, have recently arrived in Britain by boat from France.  It is noteworthy that the number of illegal immigrants from China to Britain, which attracted attention more than a decade ago, has been greatly reduced in today's refugee influx.  More than a decade ago, many Chinese people smuggled into Britain through Russia and Europe. The deaths of 58 stowaways in the port of Dover in 2000 and 23 scavengers in Merkham Bay in 2004 reflect the problem of a large number of illegal immigrants from China sneaking into Britain more than a decade ago.  The British government has also stepped up its efforts to crack down on illegal immigrants and illegal workers in the wake of the Merkham Bay tragedy, but due to the high appeal of Britain's welfare social and humanitarian policies to war-torn and economically backward areas, the problem of illegal immigration in other countries is still very serious.  The top 10 countries with the largest number of asylum seekers are Syria, Eritrea, Sudan, Iran, Afghanistan, Iraq, Pakistan, Nigeria, Bangladesh and India.  Most of the stowaways who enter the UK find it difficult to repatriate if their asylum claims are rejected. In 2016, the British government spent a huge amount of money to repatriate 6,000 foreign criminals.  Britain has a population of 70 million, but there are huge numbers of illegal immigrants, including stowaways and people who have overstayed their visas in the UK illegally.  On the one hand, these people's work income, welfare and even human rights are difficult to be guaranteed, such as being exploited by people's groups, and on the other hand, they live in society to increase the invisible pressure on the British system of free medical care, education and other systems, and the crime problem that a few people breed has caused serious losses to society.  How many illegal immigrants are there in the UK?  There are no accurate official figures, and no one seems to be able to tell.  In 2001, the Home Office estimated the number of illegal immigrants in the UK at around 430,000.  A 2017 report in the British “Guardian ” quoted senior Home Office officials as saying that 150,000 to 250,000 foreigners leave the UK each year without due dates, including 26,000 who were denied asylum applications in 2016, and more than 1.2 million people may be living in the UK illegally.

Content: A woman and a man who died with their three children while trying to reach Britain are from the village of Glynne.  The website also published the names and photos of the deceased.  French authorities on Tuesday confirmed the capsizing of a small boat carrying asylum seekers and the death of four people on board in the English Channel. The rescue operation involved several coast guard boats and a Belgian army helicopter.  British Prime Minister Boris Johnson offered his condolences to the survivors.  British Home Secretary Priti Patel expressed sympathy for the victims and said she was very sorry to hear the news.  Patel said the incident once again highlighted the dangers of crossing the canal.  He promised to do everything in his power to stop traffickers from exploiting refugees in need.  The English Channel (English Channel) is a canal in northern France and southern Britain that connects the Atlantic Ocean to the North Sea.  According to data from PA Media, more than 7,400 people reached the UK via the English Channel in small boats this year, nearly four times more than in 2019.  This year ’ s “record ” was set with the arrival of 416 refugees on September 2.  Official statistics show that from June 2019 to June 2020, more than 3,400 people who applied for asylum are under the age of 17.  Of these, nearly 2,800 were unaccompanied children.  The British government can return refugees arriving from France under the Dublin Accords.  According to the treaty, asylum seekers who have entered Europe are only allowed to apply for asylum at their place of entry on European soil.

Title: A repeat of the nightmare of 2015. Europe is facing a new migration crisis
Content: https: / / ria.ru / 20210525 / migratsiya-1733716124.html A repeat of the nightmare of 2015.  Europe is facing a new migration crisis, a repeat of the nightmare of 2015.  Europe is waiting for a new migration crisis - RIA Novosti, 25.05.2021 A repeat of the nightmare of 2015.  Europe is once again on the brink of a migration crisis.  And this is not yet the summer, which traditionally accounts for the peak of the wave of illegal migration from countries...  RIA Novosti, 25.05.2021 2021-05-25T08: 00 2021-05-25T08: 00 2021-05-25T08: 02 migrants refugees europe authors / html / head / meta [@ name = 'og: title'] / @ content / html / head / meta [@ name = 'og: description'] / @ content https: / / cdn.com 24.img.ria.ru / images / 07e5 / 05 / 18 / 1733713287 _ 0: 153: 1920: 1233 _ 1920x0 _ 80 _ 0 _ 85ca65dc729db44d8073637ad5013c74.jpg Europe is again on the verge of a migration crisis.  And this is not yet the summer, which traditionally accounts for the peak of the wave of illegal migration from Asia and Africa.Now in the center of attention is Ceuta, a Spanish enclave in North Africa, where thousands of illegal refugees from Morocco rushed.  The refugee crisis in Ceuta and Melilla (another Spanish port in Africa) is largely the result of the artificial escalation of relations between Spain and Morocco.  According to many observers, Rabat decided to take revenge on Madrid for the assistance recently provided to the Polisario Front (which for many years has been fighting for the independence of Western Sahara from Morocco).  The revenge was the actual inaction of the border guards of this country, who turned a blind eye to the crowds of migrants breaking into Ceuta.  According to The Economist magazine, in this way King Mohammed VI of Morocco “made migration a weapon ” .But in fact, the sharp influx of refugees from Africa began not only in the Spanish enclaves.  Again, a series of flimsy ships illegally transporting Africans (mainly Libyans) from Tunisia to the Italian island of Lampedusa.  Last week, 1,200 people were transferred there during 12 hours of good weather alone.  And even despite the weather, accidents were recorded: 73 refugees from Bangladesh almost drowned trying to reach the cherished island.  How long it took, no one can say.  According to the Italian Interior Ministry, 4,290 migrants reached the country ’ s shores in the first three weeks of May.  While for the whole of May last year, their number was 1654 people.  The flow of illegal refugees is also increasing between the EU and Britain.  Since January, more than three thousand people have crossed the English Channel.  And over the same period last year, this figure was 1,400 refugees – more than double the growth.  Just the other day, the Belgian coast guard rescued a sinking ship on which 49 migrants, mostly Vietnamese, tried to cross the strait.  Based on the above facts and statistics, we can safely assume that the migration crisis will return to the European agenda in the foreseeable future.  However, the numbers are not as catastrophic as they were in 2015, when Europe was literally drowned by a flood of refugees.  And the increase compared to last year is easily explained by the fact that in 2020, many people in Asia and Africa gave up their intentions to go to pandemics in Europe.  In addition, the result of the shift of public attention from the problem of migration to the fight against the covid was a noticeable decrease in the ratings of a number of parties advocating strict measures to limit the influx of immigrants (in the Western media, these political organizations are usually indiscriminately called ultra-right, even despite the rather liberal economic program of many of them).  It is quite logical that now, with the rapid return of migration problems to the agenda, many publications have sounded the alarm in connection with the imminent growth of the popularity of these political forces.  Almost all analysts agree that the crisis around Ceuta, which has not descended from the front pages of the Spanish press for several days, will significantly strengthen the anti-Islamic party Vox (Voice).  Even before the current crisis, it actively dispersed the fears of the enclave residents in connection with the influx of poor Africans.  And in the end, it won the first place in the parliamentary elections of 2019, receiving more than 35 percent of the vote – and this is in a city where 40 percent of the population is Muslim.  It would be strange if the Vox party did not now take advantage of the crisis to increase its popularity in Ceuta.  For example, a local cell of the party is publicizing protests against the fact that African migrants entering the Spanish enclave receive coronavirus vaccinations, while Spanish citizens living there wait months for their turn.  This is confirmed by events in the regional parliament of Andalusia, where after the 2018 elections, for the first time in history, the People ’ s Party took the first place and was able to form a minority government.  Until last week, it relied solely on the informal support of Vox MPs.  However, on Thursday, they announced the termination of cooperation with the senior partner in connection with the fact that the authorities of the region agreed to accept 13 minor refugees who infiltrated Ceuta.  This could lead to the fall of the regional government and early elections.  That is why the People ’ s Party is forced to show more and more rigidity in the migration issue, causing panic in the European liberal media.Even more worrying in the mainstream is the electoral situation in Italy.  After the 2015 crisis, the League party, led by Matteo Salvini, has been the consistent leader of the polls there.  Having proved himself a tough fighter against illegal migration as the Minister of Internal Affairs, he increased the leadership of his party to record levels.  At the peak of popularity in the summer of 2019, the League ’ s figures were approaching 40 percent, which gave it hope even for the formation of its government.  Based on these calculations, Salvini provoked a government crisis in order to hold early elections, but was outplayed by opponents.  Since last year, there has been a drop in the ratings of this political force, whose supporters cannot forgive the support it expressed for the technocratic government of Mario Draghi.  Liberals can breathe freely.  But the fact is that the ratings of the League, which is still in the first place in the polls, are moving on opposite courses with the rapidly growing indicators of the even more right-wing and even more anti-migrant party “Brothers of Italy ”.  According to some polls, she already came in second place after the League, behind that couple of percent.  Three years ago, its ratings fluctuated around three to four percent, and now confidently approaching 20.  If elections were held now, these two forces, with the support of Silvio Berlusconi ’ s Forward Italy party, could well form a majority government.  They do not hide their ideological continuity from the far-right Italian social movement, which was created in 1946 by former supporters of Benito Mussolini.  This legacy is clearly indicated by the logo of the party, which includes the former symbol of ISD.The growth of the popularity of the "Brothers" will contribute to the charisma of the head of the party Georgia Meloni ("Sisters of Italy", as it was nicknamed by the press) - she last year surpassed in the approval ratings of the leader of the "League", becoming the second most popular politician in the country after the current prime minister.  There is no doubt that in the event of an aggravation of the migration crisis, the League and Brothers will be able to get additional votes to their already serious ratings.  Trends in the first months of the year show that the threat of the covid is no longer deterring refugees seeking to Europe.  And this means that the nightmare of 2015 may repeat itself — and the popularity of far-right, anti-migrant, anti-Islamic, Eurosceptic parties will again sharply rise.
