background: I am a paralegal assisting a lawyer advocating for a Ukrainian family whose loved one died in the Ukrainian International Airlines flight PS 752.
title: Court rulings PS 752

passages.title: Canadian court: Iran ’ s downing of Ukraine Flight 752 was an act of terror – Radio France Internationale
passages.passage: OTTAWA (AFP) - A Canadian court today ruled that the shooting down of Ukrainian International Airlines flight PS752 by Iranian forces early last year was a deliberate "terrorist act" and that the decision will pave the way for possible compensation for the families of the victims.  On January 8, Ukraine International Airlines Flight PS752 crashed near Tehran, killing all 176 people on board, including 85 Canadian citizens and permanent residents.  Iran initially denied the Western accusations, but three days later admitted that the Iranian military shot down the other side "unintentionally".  The Ontario Superior Court of Justice in Canada said it had determined, after "weighing the odds," that the plane was hit by two missiles shortly after take-off in Tehran, as a result of a "deliberate" act.  Judge Edward Belobaba also ruled that “the plaintiff ’ s claim that the shooting down of Flight 752 was an act of terrorism. ”  The plaintiffs ’ lawyers called the ruling “unprecedented in Canadian law. ”  "This will have a significant impact on the immediate families of the victims seeking justice," they said in a statement.  The lawsuit, filed by the families of the four victims, seeks 1.5 billion Canadian dollars (about NT $35.3 billion).  They claim that Iran launched the missile attack in retaliation for the US killing of Qasem Soleimani, the commander of the Quds Force of the Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps, near Baghdad airport in Iraq, days before the crash.  A final report released in March by the Iran Civil Aviation Organisation said the missile attack and the "vigilant" response of ground forces were the result of high tensions between Iran and the United States at the time.  Eleven Ukrainian citizens were killed in the crash.  The Ukrainian side pointed out that behind the report there was a "ridiculous attempt to cover up the real cause", while Canada said the report contained "no strong facts or evidence" and promised to publish its findings soon.  Iran did not defend itself in court, but three days after the crash admitted that Iranian forces shot down the Boeing 737-800 bound for Kiev.  The court will then decide on the amount of compensation. © 2021 AFP

passages.title: Canadian court ruled the destruction of the UIA aircraft a terrorist attack: Iran responded
passages.passage: The destruction of the Boeing 737 of Ukraine International Airlines (UIA) in the vicinity of Tehran in January 2020 was a deliberate terrorist act.  According to Global News, this decision was made by the Supreme Court of the Canadian province of Ontario.  Judge Edward Belobaba ruled that "based on a balance of probabilities, the missile attacks on flight PS 752 were intentional."  “The plaintiffs proved that the shooting down of Flight 752 by the defendants was an act of terrorism and constitutes a terrorist activity, ” he said.  In his decision, the Ontario court judge relied on the opinions of two experts, one of whom concluded that Iran ’ s Revolutionary Guard knew that Flight 752 was a civilian aircraft and “deliberately shot it down for the purpose of destruction. ”  The court ruled on a civil lawsuit filed by four families of the victims on board the UIA plane.  The defendants include Iran, the Revolutionary Guard, the Iranian Armed Forces and Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei.  The ruling effectively allows families in Canada to claim damages from Iran.  Among the dead of flight 752 were 55 citizens of Canada and 30 permanent residents of the country.  Later, a spokesman for the Iranian Foreign Ministry, Saeed Khatibzadeh, said that Iran considers the decision of the court in Canada to be groundless, Anadolu reports.  “Everyone knows that the Canadian court has no jurisdiction over this plane crash.  Do not investigate events that occur outside the jurisdiction of Canada.  This decision has no grounds, objective documents and reasons, ” he said.  According to the speaker, this is a manifestation of a political approach.  As reported by OBOZREVATEL:

passages.title: The Supreme Court of the United States rejected the appeal of the National Bank of Iran.
passages.passage: The U.S. Supreme Court on Monday rejected an appeal by the National Bank of Iran over a lower court ruling that would allow alleged victims of terrorism to claim millions of dollars in compensation from the bank.  The U.S. Supreme Court on Monday rejected an appeal by the National Bank of Iran over a lower court ruling that would allow families of alleged terrorism victims to claim millions of dollars in compensation from the bank.  According to Reuters, Supreme Court judges retained a previous ruling by a federal court that allowed some alleged victims of terrorism to claim $17.6 million from the National Bank of Iran.  The ruling is the second time in two weeks that U.S. courts have ruled on compensation cases for U.S. citizens.  Iran is one of the few countries and organizations that have been accused by U.S. courts of paying compensation in such cases.  Enforcement of these sentences has often been difficult.  The U.S. Supreme Court on Wednesday rejected a lawsuit by another group of plaintiffs demanding the confiscation of Iranian artifacts at a museum in Chicago in exchange for tens of millions of dollars in compensation.  The central theme in both cases is that U.S. domestic law prevents U.S. citizens from prosecuting foreign governments and confiscating their property in U.S. courts unless the country is listed as a state sponsor of terrorism.  Iran is on the list, according to U.S. claims.  In a Supreme Court ruling on Monday, U.S. courts have ruled in four cases in favor of about 90 plaintiffs, who claim to be eligible for more than $1 billion in Iranian government debt.  The plaintiffs claim that between 1990 and 2002, they or their families were victims of attacks involving Iran.  While U.S. courts have ruled that the plaintiffs owe the Iranian government more than $1 billion, they have agreed to share $17.6 million if they win the lawsuit against the National Bank of Iran.  The plaintiffs are injured people or families of victims in the 1996 Saudi News Tower bombings, two bombings in 2001 and 2002 in Jerusalem, and the 1990 murder of an American-born rabbi in New York.  The National Bank of Iran argued that $17.6 million in assets could not be confiscated because the bank did not own the property, calling for an appeal in 2016 by Branch IX of the Court of Appeals in San Francisco.

passages.title: The Supreme Court of the United States in the case of Iranian antiquities
passages.passage: The Supreme Court ruled on Wednesday that plaintiffs in a case accusing Iran of terrorism could not confiscate Iranian antiquities at a museum in Chicago.  The US Supreme Court ruled on Wednesday that Iranian antiquities held at a museum in Chicago could not be confiscated to pay tens of millions of dollars in compensation to the families of alleged victims of terrorism.  The U.S. Supreme Court ruled Wednesday in favor of Iran with eight votes in favor of the case.  The plaintiffs wanted to confiscate a collection of Iranian art held at the University of Chicago ’ s School of Orientalism.  They hoped to use the money from the confiscation to receive $71.5 million in compensation from Iran, which the US courts have decided they are eligible for.  The case was referred to the US Supreme Court after the US Court of Appeals ruled in 2016 that the artefacts did not belong to the Iranian government in order to be confiscated.  The issue at the Supreme Court was when foreign assets could be confiscated and used to pay compensation to alleged victims of terrorism.  Iran is one of the few countries and organizations that have been accused by U.S. courts of paying compensation in such cases.  Reuters said the sentences were often difficult to enforce.  U.S. domestic law prevents U.S. citizens from prosecuting foreign governments and confiscating their property in U.S. courts, unless the country is listed as a state sponsor of terrorism.  Iran is on the list, according to U.S. claims.  U.S. law also provides that property held in the United States for commercial purposes can be confiscated.  Earlier, Supreme Court judges had expressed doubts about the possibility of confiscating non-commercial property, such as ancient Iranian artifacts.  The plaintiffs describe their case as victims of an alleged suicide attack by three Hamas members that took place in the city of Jerusalem in September 1997.  Claiming that Iran was the main culprit for training and supporting Hamas, the plaintiffs sought to confiscate a collection of Iranian antiquities, including the Persepolis Collection, held at the University of Chicago ’ s Orientalist Center.  It was previously reported that the administration of US President Donald Trump sided with Iran and the University of Chicago in this case.  The Trump administration ’ s argument is that lawsuits against foreign governments within the United States could result in other governments ’ dealings with the United States in foreign courts.  Justice Department representative Zachary Tripp told Supreme Court justices a few months ago that if Congress wanted to authorize the confiscation of antiquities, it would be explicitly stated in the law, which is currently not the case under U.S. law.

passages.title: Iran ’ s Foreign Ministry ‘ rejects ’ decision by Ontario court in Canada
passages.passage: Photo copyright Tasnim Image caption Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Bahram Ghasemi has rejected the Ontario Circuit Court ruling against Iran.  Iran ’ s Foreign Ministry spokesman Bahram Ghasemi has condemned a court action in Canada against Iran.  On Monday, June 3, an appeals court in Ontario, Canada, upheld the Iranian government ’ s conviction to pay compensation to victims of “state terrorism. ”  Iran has, of course, reserved the right to protest and follow up on this verdict.  According to Tasnim News Agency, Mr. Ghasemi has said: “Basically, the issuance of a ruling against a foreign government is contrary to the principle of equality of states and violates their immunity in international law. ”  A spokesman for Iran ’ s Foreign Ministry also said: “It is obvious that regardless of the internal divisions of power in Canada, the government of this country will be directly responsible for any material and moral damages that may result from such acts contrary to international law by various parts of the Canadian sovereignty. ”  Getty Images Image caption Survivors of the victims of a suicide bombing at the U.S. Marine Corps center in Beirut were among the plaintiffs. A Canadian court found the Iranian government responsible for damages to a group of victims and survivors of U.S. victims of a “terrorist ” operation in the 1980s through the early 2000s and ordered the Islamic Republic to seize $1.7 billion in assets.  The plaintiffs accused the Islamic Republic of supporting the groups behind the attacks and demanded compensation.  After the initial court ruling, the lawyers of the Iranian government, based on the principle of “state immunity ” in international law and the payment of compensation to the plaintiffs in the United States, did not enter the sentence and called for its annulment by the Ontario State Court of Appeals.  The Iranian Foreign Ministry also criticized the sentence, calling it unacceptable.  The Court of Appeals dismissed the arguments of Iranian government lawyers, accusing the Islamic Republic of seeking to undermine the Justice for Victims of Terrorism Act passed by the Canadian Parliament.  The court ruled that "civilized society considers the terrorist attacks associated with the complaint of American plaintiffs with disgust and considers it shocking that a foreign government should be involved in support of such atrocities."  The judges rejected the Iranian government ’ s reliance on the principle of sovereign immunity in international law and the conflict of justice for victims of terrorism, saying that the use of peaceful legal means to combat terrorism is not a problem, and that the payment of compensation to victims “is a decent measure in response to state support for terrorism and is consistent with Canada ’ s legal values. ”  AFP Image caption Iran's embassy in Canada - The court has said that the Islamic Republic's diplomatic facilities and properties cannot be confiscated; some of the plaintiffs were family members of those killed in violent operations and others were injured or disabled in such operations or those abducted and tortured by extremist groups.  The plaintiffs have previously filed lawsuits against the government of the Islamic Republic of Iran on charges of financing and arming and training Hamas and Hezbollah groups in the US courts.  The 1983 suicide bombing of the U.S. Marine Center in Beirut, in which 241 American soldiers were killed and Hezbollah was blamed, was responsible for four attacks in Lebanon, including the bombing of the U.S. Embassy in Beirut, numerous kidnappings in Lebanon in the 1980s, including the hanging of a kidnapped U.S. lieutenant colonel and several others, and the Hamas bombing of the Arab University of Jerusalem in 2002. And the bombings in Argentina, Israel and Saudi Arabia that have been attributed to groups supported by the Islamic Republic were among the cases raised in this case.  The plaintiffs extended their complaints to Canada because they did not consider the Iranian government ’ s remaining assets in the United States sufficient to pay compensation.  The Iranian government still has assets in Canada, including real estate and bank accounts.  The Justice for Victims of Terrorism Act was passed by the Canadian Parliament in 2012, which allows victims of acts of terrorism to file complaints against perpetrators and governments that help them.  Diplomatic relations between Iran and Canada were cut off in 2001 and have not yet been restored, although there have been recent reports of the two sides ’ willingness to resume relations.

passages.title: Firing of Flight 752: Ukraine says it has not received Iran's final report
passages.passage: Ukraine says it has not received Iran ’ s final report, AFP Ukraine says it has not received Iran ’ s final report on the downing of flight 752.  Ukrainian Deputy Foreign Minister Yevgeny Yinin told Radio Hermosk in Ukraine that he had not received the report.  Mr. Yenin explained in the interview, “We have repeatedly heard from Iran that the report is ready and the translation of the report is finished.  “I ’ ve heard about it once a week for the last two months, but we haven ’ t seen any evidence yet. ”  Iran ’ s Civil Aviation Organization said in a statement that a videoconference meeting was held on Monday, January 21 between the aviation accident investigation group in Iran and representatives of countries related to the accident, in which the draft outlines and the Iranian representative responded to the questions of the representatives of the countries.  It was reported that in addition to Canada, Sweden, the United Kingdom and Germany whose nationals were on board, the United States as the designer and manufacturer of the aircraft, Ukraine as the country where the aircraft was registered and operated, France as the country that had provided technical assistance, as well as representatives of the World Aviation Organization (ICAO).  According to ICAO standards, a draft disaster investigation report will be sent to countries involved in the investigation, Iran says representatives have two months to voice their opinions before the final report is published.  According to Article 13 of the Chicago Convention, the complete report of an air crash must be submitted to the World Aviation Organization no later than one year after the accident.  January 8 is the anniversary of the shooting down of a Ukrainian passenger plane.  According to ICAO rules, the report must include information and official documentation of the research team ’ s findings, the causes of the accident and the factors involved.  The families of many of the victims, as well as officials from Canada and Ukraine, say they doubt that Iran will disclose in its report what happened "without distortion or secrecy."  After reviewing the black box, Iranian aviation officials claimed that only 19 seconds of conversation between the three pilots was recorded after the first missile hit, and after the second missile, no sound was recorded from the cockpit due to "significant damage".  Canada, where most of the passengers on Flight 752 were Ukrainian citizens, is not happy with the investigation and says it could take the case to the International Court of Justice in The Hague if the families are not satisfied with the final report.  Iran has accused Canada of taking political advantage of the situation.  The Ukrainian passenger plane was shot down by two IRGC missiles on January 8 after taking off from Imam Khomeini International Airport in southern Tehran.  Iran initially denied firing missiles as the reason for the crash.

passages.title: Iran ’ s Judiciary Spokesman: Some people were charged in Zarif ’ s audio file
passages.passage: A spokesman for Iran ’ s judiciary on Tuesday said of the investigation into the audio file released by Foreign Minister Mohammad Javad Zarif: “I have already mentioned that a case has been formed in the General and Revolutionary Court of Tehran and numerous individuals who were related to the case were investigated as informed.  Some of those who were accused were banned from leaving, and some of those who were accused were accused of being charged, and the order of supply was issued for them and they were free to comply with the agreement. ”  Talayeh Gholamhossein Esmaeili, spokesman for Iran ’ s judiciary, continued in a press conference: “The investigation is ongoing by Tehran ’ s General and Revolutionary Court and we will inform as soon as the result. ”  The spokesman for Iran ’ s judiciary also commented on the verdict of 11 bank debtors and former municipal officials in Tehran: “I explained about all 11 people that the judiciary has done good for them and some of their convicts are in prison and the demands of the banks have been collected.  In many cases, after the filing, there are good interactions between us and the banks.  Esmaeili said about the case of Isa Sharifi, Qalibaf ’ s deputy at the time of his municipality in Tehran, “This case has been investigated and the verdict has been approved by the Supreme Court, and I am surprised that after this information, people in the debates are unaware of these proceedings. ”  In response to a question about the decision of the Supreme Court and the endowment of the forests of Mashhad, the spokesman of the judiciary said: "This case was investigated and with the report of the Chief Justice, the issue of Article 477 was restored and the endowment of this forest was violated and the case was sent to the Supreme Court and the verdict has not yet been announced."  Responding to a question about the latest situation in the case of the Ukrainian plane and the statements of the Ukrainian government that the families are to be compensated after the trial, he said: "In relation to this case and what was announced by the Ukrainian authorities, I must say that the competent authority to deal with this issue is the Iranian judicial authority and this is the authority of the armed forces."  Ismaili said that thorough and thorough investigations will be carried out and the case will be sent to the court with indictments and court hearings will be held.  It is not desirable for another country to comment, but the compensation, which is paid before the court and we try to pay the claims before the court order is issued. passages.title: Ontario court: Iran shooting down Ukrainian plane was' intentional and terrorism'
passages.passage: Ontario Court: The shooting of Ukrainian aircraft by Iran was' intentional and terrorist 'May 30, 1400 - May 20, 2021, 20: 18 GMT Updated 4 minutes ago Picture description, memorial to the victims - 176 Sereneges were killed Flight 752 The Ontario Supreme Court in Canada has concluded that the shooting of Ukrainian flight PS752 by Iran was a deliberate act and based on criminal law of terrorist act.  Ukraine International Airlines Flight 752 was hit by two Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps missiles in January 2020, killing 176 people.  Judge Edward Blubaba wrote in a decision issued Thursday: "By weighing the possibilities, I found that the missile attacks on Flight 752 were deliberate and directly responsible for the deaths of all those on board."  "I also realized, weighing the possibilities, that there was no armed conflict in the region at the time."  The judge said the plaintiffs had proven that the downing of the plane was based on state immunity laws, justice for victims of terrorist acts and criminal law as "terrorist activity."  Former Canadian Foreign Minister Francois Philippe Champagne said in December that he did not believe the flight was caused by human error.  The plaintiffs' lawyer said in a statement that another hearing would be held in the court to determine compensation.  Mark Arnold has previously said that the best way to get compensation for the families of the victims is to accuse the Iranian government of “committing a terrorist act. ”  He is the legal representative of the plaintiffs who lost their relatives on that flight.  Despite being informed of the charge, the Iranian government has refused to defend itself in this court.  Mark and Jonah Arnold, lawyers for the case, wrote: “The decision of the Supreme Court of Justice in Canada is unprecedented.  "This is a significant ruling in terms of the immediate impact on the families of victims seeking justice."  Habib Haghjoo, whose daughter Shahnaz Haghjoo and eight-year-old grandson Elsa lost a new one on flight 752, said it was a success for the families making the complaint.  He said: “I ’ m very happy and I think it ’ s a big step.  Canadian Foreign Minister Mark Garneau told parliament last week that Canada would soon negotiate compensation for the families of the victims.  The association representing the families of the victims has repeatedly said it wants answers and justice for the overthrow before any talks about reparations.  More than a year after the shooting down of the plane, there are still serious uncertainties about the causes of the shooting down and those involved in the “unconscionable, ” Mr. Garno told a parliamentary committee on Thursday:“ I must honestly say that the behavior of the Iranian government over the past 15 months has been unconscionable and we will not let them go to ensure accountability. ”  After months of pressure, Tehran has just agreed to hand over flight data recorders for independent analysis, he said, adding that Iran has not yet explained why it did not close its skies on the night of the incident.  Flight 752 was hit by two IRGC missiles on January 8, 2020.  Ukraine and four other countries where citizens or residents were killed - including Canada, Britain, Afghanistan and Sweden - have called on Iran to provide a full and comprehensive explanation of the downing of the plane.  The Iranian armed forces denied any responsibility within three days of the overthrow.  Authorities also allowed the occupants ’ assets scattered at the crash site to be looted and then bulldozed.  But accumulating evidence from the IRGC Aerospace Force, he said that an anti-aircraft unit mistook the Boeing 737-800 for a missile.  On that day, Iran ’ s air defenses were on high alert because of the IRGC ’ s action in firing missiles at two Iraqi bases where U.S. forces were stationed.  Iran was targeting these bases in retaliation for the killing of Qods Force commander Qassem Soleimani.  The Civil Aviation Organization recently reported in March 2021 that an anti-aircraft defense operator of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) had “mistakenly ” identified the aircraft as hostile and fired the missiles without the permission of the commanders.  According to Iran ’ s Civil Aviation Organization, the downing of the plane was due to a “chain of human errors ” that occurred on the day of the disaster.  Ukraine and Canada rejected the report.  In a video post on Facebook, Ukraine ’ s Foreign Minister Dmitry Kolba called the Iran investigation “unilateral, ” calling the evidence“ selective, ” and the result “deceptive. ”  Canada ’ s foreign and transport ministers, Mark Garneau and Omar Alghbra, said in a statement that the Iran report “makes no attempt to answer fundamental questions about what really happened, appears incomplete, and contains no facts or tangible evidence. ”

Title: Canadian court: Iran ’ s downing of Ukraine Flight 752 was an act of terror – Radio France Internationale
Content: OTTAWA (AFP) - A Canadian court today ruled that the shooting down of Ukrainian International Airlines flight PS752 by Iranian forces early last year was a deliberate "terrorist act" and that the decision will pave the way for possible compensation for the families of the victims.  On January 8, Ukraine International Airlines Flight PS752 crashed near Tehran, killing all 176 people on board, including 85 Canadian citizens and permanent residents.  Iran initially denied the Western accusations, but three days later admitted that the Iranian military shot down the other side "unintentionally".  The Ontario Superior Court of Justice in Canada said it had determined, after "weighing the odds," that the plane was hit by two missiles shortly after take-off in Tehran, as a result of a "deliberate" act.  Judge Edward Belobaba also ruled that “the plaintiff ’ s claim that the shooting down of Flight 752 was an act of terrorism. ”  The plaintiffs ’ lawyers called the ruling “unprecedented in Canadian law. ”  "This will have a significant impact on the immediate families of the victims seeking justice," they said in a statement.  The lawsuit, filed by the families of the four victims, seeks 1.5 billion Canadian dollars (about NT $35.3 billion).  They claim that Iran launched the missile attack in retaliation for the US killing of Qasem Soleimani, the commander of the Quds Force of the Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps, near Baghdad airport in Iraq, days before the crash.  A final report released in March by the Iran Civil Aviation Organisation said the missile attack and the "vigilant" response of ground forces were the result of high tensions between Iran and the United States at the time.  Eleven Ukrainian citizens were killed in the crash.  The Ukrainian side pointed out that behind the report there was a "ridiculous attempt to cover up the real cause", while Canada said the report contained "no strong facts or evidence" and promised to publish its findings soon.  Iran did not defend itself in court, but three days after the crash admitted that Iranian forces shot down the Boeing 737-800 bound for Kiev.  The court will then decide on the amount of compensation. © 2021 AFP

Title: Canadian court ruled the destruction of the UIA aircraft a terrorist attack: Iran responded
Content: The destruction of the Boeing 737 of Ukraine International Airlines (UIA) in the vicinity of Tehran in January 2020 was a deliberate terrorist act.  According to Global News, this decision was made by the Supreme Court of the Canadian province of Ontario.  Judge Edward Belobaba ruled that "based on a balance of probabilities, the missile attacks on flight PS 752 were intentional."  “The plaintiffs proved that the shooting down of Flight 752 by the defendants was an act of terrorism and constitutes a terrorist activity, ” he said.  In his decision, the Ontario court judge relied on the opinions of two experts, one of whom concluded that Iran ’ s Revolutionary Guard knew that Flight 752 was a civilian aircraft and “deliberately shot it down for the purpose of destruction. ”  The court ruled on a civil lawsuit filed by four families of the victims on board the UIA plane. Ukraine International Airlines Flight 752 was hit by two Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps missiles in January 2020, killing 176 people.  Judge Edward Blubaba wrote in a decision issued Thursday: "By weighing the possibilities, I found that the missile attacks on Flight 752 were deliberate and directly responsible for the deaths of all those on board."  "I also realized, weighing the possibilities, that there was no armed conflict in the region at the time."  The judge said the plaintiffs had proven that the downing of the plane was based on state immunity laws, justice for victims of terrorist acts and criminal law as "terrorist activity."  Former Canadian Foreign Minister Francois Philippe Champagne said in December that he did not believe the flight was caused by human error. Despite being informed of the charge, the Iranian government has refused to defend itself in this court.  Mark and Jonah Arnold, lawyers for the case, wrote: “The decision of the Supreme Court of Justice in Canada is unprecedented.  "This is a significant ruling in terms of the immediate impact on the families of victims seeking justice."  Habib Haghjoo, whose daughter Shahnaz Haghjoo and eight-year-old grandson Elsa lost a new one on flight 752, said it was a success for the families making the complaint.  He said: “I ’ m very happy and I think it ’ s a big step.  Canadian Foreign Minister Mark Garneau told parliament last week that Canada would soon negotiate compensation for the families of the victims.  The association representing the families of the victims has repeatedly said it wants answers and justice for the overthrow before any talks about reparations.  More than a year after the shooting down of the plane, there are still serious uncertainties about the causes of the shooting down and those involved in the “unconscionable, ” Mr. Garno told a parliamentary committee on Thursday:“ I must honestly say that the behavior of the Iranian government over the past 15 months has been unconscionable and we will not let them go to ensure accountability. ”  After months of pressure, Tehran has just agreed to hand over flight data recorders for independent analysis, he said, adding that Iran has not yet explained why it did not close its skies on the night of the incident.  Flight 752 was hit by two IRGC missiles on January 8, 2020.  Ukraine and four other countries where citizens or residents were killed - including Canada, Britain, Afghanistan and Sweden - have called on Iran to provide a full and comprehensive explanation of the downing of the plane.  The Iranian armed forces denied any responsibility within three days of the overthrow.  Authorities also allowed the occupants ’ assets scattered at the crash site to be looted and then bulldozed.  But accumulating evidence from the IRGC Aerospace Force, he said that an anti-aircraft unit mistook the Boeing 737-800 for a missile.  On that day, Iran ’ s air defenses were on high alert because of the IRGC ’ s action in firing missiles at two Iraqi bases where U.S. forces were stationed.  Iran was targeting these bases in retaliation for the killing of Qods Force commander Qassem Soleimani.  The Civil Aviation Organization recently reported in March 2021 that an anti-aircraft defense operator of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) had “mistakenly ” identified the aircraft as hostile and fired the missiles without the permission of the commanders.  According to Iran ’ s Civil Aviation Organization, the downing of the plane was due to a “chain of human errors ” that occurred on the day of the disaster.  Ukraine and Canada rejected the report. passages.title: Russian fishing boat detained by North Korea for 10 days and 17 crew released
passages.passage: SEOUL, July 28, 2019 (AFP) The Russian Embassy in North Korea said today that North Korea has released a Russian fishing boat detained for violating immigration regulations.  The South Korean side confirmed that the fishing boat had arrived in Sokcho this afternoon.  The Russian Embassy in North Korea said on Thursday that North Korea had detained a fishing boat carrying 15 Russian and two South Korean crew members for violating entry rules.  Russia said the ship did not violate any regulations.  The embassy said in a Facebook post that the two South Korean crew members had also been released, adding that the boat had left Wonsan, North Korea, last night.  "The vessel has separated from the Kwon San port terminal at 7.30 pm (yesterday) and is headed for Sokcho, South Korea, where the two South Korean crew members will disembark."  The embassy said it would continue to investigate the "circumstances" of the vessel's detention.  South Korea's Unification Ministry, which handles relations between the two Koreas, welcomed the "safe release" of the fishing vessel, saying it was "a positive move from a humanitarian point of view." passages.passage: archive all for today topics of the week actual popular published by the editors on Translator 03.08.20 00: 12 scout: Igor Lvovich; translator Igor Lvovich "North Korea 'ghost ships' wash up in Japan full of dead bodies" Australia - July 29, 2020  North Korea, China, squid and boats full of corpses on the coast of Japan By CNN Jul 29, 2020 North Korean fishing boat in Russian waters.  In 2017, the sea continued to bring to shore the corpses of people.  For many years, Japan ’ s northern coast has been the scene of an alarming phenomenon: North Korean fishing boats have brought to shore the bodies of dead fishermen more than 1,000 kilometers from their homeland.  The figures for 2017 were unprecedented: on the coast of Japan, more than 100 boats with 35 corpses on board were thrown out by the sea.  A year earlier, only 66 boats had been delivered.  "Ghost ships" from North Korea with the corpses of fishermen carried to the coast of Japan.  (Global Fishing Watch) No one could explain why so many of these so-called “ghost ships ” washed up on the shores of Japan this year.  One Japanese Coast Guard official said it might just be the weather like that.  Others speculate that the deterioration of North Korea ’ s aging fishing fleet is to blame.  More of these faint boats began to be nailed to the shore, though with fewer dead bodies.  This mystery has haunted the [Japanese] authorities for years, but a study published on Wednesday by the international non-profit organization Global Fishing Watch offers a new, convincing version of what is happening.  Global Fishing Watch accuses China of ‘ shadow fishing fleet ’  The authors of the report used various satellite technologies to analyze maritime traffic in northeast Asia in 2017 and 2018 and found that hundreds of Chinese fishing vessels were sailing in waters off North Korea.  Chinese trawlers appear to be illegally fishing in waters off the coast of North Korea, displacing the North Korean fleet itself, which is poorly equipped for long-range navigation, further from the North Korean coast into Russian and Japanese waters.  Fishing in North Korean waters or buying and selling North Korean fish internationally is a violation of international law.  The fishery trade with Pyongyang, worth an estimated $419 million a year, was sanctioned by the UN Security Council in 2017, as part of its efforts to punish the Kim Jong-un regime for its repeated ballistic missile tests that year.  But that, according to a report by Global Fishing Watch, does not seem to have stopped some 900 Chinese vessels in 2017 and 700 the following year.  The satellite identifies illegal vessels.  According to Global Fishing Watch, in 2017 and 2018, these Chinese vessels caught more than 160,000 metric tons of Pacific Flying Squid, one of the most valuable seafood in the region, more than South Korea and Japan combined in the same period.  The estimated catch was worth more than $614 million.  While it is unclear whether North Korea could have made so much money from fishing in its waters, it now seems clear that Pyongyang has managed to recover some of the lost profits by selling fishing rights to foreign operators, probably Chinese.  A United Nations report released in March claimed that North Korea earned approximately $167 million in 2018 by selling or transferring fishing rights in violation of UN sanctions.  Zhi Yong Park, a senior fellow at Global Fishing Watch and a co-author of the study, said the vessels were “about one-third the size of China ’ s entire long-range fishing fleet. ”  "This is the largest known case of illegal fishing by vessels from one country operating in the waters of another country," Park said.  The report exposes widespread illegal fishing in North Korean waters.  (University of Wollongong, Australia) With so many [Chinese] vessels off the North Korean coast, the country ’ s own fishing fleet has been pushed out of there and forced to move farther and farther away from its shores in order to catch the catch, and the consequences of this, according to Jung Sam Lee, another of the research authors, were deadly.  “It ’ s too dangerous for them to operate in the same waters as Chinese trawlers, ” Li said.  “That ’ s why they ’ re being forced to work in Russian and Japanese waters, and that explains why some of North Korea ’ s damaged vessels have sprung up on Japan ’ s beaches. ”  Mr. Park and other experts said they had been able to track the vessels using new satellite and radar technology that had not been available in previous years.  Open source intelligence NGOs and non-profit organizations are increasingly using these resources to analyze shipping in the hope of finding or better understanding the tactics used to evade sanctions.  According to Global Fishing Watch, vessels illegally fishing in North Korean waters are considered owned and operated by “Chinese interests ” because that is where they are based.  However, vessels engaged in illegal activities in these waters, whether moving goods at sea to avoid customs prying eyes or digging sand, often lack proper documentation, making them difficult to trace.  The waters of Northeast Asia are among the most opaque and contested seas and fisheries in the world.  China, Russia, Japan, North and South Korea are all involved in some kind of territorial dispute with each other.  Fish stocks have been declining sharply in recent years, which is another serious problem that the parties have not been able to resolve.  According to Global Fishing Watch, since 2003, stocks of flying squid in the Pacific have fallen 80 percent in South Korean waters and 82 percent in Japanese waters.  According to Global Fishing Watch, stocks of flying squid in the Pacific have fallen 80 percent in South Korean waters and 82 percent in Japanese waters since 2003.  (Global Fishing Watch) "While fishermen and their families feel their incomes are falling, scientists are losing their guesses as to the most likely reason for the decline in catches," Park wrote in a blog accompanying the study.  “Many point to overfishing as the main reason for this, and some suggest that climate change may play a role here, as changes in water temperature affect spawning and migration.  “It ’ s depressing and it doesn ’ t make sense to say it all over again. ”  The sustainability of fishing is a major concern worldwide.  This has led to the loss of money and jobs in coastal communities that rely on trade, and has led to an increase in piracy in places where the fishing industry cannot rely on a functioning coast guard, such as Somalia.  Mr. Park said that while Japan and South Korea have worked independently to make squid fisheries more sustainable, “the lack of multilateral cooperation and exchange of information between all countries involved in this transboundary fishery means that reliable scientific data and regional resource management plans cannot be obtained locally. ”  South Korea ’ s Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries said it was reviewing the findings, while Masanori Miyahara, president of the Japan Fisheries Research and Education Agency, said in a statement accompanying the Global Fishing Watch study, the lack of shared data “is a serious challenge, given the critical importance of squid in the region. ”  “Illegal fishing in these waters is a very serious issue in Japan, ” Miyahara said.  Mr Park said his team ’ s research had revealed “a fundamental failure in the proper and transparent management of the shared resource ” and there was“ an urgent need for cooperation between the countries involved in this fishery ”. North Korea detained a Russian fishing ship in 2019 due to the alleged illegal crossing of the border of the military protection zone, which the DPRK arbitrarily established 50 miles from the shore.

The fishing ship, Xianghaylin-8, was a Russian vessel carrying 15 Russian citizens and two South Korean crew members, who were traveling from the South Korean port of Sokcho to the Sea of Japan for fishing [8ea6f522-4747-4148-b819-bea652ef025d]. 
The incident occurred on the night of July 17, within 55 nautical miles of North Korean territory [8ea6f522-4747-4148-b819-bea652ef025d].

At 4 a.m. 
on July 17, the border guards went to the ship and turned off all communication devices [8ea6f522-4747-4148-b819-bea652ef025d]. 
The crew did not realize what had happened at first, thinking that the border guards had left, but soon realized they had been seized [8ea6f522-4747-4148-b819-bea652ef025d].

The sailors were escorted to the North Korean port of Wonsan, where they were held [7784f114-7cc1-4111-a819-24e94b3b7ac9]. 
The Russian Consulate General was only able to visit the passengers on Tuesday, July 23 [8ea6f522-4747-4148-b819-bea652ef025d].

The detention occurred in the Sea of Japan, where the fishing vessel was engaged in crab mining [7784f114-7cc1-4111-a819-24e94b3b7ac9]. 
The company that owns the vessel, the Northeast Fishing Company, stated that they had not violated any regulations [3dbc753d-457c-4f25-98fe-4df3b42ed82d].

The North Korean authorities indicated that the reason for the arrest was the illegal crossing of the border of the military protection zone [7784f114-7cc1-4111-a819-24e94b3b7ac9]. 
However, the company disputed this claim, stating that the ship had not violated any regulations [3dbc753d-457c-4f25-98fe-4df3b42ed82d].

The detained sailors were interrogated and searched twice a day, and were being held in closed cabins [8ea6f522-4747-4148-b819-bea652ef025d]. 
The Russian Consulate General was only able to visit the passengers on Tuesday, July 23 [8ea6f522-4747-4148-b819-bea652ef025d].

The incident occurred before the end of July 2019, as the Russian fishing boat was released on July 28, 2019 [3dbc753d-457c-4f25-98fe-4df3b42ed82d]. 
The boat had been detained for 10 days before being released [3dbc753d-457c-4f25-98fe-4df3b42ed82d].

This mystery has haunted the [Japanese] authorities for years, but a study published on Wednesday by the international non-profit organization Global Fishing Watch offers a new, convincing version of what is happening.  Global Fishing Watch accuses China of ‘ shadow fishing fleet ’  The authors of the report used various satellite technologies to analyze maritime traffic in northeast Asia in 2017 and 2018 and found that hundreds of Chinese fishing vessels were sailing in waters off North Korea.  Chinese trawlers appear to be illegally fishing in waters off the coast of North Korea, displacing the North Korean fleet itself, which is poorly equipped for long-range navigation, further from the North Korean coast into Russian and Japanese waters. According to Global Fishing Watch, in 2017 and 2018, these Chinese vessels caught more than 160,000 metric tons of Pacific Flying Squid, one of the most valuable seafood in the region, more than South Korea and Japan combined in the same period. However, vessels engaged in illegal activities in these waters, whether moving goods at sea to avoid customs prying eyes or digging sand, often lack proper documentation, making them difficult to trace.  The waters of Northeast Asia are among the most opaque and contested seas and fisheries in the world.  China, Russia, Japan, North and South Korea are all involved in some kind of territorial dispute with each other.  Fish stocks have been declining sharply in recent years, which is another serious problem that the parties have not been able to resolve. passages.title: Withdrawal from the "cultural imperialist" Whaling Commission, Japan's diplomacy turned to "Trumpism"?
passages.passage: On July 1, Japan officially re-opened the "tradition" of commercial whaling for 31 years. 9 days ago, the first batch of whalers returned to the port, bringing back a total of more than a dozen baleen whales large and small.  From Kushiro, Hokkaido, south to Shimonoseki, Yamaguchi Prefecture, the whaling craze that has not been seen for a long time, whales are slaughtered and sold in various markets, attracting many people to come and buy.  In the Kushiro market, people who have tried it have a feeling of nostalgia in addition to admiring the delicious food.  On December 26, 2018, Japan announced that it would withdraw from the International Whaling Commission (IWC) after six months, and decided to reopen the commercial whaling route, prompting criticism from many countries.  At that time, there was also a debate in Japan that the government's decision-making process was not transparent, and the idea of reviewing whether to hunt whales was also repeated and fell into heated discussion for a time.  Japan's Minister of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries, Takayama Yoshikawa, said that the resumption of whaling was the "sad wish of the people involved in the national whaling" and that although Japan withdrew from the International Whaling Commission, it still hoped that Japan would rejoin as an observer in the future to express its concern for the development of the international fishing industry.  According to Article 65 of the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS), the conservation and management of cetaceans is to be determined by "appropriate international authorities".  Originally, the International Whaling Commission was responsible for this task, after Japan's withdrawal, there will be a future Japanese whaling ship triggered by the international case may be against the court, Yoshikawa said only that "whether it will go to both sides of the complaint, but also depends on the policy judgment of various countries", now I am afraid it is too early to say.  The International Whaling Commission was established in 1946 to focus on whale conservation around the world. Japan has a long tradition of whaling since the Edo period and is the world ’ s largest consumer of whales. During the recovery period at the end of World War II, whales were once used as a source of protein for a nutritious lunch.  However, after 1970, the world's whale population significantly reduced, in order to protect the whale population, the IWC interrupted commercial whaling in 1982, and Japan finally complied with the agreement to stop commercial whaling in 1988.  However, although there is no commercial whaling, Japan continues to carry out whaling activities under the name of “survey whaling ”, but in fact, there is still a lot of whale meat coming into the market. Although the quota for survey whaling is strictly limited, it is judged that there are still many illegal sales of whale meat that are privately caught.  The taste of raw whale meat is slightly hard. It is a bit like horse meat, and the fiber is thick. It is usually eaten with ground ginger.  This time, the Japanese government has also stressed the use of a fairly high standard, from the IWC official calculation method of "no bad impact in 100 years" of the three categories of minke whales, sei whales and cloth whales.  Unlike survey whaling in the Antarctic Sea and the North Pacific, Japan has resumed commercial whaling only off the coast of Japan.  However, according to the International Convention on the Control of Whaling, signed in Washington in 1946, these three species are still listed as threatened with extinction, so the Japanese decision still attracts strong criticism from conservation groups and other foreign media.  Photo Credit: Reuters / Tachih Image Preserving Whale Culture?  Although Japan says that whaling is inherent in its traditional culture, the overall whaling market has declined significantly since it withdrew from commercial whaling in 1988, with 383 whales captured in 2018, 40% less than in 2017.  In addition to not eating whales, many young people do not know that this species has been their traditional culture.  The president of the Japan Small Whaling Association, Berryman, said: "The expansion of new routes and financial austerity, or continue to explore."  Young people do not understand whales, and in the future, they hope to at least let the local people in the fishing port experience whale cuisine again. "After 31 years of no whaling, Japan's whaling industry aging is also quite obvious, and the operators only spent a lot of time repairing their boats and whaling habitat, and they also privately told the Japanese media when they left the port:" It is a fact that they are intertwined with hope and uneasy. "In addition, because of the inability to hunt whales for the past 31 years, the Japanese government has allocated a fixed subsidy to whalers every day. Now that whaling resumes, it is like they can“ feed themselves ” and the subsidy is likely to be cut or even cancelled in 2020.  The Wall Street Journal also published an article saying that Japan's foreign policy in the future is likely to adopt a harder "Trump" line, one is to restart commercial whaling for 31 years, and the other is to directly impose semiconductor export restrictions on South Korea, the article said: "For some Japanese nationalists, after withdrawing from the IWC, which is a symbol of cultural imperialism in Europe and the United States, it is also about national independence. Say a good claim.  This use of trade as a bargaining chip in international politics is also Trump ’ s usual trick, and the newspaper said that Japan also responded to “Trump flow. ”  In addition, the Japanese government has also invested about 1.9 billion yen (about 544 million Taiwan dollars) in the resumption of whale hunting for fishing grounds and technical support for decomposition.  However, if the next 10 years still rely on government funds to continue to invest, it will still be difficult to become a self-supporting industry.  While the Japanese government is advocating the resumption of whaling, in addition to the pressure of international disapproval, what is more cruel is that the next generation has no special ideas about whaling or not. passages.title: In Japan will reduce the number of fish species available for fishing
passages.passage: Tokyo, 20: 20 — REGNUM The Japanese government plans to impose additional restrictions on the fishing of certain species of fish in coastal waters, reports NHK TV channel.  According to the plan of the Japanese government, restrictions will be imposed on 15 species of fish, including yellowtail and red sea bream.  Through this measure, the government hopes to increase the sustainability of industrial fisheries in the country and increase the total annual volume of fish caught.  Volume growth is expected to be between 1 and 4.4 tonnes over the next 10 years.  Now Japanese fishermen catch different types of fish, but with a smaller total catch.  Currently, Japan already has restrictions on catching eight species of fish, such as bluefin tuna and saury.  Government officials will consult with experts and listen to public opinion before final approval of the plan.

passages.title: Common ships will spend 6 billion yen to build new whaling mother ship
passages.passage: News from Japan (Kyodo News Agency, May 11) In the context of the commercial whaling that has resumed in Japan after 31 years in 2019, President Hideki So, the only company to carry out offshore operations, held a press conference in Tokyo on the 10th, announcing plans to spend about 6 billion yen (about 350 million yuan) to build a new whaling ship.  The company is optimistic that the Japanese government will expand the fishing quota and target sea areas in the future, and renovate the old mother ship.  Originally, it was "always said that it would cost more than 10 billion yen" (in the words of the president), but the cost was reduced by reducing the speed of the current mother ship "Nisin Maru".  It is expected to be completed in March 2024.  The government currently restricts commercial whaling to the exclusive economic zone (EEZ) of Japan, which covers only three species of minke whales, Bryde whales and Sei whales.  The new mother ship was also designed to operate outside the EEZ in the future. It can also catch large fin whales and ensure that it has the ability to reach the Antarctic waters.  The construction fee will not rely on subsidies, but will be obtained through crowdfunding through loans and online fundraising.  The president said that in order to guarantee the repayment of funds, "we hope to increase the amount of fishing in 2024."  He also stressed that the expansion of the whale meat market will be driven by higher wholesale prices and increased imports.  Japan withdrew from the International Whaling Commission (IWC) at the end of June 2019 and stopped its previous investigation of whaling activities.

passages.title: Japan ’ s Dolphin Killing Festival and the Resumption of Commercial Whaling
passages.passage: Image copyright AFP Image caption Every year for six months starting from September 1, a large-scale dolphin hunt is held in the fishing village of Taiji, Wakayama, in southern Japan.  Japan began its controversial annual dolphin hunt in the coastal town of Taiji.  Not long ago, Japan resumed commercial whaling despite international criticism.  In 2010, Dolphin Bay, a documentary film, won the Academy Award for Best Documentary, drawing global attention to the mass killing of dolphins in Japan.  The decades-old tradition in Taiji, Japan, has drawn criticism from nature and animal conservationists around the world following the release of this bloody documentary.  Dolphins are not fish, they are aquatic mammals, and they are cetaceans.  Dolphins are one of the most intelligent animals, with a friendly appearance and a playful personality, has always been very popular in human culture.  But Japan ’ s dolphin festival is their nightmare.  Dolphin killing festival and Dolphin Bay Every year for six months starting from September 1, a celebration called Dolphin Festival is held in the fishing village of Taiji Town in Wakayama, southern Japan.  Hunters drive these animals to a bay and then slaughter most of the trapped dolphins with knives and harpoons in the shallow water.  The slaughtered dolphin meat is used for food.  The remaining dolphins were sold to aquariums and marine parks.  In the past, the media reported that in the next six months, more than 20,000 dolphins and thousands of whales will be slaughtered in Taiji Bay, and the blood of the dolphins will almost stain the sea water in the bay.  In 2009, European and American marine conservationists broke through the Japanese blockade and secretly filmed a documentary, Dolphin Bay, which won the Academy Award for Best Documentary Film the following year.  The video showing the brutal killing of dolphins by fishermen in Taiji Town for the sale of dolphin meat has put the region under international pressure and controversy.  Image copyright AFP Image caption There has been much international opposition and condemnation of Japan's commercial whaling.  Environmentalists: The Hunting Extremely Cruel As the annual Dolphin Festival begins in 2019, it has become a focus of media and animal protection organizations.  Japanese media reported that the ship that went to Dolphin Bay on September 1 did not bring back any dolphins.  According to the Dolphin Project, five dolphins were killed on September 2.  The official total quota for this season allows for the killing or capture of more than 1,700 dolphins or whales.  Environmentalists say driving to hunt is extremely cruel and it can take up to 30 minutes for a dolphin to die from asphyxiation or drowning.  However, fishermen from Taiji say the livelihood of the people in the community depends on the trade.  Image copyright Getty Images / De Agostini Picture Library Image caption Japan says it is part of its culture to kill cetaceans such as dolphins.  On July 1, 2019, after Japan withdrew from the International Whaling Commission (IWC) to resume commercial whaling, its whaling fleet began a period of several months of whaling.  Commercial whaling has been banned in Japan for 31 years.  Kyodo said it was the first major international organization that Japan had withdrawn from since the end of World War II in 1945.  Whaling to the Antarctic is not a Japanese cultural tradition, but has emerged since World War II.  At that time, Japan was in ruins and its citizens lacked food and clothing.  With the encouragement of General MacArthur of the United States, Japan converted two huge US Navy ships into whaling processing vessels to travel to the Southern Ocean, which played an important role in solving the problem of Japan ’ s extreme food shortage.  Even when commercial whaling has been banned since 1986, Japanese whaling ships have killed hundreds of whales every year in the name of scientific research.  Image copyright AFP Image caption Commercial whaling after World War II played an important role in solving Japan's food shortage problem.  Japan ’ s agriculture, forestry and aquaculture officials gave the reason for whaling because eating whale meat is Japan ’ s traditional food culture, and the resumption of commercial whaling can lead to a revival of the local economy.  Apart from the reasons of cultural tradition, why does Japan insist on ignoring the international opposition to whaling?  Junko Sakuma, a former Greenpeace Japan employee interviewed by the BBC, said that whaling is operated by the Japanese government and is a huge bureaucratic structure, with research budgets, annual plans, career promotion and pension insurance benefits for relevant officials.  The constituencies concerned share the same close interests as the politicians.

passages.title: Japan to reopen commercial whaling land scholars: the United States to attract "firepower" is the best time
passages.passage: At 14: 01 on December 31, 2018, Yang Jiaxin pointed out that Japan has recently announced that it will withdraw from the International Whaling Commission (IWC) and resume commercial whaling in July next year.  Shu Jun, a researcher at the Japan Studies Center of Overseas Studies University in Shanghai's "Surging News", pointed out that although it is feared to have a negative impact on its international image, there is still a strong impetus in Japan to make such a choice.  Among them, there are elements of the whale-eating plot of the older generation of Japanese, as well as factors that politicians and local whaling industry interest groups transfer interests and carry each other.  Coupled with the "retreat" wave set off by the United States, has attracted international public fire, Japan believes this is the best time to withdraw.  Shanghai "surging news" published a Sujun article pointed out that for Japan, international coordination is its post-war repair and enhance the international image of an important link, in order to reopen commercial whaling and even withdraw from the international organization inevitably gives people the impression that it will have a negative impact on its international image.  But even so, there is still a strong impetus in Japan to make such a choice.  In the post-war era of scarcity, whale meat once again became the main non-fish meat source on the Japanese table, and whale meat dishes even appeared in free lunches for elementary school students paid for by the Japanese government.  However, today, Japan ’ s social economy has developed, whale meat is no longer irreplaceable, and many young people have never even eaten whale meat, but some older Japanese who lived in the 1950s and 1960s still occasionally miss it.  The article pointed out that, on the other hand, the real demand for whale meat in the Japanese market is very limited and shrinking, and it is better to say that the Japanese government is trying to maintain the existence of the whaling industry than to say that it is the Japanese people who cannot give up the taste of whale meat.  The Japanese government is doing this mainly out of domestic political considerations.  A whaling county-born politician who wants to stand out from his constituency as a member of Congress must look after the interests of whaling industry interests.  For example, Japan's current prime minister, Shinzo Abe, was born in Yamaguchi Prefecture, a whaling prefecture.  The article said that the reason why Japan chose to withdraw at this time should be that the ruling Abe government believes that the current international environment is the best time to withdraw.  The "retreat" of the United States, the growing anti-refugee wave in Europe, and the Brexit of the United Kingdom show that anti-globalization has risen.  There is everywhere "retreat" of the United States to attract international public opinion "firepower", Japan "homeward" withdrawal from the International Whaling Commission, in addition to the media rhetoric and criticism of individual politicians, Western countries may find it difficult to put any substantial pressure on Japan. passages.title: Japan resumes whaling after 30 years
passages.passage: Japan has left the International Whaling Commission (IWC), of which it has been a member for more than 60 years.  Now the Japanese authorities, writes Kyodo, plan to resume commercial whale hunting.  It has been banned in Japan for more than 30 years.  The decision, the agency explains, came after Tokyo ’ s latest proposal to resume whaling was rejected at the IWC ’ s annual meeting last September.  After that, Japan threatened to leave the international organization, which still does not agree on commercial whaling: some of its members are in favor of whaling, some against, others from time to time support either side.  Commenting on the situation, Japanese Cabinet Secretary General Yoshihide Suga said that the refusal of the IWS member countries to support Tokyo ’ s proposal in September last year “revealed the fact that in the organization, countries with different views, it is impossible even to try to coexist together. ”  Japan announced plans to leave the organization in December last year, which drew criticism from Greenpeace and a number of IWC members, such as Australia and New Zealand.  The International Whaling Commission was established in 1948.  Initially, it consisted of countries that supported whaling.  The purpose of this organization was to ensure “the proper conservation of whale stocks and thus enable the orderly development of whaling. ”  However, since then, more and more countries have joined the IWC, which opposed commercial whaling.  Japan has been a member of this organization since 1951.  It stopped whaling in accordance with the moratorium adopted by the Commission in 1982.  However, there are cases when whales were hunted in Japan for “research purposes ” (this happened in 1987 and in 1994), recalls Kyodo.  The international community then criticized these actions, noting that they are a cover for commercial whaling.  It is known that the meat of the caught whales, the agency said, was sold in the domestic market.  At the same time, the resumption of commercial whaling relative to individual species (such as minke whales) Tokyo, Kyodo continues, has lobbied for the past 30 years as a member of the IWC.  However, its attempts to resume whaling have each time been blocked by the so-called anti-whaling countries.  Now commercial whaling Japan, according to the Agency, plans to resume from Monday, July 1.  Hunting will be conducted within the exclusive economic zone of Japan.

passages.title: Animal Husbandry in the World + Pictures
passages.passage: They send a boat to find whales and dolphins in front of them.  After finding a flock of animals, other boats make terrible noises and sound walls as they move.  Frightened whales and dolphins swim to the bay, after the animals are exhausted, spears are thrust into their bodies, and the entire sea turns red.  Images of the sea of blood and the slaughter of animals have been repeatedly published in the media.  Japan is one of the countries that, as a tradition, kill large numbers of whales and dolphins.  Although environmental groups have repeatedly protested the move, the country withdrew from the International Whaling Commission (IWC) last year and resumed whaling.  Japan has been whaling for centuries, and its meat has been used as a key source of protein in the post-World War II years when the country was in extreme poverty.  Japanese fishermen also killed more than 300 large finned whales in the Antarctic Ocean last year, including 122 pregnant whales.  The country says it hunts for scientific research, while critics argue that killing whales is for commercial use and Japan sells and uses them for food.  In 2014, the International Court of Justice ruled that Japan ’ s Antarctic whaling program was not for scientific and research purposes and therefore had to be stopped.  However, Japanese authorities claim that the scale of whaling off beaches for commercial purposes is very small compared to whaling in the northern ocean for scientific purposes.  Apart from Japan, many other countries offer different animal sacrifices each year.  The killing of cows after bullfights in Spain, animal sacrifices in Haiti, the killing of whales in Denmark, and the killing of cows and sheep in Nepal and Africa are still held around the world, and in some cases, people are injured or killed.  Photographs published by Alistair Ward, a 22-year-old student at the University of Cambridge, of whaling in Sandavago Bay have received a lot of media attention.  People from the Faroe Islands in Denmark kill whales every year, and this tradition has been going on for centuries.  The Faroe Islands lie in northern Europe between the Norwegian Sea and the North Atlantic Ocean and are made up of 18 small islands.  Whale meat and tallow are a source of food for the nearly 59,000 islanders who are said to be spending the winter there.  The hunters at this ceremony guide the whales to the bay with their oars, and when they get close enough, the killing begins.  Even children participate in the ceremony.  Residents of the area consider whaling a collective activity that everyone can participate in.  They say this is done under national regulations and laws, so that the whales suffer the least amount of pain and suffering.  Many Faroe Islanders believe whaling is not incompatible with the ecosystem, and they hunt 800 pilot whales each year out of the 100,000 whales that surround the island.  Images of this massacre on social media caused a lot of reactions, and some of them, in response to the reaction of European animal rights defenders to the slaughter of animals in East Asia and Africa, wrote sarcastically: “Because Europeans are blond and white, the name of this work is not barbarism and the supply of meat, but the religious slaughter of Muslims is barbaric! ”  The Gadhimai Festival is another event in which thousands of cows and sheep are sacrificed.  The ceremony takes place every five years over two days in Nepal and is inspired by a Hindu religion in the village of Baryapur, which believes that sacrificing to the goddess Gadhimai will capture the devil and bring them happiness.  What animal rights advocates have been protesting at the festival is an unusual form of victimization.  In this place, the cattle are gathered in a field, and they are slashed from the back of the neck.  Animal rights advocates call it the largest animal slaughterhouse in the world because of its remarkable violence.  In addition to the whaling, the Gadhimai festival in Japan has another 3,500-year-old ceremony that takes place in Taiji.  This event is known for the hunt of dolphins by the people of the world.  The people of this city have long been engaged in fishing and whale or dolphin hunting.  Despite opposition, Taijis continue to do so for their food, claiming it has long been a source of livelihood and a part of their cultural identity.  Taiji ’ s history shows the existence of 400-year-old whaling weapons.  The World Health Organization (WHO) studied dolphin meat and declared the amount of toxins and mercury in the meat to be very high, warning people that high levels of mercury in dolphin meat cause diseases such as cancer, infertility and suppression of the immune system.  However, traditional Taiji fishermen continue to slaughter the animal, and its products can be seen in the city ’ s stores.  The people of Taiji send a boat out to hunt for the dolphins in the first place.  After finding a flock of dolphins, the other boats are arranged in the shape of an English letter V, making terrifying sounds and sound walls as they move.  Scared dolphins swim to the bay.  Then other boats chase them to throw their frightened dolphins ashore and crash into the rocks.  After the dolphins are exhausted, the spears are thrust into the bodies of these animals and the entire sea turns red.  Among the wounded dolphins, the more beautiful ones are hunted for aquariums and circuses.  In Taiji, Haiti, there is also a ceremony in which animals are killed.  Voodoo believers gather in the country in April and declare their obedience to their gods by sacrificing animals, dancing and playing music.  After the sacrifice, they pour the warm blood of the animal into a container and drink it.  Those present in the ceremony, dressed in white, shed some of this blood on themselves, and while believing that they are under the control of the spirits, they jump into the water and continue to worship.  Wearing white clothes with blood symbolizes adherence to voodoo.  Followers of the cult have combined drum dancing as an African tradition with traditional elements of the Catholic religion.  Millions of Haitians believe in voodoo, and the government adopted it as an official religion in 1960.  But in 2012, the Haitian Senate and House of Representatives decried Voodoo as the official religion with a constitutional amendment approved by their president, a move that caused widespread discontent among Haitian followers.  In Spain, bullfighting is also one of the most popular entertainment in the world.  San Fermin in Spain attracts many tourists every year.  The celebration of the release and running of angry cows among the crowd through the narrow alleys lasts a few minutes, but the celebration lasts for hours.  Cows enter the stadium after passing through the city center to witness the matador battle with the bulls.  In the past, due to the narrow streets and the lack of possibility of passing the cart, ranchers had to drive the cows on a short path to the stadium.  Over time, young people started running in front of the cows to show their courage.  Those who run in front of cows traditionally wear white shirts and trousers and a red necktie around their necks.  Every year, the ceremony leaves a number of injured and even killed.  At the end of the festivities in Spain, bullfighters circle the animals and kill them with decorated spears and knives.  Due to opposition to the ceremony, bullfighting festivals were banned in some Spanish cities, including the Canary Islands.  It is not only in rituals that animals are abused and slaughtered, but also in pictures and videos of the slaughter of pregnant cows in France, sheep in Australian slaughterhouses, the killing of goats in Thailand, the slaughter of camels in Mauritania, and the cooking of live pigs in Europe. In fact, the price of salmon to tuna is about the price, can not say how expensive.  This means that the actual market demand for whale meat is not high.  Therefore, public opinion in Japan is worried that in the reality of low supply and demand, even if the resumption of whaling, it will be difficult to let this already sunset industry "rise back to life", and the desire to revitalize the regional economy will be difficult to achieve.  Whale meat sashimi, but in fact, the price of whale meat is not particularly expensive due to the low supply and demand. (Reuters) Possible political reasons behind this.  Including Prime Minister Shinzo Abe, the constituency of the former president of the ruling Liberal Democratic Party ’ s faction, the “Chi Shih Association ”, is a land of whaling.  Therefore, there are allegations that the government is strongly promoting the resumption of whale hunting in order to continue to gain the support of local residents.  However, whether it is for cultural, industrial or political reasons, the low supply and demand of whale meat and the low price of whale meat can not be ignored, and Japan will face condemnation from international environmental groups.

report:
Japan has started hunting whales again due to several reasons.

The country officially withdrew from the International Whaling Commission (IWC) on Sunday, June 30, after 32 years to restart commercial whaling [56413e55-0f89-45e1-94f9-7626dd17cbe2]. 
This decision was made after Japan's Minister of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries, Takayama Yoshikawa, said that the resumption of whaling was the "sad wish of the people involved in the national whaling" [28c4ff25-dd87-450d-95bc-84af873027be].

One of the main reasons for Japan's decision to resume whaling is to revitalize the economy [56413e55-0f89-45e1-94f9-7626dd17cbe2]. 
Some areas that used to make a living from whaling also hope to revitalize the economy by restarting whale hunting, such as the Amikawa area in the east of Miyagi Prefecture, which was the base of the whaling port of that year [56413e55-0f89-45e1-94f9-7626dd17cbe2].

Whale meat is quite nutritious and has become an important food item for the Japanese since the end of World War II [56413e55-0f89-45e1-94f9-7626dd17cbe2]. 
However, the annual consumption of whale meat in Japan since the 1990s has been about 2,000 to 6,000 tons, and the latest figure in 2018 totals 3,000 tons [56413e55-0f89-45e1-94f9-7626dd17cbe2].

The resumption of commercial whaling is also seen as a way to maintain the existence of the whaling industry [5d5792ec-8053-43ad-948c-2ca1de7d4ea8]. 
The Japanese government is doing this mainly out of domestic political considerations [5d5792ec-8053-43ad-948c-2ca1de7d4ea8]. 
For example, Japan's current prime minister, Shinzo Abe, was born in Yamaguchi Prefecture, a whaling prefecture [5d5792ec-8053-43ad-948c-2ca1de7d4ea8].

Whaling has been a part of Japan's culture for centuries, and the country has a long history of whaling, which began in prehistoric times [56413e55-0f89-45e1-94f9-7626dd17cbe2]. 
In the Edo period, whaling gradually became an industry [56413e55-0f89-45e1-94f9-7626dd17cbe2]. 
Various parts of the whale were fully utilized, such as whale oil as a pesticide, bone nata as carving, and ambergris as a perfume [56413e55-0f89-45e1-94f9-7626dd17cbe2].

The resumption of commercial whaling is also seen as a way to gain the support of local residents [5d5792ec-8053-43ad-948c-2ca1de7d4ea8]. 
The constituency of the former president of the ruling Liberal Democratic Party's faction, the "Chi Shih Association", is a land of whaling [5d5792ec-8053-43ad-948c-2ca1de7d4ea8].

However, the actual market demand for whale meat is not high [56413e55-0f89-45e1-94f9-7626dd17cbe2]. 
The price of whale meat is not particularly expensive due to the low supply and demand [56413e55-0f89-45e1-94f9-7626dd17cbe2]. 
In the Tokyo market price in 2018, the price of "red meat level 1" whale meat used for sashimi is 1,600 yen (about HK $110) per kilogram, and the price of "umu" whale meat used for high-grade smoked is 3,000 yen (about HK $210) per kilogram [56413e55-0f89-45e1-94f9-7626dd17cbe2].

The resumption of commercial whaling has also been criticized by international environmental groups [56413e55-0f89-45e1-94f9-7626dd17cbe2]. 
The World Health Organization (WHO) has warned people that high levels of mercury in dolphin meat can cause diseases such as cancer, infertility, and suppression of the immune system [56413e55-0f89-45e1-94f9-7626dd17cbe2].

In addition, Japan's Small Whaling Association President Yoshinori Abe called the news of the resumption of commercial whaling "a shock of joy and a sense of limitlessness" [56413e55-0f89-45e1-94f9-7626dd17cbe2]. 
Prosperity again [56413e55-0f89-45e1-94f9-7626dd17cbe2].

The country plans to resume commercial whaling only off the coast of Japan [28c4ff25-dd87-450d-95bc-84af873027be]. 
However, the three species of whales that are targeted for commercial whaling, minke whales, sei whales, and cloth whales, are still listed as threatened with extinction [731b10c2-29c1-42ae-891a-8dbf676deb65].

The resumption of commercial whaling has also been criticized by conservation groups and other foreign media [28c4ff25-dd87-450d-95bc-84af873027be]. 
The International Whaling Commission was established in 1948 to focus on whale conservation around the world [731b10c2-29c1-42ae-891a-8dbf676deb65]. 
Japan has a long tradition of whaling since the Edo period and is the world's largest consumer of whales [28c4ff25-dd87-450d-95bc-84af873027be].

The resumption of commercial whaling is also seen as a way to attract "firepower" from the United States [5d5792ec-8053-43ad-948c-2ca1de7d4ea8]. 
The "retreat" of the United States, the growing anti-refugee wave in Europe, and the Brexit of the United Kingdom show that anti-globalization has risen [5d5792ec-8053-43ad-948c-2ca1de7d4ea8].
