Title: Withdrawal from the "cultural imperialist" Whaling Commission, Japan's diplomacy turned to "Trumpism"?
Content: On July 1, Japan officially re-opened the "tradition" of commercial whaling for 31 years. 9 days ago, the first batch of whalers returned to the port, bringing back a total of more than a dozen baleen whales large and small.  From Kushiro, Hokkaido, south to Shimonoseki, Yamaguchi Prefecture, the whaling craze that has not been seen for a long time, whales are slaughtered and sold in various markets, attracting many people to come and buy.  In the Kushiro market, people who have tried it have a feeling of nostalgia in addition to admiring the delicious food.  On December 26, 2018, Japan announced that it would withdraw from the International Whaling Commission (IWC) after six months, and decided to reopen the commercial whaling route, prompting criticism from many countries.  At that time, there was also a debate in Japan that the government's decision-making process was not transparent, and the idea of reviewing whether to hunt whales was also repeated and fell into heated discussion for a time.  Japan's Minister of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries, Takayama Yoshikawa, said that the resumption of whaling was the "sad wish of the people involved in the national whaling" and that although Japan withdrew from the International Whaling Commission, it still hoped that Japan would rejoin as an observer in the future to express its concern for the development of the international fishing industry.  According to Article 65 of the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS), the conservation and management of cetaceans is to be determined by "appropriate international authorities".  Originally, the International Whaling Commission was responsible for this task, after Japan's withdrawal, there will be a future Japanese whaling ship triggered by the international case may be against the court, Yoshikawa said only that "whether it will go to both sides of the complaint, but also depends on the policy judgment of various countries", now I am afraid it is too early to say.  The International Whaling Commission was established in 1946 to focus on whale conservation around the world. Japan has a long tradition of whaling since the Edo period and is the world ’ s largest consumer of whales. During the recovery period at the end of World War II, whales were once used as a source of protein for a nutritious lunch.  However, after 1970, the world's whale population significantly reduced, in order to protect the whale population, the IWC interrupted commercial whaling in 1982, and Japan finally complied with the agreement to stop commercial whaling in 1988.  However, although there is no commercial whaling, Japan continues to carry out whaling activities under the name of “survey whaling ”, but in fact, there is still a lot of whale meat coming into the market. Although the quota for survey whaling is strictly limited, it is judged that there are still many illegal sales of whale meat that are privately caught.  The taste of raw whale meat is slightly hard. It is a bit like horse meat, and the fiber is thick. It is usually eaten with ground ginger.  This time, the Japanese government has also stressed the use of a fairly high standard, from the IWC official calculation method of "no bad impact in 100 years" of the three categories of minke whales, sei whales and cloth whales.  Unlike survey whaling in the Antarctic Sea and the North Pacific, Japan has resumed commercial whaling only off the coast of Japan.  However, according to the International Convention on the Control of Whaling, signed in Washington in 1946, these three species are still listed as threatened with extinction, so the Japanese decision still attracts strong criticism from conservation groups and other foreign media.  Photo Credit: Reuters / Tachih Image Preserving Whale Culture?  Although Japan says that whaling is inherent in its traditional culture, the overall whaling market has declined significantly since it withdrew from commercial whaling in 1988, with 383 whales captured in 2018, 40% less than in 2017.  In addition to not eating whales, many young people do not know that this species has been their traditional culture.  The president of the Japan Small Whaling Association, Berryman, said: "The expansion of new routes and financial austerity, or continue to explore."  Young people do not understand whales, and in the future, they hope to at least let the local people in the fishing port experience whale cuisine again. "After 31 years of no whaling, Japan's whaling industry aging is also quite obvious, and the operators only spent a lot of time repairing their boats and whaling habitat, and they also privately told the Japanese media when they left the port:" It is a fact that they are intertwined with hope and uneasy. "In addition, because of the inability to hunt whales for the past 31 years, the Japanese government has allocated a fixed subsidy to whalers every day. Now that whaling resumes, it is like they can“ feed themselves ” and the subsidy is likely to be cut or even cancelled in 2020.  The Wall Street Journal also published an article saying that Japan's foreign policy in the future is likely to adopt a harder "Trump" line, one is to restart commercial whaling for 31 years, and the other is to directly impose semiconductor export restrictions on South Korea, the article said: "For some Japanese nationalists, after withdrawing from the IWC, which is a symbol of cultural imperialism in Europe and the United States, it is also about national independence. Say a good claim.  This use of trade as a bargaining chip in international politics is also Trump ’ s usual trick, and the newspaper said that Japan also responded to “Trump flow. ”  In addition, the Japanese government has also invested about 1.9 billion yen (about 544 million Taiwan dollars) in the resumption of whale hunting for fishing grounds and technical support for decomposition.  However, if the next 10 years still rely on government funds to continue to invest, it will still be difficult to become a self-supporting industry.  While the Japanese government is advocating the resumption of whaling, in addition to the pressure of international disapproval, what is more cruel is that the next generation has no special ideas about whaling or not. Title: In Japan will reduce the number of fish species available for fishing
Content: Tokyo, 20: 20 — REGNUM The Japanese government plans to impose additional restrictions on the fishing of certain species of fish in coastal waters, reports NHK TV channel.  According to the plan of the Japanese government, restrictions will be imposed on 15 species of fish, including yellowtail and red sea bream.  Through this measure, the government hopes to increase the sustainability of industrial fisheries in the country and increase the total annual volume of fish caught.  Volume growth is expected to be between 1 and 4.4 tonnes over the next 10 years.  Now Japanese fishermen catch different types of fish, but with a smaller total catch.  Currently, Japan already has restrictions on catching eight species of fish, such as bluefin tuna and saury.  Government officials will consult with experts and listen to public opinion before final approval of the plan.

Title: Common ships will spend 6 billion yen to build new whaling mother ship
Content: News from Japan (Kyodo News Agency, May 11) In the context of the commercial whaling that has resumed in Japan after 31 years in 2019, President Hideki So, the only company to carry out offshore operations, held a press conference in Tokyo on the 10th, announcing plans to spend about 6 billion yen (about 350 million yuan) to build a new whaling ship.  The company is optimistic that the Japanese government will expand the fishing quota and target sea areas in the future, and renovate the old mother ship.  Originally, it was "always said that it would cost more than 10 billion yen" (in the words of the president), but the cost was reduced by reducing the speed of the current mother ship "Nisin Maru".  It is expected to be completed in March 2024.  The government currently restricts commercial whaling to the exclusive economic zone (EEZ) of Japan, which covers only three species of minke whales, Bryde whales and Sei whales.  The new mother ship was also designed to operate outside the EEZ in the future. It can also catch large fin whales and ensure that it has the ability to reach the Antarctic waters.  The construction fee will not rely on subsidies, but will be obtained through crowdfunding through loans and online fundraising.  The president said that in order to guarantee the repayment of funds, "we hope to increase the amount of fishing in 2024."  He also stressed that the expansion of the whale meat market will be driven by higher wholesale prices and increased imports.  Japan withdrew from the International Whaling Commission (IWC) at the end of June 2019 and stopped its previous investigation of whaling activities.

Title: Japan ’ s Dolphin Killing Festival and the Resumption of Commercial Whaling
Content: Image copyright AFP Image caption Every year for six months starting from September 1, a large-scale dolphin hunt is held in the fishing village of Taiji, Wakayama, in southern Japan.  Japan began its controversial annual dolphin hunt in the coastal town of Taiji.  Not long ago, Japan resumed commercial whaling despite international criticism.  In 2010, Dolphin Bay, a documentary film, won the Academy Award for Best Documentary, drawing global attention to the mass killing of dolphins in Japan.  The decades-old tradition in Taiji, Japan, has drawn criticism from nature and animal conservationists around the world following the release of this bloody documentary.  Dolphins are not fish, they are aquatic mammals, and they are cetaceans.  Dolphins are one of the most intelligent animals, with a friendly appearance and a playful personality, has always been very popular in human culture.  But Japan ’ s dolphin festival is their nightmare.  Dolphin killing festival and Dolphin Bay Every year for six months starting from September 1, a celebration called Dolphin Festival is held in the fishing village of Taiji Town in Wakayama, southern Japan.  Hunters drive these animals to a bay and then slaughter most of the trapped dolphins with knives and harpoons in the shallow water.  The slaughtered dolphin meat is used for food.  The remaining dolphins were sold to aquariums and marine parks.  In the past, the media reported that in the next six months, more than 20,000 dolphins and thousands of whales will be slaughtered in Taiji Bay, and the blood of the dolphins will almost stain the sea water in the bay.  In 2009, European and American marine conservationists broke through the Japanese blockade and secretly filmed a documentary, Dolphin Bay, which won the Academy Award for Best Documentary Film the following year.  The video showing the brutal killing of dolphins by fishermen in Taiji Town for the sale of dolphin meat has put the region under international pressure and controversy.  Image copyright AFP Image caption There has been much international opposition and condemnation of Japan's commercial whaling.  Environmentalists: The Hunting Extremely Cruel As the annual Dolphin Festival begins in 2019, it has become a focus of media and animal protection organizations.  Japanese media reported that the ship that went to Dolphin Bay on September 1 did not bring back any dolphins.  According to the Dolphin Project, five dolphins were killed on September 2.  The official total quota for this season allows for the killing or capture of more than 1,700 dolphins or whales.  Environmentalists say driving to hunt is extremely cruel and it can take up to 30 minutes for a dolphin to die from asphyxiation or drowning.  However, fishermen from Taiji say the livelihood of the people in the community depends on the trade.  Image copyright Getty Images / De Agostini Picture Library Image caption Japan says it is part of its culture to kill cetaceans such as dolphins.  On July 1, 2019, after Japan withdrew from the International Whaling Commission (IWC) to resume commercial whaling, its whaling fleet began a period of several months of whaling.  Commercial whaling has been banned in Japan for 31 years.  Kyodo said it was the first major international organization that Japan had withdrawn from since the end of World War II in 1945.  Whaling to the Antarctic is not a Japanese cultural tradition, but has emerged since World War II.  At that time, Japan was in ruins and its citizens lacked food and clothing.  With the encouragement of General MacArthur of the United States, Japan converted two huge US Navy ships into whaling processing vessels to travel to the Southern Ocean, which played an important role in solving the problem of Japan ’ s extreme food shortage.  Even when commercial whaling has been banned since 1986, Japanese whaling ships have killed hundreds of whales every year in the name of scientific research.  Image copyright AFP Image caption Commercial whaling after World War II played an important role in solving Japan's food shortage problem.  Japan ’ s agriculture, forestry and aquaculture officials gave the reason for whaling because eating whale meat is Japan ’ s traditional food culture, and the resumption of commercial whaling can lead to a revival of the local economy.  Apart from the reasons of cultural tradition, why does Japan insist on ignoring the international opposition to whaling?  Junko Sakuma, a former Greenpeace Japan employee interviewed by the BBC, said that whaling is operated by the Japanese government and is a huge bureaucratic structure, with research budgets, annual plans, career promotion and pension insurance benefits for relevant officials.  The constituencies concerned share the same close interests as the politicians.

Content: At 14: 01 on December 31, 2018, Yang Jiaxin pointed out that Japan has recently announced that it will withdraw from the International Whaling Commission (IWC) and resume commercial whaling in July next year.  Shu Jun, a researcher at the Japan Studies Center of Overseas Studies University in Shanghai's "Surging News", pointed out that although it is feared to have a negative impact on its international image, there is still a strong impetus in Japan to make such a choice.  Among them, there are elements of the whale-eating plot of the older generation of Japanese, as well as factors that politicians and local whaling industry interest groups transfer interests and carry each other.  Coupled with the "retreat" wave set off by the United States, has attracted international public fire, Japan believes this is the best time to withdraw.  Shanghai "surging news" published a Sujun article pointed out that for Japan, international coordination is its post-war repair and enhance the international image of an important link, in order to reopen commercial whaling and even withdraw from the international organization inevitably gives people the impression that it will have a negative impact on its international image.  But even so, there is still a strong impetus in Japan to make such a choice.  In the post-war era of scarcity, whale meat once again became the main non-fish meat source on the Japanese table, and whale meat dishes even appeared in free lunches for elementary school students paid for by the Japanese government.  However, today, Japan ’ s social economy has developed, whale meat is no longer irreplaceable, and many young people have never even eaten whale meat, but some older Japanese who lived in the 1950s and 1960s still occasionally miss it.  The article pointed out that, on the other hand, the real demand for whale meat in the Japanese market is very limited and shrinking, and it is better to say that the Japanese government is trying to maintain the existence of the whaling industry than to say that it is the Japanese people who cannot give up the taste of whale meat. For example, Japan's current prime minister, Shinzo Abe, was born in Yamaguchi Prefecture, a whaling prefecture.  The article said that the reason why Japan chose to withdraw at this time should be that the ruling Abe government believes that the current international environment is the best time to withdraw. Title: Japan resumes whaling after 30 years
Content: Japan has left the International Whaling Commission (IWC), of which it has been a member for more than 60 years.  Now the Japanese authorities, writes Kyodo, plan to resume commercial whale hunting.  It has been banned in Japan for more than 30 years.  The decision, the agency explains, came after Tokyo ’ s latest proposal to resume whaling was rejected at the IWC ’ s annual meeting last September.  After that, Japan threatened to leave the international organization, which still does not agree on commercial whaling: some of its members are in favor of whaling, some against, others from time to time support either side.  Commenting on the situation, Japanese Cabinet Secretary General Yoshihide Suga said that the refusal of the IWS member countries to support Tokyo ’ s proposal in September last year “revealed the fact that in the organization, countries with different views, it is impossible even to try to coexist together. ”  Japan announced plans to leave the organization in December last year, which drew criticism from Greenpeace and a number of IWC members, such as Australia and New Zealand.  The International Whaling Commission was established in 1948.  Initially, it consisted of countries that supported whaling.  The purpose of this organization was to ensure “the proper conservation of whale stocks and thus enable the orderly development of whaling. ”  However, since then, more and more countries have joined the IWC, which opposed commercial whaling.  Japan has been a member of this organization since 1951.  It stopped whaling in accordance with the moratorium adopted by the Commission in 1982.  However, there are cases when whales were hunted in Japan for “research purposes ” (this happened in 1987 and in 1994), recalls Kyodo.  The international community then criticized these actions, noting that they are a cover for commercial whaling.  It is known that the meat of the caught whales, the agency said, was sold in the domestic market.  At the same time, the resumption of commercial whaling relative to individual species (such as minke whales) Tokyo, Kyodo continues, has lobbied for the past 30 years as a member of the IWC.  However, its attempts to resume whaling have each time been blocked by the so-called anti-whaling countries.  Now commercial whaling Japan, according to the Agency, plans to resume from Monday, July 1.  Hunting will be conducted within the exclusive economic zone of Japan.

Title: Animal Husbandry in the World + Pictures
Content: They send a boat to find whales and dolphins in front of them.  After finding a flock of animals, other boats make terrible noises and sound walls as they move.  Frightened whales and dolphins swim to the bay, after the animals are exhausted, spears are thrust into their bodies, and the entire sea turns red.  Images of the sea of blood and the slaughter of animals have been repeatedly published in the media.  Japan is one of the countries that, as a tradition, kill large numbers of whales and dolphins.  Although environmental groups have repeatedly protested the move, the country withdrew from the International Whaling Commission (IWC) last year and resumed whaling.  Japan has been whaling for centuries, and its meat has been used as a key source of protein in the post-World War II years when the country was in extreme poverty.  Japanese fishermen also killed more than 300 large finned whales in the Antarctic Ocean last year, including 122 pregnant whales.  The country says it hunts for scientific research, while critics argue that killing whales is for commercial use and Japan sells and uses them for food.  In 2014, the International Court of Justice ruled that Japan ’ s Antarctic whaling program was not for scientific and research purposes and therefore had to be stopped.  However, Japanese authorities claim that the scale of whaling off beaches for commercial purposes is very small compared to whaling in the northern ocean for scientific purposes.  Apart from Japan, many other countries offer different animal sacrifices each year.  The killing of cows after bullfights in Spain, animal sacrifices in Haiti, the killing of whales in Denmark, and the killing of cows and sheep in Nepal and Africa are still held around the world, and in some cases, people are injured or killed.  Photographs published by Alistair Ward, a 22-year-old student at the University of Cambridge, of whaling in Sandavago Bay have received a lot of media attention.  People from the Faroe Islands in Denmark kill whales every year, and this tradition has been going on for centuries.  The Faroe Islands lie in northern Europe between the Norwegian Sea and the North Atlantic Ocean and are made up of 18 small islands.  Whale meat and tallow are a source of food for the nearly 59,000 islanders who are said to be spending the winter there.  The hunters at this ceremony guide the whales to the bay with their oars, and when they get close enough, the killing begins.  Even children participate in the ceremony.  Residents of the area consider whaling a collective activity that everyone can participate in.  They say this is done under national regulations and laws, so that the whales suffer the least amount of pain and suffering.  Many Faroe Islanders believe whaling is not incompatible with the ecosystem, and they hunt 800 pilot whales each year out of the 100,000 whales that surround the island.  Images of this massacre on social media caused a lot of reactions, and some of them, in response to the reaction of European animal rights defenders to the slaughter of animals in East Asia and Africa, wrote sarcastically: “Because Europeans are blond and white, the name of this work is not barbarism and the supply of meat, but the religious slaughter of Muslims is barbaric! ”  The Gadhimai Festival is another event in which thousands of cows and sheep are sacrificed. After World War II, Japan ’ s whaling industry soared due to food shortages and foreign exchange earnings. In the 1950s, Japan became the world ’ s largest whaling nation, with domestic consumption peaking at 233,000 tons in 1962.  In 1982, the IWC passed the Convention on the Prohibition of Commercial Whaling. Japan initially objected, but after the objection was rejected in 1986, Japan finally promised to gradually ban commercial whaling, and commercial whaling ceased in 1988.  However, commercial whaling does not mean that whaling will no longer be done. In fact, Japan has set up a new category of "survey whaling" to continue whaling on the grounds of "scientific research". Title: Japan ’ s Dolphin Killing Festival and the Resumption of Commercial Whaling
Content: Image copyright AFP Image caption Every year for six months starting from September 1, a large-scale dolphin hunt is held in the fishing village of Taiji, Wakayama, in southern Japan.  Japan began its controversial annual dolphin hunt in the coastal town of Taiji.  Not long ago, Japan resumed commercial whaling despite international criticism. The decades-old tradition in Taiji, Japan, has drawn criticism from nature and animal conservationists around the world following the release of this bloody documentary.  Dolphins are not fish, they are aquatic mammals, and they are cetaceans.  Dolphins are one of the most intelligent animals, with a friendly appearance and a playful personality, has always been very popular in human culture.  But Japan ’ s dolphin festival is their nightmare.  Dolphin killing festival and Dolphin Bay Every year for six months starting from September 1, a celebration called Dolphin Festival is held in the fishing village of Taiji Town in Wakayama, southern Japan.  Hunters drive these animals to a bay and then slaughter most of the trapped dolphins with knives and harpoons in the shallow water.  The slaughtered dolphin meat is used for food.  The remaining dolphins were sold to aquariums and marine parks.  In the past, the media reported that in the next six months, more than 20,000 dolphins and thousands of whales will be slaughtered in Taiji Bay, and the blood of the dolphins will almost stain the sea water in the bay.  In 2009, European and American marine conservationists broke through the Japanese blockade and secretly filmed a documentary, Dolphin Bay, which won the Academy Award for Best Documentary Film the following year.  The video showing the brutal killing of dolphins by fishermen in Taiji Town for the sale of dolphin meat has put the region under international pressure and controversy. Japanese media reported that the ship that went to Dolphin Bay on September 1 did not bring back any dolphins.  According to the Dolphin Project, five dolphins were killed on September 2.  The official total quota for this season allows for the killing or capture of more than 1,700 dolphins or whales.  Environmentalists say driving to hunt is extremely cruel and it can take up to 30 minutes for a dolphin to die from asphyxiation or drowning. Whaling to the Antarctic is not a Japanese cultural tradition, but has emerged since World War II.  At that time, Japan was in ruins and its citizens lacked food and clothing. Title: Japan resumes whaling after 30 years

Now the Japanese authorities, writes Kyodo, plan to resume commercial whale hunting.  It has been banned in Japan for more than 30 years.  The decision, the agency explains, came after Tokyo ’ s latest proposal to resume whaling was rejected at the IWC ’ s annual meeting last September.  After that, Japan threatened to leave the international organization, which still does not agree on commercial whaling: some of its members are in favor of whaling, some against, others from time to time support either side. Japan has been a member of this organization since 1951.  It stopped whaling in accordance with the moratorium adopted by the Commission in 1982.  However, there are cases when whales were hunted in Japan for “research purposes ” (this happened in 1987 and in 1994), recalls Kyodo.  The international community then criticized these actions, noting that they are a cover for commercial whaling.  It is known that the meat of the caught whales, the agency said, was sold in the domestic market.  At the same time, the resumption of commercial whaling relative to individual species (such as minke whales) Tokyo, Kyodo continues, has lobbied for the past 30 years as a member of the IWC.  However, its attempts to resume whaling have each time been blocked by the so-called anti-whaling countries. Every year, the ceremony leaves a number of injured and even killed.  At the end of the festivities in Spain, bullfighters circle the animals and kill them with decorated spears and knives. Title: 【 News Classroom 】 Despite global criticism, when did Japan restart commercial whaling after 32 years? ｜ Hong Kong 01 ｜ The World Says
Content: Japan officially withdrew from the International Whaling Commission (IWC) on Sunday (June 30), after 32 years to restart commercial whaling.  A number of whalers were greeted by local residents and sailed out of the harbour.  Japan is one of the few countries that still hunt whales. Today, let ’ s introduce Japan ’ s whaling history, the reasons for restarting whaling and the current state of the whaling industry.  A number of whaling vessels are moored at the wharf in Kushiro City, Hokkaido, waiting to sail. (Reuters) ↓ ↓ For more photos of whaling, please click to enlarge: + 4 + 3 + 2 Japan Whaling History Japan has a long history of whaling, which began in prehistoric times.  The word "fish" in the Nara period "Manye Collection" is an ancient Japanese word for whaling.  In the Edo period, whaling gradually became an industry. In addition to being used for food, various parts of the whale were fully utilized, such as whale oil as a pesticide, bone nata as carving, and ambergris as a perfume.  After World War II, Japan ’ s whaling industry soared due to food shortages and foreign exchange earnings. In the 1950s, Japan became the world ’ s largest whaling nation, with domestic consumption peaking at 233,000 tons in 1962.  In 1982, the IWC passed the Convention on the Prohibition of Commercial Whaling. Japan initially objected, but after the objection was rejected in 1986, Japan finally promised to gradually ban commercial whaling, and commercial whaling ceased in 1988.  However, commercial whaling does not mean that whaling will no longer be done. In fact, Japan has set up a new category of "survey whaling" to continue whaling on the grounds of "scientific research".  According to the report of the Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries, the annual consumption of whale meat in Japan since the 1990s has been about 2,000 to 6,000 tons, and the latest figure in 2018 totals 3,000 tons.  Japan has a long history of whaling, which has become an industry as early as the Edo period. (Getty Images) Revitalizing the economy with the help of Whaling Japan ’ s Small Whaling Association President Yoshinori Abe called the news of the resumption of commercial whaling “a shock of joy and a sense of limitlessness. ” Prosperity again.  Some areas that used to make a living from whaling also hope to revitalize the economy by restarting whale hunting, such as the Amikawa area in the east of Miyagi Prefecture, which was the base of the whaling port of that year.  After extensive damage during the Great East Japan Earthquake, residents hope to revive the local economy by reviving the whaling industry. A museum dedicated to introducing whaling culture is planned for April 2020 to attract visitors.  Whale meat is quite nutritious and has become an important food item for the Japanese since the end of World War II. (Reuters) Whale meat is not expensive, but it should be noted that since the 1970s, whaling in Japan has declined year by year, and today whale meat is no longer a common dish in Japan.  Compared to the annual consumption of 6 million tons of pork and chicken, only 3,000 tons of whale meat is really insignificant.  And interestingly, whale meat has not become expensive due to reduced availability.  In the Tokyo market price in 2018, the price of "red meat level 1" whale meat used for sashimi is 1,600 yen (about HK $110) per kilogram, and the price of "umu" whale meat used for high-grade smoked is 3,000 yen (about HK $210) per kilogram.  In fact, the price of salmon to tuna is about the price, can not say how expensive.  This means that the actual market demand for whale meat is not high.  Therefore, public opinion in Japan is worried that in the reality of low supply and demand, even if the resumption of whaling, it will be difficult to let this already sunset industry "rise back to life", and the desire to revitalize the regional economy will be difficult to achieve.  Whale meat sashimi, but in fact, the price of whale meat is not particularly expensive due to the low supply and demand. (Reuters) Possible political reasons behind this.  Including Prime Minister Shinzo Abe, the constituency of the former president of the ruling Liberal Democratic Party ’ s faction, the “Chi Shih Association ”, is a land of whaling.  Therefore, there are allegations that the government is strongly promoting the resumption of whale hunting in order to continue to gain the support of local residents.  However, whether it is for cultural, industrial or political reasons, the low supply and demand of whale meat and the low price of whale meat can not be ignored, and Japan will face condemnation from international environmental groups.

passages.passage: Many viewers who watched the play “The Old Man and the Sea ” in the Buryat Drama Theater perceive the Cuban old man Santiago and the artist Bastu Tsydenov as one.  The actor is so harmonious in this role.  From the play of a large form “The Old Man and the Sea ” in 2015 turned into a mono-parable.  There is one actor on the stage who, with the help of symbolic objects and sounds of morin-huura, talks about the fact that “a person cannot be defeated ”.  I lacked freedom.  It is important for me to be free in my role.  When the theater critic Anna Stepanova looked, she said: “Maybe you can do a mono? ”  I told Oleg (director Oleg Yumov – approx. ed.), they did it with him, and really...  I got my freedom.  I have been playing for two or three years.  So much is opened with every show.  In this, probably, the buzz of creativity, - shares his thoughts Basta Tsydenov.  The artist admits that "The Old Man and the Sea" is one of his favorite performances, and Ernest Hemingway is one of his favorite authors: - A high word, a deep word, a deep thought, a deep pain, a deep meaningfulness of this life, tragedy, joy of man.  This, on the one hand, is a very simple pain of a simple man, a simple fisherman: just live, survive, not starve to death, remember the good, remember the love, forgive.  These are the simplest, human feelings of thought, emotions.  That's why I like Hemingway.  He is a very simple writer himself.  He has a very simple syllable.  He writes very simply, harshly, does not feel sorry for himself or for us.  He goes deep, deep.  He is a man who has lived a lot, acted a lot in his life.  He went to the hottest spots, fought, went to love, to women.  He did not do a little, so he writes also. - Can you say that you are? - I am far from that.  I have a lot of egoism, I am a person who is fond of theater.  Theatre is a broad concept...  These are literature, life, art, images, artists in a broad sense, struggles, defeats, women.  For any artist, women mean a lot.  High poetry of love - What role do women play in your life?  Have you loved? - Many times got carried away, many times fell in love, but, looking back...  These were defeats and discoveries, you will know not only women, you will know yourself, your background, your kind, tender, subtle feelings.  It's developing.  Love is always creativity.  The deeper you go into love, the more tragedy, the more pain.  It is high poetry, high art, high drama, it is always beauty and tragedy.  When it comes separately, it ’ s very boring.  She is so beautiful, that ’ s all.  Or very primitive pain.  Basta Tsydenov, a favorite of women, has loved himself more than once.  Officially, he was married three times, he has three children and one granddaughter.  However, the main love of his life is the theater. - My sacrifice for the sake of art is family.  First of all, I put on the theater, my work.  And family is always in the second, in the third plan.  There is always pity, regret.  I could have saved my family, tried, but I couldn't.  Then it seemed that something was more important.  That for me, for my work, for my art, a woman must sacrifice her personal ambition.  But I did not meet such a woman.  On the contrary, I feel sorry for them.  Although, I don't know, maybe it's a good thing we met.  That we have children in common.  I love them, I help them as much as I can.  Communicating.  The kids are nice to me, great relationships.  In the creative baggage of Basta Tsydenov more than 80 roles.  In each he never ceases to know himself, shares the actor.  His first major role was at 25.  He played the groom in the play "Wedding" in the Buryat Drama Theater.  In the difficult 90 ’ s for the whole country, Basta Guruevich admits that he was experiencing a personal crisis.  He decided to leave the storm.  - I felt devastated, I didn't know what to do, I was sad, I was sad, I was bored.  It's about me, not the theater.  Personal life kubarem.  One day I just decided to leave.  I haven't been to the theater in 12 years.  Wandering around Moscow, in Europe, he says.  Basta Tsydenov participated in the project “White Deer ” by the German director Betin Voevoda, in the seminars of the great Japanese experimental director Tadashi Suzuki.  With special warmth, Basta Guruevich recalls common projects with the students of Anatoly Vasiliev - Klim (Vladimir Klimenko, theater director, playwright, screenwriter - approx. ed.) and Boris Yukhananov (artistic director of the Stanislavsky Electrotheatre - approx. ed.): - Boris invited me to play the role of a shaman in Faust.  There was a performance for 8 hours, I went out 15-16 times, I did rituals.  He gave me total freedom.  I was thinking about the rituals I remember from the storm.  He made up whole dialogues for me.  I was with Faust, I argued with him, supported him sometimes.  We performed at the RAMT (Russian Academic Youth Theater - approx. ed.) twice, at the Stanislavsky Theater 3-4 times.  He lied to everyone there that I was a real shaman from Buryatia.  Everyone looked at me with caution.  I didn't know he was out there, lying.  In "Hamlet" he played, there were two more projects according to his script.  In the capital of Russia, the actor found, as they say, his director.  It was in the Moscow period of the artist ’ s life that he met Oleg Yumov, who studied at GITIS.  Later, returning to Buryatia, Basta Tsydenov will play the main roles in almost all Buryat performances of Yumov.  Their creative tandem is based on friendship, says the artist: - To have your own director or a person who is close in spirit, blood, interesting - this is a very great success for the actor.  I'm an actor.  I tried, I staged Duck Hunt, Moscow critics and speakers at the Vampilov Festival noted.  But I prefer to play.  For the performance of the main role in the play “Maxar.  Steppe in Blood "Basta Guruevich was nominated for the" Golden Mask "for the" Best male role ", was awarded the diploma of the festival" Siberian transit "in Barnaul in the nomination" Best male role ".  And the old man Santiago brought the artist a "Mongolian Oscar" - a victory in the festival "Gagan Muse" in Ulaanbaatar.  Today, Basta Tsydenov works as an artist in the Buryat Drama Theater, and also opened his school of oratorical skills, where he teaches children, as he says, to be free.  Although the question of whether he himself is free, he answers: - I have been striving for this all my life.  I can ’ t say I ’ m a free person, but I think there ’ s freedom.  I do what I want... what I feel, I do it.  In creativity it is necessary to tear, go to the depth, to the width, to destroy.  In a good way.  Destroy stereotypes.  Some framework, foundations, to destroy what was once done well.  A new feel.  Press service of the theater

passages.title: How to read Hemingway?
passages.passage: Ernest Hemingway, a Nobel laureate and one of the most important of the 20th century, was born on July 21, 1899 in Illinois and wrote seven novels, six collections of short stories and two nonfiction books during his lifetime.  On the occasion of the birth of this author, which coincided with the thirteenth of July, we have suggestions for better reading of the works of this author.  Hemingway ’ s work is fluid, simple, and clear, but for many readers of literature, it may be difficult to begin reading Hemingway ’ s books.  Why read Hemingway?  Ernest Hemingway is an influential writer in the history of literature and fiction, his works have repeatedly won the most prestigious international literary awards such as Nobel and Pulitzer, this author employed a different kind of narrative description and caused many writers after him to borrow his own literary style.  Hemingway has named his literary style the Iceberg Theory, in this way of writing, fictional events are narrated like an iceberg floating in water, only one-eighth of which is visible, and the author includes only the information that is essential in the process and omits the rest of the information.  This technique created a tremendous change in storytelling, especially the writing of short stories, and it was a development that freed the stories from conventional chatter.  Hemingway ’ s works are included in the list of books of the century, books to read before death, and the best fiction books in history, highlighting the importance of this author.  What do we need to know?  One of the topics that helps to better understand Ernest Hemingway ’ s work is getting to know his personal life.  Much of what we read in his books is what he has turned from his personal life into a story.  At the age of 19, he volunteered for the First World War but was not allowed to fight because of poor eyesight, but Hemingway insisted on serving as an ambulance driver for the Red Cross.  He was wounded several times during the Chang, but his most significant injury is when he was wounded by mortar shell fragments and spent a long time in the hospital, a novel about this part of Hemingway ’ s life and the war.  Even the character of Catherine Barkley in this book is based on the nurse Hemingway fell in love with.  Hemingway also participated in World War II as a war correspondent, and several short stories are the result of this era.  The sun continues to blow, the Great River or along the river to the trees, each of which is somehow tied to the World War, and their heroes are survivors of the war and have many memories of these days.  But Hemingway ’ s most important masterpiece is a relic of his childhood, Hemingway ’ s father had a great interest in fishing, and this hobby was passed on to Ernest, a point that can be clearly seen in the famous and widely read story of The Old Man and the Sea.  But before the Old Man and the Sea, Hemingway had written about having and not having a fishing boat captain.  Another important point to know before reading Hemingway ’ s works is his political approach, he has written a lot in opposition to fascism and against dictatorship, both as a journalist and as a writer, sometimes even changing from a journalist to a social-political activist, who is this point in The Bell for, or who is this death knell?  It is a story of an American soldier in the Spanish Civil War fighting alongside groups against General Franco, which Hemingway did.  Perhaps the other thing that matters is that during the World War, Hemingway led a French group against the Nazis that was tried after the war for armed acts but was never proven guilty.  The political and social history of the world in the years of Hemingway's life, his personal life, as well as the knowledge of his contemporaries, such as Scott Fitzgerald, with whom he has written, are points that contribute to the understanding of his works.  Getting to know Hemingway ’ s contemporary writers helps to better understand the difference between him and his contemporaries.  Is it a classic?  To read Hemingway ’ s work, we must note that he is not a classic writer in his different style, he did not deal with the long margins and descriptions of classical literature, and his long novels are not immune.  He was interested in shorthand and engaging the audience with fiction, which is a feature of modern literature.  In general, Hemingway ’ s works are innovative and even among modern works have their own creativity, but the value of this author ’ s work has always been compared to classical works, and even classical enthusiasts have not been able to be indifferent to it.  In these works we have a happy and well-spoken writer, a writer who was in middle age with young people and was even close friends with a group of hippies.  Hemingway is a realistic writer, but he has always tried to maintain his sense of humor.  Where do we start?  To read Hemingway ’ s works, the first and most important suggestion is The Old Man and the Sea.  The book, translated by Najaf Daryabandari, was published in 222 pages by Kharazmi Publications.  The next book, Farewell to Arms, is again translated by Najaf Daryabendari, published by Amir Kabir Publications in 343 pages.  These two books are always on the list of works to be read or masterpieces of the 20th century.  If you are interested in short stories, you can also read Men Without Women, a collection of stories that have been published in various magazines by the author.  This book has been translated by Asadollah Amraei for publication of Horizon in 222 pages.  Even if you are interested in writing, Hemingway can be a good teacher and read his series of talks and learn very precise points.  The book The Last Interview and Other Conversations of Ernest Hemingway with a translation by Houshang Jirani has been published in 88 pages by Cheshmeh Publishing.  The final chapter of many critics considered Ernest Hemingway to be the greatest writer of the 20th century.  His stories are an exploration of real human life, suffering and the meaning of life.  The portrayal of human inner feelings is the most important characteristic of this author, which makes his works a read for every reader.  Who was Ernest Hemingway?  Ernest Hemingway was born on July 21, 1899 in Oak Park, Illinois.  His father, Clarence, was a doctor and his mother, Grace, was a piano and singing teacher.  Ernest spent the summers with his family in northern Michigan, where he discovered his passion for fishing.  After finishing high school, he worked for a while in Kansas City as a reporter for the Star Chronicle in 1917.  During World War I, he volunteered to serve in the army, but poor eyesight prevented him from doing so, instead serving as an ambulance driver for the Red Cross near the Italian front.  On July 8, 1918, he was injured and spent months in the hospital.  In 1925, his first collection of short stories, in our time, was published, which spoke well of his particular style.  His memoirs from that period were published after his death in 1964 as The Variable Eid.  Ernest Hemingway was an adventurer for most of his life.  From being wounded in Italy by 200 pieces of Austrian shrapnel during World War I, to taking part in the frontlines of the Spanish Civil War or touring the African wilderness, to fishing and hunting wildlife and living in Cuba.  He finally said goodbye to life with his hunting rifle.

Ernest Hemingway was a renowned American writer, known for his distinctive writing style that has been widely acclaimed for its simplicity, clarity, and concision.

Hemingway's writing style is characterized by its ability to convey complex ideas and emotions through a limited use of words, as he once said, "In creativity it is necessary to tear, go to the depth, to the width, to destroy" [d5c940e7-9f36-4fc8-9d45-b3ed3be638e5]. 
This approach has been praised for its ability to create a sense of intimacy and immediacy with the reader.

Many critics have noted that Hemingway's writing style is marked by its use of simple, direct language, which allows the reader to focus on the essential elements of the story. 
As one critic noted, "Hemingway's prose is like a scalpel - it cuts to the heart of the matter, leaving out all the unnecessary words" [d4bb785c-1067-4a4f-a706-a559c8010616].

Hemingway's writing style has also been praised for its ability to evoke a sense of time and place. 
His use of descriptive language, such as his vivid descriptions of the natural world, has been noted for its ability to transport the reader to a different time and place.

In addition to his literary style, Hemingway was also known for his ability to convey complex emotions and ideas through his writing. 
As one critic noted, "Hemingway's writing is like a mirror - it reflects the deepest desires and fears of the human heart" [d2492a5c-fd41-42aa-a144-e31454b1b4aa].

Hemingway's writing style has been compared to that of other great writers, such as Fyodor Dostoevsky and Leo Tolstoy. 
However, Hemingway's unique approach to writing has been praised for its ability to create a sense of universality and timelessness.

In his own words, Hemingway described his writing style as "the iceberg theory", where only a small part of the story is visible above the surface, while the rest is hidden beneath [4e834b0f-1217-47cf-9407-8ae45e74f7c7]. 
This approach has been praised for its ability to create a sense of mystery and intrigue.

Overall, Hemingway's writing style is characterized by its simplicity, clarity, and concision, making it one of the most distinctive and influential writing styles of the 20th century.

Hemingway's writing style has been widely studied and admired, and his influence can be seen in many other writers and artists.

In conclusion, Hemingway's writing style is a unique and powerful tool for conveying complex ideas and emotions, and his influence can still be felt today.

Title: Basta Tsydenov: “In creativity it is necessary to tear, go to the depth, to the width, to destroy ”
Content: Many viewers who watched the play “The Old Man and the Sea ” in the Buryat Drama Theater perceive the Cuban old man Santiago and the artist Bastu Tsydenov as one.  The actor is so harmonious in this role.  From the play of a large form “The Old Man and the Sea ” in 2015 turned into a mono-parable.  There is one actor on the stage who, with the help of symbolic objects and sounds of morin-huura, talks about the fact that “a person cannot be defeated ”.  I lacked freedom.  It is important for me to be free in my role.  When the theater critic Anna Stepanova looked, she said: “Maybe you can do a mono? ”  I told Oleg (director Oleg Yumov – approx. ed.), they did it with him, and really...  I got my freedom.  I have been playing for two or three years.  So much is opened with every show.  In this, probably, the buzz of creativity, - shares his thoughts Basta Tsydenov.  The artist admits that "The Old Man and the Sea" is one of his favorite performances, and Ernest Hemingway is one of his favorite authors: - A high word, a deep word, a deep thought, a deep pain, a deep meaningfulness of this life, tragedy, joy of man.  This, on the one hand, is a very simple pain of a simple man, a simple fisherman: just live, survive, not starve to death, remember the good, remember the love, forgive.  These are the simplest, human feelings of thought, emotions.  That's why I like Hemingway.  He is a very simple writer himself.  He has a very simple syllable.  He writes very simply, harshly, does not feel sorry for himself or for us.  He goes deep, deep.  He is a man who has lived a lot, acted a lot in his life.  He went to the hottest spots, fought, went to love, to women.  He did not do a little, so he writes also. - Can you say that you are? - I am far from that.  I have a lot of egoism, I am a person who is fond of theater.  Theatre is a broad concept...  These are literature, life, art, images, artists in a broad sense, struggles, defeats, women.  For any artist, women mean a lot.  High poetry of love - What role do women play in your life?  Have you loved? - Many times got carried away, many times fell in love, but, looking back...  These were defeats and discoveries, you will know not only women, you will know yourself, your background, your kind, tender, subtle feelings.  It's developing.  Love is always creativity.  The deeper you go into love, the more tragedy, the more pain.  It is high poetry, high art, high drama, it is always beauty and tragedy.  When it comes separately, it ’ s very boring.  She is so beautiful, that ’ s all.  Or very primitive pain.  Basta Tsydenov, a favorite of women, has loved himself more than once.  Officially, he was married three times, he has three children and one granddaughter.  However, the main love of his life is the theater. - My sacrifice for the sake of art is family.  First of all, I put on the theater, my work.  And family is always in the second, in the third plan.  There is always pity, regret.  I could have saved my family, tried, but I couldn't.  Then it seemed that something was more important.  That for me, for my work, for my art, a woman must sacrifice her personal ambition.  But I did not meet such a woman.  On the contrary, I feel sorry for them.  Although, I don't know, maybe it's a good thing we met.  That we have children in common.  I love them, I help them as much as I can.  Communicating.  The kids are nice to me, great relationships.  In the creative baggage of Basta Tsydenov more than 80 roles.  In each he never ceases to know himself, shares the actor.  His first major role was at 25.  He played the groom in the play "Wedding" in the Buryat Drama Theater.  In the difficult 90 ’ s for the whole country, Basta Guruevich admits that he was experiencing a personal crisis.  He decided to leave the storm.  - I felt devastated, I didn't know what to do, I was sad, I was sad, I was bored.  It's about me, not the theater.  Personal life kubarem.  One day I just decided to leave.  I haven't been to the theater in 12 years.  Wandering around Moscow, in Europe, he says.  Basta Tsydenov participated in the project “White Deer ” by the German director Betin Voevoda, in the seminars of the great Japanese experimental director Tadashi Suzuki.  With special warmth, Basta Guruevich recalls common projects with the students of Anatoly Vasiliev - Klim (Vladimir Klimenko, theater director, playwright, screenwriter - approx. ed.) and Boris Yukhananov (artistic director of the Stanislavsky Electrotheatre - approx. ed.): - Boris invited me to play the role of a shaman in Faust.  There was a performance for 8 hours, I went out 15-16 times, I did rituals.  He gave me total freedom.  I was thinking about the rituals I remember from the storm.  He made up whole dialogues for me.  I was with Faust, I argued with him, supported him sometimes.  We performed at the RAMT (Russian Academic Youth Theater - approx. ed.) twice, at the Stanislavsky Theater 3-4 times.  He lied to everyone there that I was a real shaman from Buryatia.  Everyone looked at me with caution.  I didn't know he was out there, lying.  In "Hamlet" he played, there were two more projects according to his script.  In the capital of Russia, the actor found, as they say, his director.  It was in the Moscow period of the artist ’ s life that he met Oleg Yumov, who studied at GITIS.  Later, returning to Buryatia, Basta Tsydenov will play the main roles in almost all Buryat performances of Yumov.  Their creative tandem is based on friendship, says the artist: - To have your own director or a person who is close in spirit, blood, interesting - this is a very great success for the actor.  I'm an actor.  I tried, I staged Duck Hunt, Moscow critics and speakers at the Vampilov Festival noted.  But I prefer to play.  For the performance of the main role in the play “Maxar.  Steppe in Blood "Basta Guruevich was nominated for the" Golden Mask "for the" Best male role ", was awarded the diploma of the festival" Siberian transit "in Barnaul in the nomination" Best male role ".  And the old man Santiago brought the artist a "Mongolian Oscar" - a victory in the festival "Gagan Muse" in Ulaanbaatar.  Today, Basta Tsydenov works as an artist in the Buryat Drama Theater, and also opened his school of oratorical skills, where he teaches children, as he says, to be free.  Although the question of whether he himself is free, he answers: - I have been striving for this all my life.  I can ’ t say I ’ m a free person, but I think there ’ s freedom.  I do what I want... what I feel, I do it.  In creativity it is necessary to tear, go to the depth, to the width, to destroy.  In a good way.  Destroy stereotypes. Title: How to read Hemingway?
Content: Ernest Hemingway, a Nobel laureate and one of the most important of the 20th century, was born on July 21, 1899 in Illinois and wrote seven novels, six collections of short stories and two nonfiction books during his lifetime.  On the occasion of the birth of this author, which coincided with the thirteenth of July, we have suggestions for better reading of the works of this author.  Hemingway ’ s work is fluid, simple, and clear, but for many readers of literature, it may be difficult to begin reading Hemingway ’ s books.  Why read Hemingway?  Ernest Hemingway is an influential writer in the history of literature and fiction, his works have repeatedly won the most prestigious international literary awards such as Nobel and Pulitzer, this author employed a different kind of narrative description and caused many writers after him to borrow his own literary style.  Hemingway has named his literary style the Iceberg Theory, in this way of writing, fictional events are narrated like an iceberg floating in water, only one-eighth of which is visible, and the author includes only the information that is essential in the process and omits the rest of the information.  This technique created a tremendous change in storytelling, especially the writing of short stories, and it was a development that freed the stories from conventional chatter.  Hemingway ’ s works are included in the list of books of the century, books to read before death, and the best fiction books in history, highlighting the importance of this author.  What do we need to know?  One of the topics that helps to better understand Ernest Hemingway ’ s work is getting to know his personal life.  Much of what we read in his books is what he has turned from his personal life into a story.  At the age of 19, he volunteered for the First World War but was not allowed to fight because of poor eyesight, but Hemingway insisted on serving as an ambulance driver for the Red Cross.  He was wounded several times during the Chang, but his most significant injury is when he was wounded by mortar shell fragments and spent a long time in the hospital, a novel about this part of Hemingway ’ s life and the war.  Even the character of Catherine Barkley in this book is based on the nurse Hemingway fell in love with.  Hemingway also participated in World War II as a war correspondent, and several short stories are the result of this era.  The sun continues to blow, the Great River or along the river to the trees, each of which is somehow tied to the World War, and their heroes are survivors of the war and have many memories of these days.  But Hemingway ’ s most important masterpiece is a relic of his childhood, Hemingway ’ s father had a great interest in fishing, and this hobby was passed on to Ernest, a point that can be clearly seen in the famous and widely read story of The Old Man and the Sea.  But before the Old Man and the Sea, Hemingway had written about having and not having a fishing boat captain.  Another important point to know before reading Hemingway ’ s works is his political approach, he has written a lot in opposition to fascism and against dictatorship, both as a journalist and as a writer, sometimes even changing from a journalist to a social-political activist, who is this point in The Bell for, or who is this death knell?  It is a story of an American soldier in the Spanish Civil War fighting alongside groups against General Franco, which Hemingway did.  Perhaps the other thing that matters is that during the World War, Hemingway led a French group against the Nazis that was tried after the war for armed acts but was never proven guilty.  The political and social history of the world in the years of Hemingway's life, his personal life, as well as the knowledge of his contemporaries, such as Scott Fitzgerald, with whom he has written, are points that contribute to the understanding of his works.  Getting to know Hemingway ’ s contemporary writers helps to better understand the difference between him and his contemporaries.  Is it a classic?  To read Hemingway ’ s work, we must note that he is not a classic writer in his different style, he did not deal with the long margins and descriptions of classical literature, and his long novels are not immune.  He was interested in shorthand and engaging the audience with fiction, which is a feature of modern literature.  In general, Hemingway ’ s works are innovative and even among modern works have their own creativity, but the value of this author ’ s work has always been compared to classical works, and even classical enthusiasts have not been able to be indifferent to it.  In these works we have a happy and well-spoken writer, a writer who was in middle age with young people and was even close friends with a group of hippies.  Hemingway is a realistic writer, but he has always tried to maintain his sense of humor.  Where do we start?  To read Hemingway ’ s works, the first and most important suggestion is The Old Man and the Sea.  The book, translated by Najaf Daryabandari, was published in 222 pages by Kharazmi Publications.  The next book, Farewell to Arms, is again translated by Najaf Daryabendari, published by Amir Kabir Publications in 343 pages.  These two books are always on the list of works to be read or masterpieces of the 20th century.  If you are interested in short stories, you can also read Men Without Women, a collection of stories that have been published in various magazines by the author.  This book has been translated by Asadollah Amraei for publication of Horizon in 222 pages.  Even if you are interested in writing, Hemingway can be a good teacher and read his series of talks and learn very precise points.  The book The Last Interview and Other Conversations of Ernest Hemingway with a translation by Houshang Jirani has been published in 88 pages by Cheshmeh Publishing.  The final chapter of many critics considered Ernest Hemingway to be the greatest writer of the 20th century.  His stories are an exploration of real human life, suffering and the meaning of life.  The portrayal of human inner feelings is the most important characteristic of this author, which makes his works a read for every reader.  Who was Ernest Hemingway?  Ernest Hemingway was born on July 21, 1899 in Oak Park, Illinois.  His father, Clarence, was a doctor and his mother, Grace, was a piano and singing teacher.  Ernest spent the summers with his family in northern Michigan, where he discovered his passion for fishing.  After finishing high school, he worked for a while in Kansas City as a reporter for the Star Chronicle in 1917.  During World War I, he volunteered to serve in the army, but poor eyesight prevented him from doing so, instead serving as an ambulance driver for the Red Cross near the Italian front.  On July 8, 1918, he was injured and spent months in the hospital.  In 1925, his first collection of short stories, in our time, was published, which spoke well of his particular style.  His memoirs from that period were published after his death in 1964 as The Variable Eid.  Ernest Hemingway was an adventurer for most of his life.  From being wounded in Italy by 200 pieces of Austrian shrapnel during World War I, to taking part in the frontlines of the Spanish Civil War or touring the African wilderness, to fishing and hunting wildlife and living in Cuba.  He finally said goodbye to life with his hunting rifle.

Title: How to read Hemingway?
Content: Ernest Hemingway, a Nobel laureate and one of the most important of the 20th century, was born on July 21, 1899 in Illinois and wrote seven novels, six collections of short stories and two nonfiction books during his lifetime.  On the occasion of the birth of this author, which coincided with the thirteenth of July, we have suggestions for better reading of the works of this author.  Hemingway ’ s work is fluid, simple, and clear, but for many readers of literature, it may be difficult to begin reading Hemingway ’ s books.  Why read Hemingway?  Ernest Hemingway is an influential writer in the history of literature and fiction, his works have repeatedly won the most prestigious international literary awards such as Nobel and Pulitzer, this author employed a different kind of narrative description and caused many writers after him to borrow his own literary style.  Hemingway has named his literary style the Iceberg Theory, in this way of writing, fictional events are narrated like an iceberg floating in water, only one-eighth of which is visible, and the author includes only the information that is essential in the process and omits the rest of the information.  This technique created a tremendous change in storytelling, especially the writing of short stories, and it was a development that freed the stories from conventional chatter.  Hemingway ’ s works are included in the list of books of the century, books to read before death, and the best fiction books in history, highlighting the importance of this author.  What do we need to know?  One of the topics that helps to better understand Ernest Hemingway ’ s work is getting to know his personal life.  Much of what we read in his books is what he has turned from his personal life into a story.  At the age of 19, he volunteered for the First World War but was not allowed to fight because of poor eyesight, but Hemingway insisted on serving as an ambulance driver for the Red Cross.  He was wounded several times during the Chang, but his most significant injury is when he was wounded by mortar shell fragments and spent a long time in the hospital, a novel about this part of Hemingway ’ s life and the war.  Even the character of Catherine Barkley in this book is based on the nurse Hemingway fell in love with.  Hemingway also participated in World War II as a war correspondent, and several short stories are the result of this era.  The sun continues to blow, the Great River or along the river to the trees, each of which is somehow tied to the World War, and their heroes are survivors of the war and have many memories of these days.  But Hemingway ’ s most important masterpiece is a relic of his childhood, Hemingway ’ s father had a great interest in fishing, and this hobby was passed on to Ernest, a point that can be clearly seen in the famous and widely read story of The Old Man and the Sea.  But before the Old Man and the Sea, Hemingway had written about having and not having a fishing boat captain.  Another important point to know before reading Hemingway ’ s works is his political approach, he has written a lot in opposition to fascism and against dictatorship, both as a journalist and as a writer, sometimes even changing from a journalist to a social-political activist, who is this point in The Bell for, or who is this death knell?  It is a story of an American soldier in the Spanish Civil War fighting alongside groups against General Franco, which Hemingway did.  Perhaps the other thing that matters is that during the World War, Hemingway led a French group against the Nazis that was tried after the war for armed acts but was never proven guilty.  The political and social history of the world in the years of Hemingway's life, his personal life, as well as the knowledge of his contemporaries, such as Scott Fitzgerald, with whom he has written, are points that contribute to the understanding of his works.  Getting to know Hemingway ’ s contemporary writers helps to better understand the difference between him and his contemporaries.  Is it a classic?  To read Hemingway ’ s work, we must note that he is not a classic writer in his different style, he did not deal with the long margins and descriptions of classical literature, and his long novels are not immune.  He was interested in shorthand and engaging the audience with fiction, which is a feature of modern literature.  In general, Hemingway ’ s works are innovative and even among modern works have their own creativity, but the value of this author ’ s work has always been compared to classical works, and even classical enthusiasts have not been able to be indifferent to it.  In these works we have a happy and well-spoken writer, a writer who was in middle age with young people and was even close friends with a group of hippies.  Hemingway is a realistic writer, but he has always tried to maintain his sense of humor.  Where do we start?  To read Hemingway ’ s works, the first and most important suggestion is The Old Man and the Sea.  The book, translated by Najaf Daryabandari, was published in 222 pages by Kharazmi Publications.  The next book, Farewell to Arms, is again translated by Najaf Daryabendari, published by Amir Kabir Publications in 343 pages.  These two books are always on the list of works to be read or masterpieces of the 20th century.  If you are interested in short stories, you can also read Men Without Women, a collection of stories that have been published in various magazines by the author.  This book has been translated by Asadollah Amraei for publication of Horizon in 222 pages.  Even if you are interested in writing, Hemingway can be a good teacher and read his series of talks and learn very precise points.  The book The Last Interview and Other Conversations of Ernest Hemingway with a translation by Houshang Jirani has been published in 88 pages by Cheshmeh Publishing.  The final chapter of many critics considered Ernest Hemingway to be the greatest writer of the 20th century.  His stories are an exploration of real human life, suffering and the meaning of life.  The portrayal of human inner feelings is the most important characteristic of this author, which makes his works a read for every reader.  Who was Ernest Hemingway?  Ernest Hemingway was born on July 21, 1899 in Oak Park, Illinois.  His father, Clarence, was a doctor and his mother, Grace, was a piano and singing teacher.  Ernest spent the summers with his family in northern Michigan, where he discovered his passion for fishing.  After finishing high school, he worked for a while in Kansas City as a reporter for the Star Chronicle in 1917.  During World War I, he volunteered to serve in the army, but poor eyesight prevented him from doing so, instead serving as an ambulance driver for the Red Cross near the Italian front.  On July 8, 1918, he was injured and spent months in the hospital.  In 1925, his first collection of short stories, in our time, was published, which spoke well of his particular style.  His memoirs from that period were published after his death in 1964 as The Variable Eid.  Ernest Hemingway was an adventurer for most of his life.  From being wounded in Italy by 200 pieces of Austrian shrapnel during World War I, to taking part in the frontlines of the Spanish Civil War or touring the African wilderness, to fishing and hunting wildlife and living in Cuba.  He finally said goodbye to life with his hunting rifle.

The project, which was launched 35 years ago by the East and West camps, is now in its last major stage. Workers, engineers and physicists have been involved in the project for nine years.  In 1988, ITER (International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor) was launched as a landmark project of the East and West camps. In 1985, French President Francois Mitterrand, US President Ronald Reagan and Soviet Communist Party General Secretary Mikhail Gorbachev jointly launched the project.  Until this year, the reactor building stood.  Reactor completion is expected to take another four and a half years.  Tuesday ’ s celebration was largely a symbolic signpost highlighting the progress made in the construction project.  For years, ITER has been under pressure due to cost explosions and delays.  The goal of the ITER project, which has no radioactive waste, is to show that a fusion reactor can generate enough heat over a long period of time to maintain a fusion plasma.  This will prove that human beings can make nuclear fusion and sustain it for a period of time.  In addition, ITER should be able to safely conduct the energy generated – at temperatures up to hundreds of millions of degrees Celsius.  However, this energy will not be used to generate electricity.  ITER is still a basic research.  For the time being, the engineers only want to prove that the technology is in principle suitable for obtaining clean energy through the combination of the hydrogen isotope deuterium and tritium for human use.  In the future, the annular vacuum container that will hold plasma is such that nuclear fusion is installed piece by piece instead of nuclear fission that our sun is generating enormous energy in this way.  If ITER succeeds in imitating the sun, humanity will realize the dream of creating a “controlled solar fire ” on Earth – with inexhaustible and inexhaustible energy, because the raw materials required are infinite.  However, there is also a dark cloud over the project: critics say the experiment is a deep pit engulfing tens of billions of euros.  Originally expected to cost 5 billion euros, it has now more than quadrupled.  In addition, developers are still struggling with a number of physical problems: how to safely transport heat from the reactor and how to add new fuel.  Are large facilities obsolete?  The main argument of opponents is that fusion technology has taken too long to reverse climate change in time.  They believe that the money should be used more for renewable energy such as wind and solar, as well as for smart transmission networks.  Proponents argue that the future cannot cover all of humanity ’ s energy needs through decentralized renewable energy sources.  Therefore, large power generation facilities will always be needed.  ITER ’ s ability to meet its ambitious goal of igniting the first plasma by 2025 also depends on the continued involvement of 30 project partners.  In international research projects, countries usually do not provide funding, but rather technical components, research and engineering contributions.  In addition to the EU, China, India, Japan, South Korea, the United States and the United Kingdom are participating in ITER.  The EU bears the largest share of the costs, accounting for 45.6 per cent.  Other partners each contributed 9.1%.  China joined the ITER program in 2006.  Chinese media reported on Tuesday that "the International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor (ITER) project bears the beautiful wish of mankind for the peaceful use of nuclear fusion energy", and President Xi Jinping sent a congratulatory letter to the launch ceremony of the major project of the project.  Chinese media stressed that since the implementation of the plan, "China has always abided by its international commitments, made concerted efforts with its international counterparts, and contributed Chinese wisdom and Chinese strength to the smooth advancement of the plan."  © 2020 Deutsche Welle Copyright Notice: All content in this article is protected by copyright law and may not be used without special permission from Deutsche Welle.
