passages.title: Will China's nuclear fusion power generation technology become the world's first?
passages.passage: Image caption China claims to be leading the world in nuclear energy development  At a time when the world's demand for energy is increasing, but the damage to the environment is also relatively intensified, Chinese scientists are leading the development of energy that some people regard as the holy grail. BBC reporter Stephen McDonell visited a factory in Anhui that is not easy to access.  Imagine generating an infinite amount of energy with virtually no material waste – the lofty promise of nuclear fusion.  On the "Science Island" on the western outskirts of Hefei City, Anhui Province, a shiny giant circle is housed in a large circular box about the same height as two buildings, which is the Experimental Advanced Superconducting Tokamak (EAST).  In the device, hydrogen atoms fuse into helium, which can gather heat several times higher than the sun's core.  The reaction is controlled by a powerful battery.  If maintained properly, a large amount of electricity can be generated in a day.  Many countries in the world are committed to mastering nuclear fusion technology, the United States, Japan, South Korea, Brazil and the European Union are all working hard, but no team can maintain the stability of nuclear fusion like the team in Anhui.  Now it ’ s 100 seconds, and it ’ s getting longer every year.  In Anhui, scientists have begun discussions about setting the goal of extending the time by ten times, with temperatures at 100 million degrees Celsius.  Image caption Hundreds of experts work here.  But since the Soviet Union began nuclear fusion technology in the early 1950s, scientists and engineers have been unsuccessful for a reason.  Because it was really, really difficult.  Maintaining a limited fusion reaction in a controlled environment has proven feasible over the past 50 years, but the duration of fusion is still far shorter than it takes to transform into a large amount of thermal energy.  The EAST system is an enhanced version of the Russian design.  On the day of our interview, we witnessed a live debate in the control room.  There is a leakage problem — not the matter escaping but the air being sucked into the vacuum inside — and scientists have to figure out how to fix it.  The other group contacted the control room with a walkie-talkie.  They surround EAST ’ s pipelines, power rooms and ladders to find holes and fix them.  When Xi Jinping came to visit, he wanted to understand the dangers of this technology, so we asked them how they responded to the Chinese president.  "Nuclear fusion reactors are relatively safe compared to fission reactors, and magnetic confinement fusion can control fusion," said Song Yuntao, deputy director of the Plasma Institute of the Chinese Academy of Sciences.  I can turn off the power supply, which is extremely safe and will not cause any nuclear crisis.  The Chinese design is based on early Russian research.  Nuclear reactions now rely on fission and atomic fragmentation, the result of which is toxic waste that must be stored in a safe place for perhaps thousands of years.  A nuclear fusion plant is a fusion of two nuclei into a single nucleus, and then the magnetic force of the inner wall of the circle (known as plasma) reacts inside a huge pipeline.  Crucially, we were told that this would hardly produce any waste.  But this technology is not cheap.  It costs $150,000 a day just to start a machine, not including the salaries and hardware of hundreds of experts.  The Chinese government has invested heavily in the project, even though it knows that it may take decades to get fusion to power cities.  “Scientists and engineers will make a major breakthrough in fusion, plus government financial support, ” Song said.“ This is a huge project, but I personally think it will be a great sustainable development for humanity. ”  We hope to complete the design of the fusion reactor within five years, and if we succeed, it will be the world's first fusion reactor.  Song Yuntao, deputy director of the Plasma Institute of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, is looking for possible international cooperation in nuclear fusion technology because it is so expensive and difficult.  For example, China has contributed to the International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor (ITER) project in southern France, in addition to the EU countries, India, Japan, Russia, South Korea and the United States, which is expected to be tested in 2025.  At the same time, China is also accelerating its own pace of development.  The next goal proposed by the Anhui team is to design a fully fledged fusion reactor capable of generating electricity.  To achieve this, it must be larger than what we see now, and be able to contain infinite plasma reactions instead of the existing minute and a half.  "Every country has a great demand for power, and China has a clear path map for fusion power," Song said. "We hope to complete the design of the fusion reactor within five years, and if we succeed, it will be the world's first fusion reactor."  The ultimate goal is that nuclear fusion can produce more electricity than people dream of.  While it may sound far-fetched, the Chinese government is serious about the challenge.  If successful, China will eventually outperform the rest of the world in power generation in the future.

passages.title: China's "artificial sun" record
passages.passage: China's artificial sun has set a new record in its quest for fusion energy.  While similar efforts are underway in the United States, Europe, Russia and South Korea, the artificial sun improved its previous record by five times.  According to state media, China has reached another milestone in its quest to realize a fusion reactor, and one of its artificial suns has managed to maintain extreme temperatures several times higher than its previous record.  State news agency Xinhua reported that the Tokamak Advanced Experimental Superconductor (EAST) at a facility in the eastern city of Hefei maintained a plasma temperature of 120 million degrees Celsius for 101 seconds.  The report said the artificial sun also managed to maintain a temperature of 160 million degrees Celsius for 20 seconds.  Last year, EAST achieved a record 100 million degrees Celsius of plasma temperature for 20 seconds.  The experiment means that Chinese scientists have managed to maintain extremely high temperatures up to five times higher than previous experiments.  Another Chinese artificial sun project in Chengdu, the Tokamak HL-2m device, maintained temperatures of 150 million degrees Celsius for up to 10 seconds in a test late last year.  The construction and development of these artificial suns is part of China ’ s effort to reach fusion reactors that will revive hopes for clean and unlimited energy.  But there are many challenges that need to be overcome in the decades-long effort of the world ’ s scientists.  Similar efforts are underway in the United States, Europe, Russia and South Korea.  China is also one of the 35 countries involved in the International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor (ITER) project in France.  It is difficult to directly compare these types of experiments in different countries, because the devices are designed differently.  These facilities are called “artificial suns ” because they aim to replicate nuclear fusion reactions that power the sun at 15 million degrees Celsius.  When two atoms reach the fusion point, they release a large amount of energy.  To do this on Earth, scientists need to be able to maintain high temperatures for long periods of time.  Despite the advances made, fusion reactors are still a long way from being operational.  Song Yuntao, director of the Institute of Plasma Physics of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, said the latest results are a major breakthrough for physics and engineering in China.  The success of the test is the foundation for the construction of a nuclear fusion energy station in China.  China joined the ITER project in 2003 and at that time it was reported as an opportunity for its scientists to expand their expertise and gain an opportunity to emerge in the international scientific community.  The project in southern France has been repeatedly delayed, with the country ’ s latest plasma production target set for 2025.  The European Union has pledged $6.8 billion in new funding to the project in February.  Also, China National Nuclear Corporation will install the main equipment "ITER".  End of message.

passages.title: No longer fantastic. China Completes Construction of ‘ Artificial Sun ’
passages.passage: In the first thermonuclear reactor of the new type, Chinese scientists hope to get the same reaction that occurs in the bowels of the only star in the system.  Chinese physicists are completing the creation of an experimental reactor for fusion EAST, reports Asia Times.  In this device, as the publication notes, the Chinese researchers plan to create an approximate thermonuclear reaction that will create a reliable, cheap and inexhaustible source of energy at the same time.  The head of the China National Nuclear Corporation, Duan Suru, noted that scientists plan to reach "industrial volumes" of energy production this year.  It is noted that the first experimental reactor of a similar type was tested in the mid-90s, since then there has been continuous work on improving the technology.  Chinese physicists note that the “working ” temperature of a fusion reactor can be at least 105 million degrees.  The ultimate goal of the researchers is to achieve a plasma pulse in one thousand seconds.  This, according to scientists, will be enough to connect not only industrial enterprises, but also cities to the reactors.

passages.title: China's artificial sun has begun
passages.passage: China ’ s HL-2m Tokamak reactor is China ’ s largest and most advanced experimental fusion research tool, and scientists hope it could potentially provide a powerful source of clean energy.  The reactor uses a powerful magnetic field to fuse hot and thermal plasmas and has the potential to reach temperatures of more than 150 million degrees Celsius, almost 10 times hotter than the nuclear heat of the sun.  The nuclear reactor, located in southwest China's Sichuan province, was completed late last year and is often referred to as an "artificial sun" because of the enormous heat and energy it generates.  The development of nuclear fusion energy is not only a way to meet the strategic needs of China ’ s energy sector, it is also important for sustainable energy development and China ’ s national economy.  Chinese scientists have been working on smaller versions of nuclear fusion reactors since 2006 and are working with scientists to build the International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor.  Fusion produces a massive amount of energy through the fusion of atomic nuclei, and this is the opposite of nuclear fission.  Nuclear fission is used in the production of nuclear weapons and nuclear power plants, and during the process of nuclear fission, nuclear nuclei are crushed and fragmented.  Unlike nuclear fission, no greenhouse gases are emitted during fusion, and there is less risk of accidents or theft of nuclear material.  However, boiling is both extremely difficult and very expensive.  The total cost of building the International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor is estimated to be $22.5 billion.

passages.title: Atomic energy
passages.passage: Over the past 20 years, the amount of clean energy has doubled.  This energy is obtained from environmentally friendly sources - hydroelectric, nuclear, solar, wind, geothermal, tidal, biomass energy.  However, its share in the total amount of energy produced remained the same and even decreased slightly.  The fossil fuel industry is growing faster than the clean energy industry.  Many poor countries still use wood, manure and coal as their primary fuel.  The share of alternative renewable sources over the past 20 years has increased to almost 10% in 2018, and nuclear power plants, on the contrary, were closed.  And this despite the fact that solar and wind energy is unstable, it can be received only 10-30% of the time, when the sun is shining enough and the wind blows.  And hospitals, homes, cities and factories need energy all the time.  The United Nations Intergovernmental Committee on Climate Change (IPCC) has studied the CO2 content of all fuels.  Nuclear energy is one of the most environmentally friendly.  At the same time, the nuclear power plant can be used 92% of the time.  So why are we so afraid of nuclear power plants?  Nuclear energy seems like a good solution in the fight against climate change.  But there is one big problem – people don ’ t like it.  According to a 2014 Ipsos survey, nuclear power is one of the least popular.  Only 28% of respondents preferred nuclear power.  Even people are better at oil (30%).  Most people trust solar (85%) and wind energy (78%).  The fear of nuclear power is linked to three factors – the possibility of leakage, the disposal of waste and the association with nuclear weapons.  But it is difficult to make nuclear energy even safer than it is now.  According to a study conducted by one of the largest medical journals Lancet, nuclear energy is the safest among all other sources of energy.  It is safer than wind turbines and solar panels.  After reviewing data on the Fukushima and Chernobyl accidents, the WHO found that a large proportion of the damage was caused by panic.  The UN has also conducted comprehensive studies of the Chernobyl disaster.  The explosion at the Chernobyl nuclear power plant is the worst nuclear accident of all that happened.  As a result, 28 people died from acute radiation syndrome and another 15 people died over the next 25 years from thyroid cancer.  16,000 people became ill with thyroid cancer after Chernobyl, and it is estimated that 160 of them will die from this type of cancer.  The Fukushima nuclear disaster ranks second in severity.  The radiation emission was much smaller than that of Chernobyl.  There are no deaths from radiation after Fukushima.  Fifteen thousand people were killed, who were dragged out of nursing homes and hospitals.  They received a large dose of radiation just because they were moved a long distance.  In many ways, this was the result of a general panic.  For a person living in a big city, such as London, Berlin or New York, the risk of mortality increases by 2.8% from air pollution alone.  For those who live near smokers – by 1.7%.  For the liquidators of the Chernobyl accident, who received a dose of radiation of 250 millisieverts, it increased by only 1%.  By comparison, fuel energy creates uncontrolled waste in the form of greenhouse gas emissions, which kills 7 million people a year.  Therefore, the reduction of fuel energy in favor of nuclear energy has already saved the lives of 1.8 million people.  What about the waste?  Nuclear waste, as it turned out, is not so much.  If you take nuclear waste from the entire history of the United States and fill a football stadium with it, their height will be only 6 m. The waste is stored in special isolated containers, and they are constantly monitored.  In addition, development is underway to use nuclear waste as fuel.  It is the same with nuclear weapons.  There are no examples of countries with nuclear industry suddenly starting to develop nuclear weapons.  In fact, the opposite is happening.  It turns out that the only known way to get rid of a large number of nuclear weapons is to use plutonium from warheads as fuel for nuclear power plants.  Over the next 50 years, humanity will consume more energy than has been consumed in all previous history.  Earlier forecasts about the growth rate of energy consumption and the development of new energy technologies did not materialize: the level of consumption is growing much faster, and new energy sources will work on an industrial scale and at competitive prices not earlier than 2030.  The problem of the shortage of fossil energy resources is becoming more acute.  The capacity to build new hydropower plants is also very limited.  Do not forget about the fight against the “greenhouse effect ”, which imposes restrictions on the burning of oil, gas and coal in thermal power plants.  The solution to the problem can be the active development of nuclear energy, one of the youngest and fastest growing sectors of the global economy.  An increasing number of countries today come to the need to start the development of a peaceful atom.  The use of nuclear power may prove to be one of the solutions to these pressing problems, however unlikely it may seem.  But for this, the methods of its application need to be reviewed.  At the heart of the production of atomic energy is the force that holds the parts of the atom together.  If an atom is unstable, it will tend to move to a more stable state by splitting.  The instability of the atom can be natural or caused by the addition of additional neutrons to the nucleus.  When the atom becomes more stable and ejects particles, a huge amount of energy is released, which in a closed system can be used to generate enough heat to propel the turbine.  Radiation, which is often misrepresented, occurs for the most part due to natural causes.  Let ’ s see what the advantages of nuclear power are: 1 kg of uranium can produce 90,000 times more energy than 1 kg of coal.  Modern technologies make it possible to switch to a closed fuel cycle, which involves the repeated use of fuel products and the minimization of waste.  Every year, nuclear power plants in Europe avoid the emission of 700 million tons of CO2.  One job in the construction of nuclear power plants creates more than 10 jobs in related industries.  The development of nuclear energy contributes to the growth of scientific research and intellectual potential of the country.  According to the IAEA directory published in 2019, 98 nuclear reactors operated in the United States in 2018, 58 in France, 46 in China, 39 in Japan, 38 in Russia, 24 in the Republic of Korea, 22 in India, 19 in Canada, and 15 in the United Kingdom and Ukraine.  The total generating capacity of the nuclear power plant is over 380 GW.  A nuclear power plant is a complex of necessary systems, devices, equipment and structures designed to generate electricity by using the heat released in a nuclear reactor as a result of a controlled fission chain reaction of the nuclei of heavy elements (mainly uranium-233, uranium-235, plutonium-239).  The heat generated in the core of the nuclear reactor is transferred (directly or through an intermediate coolant) to the working medium (mainly water vapor), which drives steam turbines with turbogenerators, where the mechanical energy of the steam is converted into electrical energy.  Then the electricity through the wires goes to consumers.  As heat carriers, ordinary and heavy water, water vapor, liquid metals, organic liquids, some gases, for example, helium or carbon dioxide, are used.  The coolant circulates through sealed pipelines, which, in combination with circulation pumps, form a so-called reactor circuit or loop.  The circuits through which the coolant circulates are always closed to avoid leakage of radioactivity, their number is determined mainly by the type of nuclear reactor, as well as the properties of the working fluid and coolant.  Nuclear power plants can have single-circuit, double-circuit and three-circuit circuit of heat carrier operation.  Single-circuit circuit is used at nuclear power plants with channel-type reactors.  In such nuclear power plants, the coolant is also a working fluid.  In them, the boiling reactor itself is a steam generator, so the entire circuit is radioactive.  It's surrounded by biological defenses.  Two-circuit circuit circuit is used at nuclear power plants with water-water reactors.  In such nuclear power plants, water is supplied under pressure to the reactor core, which is heated.  Heat carrier energy is used in steam generator to form saturated steam.  The first circuit is radioactive and is surrounded by biological protection, except when inert gas is used as heat carrier.  The second circuit is usually radiation-safe, since the working fluid and coolant of the first circuit do not touch.  Three-circuit circuit circuit is used at nuclear power plants with fast neutron reactors with sodium coolant.  To exclude contact of radioactive sodium with water, a second circuit with non-radioactive sodium is constructed.  Thus, the scheme turns out to be three-circuit.  The peculiarity of nuclear power plants with a fast neutron reactor is that simultaneously with the generation of electrical and thermal energy, they reproduce fissile isotopes suitable for use in thermal nuclear reactors. passages.passage: The launch ceremony of the International Thermonuclear Fusion Experimental Reactor (ITER) project was held in France on July 28. Chinese President Xi Jinping sent a congratulatory letter to the launch of the project.  On July 28, the International Thermonuclear Fusion Experimental Reactor (ITER), humanity ’ s largest nuclear fusion project, began a five-year assembly project in southern France, marking a new phase for the largest nuclear fusion project in human history.  + 4 + 3 + 2 The Guardian reported on July 28 that representatives of the participating countries of the project participated in the installation and launch ceremony of ITER on the same day.  The project was jointly built by the European Union, China, the United States, Russia, the United Kingdom, India, Japan and South Korea at a total cost of 20 billion euros.  Speaking at the launch ceremony, ITER Director General Bernard Bigot said that the clean energy generated by the ITER project would be a “miracle for the planet ” and that the energy provided by nuclear fusion and other renewable energy sources would transform energy use in industries such as transport, construction and industry.  The Guardian notes that the ITER project aims to provide conceptual proof for large-scale nuclear fusion, not for future commercial use.  Consisting of millions of components, the nuclear fusion device will be the first self-heating plasma, which is expected to generate 10 times more heat than the input, far more than any previous related test, and the process itself will not produce carbon dioxide that can cause climate warming, and will produce less radioactive waste, which is expected to power magnets and scientific instruments.  The main purpose of the ITER project is to simulate the process of nuclear fusion in which the sun generates energy, so its core device, the tokamak, which controls fusion reactions, is also known as the "artificial sun".  A technician watches the circular shield at the construction site of the International Thermonuclear Fusion Experimental Reactor (ITER) in France on November 7, 2019. (Reuters) China participates in the manufacturing of core components China ’ s state media Xinhua News Agency said on July 28, 2019, that ITER is the largest and most far-reaching international scientific project in the world today.  Chinese President Xi Jinping said in a congratulatory letter on July 28 that the International Thermonuclear Fusion Experimental Reactor (ITER) project carries the beautiful wish of mankind for the peaceful use of nuclear fusion energy. Since the implementation of the project, China has always abided by its international commitments.  Xi Jinping particularly stressed that open exchanges are a key path for exploring the frontier of science, and that international scientific and technological cooperation is of great significance in addressing the global challenges facing mankind.

passages.title: Scientists to Build Artificial Solar Power Meet in France – Radio France Internationale
passages.passage: Fourteen years after receiving official approval, scientists began assembling a machine in southern France on Monday seeking to confirm whether nuclear fusion could be a safe and reliable source of energy on Earth.  In the ground-breaking International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor (ITER), components from around the world have arrived in the southern French town of Saint-Paul-les-Durance in recent months.  These components must now be painstakingly assembled to complete ITER, which has been touted as the “world ’ s largest puzzle. ”  The purpose of this experimental facility is to demonstrate that nuclear fusion can generate electricity on a large, safe and commercial scale.  “Nuclear fusion provides clean, reliable and carbon-free energy, ” said a joint statement from 35 countries participating in ITER, including the 27 EU member states, the United Kingdom, Switzerland, India, Japan, South Korea, Russia, the United States and China.  In addition, fuel for nuclear fusion can be obtained from seawater and lithium metals, which are abundant enough to supply humans for millions of years.  The statement said that such fuel, the size of a pineapple, is equivalent to 10,000 tons of coal.  ITER will be built from about 1 million components and is scheduled to begin preliminary experiments in December 2025.  The artificial solar facility is designed to generate about 500 megawatts of thermal energy, which, if sustained, can be converted into about 200 megawatts of electricity, enough to power about 200,000 homes.  (Translated by: Cao Yufan / Authored by: Liu Xueyuan) © 2020 AFP

Title: ITER – The Controlled Fire of the Sun on Earth
Content: The fusion reactor is located near the southern French coastal city of Marseille.  French President Emmanuel Macron held a "virtual" celebration of the latest progress of the project.  European Commission President von der Leyen, European Commission Energy Commissioner Kadri Simson and South Korean President Moon Jae-in participated in the ceremony by video.  The project, which was launched 35 years ago by the East and West camps, is now in its last major stage. Workers, engineers and physicists have been involved in the project for nine years.  In 1988, ITER (International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor) was launched as a landmark project of the East and West camps. In 1985, French President Francois Mitterrand, US President Ronald Reagan and Soviet Communist Party General Secretary Mikhail Gorbachev jointly launched the project.  Until this year, the reactor building stood.  Reactor completion is expected to take another four and a half years.  Tuesday ’ s celebration was largely a symbolic signpost highlighting the progress made in the construction project.  For years, ITER has been under pressure due to cost explosions and delays.  The goal of the ITER project, which has no radioactive waste, is to show that a fusion reactor can generate enough heat over a long period of time to maintain a fusion plasma.  This will prove that human beings can make nuclear fusion and sustain it for a period of time.  In addition, ITER should be able to safely conduct the energy generated – at temperatures up to hundreds of millions of degrees Celsius.  However, this energy will not be used to generate electricity.  ITER is still a basic research.  For the time being, the engineers only want to prove that the technology is in principle suitable for obtaining clean energy through the combination of the hydrogen isotope deuterium and tritium for human use.  In the future, the annular vacuum container that will hold plasma is such that nuclear fusion is installed piece by piece instead of nuclear fission that our sun is generating enormous energy in this way.  If ITER succeeds in imitating the sun, humanity will realize the dream of creating a “controlled solar fire ” on Earth – with inexhaustible and inexhaustible energy, because the raw materials required are infinite.  However, there is also a dark cloud over the project: critics say the experiment is a deep pit engulfing tens of billions of euros.  Originally expected to cost 5 billion euros, it has now more than quadrupled.  In addition, developers are still struggling with a number of physical problems: how to safely transport heat from the reactor and how to add new fuel.  Are large facilities obsolete?  The main argument of opponents is that fusion technology has taken too long to reverse climate change in time.  They believe that the money should be used more for renewable energy such as wind and solar, as well as for smart transmission networks.  Proponents argue that the future cannot cover all of humanity ’ s energy needs through decentralized renewable energy sources.  Therefore, large power generation facilities will always be needed.  ITER ’ s ability to meet its ambitious goal of igniting the first plasma by 2025 also depends on the continued involvement of 30 project partners.  In international research projects, countries usually do not provide funding, but rather technical components, research and engineering contributions.  In addition to the EU, China, India, Japan, South Korea, the United States and the United Kingdom are participating in ITER.  The EU bears the largest share of the costs, accounting for 45.6 per cent.  Other partners each contributed 9.1%.  China joined the ITER program in 2006. Title: Will China's nuclear fusion power generation technology become the world's first?
Content: Image caption China claims to be leading the world in nuclear energy development  At a time when the world's demand for energy is increasing, but the damage to the environment is also relatively intensified, Chinese scientists are leading the development of energy that some people regard as the holy grail. BBC reporter Stephen McDonell visited a factory in Anhui that is not easy to access.  Imagine generating an infinite amount of energy with virtually no material waste – the lofty promise of nuclear fusion.  On the "Science Island" on the western outskirts of Hefei City, Anhui Province, a shiny giant circle is housed in a large circular box about the same height as two buildings, which is the Experimental Advanced Superconducting Tokamak (EAST).  In the device, hydrogen atoms fuse into helium, which can gather heat several times higher than the sun's core.  The reaction is controlled by a powerful battery.  If maintained properly, a large amount of electricity can be generated in a day.  Many countries in the world are committed to mastering nuclear fusion technology, the United States, Japan, South Korea, Brazil and the European Union are all working hard, but no team can maintain the stability of nuclear fusion like the team in Anhui.  Now it ’ s 100 seconds, and it ’ s getting longer every year.  In Anhui, scientists have begun discussions about setting the goal of extending the time by ten times, with temperatures at 100 million degrees Celsius.  Image caption Hundreds of experts work here.  But since the Soviet Union began nuclear fusion technology in the early 1950s, scientists and engineers have been unsuccessful for a reason.  Because it was really, really difficult.  Maintaining a limited fusion reaction in a controlled environment has proven feasible over the past 50 years, but the duration of fusion is still far shorter than it takes to transform into a large amount of thermal energy.  The EAST system is an enhanced version of the Russian design.  On the day of our interview, we witnessed a live debate in the control room.  There is a leakage problem — not the matter escaping but the air being sucked into the vacuum inside — and scientists have to figure out how to fix it.  The other group contacted the control room with a walkie-talkie.  They surround EAST ’ s pipelines, power rooms and ladders to find holes and fix them.  When Xi Jinping came to visit, he wanted to understand the dangers of this technology, so we asked them how they responded to the Chinese president.  "Nuclear fusion reactors are relatively safe compared to fission reactors, and magnetic confinement fusion can control fusion," said Song Yuntao, deputy director of the Plasma Institute of the Chinese Academy of Sciences.  I can turn off the power supply, which is extremely safe and will not cause any nuclear crisis.  The Chinese design is based on early Russian research.  Nuclear reactions now rely on fission and atomic fragmentation, the result of which is toxic waste that must be stored in a safe place for perhaps thousands of years.  A nuclear fusion plant is a fusion of two nuclei into a single nucleus, and then the magnetic force of the inner wall of the circle (known as plasma) reacts inside a huge pipeline.  Crucially, we were told that this would hardly produce any waste.  But this technology is not cheap.  It costs $150,000 a day just to start a machine, not including the salaries and hardware of hundreds of experts.  The Chinese government has invested heavily in the project, even though it knows that it may take decades to get fusion to power cities.  “Scientists and engineers will make a major breakthrough in fusion, plus government financial support, ” Song said.“ This is a huge project, but I personally think it will be a great sustainable development for humanity. ”  We hope to complete the design of the fusion reactor within five years, and if we succeed, it will be the world's first fusion reactor.  Song Yuntao, deputy director of the Plasma Institute of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, is looking for possible international cooperation in nuclear fusion technology because it is so expensive and difficult.  For example, China has contributed to the International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor (ITER) project in southern France, in addition to the EU countries, India, Japan, Russia, South Korea and the United States, which is expected to be tested in 2025.  At the same time, China is also accelerating its own pace of development.  The next goal proposed by the Anhui team is to design a fully fledged fusion reactor capable of generating electricity.  To achieve this, it must be larger than what we see now, and be able to contain infinite plasma reactions instead of the existing minute and a half.  "Every country has a great demand for power, and China has a clear path map for fusion power," Song said. "We hope to complete the design of the fusion reactor within five years, and if we succeed, it will be the world's first fusion reactor."  The ultimate goal is that nuclear fusion can produce more electricity than people dream of.  While it may sound far-fetched, the Chinese government is serious about the challenge.  If successful, China will eventually outperform the rest of the world in power generation in the future.

Title: China's "artificial sun" record
Content: China's artificial sun has set a new record in its quest for fusion energy.  While similar efforts are underway in the United States, Europe, Russia and South Korea, the artificial sun improved its previous record by five times.  According to state media, China has reached another milestone in its quest to realize a fusion reactor, and one of its artificial suns has managed to maintain extreme temperatures several times higher than its previous record.  State news agency Xinhua reported that the Tokamak Advanced Experimental Superconductor (EAST) at a facility in the eastern city of Hefei maintained a plasma temperature of 120 million degrees Celsius for 101 seconds.  The report said the artificial sun also managed to maintain a temperature of 160 million degrees Celsius for 20 seconds.  Last year, EAST achieved a record 100 million degrees Celsius of plasma temperature for 20 seconds.  The experiment means that Chinese scientists have managed to maintain extremely high temperatures up to five times higher than previous experiments.  Another Chinese artificial sun project in Chengdu, the Tokamak HL-2m device, maintained temperatures of 150 million degrees Celsius for up to 10 seconds in a test late last year.  The construction and development of these artificial suns is part of China ’ s effort to reach fusion reactors that will revive hopes for clean and unlimited energy.  But there are many challenges that need to be overcome in the decades-long effort of the world ’ s scientists.  Similar efforts are underway in the United States, Europe, Russia and South Korea.  China is also one of the 35 countries involved in the International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor (ITER) project in France.  It is difficult to directly compare these types of experiments in different countries, because the devices are designed differently.  These facilities are called “artificial suns ” because they aim to replicate nuclear fusion reactions that power the sun at 15 million degrees Celsius.  When two atoms reach the fusion point, they release a large amount of energy.  To do this on Earth, scientists need to be able to maintain high temperatures for long periods of time.  Despite the advances made, fusion reactors are still a long way from being operational.  Song Yuntao, director of the Institute of Plasma Physics of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, said the latest results are a major breakthrough for physics and engineering in China.  The success of the test is the foundation for the construction of a nuclear fusion energy station in China.  China joined the ITER project in 2003 and at that time it was reported as an opportunity for its scientists to expand their expertise and gain an opportunity to emerge in the international scientific community.  The project in southern France has been repeatedly delayed, with the country ’ s latest plasma production target set for 2025. Title: Atomic energy
Content: Over the past 20 years, the amount of clean energy has doubled.  This energy is obtained from environmentally friendly sources - hydroelectric, nuclear, solar, wind, geothermal, tidal, biomass energy.  However, its share in the total amount of energy produced remained the same and even decreased slightly.  The fossil fuel industry is growing faster than the clean energy industry.  Many poor countries still use wood, manure and coal as their primary fuel.  The share of alternative renewable sources over the past 20 years has increased to almost 10% in 2018, and nuclear power plants, on the contrary, were closed.  And this despite the fact that solar and wind energy is unstable, it can be received only 10-30% of the time, when the sun is shining enough and the wind blows.  And hospitals, homes, cities and factories need energy all the time.  The United Nations Intergovernmental Committee on Climate Change (IPCC) has studied the CO2 content of all fuels.  Nuclear energy is one of the most environmentally friendly.  At the same time, the nuclear power plant can be used 92% of the time.  So why are we so afraid of nuclear power plants?  Nuclear energy seems like a good solution in the fight against climate change.  But there is one big problem – people don ’ t like it.  According to a 2014 Ipsos survey, nuclear power is one of the least popular.  Only 28% of respondents preferred nuclear power.  Even people are better at oil (30%).  Most people trust solar (85%) and wind energy (78%).  The fear of nuclear power is linked to three factors – the possibility of leakage, the disposal of waste and the association with nuclear weapons.  But it is difficult to make nuclear energy even safer than it is now.  According to a study conducted by one of the largest medical journals Lancet, nuclear energy is the safest among all other sources of energy.  It is safer than wind turbines and solar panels.  After reviewing data on the Fukushima and Chernobyl accidents, the WHO found that a large proportion of the damage was caused by panic.  The UN has also conducted comprehensive studies of the Chernobyl disaster.  The explosion at the Chernobyl nuclear power plant is the worst nuclear accident of all that happened.  As a result, 28 people died from acute radiation syndrome and another 15 people died over the next 25 years from thyroid cancer.  16,000 people became ill with thyroid cancer after Chernobyl, and it is estimated that 160 of them will die from this type of cancer.  The Fukushima nuclear disaster ranks second in severity.  The radiation emission was much smaller than that of Chernobyl.  There are no deaths from radiation after Fukushima.  Fifteen thousand people were killed, who were dragged out of nursing homes and hospitals.  They received a large dose of radiation just because they were moved a long distance.  In many ways, this was the result of a general panic.  For a person living in a big city, such as London, Berlin or New York, the risk of mortality increases by 2.8% from air pollution alone.  For those who live near smokers – by 1.7%.  For the liquidators of the Chernobyl accident, who received a dose of radiation of 250 millisieverts, it increased by only 1%.  By comparison, fuel energy creates uncontrolled waste in the form of greenhouse gas emissions, which kills 7 million people a year.  Therefore, the reduction of fuel energy in favor of nuclear energy has already saved the lives of 1.8 million people.  What about the waste?  Nuclear waste, as it turned out, is not so much.  If you take nuclear waste from the entire history of the United States and fill a football stadium with it, their height will be only 6 m. The waste is stored in special isolated containers, and they are constantly monitored.  In addition, development is underway to use nuclear waste as fuel.  It is the same with nuclear weapons.  There are no examples of countries with nuclear industry suddenly starting to develop nuclear weapons.  In fact, the opposite is happening.  It turns out that the only known way to get rid of a large number of nuclear weapons is to use plutonium from warheads as fuel for nuclear power plants.  Over the next 50 years, humanity will consume more energy than has been consumed in all previous history.  Earlier forecasts about the growth rate of energy consumption and the development of new energy technologies did not materialize: the level of consumption is growing much faster, and new energy sources will work on an industrial scale and at competitive prices not earlier than 2030.  The problem of the shortage of fossil energy resources is becoming more acute.  The capacity to build new hydropower plants is also very limited.  Do not forget about the fight against the “greenhouse effect ”, which imposes restrictions on the burning of oil, gas and coal in thermal power plants.  The solution to the problem can be the active development of nuclear energy, one of the youngest and fastest growing sectors of the global economy.  An increasing number of countries today come to the need to start the development of a peaceful atom.  The use of nuclear power may prove to be one of the solutions to these pressing problems, however unlikely it may seem.  But for this, the methods of its application need to be reviewed.  At the heart of the production of atomic energy is the force that holds the parts of the atom together.  If an atom is unstable, it will tend to move to a more stable state by splitting.  The instability of the atom can be natural or caused by the addition of additional neutrons to the nucleus.  When the atom becomes more stable and ejects particles, a huge amount of energy is released, which in a closed system can be used to generate enough heat to propel the turbine.  Radiation, which is often misrepresented, occurs for the most part due to natural causes.  Let ’ s see what the advantages of nuclear power are: 1 kg of uranium can produce 90,000 times more energy than 1 kg of coal.  Modern technologies make it possible to switch to a closed fuel cycle, which involves the repeated use of fuel products and the minimization of waste.  Every year, nuclear power plants in Europe avoid the emission of 700 million tons of CO2.  One job in the construction of nuclear power plants creates more than 10 jobs in related industries.  The development of nuclear energy contributes to the growth of scientific research and intellectual potential of the country.  According to the IAEA directory published in 2019, 98 nuclear reactors operated in the United States in 2018, 58 in France, 46 in China, 39 in Japan, 38 in Russia, 24 in the Republic of Korea, 22 in India, 19 in Canada, and 15 in the United Kingdom and Ukraine.  The total generating capacity of the nuclear power plant is over 380 GW.  A nuclear power plant is a complex of necessary systems, devices, equipment and structures designed to generate electricity by using the heat released in a nuclear reactor as a result of a controlled fission chain reaction of the nuclei of heavy elements (mainly uranium-233, uranium-235, plutonium-239).  The heat generated in the core of the nuclear reactor is transferred (directly or through an intermediate coolant) to the working medium (mainly water vapor), which drives steam turbines with turbogenerators, where the mechanical energy of the steam is converted into electrical energy.  Then the electricity through the wires goes to consumers.  As heat carriers, ordinary and heavy water, water vapor, liquid metals, organic liquids, some gases, for example, helium or carbon dioxide, are used.  The coolant circulates through sealed pipelines, which, in combination with circulation pumps, form a so-called reactor circuit or loop.  The circuits through which the coolant circulates are always closed to avoid leakage of radioactivity, their number is determined mainly by the type of nuclear reactor, as well as the properties of the working fluid and coolant.  Nuclear power plants can have single-circuit, double-circuit and three-circuit circuit of heat carrier operation.  Single-circuit circuit is used at nuclear power plants with channel-type reactors.  In such nuclear power plants, the coolant is also a working fluid.  In them, the boiling reactor itself is a steam generator, so the entire circuit is radioactive.  It's surrounded by biological defenses.  Two-circuit circuit circuit is used at nuclear power plants with water-water reactors.  In such nuclear power plants, water is supplied under pressure to the reactor core, which is heated.  Heat carrier energy is used in steam generator to form saturated steam.  The first circuit is radioactive and is surrounded by biological protection, except when inert gas is used as heat carrier.  The second circuit is usually radiation-safe, since the working fluid and coolant of the first circuit do not touch.  Three-circuit circuit circuit is used at nuclear power plants with fast neutron reactors with sodium coolant. Title: Scientists to Build Artificial Solar Power Meet in France – Radio France Internationale
Content: Fourteen years after receiving official approval, scientists began assembling a machine in southern France on Monday seeking to confirm whether nuclear fusion could be a safe and reliable source of energy on Earth.  In the ground-breaking International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor (ITER), components from around the world have arrived in the southern French town of Saint-Paul-les-Durance in recent months.  These components must now be painstakingly assembled to complete ITER, which has been touted as the “world ’ s largest puzzle. ”  The purpose of this experimental facility is to demonstrate that nuclear fusion can generate electricity on a large, safe and commercial scale.  “Nuclear fusion provides clean, reliable and carbon-free energy, ” said a joint statement from 35 countries participating in ITER, including the 27 EU member states, the United Kingdom, Switzerland, India, Japan, South Korea, Russia, the United States and China.  In addition, fuel for nuclear fusion can be obtained from seawater and lithium metals, which are abundant enough to supply humans for millions of years.  The statement said that such fuel, the size of a pineapple, is equivalent to 10,000 tons of coal.  ITER will be built from about 1 million components and is scheduled to begin preliminary experiments in December 2025.  The artificial solar facility is designed to generate about 500 megawatts of thermal energy, which, if sustained, can be converted into about 200 megawatts of electricity, enough to power about 200,000 homes. Title: Will China's nuclear fusion power generation technology become the world's first?
Content: Image caption China claims to be leading the world in nuclear energy development  At a time when the world's demand for energy is increasing, but the damage to the environment is also relatively intensified, Chinese scientists are leading the development of energy that some people regard as the holy grail. BBC reporter Stephen McDonell visited a factory in Anhui that is not easy to access.  Imagine generating an infinite amount of energy with virtually no material waste – the lofty promise of nuclear fusion.  On the "Science Island" on the western outskirts of Hefei City, Anhui Province, a shiny giant circle is housed in a large circular box about the same height as two buildings, which is the Experimental Advanced Superconducting Tokamak (EAST).  In the device, hydrogen atoms fuse into helium, which can gather heat several times higher than the sun's core.  The reaction is controlled by a powerful battery.  If maintained properly, a large amount of electricity can be generated in a day.  Many countries in the world are committed to mastering nuclear fusion technology, the United States, Japan, South Korea, Brazil and the European Union are all working hard, but no team can maintain the stability of nuclear fusion like the team in Anhui.  Now it ’ s 100 seconds, and it ’ s getting longer every year.  In Anhui, scientists have begun discussions about setting the goal of extending the time by ten times, with temperatures at 100 million degrees Celsius.  Image caption Hundreds of experts work here.  But since the Soviet Union began nuclear fusion technology in the early 1950s, scientists and engineers have been unsuccessful for a reason.  Because it was really, really difficult.  Maintaining a limited fusion reaction in a controlled environment has proven feasible over the past 50 years, but the duration of fusion is still far shorter than it takes to transform into a large amount of thermal energy.  The EAST system is an enhanced version of the Russian design.  On the day of our interview, we witnessed a live debate in the control room.  There is a leakage problem — not the matter escaping but the air being sucked into the vacuum inside — and scientists have to figure out how to fix it.  The other group contacted the control room with a walkie-talkie.  They surround EAST ’ s pipelines, power rooms and ladders to find holes and fix them.  When Xi Jinping came to visit, he wanted to understand the dangers of this technology, so we asked them how they responded to the Chinese president.  "Nuclear fusion reactors are relatively safe compared to fission reactors, and magnetic confinement fusion can control fusion," said Song Yuntao, deputy director of the Plasma Institute of the Chinese Academy of Sciences.  I can turn off the power supply, which is extremely safe and will not cause any nuclear crisis.  The Chinese design is based on early Russian research.  Nuclear reactions now rely on fission and atomic fragmentation, the result of which is toxic waste that must be stored in a safe place for perhaps thousands of years.  A nuclear fusion plant is a fusion of two nuclei into a single nucleus, and then the magnetic force of the inner wall of the circle (known as plasma) reacts inside a huge pipeline.  Crucially, we were told that this would hardly produce any waste.  But this technology is not cheap.  It costs $150,000 a day just to start a machine, not including the salaries and hardware of hundreds of experts.  The Chinese government has invested heavily in the project, even though it knows that it may take decades to get fusion to power cities.  “Scientists and engineers will make a major breakthrough in fusion, plus government financial support, ” Song said.“ This is a huge project, but I personally think it will be a great sustainable development for humanity. ”  We hope to complete the design of the fusion reactor within five years, and if we succeed, it will be the world's first fusion reactor.  Song Yuntao, deputy director of the Plasma Institute of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, is looking for possible international cooperation in nuclear fusion technology because it is so expensive and difficult. At the same time, China is also accelerating its own pace of development.  The next goal proposed by the Anhui team is to design a fully fledged fusion reactor capable of generating electricity.  To achieve this, it must be larger than what we see now, and be able to contain infinite plasma reactions instead of the existing minute and a half. Title: Atomic energy
Content: Over the past 20 years, the amount of clean energy has doubled.  This energy is obtained from environmentally friendly sources - hydroelectric, nuclear, solar, wind, geothermal, tidal, biomass energy.  However, its share in the total amount of energy produced remained the same and even decreased slightly.  The fossil fuel industry is growing faster than the clean energy industry.  Many poor countries still use wood, manure and coal as their primary fuel.  The share of alternative renewable sources over the past 20 years has increased to almost 10% in 2018, and nuclear power plants, on the contrary, were closed.  And this despite the fact that solar and wind energy is unstable, it can be received only 10-30% of the time, when the sun is shining enough and the wind blows.  And hospitals, homes, cities and factories need energy all the time.  The United Nations Intergovernmental Committee on Climate Change (IPCC) has studied the CO2 content of all fuels.  Nuclear energy is one of the most environmentally friendly.  At the same time, the nuclear power plant can be used 92% of the time.  So why are we so afraid of nuclear power plants?  Nuclear energy seems like a good solution in the fight against climate change.  But there is one big problem – people don ’ t like it.  According to a 2014 Ipsos survey, nuclear power is one of the least popular.  Only 28% of respondents preferred nuclear power.  Even people are better at oil (30%).  Most people trust solar (85%) and wind energy (78%).  The fear of nuclear power is linked to three factors – the possibility of leakage, the disposal of waste and the association with nuclear weapons.  But it is difficult to make nuclear energy even safer than it is now.  According to a study conducted by one of the largest medical journals Lancet, nuclear energy is the safest among all other sources of energy.  It is safer than wind turbines and solar panels.  After reviewing data on the Fukushima and Chernobyl accidents, the WHO found that a large proportion of the damage was caused by panic.  The UN has also conducted comprehensive studies of the Chernobyl disaster.  The explosion at the Chernobyl nuclear power plant is the worst nuclear accident of all that happened.  As a result, 28 people died from acute radiation syndrome and another 15 people died over the next 25 years from thyroid cancer.  16,000 people became ill with thyroid cancer after Chernobyl, and it is estimated that 160 of them will die from this type of cancer.  The Fukushima nuclear disaster ranks second in severity.  The radiation emission was much smaller than that of Chernobyl.  There are no deaths from radiation after Fukushima.  Fifteen thousand people were killed, who were dragged out of nursing homes and hospitals.  They received a large dose of radiation just because they were moved a long distance.  In many ways, this was the result of a general panic.  For a person living in a big city, such as London, Berlin or New York, the risk of mortality increases by 2.8% from air pollution alone.  For those who live near smokers – by 1.7%.  For the liquidators of the Chernobyl accident, who received a dose of radiation of 250 millisieverts, it increased by only 1%.  By comparison, fuel energy creates uncontrolled waste in the form of greenhouse gas emissions, which kills 7 million people a year.  Therefore, the reduction of fuel energy in favor of nuclear energy has already saved the lives of 1.8 million people.  What about the waste?  Nuclear waste, as it turned out, is not so much.  If you take nuclear waste from the entire history of the United States and fill a football stadium with it, their height will be only 6 m. The waste is stored in special isolated containers, and they are constantly monitored.  In addition, development is underway to use nuclear waste as fuel.  It is the same with nuclear weapons.  There are no examples of countries with nuclear industry suddenly starting to develop nuclear weapons.  In fact, the opposite is happening.  It turns out that the only known way to get rid of a large number of nuclear weapons is to use plutonium from warheads as fuel for nuclear power plants.  Over the next 50 years, humanity will consume more energy than has been consumed in all previous history.  Earlier forecasts about the growth rate of energy consumption and the development of new energy technologies did not materialize: the level of consumption is growing much faster, and new energy sources will work on an industrial scale and at competitive prices not earlier than 2030.  The problem of the shortage of fossil energy resources is becoming more acute.  The capacity to build new hydropower plants is also very limited.  Do not forget about the fight against the “greenhouse effect ”, which imposes restrictions on the burning of oil, gas and coal in thermal power plants.  The solution to the problem can be the active development of nuclear energy, one of the youngest and fastest growing sectors of the global economy.  An increasing number of countries today come to the need to start the development of a peaceful atom.  The use of nuclear power may prove to be one of the solutions to these pressing problems, however unlikely it may seem.  But for this, the methods of its application need to be reviewed.  At the heart of the production of atomic energy is the force that holds the parts of the atom together.  If an atom is unstable, it will tend to move to a more stable state by splitting.  The instability of the atom can be natural or caused by the addition of additional neutrons to the nucleus.  When the atom becomes more stable and ejects particles, a huge amount of energy is released, which in a closed system can be used to generate enough heat to propel the turbine.  Radiation, which is often misrepresented, occurs for the most part due to natural causes.  Let ’ s see what the advantages of nuclear power are: 1 kg of uranium can produce 90,000 times more energy than 1 kg of coal.  Modern technologies make it possible to switch to a closed fuel cycle, which involves the repeated use of fuel products and the minimization of waste.  Every year, nuclear power plants in Europe avoid the emission of 700 million tons of CO2.  One job in the construction of nuclear power plants creates more than 10 jobs in related industries.  The development of nuclear energy contributes to the growth of scientific research and intellectual potential of the country.  According to the IAEA directory published in 2019, 98 nuclear reactors operated in the United States in 2018, 58 in France, 46 in China, 39 in Japan, 38 in Russia, 24 in the Republic of Korea, 22 in India, 19 in Canada, and 15 in the United Kingdom and Ukraine.  The total generating capacity of the nuclear power plant is over 380 GW.  A nuclear power plant is a complex of necessary systems, devices, equipment and structures designed to generate electricity by using the heat released in a nuclear reactor as a result of a controlled fission chain reaction of the nuclei of heavy elements (mainly uranium-233, uranium-235, plutonium-239).  The heat generated in the core of the nuclear reactor is transferred (directly or through an intermediate coolant) to the working medium (mainly water vapor), which drives steam turbines with turbogenerators, where the mechanical energy of the steam is converted into electrical energy.  Then the electricity through the wires goes to consumers.  As heat carriers, ordinary and heavy water, water vapor, liquid metals, organic liquids, some gases, for example, helium or carbon dioxide, are used.  The coolant circulates through sealed pipelines, which, in combination with circulation pumps, form a so-called reactor circuit or loop.  The circuits through which the coolant circulates are always closed to avoid leakage of radioactivity, their number is determined mainly by the type of nuclear reactor, as well as the properties of the working fluid and coolant.  Nuclear power plants can have single-circuit, double-circuit and three-circuit circuit of heat carrier operation.  Single-circuit circuit is used at nuclear power plants with channel-type reactors.  In such nuclear power plants, the coolant is also a working fluid.  In them, the boiling reactor itself is a steam generator, so the entire circuit is radioactive.  It's surrounded by biological defenses.  Two-circuit circuit circuit is used at nuclear power plants with water-water reactors.  In such nuclear power plants, water is supplied under pressure to the reactor core, which is heated.  Heat carrier energy is used in steam generator to form saturated steam.  The first circuit is radioactive and is surrounded by biological protection, except when inert gas is used as heat carrier.  The second circuit is usually radiation-safe, since the working fluid and coolant of the first circuit do not touch.  Three-circuit circuit circuit is used at nuclear power plants with fast neutron reactors with sodium coolant.  To exclude contact of radioactive sodium with water, a second circuit with non-radioactive sodium is constructed.  Thus, the scheme turns out to be three-circuit. Content: The launch ceremony of the International Thermonuclear Fusion Experimental Reactor (ITER) project was held in France on July 28. On July 28, the International Thermonuclear Fusion Experimental Reactor (ITER), humanity ’ s largest nuclear fusion project, began a five-year assembly project in southern France, marking a new phase for the largest nuclear fusion project in human history.  + 4 + 3 + 2 The Guardian reported on July 28 that representatives of the participating countries of the project participated in the installation and launch ceremony of ITER on the same day. Speaking at the launch ceremony, ITER Director General Bernard Bigot said that the clean energy generated by the ITER project would be a “miracle for the planet ” and that the energy provided by nuclear fusion and other renewable energy sources would transform energy use in industries such as transport, construction and industry.  The Guardian notes that the ITER project aims to provide conceptual proof for large-scale nuclear fusion, not for future commercial use.  Consisting of millions of components, the nuclear fusion device will be the first self-heating plasma, which is expected to generate 10 times more heat than the input, far more than any previous related test, and the process itself will not produce carbon dioxide that can cause climate warming, and will produce less radioactive waste, which is expected to power magnets and scientific instruments.  The main purpose of the ITER project is to simulate the process of nuclear fusion in which the sun generates energy, so its core device, the tokamak, which controls fusion reactions, is also known as the "artificial sun". Title: Scientists to Build Artificial Solar Power Meet in France – Radio France Internationale
Content: Fourteen years after receiving official approval, scientists began assembling a machine in southern France on Monday seeking to confirm whether nuclear fusion could be a safe and reliable source of energy on Earth.  In the ground-breaking International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor (ITER), components from around the world have arrived in the southern French town of Saint-Paul-les-Durance in recent months.  These components must now be painstakingly assembled to complete ITER, which has been touted as the “world ’ s largest puzzle. ”  The purpose of this experimental facility is to demonstrate that nuclear fusion can generate electricity on a large, safe and commercial scale.  “Nuclear fusion provides clean, reliable and carbon-free energy, ” said a joint statement from 35 countries participating in ITER, including the 27 EU member states, the United Kingdom, Switzerland, India, Japan, South Korea, Russia, the United States and China.  In addition, fuel for nuclear fusion can be obtained from seawater and lithium metals, which are abundant enough to supply humans for millions of years.  The statement said that such fuel, the size of a pineapple, is equivalent to 10,000 tons of coal.  ITER will be built from about 1 million components and is scheduled to begin preliminary experiments in December 2025.  The artificial solar facility is designed to generate about 500 megawatts of thermal energy, which, if sustained, can be converted into about 200 megawatts of electricity, enough to power about 200,000 homes. passages.title: Japanese suicide toll rises for first time in 10 years – Radio France Internationale
passages.passage: TOKYO (AFP) - The Japanese government's progress in curbing the high suicide rate for years has been reversed by the epidemic.  The number of suicides in Japan last year was higher than the previous year, the first in 10 years.  Japan ’ s Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare said today that according to preliminary data, 20,919 people died by suicide in 2020, an increase of 3.7% over the previous year.  In the same period, 3,460 people died from COVID-19.  This means that for the first time in more than a decade, the number of suicides has increased year on year, with particularly high rates among women and children.  Japan has long had the highest suicide rate among the Group of Seven, but South Korea is even higher in Asia.  The Japanese government has made continuous efforts in recent years to provide better help to people with mental health needs.  Compared to some other countries, Japan ’ s epidemic is relatively mild, so it does not have to adopt strict lockdown measures like other countries. Suicide rates fell in the first half of 2020, raising hopes that the impact of the epidemic may be limited.  But the number of suicides began to rise in July after the nationwide emergency was lifted in May.  According to experts, tracking data shows that suicides usually fall in the first phase of crises, such as conflict and natural disasters, before rising sharply.  Luko Ueda, an associate professor of political economy at Waseda University in Tokyo who studies suicide in Japan, said that the increase in the number of suicides in Japan is a big deal, and she believes it is a major turning point.  She told AFP that COVID-19 was definitely an important factor, warning: “We cannot deny the possibility that the numbers will rise again this year. ” © 2021 AFP

Why among women victims more Rupert Wingfield-Hayes BBC News, Tokyo Suicides in Japan are recorded faster and more accurately than anywhere else in the world.  Unlike most countries, reporting is done on a monthly basis.  And during the Covid-19 pandemic, these statistics turned out to be more alarming than before.  In 2020, for the first time in 11 years, the number of suicides in Japan increased.  However, although the number of suicides among men decreased slightly, the increase among women was almost 15%.  In October alone, the suicide rate among women in Japan jumped more than 70% compared to the same month last year.  What's going on?  And why does the pandemic seem to affect women far more than men?  A young woman (her BBC identity unknown) met Rupert Wingfield-Hayes in Yokohama A face-to-face meeting with a young woman who repeatedly tried to commit suicide is not a pleasant experience.  I have a deep respect for people who work on suicide prevention.  I'm sitting in Yokohama's red light district in a center run by a suicide prevention charity called the Bond Project.  Anyone can enter here, no pre-registration is required.  At the table opposite, a 19-year-old woman with a short haircut is sitting motionless.  Quietly, without any emotion in her voice, she begins to tell me her story.  She said it all started when she was 15.  Her older brother began to harass her.  She eventually ran away from home, but the pain and loneliness didn ’ t go away.  Suicide seemed like the only way out.  “I ’ ve been to the hospital many times since that time last year, ” she tells me.“ I tried to kill myself many times, but I didn ’ t succeed.  It seems that attempts to die will have to be abandoned. ”  The Bond Project intervened in her life.  His staff found her a safe place to live and began intensive psychotherapy.  June Tachibana is the founder of the Bond Project, a tough woman in her 40s and a tireless optimist.  Joon Tachibana hopes the Bond Project will provide women with the help they need "When girls are in big trouble and hurt, they really don't know what to do," she says.  "We are ready to listen to them, to tell them - we are with you."  Tachibana says Covid-19 seems to be pushing vulnerable people to make a fateful decision.  She describes some of the calls her employees have received in recent months.  “We often hear ‘ I want to die ’ and ‘ I have nowhere to go, ’ ” she says.  They say, "It's so painful, I'm so lonely, I want to disappear."  The pandemic has made life much more difficult for those who are physically or sexually abused.  “The girl I spoke to the other day said her father was sexually harassing her, ” Tachibana tells me.“ But because of the covid, her father doesn ’ t work much and spends a lot of time at home, and she manages to escape from him. ”  If you look at previous crisis moments in Japan, for example, the banking crisis of 2008 or the collapse of the Japanese stock market and the real estate bubble in the early 1990s, the effect was felt mainly by middle-aged men.  During these periods, there were sharp spikes in the number of suicides among men.  A pandemic is a different story.  It affects young people, especially young women.  The reasons for this are very multifaceted.  At one time, Japan had the highest suicide rate among developed countries.  Over the past decade, it has been reduced by about a third.  Professor Michiko Ueda is one of Japan ’ s leading experts on suicide.  It tells me how alarming the growth dynamics have become over the past few months.  “This scenario leading to female suicide is very, very unusual, ” she says.  “In all the time I ’ ve been doing research on this topic, I ’ ve never seen such significant growth.  The peculiarity of the pandemic is that the industries in which many women are employed - tourism, retail trade and the food industry - have suffered the most. "  In Japan, there are more and more unmarried women living on their own.  Many of them prefer such a life to marriage, which still assumes quite traditional gender roles.  Professor Ueda says that young women are much more likely to find themselves in a state of so-called "casual employment."  Professor Michiko Ueda said: “Many women are no longer married, they have to earn a living, but they don ’ t have a regular job.  So when something happens, of course, they suffer a lot.  The number of lost jobs among non-permanent workers has increased significantly over the past eight months. ”  One month stands out.  In October last year, 879 women committed suicide.  This is more than 70% higher than in October 2019.  Newspapers are alarmed.  Some even compare the total number of suicides (both men and women) in October - 2,199 - with the total number of deaths in Japan from the coronavirus at that time - 2,087.  Something strange has happened.  On September 27 last year, a very famous and popular actress named Yuko Takeuchi was found dead in her home.  It was later reported that she had committed suicide.  Photo caption: 40-year-old Japanese actress Yuko Takeuchi was found dead in her home Yasuyuki Shimizu, a former journalist.  Today, he runs a non-profit organization dedicated to suicide in Japan.  “From the moment it becomes known about the suicide of any celebrity, the number of suicides increases and remains at this new level for about 10 days, ” he says. – For example, for the suicide of Takeuchi on September 27 in the next 10 days, 207 women committed suicide. ”  If you count the number of suicides of women about the same age as Yuko Takeuchi, the statistics become even more obvious.  "Of all age groups, Takeuchi's death has had the greatest impact on women in their 40s and 50s," says Yasuyuki Shimizu. "Suicide rates have more than doubled in this age group."  Other experts also agree that there is a link between celebrity suicides and the spike in suicides in the days that followed.  This phenomenon is not unique to Japan, and this is one of the reasons why reporting suicides is not easy.  The more celebrity suicide is discussed in the media and on social media, the more it affects other vulnerable people, especially in the early days.  Mai Suganuma works for the Shimizu organization.  Her father killed himself when she was a teenager.  Now it helps to support the families of those who have voluntarily passed away.  The pandemic makes the lives of suicide families much more difficult.  “Members of the suicide family often blame themselves for what happened, ” says Mai Suganuma. – I also blamed myself for not being able to save my father.  And now they say, "Stay at home."  I fear that this will increase the sense of guilt.  The Japanese don ’ t usually talk about death.  We don ’ t have the habit of talking about suicide. ”  Japan is now experiencing a third wave of the epidemic, and the government has declared a state of emergency for the second time.  Most likely, it will last until the end of February.  More and more restaurants, hotels and bars are being quarantined, and more people are losing their jobs. Title: Japanese suicide toll rises for first time in 10 years – Radio France Internationale
Content: TOKYO (AFP) - The Japanese government's progress in curbing the high suicide rate for years has been reversed by the epidemic.  The number of suicides in Japan last year was higher than the previous year, the first in 10 years.  Japan ’ s Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare said today that according to preliminary data, 20,919 people died by suicide in 2020, an increase of 3.7% over the previous year.  In the same period, 3,460 people died from COVID-19.  This means that for the first time in more than a decade, the number of suicides has increased year on year, with particularly high rates among women and children.  Japan has long had the highest suicide rate among the Group of Seven, but South Korea is even higher in Asia.  The Japanese government has made continuous efforts in recent years to provide better help to people with mental health needs.  Compared to some other countries, Japan ’ s epidemic is relatively mild, so it does not have to adopt strict lockdown measures like other countries. Suicide rates fell in the first half of 2020, raising hopes that the impact of the epidemic may be limited.  But the number of suicides began to rise in July after the nationwide emergency was lifted in May.  According to experts, tracking data shows that suicides usually fall in the first phase of crises, such as conflict and natural disasters, before rising sharply.  Luko Ueda, an associate professor of political economy at Waseda University in Tokyo who studies suicide in Japan, said that the increase in the number of suicides in Japan is a big deal, and she believes it is a major turning point.  She told AFP that COVID-19 was definitely an important factor, warning: “We cannot deny the possibility that the numbers will rise again this year. ” © 2021 AFP
