Title: Covid and suicides in Japan. Why there are more victims among women
Content: Covid and suicides in Japan.  Why among women victims more Rupert Wingfield-Hayes BBC News, Tokyo Suicides in Japan are recorded faster and more accurately than anywhere else in the world.  Unlike most countries, reporting is done on a monthly basis.  And during the Covid-19 pandemic, these statistics turned out to be more alarming than before.  In 2020, for the first time in 11 years, the number of suicides in Japan increased.  However, although the number of suicides among men decreased slightly, the increase among women was almost 15%.  In October alone, the suicide rate among women in Japan jumped more than 70% compared to the same month last year.  What's going on?  And why does the pandemic seem to affect women far more than men?  A young woman (her BBC identity unknown) met Rupert Wingfield-Hayes in Yokohama A face-to-face meeting with a young woman who repeatedly tried to commit suicide is not a pleasant experience.  I have a deep respect for people who work on suicide prevention.  I'm sitting in Yokohama's red light district in a center run by a suicide prevention charity called the Bond Project.  Anyone can enter here, no pre-registration is required.  At the table opposite, a 19-year-old woman with a short haircut is sitting motionless.  Quietly, without any emotion in her voice, she begins to tell me her story.  She said it all started when she was 15.  Her older brother began to harass her.  She eventually ran away from home, but the pain and loneliness didn ’ t go away.  Suicide seemed like the only way out.  “I ’ ve been to the hospital many times since that time last year, ” she tells me.“ I tried to kill myself many times, but I didn ’ t succeed.  It seems that attempts to die will have to be abandoned. ”  The Bond Project intervened in her life.  His staff found her a safe place to live and began intensive psychotherapy.  June Tachibana is the founder of the Bond Project, a tough woman in her 40s and a tireless optimist.  Joon Tachibana hopes the Bond Project will provide women with the help they need "When girls are in big trouble and hurt, they really don't know what to do," she says.  "We are ready to listen to them, to tell them - we are with you."  Tachibana says Covid-19 seems to be pushing vulnerable people to make a fateful decision.  She describes some of the calls her employees have received in recent months.  “We often hear ‘ I want to die ’ and ‘ I have nowhere to go, ’ ” she says.  They say, "It's so painful, I'm so lonely, I want to disappear."  The pandemic has made life much more difficult for those who are physically or sexually abused.  “The girl I spoke to the other day said her father was sexually harassing her, ” Tachibana tells me.“ But because of the covid, her father doesn ’ t work much and spends a lot of time at home, and she manages to escape from him. ”  If you look at previous crisis moments in Japan, for example, the banking crisis of 2008 or the collapse of the Japanese stock market and the real estate bubble in the early 1990s, the effect was felt mainly by middle-aged men.  During these periods, there were sharp spikes in the number of suicides among men.  A pandemic is a different story.  It affects young people, especially young women.  The reasons for this are very multifaceted.  At one time, Japan had the highest suicide rate among developed countries.  Over the past decade, it has been reduced by about a third.  Professor Michiko Ueda is one of Japan ’ s leading experts on suicide.  It tells me how alarming the growth dynamics have become over the past few months.  “This scenario leading to female suicide is very, very unusual, ” she says.  “In all the time I ’ ve been doing research on this topic, I ’ ve never seen such significant growth.  The peculiarity of the pandemic is that the industries in which many women are employed - tourism, retail trade and the food industry - have suffered the most. "  In Japan, there are more and more unmarried women living on their own.  Many of them prefer such a life to marriage, which still assumes quite traditional gender roles.  Professor Ueda says that young women are much more likely to find themselves in a state of so-called "casual employment."  Professor Michiko Ueda said: “Many women are no longer married, they have to earn a living, but they don ’ t have a regular job.  So when something happens, of course, they suffer a lot.  The number of lost jobs among non-permanent workers has increased significantly over the past eight months. ”  One month stands out.  In October last year, 879 women committed suicide.  This is more than 70% higher than in October 2019.  Newspapers are alarmed.  Some even compare the total number of suicides (both men and women) in October - 2,199 - with the total number of deaths in Japan from the coronavirus at that time - 2,087.  Something strange has happened.  On September 27 last year, a very famous and popular actress named Yuko Takeuchi was found dead in her home.  It was later reported that she had committed suicide.  Photo caption: 40-year-old Japanese actress Yuko Takeuchi was found dead in her home Yasuyuki Shimizu, a former journalist.  Today, he runs a non-profit organization dedicated to suicide in Japan.  “From the moment it becomes known about the suicide of any celebrity, the number of suicides increases and remains at this new level for about 10 days, ” he says. – For example, for the suicide of Takeuchi on September 27 in the next 10 days, 207 women committed suicide. ”  If you count the number of suicides of women about the same age as Yuko Takeuchi, the statistics become even more obvious.  "Of all age groups, Takeuchi's death has had the greatest impact on women in their 40s and 50s," says Yasuyuki Shimizu. "Suicide rates have more than doubled in this age group."  Other experts also agree that there is a link between celebrity suicides and the spike in suicides in the days that followed.  This phenomenon is not unique to Japan, and this is one of the reasons why reporting suicides is not easy.  The more celebrity suicide is discussed in the media and on social media, the more it affects other vulnerable people, especially in the early days.  Mai Suganuma works for the Shimizu organization.  Her father killed himself when she was a teenager.  Now it helps to support the families of those who have voluntarily passed away.  The pandemic makes the lives of suicide families much more difficult.  “Members of the suicide family often blame themselves for what happened, ” says Mai Suganuma. – I also blamed myself for not being able to save my father.  And now they say, "Stay at home."  I fear that this will increase the sense of guilt.  The Japanese don ’ t usually talk about death.  We don ’ t have the habit of talking about suicide. ”  Japan is now experiencing a third wave of the epidemic, and the government has declared a state of emergency for the second time.  Most likely, it will last until the end of February.  More and more restaurants, hotels and bars are being quarantined, and more people are losing their jobs. It seems that attempts to die will have to be abandoned. ”  The Bond Project intervened in her life.  His staff found her a safe place to live and began intensive psychotherapy.  June Tachibana is the founder of the Bond Project, a tough woman in her 40s and a tireless optimist.  Joon Tachibana hopes the Bond Project will provide women with the help they need "When girls are in big trouble and hurt, they really don't know what to do," she says.  "We are ready to listen to them, to tell them - we are with you."  Tachibana says Covid-19 seems to be pushing vulnerable people to make a fateful decision.  She describes some of the calls her employees have received in recent months.  “We often hear ‘ I want to die ’ and ‘ I have nowhere to go, ’ ” she says.  They say, "It's so painful, I'm so lonely, I want to disappear."  The pandemic has made life much more difficult for those who are physically or sexually abused.  “The girl I spoke to the other day said her father was sexually harassing her, ” Tachibana tells me.“ But because of the covid, her father doesn ’ t work much and spends a lot of time at home, and she manages to escape from him. ”  If you look at previous crisis moments in Japan, for example, the banking crisis of 2008 or the collapse of the Japanese stock market and the real estate bubble in the early 1990s, the effect was felt mainly by middle-aged men.  During these periods, there were sharp spikes in the number of suicides among men.  A pandemic is a different story.  It affects young people, especially young women.  The reasons for this are very multifaceted.  At one time, Japan had the highest suicide rate among developed countries.  Over the past decade, it has been reduced by about a third.  Professor Michiko Ueda is one of Japan ’ s leading experts on suicide.  It tells me how alarming the growth dynamics have become over the past few months.  “This scenario leading to female suicide is very, very unusual, ” she says.  “In all the time I ’ ve been doing research on this topic, I ’ ve never seen such significant growth.  The peculiarity of the pandemic is that the industries in which many women are employed - tourism, retail trade and the food industry - have suffered the most. "  In Japan, there are more and more unmarried women living on their own.  Many of them prefer such a life to marriage, which still assumes quite traditional gender roles.  Professor Ueda says that young women are much more likely to find themselves in a state of so-called "casual employment."  Professor Michiko Ueda said: “Many women are no longer married, they have to earn a living, but they don ’ t have a regular job.  So when something happens, of course, they suffer a lot.  The number of lost jobs among non-permanent workers has increased significantly over the past eight months. ”  One month stands out.  In October last year, 879 women committed suicide.  This is more than 70% higher than in October 2019.  Newspapers are alarmed.  Some even compare the total number of suicides (both men and women) in October - 2,199 - with the total number of deaths in Japan from the coronavirus at that time - 2,087.  Something strange has happened.  On September 27 last year, a very famous and popular actress named Yuko Takeuchi was found dead in her home.  It was later reported that she had committed suicide.  Photo caption: 40-year-old Japanese actress Yuko Takeuchi was found dead in her home Yasuyuki Shimizu, a former journalist.  Today, he runs a non-profit organization dedicated to suicide in Japan.  “From the moment it becomes known about the suicide of any celebrity, the number of suicides increases and remains at this new level for about 10 days, ” he says. – For example, for the suicide of Takeuchi on September 27 in the next 10 days, 207 women committed suicide. ”  If you count the number of suicides of women about the same age as Yuko Takeuchi, the statistics become even more obvious.  "Of all age groups, Takeuchi's death has had the greatest impact on women in their 40s and 50s," says Yasuyuki Shimizu. "Suicide rates have more than doubled in this age group."  Other experts also agree that there is a link between celebrity suicides and the spike in suicides in the days that followed.  This phenomenon is not unique to Japan, and this is one of the reasons why reporting suicides is not easy.  The more celebrity suicide is discussed in the media and on social media, the more it affects other vulnerable people, especially in the early days.  Mai Suganuma works for the Shimizu organization.  Her father killed himself when she was a teenager.  Now it helps to support the families of those who have voluntarily passed away.  The pandemic makes the lives of suicide families much more difficult.  “Members of the suicide family often blame themselves for what happened, ” says Mai Suganuma. – I also blamed myself for not being able to save my father.  And now they say, "Stay at home."  I fear that this will increase the sense of guilt.  The Japanese don ’ t usually talk about death.  We don ’ t have the habit of talking about suicide. ”  Japan is now experiencing a third wave of the epidemic, and the government has declared a state of emergency for the second time.  Most likely, it will last until the end of February.  More and more restaurants, hotels and bars are being quarantined, and more people are losing their jobs. passages.title: Israel, the UAE and Bahrain reach peace deals: five things that are stirring up the Middle East landscape
passages.passage: Image copyright Reuters Image caption Israel's national security adviser flew to the United Arab Emirates on September 1.  A high-level delegation from Israel and the United Arab Emirates will sign a historic peace agreement led by the United States at the White House on Tuesday, September 15, when the UAE and Israel will formally establish diplomatic relations.  U.S. President Donald Trump announced last week that Bahrain ’ s foreign minister would attend the event and sign a comprehensive normalization agreement with Israel alone.  The signing of these agreements will change the landscape in the Middle East. BBC explains why these agreements are important.  Gulf countries see more trade opportunities This agreement will help ambitious UAE.  They built up their own military forces and developed the UAE into a place of business and holiday.  The Americans used the promise of advanced weapons to help reach this agreement.  In the past, the UAE was barely able to buy weapons including the F-35 stealth fighter and the EA-18G Growler electronic fighter.  The UAE has deployed well-equipped armed forces in Libya and Yemen.  But its greatest potential enemy is Iran on the other side of the Gulf.  Israel, like the United States and the United Arab Emirates, is skeptical of Iran.  The same goes for Bahrain.  Until 1969, Iran claimed Bahrain as part of its territory.  Bahrain ’ s Sunni rulers also believe that members of its unstable Shia majority could become Iran ’ s fifth pillar.  The two Gulf states are no longer hiding ties with Israel.  They expect open trade because Israel has the most advanced high-tech industrial chain in the world.  In the non-Covid-19 era, Israelis are avid vacationers who are passionate about exploring the deserts, beaches and shopping centers around the Gulf.  There are business opportunities everywhere.  For Israel, normalization of relations with the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain is a real achievement.  In the 1920s, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu firmly believed in the strategy of building an “iron wall ” between the Jewish state and the Arab states.  The idea is that Israel ’ s strength will eventually make the Arab states realize that their only option is to acknowledge Israel ’ s existence.  Israelis don ’ t like being isolated in the Middle East.  Peace efforts with Egypt and Jordan have never been so enthusiastic.  They may be more looking forward to a better future relationship with the Gulf states far away from Jerusalem and the occupied territories.  Strengthening the anti-Iran coalition is another major advantage.  Netanyahu views Iran as Israel ’ s number one enemy, sometimes comparing its leaders to the Nazis.  He has dropped his previous complaints about the UAE arms deal.  Netanyahu is also troubled, and he is facing a possible jail term for corruption.  His handling of the COVID-19 pandemic went well in the early stages, and badly in the later stages.  Opponents gather weekly outside his Jerusalem residence.  The ceremony at the White House was appropriate.  Image copyright Reuters Image caption Trump announced the so-called Abraham Accord at the White House in August. 3.  Trump celebrated the foreign policy coup, an agreement that has implications for the president of the United States on multiple levels.  This is conducive to Trump ’ s “maximum pressure ” strategy on Iran.  In the year of the election, this helps to support his claim that he is the best trader in the world.  Anything he does that is good for Israel, or more specifically for Netanyahu ’ s government, is good for maintaining good relations with Christian evangelical voters in the United States.  These are important parts of his constituency.  If the Arab states in the Gulf can handle their relations with Israel openly, rather than secretly, then the anti-Iran “Friends of America ” coalition should work more smoothly.  Trump ’ s so-called “deal of the century ” has made peace between Israel and the Palestinians impossible.  But the Abraham Accords between Israel and the UAE are known to have led to a major shift in the Middle East landscape, which the Trump administration has called a major foreign policy coup.  Image copyright Reuters Image caption Palestinian leaders have condemned the actions of the two Gulf states to restore relations with Israel.  The Palestinians felt betrayed that they were once again the last of the tournament.  The Palestinians condemned the Abrahamic Agreement as a betrayal.  The new agreement breaks the long-standing Arab consensus that the price of establishing diplomatic relations with Israel is recognition of Palestinian independence.  But now, Israel is consolidating new public relations with the Arab states, while the Palestinians remain occupied in East Jerusalem, the West Bank, and an area the size of an open prison in Gaza.  Mohammed Al Nahyan, the de facto ruler of the UAE, said his price for the deal was Israel ’ s agreement to stop annexing large parts of the West Bank.  At least because of the current international pressure, Netanyahu seems to have abandoned the idea.  The UAE offered him a way out of the embarrassing political deadlock.  Bahrain joined the agreement and Palestinian tensions increased.  Without Saudi Arabia ’ s approval, that would never have happened.  Saudi Arabia is the leader of the Arab Peace Plan for Palestinian independence.  King Kal Salman was the administrator of two temples in Islam, which gave him great authority.  He is unlikely to suddenly recognize Israel's independence.  His son and successor, Mohammed bin Salman, may also be reluctant to do so.  Image copyright EPA Image caption An agreement between the United Arab Emirates and Israel sparked protests in Iran  Iran Has New Strategic Trouble The deal has been roundly condemned by Iran's leaders.  It ’ s not just about words, the Abrahamic Agreement puts them under even more pressure.  Trump ’ s sanctions have caused real economic pain in Iran.  Now they also have strategic problems.  Israel ’ s home air base is far from Iran, but the UAE ’ s air base is opposite the Gulf waters.  It is very important if we talk again about air strikes on Iranian nuclear bases.  Israel, the United States, Bahrain and the United Arab Emirates have a bunch of new options.  Iran has found that their room for manoeuvre has been reduced.

passages.title: Trump said about the possible desire of Palestine to normalize ties with Israel
passages.passage: US President Donald Trump believes that the state of Palestine would also like to take some steps to normalize relations with Israel.  He said this on Friday, October 23, in the presence of journalists during a telephone conversation with the leaders of Israel and Sudan.  Earlier, it was officially announced that the two countries had reached an agreement on normalizing ties through the mediation of the United States.  Thus, Sudan became another country to join the “Abrahamic Agreements ”.  “By the way, the Palestinians, if you ask about the Palestinians, want to do something about it.  They've never seen anything like it.  They want to do something.  I am sure that this will also be done, "TASS quoted the head of the White House as saying.  According to the American leader, now “at least five ” Muslim countries want to sign agreements on the normalization of relations with Israel.  And as Trump added, there will soon be many more.  Earlier in October, the Knesset of Israel approved an agreement on the normalization of relations between the Jewish state and the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain.  The agreements on normalization of relations were signed on September 15 at the White House by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, UAE Foreign Minister Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan and Bahraini Foreign Minister Abdel Latif al-Zayani.  The event was held at the White House in the presence of US President Donald Trump, his wife Melania and invited guests.  One of the points of the “Abraham accords ” implies a suspension by Israel of the extension of its sovereignty to Jewish settlements in the West Bank.  This condition is spelled out in Washington ’ s plan to resolve the Palestinian-Israeli conflict.  The signing of the agreements was condemned in Palestine.  They recalled their ambassador to the UAE and called Abu Dhabi ’ s actions an aggression against its people and a disregard for their rights and shrines.  The Arab Peace Initiative adopted in 2002, on which Palestine is based, provides for the possibility of concluding peace agreements and establishing good-neighbourly relations between the Arabs and Israel, but only if the Jewish State withdraws from the territories it occupied in 1967, including the Golan Heights and the Shab'a farms, and recognizes the State of Palestine in the West Bank and Gaza Strip, with East Jerusalem as its capital.

passages.title: NEWSru.co.il:: The Palestinian Authority is restoring relations with Israel
passages.passage: PA Civil Administration Minister Hussein al-Sheikh said the Palestinian Authority was restoring full relations with Israel.  According to the Wafa news agency, the Palestinian side will return to compliance with all the agreements that existed on May 19, 2020.  The minister said that Israel, through international mediators, had conveyed to PA President Mahmoud Abbas both written and oral commitments to abide by all agreements signed with the Palestinians.  Hamas issued a statement condemning the Palestinian Authority ’ s decision to restore relations with Israel.  The statement said that by his decision Ramallah legalizes the process of normalization of relations with Israel.  The PA chairman announced the rupture of relations with Israel after the publication of the US-prepared plan for a Palestinian-Israeli settlement - the so-called "deal of the century".  The plan provided for the extension of Israeli sovereignty to part of the territory of Judea and Samaria.  “Our rupture of agreements with the occupiers, undertaken after consultations with the leadership of the Palestinian factions, does not mean that we do not want peace.  We extend our hand and propose to hold an international conference under the auspices of the Quartet to work out a settlement mechanism, "Abbas said on June 24.  Israel has reported renouncing the annexation of Palestinian territories in normalization agreements with the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain.  The leaders of these countries declared their support for the principle of “two states ”, but noted that they do not intend to wait forever until the Palestinians agree to peace with Israel.  The Abraham Accords were perceived by the Palestinian side as a stab in the back.  Attempts to confront them have demonstrated the growing isolation of the Palestinians.  Even the Arab League refused to support them.  The rupture of relations with Israel led to the deterioration of the economic situation in the PA.  On the eve of the US presidential election, it was suggested that in the event of the victory of Democratic candidate Joe Biden, the Palestinian leadership would hurry to declare the restoration of relations, since the Palestinians themselves suffer from the rupture.

passages.title: Palestinians Condemn the Trilateral Agreement of the United Arab Emirates, the United States and Israel
passages.passage: On Thursday, August 13, the Zionist regime, along with the two countries of the United Arab Emirates and the United States, issued a joint statement announcing that they had concluded a trilateral agreement called the "Abraham Agreement" and mediated by Washington.  According to the agreement, the possibility of establishing diplomatic relations between the Zionist regime and the United Arab Emirates will be provided.  In response to this disgraceful agreement, the spokesman of the Palestinian Authority issued a statement explicitly stating that the Palestinian people strongly condemn the trilateral agreement between the Zionist regime, the United Arab Emirates and the United States.

passages.title: Trump mediates with UAE, Israel to agree to establish diplomatic relations
passages.passage: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu (left) and Prince Mohammed of Abu Dhabi, the United Arab Emirates, announced that the two countries have reached a peace agreement and relations will be fully normalized. (AFP) 2020-08-15 05: 30: 00 Palestine denounces the betrayal of Turkey's severance of diplomatic relations. On the third day, it was announced that a peace agreement had been reached, diplomatic relations would be fully normalized, and Israel agreed to suspend the annexation of Jewish settlements in the West Bank in exchange for the Arab League agreeing to become the third Arab country to recognize Israel after Egypt and Jordan, and the first Persian Gulf country to establish diplomatic relations with Israel.  The Palestinian self-rule government has been reviled by the Arab League for betrayal, Israel ’ s arch-enemy Iran has denounced it as a stupid strategy, and Turkey has threatened to sever ties with the Arab League.  In a joint statement, Trump, the first Gulf state to recognize Israel, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, and Saudi Arabia ’ s Prince Mohammed bin Zayed Al-Nahyan announced that they had agreed to normalize full Israeli-Arab relations and “chart a new path that opens up great potential in the Middle East. ”  The Israeli-Arab peace agreement, known as the "Abraham Accords" and described as a "historic" and "breakthrough for peace," will be signed at the White House. It will include strengthening bilateral economic relations, scientific and technological cooperation, the opening of direct flights, and the exchange of ambassadors and the establishment of embassies in the Arab capital Abu Dhabi and the Israeli city of Tel Aviv. Israel's new capital, Jerusalem, has established an embassy.  Please continue reading...  Suspension of the annexation of the West Bank?  However, the key to the agreement is whether Israel ’ s annexation of the West Bank will be suspended or suspended. The joint statement said that Israel will “suspend ” its declaration of sovereignty over the West Bank, but the Arab League ’ s Mohammed then said on Twitter that the agreement is a“ cessation ” of the annexation of Palestinian territory, but the hawk Netanyahu later insisted in a televised speech that the annexation plan was only "We will never renounce our rights to our territory."  The Israeli-Palestinian conflict has continued since Israel took the West Bank from the Palestinians in 1967 in the Six-Day War.  In his Middle East peace plan in January this year, Trump agreed to Israel's annexation of the West Bank of the Jordan River, with the government setting July 1 as the start date of the annexation plan.  The Palestinian Authority expressed "strong opposition and condemnation" to the establishment of diplomatic relations between Israel and Arab countries, viewing the Arab League's move as a betrayal and demanding an urgent meeting of the Arab League. Iran's Foreign Ministry criticized the establishment of diplomatic relations between the Arab League and Israel as a "strategic folly".  Israel has been boycotted by the Arab world and Muslim countries for historical and religious reasons, and isolated by its neighbors because of its geographical location.  But the United Kingdom, Germany, Bahrain, and Egypt, which has established diplomatic relations with Israel, are happy to see normalization.  U.S. President Donald Trump receives applause from the Middle East Policy team at the White House Oval Office after Israel and the United Arab Emirates reached a peace agreement.  From left, there are US Special Envoy to Iran, US Special Representative to the President and Special Representative for International Negotiations, US Ambassador to Israel Freeman, Trump son-in-law and Mideast peace plan planner Kushner, and US Treasury Secretary John Nuqin.

passages.title: Human Rights Watch: Israel and Hamas May Have Committed War Crimes
passages.passage: Human Rights Watch said on Tuesday that both Israel and Hamas may have committed war crimes during the May clashes.  During the 11-day battle, Hamas and other Palestinian groups fired thousands of rockets into Israeli territory and the Israeli army bombed the Gaza Strip from the ground and air.  Human Rights Watch said it used interviews with local residents and eyewitnesses, data analysis and digital images to produce its report.  According to the human rights organization, 62 Palestinian civilians were killed in three Israeli attacks in areas where no evidence of armed personnel has been found.  The report specifically examines Israeli air strikes on May 10 on the small town of Beit Hanoun in the northeast Gaza Strip, May 15 on the al-Shati refugee camp and May 16 on the city of Gaza.  Human Rights Watch added that “other Israeli attacks during this battle were also likely in violation of international law. ”  Eight people, including six children, were killed in an attack on May 10 that destroyed several homes.  At this point, Human Rights Watch says there is no indication of the presence of the armed forces or its use for military purposes.  “Any attack that does not have specific military objectives violates international law. ”  In the May 15 attack on the al-Shati refugee camp, a three-storey residential building was targeted and 10 people were killed.  A resident told Human Rights Watch that residents were not given any warning about the attack.  Israel claims that the reason for the attack was the presence of several senior Hamas leaders in the residential complex.  Human Rights Watch said no witnesses or family members of the victims confirmed the presence of Hamas operatives in or around the building.  It added that the building was likely targeted by a bomb produced by Boeing that the United States exported to Israel.  A third attack on May 16 killed three destroyed buildings and 44 civilians, including 18 children and 14 women, in Gaza City.  Human Rights Watch said eyewitnesses interviewed said Israel gave no warning before the attack.  Israeli army videos and pieces of munitions collected by Palestinian police show that the attack was also carried out by a one-ton Boeing bomb.  At the time of the attack, Israel said it was targeting Hamas militants' tunnels, but Human Rights Watch said it found "no evidence of military targets".  Human Rights Watch also condemned “reckless ” missile attacks on Israeli civilians and said it would address the issue in a separate report.  “Israel and the Palestinians have violated international law in this battle, which could amount to war crimes. ”  The Israeli government has not yet responded to the report, but a Hamas spokesman said: "This report shows that the occupation government acts with complete impunity and beyond the law and is never punished because of the full support of the United States."  In March, a prosecutor at the International Criminal Court announced a new and comprehensive investigation into the situation in the occupied Palestinian territories.  The main focus of the study will be the 2014 war in the Gaza Strip, but it will also look at the deaths of Palestinian protesters since 2018.  On May 27, the UN Human Rights Council approved an international investigation into the recent fighting in the Gaza Strip.  According to the local government of the Gaza Strip, 260 Palestinians, including gunmen, have been killed in the recent clashes.  The Israeli government says 13 people have been killed in the country, including a military man.  According to a report by the French news agency / Sr / Kr

passages.title: Zionists' actions in support of civil wars
passages.passage: A report published by the Al-Zaitouneh Research Center shows that the Zionist regime is leading the way in selling weapons to dictatorial regimes and spy equipment to Arab countries to spy on human rights activists along with money laundering.  The Al-Zaitouneh Research Center is an independent center in Beirut, founded in 2004, that conducts research on issues related to the Arab and Islamic world, particularly the Palestinian issue.  Unfortunately, some Arab countries and Arab political institutions are buying weapons from the Zionist regime.  This makes dialogue between Palestinian resistance groups and Arab political parties more necessary to counter such actions.  According to the report, Israel has been arming separatist movements in South Sudan, and the Sudanese have not reacted very seriously.  Referring to the nuclear actions of the Zionist regime, the report said that it is necessary to resume Arab studies on the dangers of the Zionist regime ’ s nuclear program against the Middle East.  These studies should be focused on the efforts of the Zionists in the production of chemical and biological weapons.  NSO Group Technologies is an Israeli spy company that uses its programs to spy on human rights activists and journalists around the world.  The company ’ s spy programs have also been used to assassinate Saudi activist Jamal Khashoggi, a critic of the Saudi regime, according to the report, the Zionist regime has not signed any of the agreements on the non-proliferation of nuclear, biological or chemical weapons.  Interestingly, these weapons end up in the hands of dictatorial regimes that violate human rights.  In addition, the Zionist regime is trying to support civil wars and power struggles by sending these weapons.  We are witnessing a process of money laundering and espionage along with the sale of these weapons in general, which is confirmed by the reports of international delegations and academic research.  Israel did not even sign the arms trade agreement, which was ratified by 82 countries in 2012, as it considers humanitarian and human rights issues an obstacle to its arms deals.  According to the report, the Zionist regime is working secretly with security companies in order to transfer weapons.  Spying-related technologies are another area of concern: NSO Group Technologies is one of the Zionist spy companies whose programs are used to spy on human rights activists and journalists around the world.  The company ’ s spy programs have also been used to assassinate Saudi activist Jamal Khashoggi, a critic of the Saudi regime.  According to the report, the Israeli company ’ s plans have been sold to the UAE, Morocco, Bahrain and Saudi Arabia.

passages.title: The Russian Jewish Congress commented on the accusations of human rights defenders against Israel
passages.passage: The human rights organization Human Rights Watch released a report in which it claims that the Israeli authorities commit crimes of apartheid in order to preserve the dominance of Jewish Israelis over the Palestinians.  This position is shared by the Israeli NGO B ’ Tselem, which collects information on human rights violations in the disputed territories.  These include the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, and the Gaza Strip, calling them Israeli-occupied territories.  HRW ’ s report is based on years of human rights monitoring, government planning documents, official statements, and other sources.  The experts compared the policy and real actions in the disputed territories and in Israel itself against the Palestinians and the Jewish population.  According to the organization, in July last year, a letter was sent to the Israeli authorities in which they were invited to present their vision of the situation, but a response has not yet been received.  German Zakharyaev, vice president of the Russian Jewish Congress (RJC) and president of the STMEGI Mountain Jews Foundation, called the entire HRW report not a serious study, but a damning pamphlet aimed at stigmatizing Israel as an apartheid state.  “The report is based on the false image of Israel as the country controlling the entire West Bank and Gaza Strip, but in reality it is not, only a few dozen Jewish settlements and a number of highways leading to them are under Israeli control.  The rest of the population is under the control of Mahmoud Abbas's Palestinian Authority and the Hamas movement in the Gaza Strip, "he said.  According to Zakharyaev, on the territory of Israel proper, Arab citizens are absolutely equal.  At the same time, he recognized the persistence of a significant difference in the social status and material situation of the Jewish and Arab populations.  At the same time, the vice-president of the RJC recalled that the same difference exists within the Jewish population - between immigrants from Europe and the countries of the East.  What does the report say?  Allocation of land.  It follows from the report that the authorities, both in Israel itself and in the disputed territories, mainly seek to provide land for Jewish communities.  Most Palestinians are driven into densely populated areas.  The organization also claims the existence of a certain policy of neutralization: for example, the state plan for the development of Jerusalem proceeds from the need for “confident preservation of the Jewish majority ” and even provides for desirable demographic proportions.  German Zakharyaev explained to Gazeta.ru that the Arab population prefers to live in large families and so-called hamuls, build houses near their loved ones in the territories of their towns and cities.  Moreover, he said, these structures are often illegal, allowing Palestinians to bypass the long and costly process of buying and registering property.  Cut off from the local community.  According to HRW, Israel has laws that allow hundreds of small Jewish municipalities to effectively cut off Palestinians from the local community.  In addition, according to the document, only a small part of the budget is allocated to Palestinian schools compared to the financing of schools where Jewish Israeli children study.  The report points out that in the disputed territories, the intensity of repression against Palestinians reaches the level of “systematic oppression ” as one of the hallmarks of apartheid.  The document refers to a draconian military administration for Palestinians in these territories, while Jewish Israelis living separately there are provided with the full range of rights under Israel ’ s model civil code.  Israeli political scientist, former adviser to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu Benny Briskin, said in a comment to Gazeta.ru that Israel ’ s judicial system is built in such a way that every real violation of human rights that occurs either in the disputed territories of the Palestinian Authority, or in the territory of Israel itself in relation to the Arabs, is checked and the guilty is always punished.  “Of course, there are exaggerations, but the Israeli judicial system is recognized by the whole world as serious, independent, which deals with all cases, ” he said.  Freedom of movement.  The authors of the report cite as serious violations of the fundamental rights of the Palestinians and the “inhumane actions ” against their freedom of movement in the form of the closure of the Gaza Strip and the imposition of a permit regime, the confiscation of more than a third of land in the West Bank with the forced eviction of thousands of Palestinians, the denial of housing rights, and the suspension of basic civil rights for millions of Palestinians.  Many of the violations underlying these crimes, according to the authors of the report, cannot be justified in the interests of security, including the almost complete ban on the issuance of building permits to Palestinians and the demolition of thousands of houses on the pretext of lack of such a permit.  There are also cases, according to human rights activists, when demographic goals are covered by security interests, as in the situation with the de facto freezing by the Israeli authorities of the registration of residents in the disputed territories.  The organization noted that this almost completely blocks the reunification of families of Palestinians living there and deprives residents of the Gaza Strip of the opportunity to get to the West Bank.  According to the RJC vice-president, the Gaza Strip is an independent administrative unit, from where Israel completely withdrew its army and settlements in 2005, and where today Hamas, recognized in Israel as a terrorist organization, is in power.  “Any interaction with it should be confirmed at the state and legislative level.  To date, based on security needs, some kind of restrictions are imposed.  It seems to me that it is difficult to interact with the administration, which for any reason or for no reason fires missiles at civilians, ” he said.  In addition, HRW recalled the constitutional law adopted in 2018, according to which Israel was declared the “national state of the Jewish people ”.  The authors of the document are convinced that the growing body of legislation increasingly favors Jewish settlers in the West Bank and does not extend to Palestinians living there.  As explained by German Zakharyaev, this law is designed to strengthen the status of Israel as a Jewish state.  According to the seventh paragraph of this law, the state of Israel sees the development of Jewish settlements as a national value for the entire Jewish people, he noted.  In addition, the expert drew attention to the fact that this law does not say anything about Jewish settlers in the West Bank, but only about the nature of the State of Israel.  Benny Briskin called such reports not new to Israel.  According to him, in Israel there are two points of view on this: either it is ordinary anti-Semitism, or it is left-wing liberalism.  But in any case, the result is the same - the attitude towards Israel is based on double standards, he stated.  “The approach of human rights organizations is that everything that happens in the territories they call occupied is already a crime.  It does not matter how the Jewish population behaves.  In Israel, they are already accustomed to this, ” the political scientist said.  He argues that the facts do not fit into these allegations. Title: Israel, the UAE and Bahrain reach peace deals: five things that are stirring up the Middle East landscape
Content: Image copyright Reuters Image caption Israel's national security adviser flew to the United Arab Emirates on September 1.  A high-level delegation from Israel and the United Arab Emirates will sign a historic peace agreement led by the United States at the White House on Tuesday, September 15, when the UAE and Israel will formally establish diplomatic relations.  U.S. President Donald Trump announced last week that Bahrain ’ s foreign minister would attend the event and sign a comprehensive normalization agreement with Israel alone.  The signing of these agreements will change the landscape in the Middle East. BBC explains why these agreements are important.  Gulf countries see more trade opportunities This agreement will help ambitious UAE.  They built up their own military forces and developed the UAE into a place of business and holiday.  The Americans used the promise of advanced weapons to help reach this agreement.  In the past, the UAE was barely able to buy weapons including the F-35 stealth fighter and the EA-18G Growler electronic fighter.  The UAE has deployed well-equipped armed forces in Libya and Yemen.  But its greatest potential enemy is Iran on the other side of the Gulf.  Israel, like the United States and the United Arab Emirates, is skeptical of Iran.  The same goes for Bahrain.  Until 1969, Iran claimed Bahrain as part of its territory.  Bahrain ’ s Sunni rulers also believe that members of its unstable Shia majority could become Iran ’ s fifth pillar. For Israel, normalization of relations with the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain is a real achievement.  In the 1920s, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu firmly believed in the strategy of building an “iron wall ” between the Jewish state and the Arab states.  The idea is that Israel ’ s strength will eventually make the Arab states realize that their only option is to acknowledge Israel ’ s existence.  Israelis don ’ t like being isolated in the Middle East.  Peace efforts with Egypt and Jordan have never been so enthusiastic. Title: Human Rights Watch: Israel and Hamas May Have Committed War Crimes
Content: Human Rights Watch said on Tuesday that both Israel and Hamas may have committed war crimes during the May clashes.  During the 11-day battle, Hamas and other Palestinian groups fired thousands of rockets into Israeli territory and the Israeli army bombed the Gaza Strip from the ground and air.  Human Rights Watch said it used interviews with local residents and eyewitnesses, data analysis and digital images to produce its report.  According to the human rights organization, 62 Palestinian civilians were killed in three Israeli attacks in areas where no evidence of armed personnel has been found.  The report specifically examines Israeli air strikes on May 10 on the small town of Beit Hanoun in the northeast Gaza Strip, May 15 on the al-Shati refugee camp and May 16 on the city of Gaza.  Human Rights Watch added that “other Israeli attacks during this battle were also likely in violation of international law. ”  Eight people, including six children, were killed in an attack on May 10 that destroyed several homes.  At this point, Human Rights Watch says there is no indication of the presence of the armed forces or its use for military purposes.  “Any attack that does not have specific military objectives violates international law. ”  In the May 15 attack on the al-Shati refugee camp, a three-storey residential building was targeted and 10 people were killed.  A resident told Human Rights Watch that residents were not given any warning about the attack.  Israel claims that the reason for the attack was the presence of several senior Hamas leaders in the residential complex.  Human Rights Watch said no witnesses or family members of the victims confirmed the presence of Hamas operatives in or around the building.  It added that the building was likely targeted by a bomb produced by Boeing that the United States exported to Israel.  A third attack on May 16 killed three destroyed buildings and 44 civilians, including 18 children and 14 women, in Gaza City.  Human Rights Watch said eyewitnesses interviewed said Israel gave no warning before the attack.  Israeli army videos and pieces of munitions collected by Palestinian police show that the attack was also carried out by a one-ton Boeing bomb.  At the time of the attack, Israel said it was targeting Hamas militants' tunnels, but Human Rights Watch said it found "no evidence of military targets".  Human Rights Watch also condemned “reckless ” missile attacks on Israeli civilians and said it would address the issue in a separate report.  “Israel and the Palestinians have violated international law in this battle, which could amount to war crimes. ”  The Israeli government has not yet responded to the report, but a Hamas spokesman said: "This report shows that the occupation government acts with complete impunity and beyond the law and is never punished because of the full support of the United States."  In March, a prosecutor at the International Criminal Court announced a new and comprehensive investigation into the situation in the occupied Palestinian territories.  The main focus of the study will be the 2014 war in the Gaza Strip, but it will also look at the deaths of Palestinian protesters since 2018.  On May 27, the UN Human Rights Council approved an international investigation into the recent fighting in the Gaza Strip.  According to the local government of the Gaza Strip, 260 Palestinians, including gunmen, have been killed in the recent clashes. Title: The Russian Jewish Congress commented on the accusations of human rights defenders against Israel
Content: The human rights organization Human Rights Watch released a report in which it claims that the Israeli authorities commit crimes of apartheid in order to preserve the dominance of Jewish Israelis over the Palestinians.  This position is shared by the Israeli NGO B ’ Tselem, which collects information on human rights violations in the disputed territories.  These include the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, and the Gaza Strip, calling them Israeli-occupied territories.  HRW ’ s report is based on years of human rights monitoring, government planning documents, official statements, and other sources.  The experts compared the policy and real actions in the disputed territories and in Israel itself against the Palestinians and the Jewish population.  According to the organization, in July last year, a letter was sent to the Israeli authorities in which they were invited to present their vision of the situation, but a response has not yet been received.  German Zakharyaev, vice president of the Russian Jewish Congress (RJC) and president of the STMEGI Mountain Jews Foundation, called the entire HRW report not a serious study, but a damning pamphlet aimed at stigmatizing Israel as an apartheid state.  “The report is based on the false image of Israel as the country controlling the entire West Bank and Gaza Strip, but in reality it is not, only a few dozen Jewish settlements and a number of highways leading to them are under Israeli control.  The rest of the population is under the control of Mahmoud Abbas's Palestinian Authority and the Hamas movement in the Gaza Strip, "he said.  According to Zakharyaev, on the territory of Israel proper, Arab citizens are absolutely equal.  At the same time, he recognized the persistence of a significant difference in the social status and material situation of the Jewish and Arab populations.  At the same time, the vice-president of the RJC recalled that the same difference exists within the Jewish population - between immigrants from Europe and the countries of the East.  What does the report say?  Allocation of land.  It follows from the report that the authorities, both in Israel itself and in the disputed territories, mainly seek to provide land for Jewish communities.  Most Palestinians are driven into densely populated areas.  The organization also claims the existence of a certain policy of neutralization: for example, the state plan for the development of Jerusalem proceeds from the need for “confident preservation of the Jewish majority ” and even provides for desirable demographic proportions.  German Zakharyaev explained to Gazeta.ru that the Arab population prefers to live in large families and so-called hamuls, build houses near their loved ones in the territories of their towns and cities.  Moreover, he said, these structures are often illegal, allowing Palestinians to bypass the long and costly process of buying and registering property.  Cut off from the local community.  According to HRW, Israel has laws that allow hundreds of small Jewish municipalities to effectively cut off Palestinians from the local community.  In addition, according to the document, only a small part of the budget is allocated to Palestinian schools compared to the financing of schools where Jewish Israeli children study.  The report points out that in the disputed territories, the intensity of repression against Palestinians reaches the level of “systematic oppression ” as one of the hallmarks of apartheid.  The document refers to a draconian military administration for Palestinians in these territories, while Jewish Israelis living separately there are provided with the full range of rights under Israel ’ s model civil code.  Israeli political scientist, former adviser to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu Benny Briskin, said in a comment to Gazeta.ru that Israel ’ s judicial system is built in such a way that every real violation of human rights that occurs either in the disputed territories of the Palestinian Authority, or in the territory of Israel itself in relation to the Arabs, is checked and the guilty is always punished.  “Of course, there are exaggerations, but the Israeli judicial system is recognized by the whole world as serious, independent, which deals with all cases, ” he said.  Freedom of movement.  The authors of the report cite as serious violations of the fundamental rights of the Palestinians and the “inhumane actions ” against their freedom of movement in the form of the closure of the Gaza Strip and the imposition of a permit regime, the confiscation of more than a third of land in the West Bank with the forced eviction of thousands of Palestinians, the denial of housing rights, and the suspension of basic civil rights for millions of Palestinians.  Many of the violations underlying these crimes, according to the authors of the report, cannot be justified in the interests of security, including the almost complete ban on the issuance of building permits to Palestinians and the demolition of thousands of houses on the pretext of lack of such a permit.  There are also cases, according to human rights activists, when demographic goals are covered by security interests, as in the situation with the de facto freezing by the Israeli authorities of the registration of residents in the disputed territories.  The organization noted that this almost completely blocks the reunification of families of Palestinians living there and deprives residents of the Gaza Strip of the opportunity to get to the West Bank.  According to the RJC vice-president, the Gaza Strip is an independent administrative unit, from where Israel completely withdrew its army and settlements in 2005, and where today Hamas, recognized in Israel as a terrorist organization, is in power.  “Any interaction with it should be confirmed at the state and legislative level.  To date, based on security needs, some kind of restrictions are imposed.  It seems to me that it is difficult to interact with the administration, which for any reason or for no reason fires missiles at civilians, ” he said.  In addition, HRW recalled the constitutional law adopted in 2018, according to which Israel was declared the “national state of the Jewish people ”.  The authors of the document are convinced that the growing body of legislation increasingly favors Jewish settlers in the West Bank and does not extend to Palestinians living there.  As explained by German Zakharyaev, this law is designed to strengthen the status of Israel as a Jewish state.  According to the seventh paragraph of this law, the state of Israel sees the development of Jewish settlements as a national value for the entire Jewish people, he noted.  In addition, the expert drew attention to the fact that this law does not say anything about Jewish settlers in the West Bank, but only about the nature of the State of Israel.  Benny Briskin called such reports not new to Israel.  According to him, in Israel there are two points of view on this: either it is ordinary anti-Semitism, or it is left-wing liberalism.  But in any case, the result is the same - the attitude towards Israel is based on double standards, he stated.  “The approach of human rights organizations is that everything that happens in the territories they call occupied is already a crime.  It does not matter how the Jewish population behaves.  In Israel, they are already accustomed to this, ” the political scientist said.  He argues that the facts do not fit into these allegations.  The facts that lead human rights organizations, Briskin called slanderous fabrications of one side.  “That is, they find a Palestinian who tells a story that he was told to tell by the Palestinian secret services.  This is not verified in any way and is exposed as an unquestionable fact, ” he said.  “The claims of apartheid seem particularly absurd today, when Mansour Abbas — leader of the Joint Arab List in the Knesset — holds Israel ’ s political future in the wake of the March elections.  His voice is key in determining who will form the next governing coalition in Israel: Benjamin Netanyahu and his far-right supporters or the camp of his opponents.  Both sides are courting Abbas, which is hardly a sign of apartheid, ” said German Zakharyaev, president of the STMEGI Mountain Jews Foundation.

Title: Human Rights Watch: Israel and Hamas May Have Committed War Crimes
Content: Human Rights Watch said on Tuesday that both Israel and Hamas may have committed war crimes during the May clashes.  During the 11-day battle, Hamas and other Palestinian groups fired thousands of rockets into Israeli territory and the Israeli army bombed the Gaza Strip from the ground and air.  Human Rights Watch said it used interviews with local residents and eyewitnesses, data analysis and digital images to produce its report.  According to the human rights organization, 62 Palestinian civilians were killed in three Israeli attacks in areas where no evidence of armed personnel has been found.  The report specifically examines Israeli air strikes on May 10 on the small town of Beit Hanoun in the northeast Gaza Strip, May 15 on the al-Shati refugee camp and May 16 on the city of Gaza.  Human Rights Watch added that “other Israeli attacks during this battle were also likely in violation of international law. ”  Eight people, including six children, were killed in an attack on May 10 that destroyed several homes.  At this point, Human Rights Watch says there is no indication of the presence of the armed forces or its use for military purposes.  “Any attack that does not have specific military objectives violates international law. ”  In the May 15 attack on the al-Shati refugee camp, a three-storey residential building was targeted and 10 people were killed.  A resident told Human Rights Watch that residents were not given any warning about the attack.  Israel claims that the reason for the attack was the presence of several senior Hamas leaders in the residential complex.  Human Rights Watch said no witnesses or family members of the victims confirmed the presence of Hamas operatives in or around the building.  It added that the building was likely targeted by a bomb produced by Boeing that the United States exported to Israel.  A third attack on May 16 killed three destroyed buildings and 44 civilians, including 18 children and 14 women, in Gaza City.  Human Rights Watch said eyewitnesses interviewed said Israel gave no warning before the attack.  Israeli army videos and pieces of munitions collected by Palestinian police show that the attack was also carried out by a one-ton Boeing bomb.  At the time of the attack, Israel said it was targeting Hamas militants' tunnels, but Human Rights Watch said it found "no evidence of military targets".  Human Rights Watch also condemned “reckless ” missile attacks on Israeli civilians and said it would address the issue in a separate report.  “Israel and the Palestinians have violated international law in this battle, which could amount to war crimes. ”  The Israeli government has not yet responded to the report, but a Hamas spokesman said: "This report shows that the occupation government acts with complete impunity and beyond the law and is never punished because of the full support of the United States." Benny Briskin called such reports not new to Israel.  According to him, in Israel there are two points of view on this: either it is ordinary anti-Semitism, or it is left-wing liberalism.  But in any case, the result is the same - the attitude towards Israel is based on double standards, he stated.  “The approach of human rights organizations is that everything that happens in the territories they call occupied is already a crime.  It does not matter how the Jewish population behaves.  In Israel, they are already accustomed to this, ” the political scientist said.  He argues that the facts do not fit into these allegations.  The facts that lead human rights organizations, Briskin called slanderous fabrications of one side.  “That is, they find a Palestinian who tells a story that he was told to tell by the Palestinian secret services.  This is not verified in any way and is exposed as an unquestionable fact, ” he said.  “The claims of apartheid seem particularly absurd today, when Mansour Abbas — leader of the Joint Arab List in the Knesset — holds Israel ’ s political future in the wake of the March elections.  His voice is key in determining who will form the next governing coalition in Israel: Benjamin Netanyahu and his far-right supporters or the camp of his opponents.  Both sides are courting Abbas, which is hardly a sign of apartheid, ” said German Zakharyaev, president of the STMEGI Mountain Jews Foundation.

passages.title: The opportunity that Corona gave to health tourism
passages.passage: According to IRNA, with the outbreak of the coronavirus and increasing concerns about health and treatment services, the desire to migrate to the destination countries providing these services has increased.  With the outbreak of COVID-19, shortages in hospital equipment, health and medical items increased.  Many countries faced serious challenges in providing health care, which made it difficult for citizens and migrants to live longer.  This increased the desire to travel to countries that had better facilities and services in the field of health and treatment.  The closure of the borders of some of these countries and the impossibility of travel in the first months, although with despair and survival, gradually and with limited acceptance of migrants, opened the ground for migration aimed at improving health and treatment.  It ’ s important to remember the concept of health care once again.  The upward and downward trend of health tourism, according to the announcement on Monday by the Vice-Presidency for Science and Technology, global statistics show that health tourism had a significant growth before the coronavirus outbreak, but with the beginning of the epidemic and the closure of the borders of countries to migrants, this trend has faced a significant decline.  But statistics from host countries and news of the reopening of borders show that the trend is improving.  The last decade of medical tourism boomed, with the global market generating $58.6 billion annually in 2018, and in 2019 it was expected to grow by 11% annually and reach revenues of more than $142 billion by 2026.  The growth of this sector began mainly with increasing awareness, especially among the citizens of higher income countries, of health facilities and services, and of the affordable and economic prices of developing countries.  Providing a combination of medical and tourism services has led to the development and increase of requests for the use of health tourism services.  The gradual improvement of the damage caused by the coronavirus outbreak, a researcher in the field of migration, says: Many Asian countries, as well as the Middle East, including Iran, have health facilities and capabilities that should be considered again during the coronavirus era.  Mohammad Ho said that the lower cost of treatment has attracted the attention of citizens of other countries to benefit from health services and health care, along with their vacation and leisure time, and even the offer of medical tourism visas by some countries began with the aim of attracting more foreign patients.  Some countries provided additional services and incentives for the development of health tourism, for example, in addition to discounts on transportation services, provided free accommodation and tourist attractions for migrants.  The researcher said that the quarantine and ban of international travel last year troubled the tourism industry, adding that medical tourism was one of the sectors that had the most impact from this area.  It will take some time to return to pre-epidemic income levels, but countries around the world are taking steps to restart the industry in their own countries.  According to him, countries can have a progressive vaccination program that, while providing safety for citizens, opens doors to health migrants, while generating revenue and reviving the industry, a special place not only in medical technologies but also in the field of tourism for themselves.  Coronavirus and the development of health tourism in some countries, while requiring patients to be tested for the coronavirus, have turned health services, including vaccinations, into an opportunity to attract tourists.  In parallel, compliance certifications and international standards in Covid19 medical care have been developed globally, and these approvals, which state that hospitals and clinics meet the required standards, help bring in tourists.  Iran ’ s health tourism and latent capacity to attract global medical tourism migrants in 2020 was considered due to the coronavirus outbreak.  However, as recent positive performance has become a model for success in some countries, implementing a combination of solutions can help attract medical tourists.  According to this immigration researcher, Iran can develop its latent capacity in health tourism through proper modeling of these methods and with the help of the capabilities that it has experienced in recent years through the production of advanced medical equipment, health items and the implementation of therapeutic mechanisms.  He said: With the development of technologies, especially in the field of digital, information and communication technology, new methods in medicine and tourism will help a part of the tourists who are not yet able to travel.  Along with such measures, telemedicine is also experiencing significant growth: many hospitals are expanding the provision of online pre-travel diagnosis services and post-travel counseling.  While such solutions are not as effective as in-person tourism, they have opened new doors for the development of health tourism.  The researcher emphasized that the development of vaccine technology, coupled with the health facilities and infrastructure of countries with the coronavirus and the possibility of vaccination of non-native people, has increased the field for migration with health goals.  An opportunity that Iran, with its favorable capacities in the field of health care services, including its ability to produce vaccines, can put in the new path of creating added value.

passages.title: The Necessity of Revision in the Approach of Health Tourism Policy in Iran
passages.passage: A report by the Majlis Research Center evaluated the need to review the policy approach of health tourism in Iran.  According to the Islamic Consultative Assembly Research Center, the Office of Education and Culture Studies of the Center in a report titled “The need to rethink the health tourism policy approach in Iran ” has said: According to the World Health Institute ’ s 2018 report, the global health tourism market ’ s revenue in 2017 was valued at $639 billion and is expected to reach $1,062 billion by 2025.  While according to global statistics, the share of the global medical tourism market of the health tourism market in 2017 was worth $53 billion and is expected to reach $143 billion by 2025.  Thus, the volume of health tourism turnover was more than 12 times that of medical tourism.  The report of the Majlis Research Center adds that until now, the main focus of health tourism policy in the country has been on medical tourism and health tourism, which has a far higher share of health tourism, has not been paid much attention, while the country's capacities in this area (such as hot springs, salty lakes, diverse mountain nature, forest, coastal, desert, etc.)  It is far above medical tourism.  According to the report, the remarkable point in the health tourism governance is that up to now, the strategies and policies set in this area have been systematic and systemic without regard to macro approaches.  The number of medical tourists has increased more than 30 times in the last 10 years, but this growth has not occurred in health tourism.  The report of the Majlis Research Center states that Iran has been subject to cruel sanctions in recent years, and because of the 70 percent import of medical equipment (Majlis Research Center, 2018), severe shocks have been inflicted on the health system, and because of this, the government has been forced to inject various supports and subsidies for the necessary imports, and on the other hand, due to lack of proper management of resources and equipment, beds, hospitals, medical equipment, medical staff, I'm...  It is not in line with domestic needs and the country needs to be strengthened in this regard.  Also, health tourism is rooted in the country ’ s domestic capacities and its dependence on imports is very low, because Iran, due to its high potential and climatic diversity and natural and climatic attractions, has a great competitive advantage to attract health tourists, especially from the 600 million population of neighboring countries.  Therefore, health tourism is not involved in the tensions that exist in the field of medical tourism, and with its competitive advantages, it can bring currency into the country beyond medical tourism.  Therefore, while considering the development of medical tourism, one should pay more attention to health tourism and create its value chains domestically.  The report of the Majlis Research Center adds, of course, in the field of health tourism, it should also be given serious attention that due to the cultural and indigenous demands of Islamic Iran, indigenous and creative patterns should be designed and implemented in this area, and non-scientific adaptations of the patterns of other countries and without observing the native cultural aspects should be avoided.  In the report of the parliamentary research center, it is suggested that the approaches and policies of the country in the field of health tourism be seriously reviewed and medical and health tourism based on internal needs and domestic competitive advantages be redesigned to promote health tourism based on local patterns.  In this regard, the system of health tourists, especially in the field of medical tourism, should be set up, in order to meet the necessary condition of having a standard tourism in the field of health, which is monitoring and clarifying how to service tourists from entry to exit.  Read the full report here.  End of message.

passages.title: The average check of a foreign patient in Ukrainian clinics in 2019 increased to $2800
passages.passage: The average check of a foreign patient in Ukrainian clinics in 2019 increased from $2000-2500 to almost $2800, said Vice President of the Ukrainian Association of Medical Tourism (UAMT) Igor Torsky.  “According to our annual research, there is an increase in this indicator.  In 2019, the average check of one foreign medical tourist was about $2,800.  It is possible that in 2020 this figure will be even higher, ” he said at a press conference dedicated to the Global Healthcare Travel Forum 2020, which will be held in Kyiv and Lviv region on April 22-25, 2020.  At the same time, Torsky noted that the increase in the average check of foreign patients was facilitated, in particular, by the development of high-tech medical technologies and innovative methods of treatment.  At the same time, according to him, the increase in the average check was also influenced by the pricing policy of clinics. "This is a price increase.  We do not always agree and discuss with clinics about the feasibility of such an increase.  I want to advise representatives of clinics to be careful with pricing policy, as we are in a highly competitive world of medical tourism, ” he said.  At the same time, Torsky said that the average check of foreign patients in Ukrainian clinics differs by region.  “In Kiev, the average check is about $3,240, in Lviv this amount is lower, because the structure of services differs from region to region, ” he said.  According to him, reproductive medicine and cellular technologies are the most developed in the country ’ s clinics.  “These industries are high-tech, they require fairly accurate laboratory equipment and highly qualified specialists.  Ukraine in these two areas is one of the world leaders, ” he said.  At the same time, Torsky said, in other areas of medical tourism, in particular, in dentistry, rehabilitation, oncology, the flow of medical tourists is based on "a very balanced pricing policy of clinics", as well as on the absence of the so-called "waiting list" for getting to a consultation with narrow specialists.  “To get an appointment with a specialist insured person at home, you need to wait long enough.  This is one of the reasons why patients choose Ukraine, ” said the Vice President of UAMT.  In turn, the President of UAMT and the President of the Global Healthcare Travel Council Violetta Yanyshevskaya added that foreign patients can receive high-tech treatment in Ukrainian clinics using the technologies of cyberknife, gammanozha, da Vinci robot.  “In Ukraine, there are already expensive procedures for which previously patients must travel abroad.  Now these technologies and this high-tech equipment are present and clinics can provide such services, including to foreign patients, "she said.  At the same time, Yanyshevskaya expressed the opinion that for the development of medical tourism, Ukraine should resolve a number of problems, in particular, related to visa issues for foreign patients, as well as introduce the concept of “medical tourism ” into the legislative field.  “Working groups are working so that the parliament of this convocation can develop and adopt a law on medical tourism, ” she said.  According to GHTC estimates, the global market for health-related tourism segments is estimated at $439 billion.  According to international experts, in the next 10 years it is expected to grow steadily by 10-20%.  Every year, 3-4% of the world ’ s population will go abroad for treatment and rehabilitation.  As reported with reference to UAMT, in 2018, the average check of a foreign patient who is being treated in Ukrainian clinics was $2-2.5 thousand, excluding transportation and accommodation costs.  About 120 clinics in different regions of the country took foreign patients.  In the same year, about 65 thousand foreigners came to Ukrainian clinics to be treated, about 160 thousand people left the country for treatment.  Leaders of outbound medical tourism from Ukraine are Germany and Israel and Turkey.  According to UAMT, currently in the segment of incoming medical tourism in Ukraine are mainly private clinics.

passages.title: Dental tourism, looking for a beautiful smile
passages.passage: ISNA / Khorasan Razavi Dental tourism is one of the most important forms of medical tourism and as an emerging industry, it is growing at a high rate.  The criteria for choosing a dentist for medical tourists depend on factors such as cost, location and quality of service.  The researchers noted that today ’ s unhealthy lifestyles, diets and longevity are gradually increasing the demand for quality and professional dental care.  The boom in the worldwide dental tourism market is primarily due to the increase in cases of dental malformation and the second is the increase in the desire for cosmetic dentistry.  The lower cost of treatment and better services in dental treatment in foreign country and the long waiting period for dental treatment in tourist country may boost the growth of this market in the future.  The global dental tourism market can be categorized in the type of treatment and area, and in terms of the type of treatment can be divided into preventive, restorative, prosthetic and other treatments.  Worldwide demand for cosmetic dentistry and therapeutic and restorative dentures has captured a large share of the market.  The pros of dental implant tourism, like medical tourism, are low medical costs, but there are many risks along the way.  Experts predict that the global dental implant market will reach $9 billion by 2027, making dental implants popular for a number of reasons, such as durability and usually success, which can last 20 years or more.  However, they are the best tooth replacement options and, of course, the most expensive, which in turn has led to an increase in dental tourism.  Also, market experts predict that the dental tourism industry will grow to a $5.83 billion sector by 2025, with the most important factors being the cost of treatment in countries and the lack of insurance coverage for many dental treatments.  In dental tourism, people travel abroad to receive dental care.  For example, a U.S. citizen may travel to Mexico to undergo dental implant surgery or an Australian may travel to Thailand to do oral matters.  With the above in mind, most dental tourists are from countries where the cost of treatment is very high, and the destinations in turn are countries known for their cheap services.  The results showed that the success of dental implants depends on the individual ’ s gums, which should be free of disease and infection, and patients who want to have implants but have gum disease should treat the gums first.  Dental tourism makes it difficult to achieve this goal, as it means multiple trips, and sometimes it is very unpleasant.  When the dental tourist encounters the entry of bacteria into the implant at the time of the gum surgery and the infection does not immediately show symptoms and the person returns to the origin, he will face infection after a few days.  Although infections caused by implants are treatable, they are difficult to treat and can be costly, and sometimes a lack of health standards and regulations can lead to these problems.  The researchers noted that regular dental checkups and oral hygiene will be the most important factor for reducing medical tourism trips.  Dentists, in some cases, make medical tourism more charitable, not to reduce costs, but to provide services to low-income people.  Doctors travel to poor countries to put their skills at the mercy of other people and provide the key to good oral health.  Dental tourism in the corona crisis Many patients travel to areas outside their country in search of a perfect smile to fix their oral problems.  According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), travel is likely to increase the incidence of COVID-19, and the farther the trip, the greater the risk.  It should be noted, however, that before COVID-19, travelers were also at risk of developing other diseases.  The financial impact on dental tourism has been dramatic, as this type of tourism will be difficult when patients are unwilling to perform services or unable to travel to the country due to quarantine or travel ban.
