passages.title: The main directions of beauty tourism: plastic, weight loss, sleep
passages.passage: Hair transplants in Turkey, sleep recovery in Switzerland, liposuction in Brazil: health tourism is booming and expanding horizons.  "Kommersant Style" tells about popular destinations and beauty programs from around the world.  Medical tourism is not a new phenomenon: there have always been those who want to improve their health abroad.  Many countries have their own medical specialization - they are able to do something better than others.  For example, the United States, Brazil, Japan, Mexico and Italy account for 41.4% of all global plastic surgeries.  Patients Beyond Borders estimates that 14 million people travel abroad every year to seek health care.  The obvious reason for the popularity of such tourism for many is the difference in prices.  For example, rhinoplasty in the United States will cost an average of $4.8 thousand, and in Thailand - $1.6 thousand, in a Moscow clinic - about 200 thousand rubles, depending on the complexity.  According to the WHO, Brazil has the best healthcare system in Latin America thanks to the mass accreditation of hospitals by the Joint International Commission (JCI – the largest and oldest medical accreditation organization in the world).  This led to the phenomenon of such tourism in the country.  Surgeons here are like hairdressers.  The most popular procedures in Brazil are liposuction, abdominoplasty and buttock augmentation, called brazilian butt lift.  Of course, the cult of the body is due to the hot climate.  Interestingly, every year the government subsidizes almost half a million operations, for the locals it is the “right to beauty ”.  The same operations are being carried out in neighboring Colombia.  Almost all patients are from the United States.  About 50,000 medical tourists visit the country every year.  From 2012 to 2018, medical tourism in Colombia grew by 264%.  There are more surgeons in South Korea.  It has one of the highest rates of plastic surgery in the world - about 1 million procedures per year, as well as the largest number of plastic surgeons per capita.  The country boasts a thriving tourism industry in this area.  In Korea, they strive to make facial features more Europeanized, so first of all, they change the shape of the nose, eyes (double eyelid surgery), jaws and cheekbones.  The management of Incheon Airport in Seoul even considered the possibility of creating a plastic surgery clinic in one of the terminals so that travelers did not need to travel around the city.  Photo: Getty Images Turkey, although not one of the most popular places for plastic surgery, but the leader in the market of hair transplantation.  Often on the streets of Istanbul and other major cities of the country you can meet people with bandaged heads.  For comparison, hair transplantation costs about $25 thousand in the United States and Europe, in Turkey - from $600 to $2 thousand, in a Moscow clinic - about 100 thousand rubles. for one graft (a group of one to four follicles).  According to the Hurriyet newspaper, in 2017, among 750 thousand tourists, 60 thousand came for hair transplantation.  Most are from the Middle East.  Popular destinations for dental tourism are Thailand, which is called the "Land of Smiles", Vietnam, Mexico and Costa Rica, in Europe - Hungary and Poland.  The most common procedures are the installation of implants, veneers and crowns, bleaching.  For example, Hungary has become the best place in Europe for this direction, it is visited annually by about 7 thousand patients.  This is due to favorable prices, qualified doctors and modern technologies.  Another two popular areas of tourism are the restoration of sleep and weight loss, but not just on detox programs, but thanks to sports in the camps.  Fitness camps are actually recreational sports camps for adults, where in the circle of like-minded people you can surf in Sri Lanka with the Good Story Surf school, go skating on Lake Baikal with Team Trip or learn how to ski in the vicinity of Gstaad with Pro Trener, World Class or SlimFitClub trainers.  Six Senses Douro Valley The newest wellness trend is slip-retreats, which literally teach you to sleep.  As a rule, resorts for the restoration of sleep are located in picturesque places: in the mountains, overlooking the water.  For example, in Portugal, Germany, Italy and Switzerland.  Services include a menu of pillows: from special anti-snoring to filled with water or memory foam, sleep masks and earplugs to choose from, a music library, meditation on demand, as well as staff who can advise on sleep issues.  For example, the hotel in Manhattan, The Benjamin, designed the Rest & Renew program with Rebecca Robbins, a professor of sleep medicine at Cornell University.  Similar programs have Six Senses Douro Valley in Portugal, Peak Health in Switzerland and Lefay on Lake Garda.  Berlin ’ s Swisstel included in its DeepSleep retreat sessions of aroma- and light therapy, as well as inhalation of mountain air.  Beauty tourism is a thriving niche in the industry.  Clinics and hotels offer complete packages, including transfers, flights, meals and even excursions.  According to a joint study by Visa and Oxford Economics, the global medical tourism industry will grow by 25% per year over the next ten years.  Daria Bogomolova

passages.title: 35% of global tourism revenue is Iran ’ s share
passages.passage: The advanced and widespread health services in Iran compared to neighboring countries and the relative superiority of these services in terms of price compared to many advanced countries has made the market of health and medical services in Iran attractive to citizens of other countries and a new branch of tourism called health tourism has emerged in the country.  The presence of many of these health tourists can not be limited to health services; these people can also travel to tourist or pilgrimage areas of Iran during and after treatment, which can also help the tourism development of those areas.  According to the Public Relations Department of the Institute of Cultural Heritage and Tourism, Saeed Amirian, discussed this issue at the specialized meeting of “Risk Management in Health Tourism ” held by the Institute of Tourism.  He described medical tourism as an economic activity that requires trade in services and participation of at least two medical and tourism sectors, adding that medical tourism in most cases includes dental services, cosmetic surgery and other types of surgeries.  Amirian, in the definition of health tourism, said: The use of services that improve or increase health and increase the morale of the person and in a place outside his residence for more than 24 hours is considered to be a health tourism.  Referring to the flow of patients from developed countries to developing countries to receive medical services, he said: “The intensifying factor in the flow of medical tourism in recent years is the third payer, employer or insurance, which encourages patients to find medical services at more affordable and faster prices. ”  In describing the dimensions of medical tourism in Iran, he said: Iran ’ s share of attracting this type of tourism during one year was only 350 million dollars; that is, only 0.35% of global health tourism revenue is Iran ’ s share, and with this amount of income, Iran ranks 10th in terms of attracting health tourists.  Referring to the importance of health tourism in Iran, Amirian stated: "The advanced and widespread health services in Iran compared to neighboring countries and the relative superiority of these services in terms of price compared to many advanced countries has made the market of health and health services of Iran attractive to citizens of other countries and a new branch of tourism called health tourism in the country emerges."  He went on to say something about the risk of tourism, saying: "It is mainly a defect in our knowledge of the future and risk is more in the future; risk and uncertainty start exactly where knowledge ends."  The expert added: "By stating that the risk of uncertainties with probabilities and possible outcomes is known, the risk classification is small and large scale, systematic and unsystematic.  Referring to the theoretical reflections of risk and uncertainty in tourism, Amirian said: "Risk is more as something to be avoided, but risk and uncertainty are considered as tourist attractions, especially adventure tourism."  He went on to describe the risks in tourism including individual risks for tourists, the responsibility of tourism service providers, destination risks and social risks, and by giving examples of risks in individual tourism, he explained the ways to cover risks for individual tourists, destination risks, social and tourism risks and governments and risk management.  Referring to the risk in tourism companies and its types, he said the four main strategies for risk management at the company level are knowledge, diversity, trust, and insurance, and said the risk management principle includes four steps; identification of small and large threats that the company may face in the future, analyzing risks and assessing the amount of costs that each risk may bring to the company, formulating a strategy for each possible risk and designing practical measures to deal with it and monitor damage. It is a risk to the company and a modification of past strategies and approaches.

Title: The opportunity that Corona gave to health tourism
Content: According to IRNA, with the outbreak of the coronavirus and increasing concerns about health and treatment services, the desire to migrate to the destination countries providing these services has increased.  With the outbreak of COVID-19, shortages in hospital equipment, health and medical items increased.  Many countries faced serious challenges in providing health care, which made it difficult for citizens and migrants to live longer.  This increased the desire to travel to countries that had better facilities and services in the field of health and treatment.  The closure of the borders of some of these countries and the impossibility of travel in the first months, although with despair and survival, gradually and with limited acceptance of migrants, opened the ground for migration aimed at improving health and treatment.  It ’ s important to remember the concept of health care once again.  The upward and downward trend of health tourism, according to the announcement on Monday by the Vice-Presidency for Science and Technology, global statistics show that health tourism had a significant growth before the coronavirus outbreak, but with the beginning of the epidemic and the closure of the borders of countries to migrants, this trend has faced a significant decline.  But statistics from host countries and news of the reopening of borders show that the trend is improving.  The last decade of medical tourism boomed, with the global market generating $58.6 billion annually in 2018, and in 2019 it was expected to grow by 11% annually and reach revenues of more than $142 billion by 2026.  The growth of this sector began mainly with increasing awareness, especially among the citizens of higher income countries, of health facilities and services, and of the affordable and economic prices of developing countries.  Providing a combination of medical and tourism services has led to the development and increase of requests for the use of health tourism services.  The gradual improvement of the damage caused by the coronavirus outbreak, a researcher in the field of migration, says: Many Asian countries, as well as the Middle East, including Iran, have health facilities and capabilities that should be considered again during the coronavirus era.  Mohammad Ho said that the lower cost of treatment has attracted the attention of citizens of other countries to benefit from health services and health care, along with their vacation and leisure time, and even the offer of medical tourism visas by some countries began with the aim of attracting more foreign patients.  Some countries provided additional services and incentives for the development of health tourism, for example, in addition to discounts on transportation services, provided free accommodation and tourist attractions for migrants.  The researcher said that the quarantine and ban of international travel last year troubled the tourism industry, adding that medical tourism was one of the sectors that had the most impact from this area.  It will take some time to return to pre-epidemic income levels, but countries around the world are taking steps to restart the industry in their own countries.  According to him, countries can have a progressive vaccination program that, while providing safety for citizens, opens doors to health migrants, while generating revenue and reviving the industry, a special place not only in medical technologies but also in the field of tourism for themselves.  Coronavirus and the development of health tourism in some countries, while requiring patients to be tested for the coronavirus, have turned health services, including vaccinations, into an opportunity to attract tourists.  In parallel, compliance certifications and international standards in Covid19 medical care have been developed globally, and these approvals, which state that hospitals and clinics meet the required standards, help bring in tourists.  Iran ’ s health tourism and latent capacity to attract global medical tourism migrants in 2020 was considered due to the coronavirus outbreak.  However, as recent positive performance has become a model for success in some countries, implementing a combination of solutions can help attract medical tourists.  According to this immigration researcher, Iran can develop its latent capacity in health tourism through proper modeling of these methods and with the help of the capabilities that it has experienced in recent years through the production of advanced medical equipment, health items and the implementation of therapeutic mechanisms.  He said: With the development of technologies, especially in the field of digital, information and communication technology, new methods in medicine and tourism will help a part of the tourists who are not yet able to travel.  Along with such measures, telemedicine is also experiencing significant growth: many hospitals are expanding the provision of online pre-travel diagnosis services and post-travel counseling.  While such solutions are not as effective as in-person tourism, they have opened new doors for the development of health tourism.  The researcher emphasized that the development of vaccine technology, coupled with the health facilities and infrastructure of countries with the coronavirus and the possibility of vaccination of non-native people, has increased the field for migration with health goals.  An opportunity that Iran, with its favorable capacities in the field of health care services, including its ability to produce vaccines, can put in the new path of creating added value.

Title: The Necessity of Revision in the Approach of Health Tourism Policy in Iran
Content: A report by the Majlis Research Center evaluated the need to review the policy approach of health tourism in Iran.  According to the Islamic Consultative Assembly Research Center, the Office of Education and Culture Studies of the Center in a report titled “The need to rethink the health tourism policy approach in Iran ” has said: According to the World Health Institute ’ s 2018 report, the global health tourism market ’ s revenue in 2017 was valued at $639 billion and is expected to reach $1,062 billion by 2025.  While according to global statistics, the share of the global medical tourism market of the health tourism market in 2017 was worth $53 billion and is expected to reach $143 billion by 2025.  Thus, the volume of health tourism turnover was more than 12 times that of medical tourism.  The report of the Majlis Research Center adds that until now, the main focus of health tourism policy in the country has been on medical tourism and health tourism, which has a far higher share of health tourism, has not been paid much attention, while the country's capacities in this area (such as hot springs, salty lakes, diverse mountain nature, forest, coastal, desert, etc.)  It is far above medical tourism.  According to the report, the remarkable point in the health tourism governance is that up to now, the strategies and policies set in this area have been systematic and systemic without regard to macro approaches.  The number of medical tourists has increased more than 30 times in the last 10 years, but this growth has not occurred in health tourism.  The report of the Majlis Research Center states that Iran has been subject to cruel sanctions in recent years, and because of the 70 percent import of medical equipment (Majlis Research Center, 2018), severe shocks have been inflicted on the health system, and because of this, the government has been forced to inject various supports and subsidies for the necessary imports, and on the other hand, due to lack of proper management of resources and equipment, beds, hospitals, medical equipment, medical staff, I'm...  It is not in line with domestic needs and the country needs to be strengthened in this regard.  Also, health tourism is rooted in the country ’ s domestic capacities and its dependence on imports is very low, because Iran, due to its high potential and climatic diversity and natural and climatic attractions, has a great competitive advantage to attract health tourists, especially from the 600 million population of neighboring countries.  Therefore, health tourism is not involved in the tensions that exist in the field of medical tourism, and with its competitive advantages, it can bring currency into the country beyond medical tourism.  Therefore, while considering the development of medical tourism, one should pay more attention to health tourism and create its value chains domestically.  The report of the Majlis Research Center adds, of course, in the field of health tourism, it should also be given serious attention that due to the cultural and indigenous demands of Islamic Iran, indigenous and creative patterns should be designed and implemented in this area, and non-scientific adaptations of the patterns of other countries and without observing the native cultural aspects should be avoided.  In the report of the parliamentary research center, it is suggested that the approaches and policies of the country in the field of health tourism be seriously reviewed and medical and health tourism based on internal needs and domestic competitive advantages be redesigned to promote health tourism based on local patterns.  In this regard, the system of health tourists, especially in the field of medical tourism, should be set up, in order to meet the necessary condition of having a standard tourism in the field of health, which is monitoring and clarifying how to service tourists from entry to exit. Title: The average check of a foreign patient in Ukrainian clinics in 2019 increased to $2800
Content: The average check of a foreign patient in Ukrainian clinics in 2019 increased from $2000-2500 to almost $2800, said Vice President of the Ukrainian Association of Medical Tourism (UAMT) Igor Torsky.  “According to our annual research, there is an increase in this indicator.  In 2019, the average check of one foreign medical tourist was about $2,800.  It is possible that in 2020 this figure will be even higher, ” he said at a press conference dedicated to the Global Healthcare Travel Forum 2020, which will be held in Kyiv and Lviv region on April 22-25, 2020.  At the same time, Torsky noted that the increase in the average check of foreign patients was facilitated, in particular, by the development of high-tech medical technologies and innovative methods of treatment.  At the same time, according to him, the increase in the average check was also influenced by the pricing policy of clinics. "This is a price increase.  We do not always agree and discuss with clinics about the feasibility of such an increase.  I want to advise representatives of clinics to be careful with pricing policy, as we are in a highly competitive world of medical tourism, ” he said.  At the same time, Torsky said that the average check of foreign patients in Ukrainian clinics differs by region.  “In Kiev, the average check is about $3,240, in Lviv this amount is lower, because the structure of services differs from region to region, ” he said.  According to him, reproductive medicine and cellular technologies are the most developed in the country ’ s clinics.  “These industries are high-tech, they require fairly accurate laboratory equipment and highly qualified specialists.  Ukraine in these two areas is one of the world leaders, ” he said.  At the same time, Torsky said, in other areas of medical tourism, in particular, in dentistry, rehabilitation, oncology, the flow of medical tourists is based on "a very balanced pricing policy of clinics", as well as on the absence of the so-called "waiting list" for getting to a consultation with narrow specialists.  “To get an appointment with a specialist insured person at home, you need to wait long enough.  This is one of the reasons why patients choose Ukraine, ” said the Vice President of UAMT.  In turn, the President of UAMT and the President of the Global Healthcare Travel Council Violetta Yanyshevskaya added that foreign patients can receive high-tech treatment in Ukrainian clinics using the technologies of cyberknife, gammanozha, da Vinci robot.  “In Ukraine, there are already expensive procedures for which previously patients must travel abroad.  Now these technologies and this high-tech equipment are present and clinics can provide such services, including to foreign patients, "she said.  At the same time, Yanyshevskaya expressed the opinion that for the development of medical tourism, Ukraine should resolve a number of problems, in particular, related to visa issues for foreign patients, as well as introduce the concept of “medical tourism ” into the legislative field.  “Working groups are working so that the parliament of this convocation can develop and adopt a law on medical tourism, ” she said.  According to GHTC estimates, the global market for health-related tourism segments is estimated at $439 billion.  According to international experts, in the next 10 years it is expected to grow steadily by 10-20%.  Every year, 3-4% of the world ’ s population will go abroad for treatment and rehabilitation.  As reported with reference to UAMT, in 2018, the average check of a foreign patient who is being treated in Ukrainian clinics was $2-2.5 thousand, excluding transportation and accommodation costs.  About 120 clinics in different regions of the country took foreign patients.  In the same year, about 65 thousand foreigners came to Ukrainian clinics to be treated, about 160 thousand people left the country for treatment.  Leaders of outbound medical tourism from Ukraine are Germany and Israel and Turkey.  According to UAMT, currently in the segment of incoming medical tourism in Ukraine are mainly private clinics.

Title: Dental tourism, looking for a beautiful smile
Content: ISNA / Khorasan Razavi Dental tourism is one of the most important forms of medical tourism and as an emerging industry, it is growing at a high rate.  The criteria for choosing a dentist for medical tourists depend on factors such as cost, location and quality of service.  The researchers noted that today ’ s unhealthy lifestyles, diets and longevity are gradually increasing the demand for quality and professional dental care.  The boom in the worldwide dental tourism market is primarily due to the increase in cases of dental malformation and the second is the increase in the desire for cosmetic dentistry.  The lower cost of treatment and better services in dental treatment in foreign country and the long waiting period for dental treatment in tourist country may boost the growth of this market in the future.  The global dental tourism market can be categorized in the type of treatment and area, and in terms of the type of treatment can be divided into preventive, restorative, prosthetic and other treatments.  Worldwide demand for cosmetic dentistry and therapeutic and restorative dentures has captured a large share of the market.  The pros of dental implant tourism, like medical tourism, are low medical costs, but there are many risks along the way.  Experts predict that the global dental implant market will reach $9 billion by 2027, making dental implants popular for a number of reasons, such as durability and usually success, which can last 20 years or more.  However, they are the best tooth replacement options and, of course, the most expensive, which in turn has led to an increase in dental tourism.  Also, market experts predict that the dental tourism industry will grow to a $5.83 billion sector by 2025, with the most important factors being the cost of treatment in countries and the lack of insurance coverage for many dental treatments.  In dental tourism, people travel abroad to receive dental care.  For example, a U.S. citizen may travel to Mexico to undergo dental implant surgery or an Australian may travel to Thailand to do oral matters.  With the above in mind, most dental tourists are from countries where the cost of treatment is very high, and the destinations in turn are countries known for their cheap services.  The results showed that the success of dental implants depends on the individual ’ s gums, which should be free of disease and infection, and patients who want to have implants but have gum disease should treat the gums first.  Dental tourism makes it difficult to achieve this goal, as it means multiple trips, and sometimes it is very unpleasant.  When the dental tourist encounters the entry of bacteria into the implant at the time of the gum surgery and the infection does not immediately show symptoms and the person returns to the origin, he will face infection after a few days.  Although infections caused by implants are treatable, they are difficult to treat and can be costly, and sometimes a lack of health standards and regulations can lead to these problems.  The researchers noted that regular dental checkups and oral hygiene will be the most important factor for reducing medical tourism trips.  Dentists, in some cases, make medical tourism more charitable, not to reduce costs, but to provide services to low-income people.  Doctors travel to poor countries to put their skills at the mercy of other people and provide the key to good oral health.  Dental tourism in the corona crisis Many patients travel to areas outside their country in search of a perfect smile to fix their oral problems.  According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), travel is likely to increase the incidence of COVID-19, and the farther the trip, the greater the risk.  It should be noted, however, that before COVID-19, travelers were also at risk of developing other diseases.  The financial impact on dental tourism has been dramatic, as this type of tourism will be difficult when patients are unwilling to perform services or unable to travel to the country due to quarantine or travel ban. Title: The main directions of beauty tourism: plastic, weight loss, sleep
Content: Hair transplants in Turkey, sleep recovery in Switzerland, liposuction in Brazil: health tourism is booming and expanding horizons.  "Kommersant Style" tells about popular destinations and beauty programs from around the world.  Medical tourism is not a new phenomenon: there have always been those who want to improve their health abroad.  Many countries have their own medical specialization - they are able to do something better than others. Title: The opportunity that Corona gave to health tourism
Content: According to IRNA, with the outbreak of the coronavirus and increasing concerns about health and treatment services, the desire to migrate to the destination countries providing these services has increased.  With the outbreak of COVID-19, shortages in hospital equipment, health and medical items increased.  Many countries faced serious challenges in providing health care, which made it difficult for citizens and migrants to live longer.  This increased the desire to travel to countries that had better facilities and services in the field of health and treatment.  The closure of the borders of some of these countries and the impossibility of travel in the first months, although with despair and survival, gradually and with limited acceptance of migrants, opened the ground for migration aimed at improving health and treatment.  It ’ s important to remember the concept of health care once again.  The upward and downward trend of health tourism, according to the announcement on Monday by the Vice-Presidency for Science and Technology, global statistics show that health tourism had a significant growth before the coronavirus outbreak, but with the beginning of the epidemic and the closure of the borders of countries to migrants, this trend has faced a significant decline.  But statistics from host countries and news of the reopening of borders show that the trend is improving.  The last decade of medical tourism boomed, with the global market generating $58.6 billion annually in 2018, and in 2019 it was expected to grow by 11% annually and reach revenues of more than $142 billion by 2026.  The growth of this sector began mainly with increasing awareness, especially among the citizens of higher income countries, of health facilities and services, and of the affordable and economic prices of developing countries.  Providing a combination of medical and tourism services has led to the development and increase of requests for the use of health tourism services.  The gradual improvement of the damage caused by the coronavirus outbreak, a researcher in the field of migration, says: Many Asian countries, as well as the Middle East, including Iran, have health facilities and capabilities that should be considered again during the coronavirus era.  Mohammad Ho said that the lower cost of treatment has attracted the attention of citizens of other countries to benefit from health services and health care, along with their vacation and leisure time, and even the offer of medical tourism visas by some countries began with the aim of attracting more foreign patients.  Some countries provided additional services and incentives for the development of health tourism, for example, in addition to discounts on transportation services, provided free accommodation and tourist attractions for migrants.  The researcher said that the quarantine and ban of international travel last year troubled the tourism industry, adding that medical tourism was one of the sectors that had the most impact from this area.  It will take some time to return to pre-epidemic income levels, but countries around the world are taking steps to restart the industry in their own countries.  According to him, countries can have a progressive vaccination program that, while providing safety for citizens, opens doors to health migrants, while generating revenue and reviving the industry, a special place not only in medical technologies but also in the field of tourism for themselves.  Coronavirus and the development of health tourism in some countries, while requiring patients to be tested for the coronavirus, have turned health services, including vaccinations, into an opportunity to attract tourists.  In parallel, compliance certifications and international standards in Covid19 medical care have been developed globally, and these approvals, which state that hospitals and clinics meet the required standards, help bring in tourists.  Iran ’ s health tourism and latent capacity to attract global medical tourism migrants in 2020 was considered due to the coronavirus outbreak.  However, as recent positive performance has become a model for success in some countries, implementing a combination of solutions can help attract medical tourists.  According to this immigration researcher, Iran can develop its latent capacity in health tourism through proper modeling of these methods and with the help of the capabilities that it has experienced in recent years through the production of advanced medical equipment, health items and the implementation of therapeutic mechanisms.  He said: With the development of technologies, especially in the field of digital, information and communication technology, new methods in medicine and tourism will help a part of the tourists who are not yet able to travel.  Along with such measures, telemedicine is also experiencing significant growth: many hospitals are expanding the provision of online pre-travel diagnosis services and post-travel counseling.  While such solutions are not as effective as in-person tourism, they have opened new doors for the development of health tourism.  The researcher emphasized that the development of vaccine technology, coupled with the health facilities and infrastructure of countries with the coronavirus and the possibility of vaccination of non-native people, has increased the field for migration with health goals.  An opportunity that Iran, with its favorable capacities in the field of health care services, including its ability to produce vaccines, can put in the new path of creating added value.

Title: The Necessity of Revision in the Approach of Health Tourism Policy in Iran
Content: A report by the Majlis Research Center evaluated the need to review the policy approach of health tourism in Iran.  According to the Islamic Consultative Assembly Research Center, the Office of Education and Culture Studies of the Center in a report titled “The need to rethink the health tourism policy approach in Iran ” has said: According to the World Health Institute ’ s 2018 report, the global health tourism market ’ s revenue in 2017 was valued at $639 billion and is expected to reach $1,062 billion by 2025.  While according to global statistics, the share of the global medical tourism market of the health tourism market in 2017 was worth $53 billion and is expected to reach $143 billion by 2025.  Thus, the volume of health tourism turnover was more than 12 times that of medical tourism.  The report of the Majlis Research Center adds that until now, the main focus of health tourism policy in the country has been on medical tourism and health tourism, which has a far higher share of health tourism, has not been paid much attention, while the country's capacities in this area (such as hot springs, salty lakes, diverse mountain nature, forest, coastal, desert, etc.)  It is far above medical tourism.  According to the report, the remarkable point in the health tourism governance is that up to now, the strategies and policies set in this area have been systematic and systemic without regard to macro approaches.  The number of medical tourists has increased more than 30 times in the last 10 years, but this growth has not occurred in health tourism.  The report of the Majlis Research Center states that Iran has been subject to cruel sanctions in recent years, and because of the 70 percent import of medical equipment (Majlis Research Center, 2018), severe shocks have been inflicted on the health system, and because of this, the government has been forced to inject various supports and subsidies for the necessary imports, and on the other hand, due to lack of proper management of resources and equipment, beds, hospitals, medical equipment, medical staff, I'm...  It is not in line with domestic needs and the country needs to be strengthened in this regard.  Also, health tourism is rooted in the country ’ s domestic capacities and its dependence on imports is very low, because Iran, due to its high potential and climatic diversity and natural and climatic attractions, has a great competitive advantage to attract health tourists, especially from the 600 million population of neighboring countries.  Therefore, health tourism is not involved in the tensions that exist in the field of medical tourism, and with its competitive advantages, it can bring currency into the country beyond medical tourism.  Therefore, while considering the development of medical tourism, one should pay more attention to health tourism and create its value chains domestically.  The report of the Majlis Research Center adds, of course, in the field of health tourism, it should also be given serious attention that due to the cultural and indigenous demands of Islamic Iran, indigenous and creative patterns should be designed and implemented in this area, and non-scientific adaptations of the patterns of other countries and without observing the native cultural aspects should be avoided.  In the report of the parliamentary research center, it is suggested that the approaches and policies of the country in the field of health tourism be seriously reviewed and medical and health tourism based on internal needs and domestic competitive advantages be redesigned to promote health tourism based on local patterns.  In this regard, the system of health tourists, especially in the field of medical tourism, should be set up, in order to meet the necessary condition of having a standard tourism in the field of health, which is monitoring and clarifying how to service tourists from entry to exit. Title: The average check of a foreign patient in Ukrainian clinics in 2019 increased to $2800
Content: The average check of a foreign patient in Ukrainian clinics in 2019 increased from $2000-2500 to almost $2800, said Vice President of the Ukrainian Association of Medical Tourism (UAMT) Igor Torsky.  “According to our annual research, there is an increase in this indicator.  In 2019, the average check of one foreign medical tourist was about $2,800.  It is possible that in 2020 this figure will be even higher, ” he said at a press conference dedicated to the Global Healthcare Travel Forum 2020, which will be held in Kyiv and Lviv region on April 22-25, 2020.  At the same time, Torsky noted that the increase in the average check of foreign patients was facilitated, in particular, by the development of high-tech medical technologies and innovative methods of treatment.  At the same time, according to him, the increase in the average check was also influenced by the pricing policy of clinics. "This is a price increase.  We do not always agree and discuss with clinics about the feasibility of such an increase.  I want to advise representatives of clinics to be careful with pricing policy, as we are in a highly competitive world of medical tourism, ” he said.  At the same time, Torsky said that the average check of foreign patients in Ukrainian clinics differs by region.  “In Kiev, the average check is about $3,240, in Lviv this amount is lower, because the structure of services differs from region to region, ” he said.  According to him, reproductive medicine and cellular technologies are the most developed in the country ’ s clinics.  “These industries are high-tech, they require fairly accurate laboratory equipment and highly qualified specialists.  Ukraine in these two areas is one of the world leaders, ” he said.  At the same time, Torsky said, in other areas of medical tourism, in particular, in dentistry, rehabilitation, oncology, the flow of medical tourists is based on "a very balanced pricing policy of clinics", as well as on the absence of the so-called "waiting list" for getting to a consultation with narrow specialists.  “To get an appointment with a specialist insured person at home, you need to wait long enough.  This is one of the reasons why patients choose Ukraine, ” said the Vice President of UAMT.  In turn, the President of UAMT and the President of the Global Healthcare Travel Council Violetta Yanyshevskaya added that foreign patients can receive high-tech treatment in Ukrainian clinics using the technologies of cyberknife, gammanozha, da Vinci robot.  “In Ukraine, there are already expensive procedures for which previously patients must travel abroad.  Now these technologies and this high-tech equipment are present and clinics can provide such services, including to foreign patients, "she said.  At the same time, Yanyshevskaya expressed the opinion that for the development of medical tourism, Ukraine should resolve a number of problems, in particular, related to visa issues for foreign patients, as well as introduce the concept of “medical tourism ” into the legislative field.  “Working groups are working so that the parliament of this convocation can develop and adopt a law on medical tourism, ” she said.  According to GHTC estimates, the global market for health-related tourism segments is estimated at $439 billion.  According to international experts, in the next 10 years it is expected to grow steadily by 10-20%.  Every year, 3-4% of the world ’ s population will go abroad for treatment and rehabilitation.  As reported with reference to UAMT, in 2018, the average check of a foreign patient who is being treated in Ukrainian clinics was $2-2.5 thousand, excluding transportation and accommodation costs.  About 120 clinics in different regions of the country took foreign patients.  In the same year, about 65 thousand foreigners came to Ukrainian clinics to be treated, about 160 thousand people left the country for treatment.  Leaders of outbound medical tourism from Ukraine are Germany and Israel and Turkey.  According to UAMT, currently in the segment of incoming medical tourism in Ukraine are mainly private clinics.

Title: Dental tourism, looking for a beautiful smile
Content: ISNA / Khorasan Razavi Dental tourism is one of the most important forms of medical tourism and as an emerging industry, it is growing at a high rate.  The criteria for choosing a dentist for medical tourists depend on factors such as cost, location and quality of service.  The researchers noted that today ’ s unhealthy lifestyles, diets and longevity are gradually increasing the demand for quality and professional dental care.  The boom in the worldwide dental tourism market is primarily due to the increase in cases of dental malformation and the second is the increase in the desire for cosmetic dentistry.  The lower cost of treatment and better services in dental treatment in foreign country and the long waiting period for dental treatment in tourist country may boost the growth of this market in the future.  The global dental tourism market can be categorized in the type of treatment and area, and in terms of the type of treatment can be divided into preventive, restorative, prosthetic and other treatments.  Worldwide demand for cosmetic dentistry and therapeutic and restorative dentures has captured a large share of the market.  The pros of dental implant tourism, like medical tourism, are low medical costs, but there are many risks along the way.  Experts predict that the global dental implant market will reach $9 billion by 2027, making dental implants popular for a number of reasons, such as durability and usually success, which can last 20 years or more.  However, they are the best tooth replacement options and, of course, the most expensive, which in turn has led to an increase in dental tourism.  Also, market experts predict that the dental tourism industry will grow to a $5.83 billion sector by 2025, with the most important factors being the cost of treatment in countries and the lack of insurance coverage for many dental treatments.  In dental tourism, people travel abroad to receive dental care.  For example, a U.S. citizen may travel to Mexico to undergo dental implant surgery or an Australian may travel to Thailand to do oral matters.  With the above in mind, most dental tourists are from countries where the cost of treatment is very high, and the destinations in turn are countries known for their cheap services.  The results showed that the success of dental implants depends on the individual ’ s gums, which should be free of disease and infection, and patients who want to have implants but have gum disease should treat the gums first.  Dental tourism makes it difficult to achieve this goal, as it means multiple trips, and sometimes it is very unpleasant.  When the dental tourist encounters the entry of bacteria into the implant at the time of the gum surgery and the infection does not immediately show symptoms and the person returns to the origin, he will face infection after a few days.  Although infections caused by implants are treatable, they are difficult to treat and can be costly, and sometimes a lack of health standards and regulations can lead to these problems.  The researchers noted that regular dental checkups and oral hygiene will be the most important factor for reducing medical tourism trips.  Dentists, in some cases, make medical tourism more charitable, not to reduce costs, but to provide services to low-income people.  Doctors travel to poor countries to put their skills at the mercy of other people and provide the key to good oral health.  Dental tourism in the corona crisis Many patients travel to areas outside their country in search of a perfect smile to fix their oral problems.  According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), travel is likely to increase the incidence of COVID-19, and the farther the trip, the greater the risk.  It should be noted, however, that before COVID-19, travelers were also at risk of developing other diseases.  The financial impact on dental tourism has been dramatic, as this type of tourism will be difficult when patients are unwilling to perform services or unable to travel to the country due to quarantine or travel ban. passages.title: The project of the new Azatlyk square in Naberezhnye Chelny
passages.passage: Architectural bureau DROM presented the project of transformation of the main square in Naberezhnye Chelny, Russia.  The Soviet city, built in the late 1970s around the famous KamAZ truck factory, got a fresh look at the role of public space.  http: / / navote.ru /? p = 20720 The old main square, originally conceived as an esplanade connecting the unbuilt Lenin Museum with the building of the City Council, has long lost its significance and remained a formal and devoid of any functions a relic of the past.  It was filled with people only a few times a year during city festivals, remaining empty on other days.  The architects strategically moved the pedestrian axis from the center of the square to its edge, along which there was already a line of densely planted trees.  Thus, the movement around the square lost its former ideological pathos, became protected from wind and sun, and became connected with the surrounding buildings.  The new Promenade was filled with functions - kiosks, a viewing and playing area, a podium.  The central space was turned into three squares, each of which was endowed with its own character.  The event area is a large paved space for youth activity and open markets; the Green Square is a rest on the grass and large color compositions from the Department of Greening of the city; the Culture Square is an open-air music around the modernized old fountain, the entrance to the cinema located in the building of the City Hall. For each of the squares, a unique paving was developed, created recreation areas protected from wind and sun by green hills and trees. various local breeds.  Architects have also developed unique small architectural forms - pavilions and lanterns, which establish with their simple geometric forms a connection with the aesthetics of the whole city.  They were carried out by local industrial enterprises, which specially repurposed part of their capacities for this project, thus creating a new niche for the urban economy.  The use of local materials and labor resources, careful attention to reuse, allowed to reduce the negative impact on the environment and make the project sustainable, financially feasible and context-related.  The architects paid special attention to landscaping - increased the area of ​ ​ soft surfaces, preserved almost all existing trees and added many new ones. passages.title: In the Manor Lublin will install floating fountains
passages.passage: In the park of the Lublin Manor on the surface of the Lublin pond, in addition to the already built boat station, three floating fountains will appear.  They were placed at the request of residents.  In the park "Lublin Manors" on the surface of the Lublin pond, in addition to the already built boat station, there will be three floating fountains.  It was decided to place them at the request of residents. "The central element of the estate is the Lublin pond with an area of more than 14 hectares.  Before the start of works on improvement in the reservoir was already located fountain, but during the operation it came into disrepair.  At the request of residents, it was decided to replace it, and given the size of the reservoir - to increase the number of fountains, "the Department of capital repairs of the city of Moscow.Along the long coastline of the pond, a beautiful and comfortable embankment was arranged, along which any visitor to the park can walk and enjoy a walk by the water.  In addition, the banks of the pond strengthened and carried out its environmental rehabilitation.  And the highlight of the updated reservoir will be three floating light-dynamic fountains.  They will be placed directly on the surface of the water, fixed with the help of heavy cargo anchors. "Each fountain will consist of two levels.  At the bottom there will be a stream of 16 jets.  They will diverge in different directions by 2.5 meters, and at the upper level from the center - to beat one jet.  The height of the ejection of the central jet will reach from eight to 10 meters, and the lateral ones from five to seven.  Diverging to the sides, the flow of water will resemble a wide open fan.  To be able to admire the fountains at dusk or in the dark, each of them will be supplemented with 20 lamps, ” added the press service of the Department of capremont.Moreover, the benefits of the new fountains will not only be aesthetic: water will circulate and saturate the reservoir with oxygen.  Algae will not grow, and the pond will not bloom, and its fauna will feel great in clean water.Experts highly appreciate the scale of improvement of the territory of the "Lublin Manor". "In modern cities, parks and various green spaces acquire strategic importance - they become the center of public life, and sometimes the hallmark of the city (remember at least Central Park in New York), - said the head of the working group on the development of a sustainable Russian system. Vera Burtseva. – Lublin Park was once the center of public life, however, it was a long time ago – back in the XIX century.  Since then, the park was little occupied, and over time it lost its former attractiveness.  The more encouraging is the fact that as part of the work on the comprehensive improvement of Moscow, the city authorities decided to pay attention to this park.  It is very pleasing that the project of reconstruction of the park was developed taking into account the opinion of residents ".On the territory of the park, the road network was updated, the landscape organization of the territory was competently carried out, additional facilities were built according to an individual project.  Also on the territory of the park restored the boat station, ennobled and cleaned the pond and updated the platform for dancing, the expert lists. "As a result, for residents of the south-east of Moscow, such a recreational zone has become a real gift.  In the near future, the new location will attract active citizens - for sports, holidays and just walks with the whole family, "Vera Burtseva is sure.

Creating very small or pocket parks is a solution to offset part of the lack of green spaces in urban centers, residential complexes and other areas of the city.  Stating that these parks can be a refuge against the city crowds as well as a place for rest and relaxation, Sotoudeh Nia said: In the Fajr decade two pocket parks were exploited in the neighborhoods of Resalat Three and the city of Imam (ra) eight.  He continued: Currently, three pocket parks in the neighborhoods of Buyeh 5, Hafez 2 and Resalat 10 are in the final stages of the construction and operation, and the construction of two other parks in Resalat 48 and Ozeneh are on the agenda of the organization.  Sotoudeh Nia said the work will be carried out in partnership with the Deputy of Infrastructure, Transport and Traffic Affairs, adding: Given Gorgan Municipality ’ s approach to increasing urban green space per capita and the balanced distribution of amenities throughout the city, as well as taking steps towards creating a child-friendly city, Gorgan Municipality will continue its efforts to build and operate 12 pocket parks, with the highest emphasis on creating space for children and installing playgrounds in them until the end of the year. passages.title: Pocket park, this year new renovation of 50 - citizens out of the house there is a park, you can walk, chat, fitness, enjoy the green -- News Morning Post official website
passages.passage: Morning Post reporter Yu Wenyan at the corner of Fuxing East Road and Zhonghua Road, there is a small green space of only 500 square meters, which has installed three leisure seats and some small outdoor fitness equipment, which has become a "Cao Jia Street small garden" in the eyes of nearby residents. A number of pocket parks, which are often referred to as street gardens in the past, their presence not only allows nearby residents to walk, chat, fitness, and enjoy the green, but also lights up the environmental face of the block.  It is reported that the city built 47 pocket parks last year, and this year will build or upgrade 50.  Last year, 47 pocket parks were built at the corner of Fuxing East Road and Zhonghua Road, with a small green space of only 500 square meters.  Once, it was a green space, and now, it has become a "small garden in Cao Jia Street" in the eyes of nearby residents.  In Hongkou District, after a number of illegal buildings were demolished, a pocket park was built.  For example, the Huishan Garden at 207 Lintong Road, do not look at it with an area of only 408 square meters, but "five dirty", not only has exquisite and small green products, but also fitness trails.  In order to coordinate with the surrounding architectural style, the entrance to the park has also been designed in the style of Shikumen.  More than 2,300 square meters of public green space has been built in the area of 1501 North Xinshi Road, Jiangwan Town.  If there are no pavilions and seats for rest, it is also a little larger than the green space of Cao Jia Street.  But with activities and rest facilities, it becomes a simple little park.  According to incomplete statistics, 47 pocket parks were built in the city last year.  Pocket Park is not clearly defined Pocket Park, which originated from the proposal of the New York Parks Association in 1963, originally refers to small parks scattered in high-density urban centers and distributed in plaques.  Since the beginning of just over half a century, the United States, Britain, Japan and China and other countries have begun to have their own unique "pocket park plan".  Today's pocket parks refer to small green open spaces scattered in plaques in the city.  At present, there is no clear definition of pocket parks, and various small green spaces, small parks, street gardens, and small community sports venues in the city are common pocket parks.  Liu Yuelai, a scholar at Tongji University's School of Architecture and Urban Planning, said that there is currently no clear definition of the size of the pocket park.  In terms of area, he personally feels that it can be counted as small as tens of square meters and as large as thousands of square meters.  Unlike the comprehensive park, it offers simple and short breaks, such as a walk after a meal, a small sitting or children's play.  The city's greening department said that at present, their definition of the street garden from the area generally refers to the area of 300-3000 square meters of green space.  The municipal greening and cityscape administration bureau recently introduced that this year Shencheng plans to build or upgrade 50 pocket parks.  The actual number may be more than that.  Among the 79 colorful community projects recently released in Pudong, nearly 40 projects are defined as pocket parks. The pocket park in Hongkou District is planning to build the second phase of Yongnian Li, so that the pocket park function is becoming more and more perfect.  This year, Putuo plans to build a new 10,000 li community green space with a total area of 14,930 square meters, consisting of forests, wetlands and pocket parks.  The first part covers an area of about 10,970 square meters, and is designed to be an accessible urban forest and wetland.  The second part is located at the northwest corner of Wanquan Road and Fu Ping Road, covering an area of about 3960 square meters, and is designed to be positioned as a pocket park.  Fang Yan, deputy director of the municipal greening and cityscape administration bureau, said that the greening department is trying to make more parks around the citizens, even some street gardens and pocket parks, so that people can walk in parks not far from their homes.  According to the relevant person in charge of the municipal greening and cityscape administration bureau, the goal of allowing citizens to go out 500 meters to see a 3,000 square meter park green space has been basically achieved.  However, some residents feel that the greening of Shanghai is not enough.  Shanghai is still far behind Beijing, Hangzhou, Guangzhou and other cities, as well as New York, London and Paris.  For example, according to the area of public green space in the city and the base ratio of the resident population of more than 24 million, the per capita public green space is only about 8%, while some cities in China are generally more than 10%.  Therefore, in the case of limited land resources, Shanghai can only build more "pocket parks" and make dojo in snail shells.  It is understood that there are 243 urban parks in Shanghai, and by 2020, the number of urban parks will reach 300, forming a three-level system of "pocket parks - community parks - regional parks", and basically realizing that citizens go out 500 meters to have parks.

According to Liu Yuelai, a scholar at Tongji University's School of Architecture and Urban Planning, there is currently no clear definition of the size of pocket parks, but they can range from tens of square meters to thousands of square meters [93e05d05-4e27-428b-ad4d-dbe50339cb48].

Pocket parks also offer a range of recreational and social benefits, including opportunities for walking, chatting, and fitness [93e05d05-4e27-428b-ad4d-dbe50339cb48]. 
In addition, they can serve as community hubs, fostering social connections and a sense of community among residents [93e05d05-4e27-428b-ad4d-dbe50339cb48]. 
According to Fang Yan, deputy director of the municipal greening and cityscape administration bureau, the greening department is trying to make more parks around the citizens, even some street gardens and pocket parks, so that people can walk in parks not far from their homes [93e05d05-4e27-428b-ad4d-dbe50339cb48].

Title: The project of the new Azatlyk square in Naberezhnye Chelny
Content: Architectural bureau DROM presented the project of transformation of the main square in Naberezhnye Chelny, Russia.  The Soviet city, built in the late 1970s around the famous KamAZ truck factory, got a fresh look at the role of public space.  http: / / navote.ru /? p = 20720 The old main square, originally conceived as an esplanade connecting the unbuilt Lenin Museum with the building of the City Council, has long lost its significance and remained a formal and devoid of any functions a relic of the past.  It was filled with people only a few times a year during city festivals, remaining empty on other days.  The architects strategically moved the pedestrian axis from the center of the square to its edge, along which there was already a line of densely planted trees.  Thus, the movement around the square lost its former ideological pathos, became protected from wind and sun, and became connected with the surrounding buildings.  The new Promenade was filled with functions - kiosks, a viewing and playing area, a podium.  The central space was turned into three squares, each of which was endowed with its own character.  The event area is a large paved space for youth activity and open markets; the Green Square is a rest on the grass and large color compositions from the Department of Greening of the city; the Culture Square is an open-air music around the modernized old fountain, the entrance to the cinema located in the building of the City Hall. For each of the squares, a unique paving was developed, created recreation areas protected from wind and sun by green hills and trees. various local breeds.  Architects have also developed unique small architectural forms - pavilions and lanterns, which establish with their simple geometric forms a connection with the aesthetics of the whole city.  They were carried out by local industrial enterprises, which specially repurposed part of their capacities for this project, thus creating a new niche for the urban economy.  The use of local materials and labor resources, careful attention to reuse, allowed to reduce the negative impact on the environment and make the project sustainable, financially feasible and context-related.  The architects paid special attention to landscaping - increased the area of ​ ​ soft surfaces, preserved almost all existing trees and added many new ones.
