Forbidden Love, the first original drama, was produced in 1974, but its popularity began in 2006, when Turkey established its first satellite television station, and the series began to gain global exposure.  Two years later, Waleed bin Ibrahim Al Ibrahim, owner of the Middle East Broadcasting Center (MBC) in Saudi Arabia, bought the show and made it popular in the Arab region.  Among them, “Noor ”, a Turkish love story that aired between 2005 and 2007, reached an unprecedented audience of 92 million people; in early 2010,“ One Thousand and One Nights ” was exported to about 80 countries around the world; and in 2013, “Magnificent Century ”, an epic drama about Sulaiman, the Ottoman monarch, attracted more than 500 million viewers worldwide.  Each episode is usually about 60 minutes long on weekdays, and each episode is about 160 minutes long on weekdays.  These high cost productions featuring handsome male and female actors, with gorgeous scenes and catchy songs, plus romantic and Middle Eastern TV plots such as Noor, 1001 Nights, Ertugrul, which depict love, arranged marriage, extended family, patriarchy, and righteous struggle. The series has fascinated television viewers in the Arab world.  (Getty) Turkish dramas easily surpass foreign dramas in Mexico, the United States and South Korea in the Middle East, capturing the hearts of 200 million television viewers in the region, not only because there are no other strong competitors in the region, but also because Turkish producers re-dubbed the series with Arabic names and characters. In addition, the plot of the same Islamic culture makes the local drama more suitable to the tastes of Middle Eastern people than other overseas works.  However, in recent years, the development of Turkish and Saudi Arabia has been involved in the development of Turkish drama. In March 2018, the Saudi government and MBC stopped buying Turkish drama, when Sheikh Abdulaziz al-Sheikh, the Grand Chief of Saudi Arabia, described “Noor ” as“ anti-Islamic ” and “subversive ”, and said that the TV channel that broadcast the drama was“ God ”. and the enemies of its prophets ", and many of the region's major buyers went on strike to buy local dramas.  Egypt, another major market for Turkish dramas, has also banned Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan for “revenge ” after he backed then-President Mohamed Morsi during Egypt ’ s 2013 military coup, culminating in Abdel Fattah el-Sisi ’ s coming to power.  The development of Turkish dramas in the Middle East has been affected in recent years. (Getty) At present, support for the Muslim Brotherhood and other Islamic movements remains a major controversy in both countries, and is why Turkish dramas have not been shown in the region.  As a result, local dramas in the Middle East dropped from US $80 million (about HK $621 million) per year to US $15 million (about HK $116 million) last year.  Due to the severe restrictions on development in the Arab region, local dramas have begun to look around the world in recent years. In 2018, they were released for the first time in Spain, which immediately set off a wave of drama in the region, and later expanded to several European countries, including Italy.  Jose Antonio Anton, Vice President of the Atresmedia Group, a Spanish media group that introduced local dramas, believes that Turkey is a country that combines modern and traditional aspects, and these elements are fully reflected in the local dramas, so that the world can know the country.  “Turkish dramas are generally of high quality, and the plot is also very avant-garde, containing all kinds of drama elements, such as drama, horror, crime, history, etc. ” In addition, Turkish TV has a huge budget, excellent scenes, excellent acting and outdoor video studios, which have been able to produce high quality TV series in the past two decades.  (Getty) In recent years, local dramas have also turned to the Internet, testing the water on video streaming platforms such as YouTube, Starzplay, Netflix, etc., in order to export to the world.  At the same time, the change of local dramas is not only the target of export, but also the variety of drama tends to be diversified.  The current COVID-19 pandemic has also unexpectedly provided more support for local dramas. With many countries suspending filming due to the epidemic, and stopping purchasing expensive Korean dramas in Europe and the United States, affordable local dramas will continue to attract the attention of the world.  To date, Turkey has surpassed Mexico and Brazil as the world ’ s second largest exporter of television series, after the United States, with exports in Europe, the Arab region, Central Asia and the Americas. To date, the country has contributed more than 150 TV series to an estimated 500 million viewers in 146 countries around the world.  It is estimated that the total value of domestic drama exports reached US $500 million (about HK $3.9 billion) last year, and it is expected that by 2023, TV drama exports will generate as much as US $1 billion (about HK $7.8 billion) for Turkey.  Turkish dramas successfully export soft power, bringing many tourists to Turkey, and domestic products are also popular. (Reuters) The Turkish television industry plays a major role in increasing the popularity of the country in Asia, Europe, Latin America and North Africa.  In recent years, there has been an increase in interest in local dramas around the world. This has also played a positive role in promoting Turkey ’ s national image and its manufactured goods, and the number of foreign tourists visiting Istanbul has increased, especially from countries that broadcast local dramas.  All of this suggests that Turkey ’ s soft power is being infiltrated through television dramas.  Saudi Arabia ’ s Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman announced in 2018 that he would invest US $64 billion (HK $496.8 billion) over the next decade to develop the country ’ s entertainment industry.  The National Economic Reform Roadmap “Vision 2030 ” has“ loosened ” some socially conservative policies, such as the lifting of the 35-year commercial theater operating order in 2018.  Saudi Arabia expects to expand into other cultural areas in the future, encouraging arts, musical performances and other types of entertainment.  Saudi Arabia has loosened a 35-year ban on commercial cinemas. (Getty) In addition, the country will expand its film and television industry by building infrastructure, producing localized entertainment content and creating more than 30,000 jobs.  The authorities estimate that the country will have about 350 cinemas and 2,500 movie screens by 2030, with an industry value of about US $1 billion (about HK $7.8 billion).  The country also plans to double household entertainment spending, from 3% of GDP in 2018-2019 to 6% by 2030.  On the other hand, Saudi Arabia is also cooperating with the UAE to develop the film and television industry.  Among them, the US $40 million (HK $310 million) series Kingdoms of Fire, jointly funded by the two governments, was broadcast in 2019, highlighting the Ottoman Empire as the tyrant who has ravaged the Arab world for centuries.  In addition to co-productions, long-term cooperation programs between the two media companies also include training of production and acting personnel.  Kingdoms of Fire, a collaboration between Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates, was launched in 2019. (Getty) Saudi film and television professionals are mostly young people under the age of 30, 34% of whom are women.  Many people see that the film and television development in countries and regions is becoming more and more vigorous, and they no longer oppose their children to enroll in relevant courses, believing that they can find the ideal job after graduation.  According to Mohamed Ghazala, dean of the Faculty of Film and Television Arts at Effat University, Saudi Arabia, “The demand for local talent and capabilities will continue to increase due to increased production and the opening of more cinema-related departments and institutes in Saudi universities. ” However, the Saudi film and television industry is also facing many difficulties, with 43% of the industry believing that it is mainly lack of funding, 13 A further 11% said there was a lack of training and education related to film and television

passages.title: How to stop the creation of a new Ottoman Empire
passages.passage: In the world: How to stop the creation of a new Ottoman Empire 08.10.2020, 17: 33, News of the day The events in Nagorno-Karabakh have become one of many examples of Turkey ’ s aggressive foreign policy in recent years.  President Erdogan clearly makes it clear that he harbors specific plans to dramatically increase the political influence of his country – and maybe territorial acquisitions.  What can hinder the implementation of these plans?  Everyone remembers the scene from “12 chairs ”, when“ Ostap was carried, he felt a surge of new strength and chess ideas ”, and then told the residents of Vasyukov about the prospects of becoming New Vasyuki.  “And there, as you know, maybe eight years from now, the first interplanetary chess tournament in the history of the universe will take place in Vasyuki, ” the son of a Turkishman told the stunned Vasyuki.  The main current Turkish – Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan – can also be called a great combinator.  After all, it tells the people of Turkey – a regional state whose resources are very limited – tales of how to achieve global greatness with the help of Islam, weapons, historical heritage and aggression.  On all fronts, the format of this grandeur is known.  The minimum program is to turn Turkey into a leader, or rather, the master of the “Turkic world ” consolidated by it.  A huge territory, including the Caucasus, Central Asia, part of the Russian Federation (Crimea, the North Caucasus, the Volga region, Siberia).  The optimal program is to add to the Turkic world the space of the former Ottoman Empire, that is, the Middle East and North Africa.  Erdogan ’ s maximum program (and even his ambitions have a limit) is to achieve the status of the caliph of the 21st century – the leader of the entire Muslim world.  At the same time, the difference between Recep Erdogan and Ostap Bender is that the Turkish president is a real big politician.  And he does not just talk about the greatness of Turkey, but goes along the path of achieving it, not hesitating to use force to reformat someone else ’ s space into his own.  It is enough to look at the map and see that in all the conflicts from Morocco to Kyrgyzstan and from Georgia to Somalia there is a Turkish trace.  To work there, Erdogan applies a whole set of different methods: military, ideological, economic, political and even terrorist.  Thus, Ankara uses the Nagorno-Karabakh conflict in order to squeeze out all alien forces from the Caucasus.  First, remove the Western countries in the face of France and the United States (for which Erdogan offers Russia to solve the Armenian-Azerbaijani issues tete-a-tete on the principle of how Moscow and Ankara manage the situation in Idlib), and then move Russia with Iran.  Part of Syria continues to be under Turkish occupation – and it is not clear how and on what terms the Turks will leave from there.  But the Syrian territories are not enough for Ankara – Turkey squeezes out the territorial waters of Greece and encroaches even on the Greek islands.  Not for the sake of land, but in order to control the entire Eastern Mediterranean with the help of Libya (with which there is a treaty on the division of water spaces) and cut it off from the Western Mediterranean.  In Libya itself, Turkey is imposing a vassal regime, viewing the country as a source of hydrocarbons and a gateway for African migrants to Europe (which can be opened or closed at Ankara ’ s request).  Turkey penetrates into other countries of West Africa (primarily Muslim), from where it displaces France and even the ubiquitous China.  On the other side of the Black Continent, Somalia, close to the most important oil trade routes, is a Turkish military base.  The Turkish military is also present in Qatar, posing a threat to Saudi Arabia and protecting Turkish interests in the Persian Gulf.  And the support of Hamas and other Islamic terrorist organizations not only threatens Israel ’ s security, but wins for Turkey the sympathy of the Arab street.  Finally, Turkey is established in Central Asia.  Through investments, TV series (promoting Turkish meanings and cultural images) and Islamists, seriously straining China and Russia.  A nightmare of coalitions?  International relations theorists may think that Recep Erdogan is making two serious mistakes in his political jihad for leadership.  First, it fights on multiple fronts at once, dispersing its country ’ s limited resources.  Second, he makes too many enemies.  And we are not talking about small states such as Armenia, Cyprus or Greece, whose opinion can be ignored.  Erdogan turned against himself regional leaders (Egypt, Saudi Arabia, Iran) as well as great powers like Russia, the United States, France and a little China.  As a result, before the Great Combiner of the 21st century, a scenario may materialize that the Great Combiner of the 19th century, Chancellor of the German Empire Otto von Bismarck called the “nightmare of coalitions ”.  Managing the greatest power of the time, Bismarck was well aware that German aggression could consolidate peace against Berlin, and then even a great Germany would break down.  Which, by the way, happened when the aggressive behavior of the heirs of the “Iron Chancellor ” consolidated other great powers against the Empire.  Theorists are opposed to practice.  They will point out that yes, there are pockets of resistance.  The French send troops to help Greece, Saudi Arabia imposes an embargo on Turkish goods.  However, these hotbeds do not unite, and there is no “nightmare of coalitions ”.  Perhaps because Erdogan is not opposed to Bismarck.  The elites of most of the states whose policies Erdogan opposes are of such low quality that they are not even able to realize the full danger of the Turkish threat.  Turkey is attacking Greece – and Germany wants to negotiate with it.  Paris fits in with Athens – but instead of creating a common anti-Turkish front with Moscow, it calls on the whole of Europe to accept anti-Russian sanctions because of the fake “Navalny case ”.  And the Americans do support Erdogan ’ s actions against Russia, China and Europe – and do not understand that the consolidation of the Islamic world under the rule of Turkey can lead to the expulsion of Americans from the Middle East, Central Asia, North Africa and, perhaps, even Europe.  It is not surprising that the elites of all these countries pass before the Turkish boldness, aggressiveness and game of diplomatic poker (when Turkey sharply raises the stakes and the heat of hysteria, forcing the opponent to pass).  So, no one can stop Erdogan?  The Turkish leader himself is sure of this, but he is wrong.  Yes, the elites of most countries are not eagles, but they make beautiful vultures.  They may be humiliated in front of the eastern dictator, the same Gaddafi, who broke a tent near the Elysee Palace in Paris.  But when this dictator finds himself in a difficult situation, he is simply swept away and starved.  They are also catching up with Erdogan.  After all, the entire strategy of the Turkish Akela, who has become convinced of his own power and behaves more and more aggressively and risky every time, can collapse after the first miss.  This blunder may turn out to be a situation where a single power will give back and demonstrate to the whole world (as well as to the Turkish population, who tolerate Erdogan also because of his victories) the extremely modest limits of Turkish capabilities.  We can talk about the strike of a great power – for example, Russia, which will decide with the help of precision weapons to nullify the Turkish “Bashibuzuks ” (Syrian mercenary terrorists), entrenched in Azerbaijan and threatening the Russian North Caucasus.  A strengthened regional power can also strike – the same Israel, which is not used to ceremonial with the sponsors of terrorism.  Finally, a small country can respond, which Erdogan will drive into a corner with his irrepressible aggression.  And as soon as Erdogan can not answer (and bluff is good only as long as the words do not turn into action) and retreat, vultures will immediately attack him from all sides - to finish and bite.  After that, the internal opposition of Turkey is sharply activated, which consolidates the Turkish population against the “loser president ”.  As a result, the entire house of cards of Erdogan ’ s policy will fall apart, and he risks repeating another famous scene of 12 chairs.  It was a lunar evening.  Ostap raced along the silver street easily, like an angel, starting from the sinful earth.  In view of the failed transformation of Vasyukov into the center of the universe, it was necessary to flee not among palaces, but among log houses with external shutters.  There were chess fans in the back. ”  Tags: Turkey, Armenia, Tayyip Erdogan, Nagorno-Karabakh, Russia and Turkey

passages.title: What is Turkey looking for with the ‘ establishment ’ security series?
passages.passage: What is Turkey looking for with the ‘ establishment ’ security series?  Turkish affairs expert Beryl Akmal, BBC monitoring 57 minutes ago image source, TRT Description of the picture, the organization is broadcast from the Turkish state television network Tarti, a television series that aired in Turkey in March and praised the Turkish intelligence and security agency, has become a popular program.  The series has attracted attention due to its many parallels with Turkey ’ s sharp foreign policy and nationalist rhetoric.  The series "The Establishment", broadcast on the state television network TRT, focuses on the missions of the National Intelligence and Security Agency (MITT) forces who want to return the security documents related to the stolen drone program to the country.  The series reportedly shows pictures of the new headquarters and has received positive feedback among the public.  However, critics say the series has an "informational" function.  The establishment is the latest in a popular series that opens a window into the world within Turkey ’ s ruling circles, as Ankara tries to strengthen its international power.  What is the story?  The series revolves around the operation to protect Turkey from a shadowy global network that tries to turn the world against Turkey ’ s ambitions.  A group of agents is responsible for returning documents related to the drone program to the country.  Image source, TRT1 Image Description, is the villainous Fadi in the series, whose plan is to curb Turkey ’ s ambitions; Zayed Fadi is the villainous and villainous character who is a member of the “Company ” group.  The pro-government Yeni Shafagh newspaper wrote that Fadi was an allusion to Mohammed Dahlan, the ouster and former leader of the Palestinian Fatah movement.  Fadi ’ s background is reminiscent of Dahlan, both Palestinians who grew up in refugee camps.  It is said that Dahlan was known as Abu Fadi.  Dahlan has long been on the Turkish government ’ s hate list.  The Turkish government has placed him on the "Most Wanted Terrorist List", which includes those accused of involvement in the July 2016 coup.  Images of Turkish drones appear throughout the series.  Turkey-made drones have attracted global attention in recent years and have been used in Libya, Iraq and Nagorno-Karabakh.  Image source, TRT Image caption, Turkish-made UAVs are frequently shown in the series, showing UAVs flying over northern Iraq, and emphasizing their use in operations against Kurdish forces.  In one episode of the show, Fadi said, “I can ’ t wait to see [the faces of the Turkish forces] being shocked by the drone crash. ”  The series also advertises Turkey ’ s efforts to build military hardware.  On March 23, Ismail Demir, head of defense industries, posted a video showing the conversation, talking about Turkish-made military technology that has developed despite foreign sanctions and promised that Turkey will build domestic fighters.  He said, “Don ’ t hesitate for a moment, we ’ ll do it. ”  The “terrorism ” of Turkey ’ s overseas operations is a central theme in the series, with“ terrorists ” among the evil forces working with Fadi.  The sixth episode shows a clash between "terrorists" and Turkish forces in northern Iraq, and the seventh episode shows a militant who vows to avenge his friend who was killed by Turkish forces.  The final episode of the series is an allusion to Eren Belbel, a boy who was said to have been killed in northern Turkey in 2017 by the "illegal" Kurdish Workers' Party (PKK).  See: Turkey 's booming TV series industry. To play this file please enable JavaScript or use another browser.  Turkish TV series are popular around the world, and this episode shows agents sitting next to a young boy named Eren on a plane.  He said: “The Yankees have always been very brave.  You are always very brave.  Thank you for being with us, Erin. "  The PKK has been fighting the government for decades for greater autonomy for the Kurdish minority in Turkey.  The party is on the list of terrorist organizations in Turkey, the United States and the European Union.  Turkey has carried out several operations against the group in northern Iraq.  In January, the Turkish Interior Ministry announced the start of "Operation Ern" against the PKK "in memory of Ern Nightingale, who was martyred by the separatists of the terrorist organization."  The foreign policy of Mitt ’ s characters repeatedly underscore the importance of patriotism as they fight the opposition.  In the opening scene of the first episode, neo-Nazis in Germany lead the attack on a house owned by Turkish immigrants, leaving Mitt's future agent Sardar orphaned.  The source of the image, TRT explaining the picture, the attack on Turkish immigrants in a scene from the series apparently refers to the Salingen attack.  The incident probably refers to the 1993 Salingen attack when a group of extremists set fire to a house and killed five Turks.  A diplomat promised to bring Sardar to Turkey after the raid.  When Sardar says he has no one, the diplomat replies, “You have your country. ”  The camera then focuses on the diplomatic ring, which has an image of the Turkish flag engraved on it.  The series ’ tenth episode, after a character asks about Turkey ’ s presence in Syria, focuses on Turkey ’ s military policies in the region.  “What are Italy, France, the United States and Russia doing there?  What is China doing there? ”  Another officer, referring to the Ottoman period, added: “The place we call Syria has been a part of the motherland for the last 100 years. ”  The comments echoed what Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan said in March 2020: “They ask what Turkey is doing in Syria.  But they don ’ t ask other countries that question. ”  The ninth episode shows a conversation between two agents and a local man in the Greek city of Kozani, reflecting the Turkish government ’ s criticism of the Greek government.  The man says, “They [the Greeks] don ’ t want us to have the rights of minorities.  Everyone is working to take children away from their own language, religion and culture. ”  Western Thrace Muslims in Greece are the cause of tensions between Turkey and Greece, and Ankara often accuses Athens of violating minority rights.  The impact of the series has attracted attention on social media and social media.  Image source, TRT Image Explanation, Artoghrol Uprising, is a historical representation of the T.R.T. network, which gained worldwide fame, the hashtag series Enterprise often trended on Twitter and drew significant reactions on Facebook.  According to an analysis by social media outlet Khuros, more than 620,000 tweets with the hashtag were posted between the first episode of the series in March and the last episode in June.  Each episode had more than three million viewers on YouTube, and people made passionate comments about it.  One of the comments at the bottom of the last part reads: "[This message] was sent throughout the whole series: Don't go head-to-head with the Turkish government."  High-ranking security expert Mathew Yarar praised the series for showcasing the “advances ” of the Turkish intelligence agency, the technology used in warfare and covert operations.  But some critics discredited the series as a "propaganda" series.  One user wrote, “This series is entirely a propaganda series for the ruling Justice and Development Party. ”  TV critic Sina Kluoğlu in the Milliat newspaper added: “Advertising in this type of series is natural.  The point is that it should be done cautiously. ”  Internationally Benefit?  Formation is one of several T.R.T. series that deal with national and religious issues in parallel with the government ’ s vision.  The series, centering on its story, the founder of the Ottoman Empire, gained international fame with its religious flavour and heroic stories.  The recently released “Bir Zamanlar Kibris ” depicts attacks on the island ’ s Gravey-Turkish family in 1963 before Turkey ’ s controversial intervention.  The upcoming series of Barbaros (named after the Ottoman admirals Barbaros Kheiruddin Pasha) is a narrative to highlight the heroes of the Ottoman Navy, which coincides with Ankara ’ s naval and war policy as “The Blue Homeland ”.  Tarti General Manager Ibrahim Ehren said: “We always put our finger on scripts and products that support the country ’ s history, culture, ethics and human values and we will continue to play that role.  Many of our products have attracted the attention of international viewers in recent years.

passages.title: The first round of turkeys didn ’ t stop.
passages.passage: While the coronavirus outbreak stopped imaging Turkish series, some of these series continued to work in a new way.  According to ISNA, the Al Jazeera website has reported on how to continue shooting Turkish series that broadcast with a short distance.  The report said that some production groups of Turkish series used a new method to continue shooting their series.  In this way, some parts were filmed in the home of the actors and with the camera of their mobile phones, and without violating the rules of the home quarantine, the desired parts were prepared for broadcast.  The series “Eighties ” and“ Let ’ s Go ” continue to air, reaching audiences both inside and outside Turkey.  In the new episodes, these series also deal with the coronavirus.  In the final episode of the series "Forbidden Apple", before its broadcast temporarily stops, one of the actors of the series, while sitting in a taxi, has used a disinfectant and is worried about the coronavirus.  This is the first scene of the Turkish series that deals with the issue of Corona.  In an episode of the “Miracle Doctor ” series, there is mention of a dangerous virus that has entered Turkey through an East Asian traveler, but the name of the coronavirus is not mentioned.  Turkish actors these days have shared pictures of themselves on social media and in various places have been wearing masks and gloves to warn against the spread of the coronavirus.  The comedy series "Tranquility Neighborhood" has dedicated parts to the coronavirus and the importance of prevention in order to reduce the spread of the virus and how to spend free time during the quarantine.  The series, which explores various social issues with humor, now continues through shooting on mobile phones and in the actors ’ own homes.  Gülce Biersel, author of the series, said: “Shooting on mobile phones and in the actors ’ homes was a new exercise that taught us a lot, but some of the things that are necessary for a comedy show, such as walking, running, and certain body movements, can ’ t be done.  It had to be filmed in a consistent manner.  He added that turning each actor ’ s home into a suitable location for filming was difficult.  We asked them to send us a picture of their house.  The show has 11 actors, all of whom it was difficult to coordinate, but with the effort of the actors, we overcame the technical hurdles and got the job done.  Turkish actor Genghis Buzghorud said on Twitter: “The idea of having mobile phones in our homes was Jali ’ s idea.  I welcomed it as an initiative and set up a tent in my backyard for photography.  Mohammad Oymak, president of the Association for Culture and Literature, also welcomed the idea and expressed hope that the scenes filmed in the actors ’ homes would convey happiness and hope to the viewers.  In particular, this idea has been realized through extensive efforts and cooperation between actors and their technical staff and their Internet communication.  End of message.

passages.title: Turkey's hot markets in South America
passages.passage: Turkish television series now reached South America after capturing the film market of the Indian subcontinent, the Middle East, the Caucasus, Central Asia and the Balkans.  In South America, Chile, Argentina and Mexico are among the biggest customers of Turkish TV series.  The popularity of Turkish series in the Middle East or the Caucasus may be due to cultural and historical commonalities, but what could be the reason for the booming Turkish series market on the other side of the Atlantic in South America? In this series, usually luxury cars, expensive clothes are displayed.  But the hole has a different atmosphere.  The series is filmed in the Balat district of Istanbul.  In the Balat district of Istanbul, which used to be home to Jewish, Armenian and Greek communities, it is now a simple working-class area, but thanks to the series, the neighborhood has now flourished and many cafes have opened in its corners over the past few years.  Tagus Shaw reports that at any given time during filming, about 200 fans of the Pit series gather at the scene. Hector said: “A trip to Turkey would be a dream for us. ”  His wife, Patricia, interrupts him: “In the past, we never had any idea of Turkey.  We knew a Turkey full of violence with terrorist attacks.  But now it seems to be getting better. ”  Turkey ’ s $1 billion in revenue has become the world ’ s second-largest TV series exporter after Hollywood.  Recent research by Turkish state television shows that Turkish dramas are a “soft power, ” often trying to convey a specific image in the form of a romantic historical drama from the Ottoman period, which is usually reflected in the politics of the current Turkish government.  Follow Deutsche Welle on Instagram: “We are exporting Turkish culture, language and products.  Many of them just became popular abroad through our series.  Take, for example, Turkish music, which is now popular in South America. ”  According to estimates by the Turkish film industry, the revenue of the series could reach $1 billion by 2023. passages.passage: According to the Cinema Zone, the cultural group of the Young Journalists Club, with the increasing influence of satellite networks among Iranian families, one of the most significant damage that was mentioned for these networks was the cultural impact of the works broadcast by these networks, especially the Turkish series dubbed.  The series, based on the family as the central subject, provided sexist, pornographic, aristocratic and corrupt narratives of Turkish families, which due to the visual and sexual attractions, these series were able to tell stories of love triangles, betrayal, class divisions, anti-family, mere pleasure and corruption in the context of melodrama to many audiences with their own.  The increase in the activity of satellite networks and the distribution of Turkish works in Iranian satellite networks coincided with the increase of activities in Iran ’ s home theater network; at that time, some cultural analysts considered the home theater network as a reasonable response to satellite networks and an opportunity to overcome their works, a network that had less audits on its works and could attract the audience of Turkish TV series.  But that ’ s where the mistake started.  Many of the programmers and artists who were born and raised by the IRIB moved from television to the home theater network in order to gain more profit and freedom.  This, more than ever, left the hands of the cultural authorities of the IRIB empty to produce attractive and popular works and caused the TV audience to collapse.  On the other hand, less monitoring of the home screen network caused the creators active in this network, instead of presenting a new form and production of a cultural product, to resort to repetitive and sexual formulas of Turkish series and, with a glance from the rival, produced works that even in some cases, had lower quality and content than their Turkish rivals, and even caused some Iranian families to protest against some of these works.  Works that were only economical and did not spare any effort to sell more, from unnecessarily stretching the story, music-based video clips and creating triangular and square love nodes to the inclusion of erotic sequences.  Content works that, as a cultural commodity, had a countercultural function and only filled the pockets of its creators.  This is something that even the creators of these works are aware of.  From Manouchehr Hadi, the director of the love and romance series, who himself has confessed to modeling the Turkish series, to the writer of the series Dell, who says that the reason for the increase in the series' episodes is more money.  Now, some time after increasing the activity of VOD and attracting the audience through free subscription services and attractive plans to sell the works of the home theater network at a lower price than physical broadcasters and strengthening their position among the families as a multimedia and video broadcaster, in their latest action, they have dubbed and broadcast exclusive Turkish series.  The home theater network and VOD, which were supposed to rival Turkish satellite and TV channels, have now become their second branch.  Their cultural and content performance shows that the lack of proper supervision of the production of cultural works and the transfer of the field to individuals who are concerned only with financial interests, not cultural ones, provides the way for cultural influence and the destruction of the cultural foundations of the country and Iranian families.  Now that we are living in the era of the soft cultural war, the abandonment and lack of supervision in the field of cultural production can cause irreparable damage to our country; therefore, it is recommended that we not leave the field of culture to the enemy, by increasing the controls on the production of cultural works in the home theater network, and by producing great cultural works, such as Mokhtarnameh, the lost innocence, Hazrat Yusuf, English Kiev, Imam Ali, zero degree Hats off and...  We ourselves become the issuer of TV series, not the importer of Turkish serials, which can leave Iranian families with many cultural problems.  Author: The End of the Message

Title: Middle East drama: Saudi Arabia, Turkey fight for TV audience
Content: By Paul Law Last updated: 2021-06-03 13: 00 Turkey has been a soft power powerhouse in the Middle East for more than a decade, and its TV series have swept the entire Arab region.  Last year, local dramas became the annual hit in the Arab region, including “The Ambassador ’ s Daughter ” in Saudi Arabia,“ You Knock on My Door, ” which was popular with Arab audiences, and “Miracle Doctor, ” which was adapted from a Korean drama. It is also a good word.  In the face of the threat of domestic drama, Saudi Arabia, another big brother in the Arab world, naturally does not dare to ignore it. In recent years, it has actively developed the film and television industry, and even cooperated with the United Arab Emirates in order to “fight ” with Turkey in the field of television.  Is it face, interest, or a struggle for cultural soft power?  With its huge budget, excellent scenes and excellent acting skills, Turkey has produced a high level of drama in recent years.  The Capital: Abdul Hamid is pictured. (Getty) The history of Turkish television goes back almost half a century.  Forbidden Love, the first original drama, was produced in 1974, but its popularity began in 2006, when Turkey established its first satellite television station, and the series began to gain global exposure.  Two years later, Waleed bin Ibrahim Al Ibrahim, owner of the Middle East Broadcasting Center (MBC) in Saudi Arabia, bought the show and made it popular in the Arab region.  Among them, “Noor ”, a Turkish love story that aired between 2005 and 2007, reached an unprecedented audience of 92 million people; in early 2010,“ One Thousand and One Nights ” was exported to about 80 countries around the world; and in 2013, “Magnificent Century ”, an epic drama about Sulaiman, the Ottoman monarch, attracted more than 500 million viewers worldwide.  Each episode is usually about 60 minutes long on weekdays, and each episode is about 160 minutes long on weekdays.  These high cost productions featuring handsome male and female actors, with gorgeous scenes and catchy songs, plus romantic and Middle Eastern TV plots such as Noor, 1001 Nights, Ertugrul, which depict love, arranged marriage, extended family, patriarchy, and righteous struggle. The series has fascinated television viewers in the Arab world.  (Getty) Turkish dramas easily surpass foreign dramas in Mexico, the United States and South Korea in the Middle East, capturing the hearts of 200 million television viewers in the region, not only because there are no other strong competitors in the region, but also because Turkish producers re-dubbed the series with Arabic names and characters. In addition, the plot of the same Islamic culture makes the local drama more suitable to the tastes of Middle Eastern people than other overseas works.  However, in recent years, the development of Turkish and Saudi Arabia has been involved in the development of Turkish drama. In March 2018, the Saudi government and MBC stopped buying Turkish drama, when Sheikh Abdulaziz al-Sheikh, the Grand Chief of Saudi Arabia, described “Noor ” as“ anti-Islamic ” and “subversive ”, and said that the TV channel that broadcast the drama was“ God ”. and the enemies of its prophets ", and many of the region's major buyers went on strike to buy local dramas.  Egypt, another major market for Turkish dramas, has also banned Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan for “revenge ” after he backed then-President Mohamed Morsi during Egypt ’ s 2013 military coup, culminating in Abdel Fattah el-Sisi ’ s coming to power.  The development of Turkish dramas in the Middle East has been affected in recent years. (Getty) At present, support for the Muslim Brotherhood and other Islamic movements remains a major controversy in both countries, and is why Turkish dramas have not been shown in the region.  As a result, local dramas in the Middle East dropped from US $80 million (about HK $621 million) per year to US $15 million (about HK $116 million) last year.  Due to the severe restrictions on development in the Arab region, local dramas have begun to look around the world in recent years. In 2018, they were released for the first time in Spain, which immediately set off a wave of drama in the region, and later expanded to several European countries, including Italy.  Jose Antonio Anton, Vice President of the Atresmedia Group, a Spanish media group that introduced local dramas, believes that Turkey is a country that combines modern and traditional aspects, and these elements are fully reflected in the local dramas, so that the world can know the country.  “Turkish dramas are generally of high quality, and the plot is also very avant-garde, containing all kinds of drama elements, such as drama, horror, crime, history, etc. ” In addition, Turkish TV has a huge budget, excellent scenes, excellent acting and outdoor video studios, which have been able to produce high quality TV series in the past two decades.  (Getty) In recent years, local dramas have also turned to the Internet, testing the water on video streaming platforms such as YouTube, Starzplay, Netflix, etc., in order to export to the world.  At the same time, the change of local dramas is not only the target of export, but also the variety of drama tends to be diversified.  The current COVID-19 pandemic has also unexpectedly provided more support for local dramas. With many countries suspending filming due to the epidemic, and stopping purchasing expensive Korean dramas in Europe and the United States, affordable local dramas will continue to attract the attention of the world.  To date, Turkey has surpassed Mexico and Brazil as the world ’ s second largest exporter of television series, after the United States, with exports in Europe, the Arab region, Central Asia and the Americas. To date, the country has contributed more than 150 TV series to an estimated 500 million viewers in 146 countries around the world.  It is estimated that the total value of domestic drama exports reached US $500 million (about HK $3.9 billion) last year, and it is expected that by 2023, TV drama exports will generate as much as US $1 billion (about HK $7.8 billion) for Turkey.  Turkish dramas successfully export soft power, bringing many tourists to Turkey, and domestic products are also popular. (Reuters) The Turkish television industry plays a major role in increasing the popularity of the country in Asia, Europe, Latin America and North Africa.  In recent years, there has been an increase in interest in local dramas around the world. This has also played a positive role in promoting Turkey ’ s national image and its manufactured goods, and the number of foreign tourists visiting Istanbul has increased, especially from countries that broadcast local dramas.  All of this suggests that Turkey ’ s soft power is being infiltrated through television dramas.  Saudi Arabia ’ s Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman announced in 2018 that he would invest US $64 billion (HK $496.8 billion) over the next decade to develop the country ’ s entertainment industry.  The National Economic Reform Roadmap “Vision 2030 ” has“ loosened ” some socially conservative policies, such as the lifting of the 35-year commercial theater operating order in 2018.  Saudi Arabia expects to expand into other cultural areas in the future, encouraging arts, musical performances and other types of entertainment.  Saudi Arabia has loosened a 35-year ban on commercial cinemas. (Getty) In addition, the country will expand its film and television industry by building infrastructure, producing localized entertainment content and creating more than 30,000 jobs.  The authorities estimate that the country will have about 350 cinemas and 2,500 movie screens by 2030, with an industry value of about US $1 billion (about HK $7.8 billion).  The country also plans to double household entertainment spending, from 3% of GDP in 2018-2019 to 6% by 2030.  On the other hand, Saudi Arabia is also cooperating with the UAE to develop the film and television industry.  Among them, the US $40 million (HK $310 million) series Kingdoms of Fire, jointly funded by the two governments, was broadcast in 2019, highlighting the Ottoman Empire as the tyrant who has ravaged the Arab world for centuries.  In addition to co-productions, long-term cooperation programs between the two media companies also include training of production and acting personnel.  Kingdoms of Fire, a collaboration between Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates, was launched in 2019. (Getty) Saudi film and television professionals are mostly young people under the age of 30, 34% of whom are women.  Many people see that the film and television development in countries and regions is becoming more and more vigorous, and they no longer oppose their children to enroll in relevant courses, believing that they can find the ideal job after graduation.  According to Mohamed Ghazala, dean of the Faculty of Film and Television Arts at Effat University, Saudi Arabia, “The demand for local talent and capabilities will continue to increase due to increased production and the opening of more cinema-related departments and institutes in Saudi universities. ” However, the Saudi film and television industry is also facing many difficulties, with 43% of the industry believing that it is mainly lack of funding, 13 A further 11% said there was a lack of training and education related to film and television

Title: How to stop the creation of a new Ottoman Empire
Content: In the world: How to stop the creation of a new Ottoman Empire 08.10.2020, 17: 33, News of the day The events in Nagorno-Karabakh have become one of many examples of Turkey ’ s aggressive foreign policy in recent years.  President Erdogan clearly makes it clear that he harbors specific plans to dramatically increase the political influence of his country – and maybe territorial acquisitions.  What can hinder the implementation of these plans?  Everyone remembers the scene from “12 chairs ”, when“ Ostap was carried, he felt a surge of new strength and chess ideas ”, and then told the residents of Vasyukov about the prospects of becoming New Vasyuki.  “And there, as you know, maybe eight years from now, the first interplanetary chess tournament in the history of the universe will take place in Vasyuki, ” the son of a Turkishman told the stunned Vasyuki.  The main current Turkish – Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan – can also be called a great combinator.  After all, it tells the people of Turkey – a regional state whose resources are very limited – tales of how to achieve global greatness with the help of Islam, weapons, historical heritage and aggression.  On all fronts, the format of this grandeur is known.  The minimum program is to turn Turkey into a leader, or rather, the master of the “Turkic world ” consolidated by it.  A huge territory, including the Caucasus, Central Asia, part of the Russian Federation (Crimea, the North Caucasus, the Volga region, Siberia).  The optimal program is to add to the Turkic world the space of the former Ottoman Empire, that is, the Middle East and North Africa.  Erdogan ’ s maximum program (and even his ambitions have a limit) is to achieve the status of the caliph of the 21st century – the leader of the entire Muslim world. Title: The first round of turkeys didn ’ t stop.
Content: While the coronavirus outbreak stopped imaging Turkish series, some of these series continued to work in a new way.  According to ISNA, the Al Jazeera website has reported on how to continue shooting Turkish series that broadcast with a short distance.  The report said that some production groups of Turkish series used a new method to continue shooting their series.  In this way, some parts were filmed in the home of the actors and with the camera of their mobile phones, and without violating the rules of the home quarantine, the desired parts were prepared for broadcast.  The series “Eighties ” and“ Let ’ s Go ” continue to air, reaching audiences both inside and outside Turkey.  In the new episodes, these series also deal with the coronavirus.  In the final episode of the series "Forbidden Apple", before its broadcast temporarily stops, one of the actors of the series, while sitting in a taxi, has used a disinfectant and is worried about the coronavirus.  This is the first scene of the Turkish series that deals with the issue of Corona.  In an episode of the “Miracle Doctor ” series, there is mention of a dangerous virus that has entered Turkey through an East Asian traveler, but the name of the coronavirus is not mentioned.  Turkish actors these days have shared pictures of themselves on social media and in various places have been wearing masks and gloves to warn against the spread of the coronavirus.  The comedy series "Tranquility Neighborhood" has dedicated parts to the coronavirus and the importance of prevention in order to reduce the spread of the virus and how to spend free time during the quarantine.  The series, which explores various social issues with humor, now continues through shooting on mobile phones and in the actors ’ own homes.  Gülce Biersel, author of the series, said: “Shooting on mobile phones and in the actors ’ homes was a new exercise that taught us a lot, but some of the things that are necessary for a comedy show, such as walking, running, and certain body movements, can ’ t be done.  It had to be filmed in a consistent manner.  He added that turning each actor ’ s home into a suitable location for filming was difficult.  We asked them to send us a picture of their house.  The show has 11 actors, all of whom it was difficult to coordinate, but with the effort of the actors, we overcame the technical hurdles and got the job done.  Turkish actor Genghis Buzghorud said on Twitter: “The idea of having mobile phones in our homes was Jali ’ s idea.  I welcomed it as an initiative and set up a tent in my backyard for photography.  Mohammad Oymak, president of the Association for Culture and Literature, also welcomed the idea and expressed hope that the scenes filmed in the actors ’ homes would convey happiness and hope to the viewers.  In particular, this idea has been realized through extensive efforts and cooperation between actors and their technical staff and their Internet communication.  End of message.

Title: Turkey's hot markets in South America
Content: Turkish television series now reached South America after capturing the film market of the Indian subcontinent, the Middle East, the Caucasus, Central Asia and the Balkans.  In South America, Chile, Argentina and Mexico are among the biggest customers of Turkish TV series.  The popularity of Turkish series in the Middle East or the Caucasus may be due to cultural and historical commonalities, but what could be the reason for the booming Turkish series market on the other side of the Atlantic in South America?  Tuggs Shaw, a German broadcaster, has been trying to answer this question in a report on the popularity of Turkish shows in South America.  Yamaj Okur, producer of the Çukur story series, which has been translated into Persian as “Gut ”, says that a 140-minute episode will be produced every week, which will be broadcast on Turkish television five days later.  The Trench series is currently one of Turkey ’ s most successful series.  It tells the story of a family who controls one of Istanbul ’ s most dangerous neighborhoods, the Pit.  The neighborhood has long been in the hands of small families, whose most important rule is to be strict about the distribution of drugs in the neighborhood.  If someone spreads drugs, they have to leave the neighborhood.  The first episode of the series premiered on October 23, 2017 on TV and is still ongoing.  Correspondents from Istanbul and Rio de Janeiro say the demand for Turkish TV shows has increased.  Diazis, or series, forms a separate genre on Turkish television that is more comparable to the well-known South American telenovelas.  Araya Kisternas, a Chilean couple who have been married for almost 50 years, has just discovered their love for Turkish TV shows.  They say they show love with respect in this series.  The looks are romantic and traditional families are portrayed as important and valuable.  The Chilean couple have a herd that "in modern South American nostalgia traps shows a lot of bare limbs, men kiss men, and violence is part of the film."  Juan Vicente, director of the Chilean TV channel Mega, brought the first Turkish series to South America seven years ago.  He recalls that when the show “Binbir gece ” was broadcast on the mega network, he enthralled people and saved the mega network from bankruptcy at the time.  Juwan goes on to say that since many South Americans are conservative and dream of an ideal world, Turkish TV shows are in their best interest.  Family structures in Turkey are comparable to those in South America.  The patriarchal structures with a strong grandfather or father who determines and leads everything in the family are similar to the Chilean family structure.  The traditional family structure is also popular in Turkey, thanks to Erdoğan ’ s conservative and Islamist government.  Thousands took to the streets in recent days to protest Turkey ’ s withdrawal from the Convention against Violence against Women, but the protests have not been successful so far.  Yamaj Okor, producer of The Pit, says sex, swearing, alcohol in movies and TV shows are as taboo as they were in the '90s.  Okor added, “We have to tell our stories more gently, otherwise the TV won ’ t play it. ”  The series as Turkey ’ s “soft power ” is different from most Turkish series that depict the glamorous life of the middle and upper classes.  In this series, usually luxury cars, expensive clothes are displayed.  But the hole has a different atmosphere.  The series is filmed in the Balat district of Istanbul.  In the Balat district of Istanbul, which used to be home to Jewish, Armenian and Greek communities, it is now a simple working-class area, but thanks to the series, the neighborhood has now flourished and many cafes have opened in its corners over the past few years.  Tagus Shaw reports that at any given time during filming, about 200 fans of the Pit series gather at the scene.  On the other hand, vendors are trying to sell their goods, and in the future, visitors to South America are likely to be seen in the narrow alleys of Balat.  The series was recently sold to Chile.  The Chilean couple who are fascinated by the film are also planning a trip to Turkey.  Hector said: “A trip to Turkey would be a dream for us. ”  His wife, Patricia, interrupts him: “In the past, we never had any idea of Turkey.  We knew a Turkey full of violence with terrorist attacks.  But now it seems to be getting better. ”  Turkey ’ s $1 billion in revenue has become the world ’ s second-largest TV series exporter after Hollywood.  Recent research by Turkish state television shows that Turkish dramas are a “soft power, ” often trying to convey a specific image in the form of a romantic historical drama from the Ottoman period, which is usually reflected in the politics of the current Turkish government.  Follow Deutsche Welle on Instagram: “We are exporting Turkish culture, language and products.  Many of them just became popular abroad through our series.  Take, for example, Turkish music, which is now popular in South America. ”  According to estimates by the Turkish film industry, the revenue of the series could reach $1 billion by 2023.  At the end of his report on the Turkish series, Tagus Shaw has written that the next goal of the Turkish series is to capture the film market in Spain and Italy.

In recent years, it has actively developed the film and television industry, and even cooperated with the United Arab Emirates in order to “fight ” with Turkey in the field of television.  Is it face, interest, or a struggle for cultural soft power?  With its huge budget, excellent scenes and excellent acting skills, Turkey has produced a high level of drama in recent years.  The Capital: Abdul Hamid is pictured. (Getty) The history of Turkish television goes back almost half a century.  Forbidden Love, the first original drama, was produced in 1974, but its popularity began in 2006, when Turkey established its first satellite television station, and the series began to gain global exposure.  Two years later, Waleed bin Ibrahim Al Ibrahim, owner of the Middle East Broadcasting Center (MBC) in Saudi Arabia, bought the show and made it popular in the Arab region.  Among them, “Noor ”, a Turkish love story that aired between 2005 and 2007, reached an unprecedented audience of 92 million people; in early 2010,“ One Thousand and One Nights ” was exported to about 80 countries around the world; and in 2013, “Magnificent Century ”, an epic drama about Sulaiman, the Ottoman monarch, attracted more than 500 million viewers worldwide.  Each episode is usually about 60 minutes long on weekdays, and each episode is about 160 minutes long on weekdays.  These high cost productions featuring handsome male and female actors, with gorgeous scenes and catchy songs, plus romantic and Middle Eastern TV plots such as Noor, 1001 Nights, Ertugrul, which depict love, arranged marriage, extended family, patriarchy, and righteous struggle. The series has fascinated television viewers in the Arab world.  (Getty) Turkish dramas easily surpass foreign dramas in Mexico, the United States and South Korea in the Middle East, capturing the hearts of 200 million television viewers in the region, not only because there are no other strong competitors in the region, but also because Turkish producers re-dubbed the series with Arabic names and characters. In addition, the plot of the same Islamic culture makes the local drama more suitable to the tastes of Middle Eastern people than other overseas works.  However, in recent years, the development of Turkish and Saudi Arabia has been involved in the development of Turkish drama. In March 2018, the Saudi government and MBC stopped buying Turkish drama, when Sheikh Abdulaziz al-Sheikh, the Grand Chief of Saudi Arabia, described “Noor ” as“ anti-Islamic ” and “subversive ”, and said that the TV channel that broadcast the drama was“ God ”. and the enemies of its prophets ", and many of the region's major buyers went on strike to buy local dramas.  Egypt, another major market for Turkish dramas, has also banned Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan for “revenge ” after he backed then-President Mohamed Morsi during Egypt ’ s 2013 military coup, culminating in Abdel Fattah el-Sisi ’ s coming to power.  The development of Turkish dramas in the Middle East has been affected in recent years. (Getty) At present, support for the Muslim Brotherhood and other Islamic movements remains a major controversy in both countries, and is why Turkish dramas have not been shown in the region.  As a result, local dramas in the Middle East dropped from US $80 million (about HK $621 million) per year to US $15 million (about HK $116 million) last year.  Due to the severe restrictions on development in the Arab region, local dramas have begun to look around the world in recent years. In 2018, they were released for the first time in Spain, which immediately set off a wave of drama in the region, and later expanded to several European countries, including Italy.  Jose Antonio Anton, Vice President of the Atresmedia Group, a Spanish media group that introduced local dramas, believes that Turkey is a country that combines modern and traditional aspects, and these elements are fully reflected in the local dramas, so that the world can know the country.  “Turkish dramas are generally of high quality, and the plot is also very avant-garde, containing all kinds of drama elements, such as drama, horror, crime, history, etc. ” In addition, Turkish TV has a huge budget, excellent scenes, excellent acting and outdoor video studios, which have been able to produce high quality TV series in the past two decades.  (Getty) In recent years, local dramas have also turned to the Internet, testing the water on video streaming platforms such as YouTube, Starzplay, Netflix, etc., in order to export to the world.  At the same time, the change of local dramas is not only the target of export, but also the variety of drama tends to be diversified.  The current COVID-19 pandemic has also unexpectedly provided more support for local dramas. With many countries suspending filming due to the epidemic, and stopping purchasing expensive Korean dramas in Europe and the United States, affordable local dramas will continue to attract the attention of the world.  To date, Turkey has surpassed Mexico and Brazil as the world ’ s second largest exporter of television series, after the United States, with exports in Europe, the Arab region, Central Asia and the Americas. To date, the country has contributed more than 150 TV series to an estimated 500 million viewers in 146 countries around the world.  It is estimated that the total value of domestic drama exports reached US $500 million (about HK $3.9 billion) last year, and it is expected that by 2023, TV drama exports will generate as much as US $1 billion (about HK $7.8 billion) for Turkey.  Turkish dramas successfully export soft power, bringing many tourists to Turkey, and domestic products are also popular. (Reuters) The Turkish television industry plays a major role in increasing the popularity of the country in Asia, Europe, Latin America and North Africa.  In recent years, there has been an increase in interest in local dramas around the world. This has also played a positive role in promoting Turkey ’ s national image and its manufactured goods, and the number of foreign tourists visiting Istanbul has increased, especially from countries that broadcast local dramas.  All of this suggests that Turkey ’ s soft power is being infiltrated through television dramas.  Saudi Arabia ’ s Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman announced in 2018 that he would invest US $64 billion (HK $496.8 billion) over the next decade to develop the country ’ s entertainment industry.  The National Economic Reform Roadmap “Vision 2030 ” has“ loosened ” some socially conservative policies, such as the lifting of the 35-year commercial theater operating order in 2018.  Saudi Arabia expects to expand into other cultural areas in the future, encouraging arts, musical performances and other types of entertainment.  Saudi Arabia has loosened a 35-year ban on commercial cinemas. (Getty) In addition, the country will expand its film and television industry by building infrastructure, producing localized entertainment content and creating more than 30,000 jobs.  The authorities estimate that the country will have about 350 cinemas and 2,500 movie screens by 2030, with an industry value of about US $1 billion (about HK $7.8 billion).  The country also plans to double household entertainment spending, from 3% of GDP in 2018-2019 to 6% by 2030.  On the other hand, Saudi Arabia is also cooperating with the UAE to develop the film and television industry.  Among them, the US $40 million (HK $310 million) series Kingdoms of Fire, jointly funded by the two governments, was broadcast in 2019, highlighting the Ottoman Empire as the tyrant who has ravaged the Arab world for centuries.  In addition to co-productions, long-term cooperation programs between the two media companies also include training of production and acting personnel.  Kingdoms of Fire, a collaboration between Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates, was launched in 2019. (Getty) Saudi film and television professionals are mostly young people under the age of 30, 34% of whom are women.  Many people see that the film and television development in countries and regions is becoming more and more vigorous, and they no longer oppose their children to enroll in relevant courses, believing that they can find the ideal job after graduation.  According to Mohamed Ghazala, dean of the Faculty of Film and Television Arts at Effat University, Saudi Arabia, “The demand for local talent and capabilities will continue to increase due to increased production and the opening of more cinema-related departments and institutes in Saudi universities. ” However, the Saudi film and television industry is also facing many difficulties, with 43% of the industry believing that it is mainly lack of funding, 13 A further 11% said there was a lack of training and education related to film and television

Title: How to stop the creation of a new Ottoman Empire
Content: In the world: How to stop the creation of a new Ottoman Empire 08.10.2020, 17: 33, News of the day The events in Nagorno-Karabakh have become one of many examples of Turkey ’ s aggressive foreign policy in recent years.  President Erdogan clearly makes it clear that he harbors specific plans to dramatically increase the political influence of his country – and maybe territorial acquisitions.  What can hinder the implementation of these plans?  Everyone remembers the scene from “12 chairs ”, when“ Ostap was carried, he felt a surge of new strength and chess ideas ”, and then told the residents of Vasyukov about the prospects of becoming New Vasyuki.  “And there, as you know, maybe eight years from now, the first interplanetary chess tournament in the history of the universe will take place in Vasyuki, ” the son of a Turkishman told the stunned Vasyuki.  The main current Turkish – Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan – can also be called a great combinator.  After all, it tells the people of Turkey – a regional state whose resources are very limited – tales of how to achieve global greatness with the help of Islam, weapons, historical heritage and aggression.  On all fronts, the format of this grandeur is known.  The minimum program is to turn Turkey into a leader, or rather, the master of the “Turkic world ” consolidated by it.  A huge territory, including the Caucasus, Central Asia, part of the Russian Federation (Crimea, the North Caucasus, the Volga region, Siberia).  The optimal program is to add to the Turkic world the space of the former Ottoman Empire, that is, the Middle East and North Africa.  Erdogan ’ s maximum program (and even his ambitions have a limit) is to achieve the status of the caliph of the 21st century – the leader of the entire Muslim world.  At the same time, the difference between Recep Erdogan and Ostap Bender is that the Turkish president is a real big politician.  And he does not just talk about the greatness of Turkey, but goes along the path of achieving it, not hesitating to use force to reformat someone else ’ s space into his own.  It is enough to look at the map and see that in all the conflicts from Morocco to Kyrgyzstan and from Georgia to Somalia there is a Turkish trace.  To work there, Erdogan applies a whole set of different methods: military, ideological, economic, political and even terrorist.  Thus, Ankara uses the Nagorno-Karabakh conflict in order to squeeze out all alien forces from the Caucasus.  First, remove the Western countries in the face of France and the United States (for which Erdogan offers Russia to solve the Armenian-Azerbaijani issues tete-a-tete on the principle of how Moscow and Ankara manage the situation in Idlib), and then move Russia with Iran.  Part of Syria continues to be under Turkish occupation – and it is not clear how and on what terms the Turks will leave from there.  But the Syrian territories are not enough for Ankara – Turkey squeezes out the territorial waters of Greece and encroaches even on the Greek islands.  Not for the sake of land, but in order to control the entire Eastern Mediterranean with the help of Libya (with which there is a treaty on the division of water spaces) and cut it off from the Western Mediterranean.  In Libya itself, Turkey is imposing a vassal regime, viewing the country as a source of hydrocarbons and a gateway for African migrants to Europe (which can be opened or closed at Ankara ’ s request).  Turkey penetrates into other countries of West Africa (primarily Muslim), from where it displaces France and even the ubiquitous China.  On the other side of the Black Continent, Somalia, close to the most important oil trade routes, is a Turkish military base.  The Turkish military is also present in Qatar, posing a threat to Saudi Arabia and protecting Turkish interests in the Persian Gulf.  And the support of Hamas and other Islamic terrorist organizations not only threatens Israel ’ s security, but wins for Turkey the sympathy of the Arab street.  Finally, Turkey is established in Central Asia.  Through investments, TV series (promoting Turkish meanings and cultural images) and Islamists, seriously straining China and Russia.  A nightmare of coalitions?  International relations theorists may think that Recep Erdogan is making two serious mistakes in his political jihad for leadership.  First, it fights on multiple fronts at once, dispersing its country ’ s limited resources.  Second, he makes too many enemies.  And we are not talking about small states such as Armenia, Cyprus or Greece, whose opinion can be ignored.  Erdogan turned against himself regional leaders (Egypt, Saudi Arabia, Iran) as well as great powers like Russia, the United States, France and a little China.  As a result, before the Great Combiner of the 21st century, a scenario may materialize that the Great Combiner of the 19th century, Chancellor of the German Empire Otto von Bismarck called the “nightmare of coalitions ”.  Managing the greatest power of the time, Bismarck was well aware that German aggression could consolidate peace against Berlin, and then even a great Germany would break down.  Which, by the way, happened when the aggressive behavior of the heirs of the “Iron Chancellor ” consolidated other great powers against the Empire.  Theorists are opposed to practice.  They will point out that yes, there are pockets of resistance.  The French send troops to help Greece, Saudi Arabia imposes an embargo on Turkish goods.  However, these hotbeds do not unite, and there is no “nightmare of coalitions ”.  Perhaps because Erdogan is not opposed to Bismarck.  The elites of most of the states whose policies Erdogan opposes are of such low quality that they are not even able to realize the full danger of the Turkish threat.  Turkey is attacking Greece – and Germany wants to negotiate with it.  Paris fits in with Athens – but instead of creating a common anti-Turkish front with Moscow, it calls on the whole of Europe to accept anti-Russian sanctions because of the fake “Navalny case ”.  And the Americans do support Erdogan ’ s actions against Russia, China and Europe – and do not understand that the consolidation of the Islamic world under the rule of Turkey can lead to the expulsion of Americans from the Middle East, Central Asia, North Africa and, perhaps, even Europe.  It is not surprising that the elites of all these countries pass before the Turkish boldness, aggressiveness and game of diplomatic poker (when Turkey sharply raises the stakes and the heat of hysteria, forcing the opponent to pass).  So, no one can stop Erdogan?  The Turkish leader himself is sure of this, but he is wrong.  Yes, the elites of most countries are not eagles, but they make beautiful vultures.  They may be humiliated in front of the eastern dictator, the same Gaddafi, who broke a tent near the Elysee Palace in Paris.  But when this dictator finds himself in a difficult situation, he is simply swept away and starved.  They are also catching up with Erdogan.  After all, the entire strategy of the Turkish Akela, who has become convinced of his own power and behaves more and more aggressively and risky every time, can collapse after the first miss.  This blunder may turn out to be a situation where a single power will give back and demonstrate to the whole world (as well as to the Turkish population, who tolerate Erdogan also because of his victories) the extremely modest limits of Turkish capabilities.  We can talk about the strike of a great power – for example, Russia, which will decide with the help of precision weapons to nullify the Turkish “Bashibuzuks ” (Syrian mercenary terrorists), entrenched in Azerbaijan and threatening the Russian North Caucasus.  A strengthened regional power can also strike – the same Israel, which is not used to ceremonial with the sponsors of terrorism.  Finally, a small country can respond, which Erdogan will drive into a corner with his irrepressible aggression.  And as soon as Erdogan can not answer (and bluff is good only as long as the words do not turn into action) and retreat, vultures will immediately attack him from all sides - to finish and bite.  After that, the internal opposition of Turkey is sharply activated, which consolidates the Turkish population against the “loser president ”.  As a result, the entire house of cards of Erdogan ’ s policy will fall apart, and he risks repeating another famous scene of 12 chairs.  It was a lunar evening.  Ostap raced along the silver street easily, like an angel, starting from the sinful earth.  In view of the failed transformation of Vasyukov into the center of the universe, it was necessary to flee not among palaces, but among log houses with external shutters.  There were chess fans in the back. ”  Tags: Turkey, Armenia, Tayyip Erdogan, Nagorno-Karabakh, Russia and Turkey
