passages.passage: South Korea ’ s Samsung Group Vice President Lee Jae-yong was sentenced to two and a half years in prison in January for bribing former President Park Geun-hye ’ s confidants.  As the government and business sectors recently asked the government to pardon Li, he appeared in court again on Thursday (22) on charges of fraud and stock price manipulation, the first appearance of the company after about three months.  According to South Korean media reports, 52-year-old Li Jae-rong dressed in a black suit and white shirt to appear in court.  Lee Jae-yong appeared in court 10 minutes before the start of the trial. In addition to answering that the judge did not want a jury, Lee Jae-yong remained silent.  Prosecutors alleged that in the process of promoting the merger of Samsung C & T and Cheil Industries in 2015, Samsung executives deliberately published false information to raise the share price of First Woven and depress the share price of Samsung Property in order to boost Li Zaihong ’ s acquisition of shares after First Woven was acquired by Samsung Property to become the largest shareholder and strengthen his influence on the Samsung Group.  If Li is convicted of fraud and stock price manipulation, his sentence may be increased.  Lee has so far served half of his sentence, which is 15 months.  South Korea ’ s government faces growing pressure from business and opposition parties to pardon Lee.  Utilizing Lee Jae-yong ’ s global network will help safeguard South Korea ’ s vaccine supply, according to the Federation of South Korean Industries.  Park Jen, a conservative lawmaker, also said that South Korea ’ s investment in U.S. semiconductor production will ensure that South Korea receives vaccines from the United States.  Russia plans to withdraw from the International Space Station from 2025, space agency chief Dmitry Rogozin said on Wednesday, with President Vladimir Putin's approval, Russia will build its own space station and hopes to put it into orbit by 2030, a plan that reportedly costs $6 billion (about HK $46.6 billion).  If successful, it will open a new chapter in Russia ’ s space exploration and end more than two decades of U.S.-Russian cooperation on the International Space Station.  Russian Deputy Prime Minister Yuri Borisov told Russian television last weekend that Moscow would notify its partners to leave the International Space Station from 2025.  Russia ’ s Interfax news agency reported that Rogozin said it plans to put the space station into orbit by 2030, and unlike the International Space Station, it is likely that there will not be permanent members of the Russian space station, because the space station ’ s orbit will expose the astronauts to high radiation, but Russian astronauts can go, and the space station will also use artificial intelligence and robots.  He added that Russia is ready to consider allowing foreign space visitors, “but the space station must be national … If you want to do things well, you have to do it yourself. ”  Since 1998, Russian cosmonauts have cooperated with astronauts from the United States and 16 other countries on missions to the International Space Station, one of the areas in which Moscow has worked closely with Washington.  However, the US-Russian relationship is in crisis due to issues such as human rights and hacking.  NASA ’ s Perseverance successfully extracted oxygen from the Martian atmosphere The recent mission of the Mars rover Perseverance successfully converted carbon dioxide from the Martian atmosphere into breathable pure oxygen, NASA said on Wednesday.  NASA said that the device, called MOXIE (Mars Oxygen In-Situ Resource Utilization Experiment), is the size of a toaster, and uses extreme heat to separate oxygen atoms from carbon dioxide molecules through electrolysis work. MOXIE successfully generated about 5 grams of oxygen, which can allow an astronaut to breathe for 10 minutes.  This feat marks the first time humans have extracted natural resources available for human use from the environment of another planet.  Oxygen content in the Martian atmosphere is extremely low, carbon dioxide accounts for 95% of the Martian atmosphere, and the rest is mainly composed of molecular nitrogen and argon.  Adequate oxygen supply is key to human exploration of Mars, experts believe that astronauts living and working on Mars may need 1 ton of oxygen to maintain their needs for a year, and believe that it is more practical to convert oxygen on Mars than to transport 25 tons of oxygen from Earth.  MOXIE ’ s operating concept is to produce 10 grams of oxygen per hour.  NASA says scientists plan to run the MOXIE device at least nine more times over the next two years, under different conditions and at different speeds. passages.title: "ice" shelter that will protect astronauts from adverse factors on the surface of Mars » DailyTechInfo
passages.passage: Since people who will arrive on Mars will have to spend several months or even years on the surface, they will need a safe haven that will protect them from temperature changes and from cosmic radiation breaking through the thin and rarefied atmosphere of the planet.  Moreover, for the construction of such shelters, it will be necessary to use local materials as much as possible, because the delivery of the necessary amount of composition for the manufacture of special concrete from the Earth is not yet feasible.  Scientists and experts from NASA's Langley Research Center have come up with a simple and effective solution to the above problem.  In the project developed by them shelter Mars Ice Home as the main protective layer is used ordinary ice, obtained from water extracted from the atmosphere of Mars.The design of the shelter Mars Ice Home is a large inflatable torus, closed on top of a spherical dome of a sufficiently thick layer of ice.  All the structural elements that need to be delivered from Earth are quite light and compact, and in the final design of the structure, in addition to water, some other materials that can be mined on the surface of the Red Planet are used.  In addition, the water from which the protective dome will be made can be later recycled and from it can be obtained fuel for refueling the Mars Ascent Lander spacecraft, which will take people from the surface back to orbit.  The main disadvantage is that it will take at least 400 days to extract the necessary amount of water from the atmosphere of Mars.  This problem can be solved by sending a pre-automated expedition to Mars, which will include robots that will create a foundation, pump up the shell of the shelter, collect enough water and build an ice dome during the time that people will fly to Mars.  This approach will avoid the need for hasty construction of shelter or burying deep underground immediately after the arrival of people on the planet.Mars Ice Home is still only an exciting project, not worked out to the smallest details.  However, it can serve as a starting point for other designers and specialists who will be able to produce elegant and complete solutions to the problems associated with the long stay of people on the surface of the Red Planet.

passages.title: Martian organics formed thanks to natural batteries
passages.passage: Scientists seem to have uncovered the secret of the origin of organic matter in meteorites that came from the Red Planet.  The list of participants in the process sounds like this: water, volcanic rocks, electricity.  What is nice is that such processes can take place on many bodies of the solar system.  Scientists seem to have uncovered the secret of the origin of organic matter in meteorites that came from the Red Planet.  The formation of organic matter occurs due to natural “accumulators ” consisting of water, salts and volcanic rocks.  Such conclusions are made in a scientific article published in the journal Science Advanced by a group led by Andrew Steele (Andrew Steele) from the Carnegie Scientific Institute in the USA.Recall that proteins, fats, carbohydrates, DNA, RNA and many other molecules, without which it is impossible to imagine a living organism, belong to organic substances.  Of course, not all organic matter is an integral part of living beings or is formed with their participation, so it is not necessary to equate organic matter with life. However, the presence of such molecules is the most important condition for the appearance of the biosphere.  Apparently, only organic chemistry can provide the variety, flexibility and complexity of chemical processes that are necessary for the existence of even the most primitive microbe.  In 2012, a team led by Steele studied carbon from organic molecules found in ten Martian meteorites.  The researchers came to two conclusions, pleasant and not so.  The good news is that this organics originated on Mars (rather than being brought in by pollution on Earth).  The bad news: it is not a product of the vital activity of living organisms; how was it formed in this case?  This is what the authors of a recent study found out. "Identification of the processes during which organic carbon compounds are formed on Mars is of great interest to determine its habitability potential," says Steel.Scientists used three samples of Martian meteorites.  The first is Tissint, which fell in Morocco in 2011.  The second is Nakhla, discovered in Egypt in 1911.  The third was NWA 1950, found in Morocco in 2001.  In all these celestial stones previously found inclusions of Martian organics.Meteorites were subjected to the most careful analysis.  Among the methods used were both the usual viewing of the sample in an optical microscope, and Raman spectroscopy, translucent electron microscopy, nanoscale mass spectrometry of secondary ions, X-ray absorption near the absorption edge (X-ray absorption near-edge structure) and other methods with names incomprehensible to the average person. Thanks to all these methods, the authors thoroughly studied the chemical composition and fine structure of organic inclusions and the surrounding rocks.  By the way, it turned out that the organics of meteorites are extremely similar to the substances found on the Red Planet by the MSL mission.  The detailed information obtained allowed scientists to draw conclusions about what processes could lead to the formation of these substances. It turned out that one of the necessary ingredients are volcanic minerals such as spinel.  On the Red Planet, rich in ancient volcanoes, there is no shortage of such material.  The second important component is liquid water, in huge concentrations containing various salts (in particular, perchlorates).  Such brines have never been directly detected on Mars, but, according to experts, they can exist there almost everywhere.  Finally, the third element of the “magic potion ” is carbon dioxide.  It is also, to put it mildly, not in deficit: the Martian atmosphere consists of it almost completely.  For a while, there is something like a natural battery.  As a result, organic compounds are formed from carbon CO2 and hydrogen of water. "The discovery that a natural system can essentially form a small battery based on corrosion, which controls electrochemical reactions between minerals and the surrounding liquid, has serious consequences for astrobiology," says Steele. Indeed, it turned out that the synthesis of organic matter does not need exotic conditions or components.  All the necessary ingredients are quite common for Mars, which is either already proven (volcanic minerals and carbon dioxide), or assumed (brines).  Moreover, a similar process can take place on bodies such as Europa or Enceladus.  Recall that earlier "33Live.RuNauka" (nauka.vesti.ru) wrote about how a record amount of organic matter was discovered on Mars, as well as that life in the crust of the planet could be supported by radiation.

passages.title: On Earth found able to survive on Mars bacteria
passages.passage: A microorganism capable of surviving in harsh Martian conditions has been discovered by scientists from the National University of Australia in Canberra.  We are talking about one of the strains of cyanobacteria living in hot springs and geysers.  The uniqueness of the bacterium is that it has chlorophyll, which captures the dimmest light, and red, not green.  A description of the bacterium was published in the journal Science.  One of the authors of the work, Elmars Krausch, noted the fantastic nature of this discovery, since these microbes, discovered during the study of geysers in the Chilean Andes, will be able to survive in the soil of Mars.  In the course of the experiment, strains of bacteria Chroococcidiopsis thermalis, when the light level was lowered to "Martian" values, continued to grow and produced nutrients - organic substances necessary for life, the article notes.  Thus, bacteria will be able to live on Mars and create a biosphere on its surface, the researchers conclude.  On June 7, NASA announced the discovery of organic molecules on the Red Planet.

passages.title: Converting Martian salt water into oxygen and fuel with a new technology
passages.passage: New technology allows astronauts to convert Martian saltwater into oxygen and fuel when they land on the Red Planet in 2033.  There is water on Mars, but most of it is frozen, and the rest is mixed with salt, making it useless for future astronauts who plan to land on the planet by 2033.  Now, a team of researchers at Washington University in St. Louis has developed a system that converts unusable water into fuel and oxygen.  The system uses electricity to convert saltwater into oxygen and hydrogen, and has been found to work in the Martian atmosphere at temperatures as low as -33 degrees Fahrenheit.  The saltwater electrolyser produces 25 times more oxygen than NASA ’ s MOXIE, which launched in July 2020 with the Mars 2020 rover and aims to produce a small amount of oxygen on Mars.  Vijay Ramani of the University of Washington said the technology is just as useful on Earth as it is on Mars because it can turn the oceans into a source of oxygen and fuel.  According to Inverse, the device has two parts around it, one of which separates water to form hydroxyl ions and the other separates water again to produce oxygen.  Although the technology is currently being developed on Earth, it is expensive and likely will not be able to withstand the freezing temperatures of Mars.  Ramani and other researchers decided to build a portable version of the technology that could operate on the Red Planet continuously without the need to heat or purify the water source.  Research scientist and first author of the study, Shrihari Sankarasubramanian, said: “Water-soluble perchlorates (so-called impurities) are actually functional in a Mars-like environment because they prevent water from freezing and also improve the performance of the electrolaser system by reducing electrical resistance.  The study is based on data from NASA ’ s Phoenix Mars Lander, which touched Mars in 2008.  Scientists know that in order to live on Mars, even temporarily, astronauts would have to produce some of their needs, especially oxygen for breathing and fuel for travel to Earth or beyond on the Red Planet.  NASA's Mars Endurance rover is currently traveling to Mars by carrying instruments that use electrolysis at high temperatures.  The researchers hope to work with NASA to further develop the system in the future.  End of message.

passages.title: Mars Rover Perseverance successfully tested the device to extract oxygen from the Martian atmosphere
passages.passage: An experimental device called MOXIE (Mars Oxygen In-Situ Resource Utilization Experiment) was first tested on April 20, and this test was recognized as successful: for an hour of operation, the installation the size of a conventional toaster was able to produce more than 5 grams of oxygen, writes Newsru.  The atmosphere of Mars is almost 96% carbon dioxide (CO2).  The MOXIE unit is capable of converting this carbon dioxide into oxygen and carbon monoxide (CO, carbon monoxide), which is a by-product of the processing and is released back into the atmosphere.  The process of processing carbon dioxide occurs by electrolysis of solid oxides at a temperature of 800 degrees Celsius.  During operation, the device captures carbon dioxide, passes through a filter to remove dust and compresses it, providing pressure at ground level.  The gas then passes through a heated electrolysis cell, which consists of several layers of nickel alloy and ceramics.  Ceramic elements of the cell are able to conduct current at high temperature - they pass oxygen ions and trap carbon monoxide.  The outer surface of MOXIE is covered with a thin layer of gold.  This coating protects the MOXIE surface from heating, protecting the rover electronics located next to the instrument.  Future astronauts: breathe easier.  The MOXIE technology demonstration aboard @ NASAPersevere successfully extracted oxygen from the thin Martian atmosphere — a critical component for life support on the Red Planet and rocket fuel for the trip home. https: / / t.co / HOsguer. hYgkP pic.twitter.com / SwL0etf9Uu — NASA JPL (@ NASAJPL) April 21, 2021 The maximum estimated performance of MOXIE is up to 10 grams of oxygen per hour.  The test program includes at least nine more tests over two years.  These tests will be carried out under different conditions to assess the performance of the plant.  In the future, more large-scale oxygen production on Mars may come in handy for practical purposes.  First, oxygen is used as an oxidizing agent for rocket fuel.  For example, to launch a rocket with four astronauts from Mars to Earth requires about 7 tons of fuel and 25 tons of oxygen.  The ability to produce this amount of oxygen during the astronauts ’ stay on Mars will prevent this oxygen from being delivered from Earth – delivering a large and productive oxygen generator modeled on MOXIE would be a more practical solution.  Secondly, oxygen, which makes up 21% of the Earth's atmosphere, is needed for breathing - four astronauts will be enough one ton of oxygen for a year on Mars.  We will remind, the Rover Perseverance landed in the area of 45-kilometer crater Jezero, named after the village in Bosnia and Herzegovina.  This crater is located on the western edge of the Isis Plain (a giant impact crater north of the equator of Mars).  As scientists suggest, in ancient times in the area of ​ ​ the crater Ezero was a river delta, where organic matter and other potential traces of microorganisms that could have lived on Mars about 3 billion years ago could have been collected.  The crater itself was then filled with water and was a lake.

passages.title: On the 60th Martian day, the rover “Perseverance ” obtained oxygen for breathing for 10 minutes
passages.passage: The Mars Rover “Perseverance ” on the 60th Martian day extracted oxygen from the atmosphere of the red planet.  This was reported by the American space Agency (NASA).  Oxygen from Mars, which is 96% carbon dioxide, was obtained using the apparatus MOXIE.  The test took place on April 20.  A device the size of a toaster has recycled carbon dioxide and received 5.4 grams of oxygen - enough to breathe for 10 minutes.  The device on board the six-wheeled robot is capable of producing up to 10 grams of oxygen per hour, according to NASA ’ s website.  The experiment was called an important step in the processing of carbon dioxide on Mars.  According to the deputy head of the scientific directorate of NASA Jim Reiter, scientists have come close to the goal of leading people on Mars.  Earlier, the rover, whose mission began on February 18, received real sounds from Mars.

passages.title: Mars Rover Perseverance for the first time in history was able to get oxygen from the atmosphere of Mars
passages.passage: NASA employees for the first time received oxygen from the atmosphere of Mars, which is 96% carbon dioxide, according to the website of the American space Agency.  On April 20, the Pereverance rover, which has been exploring Mars since February, processed carbon dioxide into oxygen with the help of an experimental MOXIE spacecraft installed aboard the rover.  After two hours of preparation, MOXIE began producing oxygen at a rate of six grams per hour.  During the first experiment, NASA experts received 5.4 grams of oxygen, which would be enough to breathe for 10 minutes.  In general, MOXIE is able to produce up to 10 grams of oxygen per hour.  Jim Reuter, deputy director of NASA's science directorate, called the experiment "an important first step in converting carbon dioxide into oxygen on Mars."  "We are getting closer to our goal: someday see humans on Mars," Reuters said.  According to him, oxygen is important both for breathing people and for obtaining rocket fuel.  “In the future, researchers will need to get fuel on Mars to return home, ” he said.  Minval.az

passages.title: Scientists have found organisms that can give rise to life on Mars
passages.passage: Scientists have found organisms that can give rise to life on Mars 16.02.2021, 14: 58 They are able to grow and multiply in the conditions of the red planet.  New experiments have shown that cyanobacteria, also known as blue-green algae, can successfully grow in Martian atmospheric conditions.  Of course, a few more ingredients will be needed, but when humans get to Mars, they will be able to create life support systems based on cyanobacteria for the human habitat, writes nv.ua.  "Here we show that cyanobacteria can use the gases available in the Martian atmosphere, at low overall pressure, as a source of carbon and nitrogen," said astrobiologist Cyprien Verso from the University of Bremen in Germany.  "Under these conditions, cyanobacteria retained their ability to grow in water containing only Martian dust, and they could be used to feed other microbes.  This can help make long-term missions to Mars sustainable, ” the authors of the study believe.  All types of cyanobacteria produce oxygen as a byproduct of photosynthesis, and even today they are an invaluable source of it.  For several years, scientists have speculated whether we could use the ability of cyanobacteria to produce oxygen to live on Mars.  This will bring additional benefits.  The atmosphere of Mars consists mainly of carbon dioxide (95 percent) and nitrogen (3 percent), which are fixed by cyanobacteria, turning them into organic compounds and nutrients, respectively.  However, atmospheric pressure on Mars is a big problem.  The total pressure there is less than 1% of Earth ’ s — from 6 to 11 GPa: this is too small for the presence of liquid water, while the partial pressure of gaseous nitrogen — from 0.2 to 0.3 GPa — is not enough for their metabolism.  But recreating the atmosphere, like on Earth, would be too expensive: gases would have to be imported.  So the researchers were looking for a middle ground: an atmosphere close to Martian, which allows cyanobacteria to grow well.  The authors have developed a bioreactor called Atmos, which has an atmospheric pressure of about 10 percent of Earth ’ s, but uses only what can be found on Mars, albeit in inverted proportions: 96 percent nitrogen and 4 percent carbon dioxide.  The bioreactor also included water that can be obtained on Mars from melting ice, which in some places is abundant on the surface, and a simulator of Martian regolith, a mixture of minerals created here on Earth using only what can be found on Mars.  The team chose the type of nitrogen-fixing cyanobacteria that preliminary trials showed was most likely to thrive under these conditions, Anabaena sp.  PCC 7938, and tested it in a variety of conditions.  The researchers concluded that nitrogen-fixing, oxygen-producing cyanobacteria can be grown on Mars at low pressure under controlled conditions using exclusively local ingredients.  From cyanobacteria, sugar, amino acids and other nutrients can be obtained to feed other crops, which can then be used for other purposes, such as the production of medicines.  Atmos was designed to test whether cyanobacteria can be grown under certain atmospheric conditions rather than for maximum efficiency, and the parameters of the bioreactor will depend on many factors in the mission to Mars, including the payload and mission architecture.  However, now that the concept has been proven, the team can begin work on optimizing the bioreactor system that could one day save us life on Mars. passages.title: Soviet missions to Mars: how the Soviet Union studied the Red Planet
passages.passage: The first successful Soviet Martian mission was to send to the "red planet" automatic interplanetary station of the third generation Mars-2.  Mars-2 was designed to explore Mars both from its orbit and directly from the surface of the planet.  The Mars-2 AMS consisted of an orbital station (an artificial satellite for exploring Mars) and a lander.  Navigation in space was carried out with the help of orientation to the Sun, the star Canopus and the Earth.  The Soviet Union planned to carry out serious research work on Mars, for this purpose the AMC had all the necessary equipment: an infrared photometer to study the surface relief by measuring the amount of carbon dioxide, an ultraviolet photometer to determine the density of the upper atmosphere.  Cosmic ray particle counter and many other instruments.  The lander was also automated and configured for autonomous operation and control.  The station was launched from the Baikonur Cosmodrome on May 19, 1971.  The flight of the station to Mars lasted more than 6 months.  The flight was carried out according to the program and, as they say, nothing foreshadowed trouble, only at the last stage (the most important, it should be admitted), due to incorrect calculations, the lander entered the atmosphere at an angle greater than the set one, the parachute system was ineffective in such conditions and, having passed through the atmosphere of Mars, the device crashed.  To the honor of our country, our lander, although it crashed, still became the first artificial object on the planet.  The orbital station for more than eight months carried out complex studies of Mars, having made 362 turns around the planet during the work.  The next Russian Martian mission was more successful.  When developing the Mars-3 program, the shortcomings of the previous launch were taken into account.  Launched nine days after Mars-2, the Mars-3 station successfully reached Martian orbit six months later.  The lander for the first time in history made a soft landing on the surface of the “red planet ”.  After one and a half minutes of preparatory period, the device began to work and began to broadcast a panorama of the surrounding surface, but after 14 and a half seconds, the “Martian show ” ended.  “Show ” this, of course, can be called with a big stretch: AMC transmitted only the first 79 lines of the photo-television signal, which represented a gray background without a single detail, the same happened with the broadcast from the second telefotometer.  Various versions of incorrect operation of the devices were assumed: corona discharge in the antennas of the transmitter, damage to the battery... but the final decision on the reasons for the failure was not made.  No, the Martians did something.  Mars-4 July 21, 1973 from the Baikonur cosmodrome was launched AMS Mars-4.  204 days after launch, on February 10, 1974, the spacecraft flew at a distance of 1,844 km from the surface of Mars.  Twenty-seven minutes before that, single-line optical-mechanical scanners — telophotometers — were turned on, with the help of which panoramas of two regions of the surface of Mars were taken (in the orange and red-infrared ranges).  For the first time in the practice of domestic cosmonautics, four spacecraft participated in the flight.  Mars-4 had many tasks: studying the distribution of water vapor on the disk of the planet, determining the gas composition and density of the atmosphere, measuring the flow of electrons and protons on the flight path and the planet, studying the spectra of the own glow of the atmosphere of Mars and many others.  The main task of Mars-4 was to communicate with automatic stations on the surface of Mars.  The Mars-4 spacecraft photographed Mars from a flight path.  On photographs of the surface of the planet, which are of very high quality, you can distinguish details up to 100 m in size.  This makes photography one of the main means of exploring the planet.  With its help, using color filters by synthesizing negatives, color images of a number of areas of the surface of Mars were obtained.  Color images are also of high quality and are suitable for areological-morphological and photometric studies.  Unfortunately, Mars 4 did not fulfill all the tasks assigned to it.  Mars 5 was launched four days after the launch of Mars 4.  The tasks that were assigned to him were not very different from the previous mission.  The Mars-5 station successfully entered orbit around the planet, but immediately there was a depressurization of the instrument compartment, as a result of which the station lasted only about two weeks.  The scientific instruments placed on the Mars 5 station were intended mainly for studying a number of important characteristics of the planet's surface and near-planetary space from orbit.  The device was equipped with a liman-alpha photometer, designed jointly by Soviet and French scientists, and designed to search for hydrogen in the upper atmosphere of Mars.  Installed on board the magnetometer made measurements of the magnetic field of the planet.  To measure the surface temperature, an infrared radiometer was intended, operating in the range of 8-40 microns.  The artificial satellite of Mars "Mars-5" transmitted to Earth new information about the planet and the surrounding space; from the orbit of the satellite obtained high-quality photos of the Martian surface, including color.  Studies of the magnetic field in the Martian space, conducted by the apparatus, confirmed the conclusion made on the basis of similar studies of the spacecraft "Mars-2, -3", that near the planet there is a magnetic field of about 30 gamma (7-10 times greater than the value of the interplanetary unperturbed field carried by the solar wind).  It was assumed that this magnetic field belongs to the planet itself, and Mars 5 helped to get additional arguments in favor of this hypothesis.  Similar measurements from the Mars-5 spacecraft directly measured the temperature of atomic hydrogen in the upper atmosphere of Mars for the first time.  Preliminary data processing showed that this temperature is close to 350 ° K.  Despite the fact that the work of the station did not last long, during its work, numerous information was obtained about Mars, its atmosphere and magnetic field.  Another of our lander was on Mars thanks to the AMS Mars-6, launched from the Baikonur cosmodrome on August 5, 1973.  Sadly, this time there was no soft landing.  During the descent, there was no digital information from the MX 6408M device, but with the help of the Zubr, IT and ID devices, information was obtained on overloads, temperature and pressure changes.  Just before landing, communication with the SA is lost.  The last telemetry received from him confirmed the issuance of a command to turn on the soft landing engine.  The new appearance of the signal was expected 143 seconds after the disappearance, but this did not happen, however, the data obtained during the descent has already yielded significant results and made a great contribution to the study of Mars.  The lander Mars 6 landed on the planet, for the first time transmitting to Earth data on the parameters of the Martian atmosphere obtained during the descent.  Mars-6 measured the chemical composition of the Martian atmosphere using a radiofrequency mass spectrometer.  Shortly after the opening of the main parachute, the analyzer's opening mechanism worked, and the Martian atmosphere gained access to the instrument.  Preliminary analysis suggests that the content of argon in the atmosphere of the planet can be about one-third.  This result is of fundamental importance for understanding the evolution of the Martian atmosphere.  Pressure and ambient temperature measurements were also carried out on the lander; the results of these measurements are very important both for expanding knowledge of the planet and for identifying the conditions in which future Martian stations should operate.  Together with French scientists, a radio astronomy experiment was also performed - measuring the radio emission of the Sun in the meter range.  Receiving radiation simultaneously on Earth and on board a spacecraft hundreds of millions of kilometers away from our planet, allows you to restore a three-dimensional picture of the process of generating radio waves and obtain data on the streams of charged particles responsible for these processes.  In this experiment, another task was solved - the search for short-term bursts of radio radiation, which can, as expected, occur in distant space due to explosive phenomena in the cores of galaxies, supernova flares and other processes.  Mars-7 was launched on August 9, 1973.  The Mars mission failed.  The lander passed 1400 kilometers from the surface of Mars and went into space.  Thus, the target program of Mars-7 was not fulfilled, but, making an autonomous flight, the lander retained its operability and transmitted information to the flight vehicle via radio lines KD-1 and RT-1.  Communication with the Marsa-7 spacecraft was maintained until March 25, 1974.  During the work of Mars-7 in September-November 1973, a connection was recorded between the increase in the flow of protons and the speed of the solar wind.  Preliminary processing of the data of the Mars-7ob spacecraft of the radiation intensity in the resonant Lyman-alpha atomic hydrogen line made it possible to estimate the profile of this line in interplanetary space and determine in it two components, each of which makes approximately equal contribution to the total radiation intensity. passages.title: On Mars, the level of oxygen increased sharply
passages.passage: Oxygen levels on Mars soared 5 13.11.2019, 13: 36 1,762 Why?  NASA experts conducted an analysis of seasonal changes in the composition of the atmosphere of Mars, data about which was sent by the Curiosity apparatus.  It turned out that the concentration of oxygen in the atmosphere of the planet every spring increases dramatically, and scientists do not understand why.  This is reported by slashgear.com.  For six years, the rover collected data on the atmosphere of Mars, analyzed them and sent them to Earth.  From these data, it becomes clear that the planet's atmosphere contains 95% carbon dioxide, 2.6% nitrogen, 1.9% argon, 0.16% oxygen and 0.06 carbon monoxide.  However, on Mars there is a phenomenon of molecular circulation, which is associated with seasonal changes in pressure in winter and spring.  With nitrogen and argon, the situation is similar to what the researchers predict.  With oxygen, everything is different - in the spring its content in the atmosphere of the planet begins to increase sharply and only in the fall falls to the level predicted by known chemical processes.  The amount of oxygen is different each year.  In other words, something produces it first and then removes it.  The last time the level of oxygen in the atmosphere of the red planet exceeded 30%, while in the atmosphere of the Earth it contains about 20%.  Scientists have not yet been able to say exactly what this is related to.  There is an assumption that the change in the proportion of oxygen in the atmosphere of Mars coincides with the change in the level of methane.  The publication in-space.ru specifies that "oxygen and methane can be produced both biologically, for example, by microbes, and abiotic - in chemical processes related to water and soil."

passages.title: People are preparing for the pollution of Mars - our review
passages.passage: The experiment was conducted on Earth, more precisely, in the stratosphere of our planet.  There, scientists from two space agencies sent a probe with various microorganisms to check how they would behave in the atmosphere of the red planet.  "We successfully tested a new method of placing bacteria and fungi in Martian conditions using a probe sent into the stratosphere," says Marta Filipa Cortezao of DLR.  "Some microbes, especially black mold embryos, were able to survive the journey even after exposure to very high levels of ultraviolet radiation."  Understanding how microorganisms react to space travel and the Martian environment is key to future missions.  One of the motives is that in the search for extraterrestrial life, scientists should be sure that there are no microorganisms brought from Earth.  But there are other threats.  “On long missions to Mars, we need to know that the microorganisms associated with humans would survive on the Red Planet, because some of them can threaten the lives of astronauts, ” says Katarina Zins, one of the main authors of the publication, which appeared in the publication Frontiers in Microbiology.  But such resistant to harsh conditions earthly life forms still harbor additional opportunities.  "Some microbes may be underestimated by us in the exploration of Mars.  But they are able to help us in the production of food and other materials, regardless of the Earth.  This is a key opportunity to survive away from home, ” the expert adds.  According to experts, it is very difficult to reproduce Martian conditions on Earth.  However, this was possible outside the ozone layer.  “We sent microorganisms placed inside the MARSBox (Microbes in Atmosphere for Radiation, Survival and Biological Outcomes experiment), in which both the atmosphere of Mars and the pressure were artificially maintained into the stratosphere during the entire scientific mission, ” explains the essence of the experiment Cortezao.

passages.title: Found organisms that can survive on Mars
passages.passage: Scientists at the University of Bremen in Germany have found microorganisms that can grow and develop in the Martian atmosphere.  According to the researchers, based on cyanobacteria or blue-green algae, it is possible to create life support systems for people who will live on the surface of Mars.  This is reported in an article published in the journal Frontiers in Microbiology.  Scientists have shown that cyanobacteria can support life by using the gases of the Martian atmosphere as a source of carbon and oxygen, despite the low pressure.  Blue-green algae multiplied in water with a suspension of Martian dust, which makes it possible to use them to feed other living organisms.  In addition, cyanobacteria produce oxygen as a byproduct of photosynthesis.  Researchers have developed an Atmos bioreactor that maintains atmospheric pressure at 10 percent of Earth ’ s and nitrogen and carbon dioxide concentrations of 96 percent and 4 percent, respectively.  These conditions are close to Martian, but differ from them: atmospheric pressure is a percentage of Earth's, and the proportion of carbon dioxide is 95 percent.  Water and a mixture of minerals mimicking Martian regolith were also added to the bioreactor.  For the experiment, the team chose a species of nitrogen-fixing cyanobacteria Anabaena sp.  PCC 7938, which preliminary tests have shown is most likely to thrive in these conditions.  Although the bacteria grew better on a nutrient medium, the researchers also observed growth on Martian regolith.  Then the scientists dried the culture of microorganisms and used it as a substrate for growing E. coli.  This proves that cyanobacteria on Mars can be used to feed crops that, in turn, are suitable for the synthesis of nutrients, including drugs.  Leonid Nemov

report:
Creating a sustainable atmosphere on Mars requires careful planning and consideration of various factors, including the equipment needed, worst-case scenarios, and the largest number of people that can be sustained by the atmosphere.

To create a sustainable atmosphere on Mars, it is essential to use local materials whenever possible. 
One such example is the use of cyanobacteria, which can thrive in Martian atmospheric conditions and provide a source of carbon and oxygen [0e38128c-1a86-47c4-b506-d6a220ec1b63]. 
These microorganisms can be grown in a bioreactor, such as the Atmos bioreactor developed by researchers at the University of Bremen in Germany [37fe8723-ac2b-44da-8657-c889f18cc112]. 
The bioreactor maintains atmospheric pressure at 10 percent of Earth's and nitrogen and carbon dioxide concentrations of 96 percent and 4 percent, respectively [37fe8723-ac2b-44da-8657-c889f18cc112]. 
Water and a mixture of minerals mimicking Martian regolith were also added to the bioreactor [37fe8723-ac2b-44da-8657-c889f18cc112].

Another example of local materials used in creating a sustainable atmosphere on Mars is the use of Martian dust, which can be used to feed other living organisms [0e38128c-1a86-47c4-b506-d6a220ec1b63]. 
Cyanobacteria, such as Anabaena sp. 
PCC 7938, can multiply in water with a suspension of Martian dust [37fe8723-ac2b-44da-8657-c889f18cc112]. 
These microorganisms can support life by using the gases of the Martian atmosphere as a source of carbon and oxygen, despite the low pressure [37fe8723-ac2b-44da-8657-c889f18cc112].

In addition to using local materials, it is also essential to consider the worst-case scenarios that may arise when creating a sustainable atmosphere on Mars. 
One such scenario is the potential for a sudden loss of oxygen, which could have severe consequences for the health and well-being of the colonists [929597b1-4f2a-4c5a-a5d0-cee2fa3b8d77]. 
To mitigate this risk, it is essential to have a backup system in place, such as a device that can produce oxygen from the Martian atmosphere [a9b637ed-3450-48ea-b997-51a387d2ede1].

NASA's oxygen-generating experiment on Mars, known as MOXIE, is a prime example of a device that can produce oxygen from the Martian atmosphere [a9b637ed-3450-48ea-b997-51a387d2ede1]. 
MOXIE uses extreme heat to separate oxygen atoms from carbon dioxide molecules through electrolysis [a9b637ed-3450-48ea-b997-51a387d2ede1]. 
The device is the size of a conventional toaster and can produce up to 10 grams of oxygen per hour [a9b637ed-3450-48ea-b997-51a387d2ede1]. 
MOXIE was successfully tested on April 20, and the results showed that the device can produce oxygen from the Martian atmosphere [a9b637ed-3450-48ea-b997-51a387d2ede1].

The largest number of people that can be sustained by the atmosphere on Mars is a topic of ongoing research and debate. 
However, one estimate suggests that a population of 100,000 people could be sustained by a self-sufficient ecosystem on Mars [bb994a13-0446-4387-920b-4952ad50b036]. 
This estimate is based on the idea that a large enough population would be able to produce its own food, water, and energy, reducing the need for external resources [bb994a13-0446-4387-920b-4952ad50b036].

In conclusion, creating a sustainable atmosphere on Mars requires careful planning and consideration of various factors, including the equipment needed, worst-case scenarios, and the largest number of people that can be sustained by the atmosphere. 
Using local materials, such as cyanobacteria and Martian dust, can help to create a sustainable ecosystem on Mars.

[While human-made robotic creations explore Mars for signs of ancient life and to examine and test living conditions, plans for human habitation on Mars are taking on new dimensions.  A company called ABIBOO recently unveiled its plan to build the first Martian city.  The architecture firm Abybo has completed its plan to build the first Martian city.  The first large Martian town, called Nüwa City, can accommodate 250,000 people and will be built along and inside a massive rock.  Where people will have access to sunlight without being exposed to the risk of deadly cosmic radiation.  The Martian city ’ s massive lunar and Martian corridors, a suitable place for human habitation, could begin construction by 2054, and its first potential settlers are likely to move there by 2100.  As seen in the city ’ s renderings, the interiors of Noah ’ s luxurious rooms are spectacular regardless of whether the target for 2100 is realistic or not.  According to Abibo, the company is considering the necessary arrangements for how a Martian city will operate independently and meet its needs.  Sitting next to a cliff allows expats to live in private homes and other parts of the city to be used for farming, animal husbandry and energy supply, such as the use of solar arrays.  The goal is to build a sustainable civilization on the surface of Mars that can survive without the need for continuous transportation with Earth.  However, there is no exact plan for how this idea will work.  It will certainly be a difficult path to follow.  Atmospheric pressure on Mars is 1% of Earth ’ s pressure, extremely cold temperatures and high cosmic radiation, so that any skin exposed to it would burn.  Alfredo Muñoz, founder of Abibo Architecture Studio, said: “We had to do a lot of research based on computation and working with scientists to figure out what kind of conditions we would face on Mars.  "Obviously, we have to face challenges that are completely specific to the conditions on Mars, and one of them is the activity in gravity of only a third of Earth's gravity."  Despite these challenges, there is fortunately carbon dioxide and water on the surface of Mars.  Munoz added, “Water is one of the great advantages we have on Mars and helps us get the right materials for construction.  "Basically, with water and carbon dioxide, we can make carbon, and with carbon, we can make steel."  In addition, efforts such as the production of oxygen from the Martian atmosphere, which was first carried out by the Mars rover's MAXI instrument, have raised hopes of a stable presence on Mars.  Abybo's plan is to use only Martian material to build the first Martian settlement.  The New City of Noah on Mars project is part of a larger science program organized by the Mars Society in collaboration with SONet, an international team of scientists and academics.  Munoz explained, “What we learn as we move on to develop a fully sustainable city on Mars will give us good ideas and insights about what we can do differently on Earth. ”  Many people are interested in a stable human presence on Mars.  From Carl Sagan to Robert Zubrin, to Mars enthusiast Elon Musk, to SpaceX CEO.  While some estimates by Elon Musk seem too ambitious, there is a growing consensus that any future city on Mars will eventually have to be self-sufficient.  Otherwise, the people on the Red Planet will never be independent of Earth. Title: New Discovery to Survive on Mars
Content: A new experiment conducted by researchers at the University of Bremen in Germany has shown for the first time that a type of bacteria called Anabaena cyanobacteria, or blue and green algae, can thrive in Martian atmospheric conditions, allowing it to survive on Mars.  Astronauts on Mars need oxygen, water, food, and other consumables.  So this is a significant development, as it makes it very easy to create sustainable biological systems supporting life.  Scientists have found that despite the low pressure, cyanobacteria can use gases in the Martian atmosphere, at low pressure, as a source of carbon and nitrogen.  These materials can be replicated by suspending Martian dust in water, which makes it possible for them to be used as food for other living organisms.  The researchers believe that cyanobacteria could use gases in the Martian atmosphere, with low overall pressure, as a source of carbon and nitrogen.  Cyanobacteria, or jelbecks, are a group of organisms that, like plants, make different materials from sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide, and in scientific terms, they are called phototrophs.  Unlike plants, these organisms have tissue structures that increase life expectancy on Mars.

Title: Oxygen and hydrogen on Mars proposed to get from brine
Content: Scientists have developed a method for producing oxygen and hydrogen from a liquid saline solution in Martian lakes using electrolysis.  A feature of the experiment was the use of lead-ruthenium oxide as an electrocatalyst for oxygen production.  The production of oxygen using such an installation was 25 times more energy efficient than in the case of MOXIE, launched to the Red Planet as part of the Mars 2020 mission, and the size and weight of the device for life support based on the described technology will be less than that of analogues.  The article was published in the journal PNAS.  Conditions on Mars are far from favorable for humans: the atmosphere is rarefied and 95 percent consists of carbon dioxide, and temperature changes exceed 100 degrees Celsius with an average temperature of minus 63 degrees.  Therefore, colonization of the Red Planet is impossible without the creation of a life support system that would be able to provide people with oxygen for breathing and fuel (for example, hydrogen) for energy supply and, ideally, return flight.  To solve the first problem, NASA created MOXIE (Mars Oxygen ISRU Experiment) - an experimental installation for obtaining oxygen from atmospheric carbon dioxide by electrolysis.  To test the effectiveness of such a method in the field, the installation became part of the Mars Rover Perseverance, which was launched on July 30, 2020 as part of the Mars 2020 mission.  An alternative source of not only oxygen, but also hydrogen on Mars can be water, the first direct evidence of the existence of which on the red planet was obtained in 1971.  Particularly attractive for use in applications, however, would be the reserves of salt water, impurities in which would allow it to remain in a liquid state even at low temperature and pressure.  The first traces of such brine (liquid salt solution) with magnesium perchlorate as the main component were found on Mars in 2015, and in 2018, a reservoir with a diameter of about 20 kilometers was found under the polar ice of the planet, which could have been formed due to volcanic activity.  Later, planetary scientists confirmed that such lakes on Mars really exist and can be numerous.  Now Pralay Gayen (Pralay Gayen) from the University of Washington in St. Louis together with colleagues created an installation for obtaining oxygen and hydrogen from a saline solution close in composition and temperature to that in Martian lakes.  As a brine in the experiment, a solution of magnesium perchlorate in water with a concentration of 2.8 mol per liter was used, cooled to minus 36 degrees Celsius and blown by carbon dioxide (the latter played the role of the Martian atmosphere).  As an electrocatalyst for the production of oxygen, the scientists used lead-ruthenium oxide Pb2Ru2O7-δ, the effectiveness of which they previously showed for alkaline solutions.  The electrocatalyst for hydrogen production was platinum on activated carbon - the standard catalyst in this case, and a commercially produced anion-exchange membrane was used as a separator.  Installation diagram.  In the red region, oxygen is produced, in the blue - hydrogen.  Image source: Pralay Gayen et al. / PNAS In the course of the study, scientists showed that lead-ruthenium oxide as an electrocatalyst is indeed several times more effective than the ruthenium oxide commonly used in such installations.  After the behavior of the created installation was studied in a wide range of temperatures from − 36 to 21 degrees Celsius and saw no radical fluctuations in the efficiency and rate of production.  The current output of the experimental installation was 70 percent, and the energy efficiency was in the range between 36 and 70 percent (depending on the voltage applied to the plates).  In addition, the installation was resistant to degradation of the catalyst: scientists were not able to find traces of ruthenium in the solution after 300-minute operation of the device.  The rate of production of oxygen (blue dots) and hydrogen (red dots), depending on the density of the cathode current.  Image source: Pralay Gayen et al. / PNAS Also, the researchers compared the achieved rate of oxygen production with MOXIE values of 10-22 grams per hour: it turned out that with the same energy supply, the created installation produces 25 times more oxygen than the experiment on the Mars Rover “Perseverance ”.  To have the same rate of oxygen production as MOXIE, the device would have to have electrodes with an area of ​ ​ 28-62 square centimeters, and to ensure the vital activity of a sleeping and actively moving person, this parameter would have to be 375 and 1235 square centimeters, respectively.  At the same time, the mass and volume of the installation will be less than if you use the technology inherent in MOXIE.  Moreover, the developed method of obtaining oxygen does not require its subsequent purification, while during electrolysis in MOXIE, carbon monoxide is also produced, which must be filtered.  Dependence on the power consumption of the rate of oxygen production of the installation (blue line), as well as its capes and volume to ensure various modes of human life (black lines).  The blue dot is the power and rate of oxygen production at MOXIE.  Image source: Pralay Gayen et al. / PNAS Previously, we talked about another method of obtaining oxygen from carbon dioxide in the Martian atmosphere (like MOXIE): scientists proposed to do this using low-temperature plasma.  And what is the role of the Mars Rover “Perseverance ” in addition to checking the method of oxygen production, you can read in our material“ Mars, there and back ”.  Nikita Kozyrev

Title: A million people will live on Mars!
Content: Currently, there are almost 50 projects of manned flights to Mars.  The most grandiose of them belongs to the American engineer and entrepreneur Elon Musk, who plans to transport a million people to the Red Planet in the coming decades to create an independent civilization.  This idea seems absolutely fantastic – and meanwhile, the company Srace X, led by Mask, announced that very soon will begin the first flights of its space shuttles.  Go to the Red Planet!  At the International Astronomical Congress held in September 2016 in Mexico, the report of the engineer and entrepreneur made a real sensation.  According to Elon Musk, only the resettlement of a significant part of earthlings to Mars will save humanity from possible extinction.  Life on our planet can be interrupted by many factors: the explosion of a nearby supernova, superflares on the Sun, falling into a black hole, a global epidemic, a collision with a huge asteroid, a man-made disaster.  A large colony of people on another planet will ensure the continued existence of terrestrial civilization.  Why choose Mars?  Compared to other celestial bodies of the solar system, it is better suited for the possible life of earthlings.  The day here lasts 24 hours 37 minutes - that is, suitable for our residents and plants.  Gravity is much smaller than the earth, but is quite suitable for the normal functioning of the human body.  Finally, there is water – albeit in the form of polar ice caps, but it can be easily reached, and pieces of ice melt and use.  The rest of the planets of the solar system are practically unsuitable for such a mission: Mercury has extremely high surface temperatures during the day and very low at night, Venus has a too aggressive atmosphere, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune are mostly composed of liquefied gas.  The closest suitable celestial body to us is the Moon, but it depends entirely on the Earth and in the event of a space disaster may die with it.  Why is the number of one million people chosen?  According to experts, this is the minimum number of people so that their colony can become completely independent and develop.  It will have specialists of all the necessary professions, it will cope with possible diseases and epidemics, as well as ensure a stable natural population growth.  At first, the colonists will face the most difficult task - to turn the Red Planet into their home.  The set of actions to achieve this goal, Maek called the term “terraforming ” – that is, changing the conditions of life on another planet in such a way that they resemble earthly ones.  First of all, you need to melt a sufficient amount of ice at the south pole of the planet, since it will turn to the Sun in the summer, which means that it will be easier to do this than at the north pole.  The water accumulated here is enough to create an ocean several meters deep on the planet.  As the ice cap decreases, a chain reaction will begin - water vapor will begin to compact the atmosphere, which, in turn, will retain more solar heat, due to which the melting process will be more intense.  Technically, it can be launched using nuclear charges or placing laser devices over the south pole of Mars.  After liquid water appears on the planet, you need to start planting plants: initially it will be mosses, but later - vast forests that will saturate the atmosphere of Mars with oxygen (now it is 95% carbon dioxide).  According to Musk, the cultivation of “green lungs ” and the creation of a livable air without spacesuits will take from 300 to 1000 years.  But after that, the Red Planet can be considered terraformed, and people will choose where they live - on Mars or on Earth.  100 thousand flights Elon Maek listed the things and equipment that the first colonists needed.  First of all, these are devices for the production and conversion of energy - nuclear or space.  The most promising direction, the researchers of the company Srace X consider the delivery to Mars of a large number of light folding solar panels.  It will also require a huge amount of plants, both to create oxygen and to supply the settlers with food.  Until the atmosphere of the planet is formed properly, earthlings will need means of protection from solar radiation - after all, until this time, Martian cities will have to be under special domes.  First, the settlers will build small houses, then they will equip complexes, where there will be not only housing, but also schools, hospitals, shops, etc.  Experts Srace X calculated: one flight with the colonists should account for nine flights with payload.  It is based on a ship capable of carrying 100 passengers.  Thus, the total number of flights required to create a million colony on the Red Planet will be about 100 thousand (10 thousand - passenger flights, 90 thousand - cargo).  Elon Maek has already announced that the first expeditions for the delivery of goods should begin at the end of 2022.  By 2035, spacecraft will be built capable of reaching the Red Planet in 80 days, and a million colonists will arrive on Mars within the next few decades.  The main obstacle to the implementation of such a large-scale project, according to Musk and his team, is the high cost of a flight to the Red Planet.  In fact, it is steadily declining.  In 1989, the US national aerospace agency YABA estimated sending astronauts to Mars at $450 billion.  It was assumed that there will be from four to six earthlings — that is, each place was estimated at about $100 billion.  But already in 2004, the same agency reduced the cost of the project nine times — to $50 billion.  Thus, the flight of one person would cost a little more than 10 billion dollars.  This figure is still too high, but the trend towards its decline is clearly visible, and therefore such a task can be solved.  Elon Maek believes that the optimal amount for a flight of one person should be 500 thousand dollars – this is the approximate cost of a middle-class house in a good place.  Moreover, people should understand that they will become real space pioneers, the first permanent residents of another planet – and therefore must pay for their flight themselves.  Opinions of economists and psychologists are unambiguous: only in the United States there are at least a million people who will agree to pay such money for an unprecedented space travel.  But how to reduce the cost of flying each person from 10 billion to 500 thousand dollars, that is, 20 thousand times?  Elon Mayek knows the answer to that question.  Rocket from a private company Team plan Srace X works in two directions.  The first of these is the creation of spacecraft, each of which will be able to carry at least 100 people.  The company Ilona Mask has a successful experience in the construction of devices of a new type.  The engineer and entrepreneur himself says that the huge cost of missiles is primarily a consequence of the lack of competition and the presence of a huge number of subcontractors.  NASA constantly entrusts the execution of its orders only to a few companies.  For example, ULA (United Launch Alliance), a joint venture owned by Boeing and Lockheed Martin, regularly performs missions of the space agency and the US Department of Defense, but at the same time receives more for each launch than anyone else in the world.  Under the pretext of national security, the system of government orders in this area is completely opaque, and the task of many companies is not to reduce the cost of the spacecraft, but to make it more expensive for their own benefit.  In turn, having received the order, large companies transfer it in parts to small subcontractors, who also inflate prices.  But the main thing is that in the absence of competition, there is no need to invent something new!  As a result, the technology of modern spacecraft at best dates back to the 1990s, and the costs of their production and launch are declining extremely slowly.  SpaceX was the first company to start working on a fundamentally different scheme.  Not fulfilling an order, but creating your own device, cheaper and more reliable, which can then be offered to space agencies and organizations.  The company was founded in 2002 with the personal funds of Elon Musk, received from the development and operation of the largest electronic payment system in the United States.  The company created its first rocket, called the Falcon 1 (translated from English “falcon ”).  The two-stage vehicle and its engine were made by Space X workers without the help of intermediaries.  The first three launches ended in accidents.  But the fourth flight, which took place in 2008, was successful.  A cargo detachment simulation was conducted (it remained in the rocket so as not to increase the amount of space debris), and the first stage made a safe landing.  At the same time, Elon Maek, who was in the Mission Control Center at Cape Canaveral, heard the clap, ran out into the street in despair - he thought that this test ended in an explosion.  But it turned out that the sound was caused by the passage of the disconnected first stage of the rocket sound barrier.  The successful launch of the Falcon 1 cost $7.9 million – three times cheaper than the best alternative indicators. Title: Perseverance makes oxygen on Mars for the first time outside of Earth - Technology
Content: NASA said today that the Mars rover "perseverance" continues to make history, yesterday successfully converted carbon dioxide into oxygen in the Martian atmosphere, the first successful oxygenation on another planet.  "Turning carbon dioxide into oxygen on Mars is a very important first step," said Jim Reuter, NASA's deputy director of space technology missions.  Perseverance uses the Mars Oxygen In situ Resource Utilization Experiment (MOXIE) built in front of its right and designed by MIT to produce oxygen. This car battery-sized gold box uses electricity and chemical properties to break down carbon dioxide molecules and successfully produce oxygen.  Since carbon dioxide is composed of 1 carbon atom and 2 oxygen atoms, the by-product of MOXIE's oxygen production is carbon monoxide.  MOXIE not only can produce oxygen for future astronauts to breathe on Mars, but also need not drag a large amount of oxygen from Earth as a propellant in the future, which is expected to pave the way for future human exploration.  MOXIE ’ s first score was to produce 5 grams of oxygen, equivalent to the amount an astronaut needs to breathe for 10 minutes of normal activity.  MOXIE was originally designed to produce up to 10 grams of oxygen per hour, and engineers will now conduct more experiments to try to increase production.  MOXIE is made of heat-resistant materials such as nickel alloys, which can withstand high temperatures of 800 degrees Celsius. The thin gold coating on the top ensures that it will not cause damage to the car ’ s Perseverance.  MIT engineer Michael Hecht said the one-ton version of MOXIE could produce about 25 tons of oxygen needed for a rocket to launch from Mars.  Since 96% of the Martian atmosphere is carbon dioxide, producing oxygen from the Martian atmosphere is much more feasible than extracting ice from the Martian surface. Title: NASA ’ s Mars Rover Perseverance will turn CO2 into oxygen on the planet
Content: NASA ’ s Perseverance rover will turn CO2 into oxygen on the planet 09.08.2020, 20: 30, Miscellaneous NASA ’ s Perseverance rover, launched on July 30, equipped with a variety of advanced technological systems, will try to convert CO2 on the surface of the planet into oxygen.  This is a very important step towards detecting signs of life on Mars.  In translation, the name Perseverance means perseverance, perseverance.  The device was developed by specialists from the Jet Propulsion Laboratory of the California Institute of Technology.  In order to generate oxygen on the Red Planet, the rover was equipped with the experimental Mars Oxygen In-situ Resource Utilization Experiment or MOXIE.  The device was developed by scientists at the University of Massachusetts to produce from the atmosphere of the planet necessary for life gas.  Oxygen is very cumbersome for space transportation to Mars.  Experts doubt that the astronauts will be able to deliver it in the right number for people and refueling ships.  This problem will try to cope with the device MOXIE.

Title: Secrets of the Fourth Planet
Content: 2050.  Humanity has finally become an interplanetary species, establishing a colony on Mars that is home to about a million people — more than Amsterdam or Athens.  This is not the beginning of a new science fiction novel or the plot of the film.  This is a vision of the future that Elon Musk recently shared.  The entrepreneur often paints the most fantastic scenarios, but one cannot blame him: it is not only him who is drawn to Mars.  Unfriendly neighbor Mars is not the most hospitable world, if you compare it with the Earth.  The force of gravity here is only 37.5% of the earth ’ s.  The temperature on the surface ranges from freezing -153 ° C to comfortable + 20 ° C.  However, a thin, unsuitable for humans atmosphere, consisting mainly of carbon dioxide, nitrogen and argon, is not able to effectively trap heat from sunlight.  If you were standing on the Martian equator at noon, your feet would have a temperature of + 24 ° C and your head would have a temperature of 0 ° C.  In addition, the pressure on the red planet is much lower – even at the top of Everest on Earth, it is 50 times greater than on the surface of Mars.  However, these worlds have a lot in common.  Beneath our feet is solid land, the area of which is comparable to the land area on our planet, although Mars is about half its size.  The duration of the day, which is called soles, is 24.6 hours, and close to the Earth's angle of inclination of the axis of rotation (23.5 for the Earth and 25.2 for Mars) provides the world with pronounced seasons, which, however, last longer than ours.  For example, spring in the northern hemisphere lasts as much as 194 solas - this is the longest season on the planet.  But the main similarity of the planets remains in the distant past.  Numerous evidence points to the fact that Mars used to be warmer, had a denser atmosphere, and its surface was covered with water - the cradle of intelligent life on our home planet.  That ’ s why researchers are looking so closely at this harsh world.  The chances of life on Mars are slim.  For example, in 2018, a group of European scientists found signs of the existence of a liquid lake hidden 1.5 km below the surface of the southern polar glacier.  Microbes may exist in such a reservoir, but this is only a hypothesis that is difficult to test.  Therefore, scientists rely on the search for signs of the existence of a past life.  It may not sound so exciting, but even such a find will be colossal.  Otherwise, we will face a much larger scientific mystery: why the Earth gave life, and the neighboring world with the right conditions - not.  The race for Martian life began in the 19th century.  In 1877, the Italian astronomer Giovanni Schiaparelli looked through the telescope Mars, which no one imagined, and even made a map.  It depicted seas and continents, as well as an extensive network of lines, which the astronomer called channels.  The word itself prompted the idea of ​ ​ the man-made origin of these objects.  It was later established that the channels were an optical illusion, but the idea of the existence of the Martian civilization that built them was picked up by others.  Astronomers such as American Percival Lowell or Frenchman Camille Flammarion believed in the habitability of the Red Planet, and science fiction writers such as Edgar Burroughs and H.G. Wells.  Of course, this theory was not accepted by everyone, but it was not possible to test it for a long time.  That all changed in the 1950s.  After the launch of the first Soviet satellite in 1957 and the start of the space race, the views of the USSR and the United States quickly rushed beyond the Earth ’ s orbit and even the Moon.  Already in the 1960s, the first automatic interplanetary stations rushed to the Red Planet.  No one thought about landing or orbiters at that time.  AMS sent to other worlds had to fly by, trying to take as many pictures as possible and send them to Earth.  But this task was not easy either.  The first attempt to send a research apparatus to the Red Planet was made by the Soviet Union in 1960, but it, like many others after it, failed.  Soviet devices died, not having time to leave the orbit of the Earth, at best broke down in flight to Mars.  In 1964, NASA entered the game, but its debut was unsuccessful.  The second attempt was successful.  Mariner 4 arrived safely on Mars in 1965.  It flew about 10 thousand km above the surface of the planet and sent 22 photos to Earth.  These were the first images of Mars from such a short distance.  There were no channels on them, but scientists saw the craters decorating the Martian earth, and confirmed that the atmosphere of the planet consists of carbon dioxide.  NASA has been successful ever since.  Until the end of the decade, the agency launched two more AMS, which managed to take two hundred photos, as well as carry out measurements of the surface and temperature of Mars.  The first spacecraft to make a soft landing on Mars was the Soviet Mars-3, but on the surface it worked for a few seconds The Soviet Union caught up with the Americans only in 1971, but by that time the ambitions of local scientists and engineers had grown.  Just flying over the surface wasn ’ t enough.  In 1971, the Soviet Union sent to the Red Planet at once two AMS - "Mars-2" and "Mars-3", which included both orbiters and lander.  These missions have been successful.  Orbiters have been orbiting the planet for months, transmitting data.  As for the landers, one crashed during the landing, and the second successfully inscribed his name in history.  "Mars-3" was the first device to make a soft landing on the red planet, even if it worked in a matter of seconds.  1971 proved to be a fruitful year for the study of the fourth planet.  That year, the American orbiter Mariner 9 arrived, which not only took thousands of photos and made a map of 85% of its surface, but also helped to see the main attractions of Mars.  For example, data from Mariner 9 helped establish the height of Olympus, the tallest volcano in the solar system, which rises 25 km and the diameter of the base is 600 km.  And the NASA research apparatus helped to estimate the scale of the Mariner Valley - the famous system of canyons, which stretches for 4 thousand km along the Martian equator and crashes 7 km deep into the surface of the planet.  The system, named after the probe, is four times deeper and five times longer than the Grand Canyon on Earth.  The next breakthrough in the study of Mars was made only in 1976, when NASA delivered there two AMS - "Viking 1" and "Viking 2".  Like the Soviet Mars, they were equipped with orbiters and landers, but the Vikings were more successful.  They successfully placed in orbit and landed on the surface of the planet, having worked for more than one year.  The Viking 1 lander fell silent only in 1982, and even then after an erroneous command from Earth.  During this time, they replenished the Martian photo archive with tens of thousands of images, but most importantly - they conducted the first field experiments to search for traces of life.  Alas, they did not give a convincing "yes" or a definite "no", but still it was a breakthrough, since previously Mars was studied on the principle of "look, but do not touch".  "Vikings" involuntarily added fuel to the fire of the myth of the Martian civilization, when one of the orbiters sent a curious picture.  It showed a pile of stones, one of which was strikingly reminiscent of a human face.  NASA researchers immediately realized that this is a game of light and shadow, but the impressionable public began to build theories about the remains of an ancient Martian city that rests underground.  The tradition of looking for the usual forms in photos of the Red Planet is still alive today, and those who want to constantly find rodents and insects in the pictures.  But these are just illusions.  Face on Mars.  This image, taken in the AMC "Viking 1" 1976, refreshed the myth of the existence of a developed Martian civilization After the "Vikings" study of the red planet for many years stalled.  For two decades, the US and the USSR, and subsequently Russia, continued to send mechanical researchers, but the attempts were mostly unsuccessful.  A new breakthrough occurred in the second half of the 1990s.  In 1997, NASA delivered the Mars Global Surveyor orbiter to Mars, which helped make a revolutionary discovery: somewhere under the surface of a dead planet, water can still flow, the hunt for which continues to this day.  In the same year, the Pathfinder landed on the surface, which has not happened since the time of the Vikings.  But much more interesting was the cargo that Pathfinder brought with him. Title: Astronomers: Venus may be habitable until mysterious event occurs
Content: 2019-09-21 15: 46 [News / Roundup] Michael Way, a scholar at NASA ’ s Goddard Space Science Research Center, presented his recent research at the 2019 European Planetary Science Conference (EPSC-DPS) in Geneva, which shows that Venus may maintain habitable conditions for billions of years, but a mysterious event has suddenly changed the planet ’ s environment.  According to CNN, Venus, like other planets in the solar system, formed 4.5 billion years ago. Its current atmosphere is full of toxic gases and is 90 times thicker than the Earth's atmosphere, and the surface temperature is 864 degrees Fahrenheit (about 462 degrees Celsius), enough to melt lead, so that Venus is a place of death.  But Michael Weiss compared Venus to five climate simulations, each of which showed that Venus could support liquid water and temperate climates for at least 3 billion years, with temperatures as high as 122 degrees Fahrenheit (50 degrees Celsius) and as low as 68 degrees Fahrenheit (20 degrees Celsius), until some cause of release of carbon dioxide from rocks 750 million to 700 million years ago changed Venus ’ s climate.  Astronomers in the past thought that Venus was too close to the Sun to maintain liquid water on the surface, but all the simulations created by the Michael Weiss team found that the surface temperature of Venus allows liquid water to persist.  These simulations show that Venus underwent a rapid cooling phase after its formation, and the atmosphere began to fill with carbon dioxide, but if it is similar to Earth's evolution, the atmospheric carbon dioxide will be absorbed by the surface silicates, and the composition of the atmosphere gradually becomes a combination of nitrogen and a small amount of carbon dioxide and methane, providing stability.  However, a mysterious event about 700 million years ago caused carbon dioxide from the surface rocks of Venus to escape into the atmosphere and not be absorbed back, and such a large amount of carbon dioxide caused the greenhouse effect to get out of control.  Researchers believe that the mysterious event may be volcanic activity, because magma releases carbon dioxide into the atmosphere, and as the magma cools, the carbon dioxide can no longer be absorbed back to the surface, but the reasoning needs to be further proved.  Michael Wei said that the importance of this research is to re-understand the "Venus region", where the planet is still possible to maintain liquid water and temperate climate, and in the future, we will continue to explore the mysterious events in the end, the cooling rate after the formation of Venus, whether there is real water on the surface, carbon dioxide only once or more issues.
