Title: There is no life in the closest star system to Earth.
Content: Alpha Centauri made a harsh verdict on whether there is life on exoplanets Alpha Centauri tried to find out American astrophysicists.  Scientists from the Georgia Institute of Technology and NASA conducted studies of the celestial bodies of the nearest star system to us.  Alpha Centauri is the closest to the Sun and historically the most known to mankind triple star system.  In the night sky it can be seen with the naked eye.  It was from there that scientists and science fiction writers expected to meet space caravans of aliens.  Astrophysicists from the Georgia Institute of Technology, together with NASA experts, conducted a series of studies of the star system in the hope of finding inhabited worlds.  With the help of modeling the orbits of the proposed exoplanets and the influence on them of the gravity of the three luminaries of Alpha Centauri, they were able to establish that the development of complex life depends mainly on the stability of the tilt of the axis of rotation of the proposed planet.  This largely depends on the stability of the climate, allowing the development of living organisms.  Our Earth in this sense can be considered almost a standard.  The axis is slightly inclined relative to the plane of the orbit and its oscillations are minimized due to the gravity of our satellite.  “If we didn ’ t have the moon, the tilt of the Earth ’ s axis could change by about 60 degrees.  Perhaps then the Earth would look like Mars, ” says study leader Billy Quarles.  Comparison of the history of the formation of the Earth and Mars, according to scientists, allows you to visualize the theory of the origin, and then the preservation of life.  The axis of rotation of our planet is relatively stable and inclined by 22-24 degrees.  But Mars, without such a large satellite balancer, every 2 million years changes the inclination of its axis from 10 to 60 degrees.  As a result, the condensate of the already rarefied Martian atmosphere from the white caps at the poles turns into a cold ice belt of the equator.  In such extreme conditions, the planet is simply not able to support the evolution of complex life forms.  That's the system Alpha Centravra scientists have made a harsh verdict - it is highly likely uninhabited.  There's good news, though.  According to astrophysicists, even if suitable exoplanets are not found near the Sun, they can be a little further, in other star systems, the number of which in the universe is infinite.  Andrey Sidorenko.  TV Center.

Title: Fantasies and reality. Which of the world powers will be the first to write their Martian chronicles
Content: In the story, Soviet cosmonauts go to the aid of aliens who have suffered an accident near Mars.  Starring Otar Koberidze (left) and Boris Borisenok / A shot from the film “Dream towards ” / 1963 Roscosmos this year plans to study the question of how to change the human body at the level of genetic engineering for flights into deep space.  The project will involve the Institute of Biomedical Problems of the Russian Academy of Sciences (RAS), the Federal Biomedical Agency, as well as medical institutions of the Ministry of Health.  What is happening in the industry today and how to return our country to unconditional leadership in space, was understood by “Evening Moscow ”.  I think Yuri Gagarin would be disappointed if, having looked into the relatively near future, he found out that his country, which opened the door to a new world for humanity, stopped on the threshold and with incomprehensible politeness skips ahead of competitors.  On April 16, when we were still not cool off from the lush celebrations associated with astronautics Day, NASA signed a contract worth almost $3 billion, entrusting Space X with the development of the HLS Starship lander, which should take two astronauts to the moon, and a week later bring them home.  If such an agreement had been concluded in our country, it would have been a much more valuable contribution to the continuation of the Gagarin case than all the articles and films about the first cosmonaut taken together.  It is planned that Starship will replace the existing space transportation systems Falcon 9, Falcon Heavy and Dragon, which are also created by Space X.  The strategic goal of Starship goes beyond Earth and lunar orbits and involves a manned flight to Mars.  With the modernization of the ship in the future, its versions will be able to make interstellar flights.  One of the quick and obvious opportunities to cover costs is commercial suborbital flights within the Earth over long distances.  A hundred years ago, Mars was the cherished dream of the Russian man.  Red Count Alexei Tolstoy wrote a wonderful story about the Red Planet "Aelita".  Engineer Friedrich Zander, whose name is one of the Moscow streets, formulated a romantic motto: "Forward to Mars!"  Colonization of Mars was part of the schedule of space conquest, compiled by Konstantin Tsiolkovsky.  According to the main theorist of astronautics, the research base on the moon was supposed to appear in 2015.  The industrial development of Mars, as well as Venus and Mercury, is attributed to the sky-high distance - 2700.  In the atmosphere of romantic dreams and technological challenges, the genius of Sergei Korolev was formed, who in the early 1960s, even before the Americans, sent 5 spacecraft to Mars.  The first launches ended in failure, but in 1962, a Soviet satellite first approached the Red Planet and conducted important experiments.  Unfortunately, our dream of Mars has moved to America.  Previously, the descendants of the conquerors of the West looked at Mars with childish ignorance — like the way American tourists walk around Paris.  In 1938, a radio play based on Wells ’ book War of the Worlds caused widespread panic.  But now three American spacecraft are operating in the orbit of Mars, and two rovers are on the surface.  Elon Musk ’ s ambitions have matured in a competitive atmosphere.  In addition to NASA, plans for flights to Mars are hatched by private companies Lockheed Martin, Boeing, Sierra Nevada Corporation. frame from the film "The Martian" / 2015 The owner and chief engineer of the company Space X Elon Musk promises the first manned flight to Mars in 2024-2026 years.  And by 2050, according to his vision, a million earthlings will move to Mars.  Architectural bureaus are already creating projects of Martian dwellings, physiologists are thinking about the Martian diet, and biochemists are making plans to change the Martian atmosphere to acceptable parameters.  Almost inevitably, terrestrial settlers on Mars will feed on insects that will provide them with proteins.  Europeans to withstand such a diet will be extremely difficult, so with a high probability to master Mars will come from Asia.  Elon Musk understands that an expedition to Mars, which, under optimal ballistic conditions, will take 6 months in one direction, carries a huge risk.  The first colonists clearly will not be able to quickly (and perhaps never) return to Earth.  Musk said, “Are you ready to die?  If there is no problem with that, you are a great candidate! ”  However, the businessman himself is not going to Mars.  There is no doubt that when the time comes, there will be no escape from those who want it.  The first analysis of the expedition to Mars was made immediately after World War II by Werner von Braun, who at that time was sitting without a job, hiding the SS uniform and waiting for an invitation to the United States.  But these were theoretical quirks.  At the beginning of the space age, thanks to energy and dedication, the Queen of the USSR was the undisputed leader in interplanetary flights, having carried out a number of unique expeditions to the nearest celestial objects.  Unfortunately, gradually our attraction to the stars weakened.  I think this is largely due to the fact that cosmonautics ceased to serve as a propaganda argument in the dispute between the two superpowers.  Our interplanetary plans are modest.  2022 is a joint mission with Europe to Mars on our Proton M rocket and with the Russian Kazachok landing platform.  In 2021, we are going to launch the Luna-25 spacecraft with a lander.  The last flight of the machine to the moon took place in 1976.  Then there will be more machines.  And in 2030, Dmitry Rogozin promises a manned expedition to the moon.  Photo: twitter.com / roscosmos The success of Russian plans depends on whether it will be possible to bring to mind the family of missiles "Angara".  There are doubts about this, if only for the reason that work on “Angara ” has been underway since the 1980s.  One has to wonder how in five years Elon Musk managed to put into orbit the Falcon 9 rocket, which was trusted by space crews.  In addition, Elon Musk built a private spaceport Boca Chica in Texas, spending tens of times less money than we threatened on the “East ”.  And for some reason it was without astronomical embezzlement and avalanche of criminal cases...  Mars in the last decade has been the main object of attraction for spacecraft.  Currently, in the vicinity of the red planet are just three Earth apparatus.  The American mission Perseverance (Perseverance), during which on April 19 (a week after our Cosmonautics Day) on Mars for the first time flew a jet helicopter Ingenuity (Inventiveness) - 3 meters and 40 seconds of flight.  As well as a satellite from the UAE and a Chinese ship.  By the way, the Ingenuity helicopter did not become a pioneer in terms of independent movement in the atmosphere of another planet.  The first such cruise was made in 1985 by the Soviet apparatus Vega-1 in the atmosphere of Venus.  But this era has long passed...  The cost of the Perseverance mission is $2 billion.  If we take into account that the financing of the expedition was started 7 years ago, in terms of money it is quite possible for Roscosmos, whose annual budget even now, after several drops in the ruble, is equal to just $2 billion.  The scientific potential of Russian cosmonautics, despite all the problems, is still high and allows us to swing at the most difficult tasks.  Where are you, romantics?  Ilona Mask is often called an adventurer who feeds the public with chimerical promises.  Without in any way acting as his lawyer, I note that it is precisely such accusations that ordinary people threw at the great inventors and innovators.  From Archimedes to Tsiolkovsky, they walked in eccentrics, and many, like Korolev and Babilov, were innocent victims.  The phenomenon of Elon Musk is a contradictory mosaic, but for us two fundamental points are important.  First: Musk fuels public interest in science and serves as a magnet for attracting ambitious and curious young people to research.  We would like such popularizers, but they are not visible on our horizon.  And the second.  Elon Musk is the first private trader who came with his ideas in space.  This is a mandatory stage in the development of the industry, but in Russia, unfortunately, entrepreneurs do not look at the stars.  No one even went to space tourists.  They prefer to lie in a hammock on the grass at home.  Elon Musk / Photo: twitter.com / mfame _ guru Incidentally, 20 years ago Elon Musk came to Russia twice, but he was not yet a billionaire. Our officials considered the businessman a frivolous person, because they were confident that only the state could deal with space. Title: Air & Space (USA): a million people on Mars? It is possible. But the colonists will have to change their diet and learn to eat crickets – Rambler
Content: Air & Space (USA): a million people on Mars? It is possible.  But the colonists will have to change their diet and learn to eat crickets A self-sufficient population of a million people could appear on Mars within 100 years.  At first, 12 people will land there, after which numerous spacecraft should begin transporting passengers about once every 26 months.  But will humans be able to have children on Mars?  And how to solve the problem with nutrition?  A sustainable and self-sufficient population of one million people could appear on Mars within 100 years, according to a new study with modeling elements conducted by Kevin Cannon and Daniel Britt of the University of Central Florida.  In their study, they relied on a plan drawn up by Elon Musk of SpaceX.  To begin with, he planned a landing on the Red Planet of 12 people, after which numerous spacecraft should begin to carry passengers, from 100 to 200 people per flight, which will be carried out at each opportunity approximately once every 26 months.  Population growth will be ensured both by immigration and by the birth of children on Mars.  Cannon and Britt in their study show that four of the five main "consumables" necessary for Martian settlements (energy, water, oxygen and building materials) can be mined on the surface of Mars in sufficient quantities.  On Mars, only food can not be obtained from raw materials.  So how do we solve the food problem?  The authors propose to grow plants, breed insects and engage in meat cattle breeding of cellular genetic direction.  In the past, it was suggested to grow plants quite often, but it is very important to plant high-calorie crops in order to feed so many people.  Breeding insects is also very useful, as it will give a large number of calories per unit area.  For these purposes, homemade crickets are best suited, and they are already used in some cereal bars.  Protein-rich foods can also be obtained from cells grown in bioreactors.  Interestingly, fish on Mars will be more popular than cage-grown meat, because this culture can be preserved at lower temperatures (about 20 degrees Celsius), while warm-blooded animal cells need 37 degrees Celsius.  To me such ideas and extrapolations seem very intriguing.  But life on Mars may not be as easy as it seems, even if people will enjoy the fruits of technological progress.  Growing plants in Martian soil will be very difficult, because there are large amounts of chloric acid salt and other chemicals in sediments.  The same authors conducted another study on this topic, using soil close in composition to Martian.  Now: their plants died quickly, and earthworms suffocated in this land.  Biological factors must also be taken into account.  It is far from clear whether people will be able to easily give birth to children on Mars, because Martian gravity is only 38% of Earth ’ s.  The human body adapts to earthly conditions, and when the constant physical quantity is two-thirds less than usual, unexpected complications may occur.  Martian farmers may face other problems, including unfamiliar plant diseases that will destroy crops, causing hunger among the settlers.  The upside is that efficient and sustainable food production technologies on Mars can benefit many more people adapting to climate change on Earth, and therefore can prove invaluable to our entire civilization.  Musk ’ s idea of a million people living on Mars is unlikely to materialize in the near future.  But it ’ s becoming more real as NASA ’ s independent planetary protection watchdog recently issued new recommendations that could lead to a relaxation of sterility requirements when landing in certain areas of Mars where local life is unlikely to exist.  If people come to the Red Planet in passenger spacecraft to settle there, they will most likely settle in these places.  Air & Space (USA)

Title: Earth is attacking. What will China, the United States and the Emirates look for on Mars?
Content: On the night of July 15, the UAE will send its first orbiter to Mars.  Also in July, the launch of their research missions planned by China and the United States.  What and how they will look for on the red planet, says Focus October 30, 1938, the United States was engulfed in mass panic.  People called newspapers and police stations, believing that the Earth had been attacked by the Martians.  This reaction was caused by the radio play of the novel by H.G. Wells "War of the Worlds", which the audience took at face value.  After almost 100 years, we know for sure that the Martians will not arrive, because they do not exist, and in general - if there is life on the Red Planet, then microscopic and well hidden.  Earth has been conquering Mars with varying success for more than half a century.  This year, humanity will make an unprecedented breakthrough towards the Red Planet: three countries will send research missions to it at once.  Hope Country: United Arab Emirates Start date: July 15, 2020  Arrival time: February 2021 Type of research vehicle: orbiter Mission duration: 1 Martian year (687 Earth days) Mission objectives: to provide a holistic picture of the Martian atmosphere and weather The times when space exploration was the monopoly of superpowers are long past.  Today, more and more countries and private companies are looking to the stars, and the United Arab Emirates seems to want to be among the pioneers.  The UAE may become the first Arab state to launch an interplanetary mission.  The UAE did not pursue a more ambitious goal of landing on the planet – in the history of Mars exploration, there were far more failed attempts to do this than successful ones.  Preferably confined to an orbital probe.  The research apparatus with a mass of 1.3 tons will make a full orbit around the planet every 55 hours, then approaching it for 20 thousand km, then moving away to 43 thousand.  On board, it will carry infrared and ultraviolet spectrometers, as well as a camera that can not only take pictures, but also shoot video in 4K resolution.  With the help of these tools, Arab scientists want to carefully study the Martian atmosphere, to understand the mechanisms due to which it loses much needed oxygen on Earth.  In addition, they are interested in the weather systems of Mars.  Thanks to the features of the orbit of the probe, they will be able to observe how the weather changes throughout the entire Martian days (24 hours).  38 minutes of Earth time) at one point or another on the planet.  This year, the UAE is sending a probe to Mars, and in 100 years they want to build a city there Data that researchers will receive during the mission will not settle in closed laboratories.  The UAE plans to share them with colleagues from 200 scientific institutions around the world in the hope that the new information will help to better understand the history and mechanisms of functioning of the Martian climate.  However, the Arab mission to Mars does not only pursue scientific goals.  Its organizers hope that the conquest of the neighboring planet will inspire young people and help educate a new generation of scientists and engineers - specialists who can prove that the Emirates is more than just a country with rich oil deposits.  “It is a matter of the future of the UAE and our survival, ” said Omran Sharaf, the head of the mission.  In the view of local scientists, Mars does play a significant role in the future, and perhaps in the survival of the state.  After all, they plan to build an entire city on the Red Planet within the next century.  With an eye on all this, it is obvious that for their first "scout" they chose the most appropriate name - "Al Amal", which means "Hope".  Question to Heaven Country: China Start date: July 23, 2020  Arrival time: February 2021 Type of research vehicle: Mars rover, orbiter and lander Planned mission duration: Rover - 90 sols (equal to 92 Earth days), probe - 1 Martian year (687 Earth days) Mission objectives: study of the magnetosphere, ionosphere and atmosphere of Mars, mapping of terrain, observation of dust storms, study of the composition of rocks and soil, mineral distribution Another debutant in the conquest of Mars will be China.  Local scientists decided to act on a much larger scale than their Arab counterparts.  They will send a rover, landing and orbiters to Mars.  The mission was named Tianwen-1 (Questions to Heaven) after a poem written more than 2,000 years ago.  Each machine has its own task.  For example, the probe, which will be located in the orbit of Mars, will study the geological structure and natural conditions of the planet, as well as transmit data to Earth.  On the lander lies perhaps the most important part of the mission - the actual delivery of equipment to Mars.  This process takes about seven minutes, but this time period is called “seven minutes of nightmare ”.  It depends on China whether it will have its own research apparatus on another planet or it will simply deliver a heap of expensive, high-tech garbage there.  China will name all missions to study other planets Tianwen ("Questions to the Sky") - after the ancient work of the poet Qu Yuan Landing will be broken down into four stages.  First, the aerodynamic brake will slow the device from 4.8 km / s to 460 m / s.  Then the parachute will open, which will reduce the speed to 95 m / s., and then reverse engines will go in the course.  They'll slow the lander down to 3.5 m / s.  The final stage of braking starts at a mark of only 100 m from the surface of the planet.  Ideally, it will end with a soft landing, after which the rover will smoothly move to the surface of the planet.  The first Chinese rover will be equipped with several scientific instruments, including a GPR.  With the help of this device, he will be able to literally look underground.  Earlier this year, this tool helped archaeologists without excavation to make a map of the ancient Roman city, which for many years rests underground.  The rover will not have to search for lost settlements, but he will be able to examine underground geological objects with the help of GPR.  As in the case of the Arab mission to Mars, the Chinese pursue not only scientific goals.  First, it will be a major test of the country ’ s technological achievements.  Secondly, it has a strong reputation subtext.  China already has a successful lunar program – in January last year, its Chang ’ e 4 research apparatus was the first in history to make a soft landing on the far side of the moon.  In early summer, the country launched the last satellite in its global navigation system, which will compete with the American GPS.  Conquering Mars will strengthen China ’ s position as the world ’ s leading space power.  Perseverance and resourcefulness Country: USA Start date: July 30, 2020  Arrival time: February 18, 2021 Type of research vehicle: Rover and helicopter Planned duration of the mission: 1 Martian year (687 Earth days) Mission objectives: search for traces of the existence of life in the past, collect samples, prepare for future missions with the participation of people In the conquest of Mars, the United States is the leader.  The local aerospace agency NASA was the first to deliver a research probe to the Red Planet, the first to land a lander there that lasted longer than a few seconds, its rovers were the first to wheel on the surface of another world.  Today, three of its probes orbit Mars, two more research vehicles are working on the surface of the planet, and soon they will be joined by another.  NASA will send a new rover Perseverance (“Perseverance ”).  The American space agency has a tradition, according to which the names for rovers come up with schoolchildren.  NASA did not deviate from it this time.  The name of the rover "Perseverance" was born in the head of seventh-grader Alexander Mazer, who believed that this feature of human character should be immortalized in it.  In an essay in which the student explained his choice, he noted that in the conquest of Mars, humanity can wait for many difficulties, but it is perseverance that will not allow him to give up and help move towards the goal, no matter what.  However, Perseverance can boast not only a loud name.  Despite its resemblance to Curiosity, which has been traveling on Mars since 2012, the new rover has the most modern technical equipment.  NASA calls Perseverance the most advanced of the rovers he created.  "There is every reason to believe that in the coming years Mars and all its secrets will become more and more understandable to the inhabitants of the Earth" Carl Sagan, astronomer He is equipped with a number of scientific tools that will help him monitor important meteorological indicators (humidity, temperature, wind speed, etc.), recognize the chemical composition of materials on the surface, consider objects the size of a grain of salt and look for organic compounds that would indicate the existence of Martian life in the past or have been exposed. impact of water. Content: South Korea ’ s Samsung Group Vice President Lee Jae-yong was sentenced to two and a half years in prison in January for bribing former President Park Geun-hye ’ s confidants.  As the government and business sectors recently asked the government to pardon Li, he appeared in court again on Thursday (22) on charges of fraud and stock price manipulation, the first appearance of the company after about three months.  According to South Korean media reports, 52-year-old Li Jae-rong dressed in a black suit and white shirt to appear in court.  Lee Jae-yong appeared in court 10 minutes before the start of the trial. In addition to answering that the judge did not want a jury, Lee Jae-yong remained silent.  Prosecutors alleged that in the process of promoting the merger of Samsung C & T and Cheil Industries in 2015, Samsung executives deliberately published false information to raise the share price of First Woven and depress the share price of Samsung Property in order to boost Li Zaihong ’ s acquisition of shares after First Woven was acquired by Samsung Property to become the largest shareholder and strengthen his influence on the Samsung Group.  If Li is convicted of fraud and stock price manipulation, his sentence may be increased.  Lee has so far served half of his sentence, which is 15 months.  South Korea ’ s government faces growing pressure from business and opposition parties to pardon Lee.  Utilizing Lee Jae-yong ’ s global network will help safeguard South Korea ’ s vaccine supply, according to the Federation of South Korean Industries.  Park Jen, a conservative lawmaker, also said that South Korea ’ s investment in U.S. semiconductor production will ensure that South Korea receives vaccines from the United States.  Russia plans to withdraw from the International Space Station from 2025, space agency chief Dmitry Rogozin said on Wednesday, with President Vladimir Putin's approval, Russia will build its own space station and hopes to put it into orbit by 2030, a plan that reportedly costs $6 billion (about HK $46.6 billion).  If successful, it will open a new chapter in Russia ’ s space exploration and end more than two decades of U.S.-Russian cooperation on the International Space Station.  Russian Deputy Prime Minister Yuri Borisov told Russian television last weekend that Moscow would notify its partners to leave the International Space Station from 2025.  Russia ’ s Interfax news agency reported that Rogozin said it plans to put the space station into orbit by 2030, and unlike the International Space Station, it is likely that there will not be permanent members of the Russian space station, because the space station ’ s orbit will expose the astronauts to high radiation, but Russian astronauts can go, and the space station will also use artificial intelligence and robots.  He added that Russia is ready to consider allowing foreign space visitors, “but the space station must be national … If you want to do things well, you have to do it yourself. ”  Since 1998, Russian cosmonauts have cooperated with astronauts from the United States and 16 other countries on missions to the International Space Station, one of the areas in which Moscow has worked closely with Washington.  However, the US-Russian relationship is in crisis due to issues such as human rights and hacking.  NASA ’ s Perseverance successfully extracted oxygen from the Martian atmosphere The recent mission of the Mars rover Perseverance successfully converted carbon dioxide from the Martian atmosphere into breathable pure oxygen, NASA said on Wednesday.  NASA said that the device, called MOXIE (Mars Oxygen In-Situ Resource Utilization Experiment), is the size of a toaster, and uses extreme heat to separate oxygen atoms from carbon dioxide molecules through electrolysis work. MOXIE successfully generated about 5 grams of oxygen, which can allow an astronaut to breathe for 10 minutes.  This feat marks the first time humans have extracted natural resources available for human use from the environment of another planet.  Oxygen content in the Martian atmosphere is extremely low, carbon dioxide accounts for 95% of the Martian atmosphere, and the rest is mainly composed of molecular nitrogen and argon.  Adequate oxygen supply is key to human exploration of Mars, experts believe that astronauts living and working on Mars may need 1 ton of oxygen to maintain their needs for a year, and believe that it is more practical to convert oxygen on Mars than to transport 25 tons of oxygen from Earth.  MOXIE ’ s operating concept is to produce 10 grams of oxygen per hour.  NASA says scientists plan to run the MOXIE device at least nine more times over the next two years, under different conditions and at different speeds. Title: "ice" shelter that will protect astronauts from adverse factors on the surface of Mars » DailyTechInfo
Content: Since people who will arrive on Mars will have to spend several months or even years on the surface, they will need a safe haven that will protect them from temperature changes and from cosmic radiation breaking through the thin and rarefied atmosphere of the planet.  Moreover, for the construction of such shelters, it will be necessary to use local materials as much as possible, because the delivery of the necessary amount of composition for the manufacture of special concrete from the Earth is not yet feasible.  Scientists and experts from NASA's Langley Research Center have come up with a simple and effective solution to the above problem.  In the project developed by them shelter Mars Ice Home as the main protective layer is used ordinary ice, obtained from water extracted from the atmosphere of Mars.The design of the shelter Mars Ice Home is a large inflatable torus, closed on top of a spherical dome of a sufficiently thick layer of ice.  All the structural elements that need to be delivered from Earth are quite light and compact, and in the final design of the structure, in addition to water, some other materials that can be mined on the surface of the Red Planet are used.  In addition, the water from which the protective dome will be made can be later recycled and from it can be obtained fuel for refueling the Mars Ascent Lander spacecraft, which will take people from the surface back to orbit.  The main disadvantage is that it will take at least 400 days to extract the necessary amount of water from the atmosphere of Mars.  This problem can be solved by sending a pre-automated expedition to Mars, which will include robots that will create a foundation, pump up the shell of the shelter, collect enough water and build an ice dome during the time that people will fly to Mars.  This approach will avoid the need for hasty construction of shelter or burying deep underground immediately after the arrival of people on the planet.Mars Ice Home is still only an exciting project, not worked out to the smallest details.  However, it can serve as a starting point for other designers and specialists who will be able to produce elegant and complete solutions to the problems associated with the long stay of people on the surface of the Red Planet.

Title: Martian organics formed thanks to natural batteries
Content: Scientists seem to have uncovered the secret of the origin of organic matter in meteorites that came from the Red Planet.  The list of participants in the process sounds like this: water, volcanic rocks, electricity.  What is nice is that such processes can take place on many bodies of the solar system.  Scientists seem to have uncovered the secret of the origin of organic matter in meteorites that came from the Red Planet.  The formation of organic matter occurs due to natural “accumulators ” consisting of water, salts and volcanic rocks.  Such conclusions are made in a scientific article published in the journal Science Advanced by a group led by Andrew Steele (Andrew Steele) from the Carnegie Scientific Institute in the USA.Recall that proteins, fats, carbohydrates, DNA, RNA and many other molecules, without which it is impossible to imagine a living organism, belong to organic substances.  Of course, not all organic matter is an integral part of living beings or is formed with their participation, so it is not necessary to equate organic matter with life. However, the presence of such molecules is the most important condition for the appearance of the biosphere.  Apparently, only organic chemistry can provide the variety, flexibility and complexity of chemical processes that are necessary for the existence of even the most primitive microbe.  In 2012, a team led by Steele studied carbon from organic molecules found in ten Martian meteorites.  The researchers came to two conclusions, pleasant and not so.  The good news is that this organics originated on Mars (rather than being brought in by pollution on Earth).  The bad news: it is not a product of the vital activity of living organisms; how was it formed in this case?  This is what the authors of a recent study found out. "Identification of the processes during which organic carbon compounds are formed on Mars is of great interest to determine its habitability potential," says Steel.Scientists used three samples of Martian meteorites.  The first is Tissint, which fell in Morocco in 2011.  The second is Nakhla, discovered in Egypt in 1911.  The third was NWA 1950, found in Morocco in 2001.  In all these celestial stones previously found inclusions of Martian organics.Meteorites were subjected to the most careful analysis.  Among the methods used were both the usual viewing of the sample in an optical microscope, and Raman spectroscopy, translucent electron microscopy, nanoscale mass spectrometry of secondary ions, X-ray absorption near the absorption edge (X-ray absorption near-edge structure) and other methods with names incomprehensible to the average person. Thanks to all these methods, the authors thoroughly studied the chemical composition and fine structure of organic inclusions and the surrounding rocks.  By the way, it turned out that the organics of meteorites are extremely similar to the substances found on the Red Planet by the MSL mission.  The detailed information obtained allowed scientists to draw conclusions about what processes could lead to the formation of these substances. It turned out that one of the necessary ingredients are volcanic minerals such as spinel.  On the Red Planet, rich in ancient volcanoes, there is no shortage of such material.  The second important component is liquid water, in huge concentrations containing various salts (in particular, perchlorates).  Such brines have never been directly detected on Mars, but, according to experts, they can exist there almost everywhere.  Finally, the third element of the “magic potion ” is carbon dioxide.  It is also, to put it mildly, not in deficit: the Martian atmosphere consists of it almost completely.  For a while, there is something like a natural battery.  As a result, organic compounds are formed from carbon CO2 and hydrogen of water. "The discovery that a natural system can essentially form a small battery based on corrosion, which controls electrochemical reactions between minerals and the surrounding liquid, has serious consequences for astrobiology," says Steele. Indeed, it turned out that the synthesis of organic matter does not need exotic conditions or components.  All the necessary ingredients are quite common for Mars, which is either already proven (volcanic minerals and carbon dioxide), or assumed (brines).  Moreover, a similar process can take place on bodies such as Europa or Enceladus.  Recall that earlier "33Live.RuNauka" (nauka.vesti.ru) wrote about how a record amount of organic matter was discovered on Mars, as well as that life in the crust of the planet could be supported by radiation.

Title: On Earth found able to survive on Mars bacteria
Content: A microorganism capable of surviving in harsh Martian conditions has been discovered by scientists from the National University of Australia in Canberra.  We are talking about one of the strains of cyanobacteria living in hot springs and geysers. In the course of the experiment, strains of bacteria Chroococcidiopsis thermalis, when the light level was lowered to "Martian" values, continued to grow and produced nutrients - organic substances necessary for life, the article notes. Title: Converting Martian salt water into oxygen and fuel with a new technology
Content: New technology allows astronauts to convert Martian saltwater into oxygen and fuel when they land on the Red Planet in 2033.  There is water on Mars, but most of it is frozen, and the rest is mixed with salt, making it useless for future astronauts who plan to land on the planet by 2033.  Now, a team of researchers at Washington University in St. Louis has developed a system that converts unusable water into fuel and oxygen.  The system uses electricity to convert saltwater into oxygen and hydrogen, and has been found to work in the Martian atmosphere at temperatures as low as -33 degrees Fahrenheit.  The saltwater electrolyser produces 25 times more oxygen than NASA ’ s MOXIE, which launched in July 2020 with the Mars 2020 rover and aims to produce a small amount of oxygen on Mars.  Vijay Ramani of the University of Washington said the technology is just as useful on Earth as it is on Mars because it can turn the oceans into a source of oxygen and fuel.  According to Inverse, the device has two parts around it, one of which separates water to form hydroxyl ions and the other separates water again to produce oxygen.  Although the technology is currently being developed on Earth, it is expensive and likely will not be able to withstand the freezing temperatures of Mars.  Ramani and other researchers decided to build a portable version of the technology that could operate on the Red Planet continuously without the need to heat or purify the water source.  Research scientist and first author of the study, Shrihari Sankarasubramanian, said: “Water-soluble perchlorates (so-called impurities) are actually functional in a Mars-like environment because they prevent water from freezing and also improve the performance of the electrolaser system by reducing electrical resistance.  The study is based on data from NASA ’ s Phoenix Mars Lander, which touched Mars in 2008.  Scientists know that in order to live on Mars, even temporarily, astronauts would have to produce some of their needs, especially oxygen for breathing and fuel for travel to Earth or beyond on the Red Planet.  NASA's Mars Endurance rover is currently traveling to Mars by carrying instruments that use electrolysis at high temperatures.  The researchers hope to work with NASA to further develop the system in the future.  End of message.

Title: Mars Rover Perseverance successfully tested the device to extract oxygen from the Martian atmosphere
Content: An experimental device called MOXIE (Mars Oxygen In-Situ Resource Utilization Experiment) was first tested on April 20, and this test was recognized as successful: for an hour of operation, the installation the size of a conventional toaster was able to produce more than 5 grams of oxygen, writes Newsru.  The atmosphere of Mars is almost 96% carbon dioxide (CO2).  The MOXIE unit is capable of converting this carbon dioxide into oxygen and carbon monoxide (CO, carbon monoxide), which is a by-product of the processing and is released back into the atmosphere.  The process of processing carbon dioxide occurs by electrolysis of solid oxides at a temperature of 800 degrees Celsius.  During operation, the device captures carbon dioxide, passes through a filter to remove dust and compresses it, providing pressure at ground level.  The gas then passes through a heated electrolysis cell, which consists of several layers of nickel alloy and ceramics.  Ceramic elements of the cell are able to conduct current at high temperature - they pass oxygen ions and trap carbon monoxide.  The outer surface of MOXIE is covered with a thin layer of gold.  This coating protects the MOXIE surface from heating, protecting the rover electronics located next to the instrument.  Future astronauts: breathe easier.  The MOXIE technology demonstration aboard @ NASAPersevere successfully extracted oxygen from the thin Martian atmosphere — a critical component for life support on the Red Planet and rocket fuel for the trip home. https: / / t.co / HOsguer. hYgkP pic.twitter.com / SwL0etf9Uu — NASA JPL (@ NASAJPL) April 21, 2021 The maximum estimated performance of MOXIE is up to 10 grams of oxygen per hour.  The test program includes at least nine more tests over two years.  These tests will be carried out under different conditions to assess the performance of the plant.  In the future, more large-scale oxygen production on Mars may come in handy for practical purposes.  First, oxygen is used as an oxidizing agent for rocket fuel.  For example, to launch a rocket with four astronauts from Mars to Earth requires about 7 tons of fuel and 25 tons of oxygen.  The ability to produce this amount of oxygen during the astronauts ’ stay on Mars will prevent this oxygen from being delivered from Earth – delivering a large and productive oxygen generator modeled on MOXIE would be a more practical solution.  Secondly, oxygen, which makes up 21% of the Earth's atmosphere, is needed for breathing - four astronauts will be enough one ton of oxygen for a year on Mars.  We will remind, the Rover Perseverance landed in the area of 45-kilometer crater Jezero, named after the village in Bosnia and Herzegovina.  This crater is located on the western edge of the Isis Plain (a giant impact crater north of the equator of Mars).  As scientists suggest, in ancient times in the area of ​ ​ the crater Ezero was a river delta, where organic matter and other potential traces of microorganisms that could have lived on Mars about 3 billion years ago could have been collected.  The crater itself was then filled with water and was a lake.

Title: Scientists have found organisms that can give rise to life on Mars
Content: Scientists have found organisms that can give rise to life on Mars 16.02.2021, 14: 58 They are able to grow and multiply in the conditions of the red planet.  New experiments have shown that cyanobacteria, also known as blue-green algae, can successfully grow in Martian atmospheric conditions.  Of course, a few more ingredients will be needed, but when humans get to Mars, they will be able to create life support systems based on cyanobacteria for the human habitat, writes nv.ua.  "Here we show that cyanobacteria can use the gases available in the Martian atmosphere, at low overall pressure, as a source of carbon and nitrogen," said astrobiologist Cyprien Verso from the University of Bremen in Germany.  "Under these conditions, cyanobacteria retained their ability to grow in water containing only Martian dust, and they could be used to feed other microbes.  This can help make long-term missions to Mars sustainable, ” the authors of the study believe.  All types of cyanobacteria produce oxygen as a byproduct of photosynthesis, and even today they are an invaluable source of it.  For several years, scientists have speculated whether we could use the ability of cyanobacteria to produce oxygen to live on Mars.  This will bring additional benefits.  The atmosphere of Mars consists mainly of carbon dioxide (95 percent) and nitrogen (3 percent), which are fixed by cyanobacteria, turning them into organic compounds and nutrients, respectively.  However, atmospheric pressure on Mars is a big problem.  The total pressure there is less than 1% of Earth ’ s — from 6 to 11 GPa: this is too small for the presence of liquid water, while the partial pressure of gaseous nitrogen — from 0.2 to 0.3 GPa — is not enough for their metabolism.  But recreating the atmosphere, like on Earth, would be too expensive: gases would have to be imported.  So the researchers were looking for a middle ground: an atmosphere close to Martian, which allows cyanobacteria to grow well.  The authors have developed a bioreactor called Atmos, which has an atmospheric pressure of about 10 percent of Earth ’ s, but uses only what can be found on Mars, albeit in inverted proportions: 96 percent nitrogen and 4 percent carbon dioxide.  The bioreactor also included water that can be obtained on Mars from melting ice, which in some places is abundant on the surface, and a simulator of Martian regolith, a mixture of minerals created here on Earth using only what can be found on Mars. Title: Soviet missions to Mars: how the Soviet Union studied the Red Planet
Content: The first successful Soviet Martian mission was to send to the "red planet" automatic interplanetary station of the third generation Mars-2.  Mars-2 was designed to explore Mars both from its orbit and directly from the surface of the planet.  The Mars-2 AMS consisted of an orbital station (an artificial satellite for exploring Mars) and a lander.  Navigation in space was carried out with the help of orientation to the Sun, the star Canopus and the Earth.  The Soviet Union planned to carry out serious research work on Mars, for this purpose the AMC had all the necessary equipment: an infrared photometer to study the surface relief by measuring the amount of carbon dioxide, an ultraviolet photometer to determine the density of the upper atmosphere.  Cosmic ray particle counter and many other instruments.  The lander was also automated and configured for autonomous operation and control.  The station was launched from the Baikonur Cosmodrome on May 19, 1971.  The flight of the station to Mars lasted more than 6 months.  The flight was carried out according to the program and, as they say, nothing foreshadowed trouble, only at the last stage (the most important, it should be admitted), due to incorrect calculations, the lander entered the atmosphere at an angle greater than the set one, the parachute system was ineffective in such conditions and, having passed through the atmosphere of Mars, the device crashed.  To the honor of our country, our lander, although it crashed, still became the first artificial object on the planet.  The orbital station for more than eight months carried out complex studies of Mars, having made 362 turns around the planet during the work.  The next Russian Martian mission was more successful.  When developing the Mars-3 program, the shortcomings of the previous launch were taken into account.  Launched nine days after Mars-2, the Mars-3 station successfully reached Martian orbit six months later.  The lander for the first time in history made a soft landing on the surface of the “red planet ”.  After one and a half minutes of preparatory period, the device began to work and began to broadcast a panorama of the surrounding surface, but after 14 and a half seconds, the “Martian show ” ended.  “Show ” this, of course, can be called with a big stretch: AMC transmitted only the first 79 lines of the photo-television signal, which represented a gray background without a single detail, the same happened with the broadcast from the second telefotometer.  Various versions of incorrect operation of the devices were assumed: corona discharge in the antennas of the transmitter, damage to the battery... but the final decision on the reasons for the failure was not made.  No, the Martians did something.  Mars-4 July 21, 1973 from the Baikonur cosmodrome was launched AMS Mars-4.  204 days after launch, on February 10, 1974, the spacecraft flew at a distance of 1,844 km from the surface of Mars.  Twenty-seven minutes before that, single-line optical-mechanical scanners — telophotometers — were turned on, with the help of which panoramas of two regions of the surface of Mars were taken (in the orange and red-infrared ranges).  For the first time in the practice of domestic cosmonautics, four spacecraft participated in the flight.  Mars-4 had many tasks: studying the distribution of water vapor on the disk of the planet, determining the gas composition and density of the atmosphere, measuring the flow of electrons and protons on the flight path and the planet, studying the spectra of the own glow of the atmosphere of Mars and many others.  The main task of Mars-4 was to communicate with automatic stations on the surface of Mars.  The Mars-4 spacecraft photographed Mars from a flight path.  On photographs of the surface of the planet, which are of very high quality, you can distinguish details up to 100 m in size.  This makes photography one of the main means of exploring the planet.  With its help, using color filters by synthesizing negatives, color images of a number of areas of the surface of Mars were obtained.  Color images are also of high quality and are suitable for areological-morphological and photometric studies.  Unfortunately, Mars 4 did not fulfill all the tasks assigned to it.  Mars 5 was launched four days after the launch of Mars 4.  The tasks that were assigned to him were not very different from the previous mission.  The Mars-5 station successfully entered orbit around the planet, but immediately there was a depressurization of the instrument compartment, as a result of which the station lasted only about two weeks.  The scientific instruments placed on the Mars 5 station were intended mainly for studying a number of important characteristics of the planet's surface and near-planetary space from orbit.  The device was equipped with a liman-alpha photometer, designed jointly by Soviet and French scientists, and designed to search for hydrogen in the upper atmosphere of Mars.  Installed on board the magnetometer made measurements of the magnetic field of the planet.  To measure the surface temperature, an infrared radiometer was intended, operating in the range of 8-40 microns.  The artificial satellite of Mars "Mars-5" transmitted to Earth new information about the planet and the surrounding space; from the orbit of the satellite obtained high-quality photos of the Martian surface, including color.  Studies of the magnetic field in the Martian space, conducted by the apparatus, confirmed the conclusion made on the basis of similar studies of the spacecraft "Mars-2, -3", that near the planet there is a magnetic field of about 30 gamma (7-10 times greater than the value of the interplanetary unperturbed field carried by the solar wind).  It was assumed that this magnetic field belongs to the planet itself, and Mars 5 helped to get additional arguments in favor of this hypothesis.  Similar measurements from the Mars-5 spacecraft directly measured the temperature of atomic hydrogen in the upper atmosphere of Mars for the first time.  Preliminary data processing showed that this temperature is close to 350 ° K.  Despite the fact that the work of the station did not last long, during its work, numerous information was obtained about Mars, its atmosphere and magnetic field.  Another of our lander was on Mars thanks to the AMS Mars-6, launched from the Baikonur cosmodrome on August 5, 1973.  Sadly, this time there was no soft landing.  During the descent, there was no digital information from the MX 6408M device, but with the help of the Zubr, IT and ID devices, information was obtained on overloads, temperature and pressure changes.  Just before landing, communication with the SA is lost.  The last telemetry received from him confirmed the issuance of a command to turn on the soft landing engine.  The new appearance of the signal was expected 143 seconds after the disappearance, but this did not happen, however, the data obtained during the descent has already yielded significant results and made a great contribution to the study of Mars.  The lander Mars 6 landed on the planet, for the first time transmitting to Earth data on the parameters of the Martian atmosphere obtained during the descent.  Mars-6 measured the chemical composition of the Martian atmosphere using a radiofrequency mass spectrometer.  Shortly after the opening of the main parachute, the analyzer's opening mechanism worked, and the Martian atmosphere gained access to the instrument.  Preliminary analysis suggests that the content of argon in the atmosphere of the planet can be about one-third.  This result is of fundamental importance for understanding the evolution of the Martian atmosphere.  Pressure and ambient temperature measurements were also carried out on the lander; the results of these measurements are very important both for expanding knowledge of the planet and for identifying the conditions in which future Martian stations should operate.  Together with French scientists, a radio astronomy experiment was also performed - measuring the radio emission of the Sun in the meter range.  Receiving radiation simultaneously on Earth and on board a spacecraft hundreds of millions of kilometers away from our planet, allows you to restore a three-dimensional picture of the process of generating radio waves and obtain data on the streams of charged particles responsible for these processes.  In this experiment, another task was solved - the search for short-term bursts of radio radiation, which can, as expected, occur in distant space due to explosive phenomena in the cores of galaxies, supernova flares and other processes.  Mars-7 was launched on August 9, 1973.  The Mars mission failed.  The lander passed 1400 kilometers from the surface of Mars and went into space.  Thus, the target program of Mars-7 was not fulfilled, but, making an autonomous flight, the lander retained its operability and transmitted information to the flight vehicle via radio lines KD-1 and RT-1.  Communication with the Marsa-7 spacecraft was maintained until March 25, 1974. Title: On Mars, the level of oxygen increased sharply
Content: Oxygen levels on Mars soared 5 13.11.2019, 13: 36 1,762 Why?  NASA experts conducted an analysis of seasonal changes in the composition of the atmosphere of Mars, data about which was sent by the Curiosity apparatus.  It turned out that the concentration of oxygen in the atmosphere of the planet every spring increases dramatically, and scientists do not understand why.  This is reported by slashgear.com.  For six years, the rover collected data on the atmosphere of Mars, analyzed them and sent them to Earth.  From these data, it becomes clear that the planet's atmosphere contains 95% carbon dioxide, 2.6% nitrogen, 1.9% argon, 0.16% oxygen and 0.06 carbon monoxide.  However, on Mars there is a phenomenon of molecular circulation, which is associated with seasonal changes in pressure in winter and spring.  With nitrogen and argon, the situation is similar to what the researchers predict.  With oxygen, everything is different - in the spring its content in the atmosphere of the planet begins to increase sharply and only in the fall falls to the level predicted by known chemical processes.  The amount of oxygen is different each year.  In other words, something produces it first and then removes it.  The last time the level of oxygen in the atmosphere of the red planet exceeded 30%, while in the atmosphere of the Earth it contains about 20%.  Scientists have not yet been able to say exactly what this is related to.  There is an assumption that the change in the proportion of oxygen in the atmosphere of Mars coincides with the change in the level of methane.  The publication in-space.ru specifies that "oxygen and methane can be produced both biologically, for example, by microbes, and abiotic - in chemical processes related to water and soil."

Title: Oxygen and hydrogen on Mars proposed to get from brine
Content: Scientists have developed a method for producing oxygen and hydrogen from a liquid saline solution in Martian lakes using electrolysis.  A feature of the experiment was the use of lead-ruthenium oxide as an electrocatalyst for oxygen production.  The production of oxygen using such an installation was 25 times more energy efficient than in the case of MOXIE, launched to the Red Planet as part of the Mars 2020 mission, and the size and weight of the device for life support based on the described technology will be less than that of analogues.  The article was published in the journal PNAS.  Conditions on Mars are far from favorable for humans: the atmosphere is rarefied and 95 percent consists of carbon dioxide, and temperature changes exceed 100 degrees Celsius with an average temperature of minus 63 degrees.  Therefore, colonization of the Red Planet is impossible without the creation of a life support system that would be able to provide people with oxygen for breathing and fuel (for example, hydrogen) for energy supply and, ideally, return flight.  To solve the first problem, NASA created MOXIE (Mars Oxygen ISRU Experiment) - an experimental installation for obtaining oxygen from atmospheric carbon dioxide by electrolysis.  To test the effectiveness of such a method in the field, the installation became part of the Mars Rover Perseverance, which was launched on July 30, 2020 as part of the Mars 2020 mission.  An alternative source of not only oxygen, but also hydrogen on Mars can be water, the first direct evidence of the existence of which on the red planet was obtained in 1971.  Particularly attractive for use in applications, however, would be the reserves of salt water, impurities in which would allow it to remain in a liquid state even at low temperature and pressure.  The first traces of such brine (liquid salt solution) with magnesium perchlorate as the main component were found on Mars in 2015, and in 2018, a reservoir with a diameter of about 20 kilometers was found under the polar ice of the planet, which could have been formed due to volcanic activity.  Later, planetary scientists confirmed that such lakes on Mars really exist and can be numerous.  Now Pralay Gayen (Pralay Gayen) from the University of Washington in St. Louis together with colleagues created an installation for obtaining oxygen and hydrogen from a saline solution close in composition and temperature to that in Martian lakes.  As a brine in the experiment, a solution of magnesium perchlorate in water with a concentration of 2.8 mol per liter was used, cooled to minus 36 degrees Celsius and blown by carbon dioxide (the latter played the role of the Martian atmosphere).  As an electrocatalyst for the production of oxygen, the scientists used lead-ruthenium oxide Pb2Ru2O7-δ, the effectiveness of which they previously showed for alkaline solutions.  The electrocatalyst for hydrogen production was platinum on activated carbon - the standard catalyst in this case, and a commercially produced anion-exchange membrane was used as a separator.  Installation diagram.  In the red region, oxygen is produced, in the blue - hydrogen.  Image source: Pralay Gayen et al. / PNAS In the course of the study, scientists showed that lead-ruthenium oxide as an electrocatalyst is indeed several times more effective than the ruthenium oxide commonly used in such installations.  After the behavior of the created installation was studied in a wide range of temperatures from − 36 to 21 degrees Celsius and saw no radical fluctuations in the efficiency and rate of production.  The current output of the experimental installation was 70 percent, and the energy efficiency was in the range between 36 and 70 percent (depending on the voltage applied to the plates).  In addition, the installation was resistant to degradation of the catalyst: scientists were not able to find traces of ruthenium in the solution after 300-minute operation of the device.  The rate of production of oxygen (blue dots) and hydrogen (red dots), depending on the density of the cathode current.  Image source: Pralay Gayen et al. / PNAS Also, the researchers compared the achieved rate of oxygen production with MOXIE values of 10-22 grams per hour: it turned out that with the same energy supply, the created installation produces 25 times more oxygen than the experiment on the Mars Rover “Perseverance ”.  To have the same rate of oxygen production as MOXIE, the device would have to have electrodes with an area of ​ ​ 28-62 square centimeters, and to ensure the vital activity of a sleeping and actively moving person, this parameter would have to be 375 and 1235 square centimeters, respectively.  At the same time, the mass and volume of the installation will be less than if you use the technology inherent in MOXIE.  Moreover, the developed method of obtaining oxygen does not require its subsequent purification, while during electrolysis in MOXIE, carbon monoxide is also produced, which must be filtered.  Dependence on the power consumption of the rate of oxygen production of the installation (blue line), as well as its capes and volume to ensure various modes of human life (black lines).  The blue dot is the power and rate of oxygen production at MOXIE.  Image source: Pralay Gayen et al. / PNAS Previously, we talked about another method of obtaining oxygen from carbon dioxide in the Martian atmosphere (like MOXIE): scientists proposed to do this using low-temperature plasma.  And what is the role of the Mars Rover “Perseverance ” in addition to checking the method of oxygen production, you can read in our material“ Mars, there and back ”.  Nikita Kozyrev

Title: A million people will live on Mars!
Content: Currently, there are almost 50 projects of manned flights to Mars.  The most grandiose of them belongs to the American engineer and entrepreneur Elon Musk, who plans to transport a million people to the Red Planet in the coming decades to create an independent civilization.  This idea seems absolutely fantastic – and meanwhile, the company Srace X, led by Mask, announced that very soon will begin the first flights of its space shuttles.  Go to the Red Planet!  At the International Astronomical Congress held in September 2016 in Mexico, the report of the engineer and entrepreneur made a real sensation.  According to Elon Musk, only the resettlement of a significant part of earthlings to Mars will save humanity from possible extinction.  Life on our planet can be interrupted by many factors: the explosion of a nearby supernova, superflares on the Sun, falling into a black hole, a global epidemic, a collision with a huge asteroid, a man-made disaster.  A large colony of people on another planet will ensure the continued existence of terrestrial civilization.  Why choose Mars?  Compared to other celestial bodies of the solar system, it is better suited for the possible life of earthlings.  The day here lasts 24 hours 37 minutes - that is, suitable for our residents and plants.  Gravity is much smaller than the earth, but is quite suitable for the normal functioning of the human body.  Finally, there is water – albeit in the form of polar ice caps, but it can be easily reached, and pieces of ice melt and use.  The rest of the planets of the solar system are practically unsuitable for such a mission: Mercury has extremely high surface temperatures during the day and very low at night, Venus has a too aggressive atmosphere, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune are mostly composed of liquefied gas.  The closest suitable celestial body to us is the Moon, but it depends entirely on the Earth and in the event of a space disaster may die with it.  Why is the number of one million people chosen?  According to experts, this is the minimum number of people so that their colony can become completely independent and develop.  It will have specialists of all the necessary professions, it will cope with possible diseases and epidemics, as well as ensure a stable natural population growth.  At first, the colonists will face the most difficult task - to turn the Red Planet into their home.  The set of actions to achieve this goal, Maek called the term “terraforming ” – that is, changing the conditions of life on another planet in such a way that they resemble earthly ones.  First of all, you need to melt a sufficient amount of ice at the south pole of the planet, since it will turn to the Sun in the summer, which means that it will be easier to do this than at the north pole.  The water accumulated here is enough to create an ocean several meters deep on the planet.  As the ice cap decreases, a chain reaction will begin - water vapor will begin to compact the atmosphere, which, in turn, will retain more solar heat, due to which the melting process will be more intense.  Technically, it can be launched using nuclear charges or placing laser devices over the south pole of Mars.  After liquid water appears on the planet, you need to start planting plants: initially it will be mosses, but later - vast forests that will saturate the atmosphere of Mars with oxygen (now it is 95% carbon dioxide).  According to Musk, the cultivation of “green lungs ” and the creation of a livable air without spacesuits will take from 300 to 1000 years.  But after that, the Red Planet can be considered terraformed, and people will choose where they live - on Mars or on Earth.  100 thousand flights Elon Maek listed the things and equipment that the first colonists needed.  First of all, these are devices for the production and conversion of energy - nuclear or space.  The most promising direction, the researchers of the company Srace X consider the delivery to Mars of a large number of light folding solar panels.  It will also require a huge amount of plants, both to create oxygen and to supply the settlers with food.  Until the atmosphere of the planet is formed properly, earthlings will need means of protection from solar radiation - after all, until this time, Martian cities will have to be under special domes.  First, the settlers will build small houses, then they will equip complexes, where there will be not only housing, but also schools, hospitals, shops, etc.  Experts Srace X calculated: one flight with the colonists should account for nine flights with payload.  It is based on a ship capable of carrying 100 passengers.  Thus, the total number of flights required to create a million colony on the Red Planet will be about 100 thousand (10 thousand - passenger flights, 90 thousand - cargo).  Elon Maek has already announced that the first expeditions for the delivery of goods should begin at the end of 2022.  By 2035, spacecraft will be built capable of reaching the Red Planet in 80 days, and a million colonists will arrive on Mars within the next few decades.  The main obstacle to the implementation of such a large-scale project, according to Musk and his team, is the high cost of a flight to the Red Planet.  In fact, it is steadily declining.  In 1989, the US national aerospace agency YABA estimated sending astronauts to Mars at $450 billion.  It was assumed that there will be from four to six earthlings — that is, each place was estimated at about $100 billion.  But already in 2004, the same agency reduced the cost of the project nine times — to $50 billion.  Thus, the flight of one person would cost a little more than 10 billion dollars.  This figure is still too high, but the trend towards its decline is clearly visible, and therefore such a task can be solved.  Elon Maek believes that the optimal amount for a flight of one person should be 500 thousand dollars – this is the approximate cost of a middle-class house in a good place.  Moreover, people should understand that they will become real space pioneers, the first permanent residents of another planet – and therefore must pay for their flight themselves.  Opinions of economists and psychologists are unambiguous: only in the United States there are at least a million people who will agree to pay such money for an unprecedented space travel.  But how to reduce the cost of flying each person from 10 billion to 500 thousand dollars, that is, 20 thousand times?  Elon Mayek knows the answer to that question.  Rocket from a private company Team plan Srace X works in two directions.  The first of these is the creation of spacecraft, each of which will be able to carry at least 100 people.  The company Ilona Mask has a successful experience in the construction of devices of a new type.  The engineer and entrepreneur himself says that the huge cost of missiles is primarily a consequence of the lack of competition and the presence of a huge number of subcontractors.  NASA constantly entrusts the execution of its orders only to a few companies.  For example, ULA (United Launch Alliance), a joint venture owned by Boeing and Lockheed Martin, regularly performs missions of the space agency and the US Department of Defense, but at the same time receives more for each launch than anyone else in the world.  Under the pretext of national security, the system of government orders in this area is completely opaque, and the task of many companies is not to reduce the cost of the spacecraft, but to make it more expensive for their own benefit.  In turn, having received the order, large companies transfer it in parts to small subcontractors, who also inflate prices.  But the main thing is that in the absence of competition, there is no need to invent something new!  As a result, the technology of modern spacecraft at best dates back to the 1990s, and the costs of their production and launch are declining extremely slowly.  SpaceX was the first company to start working on a fundamentally different scheme.  Not fulfilling an order, but creating your own device, cheaper and more reliable, which can then be offered to space agencies and organizations.  The company was founded in 2002 with the personal funds of Elon Musk, received from the development and operation of the largest electronic payment system in the United States.  The company created its first rocket, called the Falcon 1 (translated from English “falcon ”).  The two-stage vehicle and its engine were made by Space X workers without the help of intermediaries.  The first three launches ended in accidents.  But the fourth flight, which took place in 2008, was successful.  A cargo detachment simulation was conducted (it remained in the rocket so as not to increase the amount of space debris), and the first stage made a safe landing.  At the same time, Elon Maek, who was in the Mission Control Center at Cape Canaveral, heard the clap, ran out into the street in despair - he thought that this test ended in an explosion. Title: Perseverance makes oxygen on Mars for the first time outside of Earth - Technology
Content: NASA said today that the Mars rover "perseverance" continues to make history, yesterday successfully converted carbon dioxide into oxygen in the Martian atmosphere, the first successful oxygenation on another planet.  "Turning carbon dioxide into oxygen on Mars is a very important first step," said Jim Reuter, NASA's deputy director of space technology missions.  Perseverance uses the Mars Oxygen In situ Resource Utilization Experiment (MOXIE) built in front of its right and designed by MIT to produce oxygen. This car battery-sized gold box uses electricity and chemical properties to break down carbon dioxide molecules and successfully produce oxygen.  Since carbon dioxide is composed of 1 carbon atom and 2 oxygen atoms, the by-product of MOXIE's oxygen production is carbon monoxide.  MOXIE not only can produce oxygen for future astronauts to breathe on Mars, but also need not drag a large amount of oxygen from Earth as a propellant in the future, which is expected to pave the way for future human exploration.  MOXIE ’ s first score was to produce 5 grams of oxygen, equivalent to the amount an astronaut needs to breathe for 10 minutes of normal activity.  MOXIE was originally designed to produce up to 10 grams of oxygen per hour, and engineers will now conduct more experiments to try to increase production.  MOXIE is made of heat-resistant materials such as nickel alloys, which can withstand high temperatures of 800 degrees Celsius. The thin gold coating on the top ensures that it will not cause damage to the car ’ s Perseverance.  MIT engineer Michael Hecht said the one-ton version of MOXIE could produce about 25 tons of oxygen needed for a rocket to launch from Mars.  Since 96% of the Martian atmosphere is carbon dioxide, producing oxygen from the Martian atmosphere is much more feasible than extracting ice from the Martian surface. Content: 2050.  Humanity has finally become an interplanetary species, establishing a colony on Mars that is home to about a million people — more than Amsterdam or Athens.
