The entrepreneur often paints the most fantastic scenarios, but one cannot blame him: it is not only him who is drawn to Mars.  Unfriendly neighbor Mars is not the most hospitable world, if you compare it with the Earth.  The force of gravity here is only 37.5% of the earth ’ s.  The temperature on the surface ranges from freezing -153 ° C to comfortable + 20 ° C.  However, a thin, unsuitable for humans atmosphere, consisting mainly of carbon dioxide, nitrogen and argon, is not able to effectively trap heat from sunlight.  If you were standing on the Martian equator at noon, your feet would have a temperature of + 24 ° C and your head would have a temperature of 0 ° C.  In addition, the pressure on the red planet is much lower – even at the top of Everest on Earth, it is 50 times greater than on the surface of Mars.  However, these worlds have a lot in common.  Beneath our feet is solid land, the area of which is comparable to the land area on our planet, although Mars is about half its size.  The duration of the day, which is called soles, is 24.6 hours, and close to the Earth's angle of inclination of the axis of rotation (23.5 for the Earth and 25.2 for Mars) provides the world with pronounced seasons, which, however, last longer than ours.  For example, spring in the northern hemisphere lasts as much as 194 solas - this is the longest season on the planet.  But the main similarity of the planets remains in the distant past.  Numerous evidence points to the fact that Mars used to be warmer, had a denser atmosphere, and its surface was covered with water - the cradle of intelligent life on our home planet.  That ’ s why researchers are looking so closely at this harsh world.  The chances of life on Mars are slim.  For example, in 2018, a group of European scientists found signs of the existence of a liquid lake hidden 1.5 km below the surface of the southern polar glacier.  Microbes may exist in such a reservoir, but this is only a hypothesis that is difficult to test.  Therefore, scientists rely on the search for signs of the existence of a past life.  It may not sound so exciting, but even such a find will be colossal.  Otherwise, we will face a much larger scientific mystery: why the Earth gave life, and the neighboring world with the right conditions - not.  The race for Martian life began in the 19th century.  In 1877, the Italian astronomer Giovanni Schiaparelli looked through the telescope Mars, which no one imagined, and even made a map.  It depicted seas and continents, as well as an extensive network of lines, which the astronomer called channels.  The word itself prompted the idea of ​ ​ the man-made origin of these objects.  It was later established that the channels were an optical illusion, but the idea of the existence of the Martian civilization that built them was picked up by others.  Astronomers such as American Percival Lowell or Frenchman Camille Flammarion believed in the habitability of the Red Planet, and science fiction writers such as Edgar Burroughs and H.G. Wells.  Of course, this theory was not accepted by everyone, but it was not possible to test it for a long time.  That all changed in the 1950s.  After the launch of the first Soviet satellite in 1957 and the start of the space race, the views of the USSR and the United States quickly rushed beyond the Earth ’ s orbit and even the Moon.  Already in the 1960s, the first automatic interplanetary stations rushed to the Red Planet.  No one thought about landing or orbiters at that time.  AMS sent to other worlds had to fly by, trying to take as many pictures as possible and send them to Earth.  But this task was not easy either.  The first attempt to send a research apparatus to the Red Planet was made by the Soviet Union in 1960, but it, like many others after it, failed.  Soviet devices died, not having time to leave the orbit of the Earth, at best broke down in flight to Mars.  In 1964, NASA entered the game, but its debut was unsuccessful.  The second attempt was successful.  Mariner 4 arrived safely on Mars in 1965.  It flew about 10 thousand km above the surface of the planet and sent 22 photos to Earth.  These were the first images of Mars from such a short distance.  There were no channels on them, but scientists saw the craters decorating the Martian earth, and confirmed that the atmosphere of the planet consists of carbon dioxide.  NASA has been successful ever since.  Until the end of the decade, the agency launched two more AMS, which managed to take two hundred photos, as well as carry out measurements of the surface and temperature of Mars.  The first spacecraft to make a soft landing on Mars was the Soviet Mars-3, but on the surface it worked for a few seconds The Soviet Union caught up with the Americans only in 1971, but by that time the ambitions of local scientists and engineers had grown.  Just flying over the surface wasn ’ t enough.  In 1971, the Soviet Union sent to the Red Planet at once two AMS - "Mars-2" and "Mars-3", which included both orbiters and lander.  These missions have been successful.  Orbiters have been orbiting the planet for months, transmitting data.  As for the landers, one crashed during the landing, and the second successfully inscribed his name in history.  "Mars-3" was the first device to make a soft landing on the red planet, even if it worked in a matter of seconds.  1971 proved to be a fruitful year for the study of the fourth planet.  That year, the American orbiter Mariner 9 arrived, which not only took thousands of photos and made a map of 85% of its surface, but also helped to see the main attractions of Mars.  For example, data from Mariner 9 helped establish the height of Olympus, the tallest volcano in the solar system, which rises 25 km and the diameter of the base is 600 km.  And the NASA research apparatus helped to estimate the scale of the Mariner Valley - the famous system of canyons, which stretches for 4 thousand km along the Martian equator and crashes 7 km deep into the surface of the planet.  The system, named after the probe, is four times deeper and five times longer than the Grand Canyon on Earth.  The next breakthrough in the study of Mars was made only in 1976, when NASA delivered there two AMS - "Viking 1" and "Viking 2".  Like the Soviet Mars, they were equipped with orbiters and landers, but the Vikings were more successful.  They successfully placed in orbit and landed on the surface of the planet, having worked for more than one year.  The Viking 1 lander fell silent only in 1982, and even then after an erroneous command from Earth.  During this time, they replenished the Martian photo archive with tens of thousands of images, but most importantly - they conducted the first field experiments to search for traces of life.  Alas, they did not give a convincing "yes" or a definite "no", but still it was a breakthrough, since previously Mars was studied on the principle of "look, but do not touch".  "Vikings" involuntarily added fuel to the fire of the myth of the Martian civilization, when one of the orbiters sent a curious picture.  It showed a pile of stones, one of which was strikingly reminiscent of a human face.  NASA researchers immediately realized that this is a game of light and shadow, but the impressionable public began to build theories about the remains of an ancient Martian city that rests underground.  The tradition of looking for the usual forms in photos of the Red Planet is still alive today, and those who want to constantly find rodents and insects in the pictures.  But these are just illusions.  Face on Mars.  This image, taken in the AMC "Viking 1" 1976, refreshed the myth of the existence of a developed Martian civilization After the "Vikings" study of the red planet for many years stalled.  For two decades, the US and the USSR, and subsequently Russia, continued to send mechanical researchers, but the attempts were mostly unsuccessful.  A new breakthrough occurred in the second half of the 1990s.  In 1997, NASA delivered the Mars Global Surveyor orbiter to Mars, which helped make a revolutionary discovery: somewhere under the surface of a dead planet, water can still flow, the hunt for which continues to this day.  In the same year, the Pathfinder landed on the surface, which has not happened since the time of the Vikings.  But much more interesting was the cargo that Pathfinder brought with him.  With him on the planet arrived the first mobile research apparatus Sojourner, able to move on

Title: Astronomers: Venus may be habitable until mysterious event occurs
Content: 2019-09-21 15: 46 [News / Roundup] Michael Way, a scholar at NASA ’ s Goddard Space Science Research Center, presented his recent research at the 2019 European Planetary Science Conference (EPSC-DPS) in Geneva, which shows that Venus may maintain habitable conditions for billions of years, but a mysterious event has suddenly changed the planet ’ s environment.  According to CNN, Venus, like other planets in the solar system, formed 4.5 billion years ago. Its current atmosphere is full of toxic gases and is 90 times thicker than the Earth's atmosphere, and the surface temperature is 864 degrees Fahrenheit (about 462 degrees Celsius), enough to melt lead, so that Venus is a place of death.  But Michael Weiss compared Venus to five climate simulations, each of which showed that Venus could support liquid water and temperate climates for at least 3 billion years, with temperatures as high as 122 degrees Fahrenheit (50 degrees Celsius) and as low as 68 degrees Fahrenheit (20 degrees Celsius), until some cause of release of carbon dioxide from rocks 750 million to 700 million years ago changed Venus ’ s climate.  Astronomers in the past thought that Venus was too close to the Sun to maintain liquid water on the surface, but all the simulations created by the Michael Weiss team found that the surface temperature of Venus allows liquid water to persist.  These simulations show that Venus underwent a rapid cooling phase after its formation, and the atmosphere began to fill with carbon dioxide, but if it is similar to Earth's evolution, the atmospheric carbon dioxide will be absorbed by the surface silicates, and the composition of the atmosphere gradually becomes a combination of nitrogen and a small amount of carbon dioxide and methane, providing stability.  However, a mysterious event about 700 million years ago caused carbon dioxide from the surface rocks of Venus to escape into the atmosphere and not be absorbed back, and such a large amount of carbon dioxide caused the greenhouse effect to get out of control.  Researchers believe that the mysterious event may be volcanic activity, because magma releases carbon dioxide into the atmosphere, and as the magma cools, the carbon dioxide can no longer be absorbed back to the surface, but the reasoning needs to be further proved.  Michael Wei said that the importance of this research is to re-understand the "Venus region", where the planet is still possible to maintain liquid water and temperate climate, and in the future, we will continue to explore the mysterious events in the end, the cooling rate after the formation of Venus, whether there is real water on the surface, carbon dioxide only once or more issues. Title: There is no life in the closest star system to Earth.
Content: Alpha Centauri made a harsh verdict on whether there is life on exoplanets Alpha Centauri tried to find out American astrophysicists.  Scientists from the Georgia Institute of Technology and NASA conducted studies of the celestial bodies of the nearest star system to us.  Alpha Centauri is the closest to the Sun and historically the most known to mankind triple star system.  In the night sky it can be seen with the naked eye.  It was from there that scientists and science fiction writers expected to meet space caravans of aliens.  Astrophysicists from the Georgia Institute of Technology, together with NASA experts, conducted a series of studies of the star system in the hope of finding inhabited worlds.  With the help of modeling the orbits of the proposed exoplanets and the influence on them of the gravity of the three luminaries of Alpha Centauri, they were able to establish that the development of complex life depends mainly on the stability of the tilt of the axis of rotation of the proposed planet.  This largely depends on the stability of the climate, allowing the development of living organisms.  Our Earth in this sense can be considered almost a standard.  The axis is slightly inclined relative to the plane of the orbit and its oscillations are minimized due to the gravity of our satellite.  “If we didn ’ t have the moon, the tilt of the Earth ’ s axis could change by about 60 degrees.  Perhaps then the Earth would look like Mars, ” says study leader Billy Quarles.  Comparison of the history of the formation of the Earth and Mars, according to scientists, allows you to visualize the theory of the origin, and then the preservation of life.  The axis of rotation of our planet is relatively stable and inclined by 22-24 degrees.  But Mars, without such a large satellite balancer, every 2 million years changes the inclination of its axis from 10 to 60 degrees.  As a result, the condensate of the already rarefied Martian atmosphere from the white caps at the poles turns into a cold ice belt of the equator.  In such extreme conditions, the planet is simply not able to support the evolution of complex life forms.  That's the system Alpha Centravra scientists have made a harsh verdict - it is highly likely uninhabited.  There's good news, though.  According to astrophysicists, even if suitable exoplanets are not found near the Sun, they can be a little further, in other star systems, the number of which in the universe is infinite.  Andrey Sidorenko.  TV Center.

Title: Fantasies and reality. Which of the world powers will be the first to write their Martian chronicles
Content: In the story, Soviet cosmonauts go to the aid of aliens who have suffered an accident near Mars.  Starring Otar Koberidze (left) and Boris Borisenok / A shot from the film “Dream towards ” / 1963 Roscosmos this year plans to study the question of how to change the human body at the level of genetic engineering for flights into deep space.  The project will involve the Institute of Biomedical Problems of the Russian Academy of Sciences (RAS), the Federal Biomedical Agency, as well as medical institutions of the Ministry of Health.  What is happening in the industry today and how to return our country to unconditional leadership in space, was understood by “Evening Moscow ”.  I think Yuri Gagarin would be disappointed if, having looked into the relatively near future, he found out that his country, which opened the door to a new world for humanity, stopped on the threshold and with incomprehensible politeness skips ahead of competitors.  On April 16, when we were still not cool off from the lush celebrations associated with astronautics Day, NASA signed a contract worth almost $3 billion, entrusting Space X with the development of the HLS Starship lander, which should take two astronauts to the moon, and a week later bring them home.  If such an agreement had been concluded in our country, it would have been a much more valuable contribution to the continuation of the Gagarin case than all the articles and films about the first cosmonaut taken together.  It is planned that Starship will replace the existing space transportation systems Falcon 9, Falcon Heavy and Dragon, which are also created by Space X.  The strategic goal of Starship goes beyond Earth and lunar orbits and involves a manned flight to Mars.  With the modernization of the ship in the future, its versions will be able to make interstellar flights.  One of the quick and obvious opportunities to cover costs is commercial suborbital flights within the Earth over long distances.  A hundred years ago, Mars was the cherished dream of the Russian man.  Red Count Alexei Tolstoy wrote a wonderful story about the Red Planet "Aelita".  Engineer Friedrich Zander, whose name is one of the Moscow streets, formulated a romantic motto: "Forward to Mars!"  Colonization of Mars was part of the schedule of space conquest, compiled by Konstantin Tsiolkovsky.  According to the main theorist of astronautics, the research base on the moon was supposed to appear in 2015.  The industrial development of Mars, as well as Venus and Mercury, is attributed to the sky-high distance - 2700.  In the atmosphere of romantic dreams and technological challenges, the genius of Sergei Korolev was formed, who in the early 1960s, even before the Americans, sent 5 spacecraft to Mars.  The first launches ended in failure, but in 1962, a Soviet satellite first approached the Red Planet and conducted important experiments.  Unfortunately, our dream of Mars has moved to America.  Previously, the descendants of the conquerors of the West looked at Mars with childish ignorance — like the way American tourists walk around Paris.  In 1938, a radio play based on Wells ’ book War of the Worlds caused widespread panic.  But now three American spacecraft are operating in the orbit of Mars, and two rovers are on the surface.  Elon Musk ’ s ambitions have matured in a competitive atmosphere.  In addition to NASA, plans for flights to Mars are hatched by private companies Lockheed Martin, Boeing, Sierra Nevada Corporation. frame from the film "The Martian" / 2015 The owner and chief engineer of the company Space X Elon Musk promises the first manned flight to Mars in 2024-2026 years.  And by 2050, according to his vision, a million earthlings will move to Mars.  Architectural bureaus are already creating projects of Martian dwellings, physiologists are thinking about the Martian diet, and biochemists are making plans to change the Martian atmosphere to acceptable parameters.  Almost inevitably, terrestrial settlers on Mars will feed on insects that will provide them with proteins.  Europeans to withstand such a diet will be extremely difficult, so with a high probability to master Mars will come from Asia.  Elon Musk understands that an expedition to Mars, which, under optimal ballistic conditions, will take 6 months in one direction, carries a huge risk.  The first colonists clearly will not be able to quickly (and perhaps never) return to Earth.  Musk said, “Are you ready to die?  If there is no problem with that, you are a great candidate! ”  However, the businessman himself is not going to Mars.  There is no doubt that when the time comes, there will be no escape from those who want it.  The first analysis of the expedition to Mars was made immediately after World War II by Werner von Braun, who at that time was sitting without a job, hiding the SS uniform and waiting for an invitation to the United States.  But these were theoretical quirks.  At the beginning of the space age, thanks to energy and dedication, the Queen of the USSR was the undisputed leader in interplanetary flights, having carried out a number of unique expeditions to the nearest celestial objects.  Unfortunately, gradually our attraction to the stars weakened.  I think this is largely due to the fact that cosmonautics ceased to serve as a propaganda argument in the dispute between the two superpowers.  Our interplanetary plans are modest.  2022 is a joint mission with Europe to Mars on our Proton M rocket and with the Russian Kazachok landing platform.  In 2021, we are going to launch the Luna-25 spacecraft with a lander.  The last flight of the machine to the moon took place in 1976.  Then there will be more machines.  And in 2030, Dmitry Rogozin promises a manned expedition to the moon.  Photo: twitter.com / roscosmos The success of Russian plans depends on whether it will be possible to bring to mind the family of missiles "Angara".  There are doubts about this, if only for the reason that work on “Angara ” has been underway since the 1980s.  One has to wonder how in five years Elon Musk managed to put into orbit the Falcon 9 rocket, which was trusted by space crews.  In addition, Elon Musk built a private spaceport Boca Chica in Texas, spending tens of times less money than we threatened on the “East ”.  And for some reason it was without astronomical embezzlement and avalanche of criminal cases...  Mars in the last decade has been the main object of attraction for spacecraft.  Currently, in the vicinity of the red planet are just three Earth apparatus.  The American mission Perseverance (Perseverance), during which on April 19 (a week after our Cosmonautics Day) on Mars for the first time flew a jet helicopter Ingenuity (Inventiveness) - 3 meters and 40 seconds of flight.  As well as a satellite from the UAE and a Chinese ship.  By the way, the Ingenuity helicopter did not become a pioneer in terms of independent movement in the atmosphere of another planet.  The first such cruise was made in 1985 by the Soviet apparatus Vega-1 in the atmosphere of Venus.  But this era has long passed...  The cost of the Perseverance mission is $2 billion.  If we take into account that the financing of the expedition was started 7 years ago, in terms of money it is quite possible for Roscosmos, whose annual budget even now, after several drops in the ruble, is equal to just $2 billion.  The scientific potential of Russian cosmonautics, despite all the problems, is still high and allows us to swing at the most difficult tasks.  Where are you, romantics?  Ilona Mask is often called an adventurer who feeds the public with chimerical promises.  Without in any way acting as his lawyer, I note that it is precisely such accusations that ordinary people threw at the great inventors and innovators.  From Archimedes to Tsiolkovsky, they walked in eccentrics, and many, like Korolev and Babilov, were innocent victims.  The phenomenon of Elon Musk is a contradictory mosaic, but for us two fundamental points are important.  First: Musk fuels public interest in science and serves as a magnet for attracting ambitious and curious young people to research.  We would like such popularizers, but they are not visible on our horizon.  And the second.  Elon Musk is the first private trader who came with his ideas in space.  This is a mandatory stage in the development of the industry, but in Russia, unfortunately, entrepreneurs do not look at the stars.  No one even went to space tourists.  They prefer to lie in a hammock on the grass at home.  Elon Musk / Photo: twitter.com / mfame _ guru Incidentally, 20 years ago Elon Musk came to Russia twice, but he was not yet a billionaire.  The self-confident young man offered cooperation in the creation of new rocket technology for manned flights with a distant eye on the Martian expedition.  Our officials considered the businessman a frivolous person, because they were confident that only the state could deal with space. Title: Air & Space (USA): a million people on Mars? It is possible. But the colonists will have to change their diet and learn to eat crickets – Rambler
Content: Air & Space (USA): a million people on Mars? It is possible.  But the colonists will have to change their diet and learn to eat crickets A self-sufficient population of a million people could appear on Mars within 100 years.  At first, 12 people will land there, after which numerous spacecraft should begin transporting passengers about once every 26 months.  But will humans be able to have children on Mars?  And how to solve the problem with nutrition?  A sustainable and self-sufficient population of one million people could appear on Mars within 100 years, according to a new study with modeling elements conducted by Kevin Cannon and Daniel Britt of the University of Central Florida.  In their study, they relied on a plan drawn up by Elon Musk of SpaceX.  To begin with, he planned a landing on the Red Planet of 12 people, after which numerous spacecraft should begin to carry passengers, from 100 to 200 people per flight, which will be carried out at each opportunity approximately once every 26 months.  Population growth will be ensured both by immigration and by the birth of children on Mars.  Cannon and Britt in their study show that four of the five main "consumables" necessary for Martian settlements (energy, water, oxygen and building materials) can be mined on the surface of Mars in sufficient quantities.  On Mars, only food can not be obtained from raw materials.  So how do we solve the food problem?  The authors propose to grow plants, breed insects and engage in meat cattle breeding of cellular genetic direction.  In the past, it was suggested to grow plants quite often, but it is very important to plant high-calorie crops in order to feed so many people.  Breeding insects is also very useful, as it will give a large number of calories per unit area.  For these purposes, homemade crickets are best suited, and they are already used in some cereal bars.  Protein-rich foods can also be obtained from cells grown in bioreactors.  Interestingly, fish on Mars will be more popular than cage-grown meat, because this culture can be preserved at lower temperatures (about 20 degrees Celsius), while warm-blooded animal cells need 37 degrees Celsius.  To me such ideas and extrapolations seem very intriguing.  But life on Mars may not be as easy as it seems, even if people will enjoy the fruits of technological progress.  Growing plants in Martian soil will be very difficult, because there are large amounts of chloric acid salt and other chemicals in sediments.  The same authors conducted another study on this topic, using soil close in composition to Martian.  Now: their plants died quickly, and earthworms suffocated in this land.  Biological factors must also be taken into account.  It is far from clear whether people will be able to easily give birth to children on Mars, because Martian gravity is only 38% of Earth ’ s.  The human body adapts to earthly conditions, and when the constant physical quantity is two-thirds less than usual, unexpected complications may occur.  Martian farmers may face other problems, including unfamiliar plant diseases that will destroy crops, causing hunger among the settlers.  The upside is that efficient and sustainable food production technologies on Mars can benefit many more people adapting to climate change on Earth, and therefore can prove invaluable to our entire civilization.  Musk ’ s idea of a million people living on Mars is unlikely to materialize in the near future.  But it ’ s becoming more real as NASA ’ s independent planetary protection watchdog recently issued new recommendations that could lead to a relaxation of sterility requirements when landing in certain areas of Mars where local life is unlikely to exist.  If people come to the Red Planet in passenger spacecraft to settle there, they will most likely settle in these places.  Air & Space (USA)

Title: Earth is attacking. What will China, the United States and the Emirates look for on Mars?
Content: On the night of July 15, the UAE will send its first orbiter to Mars.  Also in July, the launch of their research missions planned by China and the United States.  What and how they will look for on the red planet, says Focus October 30, 1938, the United States was engulfed in mass panic.  People called newspapers and police stations, believing that the Earth had been attacked by the Martians.  This reaction was caused by the radio play of the novel by H.G. Wells "War of the Worlds", which the audience took at face value.  After almost 100 years, we know for sure that the Martians will not arrive, because they do not exist, and in general - if there is life on the Red Planet, then microscopic and well hidden.  Earth has been conquering Mars with varying success for more than half a century.  This year, humanity will make an unprecedented breakthrough towards the Red Planet: three countries will send research missions to it at once.  Hope Country: United Arab Emirates Start date: July 15, 2020  Arrival time: February 2021 Type of research vehicle: orbiter Mission duration: 1 Martian year (687 Earth days) Mission objectives: to provide a holistic picture of the Martian atmosphere and weather The times when space exploration was the monopoly of superpowers are long past.  Today, more and more countries and private companies are looking to the stars, and the United Arab Emirates seems to want to be among the pioneers.  The UAE may become the first Arab state to launch an interplanetary mission.  The UAE did not pursue a more ambitious goal of landing on the planet – in the history of Mars exploration, there were far more failed attempts to do this than successful ones.  Preferably confined to an orbital probe.  The research apparatus with a mass of 1.3 tons will make a full orbit around the planet every 55 hours, then approaching it for 20 thousand km, then moving away to 43 thousand.  On board, it will carry infrared and ultraviolet spectrometers, as well as a camera that can not only take pictures, but also shoot video in 4K resolution.  With the help of these tools, Arab scientists want to carefully study the Martian atmosphere, to understand the mechanisms due to which it loses much needed oxygen on Earth.  In addition, they are interested in the weather systems of Mars.  Thanks to the features of the orbit of the probe, they will be able to observe how the weather changes throughout the entire Martian days (24 hours).  38 minutes of Earth time) at one point or another on the planet.  This year, the UAE is sending a probe to Mars, and in 100 years they want to build a city there Data that researchers will receive during the mission will not settle in closed laboratories.  The UAE plans to share them with colleagues from 200 scientific institutions around the world in the hope that the new information will help to better understand the history and mechanisms of functioning of the Martian climate.  However, the Arab mission to Mars does not only pursue scientific goals.  Its organizers hope that the conquest of the neighboring planet will inspire young people and help educate a new generation of scientists and engineers - specialists who can prove that the Emirates is more than just a country with rich oil deposits.  “It is a matter of the future of the UAE and our survival, ” said Omran Sharaf, the head of the mission.  In the view of local scientists, Mars does play a significant role in the future, and perhaps in the survival of the state.  After all, they plan to build an entire city on the Red Planet within the next century.  With an eye on all this, it is obvious that for their first "scout" they chose the most appropriate name - "Al Amal", which means "Hope".  Question to Heaven Country: China Start date: July 23, 2020  Arrival time: February 2021 Type of research vehicle: Mars rover, orbiter and lander Planned mission duration: Rover - 90 sols (equal to 92 Earth days), probe - 1 Martian year (687 Earth days) Mission objectives: study of the magnetosphere, ionosphere and atmosphere of Mars, mapping of terrain, observation of dust storms, study of the composition of rocks and soil, mineral distribution Another debutant in the conquest of Mars will be China.  Local scientists decided to act on a much larger scale than their Arab counterparts.  They will send a rover, landing and orbiters to Mars.  The mission was named Tianwen-1 (Questions to Heaven) after a poem written more than 2,000 years ago.  Each machine has its own task.  For example, the probe, which will be located in the orbit of Mars, will study the geological structure and natural conditions of the planet, as well as transmit data to Earth.  On the lander lies perhaps the most important part of the mission - the actual delivery of equipment to Mars.  This process takes about seven minutes, but this time period is called “seven minutes of nightmare ”.  It depends on China whether it will have its own research apparatus on another planet or it will simply deliver a heap of expensive, high-tech garbage there.  China will name all missions to study other planets Tianwen ("Questions to the Sky") - after the ancient work of the poet Qu Yuan Landing will be broken down into four stages.  First, the aerodynamic brake will slow the device from 4.8 km / s to 460 m / s.  Then the parachute will open, which will reduce the speed to 95 m / s., and then reverse engines will go in the course.  They'll slow the lander down to 3.5 m / s.  The final stage of braking starts at a mark of only 100 m from the surface of the planet.  Ideally, it will end with a soft landing, after which the rover will smoothly move to the surface of the planet.  The first Chinese rover will be equipped with several scientific instruments, including a GPR.  With the help of this device, he will be able to literally look underground.  Earlier this year, this tool helped archaeologists without excavation to make a map of the ancient Roman city, which for many years rests underground.  The rover will not have to search for lost settlements, but he will be able to examine underground geological objects with the help of GPR.  As in the case of the Arab mission to Mars, the Chinese pursue not only scientific goals.  First, it will be a major test of the country ’ s technological achievements.  Secondly, it has a strong reputation subtext.  China already has a successful lunar program – in January last year, its Chang ’ e 4 research apparatus was the first in history to make a soft landing on the far side of the moon.  In early summer, the country launched the last satellite in its global navigation system, which will compete with the American GPS.  Conquering Mars will strengthen China ’ s position as the world ’ s leading space power.  Perseverance and resourcefulness Country: USA Start date: July 30, 2020  Arrival time: February 18, 2021 Type of research vehicle: Rover and helicopter Planned duration of the mission: 1 Martian year (687 Earth days) Mission objectives: search for traces of the existence of life in the past, collect samples, prepare for future missions with the participation of people In the conquest of Mars, the United States is the leader.  The local aerospace agency NASA was the first to deliver a research probe to the Red Planet, the first to land a lander there that lasted longer than a few seconds, its rovers were the first to wheel on the surface of another world.  Today, three of its probes orbit Mars, two more research vehicles are working on the surface of the planet, and soon they will be joined by another.  NASA will send a new rover Perseverance (“Perseverance ”).  The American space agency has a tradition, according to which the names for rovers come up with schoolchildren.  NASA did not deviate from it this time.  The name of the rover "Perseverance" was born in the head of seventh-grader Alexander Mazer, who believed that this feature of human character should be immortalized in it.  In an essay in which the student explained his choice, he noted that in the conquest of Mars, humanity can wait for many difficulties, but it is perseverance that will not allow him to give up and help move towards the goal, no matter what.  However, Perseverance can boast not only a loud name.  Despite its resemblance to Curiosity, which has been traveling on Mars since 2012, the new rover has the most modern technical equipment. Content: South Korea ’ s Samsung Group Vice President Lee Jae-yong was sentenced to two and a half years in prison in January for bribing former President Park Geun-hye ’ s confidants.  As the government and business sectors recently asked the government to pardon Li, he appeared in court again on Thursday (22) on charges of fraud and stock price manipulation, the first appearance of the company after about three months.  According to South Korean media reports, 52-year-old Li Jae-rong dressed in a black suit and white shirt to appear in court.  Lee Jae-yong appeared in court 10 minutes before the start of the trial. In addition to answering that the judge did not want a jury, Lee Jae-yong remained silent.  Prosecutors alleged that in the process of promoting the merger of Samsung C & T and Cheil Industries in 2015, Samsung executives deliberately published false information to raise the share price of First Woven and depress the share price of Samsung Property in order to boost Li Zaihong ’ s acquisition of shares after First Woven was acquired by Samsung Property to become the largest shareholder and strengthen his influence on the Samsung Group.  If Li is convicted of fraud and stock price manipulation, his sentence may be increased.  Lee has so far served half of his sentence, which is 15 months.  South Korea ’ s government faces growing pressure from business and opposition parties to pardon Lee.  Utilizing Lee Jae-yong ’ s global network will help safeguard South Korea ’ s vaccine supply, according to the Federation of South Korean Industries.  Park Jen, a conservative lawmaker, also said that South Korea ’ s investment in U.S. semiconductor production will ensure that South Korea receives vaccines from the United States.  Russia plans to withdraw from the International Space Station from 2025, space agency chief Dmitry Rogozin said on Wednesday, with President Vladimir Putin's approval, Russia will build its own space station and hopes to put it into orbit by 2030, a plan that reportedly costs $6 billion (about HK $46.6 billion).  If successful, it will open a new chapter in Russia ’ s space exploration and end more than two decades of U.S.-Russian cooperation on the International Space Station.  Russian Deputy Prime Minister Yuri Borisov told Russian television last weekend that Moscow would notify its partners to leave the International Space Station from 2025.  Russia ’ s Interfax news agency reported that Rogozin said it plans to put the space station into orbit by 2030, and unlike the International Space Station, it is likely that there will not be permanent members of the Russian space station, because the space station ’ s orbit will expose the astronauts to high radiation, but Russian astronauts can go, and the space station will also use artificial intelligence and robots.  He added that Russia is ready to consider allowing foreign space visitors, “but the space station must be national … If you want to do things well, you have to do it yourself. ”  Since 1998, Russian cosmonauts have cooperated with astronauts from the United States and 16 other countries on missions to the International Space Station, one of the areas in which Moscow has worked closely with Washington.  However, the US-Russian relationship is in crisis due to issues such as human rights and hacking.  NASA ’ s Perseverance successfully extracted oxygen from the Martian atmosphere The recent mission of the Mars rover Perseverance successfully converted carbon dioxide from the Martian atmosphere into breathable pure oxygen, NASA said on Wednesday.  NASA said that the device, called MOXIE (Mars Oxygen In-Situ Resource Utilization Experiment), is the size of a toaster, and uses extreme heat to separate oxygen atoms from carbon dioxide molecules through electrolysis work. MOXIE successfully generated about 5 grams of oxygen, which can allow an astronaut to breathe for 10 minutes.  This feat marks the first time humans have extracted natural resources available for human use from the environment of another planet.  Oxygen content in the Martian atmosphere is extremely low, carbon dioxide accounts for 95% of the Martian atmosphere, and the rest is mainly composed of molecular nitrogen and argon.  Adequate oxygen supply is key to human exploration of Mars, experts believe that astronauts living and working on Mars may need 1 ton of oxygen to maintain their needs for a year, and believe that it is more practical to convert oxygen on Mars than to transport 25 tons of oxygen from Earth.  MOXIE ’ s operating concept is to produce 10 grams of oxygen per hour.  NASA says scientists plan to run the MOXIE device at least nine more times over the next two years, under different conditions and at different speeds. Title: "ice" shelter that will protect astronauts from adverse factors on the surface of Mars » DailyTechInfo
Content: Since people who will arrive on Mars will have to spend several months or even years on the surface, they will need a safe haven that will protect them from temperature changes and from cosmic radiation breaking through the thin and rarefied atmosphere of the planet.  Moreover, for the construction of such shelters, it will be necessary to use local materials as much as possible, because the delivery of the necessary amount of composition for the manufacture of special concrete from the Earth is not yet feasible.  Scientists and experts from NASA's Langley Research Center have come up with a simple and effective solution to the above problem.  In the project developed by them shelter Mars Ice Home as the main protective layer is used ordinary ice, obtained from water extracted from the atmosphere of Mars.The design of the shelter Mars Ice Home is a large inflatable torus, closed on top of a spherical dome of a sufficiently thick layer of ice.  All the structural elements that need to be delivered from Earth are quite light and compact, and in the final design of the structure, in addition to water, some other materials that can be mined on the surface of the Red Planet are used.  In addition, the water from which the protective dome will be made can be later recycled and from it can be obtained fuel for refueling the Mars Ascent Lander spacecraft, which will take people from the surface back to orbit.  The main disadvantage is that it will take at least 400 days to extract the necessary amount of water from the atmosphere of Mars.  This problem can be solved by sending a pre-automated expedition to Mars, which will include robots that will create a foundation, pump up the shell of the shelter, collect enough water and build an ice dome during the time that people will fly to Mars.  This approach will avoid the need for hasty construction of shelter or burying deep underground immediately after the arrival of people on the planet.Mars Ice Home is still only an exciting project, not worked out to the smallest details.  However, it can serve as a starting point for other designers and specialists who will be able to produce elegant and complete solutions to the problems associated with the long stay of people on the surface of the Red Planet.

Title: Martian organics formed thanks to natural batteries
Content: Scientists seem to have uncovered the secret of the origin of organic matter in meteorites that came from the Red Planet.  The list of participants in the process sounds like this: water, volcanic rocks, electricity.  What is nice is that such processes can take place on many bodies of the solar system.  Scientists seem to have uncovered the secret of the origin of organic matter in meteorites that came from the Red Planet.  The formation of organic matter occurs due to natural “accumulators ” consisting of water, salts and volcanic rocks.  Such conclusions are made in a scientific article published in the journal Science Advanced by a group led by Andrew Steele (Andrew Steele) from the Carnegie Scientific Institute in the USA.Recall that proteins, fats, carbohydrates, DNA, RNA and many other molecules, without which it is impossible to imagine a living organism, belong to organic substances.  Of course, not all organic matter is an integral part of living beings or is formed with their participation, so it is not necessary to equate organic matter with life. However, the presence of such molecules is the most important condition for the appearance of the biosphere.  Apparently, only organic chemistry can provide the variety, flexibility and complexity of chemical processes that are necessary for the existence of even the most primitive microbe.  In 2012, a team led by Steele studied carbon from organic molecules found in ten Martian meteorites.  The researchers came to two conclusions, pleasant and not so.  The good news is that this organics originated on Mars (rather than being brought in by pollution on Earth).  The bad news: it is not a product of the vital activity of living organisms; how was it formed in this case?  This is what the authors of a recent study found out. "Identification of the processes during which organic carbon compounds are formed on Mars is of great interest to determine its habitability potential," says Steel.Scientists used three samples of Martian meteorites.  The first is Tissint, which fell in Morocco in 2011.  The second is Nakhla, discovered in Egypt in 1911.  The third was NWA 1950, found in Morocco in 2001.  In all these celestial stones previously found inclusions of Martian organics.Meteorites were subjected to the most careful analysis.  Among the methods used were both the usual viewing of the sample in an optical microscope, and Raman spectroscopy, translucent electron microscopy, nanoscale mass spectrometry of secondary ions, X-ray absorption near the absorption edge (X-ray absorption near-edge structure) and other methods with names incomprehensible to the average person. Thanks to all these methods, the authors thoroughly studied the chemical composition and fine structure of organic inclusions and the surrounding rocks.  By the way, it turned out that the organics of meteorites are extremely similar to the substances found on the Red Planet by the MSL mission.  The detailed information obtained allowed scientists to draw conclusions about what processes could lead to the formation of these substances. It turned out that one of the necessary ingredients are volcanic minerals such as spinel.  On the Red Planet, rich in ancient volcanoes, there is no shortage of such material.  The second important component is liquid water, in huge concentrations containing various salts (in particular, perchlorates).  Such brines have never been directly detected on Mars, but, according to experts, they can exist there almost everywhere.  Finally, the third element of the “magic potion ” is carbon dioxide.  It is also, to put it mildly, not in deficit: the Martian atmosphere consists of it almost completely.  For a while, there is something like a natural battery.  As a result, organic compounds are formed from carbon CO2 and hydrogen of water. "The discovery that a natural system can essentially form a small battery based on corrosion, which controls electrochemical reactions between minerals and the surrounding liquid, has serious consequences for astrobiology," says Steele. Indeed, it turned out that the synthesis of organic matter does not need exotic conditions or components.  All the necessary ingredients are quite common for Mars, which is either already proven (volcanic minerals and carbon dioxide), or assumed (brines).  Moreover, a similar process can take place on bodies such as Europa or Enceladus.  Recall that earlier "33Live.RuNauka" (nauka.vesti.ru) wrote about how a record amount of organic matter was discovered on Mars, as well as that life in the crust of the planet could be supported by radiation.

Title: On Earth found able to survive on Mars bacteria
Content: A microorganism capable of surviving in harsh Martian conditions has been discovered by scientists from the National University of Australia in Canberra.  We are talking about one of the strains of cyanobacteria living in hot springs and geysers. In the course of the experiment, strains of bacteria Chroococcidiopsis thermalis, when the light level was lowered to "Martian" values, continued to grow and produced nutrients - organic substances necessary for life, the article notes. Title: Converting Martian salt water into oxygen and fuel with a new technology
Content: New technology allows astronauts to convert Martian saltwater into oxygen and fuel when they land on the Red Planet in 2033.  There is water on Mars, but most of it is frozen, and the rest is mixed with salt, making it useless for future astronauts who plan to land on the planet by 2033.  Now, a team of researchers at Washington University in St. Louis has developed a system that converts unusable water into fuel and oxygen.  The system uses electricity to convert saltwater into oxygen and hydrogen, and has been found to work in the Martian atmosphere at temperatures as low as -33 degrees Fahrenheit.  The saltwater electrolyser produces 25 times more oxygen than NASA ’ s MOXIE, which launched in July 2020 with the Mars 2020 rover and aims to produce a small amount of oxygen on Mars.  Vijay Ramani of the University of Washington said the technology is just as useful on Earth as it is on Mars because it can turn the oceans into a source of oxygen and fuel.  According to Inverse, the device has two parts around it, one of which separates water to form hydroxyl ions and the other separates water again to produce oxygen.  Although the technology is currently being developed on Earth, it is expensive and likely will not be able to withstand the freezing temperatures of Mars.  Ramani and other researchers decided to build a portable version of the technology that could operate on the Red Planet continuously without the need to heat or purify the water source.  Research scientist and first author of the study, Shrihari Sankarasubramanian, said: “Water-soluble perchlorates (so-called impurities) are actually functional in a Mars-like environment because they prevent water from freezing and also improve the performance of the electrolaser system by reducing electrical resistance.  The study is based on data from NASA ’ s Phoenix Mars Lander, which touched Mars in 2008.  Scientists know that in order to live on Mars, even temporarily, astronauts would have to produce some of their needs, especially oxygen for breathing and fuel for travel to Earth or beyond on the Red Planet.  NASA's Mars Endurance rover is currently traveling to Mars by carrying instruments that use electrolysis at high temperatures.  The researchers hope to work with NASA to further develop the system in the future.  End of message.

Title: Mars Rover Perseverance successfully tested the device to extract oxygen from the Martian atmosphere
Content: An experimental device called MOXIE (Mars Oxygen In-Situ Resource Utilization Experiment) was first tested on April 20, and this test was recognized as successful: for an hour of operation, the installation the size of a conventional toaster was able to produce more than 5 grams of oxygen, writes Newsru.  The atmosphere of Mars is almost 96% carbon dioxide (CO2).  The MOXIE unit is capable of converting this carbon dioxide into oxygen and carbon monoxide (CO, carbon monoxide), which is a by-product of the processing and is released back into the atmosphere.  The process of processing carbon dioxide occurs by electrolysis of solid oxides at a temperature of 800 degrees Celsius.  During operation, the device captures carbon dioxide, passes through a filter to remove dust and compresses it, providing pressure at ground level.  The gas then passes through a heated electrolysis cell, which consists of several layers of nickel alloy and ceramics.  Ceramic elements of the cell are able to conduct current at high temperature - they pass oxygen ions and trap carbon monoxide.  The outer surface of MOXIE is covered with a thin layer of gold.  This coating protects the MOXIE surface from heating, protecting the rover electronics located next to the instrument.  Future astronauts: breathe easier.  The MOXIE technology demonstration aboard @ NASAPersevere successfully extracted oxygen from the thin Martian atmosphere — a critical component for life support on the Red Planet and rocket fuel for the trip home. https: / / t.co / HOsguer. hYgkP pic.twitter.com / SwL0etf9Uu — NASA JPL (@ NASAJPL) April 21, 2021 The maximum estimated performance of MOXIE is up to 10 grams of oxygen per hour.  The test program includes at least nine more tests over two years.  These tests will be carried out under different conditions to assess the performance of the plant.  In the future, more large-scale oxygen production on Mars may come in handy for practical purposes.  First, oxygen is used as an oxidizing agent for rocket fuel.  For example, to launch a rocket with four astronauts from Mars to Earth requires about 7 tons of fuel and 25 tons of oxygen.  The ability to produce this amount of oxygen during the astronauts ’ stay on Mars will prevent this oxygen from being delivered from Earth – delivering a large and productive oxygen generator modeled on MOXIE would be a more practical solution.  Secondly, oxygen, which makes up 21% of the Earth's atmosphere, is needed for breathing - four astronauts will be enough one ton of oxygen for a year on Mars.  We will remind, the Rover Perseverance landed in the area of 45-kilometer crater Jezero, named after the village in Bosnia and Herzegovina.  This crater is located on the western edge of the Isis Plain (a giant impact crater north of the equator of Mars).  As scientists suggest, in ancient times in the area of ​ ​ the crater Ezero was a river delta, where organic matter and other potential traces of microorganisms that could have lived on Mars about 3 billion years ago could have been collected.  The crater itself was then filled with water and was a lake.

Title: Scientists have found organisms that can give rise to life on Mars
Content: Scientists have found organisms that can give rise to life on Mars 16.02.2021, 14: 58 They are able to grow and multiply in the conditions of the red planet.  New experiments have shown that cyanobacteria, also known as blue-green algae, can successfully grow in Martian atmospheric conditions.  Of course, a few more ingredients will be needed, but when humans get to Mars, they will be able to create life support systems based on cyanobacteria for the human habitat, writes nv.ua.  "Here we show that cyanobacteria can use the gases available in the Martian atmosphere, at low overall pressure, as a source of carbon and nitrogen," said astrobiologist Cyprien Verso from the University of Bremen in Germany.  "Under these conditions, cyanobacteria retained their ability to grow in water containing only Martian dust, and they could be used to feed other microbes.  This can help make long-term missions to Mars sustainable, ” the authors of the study believe.  All types of cyanobacteria produce oxygen as a byproduct of photosynthesis, and even today they are an invaluable source of it.  For several years, scientists have speculated whether we could use the ability of cyanobacteria to produce oxygen to live on Mars.  This will bring additional benefits.  The atmosphere of Mars consists mainly of carbon dioxide (95 percent) and nitrogen (3 percent), which are fixed by cyanobacteria, turning them into organic compounds and nutrients, respectively.  However, atmospheric pressure on Mars is a big problem.  The total pressure there is less than 1% of Earth ’ s — from 6 to 11 GPa: this is too small for the presence of liquid water, while the partial pressure of gaseous nitrogen — from 0.2 to 0.3 GPa — is not enough for their metabolism.  But recreating the atmosphere, like on Earth, would be too expensive: gases would have to be imported.  So the researchers were looking for a middle ground: an atmosphere close to Martian, which allows cyanobacteria to grow well.  The authors have developed a bioreactor called Atmos, which has an atmospheric pressure of about 10 percent of Earth ’ s, but uses only what can be found on Mars, albeit in inverted proportions: 96 percent nitrogen and 4 percent carbon dioxide.  The bioreactor also included water that can be obtained on Mars from melting ice, which in some places is abundant on the surface, and a simulator of Martian regolith, a mixture of minerals created here on Earth using only what can be found on Mars.  The team chose the type of nitrogen-fixing cyanobacteria that preliminary trials showed was most likely to thrive under these conditions, Anabaena sp.  PCC 7938, and tested it in a variety of conditions.  The researchers concluded that nitrogen-fixing, oxygen-producing cyanobacteria can be grown on Mars at low pressure under controlled conditions using exclusively local ingredients.  From cyanobacteria, sugar, amino acids and other nutrients can be obtained to feed other crops, which can then be used for other purposes, such as the production of medicines.  Atmos was designed to test whether cyanobacteria can be grown under certain atmospheric conditions rather than for maximum efficiency, and the parameters of the bioreactor will depend on many factors in the mission to Mars, including the payload and mission architecture.  However, now that the concept has been proven, the team can begin work on optimizing the bioreactor system that could one day save us life on Mars. Title: Soviet missions to Mars: how the Soviet Union studied the Red Planet
Content: The first successful Soviet Martian mission was to send to the "red planet" automatic interplanetary station of the third generation Mars-2.  Mars-2 was designed to explore Mars both from its orbit and directly from the surface of the planet.  The Mars-2 AMS consisted of an orbital station (an artificial satellite for exploring Mars) and a lander.  Navigation in space was carried out with the help of orientation to the Sun, the star Canopus and the Earth.  The Soviet Union planned to carry out serious research work on Mars, for this purpose the AMC had all the necessary equipment: an infrared photometer to study the surface relief by measuring the amount of carbon dioxide, an ultraviolet photometer to determine the density of the upper atmosphere.  Cosmic ray particle counter and many other instruments.  The lander was also automated and configured for autonomous operation and control.  The station was launched from the Baikonur Cosmodrome on May 19, 1971.  The flight of the station to Mars lasted more than 6 months.  The flight was carried out according to the program and, as they say, nothing foreshadowed trouble, only at the last stage (the most important, it should be admitted), due to incorrect calculations, the lander entered the atmosphere at an angle greater than the set one, the parachute system was ineffective in such conditions and, having passed through the atmosphere of Mars, the device crashed.  To the honor of our country, our lander, although it crashed, still became the first artificial object on the planet.  The orbital station for more than eight months carried out complex studies of Mars, having made 362 turns around the planet during the work.  The next Russian Martian mission was more successful.  When developing the Mars-3 program, the shortcomings of the previous launch were taken into account.  Launched nine days after Mars-2, the Mars-3 station successfully reached Martian orbit six months later.  The lander for the first time in history made a soft landing on the surface of the “red planet ”.  After one and a half minutes of preparatory period, the device began to work and began to broadcast a panorama of the surrounding surface, but after 14 and a half seconds, the “Martian show ” ended.  “Show ” this, of course, can be called with a big stretch: AMC transmitted only the first 79 lines of the photo-television signal, which represented a gray background without a single detail, the same happened with the broadcast from the second telefotometer.  Various versions of incorrect operation of the devices were assumed: corona discharge in the antennas of the transmitter, damage to the battery... but the final decision on the reasons for the failure was not made.  No, the Martians did something.  Mars-4 July 21, 1973 from the Baikonur cosmodrome was launched AMS Mars-4.  204 days after launch, on February 10, 1974, the spacecraft flew at a distance of 1,844 km from the surface of Mars.  Twenty-seven minutes before that, single-line optical-mechanical scanners — telophotometers — were turned on, with the help of which panoramas of two regions of the surface of Mars were taken (in the orange and red-infrared ranges).  For the first time in the practice of domestic cosmonautics, four spacecraft participated in the flight.  Mars-4 had many tasks: studying the distribution of water vapor on the disk of the planet, determining the gas composition and density of the atmosphere, measuring the flow of electrons and protons on the flight path and the planet, studying the spectra of the own glow of the atmosphere of Mars and many others.  The main task of Mars-4 was to communicate with automatic stations on the surface of Mars.  The Mars-4 spacecraft photographed Mars from a flight path.  On photographs of the surface of the planet, which are of very high quality, you can distinguish details up to 100 m in size.  This makes photography one of the main means of exploring the planet.  With its help, using color filters by synthesizing negatives, color images of a number of areas of the surface of Mars were obtained.  Color images are also of high quality and are suitable for areological-morphological and photometric studies.  Unfortunately, Mars 4 did not fulfill all the tasks assigned to it.  Mars 5 was launched four days after the launch of Mars 4.  The tasks that were assigned to him were not very different from the previous mission.  The Mars-5 station successfully entered orbit around the planet, but immediately there was a depressurization of the instrument compartment, as a result of which the station lasted only about two weeks.  The scientific instruments placed on the Mars 5 station were intended mainly for studying a number of important characteristics of the planet's surface and near-planetary space from orbit.  The device was equipped with a liman-alpha photometer, designed jointly by Soviet and French scientists, and designed to search for hydrogen in the upper atmosphere of Mars.  Installed on board the magnetometer made measurements of the magnetic field of the planet.  To measure the surface temperature, an infrared radiometer was intended, operating in the range of 8-40 microns.  The artificial satellite of Mars "Mars-5" transmitted to Earth new information about the planet and the surrounding space; from the orbit of the satellite obtained high-quality photos of the Martian surface, including color.  Studies of the magnetic field in the Martian space, conducted by the apparatus, confirmed the conclusion made on the basis of similar studies of the spacecraft "Mars-2, -3", that near the planet there is a magnetic field of about 30 gamma (7-10 times greater than the value of the interplanetary unperturbed field carried by the solar wind).  It was assumed that this magnetic field belongs to the planet itself, and Mars 5 helped to get additional arguments in favor of this hypothesis.  Similar measurements from the Mars-5 spacecraft directly measured the temperature of atomic hydrogen in the upper atmosphere of Mars for the first time.  Preliminary data processing showed that this temperature is close to 350 ° K.  Despite the fact that the work of the station did not last long, during its work, numerous information was obtained about Mars, its atmosphere and magnetic field.  Another of our lander was on Mars thanks to the AMS Mars-6, launched from the Baikonur cosmodrome on August 5, 1973.  Sadly, this time there was no soft landing.  During the descent, there was no digital information from the MX 6408M device, but with the help of the Zubr, IT and ID devices, information was obtained on overloads, temperature and pressure changes.  Just before landing, communication with the SA is lost.  The last telemetry received from him confirmed the issuance of a command to turn on the soft landing engine.  The new appearance of the signal was expected 143 seconds after the disappearance, but this did not happen, however, the data obtained during the descent has already yielded significant results and made a great contribution to the study of Mars.  The lander Mars 6 landed on the planet, for the first time transmitting to Earth data on the parameters of the Martian atmosphere obtained during the descent.  Mars-6 measured the chemical composition of the Martian atmosphere using a radiofrequency mass spectrometer.  Shortly after the opening of the main parachute, the analyzer's opening mechanism worked, and the Martian atmosphere gained access to the instrument.  Preliminary analysis suggests that the content of argon in the atmosphere of the planet can be about one-third.  This result is of fundamental importance for understanding the evolution of the Martian atmosphere.  Pressure and ambient temperature measurements were also carried out on the lander; the results of these measurements are very important both for expanding knowledge of the planet and for identifying the conditions in which future Martian stations should operate.  Together with French scientists, a radio astronomy experiment was also performed - measuring the radio emission of the Sun in the meter range.  Receiving radiation simultaneously on Earth and on board a spacecraft hundreds of millions of kilometers away from our planet, allows you to restore a three-dimensional picture of the process of generating radio waves and obtain data on the streams of charged particles responsible for these processes.  In this experiment, another task was solved - the search for short-term bursts of radio radiation, which can, as expected, occur in distant space due to explosive phenomena in the cores of galaxies, supernova flares and other processes.  Mars-7 was launched on August 9, 1973.  The Mars mission failed.  The lander passed 1400 kilometers from the surface of Mars and went into space.  Thus, the target program of Mars-7 was not fulfilled, but, making an autonomous flight, the lander retained its operability and transmitted information to the flight vehicle via radio lines KD-1 and RT-1.  Communication with the Marsa-7 spacecraft was maintained until March 25, 1974.  During the work of Mars-7 in September-November 1973, a connection was recorded between the increase in the flow of protons and the speed of the solar wind.  Preliminary processing of the data of the Mars-7ob spacecraft of the radiation intensity in the resonant Lyman-alpha atomic hydrogen line made it possible to estimate the profile of this line in interplanetary space and determine in it two components, each of which makes approximately equal contribution to the total radiation intensity. Title: On Mars, the level of oxygen increased sharply
Content: Oxygen levels on Mars soared 5 13.11.2019, 13: 36 1,762 Why?  NASA experts conducted an analysis of seasonal changes in the composition of the atmosphere of Mars, data about which was sent by the Curiosity apparatus.  It turned out that the concentration of oxygen in the atmosphere of the planet every spring increases dramatically, and scientists do not understand why.  This is reported by slashgear.com.  For six years, the rover collected data on the atmosphere of Mars, analyzed them and sent them to Earth.  From these data, it becomes clear that the planet's atmosphere contains 95% carbon dioxide, 2.6% nitrogen, 1.9% argon, 0.16% oxygen and 0.06 carbon monoxide.  However, on Mars there is a phenomenon of molecular circulation, which is associated with seasonal changes in pressure in winter and spring.  With nitrogen and argon, the situation is similar to what the researchers predict.  With oxygen, everything is different - in the spring its content in the atmosphere of the planet begins to increase sharply and only in the fall falls to the level predicted by known chemical processes.  The amount of oxygen is different each year.  In other words, something produces it first and then removes it.  The last time the level of oxygen in the atmosphere of the red planet exceeded 30%, while in the atmosphere of the Earth it contains about 20%.  Scientists have not yet been able to say exactly what this is related to.  There is an assumption that the change in the proportion of oxygen in the atmosphere of Mars coincides with the change in the level of methane.  The publication in-space.ru specifies that "oxygen and methane can be produced both biologically, for example, by microbes, and abiotic - in chemical processes related to water and soil."

Title: People are preparing for the pollution of Mars - our review
Content: The experiment was conducted on Earth, more precisely, in the stratosphere of our planet.  There, scientists from two space agencies sent a probe with various microorganisms to check how they would behave in the atmosphere of the red planet.  "We successfully tested a new method of placing bacteria and fungi in Martian conditions using a probe sent into the stratosphere," says Marta Filipa Cortezao of DLR.  "Some microbes, especially black mold embryos, were able to survive the journey even after exposure to very high levels of ultraviolet radiation."  Understanding how microorganisms react to space travel and the Martian environment is key to future missions.  One of the motives is that in the search for extraterrestrial life, scientists should be sure that there are no microorganisms brought from Earth.  But there are other threats.  “On long missions to Mars, we need to know that the microorganisms associated with humans would survive on the Red Planet, because some of them can threaten the lives of astronauts, ” says Katarina Zins, one of the main authors of the publication, which appeared in the publication Frontiers in Microbiology.  But such resistant to harsh conditions earthly life forms still harbor additional opportunities.  "Some microbes may be underestimated by us in the exploration of Mars.  But they are able to help us in the production of food and other materials, regardless of the Earth.  This is a key opportunity to survive away from home, ” the expert adds.  According to experts, it is very difficult to reproduce Martian conditions on Earth.  However, this was possible outside the ozone layer.  “We sent microorganisms placed inside the MARSBox (Microbes in Atmosphere for Radiation, Survival and Biological Outcomes experiment), in which both the atmosphere of Mars and the pressure were artificially maintained into the stratosphere during the entire scientific mission, ” explains the essence of the experiment Cortezao.

Title: Found organisms that can survive on Mars
Content: Scientists at the University of Bremen in Germany have found microorganisms that can grow and develop in the Martian atmosphere.  According to the researchers, based on cyanobacteria or blue-green algae, it is possible to create life support systems for people who will live on the surface of Mars.  This is reported in an article published in the journal Frontiers in Microbiology.  Scientists have shown that cyanobacteria can support life by using the gases of the Martian atmosphere as a source of carbon and oxygen, despite the low pressure.  Blue-green algae multiplied in water with a suspension of Martian dust, which makes it possible to use them to feed other living organisms.  In addition, cyanobacteria produce oxygen as a byproduct of photosynthesis.  Researchers have developed an Atmos bioreactor that maintains atmospheric pressure at 10 percent of Earth ’ s and nitrogen and carbon dioxide concentrations of 96 percent and 4 percent, respectively.  These conditions are close to Martian, but differ from them: atmospheric pressure is a percentage of Earth's, and the proportion of carbon dioxide is 95 percent.  Water and a mixture of minerals mimicking Martian regolith were also added to the bioreactor.  For the experiment, the team chose a species of nitrogen-fixing cyanobacteria Anabaena sp.  PCC 7938, which preliminary tests have shown is most likely to thrive in these conditions.  Although the bacteria grew better on a nutrient medium, the researchers also observed growth on Martian regolith.  Then the scientists dried the culture of microorganisms and used it as a substrate for growing E. coli.  This proves that cyanobacteria on Mars can be used to feed crops that, in turn, are suitable for the synthesis of nutrients, including drugs.  Leonid Nemov

passages.title: Bayer lost the first stage of the court in the United States in the case of a potentially carcinogenic herbicide Roundup
passages.passage: This content was published on March 20, 2019.  9: 26 in San Francisco.  March 20.  German chemical company Bayer AG lost the first stage of the trial in the United States in the case of a potentially carcinogenic herbicide Roundup, developed by the American company Monsanto, which since June last year came under the control of Bayer.  According to The Wall Street Journal, a jury in San Francisco ruled that plaintiff Edwin Hardeman contracted cancer as a result of the use of the herbicide Roundup.  During the first stage, only evidence of the potential harm of Roundup and its active substance, glyphosate, was considered.  In the second phase of the trial, which begins on March 20, six jurors must determine whether Monsanto should be held accountable.  Their decision could mean significant financial losses for Monsanto and Bayer, as their turn is waiting for about 11.2 thousand related to Roundup claims.  According to Bloomberg Intelligence analyst Holly Froome, the aggregate payments for all claims could exceed $5 billion.  Another six hearings are already scheduled for 2019.  Shares of Bayer fell more than 10% at the opening of trading in Frankfurt on Wednesday, then the fall slowed to 9.9%.  In August last year, a court in the United States ruled that Bayer should pay $289.2 million to school gardener Diwayne Johnson, who contracted cancer as a result of the use of the herbicide Roundup.  A few months later, the amount was reduced to $78.5 million as a result of Bayer ’ s appeal.  During the second stage, as in the case of D. Johnson, the jury will have to consider the role of Monsanto in concealing data on the dangers of glyphosate.  According to the plaintiffs, the company did not warn buyers of its products that herbicides can lead to cancer.  There is no consensus on the effects of glyphosate, the most common element in herbicides.  The International Agency for Research on Cancer considers this substance "probably carcinogenic", while the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) of the United States claims that glyphosate is safe when used cautiously. passages.passage: Bayer reported an unsuccessful quarter due to the pandemic and lawsuits Bayer published a report for the third quarter, according to which revenue and sales of the company decreased.  The pharmaceutical industry of the corporation tried as a result of the COVID-19 pandemic and legal proceedings.  German chemical-pharmaceutical transnational corporation Bayer published a report for the third quarter of 2020 fiscal year, which states that the manufacturer of medicines suffered due to the coronavirus pandemic, resulting in net losses of the company amounted to $3.2 billion, and revenue decreased by 4.2% to $36.8 billion.  In general, Bayer sales in the third quarter fell by 13.5% compared to the same period of 2019 - to $9.9 billion.  Sales in the pharmaceutical sector decreased by 6.1%, reaching $4.9 billion.  Among the positive aspects, we can note the increase in sales of oral anticoagulant "Xarelto" by 13.8%, which has a special demand in Germany and Russia; ophthalmic drug "Eilea", actively sold in China; anti-cancer drug "Stivarga" by 17.5%, especially in the United States.  COVID-19 is said to have exacerbated the problems Bayer faced after its acquisition of agricultural company Monsanto two years ago.  This summer, the pharmaceutical company pledged to pay $10.9 billion in court compensation for cancer patients from the herbicide Roundup, which went to Bayer from Monsanto.  More than 125,000 people filed their claims.  However, it has not yet been established whether this herbicide causes cancer.  Bayer said it would need an additional $750 million to pay off the debt.  Against the background of litigation, the shares of the drug manufacturer fell to record low values (by 43% since the beginning of the year).  In the second quarter, net losses amounted to $11 billion due to the need to pay compensation.  The company has already paid off its debt in 80,000 lawsuits.  Bayer CFO Wolfgang Nickle stressed that the third quarter was difficult mainly due to problems in the agricultural sector of the corporation.  The company is gradually restoring its position in the field of production of medicines.  Photo: Bayer AG Vladimir Zabolotskikh pharmvestnik

passages.title: Monsanto's second defeat
passages.passage: The second defeat in the US court suffered in the last 8 months Monsanto Company.  On Wednesday, the Federal District of San Francisco ordered the world leader of plant biotechnology to pay more than $80 million to Edwin Hardman.  The 70-year-old farmer, who for 25 years sprayed the most famous herbicide Monsanto Roundup on his site, was diagnosed with cancer of the lymphatic system.  During the trial, which lasted a month, the jury ruled that the plaintiff developed cancer as a result of the use of Roundup (the main active ingredient of which is glyphosate) and that Monsanto did not properly inform consumers about the dangers of its products.  German chemical company Bayer, which owns Monsanto Company today, said it was "disappointed by the jury's decision" and would appeal the verdict.  In the United States, another 11,000 Roundup lawsuits are on the way; six hearings are scheduled this year alone.  Since its purchase of Monsanto last June, Bayer has lost more than 45% of its market value.  The news of the second verdict further plunged into the "red" actions of the chemical giant.  The first person to win the case against Monsanto was school gardener Diwayne Johnson, who used the herbicide extensively.  In August last year, a California court ordered to pay him more than $289 million, later the amount of compensation was reduced to $78 million.
