passages.title: Detecting plastic particles in water bottles
passages.passage: Tests on large company water bottles show that almost all of them contain tiny plastic particles.  In the largest study of its kind, 250 bottles purchased in nine different countries were tested.  The study, led by the press organization Orb Media, found that on average, there are 10 plastic particles per liter of water, each wider than a human hair (more than 100 microns) in diameter.  Manufacturers whose products were tested told the BBC that their factories operate to the highest standard.  The experiments were conducted at New York State University in Fredonia.  Sherry Mason, a chemistry professor at the university who conducted the analysis, told the BBC: “Bottle after bottle, Mark after Mark had plastic particles. ”  “The goal is not to make certain brands conspicuous; this experiment shows that the problem is universal, and plastic has become such a pervasive material in our society that it has found its way into all of the products we consume. ”  There is currently no evidence that microplastics are harmful, but understanding the potential consequences is a matter of scientific investigation.  Commenting on the results, Professor Mason said: “The numbers we see are not catastrophic, but they are a cause for concern.  Experts told the BBC that people in countries where tap water is likely to be contaminated should continue to use bottled water.  Playback of this file on your device is not supported.  Thousands of plastic particles in drinking water bottles from manufacturers have responded to the BBC by insisting that their products meet the highest standards of safety and quality.  They also noted the lack of regulations regulating microplastics and their standard testing practices.  Professor Mason found plastic particles in samples of tap water last year, and other researchers have found them in seafood, beer, sea salt and even air.  The new study comes amid further attention to the increasing penetration of plastic materials into nature following the BBC's second series "Blue Planet", in which Sir David Attenborough highlighted the threat of plastic waste in the oceans.  Aquaphina, Dasani, Evian, Nesli Pure Life and San Pellegrino as internationally recognized products, and Aqua (Indonesia), Bisleri (India), Opura (Mexico), Gerolsteiner (Germany), Minalba (Brazil) and Vahaha (China) as national products were reviewed in this study.  The number of particles smaller than 100 microns (one thousandth of a millimeter per micron) was much higher than the number of particles larger than 100 microns, which averaged 314 particles per liter.  The chemical composition of this group of smaller particles was not confirmed, but Professor Mason said they could also be expected to be plastic.  One obvious question was how the plastic got into the water.  One theory is that due to the amount of polypropylin used in production in the bottle, the process of opening the bottle may cause it to leak into the water.

passages.title: Russia: Environmental issues turn into political issues
passages.passage: For the second month in Russia, the scandal continues around the Yadrovo test site near Moscow in the city of Volokolamsk, where mass poisoning of children occurred due to emissions from the test site, after which rallies began.  Protests continue in mid-April, and the city authorities, meanwhile, intend to introduce a state of emergency and solve the problem with the landfill.  The situation in Volokolamsk is a sign of a deeper problem, which is associated with the annual growth of industrial and consumer waste in the country, which has nowhere to go.  The state to solve the problem announced garbage reform, which for various reasons has stalled.  The environmental crisis, meanwhile, has begun a transition into a political channel, which does not bode well for the authorities, experts say.  According to Rosstat, from 2006 to 2016, the formation of production and consumption waste in the country increased by 55% to 5.4 billion tons per year, and in comparison with 2003 - by 108%.  Data for 2017 are not available.  The special representative of the President of the Russian Federation on environmental protection, ecology and transport Sergey Ivanov at the end of 2016 estimated at 100 billion tons the volume of accumulated in the country for all time undisposed waste.  The accumulation of waste appears to be related to the underdeveloped recycling market.  Secondary use, according to the Ministry of Natural Resources, is limited to the processing of 50% of industrial waste and 10% of municipal waste.  Everything else is sent to landfills and buried in landfills.  In turn, representatives of Rosprirodnadzor said in 2016 that the existing capacities of the landfills will be enough to receive new waste for another 3-4 years.  The most acute situation with the loading of landfills is in the Central, North-Western, Volga, Siberian and North Caucasian districts.  The lack of space not only at landfills, but also at landfills, is stated in the “Final report of the ONF for the Year of Ecology 2017 ”.  “There are almost no free and suitable places for waste disposal, ” the authors write.  The situation is aggravated by the spread of illegal garbage dumps, which usually appear in forests.  At the end of 2017, Sergei Ivanov estimated the number of illegal dumps in the country at 60 thousand (it is assumed that the number of legal dumps is 4 thousand).  The cost of eliminating environmental damage from their work, he estimated at “trillions of rubles. ”  Political scientist Georgy Bovt is convinced that the work of illegal dumps is carried out with the tacit permission of the regional authorities.  “There are very specific people here.  Municipal authorities simply cannot fail to be a part of it.  For the sake of curiosity, ask in the search engine “garbage collection ”.  You will receive dozens of proposals, most of which will be related to illegal business, ” he writes in his column.  “The profitability of the shadow business associated with waste, only slightly lost [until 2016] revenues from drug trafficking, ” said Deputy Minister of Natural Resources Artem Sidorov.  Hazards to nature and health Landfills and landfills contain a considerable amount of waste that is hazardous to nature and health.  According to the latest report of Rosprirodnadzor, published in February 2018, at the beginning of 2016 in Russia there were 743 objects with a particularly harmful impact on the environment.  And these are only those that were at that time on the account of the department.  Due to the lack of separate garbage collection, extremely toxic materials fall into the garbage dumps, including mercury (from lamps and thermometer), nickel, cadmium and lead (from batteries and accumulators), etc.  The country has no capacity to accommodate or dispose of such waste, follows from the data of the meeting of the board of the Ministry of Natural Resources on plans for 2018.  Every year, the volume of waste of the second and first hazard classes (highly hazardous and extremely hazardous) increases by 300 thousand and 30 thousand tons, respectively.  In addition to waste officially recognized as dangerous, landfills, according to the ONF report, get cheap types of packaging, which “can have a strong negative impact on nature and health. ”  “For example, foamed polystyrene, which is almost not processed and when heated emits carcinogens.  In addition, manufacturers of goods often use multicomponent packaging, that is, consisting of and assembled from various materials, which, due to the need for additional separation into components, are usually ignored by processors as unprofitable and as a result they are sent to landfill, ” the report says.  According to the analytical department of the Federation Council, the contribution of environmental problems to public health is estimated by different specialists in the range of 10-50%, and in the near future “due to the progressive environmental crisis and the low level of material provision of medical institutions ” this contribution will grow to 60% or more.  However, according to the requirements of the World Health Organization, this contribution should not exceed 25%.  To solve the problem in 2015, Russia launched a reform in the field of waste management, which involves the gradual abandonment of burial in favor of recycling.  According to the idea of the government, manufacturers and importers of certain goods must either process the waste themselves or pay an environmental fee to the budget, with the money of which the state is going to build processing plants and organize a system of separate reception of garbage.  However, on the one hand, the collection rate was below the expectations of the state, and, on the other hand, state bodies for more than two years of reform, according to the ONF, could not combine their efforts and distribute powers among themselves.  In this regard, according to the authors of the report, the situation in this area has practically not changed.  Against this background, the authorities continue to develop plans for the construction of incinerators, which contradicts the ideas of reform.  In particular, four such enterprises are planned to be built in the Moscow region, another in Tatarstan.  However, according to ONF, the new plants in the Moscow region will not cope with the influx of garbage from the capital.  Their total capacity is 2.8 million tons per year, while the actual formation of only municipal waste in Moscow, subject to export to other subjects, is 6 million tons, the report says.  Moreover, three of the four plots allocated for the plants are located in a densely populated recreational area, which causes discontent among the local population, according to the report of the Council for the Development of Civil Society and Human Rights under the President of the Russian Federation.  “To date, neither Rosprirodnadzor nor the population has the necessary information about the detailed characteristics of the incinerators planned for construction and convincing evidence of their safety for the environment and the health of citizens, ” the report says.  As a result of the operation of these plants, ash and slag will be formed in the amount of 30% of the initial volume of waste, which have a higher hazard class and require placement on special landfills. Title: Bayer lost the first stage of the court in the United States in the case of a potentially carcinogenic herbicide Roundup
Content: This content was published on March 20, 2019.  9: 26 in San Francisco.  March 20.  German chemical company Bayer AG lost the first stage of the trial in the United States in the case of a potentially carcinogenic herbicide Roundup, developed by the American company Monsanto, which since June last year came under the control of Bayer.  According to The Wall Street Journal, a jury in San Francisco ruled that plaintiff Edwin Hardeman contracted cancer as a result of the use of the herbicide Roundup.  During the first stage, only evidence of the potential harm of Roundup and its active substance, glyphosate, was considered.  In the second phase of the trial, which begins on March 20, six jurors must determine whether Monsanto should be held accountable.  Their decision could mean significant financial losses for Monsanto and Bayer, as their turn is waiting for about 11.2 thousand related to Roundup claims.  According to Bloomberg Intelligence analyst Holly Froome, the aggregate payments for all claims could exceed $5 billion.  Another six hearings are already scheduled for 2019.  Shares of Bayer fell more than 10% at the opening of trading in Frankfurt on Wednesday, then the fall slowed to 9.9%.  In August last year, a court in the United States ruled that Bayer should pay $289.2 million to school gardener Diwayne Johnson, who contracted cancer as a result of the use of the herbicide Roundup.  A few months later, the amount was reduced to $78.5 million as a result of Bayer ’ s appeal.  During the second stage, as in the case of D. Johnson, the jury will have to consider the role of Monsanto in concealing data on the dangers of glyphosate.  According to the plaintiffs, the company did not warn buyers of its products that herbicides can lead to cancer.  There is no consensus on the effects of glyphosate, the most common element in herbicides.  The International Agency for Research on Cancer considers this substance "probably carcinogenic", while the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) of the United States claims that glyphosate is safe when used cautiously. Title: Detecting plastic particles in water bottles
Content: Tests on large company water bottles show that almost all of them contain tiny plastic particles.  In the largest study of its kind, 250 bottles purchased in nine different countries were tested.  The study, led by the press organization Orb Media, found that on average, there are 10 plastic particles per liter of water, each wider than a human hair (more than 100 microns) in diameter.  Manufacturers whose products were tested told the BBC that their factories operate to the highest standard.  The experiments were conducted at New York State University in Fredonia.  Sherry Mason, a chemistry professor at the university who conducted the analysis, told the BBC: “Bottle after bottle, Mark after Mark had plastic particles. ”  “The goal is not to make certain brands conspicuous; this experiment shows that the problem is universal, and plastic has become such a pervasive material in our society that it has found its way into all of the products we consume. ”  There is currently no evidence that microplastics are harmful, but understanding the potential consequences is a matter of scientific investigation.  Commenting on the results, Professor Mason said: “The numbers we see are not catastrophic, but they are a cause for concern.  Experts told the BBC that people in countries where tap water is likely to be contaminated should continue to use bottled water.  Playback of this file on your device is not supported.  Thousands of plastic particles in drinking water bottles from manufacturers have responded to the BBC by insisting that their products meet the highest standards of safety and quality.  They also noted the lack of regulations regulating microplastics and their standard testing practices.  Professor Mason found plastic particles in samples of tap water last year, and other researchers have found them in seafood, beer, sea salt and even air. Title: Russia: Environmental issues turn into political issues
Content: For the second month in Russia, the scandal continues around the Yadrovo test site near Moscow in the city of Volokolamsk, where mass poisoning of children occurred due to emissions from the test site, after which rallies began.  Protests continue in mid-April, and the city authorities, meanwhile, intend to introduce a state of emergency and solve the problem with the landfill.  The situation in Volokolamsk is a sign of a deeper problem, which is associated with the annual growth of industrial and consumer waste in the country, which has nowhere to go.  The state to solve the problem announced garbage reform, which for various reasons has stalled.  The environmental crisis, meanwhile, has begun a transition into a political channel, which does not bode well for the authorities, experts say.  According to Rosstat, from 2006 to 2016, the formation of production and consumption waste in the country increased by 55% to 5.4 billion tons per year, and in comparison with 2003 - by 108%.  Data for 2017 are not available.  The special representative of the President of the Russian Federation on environmental protection, ecology and transport Sergey Ivanov at the end of 2016 estimated at 100 billion tons the volume of accumulated in the country for all time undisposed waste.  The accumulation of waste appears to be related to the underdeveloped recycling market.  Secondary use, according to the Ministry of Natural Resources, is limited to the processing of 50% of industrial waste and 10% of municipal waste.  Everything else is sent to landfills and buried in landfills.  In turn, representatives of Rosprirodnadzor said in 2016 that the existing capacities of the landfills will be enough to receive new waste for another 3-4 years.  The most acute situation with the loading of landfills is in the Central, North-Western, Volga, Siberian and North Caucasian districts.  The lack of space not only at landfills, but also at landfills, is stated in the “Final report of the ONF for the Year of Ecology 2017 ”.  “There are almost no free and suitable places for waste disposal, ” the authors write.  The situation is aggravated by the spread of illegal garbage dumps, which usually appear in forests.  At the end of 2017, Sergei Ivanov estimated the number of illegal dumps in the country at 60 thousand (it is assumed that the number of legal dumps is 4 thousand).  The cost of eliminating environmental damage from their work, he estimated at “trillions of rubles. ”  Political scientist Georgy Bovt is convinced that the work of illegal dumps is carried out with the tacit permission of the regional authorities.  “There are very specific people here.  Municipal authorities simply cannot fail to be a part of it.  For the sake of curiosity, ask in the search engine “garbage collection ”.  You will receive dozens of proposals, most of which will be related to illegal business, ” he writes in his column.  “The profitability of the shadow business associated with waste, only slightly lost [until 2016] revenues from drug trafficking, ” said Deputy Minister of Natural Resources Artem Sidorov.  Hazards to nature and health Landfills and landfills contain a considerable amount of waste that is hazardous to nature and health.  According to the latest report of Rosprirodnadzor, published in February 2018, at the beginning of 2016 in Russia there were 743 objects with a particularly harmful impact on the environment.  And these are only those that were at that time on the account of the department.  Due to the lack of separate garbage collection, extremely toxic materials fall into the garbage dumps, including mercury (from lamps and thermometer), nickel, cadmium and lead (from batteries and accumulators), etc.  The country has no capacity to accommodate or dispose of such waste, follows from the data of the meeting of the board of the Ministry of Natural Resources on plans for 2018.  Every year, the volume of waste of the second and first hazard classes (highly hazardous and extremely hazardous) increases by 300 thousand and 30 thousand tons, respectively.  In addition to waste officially recognized as dangerous, landfills, according to the ONF report, get cheap types of packaging, which “can have a strong negative impact on nature and health. ”  “For example, foamed polystyrene, which is almost not processed and when heated emits carcinogens.  In addition, manufacturers of goods often use multicomponent packaging, that is, consisting of and assembled from various materials, which, due to the need for additional separation into components, are usually ignored by processors as unprofitable and as a result they are sent to landfill, ” the report says.  According to the analytical department of the Federation Council, the contribution of environmental problems to public health is estimated by different specialists in the range of 10-50%, and in the near future “due to the progressive environmental crisis and the low level of material provision of medical institutions ” this contribution will grow to 60% or more.  However, according to the requirements of the World Health Organization, this contribution should not exceed 25%.  To solve the problem in 2015, Russia launched a reform in the field of waste management, which involves the gradual abandonment of burial in favor of recycling.  According to the idea of the government, manufacturers and importers of certain goods must either process the waste themselves or pay an environmental fee to the budget, with the money of which the state is going to build processing plants and organize a system of separate reception of garbage.  However, on the one hand, the collection rate was below the expectations of the state, and, on the other hand, state bodies for more than two years of reform, according to the ONF, could not combine their efforts and distribute powers among themselves.  In this regard, according to the authors of the report, the situation in this area has practically not changed.  Against this background, the authorities continue to develop plans for the construction of incinerators, which contradicts the ideas of reform.  In particular, four such enterprises are planned to be built in the Moscow region, another in Tatarstan.  However, according to ONF, the new plants in the Moscow region will not cope with the influx of garbage from the capital.  Their total capacity is 2.8 million tons per year, while the actual formation of only municipal waste in Moscow, subject to export to other subjects, is 6 million tons, the report says.  Moreover, three of the four plots allocated for the plants are located in a densely populated recreational area, which causes discontent among the local population, according to the report of the Council for the Development of Civil Society and Human Rights under the President of the Russian Federation.  “To date, neither Rosprirodnadzor nor the population has the necessary information about the detailed characteristics of the incinerators planned for construction and convincing evidence of their safety for the environment and the health of citizens, ” the report says.  As a result of the operation of these plants, ash and slag will be formed in the amount of 30% of the initial volume of waste, which have a higher hazard class and require placement on special landfills.  According to Nikolai Kichigin, associate professor at the Higher School of Urban Studies, there is nothing wrong with burning garbage (in some European countries, according to him, up to 50% of garbage is burned), but provided that the garbage is carefully sorted before this.  But in Russia, this condition has not yet been met.  In addition to the environmental crisis, problems with garbage, according to some experts, caused political difficulties.  According to political scientist Lilia Shevtsova, the events in Volokolamsk, caused by the mass poisoning of children, became one of the reasons for the “blow to the new presidency [of Vladimir Putin]. ”  Rallies in Volokolamsk are a sign of “changes in public consciousness and a serious challenge to the authorities, ” said Maxim Artemyev, an associate professor at the Russian State Humanitarian Institute.  “Environmental issues are at the forefront of the agenda of political and public life.  A few years ago in Italy, the garbage collection crisis in Naples was one of the reasons for the fall of the government of Roman Prodi, ” he said.

Title: Russia: Environmental issues turn into political issues
Content: For the second month in Russia, the scandal continues around the Yadrovo test site near Moscow in the city of Volokolamsk, where mass poisoning of children occurred due to emissions from the test site, after which rallies began.  Protests continue in mid-April, and the city authorities, meanwhile, intend to introduce a state of emergency and solve the problem with the landfill.  The situation in Volokolamsk is a sign of a deeper problem, which is associated with the annual growth of industrial and consumer waste in the country, which has nowhere to go.  The state to solve the problem announced garbage reform, which for various reasons has stalled.  The environmental crisis, meanwhile, has begun a transition into a political channel, which does not bode well for the authorities, experts say.  According to Rosstat, from 2006 to 2016, the formation of production and consumption waste in the country increased by 55% to 5.4 billion tons per year, and in comparison with 2003 - by 108%.  Data for 2017 are not available.  The special representative of the President of the Russian Federation on environmental protection, ecology and transport Sergey Ivanov at the end of 2016 estimated at 100 billion tons the volume of accumulated in the country for all time undisposed waste.  The accumulation of waste appears to be related to the underdeveloped recycling market.  Secondary use, according to the Ministry of Natural Resources, is limited to the processing of 50% of industrial waste and 10% of municipal waste.  Everything else is sent to landfills and buried in landfills.  In turn, representatives of Rosprirodnadzor said in 2016 that the existing capacities of the landfills will be enough to receive new waste for another 3-4 years.  The most acute situation with the loading of landfills is in the Central, North-Western, Volga, Siberian and North Caucasian districts.  The lack of space not only at landfills, but also at landfills, is stated in the “Final report of the ONF for the Year of Ecology 2017 ”.  “There are almost no free and suitable places for waste disposal, ” the authors write.  The situation is aggravated by the spread of illegal garbage dumps, which usually appear in forests.  At the end of 2017, Sergei Ivanov estimated the number of illegal dumps in the country at 60 thousand (it is assumed that the number of legal dumps is 4 thousand).  The cost of eliminating environmental damage from their work, he estimated at “trillions of rubles. ”  Political scientist Georgy Bovt is convinced that the work of illegal dumps is carried out with the tacit permission of the regional authorities.  “There are very specific people here.  Municipal authorities simply cannot fail to be a part of it.  For the sake of curiosity, ask in the search engine “garbage collection ”.  You will receive dozens of proposals, most of which will be related to illegal business, ” he writes in his column.  “The profitability of the shadow business associated with waste, only slightly lost [until 2016] revenues from drug trafficking, ” said Deputy Minister of Natural Resources Artem Sidorov.  Hazards to nature and health Landfills and landfills contain a considerable amount of waste that is hazardous to nature and health.  According to the latest report of Rosprirodnadzor, published in February 2018, at the beginning of 2016 in Russia there were 743 objects with a particularly harmful impact on the environment.  And these are only those that were at that time on the account of the department.  Due to the lack of separate garbage collection, extremely toxic materials fall into the garbage dumps, including mercury (from lamps and thermometer), nickel, cadmium and lead (from batteries and accumulators), etc.  The country has no capacity to accommodate or dispose of such waste, follows from the data of the meeting of the board of the Ministry of Natural Resources on plans for 2018.  Every year, the volume of waste of the second and first hazard classes (highly hazardous and extremely hazardous) increases by 300 thousand and 30 thousand tons, respectively.  In addition to waste officially recognized as dangerous, landfills, according to the ONF report, get cheap types of packaging, which “can have a strong negative impact on nature and health. ”  “For example, foamed polystyrene, which is almost not processed and when heated emits carcinogens.  In addition, manufacturers of goods often use multicomponent packaging, that is, consisting of and assembled from various materials, which, due to the need for additional separation into components, are usually ignored by processors as unprofitable and as a result they are sent to landfill, ” the report says.  According to the analytical department of the Federation Council, the contribution of environmental problems to public health is estimated by different specialists in the range of 10-50%, and in the near future “due to the progressive environmental crisis and the low level of material provision of medical institutions ” this contribution will grow to 60% or more.  However, according to the requirements of the World Health Organization, this contribution should not exceed 25%.  To solve the problem in 2015, Russia launched a reform in the field of waste management, which involves the gradual abandonment of burial in favor of recycling.  According to the idea of the government, manufacturers and importers of certain goods must either process the waste themselves or pay an environmental fee to the budget, with the money of which the state is going to build processing plants and organize a system of separate reception of garbage.  However, on the one hand, the collection rate was below the expectations of the state, and, on the other hand, state bodies for more than two years of reform, according to the ONF, could not combine their efforts and distribute powers among themselves.  In this regard, according to the authors of the report, the situation in this area has practically not changed.  Against this background, the authorities continue to develop plans for the construction of incinerators, which contradicts the ideas of reform.  In particular, four such enterprises are planned to be built in the Moscow region, another in Tatarstan.  However, according to ONF, the new plants in the Moscow region will not cope with the influx of garbage from the capital.  Their total capacity is 2.8 million tons per year, while the actual formation of only municipal waste in Moscow, subject to export to other subjects, is 6 million tons, the report says.  Moreover, three of the four plots allocated for the plants are located in a densely populated recreational area, which causes discontent among the local population, according to the report of the Council for the Development of Civil Society and Human Rights under the President of the Russian Federation.  “To date, neither Rosprirodnadzor nor the population has the necessary information about the detailed characteristics of the incinerators planned for construction and convincing evidence of their safety for the environment and the health of citizens, ” the report says.  As a result of the operation of these plants, ash and slag will be formed in the amount of 30% of the initial volume of waste, which have a higher hazard class and require placement on special landfills.  According to Nikolai Kichigin, associate professor at the Higher School of Urban Studies, there is nothing wrong with burning garbage (in some European countries, according to him, up to 50% of garbage is burned), but provided that the garbage is carefully sorted before this.  But in Russia, this condition has not yet been met.  In addition to the environmental crisis, problems with garbage, according to some experts, caused political difficulties.  According to political scientist Lilia Shevtsova, the events in Volokolamsk, caused by the mass poisoning of children, became one of the reasons for the “blow to the new presidency [of Vladimir Putin]. ”  Rallies in Volokolamsk are a sign of “changes in public consciousness and a serious challenge to the authorities, ” said Maxim Artemyev, an associate professor at the Russian State Humanitarian Institute.  “Environmental issues are at the forefront of the agenda of political and public life.  A few years ago in Italy, the garbage collection crisis in Naples was one of the reasons for the fall of the government of Roman Prodi, ” he said.

title: "Portrait of a Lady" found

passages.title: The stolen painting returned home.
passages.passage: A painting by Gustav Klimt, a famous Austrian artist, discovered after decades at the site of the robbery, is on display again in its former location.  In February 1997, a painting by Gustav Klimt was stolen from the Ricci Odi art gallery in Piacenza.  The painting, known as “Portrait of a Young Woman, ” was the gallery ’ s most valuable work.  The painting was discovered at the scene of the robbery.  Workers at the Ricci Odi Gallery in Piacenza, after cleaning the outer wall of the gallery, came upon a secret door containing a portrait of a young woman.  Workers discovered the artwork while it was placed in a plastic bag.  Upon the discovery of the painting, the thieves admitted that they had returned the artwork to the scene of the theft.  After one of Caravaggio ’ s paintings stolen from a church in Sicily in 1969, it is considered the second most valuable art stolen in Italy.  The portrait of a young woman doubled in value when, shortly before it disappeared, an art student noticed that the portrait of the young woman had been painted on the portrait of another young woman.  It became the only painting by Gustav Klimt in the art world that has been painted twice.  Due to the closure of galleries and museums in Italy due to the spread of the coronavirus, it has not been possible for the public to visit the work in person, and officials of the Ricci Odi Gallery have provided the opportunity to visit the painting in its former exhibition.  Upon the return of the painting, the gallery ’ s director, Massimo Ferrari, referred to it as part of his gallery identity.  This painting is one of the works that Klimt created in the last years of his life.  End of message.

passages.title: Krimut painting worth 79.3 billion won found in garbage bag
passages.passage: A Klimt painting worth 79.3 billion won was found in a garbage bag.  13, 2019 07: 35. by Ren Bo-mei bom @ donga.com.  Gustav Klimt ’ s supposedly stolen work reappeared in the museum ’ s walls 22 years later.  Italy's Ansa news agency reported on the 10th (local time) that in Piacenza, the Ricky Ordi Museum of Modern Art has found a work suspected to have been lost in 1997, which is believed to be Klimt's Portrait of a Woman (photo).  According to the "Daily Telegraph" reported that on the same day, the museum's gardener found a metal plate attached to the wall while cleaning the climbing tiger on the outer wall of the building.  After opening, you see a gap connecting the inner and outer walls of the building with a black bag inside.  The gardener said, “At first I thought it was rubbish. ” Laura Bonpanti, the museum ’ s deputy curator, said:“ From the privy seal or seal on the back of the work, it seems to be the real thing. ”  It seems to be the best Christmas gift. ” If it is authentic, its value is estimated to reach 60 million euros (about 79,306.92 billion won).  The head of the Cultural Advisory Committee of Piacenza did not rule out the possibility of the theft of the works and their return.  "Immediately after the theft, we conducted a thorough search of all parts of the museum and the courtyard at the time," the person in charge said in the square.  The strangest thing is that the work is in very good condition.  I can't see it staying there for 22 years. '  In 1996, about 10 months before her disappearance, Portrait of a Woman was revealed to be the only work Klimt had ever painted on any of his other works.  At the time, X-ray analysis showed that Portrait of a Woman was supposedly painted on another of Klimt's paintings, Portrait of a Young Woman, which had been stolen in 1912.  한국어

passages.title: Found in the wall of the gallery picture Klimt recognized as the original
passages.passage: ROME, 17 Jan – RIA Novosti, Alexander Logunov.  Experts confirmed the authenticity of the found picture of the Austrian artist Gustav Klimt “Portrait of a woman ”, which was stolen in 1997 from a gallery in the Italian Piacenza, told RIA Novosti the head of the staff of the police department of the city Filippo Sordi.  The "Portrait of a Woman", believed to have been stolen from the Ricci Oddy Gallery since 1997, was discovered in mid-December by gardeners who were cleaning the walls from ivy.  The picture lay in a niche behind a partition in a black bag, which was hidden by thick vegetation.  Doubts art critics in the authenticity of the find was caused by the fact that the picture remained in excellent condition, being, presumably, abandoned by robbers 22 years ago.  “The research lasted a month from the discovery, experts appointed by the prosecutor ’ s office confirmed the authenticity of the painting, ” Sordi said.  According to him, now there are new examinations of the canvas for the left fingerprints and other evidence that can shed light on the mystery of the abduction of the portrait.  According to one of the most common versions, the kidnappers left the picture in a secluded place immediately after the crime, but were unable to return for it because of the uproar.  "As long as the painting is kept in a guarded safe by the Italian Central Bank, it remains at the disposal of the judiciary," Sordi said.  Despite the fact that the authenticity of the work has been established, investigators do not yet give an answer to another question of this detective story: whether the picture could all this time be in the chamber or was secretly planted there shortly before the discovery.  As told RIA Novosti, the president of the gallery of contemporary art Massimo Ferrari, on the day of discovery of the picture, the museum staff managed to get acquainted with the state of the picture.  “It ’ s too well preserved, especially when it comes to small scratches and a back with traces of wax.  If it was a fake, it would have to be made by a skilled craftsman, ” said the head of the gallery.  According to him, the traces that could be seen on the surface of the painting were quite comparable with other paintings of the museum.  In the conversation, Ferrari, however, does not hide the disappointment that the timing of the return of the portrait of Klimt to Piacenza remains unknown.  A small gallery has already planned for this year a series of events with the participation of the acquired canvas.  "Portrait of a Woman" was included in the list of the most wanted works of world art.  A small picture in green colors hit the front pages of newspapers a year before it disappeared.  In 1996, an 18-year-old student, flipping through a catalog of Klimat ’ s works in the gallery, drew attention to another female portrait that no one had seen since 1912.  As shown by x-rays conducted at the local hospital and subsequent studies, Klimt rewrote an earlier picture, which presumably depicted his deceased muse Maria Munch.  A new version of the painting, painted between 1916-1918, was soon acquired by the Italian collector Ricci Oddi.  However, to appear before the public with a newly acquired history of the picture was not destined.  In February 1997, shortly before the opening of the exhibition dedicated to Klimt, the painting was stolen.  In the conditions of the beginning of repair and turmoil around the organization of the show, the disappearance of the canvas was noticed a few days later.  The main version of the theft was built around the frame found on the roof, which gave reason to believe that the picture was pulled up with a fishing rod, but it is possible that the thieves entered the gallery from the front entrance - it is still unclear whether the outdated alarm system worked.  In 2016, new details emerged in the form of DNA samples found on the frame, but nothing has been reported since.

passages.title: In Italy found “Portrait of a woman ” Klimt, stolen 22 years ago
passages.passage: December 12, Minsk / Corr.  BELTA /.  In the Italian city of Piacenza found a picture of the Austrian artist Gustav Klimt “Portrait of a woman ”, the cost of which is 60 million euros, reports the BBC.  It is noted that the painting was stolen in 1997 from the Galleria Ricci Oddi and was included in the list of the most wanted art objects in Italy.  The frame of the picture was then found on the roof of the gallery, and the work of art itself disappeared.  On December 10, 2019, the painting was discovered by an employee who cleaned the walls of the gallery from ivy.  He found a cavity closed by an iron door in the wall, and inside in a black plastic garbage bag lay a picture.  The gallery staff found out that this is Klimt ’ s “Portrait of a Woman ”.  They studied the seals and stamps on the back of the canvas and believe that the find is the original.  However, finally its authenticity will be established by experts.  Gustav Klimt painted Portrait of a Woman in 1916 or 1917.  In 1925, the painting was bought by the aristocrat from Piacenza Giuseppe Ricci Oddi.  The collector bequeathed his collection of art to the city, and after his death they were exhibited in the gallery in his name.  "Portrait of a Woman" was the most valuable exhibit of the Ricci Oddi Gallery.

passages.passage: The Belverede.Wien Museum Image caption A critic of the Kiss has called the "Image of Humanity" all great artists have a handwriting that is more or less recognizable, but if there is one whose works can be truly considered unique and imitable, Gustav Klimt is an Austrian artist of the early 20th century.  Klimt is hard to imitate in the days of “mechanical reproduction, ” as Walter Benjamin put it, but no one has ever been able to replicate the artist ’ s work with that stunning focus, balance, and harmonic balance.  Klimt ’ s art has a twofold and sometimes contradictory aspect: he was on the one hand a pioneer and avant-garde artist of his time who influenced a generation of modernist artists with impressive innovations and bold experiences, but on the other hand he based his art on simple and familiar themes that are beautiful and caressing to every eye.  Klimt ’ s paintings are easily adapted to any look and “eat ” the wall of any bedroom, living room or office.  It should not be forgotten that this perfection has been achieved with a lifetime of effort and struggle.  The revolution in the decorative art of Vienna at the beginning of the 20th century and the period known as the "end of the century" or "degeneration" stage was one of the main bases of modern art.  Gustav Klimt, with his revolt against academic painting, is one of the main representatives of the Art Nouveau style, which together with a group of modernist artists affiliated with the Céción exhibition created the Yogendale Steele (Young Style).  Classical and “scholastic ” painters considered Klimt ’ s work to be more of an arrangement and decor that moves away from“ the higher purposes of art. ”  In contrast to Klimt and his friends, they believed that the artist should have complete freedom in creativity and taste testing, and that no authority had the right to set a course for him.  Unlike many of his fellow artists, Klimt studied not at the Vienna School of Art, but at the Academy of Industrial and Applied Arts.  In the first phase of Klimt ’ s career, which he co-operated with his younger brother in a workshop, the combination of artistic creation and craftsmanship forms an intense combination that is both beautiful and “beneficial. ”  In the "Gesst" school, these compositional works, which could be a mixture of painting, sculpture and architecture, were called "art collections".  The aim of these "artisan artists" was to create harmonic forms and eye-catching compositions that can be used both in functional industries such as consumer appliances and furniture, as well as in the decoration of halls, interior decoration and architectural style of facades.  It was a poem of fine writing and color.  He has more than three thousand designs left, revealing his precise look and powerful hand.  Her bold and agile pen in drawing human figures and postures, especially nude women, taught a group of younger artists such as Egon Schiele.  Your client was a great designer.  He has more than three thousand designs left, revealing his precise look and powerful hand.  Her bold and agile pen in drawing human figures and postures, especially nude women, taught a group of younger artists such as Egon Schiele.  Klimt came up with a string of sketches as “metaphors, ” many of which are“ black-haired ” for his larger works and color paintings.  These works usually have a dramatic background or reference, in ancient mythology or tragic heroes, such as Salome, Judith, Danae and Athena.  He was very close to the stage of his career.  In many of these works he has a tendency to symbolism, which was one of the main trends in the art of the day.  As a passionate poet, he tries to embody general and abstract concepts such as life, death, philosophy, music, lust and jealousy with subtle and symbolic lines and forms.  In a series of colorful designs and paintings, "Hope" is a pregnant woman who is staring at her bulging stomach.  Despite Klimt ’ s mastery of design, he shuns accurate representations of the real world in colorful paintings.  His human figures change shape, along with the wave of lines and the dance of forms.  Klimt always fills the place of the "natural" motif with small and compact designs, so that the main texture of the figures and their surroundings is full of spirit and movement.  The Klimt gives the viewer the freedom to see the work in his own way and to evaluate and interpret it with his own mood.  In his art, he finds something hidden with a profound meaning that cannot be expressed; or he simply looks and moves the eye around the angles of lines, designs, and colors, and enjoys their harmony.  Klimt has something for every view and taste, and approaching his art does not require an expert.  Klimt's paintings are best known for their works known as the "Golden Age" and were created more or less during his artistic maturity, around the age of 40.  His father was an avid engraver and worked with gold.  It can be said that he inherited his love of gold from his father, but his familiarity with Byzantine tiles and paintings undoubtedly contributed to his interest in gold motifs.  Photo copyright Reuters Image caption Gustav Klimt, like Toulouse Lautrec, reproduced his works and marketed them for sale from iconography and the role of saints, not to mention the cleverness or use of gold water, an invention characterized in modern art by Klimt's work.  You have made your beanstalk with earthworms.  In his works, there are usually beautiful, naked and charming women in place of saints.  He may follow the Father ’ s tradition, showing each figure as a “piece of jewelry. ”  Perhaps the most famous of these is "The Kiss".  It all revolves around a love kiss.  Men and women kneel before each other in an ethereal space.  The man is strong, and the woman is strong, and he is strong.  The man ’ s coat is of angular and “hard ” roles, while the woman ’ s coat is covered with round and“ soft ” roles.  He is naked and alone, and does not reveal anything about the position of man or woman.  They are just two ordinary people who are intertwined with two different organs and can belong to any age and culture.  A critic has dubbed this position “the image of humanity. ”  By the end of Klimt ’ s life, the cold and grim charm of Expressionism had filled the air, but Klimt was more inclined to praise the joy of life, the joy of love, and the drink.  Her lively and beautiful nature is best seen in her natural landscapes and female portraits, which she brought to the canvas in the last decade of her life, from 1908 to 1918, with stunning perfection.  In these works, Klimt has achieved a calm and harmonious style that can be felt like a musical drum.  But sometimes in this tender and caressing song, the mood of the tumultuous times is felt, even in lyrical paintings such as Kiss or "Affection", there is a hidden anxiety that tells the lovers to never end this infinite moment.  If they look back, a great disaster awaits them.  Today, some of your church work is everywhere.  Many people have his work at home, enjoy the harmony of colors and the harmonious balance of designs without ever hearing his name.  This year, 150 years after Klimt ’ s birth, his name will be heard more often.

Title: The stolen painting returned home.
Content: A painting by Gustav Klimt, a famous Austrian artist, discovered after decades at the site of the robbery, is on display again in its former location.  In February 1997, a painting by Gustav Klimt was stolen from the Ricci Odi art gallery in Piacenza.  The painting, known as “Portrait of a Young Woman, ” was the gallery ’ s most valuable work.  The painting was discovered at the scene of the robbery.  Workers at the Ricci Odi Gallery in Piacenza, after cleaning the outer wall of the gallery, came upon a secret door containing a portrait of a young woman.  Workers discovered the artwork while it was placed in a plastic bag.  Upon the discovery of the painting, the thieves admitted that they had returned the artwork to the scene of the theft.  After one of Caravaggio ’ s paintings stolen from a church in Sicily in 1969, it is considered the second most valuable art stolen in Italy.  The portrait of a young woman doubled in value when, shortly before it disappeared, an art student noticed that the portrait of the young woman had been painted on the portrait of another young woman.  It became the only painting by Gustav Klimt in the art world that has been painted twice.  Due to the closure of galleries and museums in Italy due to the spread of the coronavirus, it has not been possible for the public to visit the work in person, and officials of the Ricci Odi Gallery have provided the opportunity to visit the painting in its former exhibition.  Upon the return of the painting, the gallery ’ s director, Massimo Ferrari, referred to it as part of his gallery identity.  This painting is one of the works that Klimt created in the last years of his life.  End of message.

Title: Found in the wall of the gallery picture Klimt recognized as the original
Content: ROME, 17 Jan – RIA Novosti, Alexander Logunov.  Experts confirmed the authenticity of the found picture of the Austrian artist Gustav Klimt “Portrait of a woman ”, which was stolen in 1997 from a gallery in the Italian Piacenza, told RIA Novosti the head of the staff of the police department of the city Filippo Sordi.  The "Portrait of a Woman", believed to have been stolen from the Ricci Oddy Gallery since 1997, was discovered in mid-December by gardeners who were cleaning the walls from ivy.  The picture lay in a niche behind a partition in a black bag, which was hidden by thick vegetation.  Doubts art critics in the authenticity of the find was caused by the fact that the picture remained in excellent condition, being, presumably, abandoned by robbers 22 years ago.  “The research lasted a month from the discovery, experts appointed by the prosecutor ’ s office confirmed the authenticity of the painting, ” Sordi said.  According to him, now there are new examinations of the canvas for the left fingerprints and other evidence that can shed light on the mystery of the abduction of the portrait.  According to one of the most common versions, the kidnappers left the picture in a secluded place immediately after the crime, but were unable to return for it because of the uproar.  "As long as the painting is kept in a guarded safe by the Italian Central Bank, it remains at the disposal of the judiciary," Sordi said.  Despite the fact that the authenticity of the work has been established, investigators do not yet give an answer to another question of this detective story: whether the picture could all this time be in the chamber or was secretly planted there shortly before the discovery.  As told RIA Novosti, the president of the gallery of contemporary art Massimo Ferrari, on the day of discovery of the picture, the museum staff managed to get acquainted with the state of the picture.  “It ’ s too well preserved, especially when it comes to small scratches and a back with traces of wax.  If it was a fake, it would have to be made by a skilled craftsman, ” said the head of the gallery.  According to him, the traces that could be seen on the surface of the painting were quite comparable with other paintings of the museum.  In the conversation, Ferrari, however, does not hide the disappointment that the timing of the return of the portrait of Klimt to Piacenza remains unknown.  A small gallery has already planned for this year a series of events with the participation of the acquired canvas.  "Portrait of a Woman" was included in the list of the most wanted works of world art.  A small picture in green colors hit the front pages of newspapers a year before it disappeared.  In 1996, an 18-year-old student, flipping through a catalog of Klimat ’ s works in the gallery, drew attention to another female portrait that no one had seen since 1912.  As shown by x-rays conducted at the local hospital and subsequent studies, Klimt rewrote an earlier picture, which presumably depicted his deceased muse Maria Munch.  A new version of the painting, painted between 1916-1918, was soon acquired by the Italian collector Ricci Oddi.  However, to appear before the public with a newly acquired history of the picture was not destined.  In February 1997, shortly before the opening of the exhibition dedicated to Klimt, the painting was stolen.  In the conditions of the beginning of repair and turmoil around the organization of the show, the disappearance of the canvas was noticed a few days later.  The main version of the theft was built around the frame found on the roof, which gave reason to believe that the picture was pulled up with a fishing rod, but it is possible that the thieves entered the gallery from the front entrance - it is still unclear whether the outdated alarm system worked.  In 2016, new details emerged in the form of DNA samples found on the frame, but nothing has been reported since.

Title: In Italy found “Portrait of a woman ” Klimt, stolen 22 years ago
Content: December 12, Minsk / Corr.  BELTA /.  In the Italian city of Piacenza found a picture of the Austrian artist Gustav Klimt “Portrait of a woman ”, the cost of which is 60 million euros, reports the BBC.  It is noted that the painting was stolen in 1997 from the Galleria Ricci Oddi and was included in the list of the most wanted art objects in Italy.  The frame of the picture was then found on the roof of the gallery, and the work of art itself disappeared.  On December 10, 2019, the painting was discovered by an employee who cleaned the walls of the gallery from ivy.  He found a cavity closed by an iron door in the wall, and inside in a black plastic garbage bag lay a picture.  The gallery staff found out that this is Klimt ’ s “Portrait of a Woman ”.  They studied the seals and stamps on the back of the canvas and believe that the find is the original.  However, finally its authenticity will be established by experts.  Gustav Klimt painted Portrait of a Woman in 1916 or 1917.  In 1925, the painting was bought by the aristocrat from Piacenza Giuseppe Ricci Oddi.  The collector bequeathed his collection of art to the city, and after his death they were exhibited in the gallery in his name.  "Portrait of a Woman" was the most valuable exhibit of the Ricci Oddi Gallery.

Title: Gustav Klimt, a needless artist of experts
Content: The Belverede.Wien Museum Image caption A critic of the Kiss has called the "Image of Humanity" all great artists have a handwriting that is more or less recognizable, but if there is one whose works can be truly considered unique and imitable, Gustav Klimt is an Austrian artist of the early 20th century.  Klimt is hard to imitate in the days of “mechanical reproduction, ” as Walter Benjamin put it, but no one has ever been able to replicate the artist ’ s work with that stunning focus, balance, and harmonic balance.  Klimt ’ s art has a twofold and sometimes contradictory aspect: he was on the one hand a pioneer and avant-garde artist of his time who influenced a generation of modernist artists with impressive innovations and bold experiences, but on the other hand he based his art on simple and familiar themes that are beautiful and caressing to every eye.  Klimt ’ s paintings are easily adapted to any look and “eat ” the wall of any bedroom, living room or office.  It should not be forgotten that this perfection has been achieved with a lifetime of effort and struggle.  The revolution in the decorative art of Vienna at the beginning of the 20th century and the period known as the "end of the century" or "degeneration" stage was one of the main bases of modern art.  Gustav Klimt, with his revolt against academic painting, is one of the main representatives of the Art Nouveau style, which together with a group of modernist artists affiliated with the Céción exhibition created the Yogendale Steele (Young Style).  Classical and “scholastic ” painters considered Klimt ’ s work to be more of an arrangement and decor that moves away from“ the higher purposes of art. ”  In contrast to Klimt and his friends, they believed that the artist should have complete freedom in creativity and taste testing, and that no authority had the right to set a course for him.  Unlike many of his fellow artists, Klimt studied not at the Vienna School of Art, but at the Academy of Industrial and Applied Arts.  In the first phase of Klimt ’ s career, which he co-operated with his younger brother in a workshop, the combination of artistic creation and craftsmanship forms an intense combination that is both beautiful and “beneficial. ”  In the "Gesst" school, these compositional works, which could be a mixture of painting, sculpture and architecture, were called "art collections".  The aim of these "artisan artists" was to create harmonic forms and eye-catching compositions that can be used both in functional industries such as consumer appliances and furniture, as well as in the decoration of halls, interior decoration and architectural style of facades.  It was a poem of fine writing and color.  He has more than three thousand designs left, revealing his precise look and powerful hand.  Her bold and agile pen in drawing human figures and postures, especially nude women, taught a group of younger artists such as Egon Schiele.  Your client was a great designer. Klimt came up with a string of sketches as “metaphors, ” many of which are“ black-haired ” for his larger works and color paintings.  These works usually have a dramatic background or reference, in ancient mythology or tragic heroes, such as Salome, Judith, Danae and Athena.  He was very close to the stage of his career.  In many of these works he has a tendency to symbolism, which was one of the main trends in the art of the day.  As a passionate poet, he tries to embody general and abstract concepts such as life, death, philosophy, music, lust and jealousy with subtle and symbolic lines and forms.  In a series of colorful designs and paintings, "Hope" is a pregnant woman who is staring at her bulging stomach.  Despite Klimt ’ s mastery of design, he shuns accurate representations of the real world in colorful paintings.  His human figures change shape, along with the wave of lines and the dance of forms.  Klimt always fills the place of the "natural" motif with small and compact designs, so that the main texture of the figures and their surroundings is full of spirit and movement.  The Klimt gives the viewer the freedom to see the work in his own way and to evaluate and interpret it with his own mood.  In his art, he finds something hidden with a profound meaning that cannot be expressed; or he simply looks and moves the eye around the angles of lines, designs, and colors, and enjoys their harmony.  Klimt has something for every view and taste, and approaching his art does not require an expert.  Klimt's paintings are best known for their works known as the "Golden Age" and were created more or less during his artistic maturity, around the age of 40.  His father was an avid engraver and worked with gold.  It can be said that he inherited his love of gold from his father, but his familiarity with Byzantine tiles and paintings undoubtedly contributed to his interest in gold motifs. You have made your beanstalk with earthworms.  In his works, there are usually beautiful, naked and charming women in place of saints.  He may follow the Father ’ s tradition, showing each figure as a “piece of jewelry. ”  Perhaps the most famous of these is "The Kiss".  It all revolves around a love kiss.  Men and women kneel before each other in an ethereal space.  The man is strong, and the woman is strong, and he is strong.  The man ’ s coat is of angular and “hard ” roles, while the woman ’ s coat is covered with round and“ soft ” roles.  He is naked and alone, and does not reveal anything about the position of man or woman.  They are just two ordinary people who are intertwined with two different organs and can belong to any age and culture.  A critic has dubbed this position “the image of humanity. ”  By the end of Klimt ’ s life, the cold and grim charm of Expressionism had filled the air, but Klimt was more inclined to praise the joy of life, the joy of love, and the drink.  Her lively and beautiful nature is best seen in her natural landscapes and female portraits, which she brought to the canvas in the last decade of her life, from 1908 to 1918, with stunning perfection.  In these works, Klimt has achieved a calm and harmonious style that can be felt like a musical drum.  But sometimes in this tender and caressing song, the mood of the tumultuous times is felt, even in lyrical paintings such as Kiss or "Affection", there is a hidden anxiety that tells the lovers to never end this infinite moment.  If they look back, a great disaster awaits them.  Today, some of your church work is everywhere.  Many people have his work at home, enjoy the harmony of colors and the harmonious balance of designs without ever hearing his name.  This year, 150 years after Klimt ’ s birth, his name will be heard more often.

Title: The stolen painting returned home.
Content: A painting by Gustav Klimt, a famous Austrian artist, discovered after decades at the site of the robbery, is on display again in its former location.  In February 1997, a painting by Gustav Klimt was stolen from the Ricci Odi art gallery in Piacenza.  The painting, known as “Portrait of a Young Woman, ” was the gallery ’ s most valuable work.  The painting was discovered at the scene of the robbery.  Workers at the Ricci Odi Gallery in Piacenza, after cleaning the outer wall of the gallery, came upon a secret door containing a portrait of a young woman.  Workers discovered the artwork while it was placed in a plastic bag.  Upon the discovery of the painting, the thieves admitted that they had returned the artwork to the scene of the theft.  After one of Caravaggio ’ s paintings stolen from a church in Sicily in 1969, it is considered the second most valuable art stolen in Italy.  The portrait of a young woman doubled in value when, shortly before it disappeared, an art student noticed that the portrait of the young woman had been painted on the portrait of another young woman.  It became the only painting by Gustav Klimt in the art world that has been painted twice.  Due to the closure of galleries and museums in Italy due to the spread of the coronavirus, it has not been possible for the public to visit the work in person, and officials of the Ricci Odi Gallery have provided the opportunity to visit the painting in its former exhibition.  Upon the return of the painting, the gallery ’ s director, Massimo Ferrari, referred to it as part of his gallery identity.  This painting is one of the works that Klimt created in the last years of his life.  End of message.

Title: Found in the wall of the gallery picture Klimt recognized as the original
Content: ROME, 17 Jan – RIA Novosti, Alexander Logunov.  Experts confirmed the authenticity of the found picture of the Austrian artist Gustav Klimt “Portrait of a woman ”, which was stolen in 1997 from a gallery in the Italian Piacenza, told RIA Novosti the head of the staff of the police department of the city Filippo Sordi.  The "Portrait of a Woman", believed to have been stolen from the Ricci Oddy Gallery since 1997, was discovered in mid-December by gardeners who were cleaning the walls from ivy.  The picture lay in a niche behind a partition in a black bag, which was hidden by thick vegetation.  Doubts art critics in the authenticity of the find was caused by the fact that the picture remained in excellent condition, being, presumably, abandoned by robbers 22 years ago.  “The research lasted a month from the discovery, experts appointed by the prosecutor ’ s office confirmed the authenticity of the painting, ” Sordi said.  According to him, now there are new examinations of the canvas for the left fingerprints and other evidence that can shed light on the mystery of the abduction of the portrait.  According to one of the most common versions, the kidnappers left the picture in a secluded place immediately after the crime, but were unable to return for it because of the uproar.  "As long as the painting is kept in a guarded safe by the Italian Central Bank, it remains at the disposal of the judiciary," Sordi said.  Despite the fact that the authenticity of the work has been established, investigators do not yet give an answer to another question of this detective story: whether the picture could all this time be in the chamber or was secretly planted there shortly before the discovery.  As told RIA Novosti, the president of the gallery of contemporary art Massimo Ferrari, on the day of discovery of the picture, the museum staff managed to get acquainted with the state of the picture.  “It ’ s too well preserved, especially when it comes to small scratches and a back with traces of wax.  If it was a fake, it would have to be made by a skilled craftsman, ” said the head of the gallery.  According to him, the traces that could be seen on the surface of the painting were quite comparable with other paintings of the museum.  In the conversation, Ferrari, however, does not hide the disappointment that the timing of the return of the portrait of Klimt to Piacenza remains unknown.  A small gallery has already planned for this year a series of events with the participation of the acquired canvas.  "Portrait of a Woman" was included in the list of the most wanted works of world art.  A small picture in green colors hit the front pages of newspapers a year before it disappeared.  In 1996, an 18-year-old student, flipping through a catalog of Klimat ’ s works in the gallery, drew attention to another female portrait that no one had seen since 1912.  As shown by x-rays conducted at the local hospital and subsequent studies, Klimt rewrote an earlier picture, which presumably depicted his deceased muse Maria Munch.  A new version of the painting, painted between 1916-1918, was soon acquired by the Italian collector Ricci Oddi.  However, to appear before the public with a newly acquired history of the picture was not destined.  In February 1997, shortly before the opening of the exhibition dedicated to Klimt, the painting was stolen.  In the conditions of the beginning of repair and turmoil around the organization of the show, the disappearance of the canvas was noticed a few days later.  The main version of the theft was built around the frame found on the roof, which gave reason to believe that the picture was pulled up with a fishing rod, but it is possible that the thieves entered the gallery from the front entrance - it is still unclear whether the outdated alarm system worked.  In 2016, new details emerged in the form of DNA samples found on the frame, but nothing has been reported since.

Title: In Italy found “Portrait of a woman ” Klimt, stolen 22 years ago
Content: December 12, Minsk / Corr.  BELTA /.  In the Italian city of Piacenza found a picture of the Austrian artist Gustav Klimt “Portrait of a woman ”, the cost of which is 60 million euros, reports the BBC.  It is noted that the painting was stolen in 1997 from the Galleria Ricci Oddi and was included in the list of the most wanted art objects in Italy.  The frame of the picture was then found on the roof of the gallery, and the work of art itself disappeared.  On December 10, 2019, the painting was discovered by an employee who cleaned the walls of the gallery from ivy.  He found a cavity closed by an iron door in the wall, and inside in a black plastic garbage bag lay a picture.  The gallery staff found out that this is Klimt ’ s “Portrait of a Woman ”.  They studied the seals and stamps on the back of the canvas and believe that the find is the original.  However, finally its authenticity will be established by experts.  Gustav Klimt painted Portrait of a Woman in 1916 or 1917.  In 1925, the painting was bought by the aristocrat from Piacenza Giuseppe Ricci Oddi.  The collector bequeathed his collection of art to the city, and after his death they were exhibited in the gallery in his name.  "Portrait of a Woman" was the most valuable exhibit of the Ricci Oddi Gallery.

Title: Gustav Klimt, a needless artist of experts
Content: The Belverede.Wien Museum Image caption A critic of the Kiss has called the "Image of Humanity" all great artists have a handwriting that is more or less recognizable, but if there is one whose works can be truly considered unique and imitable, Gustav Klimt is an Austrian artist of the early 20th century.  Klimt is hard to imitate in the days of “mechanical reproduction, ” as Walter Benjamin put it, but no one has ever been able to replicate the artist ’ s work with that stunning focus, balance, and harmonic balance.  Klimt ’ s art has a twofold and sometimes contradictory aspect: he was on the one hand a pioneer and avant-garde artist of his time who influenced a generation of modernist artists with impressive innovations and bold experiences, but on the other hand he based his art on simple and familiar themes that are beautiful and caressing to every eye.  Klimt ’ s paintings are easily adapted to any look and “eat ” the wall of any bedroom, living room or office.  It should not be forgotten that this perfection has been achieved with a lifetime of effort and struggle.  The revolution in the decorative art of Vienna at the beginning of the 20th century and the period known as the "end of the century" or "degeneration" stage was one of the main bases of modern art.  Gustav Klimt, with his revolt against academic painting, is one of the main representatives of the Art Nouveau style, which together with a group of modernist artists affiliated with the Céción exhibition created the Yogendale Steele (Young Style).  Classical and “scholastic ” painters considered Klimt ’ s work to be more of an arrangement and decor that moves away from“ the higher purposes of art. ”  In contrast to Klimt and his friends, they believed that the artist should have complete freedom in creativity and taste testing, and that no authority had the right to set a course for him.  Unlike many of his fellow artists, Klimt studied not at the Vienna School of Art, but at the Academy of Industrial and Applied Arts.  In the first phase of Klimt ’ s career, which he co-operated with his younger brother in a workshop, the combination of artistic creation and craftsmanship forms an intense combination that is both beautiful and “beneficial. ”  In the "Gesst" school, these compositional works, which could be a mixture of painting, sculpture and architecture, were called "art collections".  The aim of these "artisan artists" was to create harmonic forms and eye-catching compositions that can be used both in functional industries such as consumer appliances and furniture, as well as in the decoration of halls, interior decoration and architectural style of facades.  It was a poem of fine writing and color.  He has more than three thousand designs left, revealing his precise look and powerful hand.  Her bold and agile pen in drawing human figures and postures, especially nude women, taught a group of younger artists such as Egon Schiele.  Your client was a great designer.  He has more than three thousand designs left, revealing his precise look and powerful hand.  Her bold and agile pen in drawing human figures and postures, especially nude women, taught a group of younger artists such as Egon Schiele.  Klimt came up with a string of sketches as “metaphors, ” many of which are“ black-haired ” for his larger works and color paintings.  These works usually have a dramatic background or reference, in ancient mythology or tragic heroes, such as Salome, Judith, Danae and Athena.  He was very close to the stage of his career.  In many of these works he has a tendency to symbolism, which was one of the main trends in the art of the day.  As a passionate poet, he tries to embody general and abstract concepts such as life, death, philosophy, music, lust and jealousy with subtle and symbolic lines and forms.  In a series of colorful designs and paintings, "Hope" is a pregnant woman who is staring at her bulging stomach.  Despite Klimt ’ s mastery of design, he shuns accurate representations of the real world in colorful paintings.  His human figures change shape, along with the wave of lines and the dance of forms.  Klimt always fills the place of the "natural" motif with small and compact designs, so that the main texture of the figures and their surroundings is full of spirit and movement.  The Klimt gives the viewer the freedom to see the work in his own way and to evaluate and interpret it with his own mood.  In his art, he finds something hidden with a profound meaning that cannot be expressed; or he simply looks and moves the eye around the angles of lines, designs, and colors, and enjoys their harmony.  Klimt has something for every view and taste, and approaching his art does not require an expert.  Klimt's paintings are best known for their works known as the "Golden Age" and were created more or less during his artistic maturity, around the age of 40.  His father was an avid engraver and worked with gold.  It can be said that he inherited his love of gold from his father, but his familiarity with Byzantine tiles and paintings undoubtedly contributed to his interest in gold motifs.  Photo copyright Reuters Image caption Gustav Klimt, like Toulouse Lautrec, reproduced his works and marketed them for sale from iconography and the role of saints, not to mention the cleverness or use of gold water, an invention characterized in modern art by Klimt's work.  You have made your beanstalk with earthworms.  In his works, there are usually beautiful, naked and charming women in place of saints.  He may follow the Father ’ s tradition, showing each figure as a “piece of jewelry. ”  Perhaps the most famous of these is "The Kiss".  It all revolves around a love kiss.  Men and women kneel before each other in an ethereal space.  The man is strong, and the woman is strong, and he is strong.  The man ’ s coat is of angular and “hard ” roles, while the woman ’ s coat is covered with round and“ soft ” roles.  He is naked and alone, and does not reveal anything about the position of man or woman.  They are just two ordinary people who are intertwined with two different organs and can belong to any age and culture.  A critic has dubbed this position “the image of humanity. ”  By the end of Klimt ’ s life, the cold and grim charm of Expressionism had filled the air, but Klimt was more inclined to praise the joy of life, the joy of love, and the drink.  Her lively and beautiful nature is best seen in her natural landscapes and female portraits, which she brought to the canvas in the last decade of her life, from 1908 to 1918, with stunning perfection.  In these works, Klimt has achieved a calm and harmonious style that can be felt like a musical drum.  But sometimes in this tender and caressing song, the mood of the tumultuous times is felt, even in lyrical paintings such as Kiss or "Affection", there is a hidden anxiety that tells the lovers to never end this infinite moment.  If they look back, a great disaster awaits them.  Today, some of your church work is everywhere.  Many people have his work at home, enjoy the harmony of colors and the harmonious balance of designs without ever hearing his name.  This year, 150 years after Klimt ’ s birth, his name will be heard more often.
