passages.title: What is the origin of the food crisis in Latin America?
passages.passage: According to the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) website, the Latin American and Caribbean region produces enough food to meet the needs of all its inhabitants.  So the main problem with hunger in the region is not the lack of food, but the obstacles and difficulties faced by the poor to obtain it.  FAO Deputy General and Representative of the Organization for Latin America Julio Bardege told DW on the occasion of World Food Day that hunger in Latin America is due to insufficient income and significant economic inequality, which afflicts millions of people in the region.  According to a new report by the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO), food prices remained high for a seventh consecutive month in the last month of 2020, with dairy products and vegetable oils driving the biggest price increases.  According to the FAO, the rise in food prices was due to higher demand and weaker dollar values.  According to experts, although there is no pressure on food shortages, the impact of the epidemic on the supply chain and the restriction of traffic has caused damage to farms.  Latin America and the Caribbean, which produce more than 14 percent of the world ’ s food, are also looking to reshape their farming arrangements to feed 10 billion people by 2050.  However, the COVID-19 epidemic has caused an unprecedented setback in the region ’ s struggle against hunger, adding more than 20 million people to the ranks of poverty.  The unprecedented health crisis that has plagued the world for nearly two years has also hit Latin America.  Latin America, which was among the most vulnerable regions in the world due to the epidemic, has seen the spread of poverty and food shortages in recent decades, not only due to the spread of the coronavirus and the increase in deaths caused by it, but also due to numerous other factors such as climate change, mismanagement and the increasing deterioration of the labor market and sanctions.  The epidemic puts 45 million people in Latin America in a state of absolute poverty.  A situation that has sounded warnings and alarms about the lack of social security networks to reduce the consequences of the epidemic in Latin America.  The NGO Action Against Hunger reported a three-fold increase in the number of people suffering from food insecurity in Latin America in 2020 due to the outbreak of COVID-19.  In Peru, 80 percent of people lost their jobs or their incomes dropped by an average of 33 percent, according to the Humanitarian Institute ’ s survey.  The 20% drop in global food production due to climate change is another crisis that experts have warned of.  Studies show that climate change has reduced global food production by more than 20 percent in the past 60 years.  Farmers have one-fifth less food than they had in 1961; in warmer regions such as Latin America and Africa, the decline is up to 34 percent.  According to available data, the United States only sees growth of 5 to 15 percent, while the world's population is projected to reach 10 billion by 2050.  Climate change has changed the favorable conditions for growing crops and is hurting the food chain in the future.  Experts believe that temperature in plant growth and development is one of the important factors.  Temperature, along with the surface of light; carbon dioxide, temperature humidity, water and nutrients, affect the growth and ultimately the production of crops.  All of these factors need to be balanced.  While the global population continues to rise, a new study suggests that agricultural productivity has fallen sharply due to the effects of climate change.  On the other hand, some coercive measures by the hegemonic powers against the countries of the Latin American resistance, such as Venezuela, have exacerbated the food crisis in the region.  Along with mismanagement of the country ’ s food security, the impact of sanctions has affected 96 percent of Venezuelans, according to a new study.  The region ’ s response to the epidemic of the Director General of the Latin American Regional Agricultural Organization has increased despite the region ’ s worsening agricultural export unemployment during the epidemic.  In response to COVID-19 pandemic, the director of the Food and Agriculture Organization has sought to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of food production with a strategic approach, and has made a huge change in the agricultural sector with new regional initiatives.  The senior official of the agricultural organization of the region also emphasized the need for large-scale investments, especially in supply chain infrastructure and agricultural innovations, expressed hope about the region ’ s significant capacities, such as the enormous natural resources of the region, abundance of fresh water and fertile lands, as well as diverse ecosystems.  Despite this, the devastating effects of the epidemic will continue to plague the Latin American region.  Predictably, in most of these countries, rising debt due to the injection of emergency funds into the health sector and the provision of direct assistance to affected families and industrial sectors affected by the recession reduced economic activity by 7.7% in 2020.  The unemployment rate, which is the main cause of poverty, increased by 2.6 percent and with a significant portion of the workforce leaving, it reached 10.7 percent from its previous year in 2019.  In the same vein, because it was not possible for many jobs to work remotely, only 21.3 percent of those employed in the Latin American region were able to continue working this way.  According to the study, the highest unemployment rate was found in Peru (39.5%), Argentina (20.9%), Colombia (21.8%), Costa Rica (20.1%), and in the poorest households, informal work dominated.  According to the website Wordo Mitters, more than 33,581 million people in Latin America and the Caribbean have been infected with the coronavirus, and more than 1.2 million people have died from the disease.

passages.title: Climate Change Impact Assessment on Taiwan ’ s Human Resources (Part I)
passages.passage: Rising temperatures, intense heat, drought, orchard burning and heavy rain are expected to increasingly undermine agricultural productivity.  Challenges to livestock health, expected increases, declining crop yields and quality, and changes in extreme weather threaten rural livelihoods, food security, and price stability.  Pixabay economic growth is engulfed if we do not make substantial and sustained global mitigation of climate change, and regional adaptation efforts, it is expected to cost us infrastructure and property, increasingly, and hinder economic growth.  In the absence of major global mitigation actions and regional adaptation efforts, rising temperatures, rising sea levels and changes in extreme weather will continue to destroy infrastructure and property, labor productivity, and community vitality, especially as regional economies and industries that rely on natural resources and climate-friendly conditions, such as agriculture, tourism, and fisheries, are increasingly vulnerable to climate change.  Rising temperatures are expected to reduce the efficiency of power generation and increase energy demand, which in turn increases the cost of electricity.  Climate change is also expected to increasingly affect trade and the economy, including import and export prices, as well as businesses with overseas operations and supply chains.  In a moderately warm world, some aspects of the economy may improve slightly in the short term.  However, if the world does not reduce greenhouse gas emissions significantly and continuously, the planet is expected to continue to warm, causing significant net damage to the economy this century, especially as adaptation efforts are thwarted.  It is expected that the annual losses in some sectors of the economy will reach hundreds of billions of dollars by the end of the century, continuing to grow at the rate of past emissions.  Agriculture is highly challenged and threatened by rising temperatures, heat, drought, orchard burning and heavy rains, which are expected to increasingly undermine agricultural productivity.  Challenges to livestock health, expected increases, declining crop yields and quality, and changes in extreme weather threaten rural livelihoods, food security, and price stability.  Climate change poses many challenges to maintaining and improving crop productivity, livestock health and the economic viability of rural communities.  While some regions may see gains in productivity favoring expanded or alternative crops in the coming decades, overall, production of major crops is expected to decline due to higher temperatures, potentially altering water availability, soil erosion, and outbreaks of disease and pests.  Rising temperatures during the growing season are expected to be the biggest factor in the decline in agricultural productivity.  If the temperature at night exceeds 35 ° C, it will cause rice to be unable to pollinate; it will also aggravate the impact of diseases and pests, affecting the harvest of crops; high temperature and rain will make the soil unable to maintain nutrients, reduce crop yields and increase production costs.  The expected increase in extreme hot weather is expected to result in further heat stress for livestock, resulting in significant economic losses for producers.  Climate change is also likely to cause large-scale changes in the supply and prices of many agricultural products around the world, and the global supply and prices of agricultural products will also change dramatically.  These changes threaten future gains in commodity crop production and endanger rural livelihoods.  Agricultural production is an industry that is highly dependent on natural resources such as water, soil and biodiversity.  Climate change causes global temperature increases and uneven rainfall, disrupting crop growth, affecting the original habitats of ecosystems, and affecting the yield and quality of agricultural products, endangering food security and productivity, and causing loss of biodiversity.  There are many adaptation strategies to cope with climate variability, while reversing the adverse effects of change on agricultural production.  These include changes in production content, production inputs, the adoption of new technologies, and changes in management principles.  However, these strategies have limitations under severe climate change impacts and require both long-term and short-term investments.  High risk to health Climate change Air quality and health risks from extreme weather, air quality, and insects and pests, diseases transmitted through food and water supplies, are increasingly threatening the health and well-being of already vulnerable people; changes in temperature and precipitation increase air quality and health risks from wildfires (or incineration) and ground ozone pollution; rising air and water temperatures and more intense extreme weather are expected to increase exposure to waterborne diseases and foodborne diseases (food Sexual diseases), affecting the safety of food and water supplies.  Due to climate change, the frequency and severity of allergic diseases, including asthma and pollen fever, are expected to increase.  It also changes and expands the geographical distribution of disease-carrying insects and pests, exposing more people to the lice that bring Lyme disease and the mosquitoes that transmit Zika virus (such as dengue, yellow fever, Japanese encephalitis and Nile virus), which affect different transregions.  For example, communities in southwestern Taiwan are particularly vulnerable to the combined health effects of vector-borne diseases and high temperatures and floods.  Extreme and climate-related weather can have lasting mental health effects on communities, with adverse consequences, in particular resulting in degradation of livelihoods or relocation of communities.  Including the elderly, children, people in low-income communities and some indigenous and new communities, they tend to be disproportionately affected by the health impacts of climate change and are less resilient.  This helps individuals, communities, and counties to prepare for climate change risks with policies and programs to adapt and mitigate to reduce the number of injuries, illnesses, and deaths from adverse health outcomes.  According to the study, if the average temperature in Taiwan increases by 1 ° C in the future, the high risk of dengue fever will increase to 86, affecting more than 7 million people. In addition, the number of medium-risk areas has also increased to 203, and the future warming status will significantly increase the prevalence of dengue fever in Taiwan.  In addition, the increase in temperature in Taiwan will also increase the risk of related infectious diseases, and the impact of rainfall changes on infectious diseases will be more significant when the "daily extreme rainfall" is greater than 200mm.  In the face of the impact of climate change on public health, the adaptation that must be considered and prepared can be classified as at least three major aspects of infectious diseases, chronic non-communicable diseases and emergency medical care.  The main adjustment policies can basically be considered from the angle of strengthening and prevention.

passages.passage: In addition to the most obvious examples of melting ice, rising sea water, and global warming, climate change is actually forcing ecosystem changes, including the animals that live in it and our human habits, emotions and lifestyles, and even the flight of aircraft.  Climate change refers to the fluctuation of the climate over a period of time, which can also refer to decades or millions of years, and the range of fluctuations can be regional or global, and its average meteorological index changes.  At present, the most discussed climate change is about environmental policy, the impact on the contemporary climate, that is, the impact of human factors on the climate, especially the issue of global warming.  For the current global warming, most climate scientists believe that "human activity is most likely the main cause of global warming for nearly half a century."  The causes of climate change affect climate change from a variety of factors, including solar radiation, changes in the Earth's orbit, mountain building, greenhouse gas emissions, and more (discussed below).  Due to the slow response of many factors that indirectly affect the climate on the surface, such as changes in ocean temperature, melting of icebergs, etc., climate change can take centuries or even longer to manifest in relation to changes in factors that directly affect the climate.  Since the development of agriculture, especially since the beginning of the industrial revolution, fossil fuel burning, deforestation, rice cultivation, animal husbandry, industrial production and other human activities have increased.  Greenhouse gases in the atmosphere, such as carbon dioxide, methane and water vapor, absorb infrared radiation from the Earth's surface and then re-radiate, causing the greenhouse effect.  ◆ Ice cover, sea ice, land vegetation, ocean temperature, weathering rate, ocean circulation and greenhouse gas concentration are directly or indirectly affected by the atmosphere.  However, they also all feed back into the atmosphere and affect it in different ways.  Periodic changes in Earth ’ s orbit and an axial tilt relative to the Sun (tens of thousands to hundreds of thousands of years) affect how solar radiation is distributed on the Earth ’ s surface.  ◆ Plate tectonic motion changes the shape, size, location and height of the continental mass and the bathymetry of the ocean, which has a strong impact on the atmosphere and ocean circulation.  ◆ The brightness of the sun continues to increase with the aging of the star, and over time, the sun will transfer more and more energy to the Earth's atmosphere.  Climate change affects weather patterns, and meteorological elements such as temperature, humidity, wind speed, rainfall and extreme weather events can affect the emission, chemical properties, deposition and transport of air pollutants.  Increased carbon dioxide levels and rising temperatures in the atmosphere will prolong the pollen transmission season and increase pollen concentration, leading to allergies and asthma in some people.  ◆ The most familiar and predictable phenomenon is the seasonal cycle, where people adjust their clothing, outdoor activities, thermostats and agricultural practices.  Human societies have changed in terms of adaptive change, despite overwhelming evidence that certain societies and civilizations have collapsed in the face of rapid and severe climate change.  ◆ Complex feedbacks between climate components create “tipping points ” in the climate system, where small, gradual changes in one component of the system can lead to sudden climate changes.  The history of life is strongly influenced by climate change, some of which fundamentally alter the evolutionary process.  Climate change, in addition to the most obvious melting of ice, rising sea water, and global warming, actually forces ecosystems, including the animals that live in them, and us humans, to adapt to its effects in unexpected ways.  Here are six of them: 1. Reduced human sexual behavior In an aging society with fewer children, there are many reasons for the decline in birth rate. In addition to the popularity of contraceptive methods and economic recession, it is also related to climate change.  Research papers from the National Institute of Economic Research in the United States found that the weather affects sexual desire and reduces the birth rate.  On nights with temperatures above 26.6 degrees Celsius, the birth rate after 8 to 10 months from that date is 0.4% lower than the average.  In other words, every night of high temperatures lowers the total number of babies born in the United States by about 1,000.  “1,000 people ” may seem like a drop in the ocean for the U.S. population, but it is estimated that the hot summer nights will surge from 30 days a year to 90 days in the future, and 100,000 fewer babies will be born each year.  2. Do not sleep at night in the city life, no matter how many students or office workers are disturbed by sleep debt.  Chronic fatigue caused by chronic insomnia and lack of sleep can lead to long-term depression, heart disease, dementia, cancer, etc.  If climate change trends continue, the lack of sleep in urban areas will only worsen.  MIT Media Lab estimates that by 2050, there will be six more sleepless nights per 100 Americans per year, rising to 14 by 2099.  As with other climate change impacts, the poor are often the first to bear the brunt, with families who can ’ t afford air conditioning and the elderly who are afraid of the cold and the heat most affected.  3. Hot to irritable, people more violent The so-called "hot to irritable" is definitely not just talk, heat waves not only make us upset and irritable, reckless, and more likely to misunderstand other people's actions contain hostility.  In fact, the crime rate in hot areas is higher than in other areas.  A study of nearly 60 countries last year found that the hotter the weather, the higher the chance of violent crime, and that murders are expected to rise by 6% for every 1 degree Celsius rise in global temperatures in the future.  In the past summer, 40 flights in Phoenix alone were canceled due to extremely hot weather (not haze or hurricanes). Why?  Because the density of hot air is lower than that of cold air, the hotter the air, the less air molecules are available to support the fuselage, and the difficulty of aircraft takeoff increases.  In fact, long runways help aircraft generate more lift, so low air density does not necessarily prevent aircraft from taking off, but it is certainly a difficult problem for some smaller airports such as Phoenix.  5. Polar bear hybrid grizzly polar bear Global warming, continuous melting of ice, originally mainly out of floating ice polar bear forced to retreat inland, mating season in the land meet grizzly bear mixed, mixed into grizzly polar bear, faded snow white fur, replaced with grizzly brown fur.  It is said that this natural hybrid is the expedient measure for polar bears to survive in global warming, because the grizzly bear gene can adapt to a warmer climate, and the offspring of the two bears will lose the thick fur used to keep warm, making the grizzly bear more heat resistant.  Although it may appear to be beneficial for survival, the survival of the real polar bear is increasingly at risk, said Andrew Derocher, a professor of biology at the University of Alberta. “I don ’ t want to say that, but from a genetic perspective, grizzly bears have a great chance of eventually eating the polar bear. ”  The number of shark attacks on humans has increased year by year, and scientists estimate there are two reasons.  One is that rising sea temperatures push sharks north, and the other is that the summer extension makes more swimmers come to the beach to play with the water. The combination of the two increases the chance of shark attacks.  Shark attacks on humans have made shark hunters "famous" and angered sharks, which is also the main reason for the increase in shark attacks.  Last year there were 156 shark attacks due to human provocation.  Evidence for climate change All historical science has a problem: As they explore further in time, they increasingly rely on piecemeal and indirect evidence.  The history of the Earth system is no exception.  High-quality instrumental records spanning the last century exist in most parts of the world, but records became scarce in the 19th century and were rarely recorded until the late 18th century.  Other historical documents, including ship logs, diaries, court and church records, and tax bills, can sometimes be used.  In a strictly geographic setting, these sources can provide information on frosts, droughts, floods, sea ice, monsoon dates, and other climate features that in some cases date back hundreds of years.  Fortunately, climate change also leaves a variety of features in nature.  Climate affects the growth of trees and corals, the abundance and geographical distribution of animal and plant species, the chemistry of oceans and lakes, the accumulation of ice in cold areas, and the erosion and deposition of material on the Earth's surface.  Paleoclimatists study the traces of these effects and devise clever and subtle ways to obtain information about past climates.  Much of the evidence for climate change in the past is indirect, so paleontology requires a lot of investigative work.  Where possible, paleoclimatologists try to cross-examine their conclusions with multiple lines of evidence.  They often face conflicting evidence, but, like other sciences, this often leads to a deeper understanding of the Earth system and its complex history. passages.title: The Gretinist Myth of the Climate Crisis
passages.passage: One of the most inhumane totalitarian ideologies in the history of mankind and one of the most popular aggressive sects of the present time is the myth of the climate crisis.  The mouthpieces of aggressive gretinism regularly declare about the alleged climate crisis affecting the planet: I ask the media to treat the crisis as a crisis...  We are facing an existential threat, and there is no longer time to continue on this path of madness...... as one can expect countries like India, Colombia or Nigeria to care about the climate crisis...  … I am told that I must learn to become a climatologist so that I can “solve the climate crisis ”.  The climate crisis has already been resolved.  On Monday, Greta Thunberg and 15 other children filed a complaint with the United Nations alleging that the world ’ s five largest economies violated human rights by failing to take adequate measures to stop the unfolding climate crisis.  Thunberg and 15 other children accuse countries of “inadequate ” national commitments to curb the climate crisis, as their actions will not stop the global temperature rise below 2 ° C, as agreed in the Paris climate agreement.  Without these vital actions, they argue that the climate crisis will put their livelihoods at risk – from more dangerous storms, food crises, rising sea levels and more.  The lawsuit accuses Germany, France, Brazil, Argentina and Turkey of failing to comply with their obligations under the Convention on the Rights of the Child.  These countries differ in that they are the world ’ s five largest emitters of greenhouse gases, which are the direct cause of the climate crisis.  What is a climate crisis?  Is it happening now?  Does humanity need to do something about it?  And if you do, what?  A short article will not replace large-scale and detailed studies of specialists in a number of scientific disciplines - climatology, paleoclimatology, physics and chemistry of the atmosphere, geology, astronomy, biology, medicine, economics.  It formulates only a few basic theses on the main trends in the evolution of the global climate, forecasts of climatic changes, their consequences for humans.  First of all, those interested in the topic should not mix the problems of ecology (air pollution, water, soil in places of human life and work) and climate issues (the temperature of the planet's air, its humidity, the frequency and intensity of certain natural phenomena).  Environmental problems (primarily the production and disposal of garbage, emissions of hazardous substances, industrial and energy waste, emissions of gasoline engines, etc.) caused by human activities threaten the health and lives of millions of people, deserve the most serious attention and solutions.  Citizens who advocate for the solution of environmental problems are highly respected and deserve every support.  Climate change is largely caused not by human activities, but by natural factors, their impact on the health and lives of millions of people is minimal, and in recent decades, mostly positive; in addition, the degree of their impact on human life is constantly declining.  The struggle against climate change is as expedient as the struggle to change the motion of the planets or the intensity of the radiance of the sun, and persons depicting such a struggle join the ranks of the aggressive sects of climate alarmists and gretinists.  The topic of interest should also not be confused with climate and weather.  Climate is a long-term (according to the existing agreement between climatologists - at least three decades) weather regime.  Therefore, if you hear (read) statements about the need to combat climate change because, for example, there was no snow this year, or the last two summers were especially hot, or as a result of last year ’ s fires burned so many hectares of forest, then this is a clear confirmation that the person making such statements is either incompetent in climate and climate change issues, or deliberately misleading the public.  Area of fires in Australia (ha), 1920-2020 3.  Since a crisis in the most general sense is a radical change in the state of a phenomenon, a climate crisis can be called such a significant climate change, which would have the following characteristics: - it would be large-scale (for example, there was a significant increase in air temperature, radically different in its magnitude from traditional climate changes); - it would be very rapid (for example, the increase in air temperature occurred much faster than ever before); - it would have especially severe consequences for humans (for example, long - term increases in air temperature have led to increased mortality).  If none of these signs of a climate crisis is observed, then there is therefore no climate crisis itself, and the usual climate changes are taking place instead of the crisis.  The climate of planet Earth is constantly changing.  It has changed in the past, it has changed in the present, it will change in the future – as long as our planet exists.  Constant change is an inherent feature of the global climate.  There is no fundamental disagreement about the fact of climate change among scientists.  There is indeed a scientific consensus, but only on this issue: Earth ’ s climate change is and is happening all the time.  Attempts by climate alarmists and gretinists to spread the myth that their opponents deny the very fact of climate change are unscrupulous propaganda.  Differences between experts exist not on the fact of climate change, but on other issues.  In particular, there are disagreements about: — the ratio of current and historically observed levels of global temperature, — the direction of climate change, — the magnitude (scale) of climate change, — the speed of climate change, — the causes of climate change, — the predictions of climate change, — the effects of climate change on humans, — the optimal strategy for mankind ’ s response to climate change.  The correct answers to many of these questions depend crucially on the time horizon chosen — 40, 80, 1,000, 10,000, hundreds of thousands, or millions of years.  Depending on the time horizon, the answers to these questions are different, including the exact opposite.  The global climate is one of the most complex natural systems.  The laws of climate change are currently completely unknown to mankind.  Historically, climate change has seen both long - term, relatively stable trends and cycles of varying durations and frequencies, as well as abrupt, crisis phenomena that radically changed the climate in a short time.  Over the past fifty million years, the global climate of the Earth has generally tended to cool down.  Over shorter periods of time (for example, in the last 800,000 years), climate change has been largely cyclical.  The time horizons of different climatic cycles are different - from the well-known annual cycle (winter - spring - summer - autumn) to cycles lasting 70-80 years, 1300 years, about 100 thousand years (Milankovitch cycles).  Reconstruction of temperature, CO2 concentration, dust according to the ice cores of Vostok 11 station.  In the history of global climate, there have been both climate crises and climate catastrophes (as, for example, during the late Dryas (about 12,000 years ago, when temperatures fell by about 10 ° C for a hundred years and perhaps even faster).  The current level of global temperature is not unique in historical perspective.  The average annual temperature of planet Earth is currently estimated at about 14.5 degrees Celsius.  In the history of the planet there were periods when the air temperature was lower than the current – in the early Permian period, in the Oligocene, during the periodic glaciations of the Pleistocene.  For most of the last half billion years, the air temperature on the surface of the Earth has been markedly higher than today, and for about half of this period it was about 10-15 ° C higher than today (that is, in the range of 25-30 ° C).  Global temperature over the past 60 million years 13.  During the regular glaciations of the Pleistocene, cold periods lasted about 90 thousand years and had peak temperatures about 10 ° C below the current one.  Long glaciations were replaced by short (4-6 thousand years) warm interglacial periods with temperatures 1-3 ° C higher than the current one.  About 10 thousand years ago, another sharp increase in temperature (about 10 ° C) began, thanks to which the colossal glaciers that occupied a significant part of the territory of Eurasia and North America melted.  This period, in which we were lucky to live, was called the climatic optimum of the Holocene.  Global warming of the climate has played a key role in mastering the secrets of agriculture and the transition of mankind to the civilizational stage of its development.  Over the past 10 thousand years, there have been at least 5 warm periods - the so-called "climatic optimum", during each of which for 150-300 years the temperature on the planet was 1-3 ° C higher than the current one. passages.title: Reduce Global Warming by Modifying Food Production Methods
passages.passage: In their new study, researchers from the University of Oxford found that modifying the way food is produced could be a good way to reduce global warming and climate change.  A new study shows that wind power and geothermal energy are not enough to keep the Earth cool.  Even if the energy transition takes place entirely in environmentally friendly ways, greenhouse gas emissions from the world ’ s food system will be exposed to heat.  In the new study, researchers from the University of Oxford suggest that to prevent climate change and extreme heat, all food production sectors must be rapidly and significantly modified.  In addition to replacing fossil fuels with environmentally friendly fuels, the food system also needs to change and reform.  Michael Clark and his colleagues believe that if things continue the same way, harmful emissions from agriculture will be released between 2020 and 2100.  Carbon dioxide is released as a result of many activities, including cutting down trees in tropical forests, using agricultural machinery, and using chemicals in agriculture.  The use of fertilizers can lead to the release of nitrous oxide, and cows also emit methane, which is a potent warming gas.  In this project, the researchers examined forests in the United States and applied standard hypotheses about how diets might improve economic conditions in communities.  As income increases, people tend to consume more meat, dairy, eggs and animal products.  The production of animal products has many negative effects on the climate and environment.  The researchers proposed an experiment in which all sources of greenhouse gas emissions were eliminated.  This test requires a complete modification of electric vehicles, buildings that draw their heat from geothermal sources, and so on.  Clark said such a situation would be really scary.  Researchers and food policy experts already know that food production plays a significant role in global warming, but adopting this proposed new strategy is far more rigorous and complex.  Clark said: “The good thing is that there ’ s a lot we can do to fix this problem, but it needs to be done a little bit of everything.  In the project, the researchers examined the impact of five important agricultural strategies, including rapidly strengthening land to reduce deforestation and changing diets with less animal products.  None of these strategies alone can do enough to reduce heat emissions, but advancing all of these strategies together could make it possible to achieve the ultimate goal.  End of message.

passages.title: In the North Caucasus and southern Russia will increase snowfall and droughts
passages.passage: Climatologists predict that in the 21st century, the amount and intensity of snowfall will increase throughout Russia, and in some regions, arid conditions are expected to worsen.  This is reported by RIA Novosti with reference to the national report “Global climate and soil cover of Russia: assessment of risks and environmental and economic consequences of land degradation ”.  The study was conducted with the aim of developing measures for adapting agricultural and forest management systems and technologies to climate change.  Discussion of the report, analyzing the forecast scenarios of climate change and their impact on agriculture and forestry, was held at the Vasily Dokuchaev Soil Institute.  According to scientists, if at the beginning of the XXI century in Russia there was a small increase in precipitation, then by the middle of the century it will increase, especially in the eastern and northern regions of the country.  “The increase in summer precipitation is most significant, mainly in the north and east of Russia.  In the south of the European part of Russia - in the Southern and North Caucasus Federal Districts - the worsening of arid (on average per year) conditions is expected, "the study says.  At the same time, more "sharp" precipitation will probably occur in the form of separate showers or snowfalls.  There will also be more floods and floods.  Note that recently, scientists said that in 30 years the climate of the Rostov region in 30 years may change to subtropical, and the weather on the coast of the Sea of Azov will be close to the climate of Abkhazia and Sochi.  So far, we are lagging behind in temperatures: in the subtropics, the annual is + 11, we have + 9.95, - said Lyudmila Bespalova, Doctor of Geographical Sciences.  In her opinion, the summer shallowing of the Don in 2017, when the water left the coast by ten meters, is one of the brightest examples of climate change.  Changes in climatic conditions can lead not only to a change in flora and fauna, but also to a change in the economy of the region.  For example, Don farmers will have to breed new varieties of wheat and shift the timing of crops.

passages.title: Climate change and water scarcity are top priorities.
passages.passage: Assistant Professor of Water Engineering at the Faculty of Agriculture of Shahrekord University said: “The main priority of the authorities should be water shortage and climate change, so that water factories are moved to the seaside and agriculture in areas that are facing water shortage is limited. ”  He said: “It ’ s been a long time, it ’ s been a long time, it ’ s been a long time, it ’ s been a long time.  “When we talk about climate change, we mean meteorological parameters that have been measured over long periods of time, and these changes manifest themselves in either natural or artificial forms, which are caused by humans.  Nasr Esfahani said: “Various factors such as sunspots, changes in the earth ’ s crust, changes in vegetation or the movement of continents, or changes in ocean temperature naturally cause climate change.  “What has happened in the past year is that humans have caused an imbalance in meteorological parameters due to excessive consumption of natural resources, including oil, gas and fossil fuels, and by destroying natural resources such as forests and expanding factories and cities.  The university professor pointed out that the country is climatally located in a dry region, saying: "We should not expect the climate to change from dry to wet, because this is a very wrong expectation that some in the society suggest this."  He said: "Climate change has become very clear in the last 40 years, so we have to adapt to this situation that has been fluctuating and know that drought or drought fluctuations are part of the nature of the region's climate."  Nasr Isfahani said: "In this situation, climate change is occurring and extreme phenomena such as severe droughts, drought, heat and cold are increasing, there is no alternative but to adapt to them, for example, agricultural products can be used to prevent frostbite, to use resistant products.  Regarding water resources, he said: “At the same time as the climate change, the consumption of water resources has greatly expanded, especially in the last 50 years, when agriculture has been the center of development in the country. ”  The university professor said: "If we examine the rainfall parameter in more detail, we see that the average rainfall has not changed, but the extremes have changed a lot and these changes are significant, on the other hand, the effective rainfall has not changed and the ineffective rainfall has increased, which means that there is a shortage of water resources."  He said: "What has been observed is that, contrary to the rainfall parameter, changes in the temperature parameter, especially the minimum temperature, are highly effective and the trend of increasing the minimum temperature is observed in many stations in the country."  Nasr Esfahani pointed out that in mountainous areas the precipitation has changed from solid to liquid state, adding: "When there is snow in the region, because the snow is slowly melting and sinking into underground sources, it feeds them, on the other hand, the occurrence of rain brings water runoff, which feeds surface water instead of feeding groundwater resources."  He added that excessive consumption of water resources, expansion of the area under cultivation, non-observance of the cultivation pattern and the use of traditional methods for irrigation have led to the reduction of groundwater.  Assistant Professor of Water Engineering at Shahrekord University emphasized: "The authorities were aware of the current situation, but they did not think that the effects of climate change would be egregious and misrepresented, and today we face a fundamental problem, for example, if there was a shortage of water, it was solved by harvesting from underground water resources and we assigned this problem to the future."  He continued: “We have reached a point where groundwater resources are not the answer to the shortage of water, and this problem has become such that measures must be taken.  Nasr Esfahani said that for short-term purposes, water resources have not been considered because steel and water mills have been built in the country, which if this decision process continues, despite the lack of water resources, will still be built in the future.  “We should not expect that one day our country will be as abundant as Europe, because the lack of rainfall in our region has been caused by the rotation of the earth and the circulation of the atmosphere, so in addition to adapting to climate change, if there is to be a cost to this, it should be done today and we should not postpone those costs to the future, because we may face more limitations in the future. ”  The university professor noted that the main priority of the authorities should be water scarcity and climate change, so that water factories are moved to the seaside and agriculture is limited in areas with water scarcity.  End of message.

passages.title: Land abuse contributes to climate change
passages.passage: The land is often abused and contributes to the harm of climate change 2019-08-06 16: 42 Taiwan Awakening News reporter Zhuang Ruimeng / Taipei reported that the land has been used by humans to cultivate and lose its original function of absorbing carbon.  (Photo by M. Prinke on Flicker under Creative Commons license) Share Facebook Treating land better helps humanity fight climate change.  The UN Intergovernmental Panel of Experts on Climate Change, which is currently meeting, will present an updated report on the current state of human land use.  Experts pointed out that due to human behavior, land has changed from carbon capture to carbon release, threatening to exacerbate the power of climate change, and highlighting the importance of land use.  According to The Independent, global soils can currently absorb 1% of carbon, down from 7% in the past.  If the land is cultivated in a more sustainable way, carbon will be absorbed by the soil to become a carbon reservoir.  Currently, 1 / 3 of all pollution emissions come from land.  “If we take the severity of the climate problem seriously now, it will be worse if we don ’ t have land as a carbon reservoir, ” said Li Wen, a representative of the World Resources Institute. The scientists also pointed out that continued pressure on land, including the provision of food, wood and plant raw materials to meet increasing population needs, will make carbon reduction targets more difficult to achieve.  In addition, 33% of arable land has been used to grow crops that provide animal feed.  Professor Lixon of the University of Clanfield in the UK also believes that the latest IPCC report will provide more evidence that land degradation will also exacerbate climate change and lead to an increase in the crisis.  Addressing land abuse can focus on intensive agriculture, which involves farming on as small a land as possible, allowing more natural land to absorb carbon dioxide, according to the BBC.  Another option is to farm in a less dense and friendly climate.  Either way, however, the IPCC report will point out that poor farmers will be the group most affected by global warming.  Professor Berman, of the University of Oxford ’ s Institute of Environmental Change, said climate change had led to soil erosion in the south of the UK through more intense rainfall.  “Warmer temperatures and heavier rainfall will worsen soil erosion, soil compaction, loss of organic matter and biodiversity, and soil and rock flows, ” said Li Huicheng, chairman of the IPCC.“ I hope this report will serve to remind the world more about the threat that climate change poses to land. ”  [More details, see here]

report:
Climate change is having a profound impact on agriculture worldwide. 
Rising temperatures are affecting crop yields and changing the growing conditions for various crops. 
According to the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO), the average global temperature has risen by about 1 degree Celsius since the late 19th century [afa40ca1-54bf-4f3e-bacc-fd8dec6e3b3b].

Temperature changes are affecting the growth and development of crops. 
Rising temperatures during the growing season are causing rice to be unable to pollinate, leading to reduced crop yields [a9485530-47ec-4015-8f1f-55d0e9b989ec]. 
High temperatures and rainfall are also making the soil unable to maintain nutrients, reducing crop yields and increasing production costs [a9485530-47ec-4015-8f1f-55d0e9b989ec].

Shifts in rainfall patterns are also affecting agriculture. 
In Latin America, where the region produces enough food to meet the needs of all its inhabitants, food prices remained high for a seventh consecutive month in the last month of 2020, with dairy products and vegetable oils driving the biggest price increases [afa40ca1-54bf-4f3e-bacc-fd8dec6e3b3b]. 
This is due to higher demand and weaker dollar values, but also exacerbated by the impact of the epidemic on the supply chain and the restriction of traffic [afa40ca1-54bf-4f3e-bacc-fd8dec6e3b3b].

Climate change is also affecting the growth of trees and corals, the abundance and geographical distribution of animal and plant species, the chemistry of oceans and lakes, and the accumulation of ice in cold areas [1c7c68e4-b52b-4543-a8b0-33337b2f78cd]. 
These changes are a result of climate change, which is causing global temperature increases and uneven rainfall [1c7c68e4-b52b-4543-a8b0-33337b2f78cd].

In addition, climate change is affecting the health and well-being of people, particularly vulnerable populations such as the elderly, children, and people in low-income communities [1c7c68e4-b52b-4543-a8b0-33337b2f78cd]. 
The increase in temperature is also affecting the risk of diseases, such as dengue fever, which is expected to increase to 86% in Taiwan if the average temperature rises by 1 degree Celsius [a9485530-47ec-4015-8f1f-55d0e9b989ec].

To mitigate the effects of climate change on agriculture, researchers from the University of Oxford suggest that modifying the way food is produced could be a good way to reduce global warming and climate change [c7fb8d94-f9d3-470a-99dc-f84e0043fe94]. 
This includes replacing fossil fuels with environmentally friendly fuels and changing agricultural practices to reduce greenhouse gas emissions [c7fb8d94-f9d3-470a-99dc-f84e0043fe94].

Furthermore, climate change is affecting the land and its ability to absorb carbon. 
The land is often abused and contributes to the harm of climate change [8973d6cd-8e11-4ba7-8096-34dcc0e122d6]. 
Global soils can currently absorb 1% of carbon, down from 7% in the past [8973d6cd-8e11-4ba7-8096-34dcc0e122d6]. 
This is due to human behavior, which has changed the land from carbon capture to carbon release [8973d6cd-8e11-4ba7-8096-34dcc0e122d6].

In conclusion, climate change is having a significant impact on agriculture worldwide. 
Rising temperatures, shifts in rainfall patterns, and changes in carbon dioxide levels are affecting crop yields, growing conditions, and the health and well-being of people. 
To mitigate these effects, researchers suggest modifying agricultural practices and reducing greenhouse gas emissions.

Title: What is the origin of the food crisis in Latin America?
Content: According to the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) website, the Latin American and Caribbean region produces enough food to meet the needs of all its inhabitants.  So the main problem with hunger in the region is not the lack of food, but the obstacles and difficulties faced by the poor to obtain it.  FAO Deputy General and Representative of the Organization for Latin America Julio Bardege told DW on the occasion of World Food Day that hunger in Latin America is due to insufficient income and significant economic inequality, which afflicts millions of people in the region.  According to a new report by the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO), food prices remained high for a seventh consecutive month in the last month of 2020, with dairy products and vegetable oils driving the biggest price increases.  According to the FAO, the rise in food prices was due to higher demand and weaker dollar values.  According to experts, although there is no pressure on food shortages, the impact of the epidemic on the supply chain and the restriction of traffic has caused damage to farms.  Latin America and the Caribbean, which produce more than 14 percent of the world ’ s food, are also looking to reshape their farming arrangements to feed 10 billion people by 2050.  However, the COVID-19 epidemic has caused an unprecedented setback in the region ’ s struggle against hunger, adding more than 20 million people to the ranks of poverty.  The unprecedented health crisis that has plagued the world for nearly two years has also hit Latin America.  Latin America, which was among the most vulnerable regions in the world due to the epidemic, has seen the spread of poverty and food shortages in recent decades, not only due to the spread of the coronavirus and the increase in deaths caused by it, but also due to numerous other factors such as climate change, mismanagement and the increasing deterioration of the labor market and sanctions.  The epidemic puts 45 million people in Latin America in a state of absolute poverty.  A situation that has sounded warnings and alarms about the lack of social security networks to reduce the consequences of the epidemic in Latin America.  The NGO Action Against Hunger reported a three-fold increase in the number of people suffering from food insecurity in Latin America in 2020 due to the outbreak of COVID-19.  In Peru, 80 percent of people lost their jobs or their incomes dropped by an average of 33 percent, according to the Humanitarian Institute ’ s survey.  The 20% drop in global food production due to climate change is another crisis that experts have warned of.  Studies show that climate change has reduced global food production by more than 20 percent in the past 60 years.  Farmers have one-fifth less food than they had in 1961; in warmer regions such as Latin America and Africa, the decline is up to 34 percent.  According to available data, the United States only sees growth of 5 to 15 percent, while the world's population is projected to reach 10 billion by 2050.  Climate change has changed the favorable conditions for growing crops and is hurting the food chain in the future.  Experts believe that temperature in plant growth and development is one of the important factors.  Temperature, along with the surface of light; carbon dioxide, temperature humidity, water and nutrients, affect the growth and ultimately the production of crops.  All of these factors need to be balanced.  While the global population continues to rise, a new study suggests that agricultural productivity has fallen sharply due to the effects of climate change.  On the other hand, some coercive measures by the hegemonic powers against the countries of the Latin American resistance, such as Venezuela, have exacerbated the food crisis in the region.  Along with mismanagement of the country ’ s food security, the impact of sanctions has affected 96 percent of Venezuelans, according to a new study.  The region ’ s response to the epidemic of the Director General of the Latin American Regional Agricultural Organization has increased despite the region ’ s worsening agricultural export unemployment during the epidemic.  In response to COVID-19 pandemic, the director of the Food and Agriculture Organization has sought to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of food production with a strategic approach, and has made a huge change in the agricultural sector with new regional initiatives.  The senior official of the agricultural organization of the region also emphasized the need for large-scale investments, especially in supply chain infrastructure and agricultural innovations, expressed hope about the region ’ s significant capacities, such as the enormous natural resources of the region, abundance of fresh water and fertile lands, as well as diverse ecosystems.  Despite this, the devastating effects of the epidemic will continue to plague the Latin American region.  Predictably, in most of these countries, rising debt due to the injection of emergency funds into the health sector and the provision of direct assistance to affected families and industrial sectors affected by the recession reduced economic activity by 7.7% in 2020.  The unemployment rate, which is the main cause of poverty, increased by 2.6 percent and with a significant portion of the workforce leaving, it reached 10.7 percent from its previous year in 2019.  In the same vein, because it was not possible for many jobs to work remotely, only 21.3 percent of those employed in the Latin American region were able to continue working this way. Title: Climate Change Impact Assessment on Taiwan ’ s Human Resources (Part I)
Content: Rising temperatures, intense heat, drought, orchard burning and heavy rain are expected to increasingly undermine agricultural productivity.  Challenges to livestock health, expected increases, declining crop yields and quality, and changes in extreme weather threaten rural livelihoods, food security, and price stability.  Pixabay economic growth is engulfed if we do not make substantial and sustained global mitigation of climate change, and regional adaptation efforts, it is expected to cost us infrastructure and property, increasingly, and hinder economic growth.  In the absence of major global mitigation actions and regional adaptation efforts, rising temperatures, rising sea levels and changes in extreme weather will continue to destroy infrastructure and property, labor productivity, and community vitality, especially as regional economies and industries that rely on natural resources and climate-friendly conditions, such as agriculture, tourism, and fisheries, are increasingly vulnerable to climate change.  Rising temperatures are expected to reduce the efficiency of power generation and increase energy demand, which in turn increases the cost of electricity.  Climate change is also expected to increasingly affect trade and the economy, including import and export prices, as well as businesses with overseas operations and supply chains.  In a moderately warm world, some aspects of the economy may improve slightly in the short term.  However, if the world does not reduce greenhouse gas emissions significantly and continuously, the planet is expected to continue to warm, causing significant net damage to the economy this century, especially as adaptation efforts are thwarted.  It is expected that the annual losses in some sectors of the economy will reach hundreds of billions of dollars by the end of the century, continuing to grow at the rate of past emissions.  Agriculture is highly challenged and threatened by rising temperatures, heat, drought, orchard burning and heavy rains, which are expected to increasingly undermine agricultural productivity.  Challenges to livestock health, expected increases, declining crop yields and quality, and changes in extreme weather threaten rural livelihoods, food security, and price stability.  Climate change poses many challenges to maintaining and improving crop productivity, livestock health and the economic viability of rural communities.  While some regions may see gains in productivity favoring expanded or alternative crops in the coming decades, overall, production of major crops is expected to decline due to higher temperatures, potentially altering water availability, soil erosion, and outbreaks of disease and pests.  Rising temperatures during the growing season are expected to be the biggest factor in the decline in agricultural productivity.  If the temperature at night exceeds 35 ° C, it will cause rice to be unable to pollinate; it will also aggravate the impact of diseases and pests, affecting the harvest of crops; high temperature and rain will make the soil unable to maintain nutrients, reduce crop yields and increase production costs.  The expected increase in extreme hot weather is expected to result in further heat stress for livestock, resulting in significant economic losses for producers.  Climate change is also likely to cause large-scale changes in the supply and prices of many agricultural products around the world, and the global supply and prices of agricultural products will also change dramatically.  These changes threaten future gains in commodity crop production and endanger rural livelihoods.  Agricultural production is an industry that is highly dependent on natural resources such as water, soil and biodiversity.  Climate change causes global temperature increases and uneven rainfall, disrupting crop growth, affecting the original habitats of ecosystems, and affecting the yield and quality of agricultural products, endangering food security and productivity, and causing loss of biodiversity.  There are many adaptation strategies to cope with climate variability, while reversing the adverse effects of change on agricultural production.  These include changes in production content, production inputs, the adoption of new technologies, and changes in management principles.  However, these strategies have limitations under severe climate change impacts and require both long-term and short-term investments.  High risk to health Climate change Air quality and health risks from extreme weather, air quality, and insects and pests, diseases transmitted through food and water supplies, are increasingly threatening the health and well-being of already vulnerable people; changes in temperature and precipitation increase air quality and health risks from wildfires (or incineration) and ground ozone pollution; rising air and water temperatures and more intense extreme weather are expected to increase exposure to waterborne diseases and foodborne diseases (food Sexual diseases), affecting the safety of food and water supplies.  Due to climate change, the frequency and severity of allergic diseases, including asthma and pollen fever, are expected to increase.  It also changes and expands the geographical distribution of disease-carrying insects and pests, exposing more people to the lice that bring Lyme disease and the mosquitoes that transmit Zika virus (such as dengue, yellow fever, Japanese encephalitis and Nile virus), which affect different transregions.  For example, communities in southwestern Taiwan are particularly vulnerable to the combined health effects of vector-borne diseases and high temperatures and floods.  Extreme and climate-related weather can have lasting mental health effects on communities, with adverse consequences, in particular resulting in degradation of livelihoods or relocation of communities.  Including the elderly, children, people in low-income communities and some indigenous and new communities, they tend to be disproportionately affected by the health impacts of climate change and are less resilient.  This helps individuals, communities, and counties to prepare for climate change risks with policies and programs to adapt and mitigate to reduce the number of injuries, illnesses, and deaths from adverse health outcomes.  According to the study, if the average temperature in Taiwan increases by 1 ° C in the future, the high risk of dengue fever will increase to 86, affecting more than 7 million people. In addition, the number of medium-risk areas has also increased to 203, and the future warming status will significantly increase the prevalence of dengue fever in Taiwan.  In addition, the increase in temperature in Taiwan will also increase the risk of related infectious diseases, and the impact of rainfall changes on infectious diseases will be more significant when the "daily extreme rainfall" is greater than 200mm.  In the face of the impact of climate change on public health, the adaptation that must be considered and prepared can be classified as at least three major aspects of infectious diseases, chronic non-communicable diseases and emergency medical care.  The main adjustment policies can basically be considered from the angle of strengthening and prevention.

Content: In addition to the most obvious examples of melting ice, rising sea water, and global warming, climate change is actually forcing ecosystem changes, including the animals that live in it and our human habits, emotions and lifestyles, and even the flight of aircraft.  Climate change refers to the fluctuation of the climate over a period of time, which can also refer to decades or millions of years, and the range of fluctuations can be regional or global, and its average meteorological index changes.  At present, the most discussed climate change is about environmental policy, the impact on the contemporary climate, that is, the impact of human factors on the climate, especially the issue of global warming.  For the current global warming, most climate scientists believe that "human activity is most likely the main cause of global warming for nearly half a century."  The causes of climate change affect climate change from a variety of factors, including solar radiation, changes in the Earth's orbit, mountain building, greenhouse gas emissions, and more (discussed below).  Due to the slow response of many factors that indirectly affect the climate on the surface, such as changes in ocean temperature, melting of icebergs, etc., climate change can take centuries or even longer to manifest in relation to changes in factors that directly affect the climate.  Since the development of agriculture, especially since the beginning of the industrial revolution, fossil fuel burning, deforestation, rice cultivation, animal husbandry, industrial production and other human activities have increased.  Greenhouse gases in the atmosphere, such as carbon dioxide, methane and water vapor, absorb infrared radiation from the Earth's surface and then re-radiate, causing the greenhouse effect.  ◆ Ice cover, sea ice, land vegetation, ocean temperature, weathering rate, ocean circulation and greenhouse gas concentration are directly or indirectly affected by the atmosphere.  However, they also all feed back into the atmosphere and affect it in different ways.  Periodic changes in Earth ’ s orbit and an axial tilt relative to the Sun (tens of thousands to hundreds of thousands of years) affect how solar radiation is distributed on the Earth ’ s surface.  ◆ Plate tectonic motion changes the shape, size, location and height of the continental mass and the bathymetry of the ocean, which has a strong impact on the atmosphere and ocean circulation.  ◆ The brightness of the sun continues to increase with the aging of the star, and over time, the sun will transfer more and more energy to the Earth's atmosphere.  Climate change affects weather patterns, and meteorological elements such as temperature, humidity, wind speed, rainfall and extreme weather events can affect the emission, chemical properties, deposition and transport of air pollutants.  Increased carbon dioxide levels and rising temperatures in the atmosphere will prolong the pollen transmission season and increase pollen concentration, leading to allergies and asthma in some people.  ◆ The most familiar and predictable phenomenon is the seasonal cycle, where people adjust their clothing, outdoor activities, thermostats and agricultural practices.  Human societies have changed in terms of adaptive change, despite overwhelming evidence that certain societies and civilizations have collapsed in the face of rapid and severe climate change.  ◆ Complex feedbacks between climate components create “tipping points ” in the climate system, where small, gradual changes in one component of the system can lead to sudden climate changes.  The history of life is strongly influenced by climate change, some of which fundamentally alter the evolutionary process.  Climate change, in addition to the most obvious melting of ice, rising sea water, and global warming, actually forces ecosystems, including the animals that live in them, and us humans, to adapt to its effects in unexpected ways.  Here are six of them: 1. Reduced human sexual behavior In an aging society with fewer children, there are many reasons for the decline in birth rate. In addition to the popularity of contraceptive methods and economic recession, it is also related to climate change.  Research papers from the National Institute of Economic Research in the United States found that the weather affects sexual desire and reduces the birth rate.  On nights with temperatures above 26.6 degrees Celsius, the birth rate after 8 to 10 months from that date is 0.4% lower than the average.  In other words, every night of high temperatures lowers the total number of babies born in the United States by about 1,000.  “1,000 people ” may seem like a drop in the ocean for the U.S. population, but it is estimated that the hot summer nights will surge from 30 days a year to 90 days in the future, and 100,000 fewer babies will be born each year.  2. Do not sleep at night in the city life, no matter how many students or office workers are disturbed by sleep debt.  Chronic fatigue caused by chronic insomnia and lack of sleep can lead to long-term depression, heart disease, dementia, cancer, etc.  If climate change trends continue, the lack of sleep in urban areas will only worsen.  MIT Media Lab estimates that by 2050, there will be six more sleepless nights per 100 Americans per year, rising to 14 by 2099.  As with other climate change impacts, the poor are often the first to bear the brunt, with families who can ’ t afford air conditioning and the elderly who are afraid of the cold and the heat most affected.  3. Hot to irritable, people more violent The so-called "hot to irritable" is definitely not just talk, heat waves not only make us upset and irritable, reckless, and more likely to misunderstand other people's actions contain hostility.  In fact, the crime rate in hot areas is higher than in other areas.  A study of nearly 60 countries last year found that the hotter the weather, the higher the chance of violent crime, and that murders are expected to rise by 6% for every 1 degree Celsius rise in global temperatures in the future.  In the past summer, 40 flights in Phoenix alone were canceled due to extremely hot weather (not haze or hurricanes). Why?  Because the density of hot air is lower than that of cold air, the hotter the air, the less air molecules are available to support the fuselage, and the difficulty of aircraft takeoff increases.  In fact, long runways help aircraft generate more lift, so low air density does not necessarily prevent aircraft from taking off, but it is certainly a difficult problem for some smaller airports such as Phoenix.  5. Polar bear hybrid grizzly polar bear Global warming, continuous melting of ice, originally mainly out of floating ice polar bear forced to retreat inland, mating season in the land meet grizzly bear mixed, mixed into grizzly polar bear, faded snow white fur, replaced with grizzly brown fur.  It is said that this natural hybrid is the expedient measure for polar bears to survive in global warming, because the grizzly bear gene can adapt to a warmer climate, and the offspring of the two bears will lose the thick fur used to keep warm, making the grizzly bear more heat resistant.  Although it may appear to be beneficial for survival, the survival of the real polar bear is increasingly at risk, said Andrew Derocher, a professor of biology at the University of Alberta. “I don ’ t want to say that, but from a genetic perspective, grizzly bears have a great chance of eventually eating the polar bear. ”  The number of shark attacks on humans has increased year by year, and scientists estimate there are two reasons.  One is that rising sea temperatures push sharks north, and the other is that the summer extension makes more swimmers come to the beach to play with the water. The combination of the two increases the chance of shark attacks.  Shark attacks on humans have made shark hunters "famous" and angered sharks, which is also the main reason for the increase in shark attacks.  Last year there were 156 shark attacks due to human provocation.  Evidence for climate change All historical science has a problem: As they explore further in time, they increasingly rely on piecemeal and indirect evidence.  The history of the Earth system is no exception.  High-quality instrumental records spanning the last century exist in most parts of the world, but records became scarce in the 19th century and were rarely recorded until the late 18th century.  Other historical documents, including ship logs, diaries, court and church records, and tax bills, can sometimes be used.  In a strictly geographic setting, these sources can provide information on frosts, droughts, floods, sea ice, monsoon dates, and other climate features that in some cases date back hundreds of years.  Fortunately, climate change also leaves a variety of features in nature.  Climate affects the growth of trees and corals, the abundance and geographical distribution of animal and plant species, the chemistry of oceans and lakes, the accumulation of ice in cold areas, and the erosion and deposition of material on the Earth's surface.  Paleoclimatists study the traces of these effects and devise clever and subtle ways to obtain information about past climates.  Much of the evidence for climate change in the past is indirect, so paleontology requires a lot of investigative work.  Where possible, paleoclimatologists try to cross-examine their conclusions with multiple lines of evidence.  They often face conflicting evidence, but, like other sciences, this often leads to a deeper understanding of the Earth system and its complex history.
