Title: The Gretinist Myth of the Climate Crisis
Content: One of the most inhumane totalitarian ideologies in the history of mankind and one of the most popular aggressive sects of the present time is the myth of the climate crisis.  The mouthpieces of aggressive gretinism regularly declare about the alleged climate crisis affecting the planet: I ask the media to treat the crisis as a crisis...  We are facing an existential threat, and there is no longer time to continue on this path of madness...... as one can expect countries like India, Colombia or Nigeria to care about the climate crisis...  … I am told that I must learn to become a climatologist so that I can “solve the climate crisis ”.  The climate crisis has already been resolved.  On Monday, Greta Thunberg and 15 other children filed a complaint with the United Nations alleging that the world ’ s five largest economies violated human rights by failing to take adequate measures to stop the unfolding climate crisis.  Thunberg and 15 other children accuse countries of “inadequate ” national commitments to curb the climate crisis, as their actions will not stop the global temperature rise below 2 ° C, as agreed in the Paris climate agreement.  Without these vital actions, they argue that the climate crisis will put their livelihoods at risk – from more dangerous storms, food crises, rising sea levels and more.  The lawsuit accuses Germany, France, Brazil, Argentina and Turkey of failing to comply with their obligations under the Convention on the Rights of the Child.  These countries differ in that they are the world ’ s five largest emitters of greenhouse gases, which are the direct cause of the climate crisis.  What is a climate crisis?  Is it happening now?  Does humanity need to do something about it?  And if you do, what?  A short article will not replace large-scale and detailed studies of specialists in a number of scientific disciplines - climatology, paleoclimatology, physics and chemistry of the atmosphere, geology, astronomy, biology, medicine, economics.  It formulates only a few basic theses on the main trends in the evolution of the global climate, forecasts of climatic changes, their consequences for humans.  First of all, those interested in the topic should not mix the problems of ecology (air pollution, water, soil in places of human life and work) and climate issues (the temperature of the planet's air, its humidity, the frequency and intensity of certain natural phenomena).  Environmental problems (primarily the production and disposal of garbage, emissions of hazardous substances, industrial and energy waste, emissions of gasoline engines, etc.) caused by human activities threaten the health and lives of millions of people, deserve the most serious attention and solutions.  Citizens who advocate for the solution of environmental problems are highly respected and deserve every support.  Climate change is largely caused not by human activities, but by natural factors, their impact on the health and lives of millions of people is minimal, and in recent decades, mostly positive; in addition, the degree of their impact on human life is constantly declining.  The struggle against climate change is as expedient as the struggle to change the motion of the planets or the intensity of the radiance of the sun, and persons depicting such a struggle join the ranks of the aggressive sects of climate alarmists and gretinists.  The topic of interest should also not be confused with climate and weather.  Climate is a long-term (according to the existing agreement between climatologists - at least three decades) weather regime.  Therefore, if you hear (read) statements about the need to combat climate change because, for example, there was no snow this year, or the last two summers were especially hot, or as a result of last year ’ s fires burned so many hectares of forest, then this is a clear confirmation that the person making such statements is either incompetent in climate and climate change issues, or deliberately misleading the public.  Area of fires in Australia (ha), 1920-2020 3.  Since a crisis in the most general sense is a radical change in the state of a phenomenon, a climate crisis can be called such a significant climate change, which would have the following characteristics: - it would be large-scale (for example, there was a significant increase in air temperature, radically different in its magnitude from traditional climate changes); - it would be very rapid (for example, the increase in air temperature occurred much faster than ever before); - it would have especially severe consequences for humans (for example, long - term increases in air temperature have led to increased mortality).  If none of these signs of a climate crisis is observed, then there is therefore no climate crisis itself, and the usual climate changes are taking place instead of the crisis.  The climate of planet Earth is constantly changing.  It has changed in the past, it has changed in the present, it will change in the future – as long as our planet exists.  Constant change is an inherent feature of the global climate.  There is no fundamental disagreement about the fact of climate change among scientists.  There is indeed a scientific consensus, but only on this issue: Earth ’ s climate change is and is happening all the time.  Attempts by climate alarmists and gretinists to spread the myth that their opponents deny the very fact of climate change are unscrupulous propaganda.  Differences between experts exist not on the fact of climate change, but on other issues.  In particular, there are disagreements about: — the ratio of current and historically observed levels of global temperature, — the direction of climate change, — the magnitude (scale) of climate change, — the speed of climate change, — the causes of climate change, — the predictions of climate change, — the effects of climate change on humans, — the optimal strategy for mankind ’ s response to climate change.  The correct answers to many of these questions depend crucially on the time horizon chosen — 40, 80, 1,000, 10,000, hundreds of thousands, or millions of years.  Depending on the time horizon, the answers to these questions are different, including the exact opposite.  The global climate is one of the most complex natural systems.  The laws of climate change are currently completely unknown to mankind.  Historically, climate change has seen both long - term, relatively stable trends and cycles of varying durations and frequencies, as well as abrupt, crisis phenomena that radically changed the climate in a short time.  Over the past fifty million years, the global climate of the Earth has generally tended to cool down.  Over shorter periods of time (for example, in the last 800,000 years), climate change has been largely cyclical.  The time horizons of different climatic cycles are different - from the well-known annual cycle (winter - spring - summer - autumn) to cycles lasting 70-80 years, 1300 years, about 100 thousand years (Milankovitch cycles).  Reconstruction of temperature, CO2 concentration, dust according to the ice cores of Vostok 11 station.  In the history of global climate, there have been both climate crises and climate catastrophes (as, for example, during the late Dryas (about 12,000 years ago, when temperatures fell by about 10 ° C for a hundred years and perhaps even faster).  The current level of global temperature is not unique in historical perspective.  The average annual temperature of planet Earth is currently estimated at about 14.5 degrees Celsius.  In the history of the planet there were periods when the air temperature was lower than the current – in the early Permian period, in the Oligocene, during the periodic glaciations of the Pleistocene.  For most of the last half billion years, the air temperature on the surface of the Earth has been markedly higher than today, and for about half of this period it was about 10-15 ° C higher than today (that is, in the range of 25-30 ° C).  Global temperature over the past 60 million years 13.  During the regular glaciations of the Pleistocene, cold periods lasted about 90 thousand years and had peak temperatures about 10 ° C below the current one.  Long glaciations were replaced by short (4-6 thousand years) warm interglacial periods with temperatures 1-3 ° C higher than the current one.  About 10 thousand years ago, another sharp increase in temperature (about 10 ° C) began, thanks to which the colossal glaciers that occupied a significant part of the territory of Eurasia and North America melted.  This period, in which we were lucky to live, was called the climatic optimum of the Holocene.  Global warming of the climate has played a key role in mastering the secrets of agriculture and the transition of mankind to the civilizational stage of its development.  Over the past 10 thousand years, there have been at least 5 warm periods - the so-called "climatic optimum", during each of which for 150-300 years the temperature on the planet was 1-3 ° C higher than the current one. Title: Reduce Global Warming by Modifying Food Production Methods
Content: In their new study, researchers from the University of Oxford found that modifying the way food is produced could be a good way to reduce global warming and climate change.  A new study shows that wind power and geothermal energy are not enough to keep the Earth cool.  Even if the energy transition takes place entirely in environmentally friendly ways, greenhouse gas emissions from the world ’ s food system will be exposed to heat.  In the new study, researchers from the University of Oxford suggest that to prevent climate change and extreme heat, all food production sectors must be rapidly and significantly modified.  In addition to replacing fossil fuels with environmentally friendly fuels, the food system also needs to change and reform.  Michael Clark and his colleagues believe that if things continue the same way, harmful emissions from agriculture will be released between 2020 and 2100.  Carbon dioxide is released as a result of many activities, including cutting down trees in tropical forests, using agricultural machinery, and using chemicals in agriculture.  The use of fertilizers can lead to the release of nitrous oxide, and cows also emit methane, which is a potent warming gas.  In this project, the researchers examined forests in the United States and applied standard hypotheses about how diets might improve economic conditions in communities.  As income increases, people tend to consume more meat, dairy, eggs and animal products.  The production of animal products has many negative effects on the climate and environment.  The researchers proposed an experiment in which all sources of greenhouse gas emissions were eliminated.  This test requires a complete modification of electric vehicles, buildings that draw their heat from geothermal sources, and so on.  Clark said such a situation would be really scary.  Researchers and food policy experts already know that food production plays a significant role in global warming, but adopting this proposed new strategy is far more rigorous and complex.  Clark said: “The good thing is that there ’ s a lot we can do to fix this problem, but it needs to be done a little bit of everything.  In the project, the researchers examined the impact of five important agricultural strategies, including rapidly strengthening land to reduce deforestation and changing diets with less animal products.  None of these strategies alone can do enough to reduce heat emissions, but advancing all of these strategies together could make it possible to achieve the ultimate goal.  End of message.

Content: Climatologists predict that in the 21st century, the amount and intensity of snowfall will increase throughout Russia, and in some regions, arid conditions are expected to worsen. Title: Climate change and water scarcity are top priorities.
Content: Assistant Professor of Water Engineering at the Faculty of Agriculture of Shahrekord University said: “The main priority of the authorities should be water shortage and climate change, so that water factories are moved to the seaside and agriculture in areas that are facing water shortage is limited. ”  He said: “It ’ s been a long time, it ’ s been a long time, it ’ s been a long time, it ’ s been a long time.  “When we talk about climate change, we mean meteorological parameters that have been measured over long periods of time, and these changes manifest themselves in either natural or artificial forms, which are caused by humans.  Nasr Esfahani said: “Various factors such as sunspots, changes in the earth ’ s crust, changes in vegetation or the movement of continents, or changes in ocean temperature naturally cause climate change.  “What has happened in the past year is that humans have caused an imbalance in meteorological parameters due to excessive consumption of natural resources, including oil, gas and fossil fuels, and by destroying natural resources such as forests and expanding factories and cities.  The university professor pointed out that the country is climatally located in a dry region, saying: "We should not expect the climate to change from dry to wet, because this is a very wrong expectation that some in the society suggest this."  He said: "Climate change has become very clear in the last 40 years, so we have to adapt to this situation that has been fluctuating and know that drought or drought fluctuations are part of the nature of the region's climate."  Nasr Isfahani said: "In this situation, climate change is occurring and extreme phenomena such as severe droughts, drought, heat and cold are increasing, there is no alternative but to adapt to them, for example, agricultural products can be used to prevent frostbite, to use resistant products.  Regarding water resources, he said: “At the same time as the climate change, the consumption of water resources has greatly expanded, especially in the last 50 years, when agriculture has been the center of development in the country. ”  The university professor said: "If we examine the rainfall parameter in more detail, we see that the average rainfall has not changed, but the extremes have changed a lot and these changes are significant, on the other hand, the effective rainfall has not changed and the ineffective rainfall has increased, which means that there is a shortage of water resources."  He said: "What has been observed is that, contrary to the rainfall parameter, changes in the temperature parameter, especially the minimum temperature, are highly effective and the trend of increasing the minimum temperature is observed in many stations in the country."  Nasr Esfahani pointed out that in mountainous areas the precipitation has changed from solid to liquid state, adding: "When there is snow in the region, because the snow is slowly melting and sinking into underground sources, it feeds them, on the other hand, the occurrence of rain brings water runoff, which feeds surface water instead of feeding groundwater resources."  He added that excessive consumption of water resources, expansion of the area under cultivation, non-observance of the cultivation pattern and the use of traditional methods for irrigation have led to the reduction of groundwater.  Assistant Professor of Water Engineering at Shahrekord University emphasized: "The authorities were aware of the current situation, but they did not think that the effects of climate change would be egregious and misrepresented, and today we face a fundamental problem, for example, if there was a shortage of water, it was solved by harvesting from underground water resources and we assigned this problem to the future."  He continued: “We have reached a point where groundwater resources are not the answer to the shortage of water, and this problem has become such that measures must be taken.  Nasr Esfahani said that for short-term purposes, water resources have not been considered because steel and water mills have been built in the country, which if this decision process continues, despite the lack of water resources, will still be built in the future.  “We should not expect that one day our country will be as abundant as Europe, because the lack of rainfall in our region has been caused by the rotation of the earth and the circulation of the atmosphere, so in addition to adapting to climate change, if there is to be a cost to this, it should be done today and we should not postpone those costs to the future, because we may face more limitations in the future. ”  The university professor noted that the main priority of the authorities should be water scarcity and climate change, so that water factories are moved to the seaside and agriculture is limited in areas with water scarcity.  End of message.

Title: Land abuse contributes to climate change
Content: The land is often abused and contributes to the harm of climate change 2019-08-06 16: 42 Taiwan Awakening News reporter Zhuang Ruimeng / Taipei reported that the land has been used by humans to cultivate and lose its original function of absorbing carbon.  (Photo by M. Prinke on Flicker under Creative Commons license) Share Facebook Treating land better helps humanity fight climate change.  The UN Intergovernmental Panel of Experts on Climate Change, which is currently meeting, will present an updated report on the current state of human land use.  Experts pointed out that due to human behavior, land has changed from carbon capture to carbon release, threatening to exacerbate the power of climate change, and highlighting the importance of land use.  According to The Independent, global soils can currently absorb 1% of carbon, down from 7% in the past.  If the land is cultivated in a more sustainable way, carbon will be absorbed by the soil to become a carbon reservoir.  Currently, 1 / 3 of all pollution emissions come from land.  “If we take the severity of the climate problem seriously now, it will be worse if we don ’ t have land as a carbon reservoir, ” said Li Wen, a representative of the World Resources Institute. The scientists also pointed out that continued pressure on land, including the provision of food, wood and plant raw materials to meet increasing population needs, will make carbon reduction targets more difficult to achieve.  In addition, 33% of arable land has been used to grow crops that provide animal feed.  Professor Lixon of the University of Clanfield in the UK also believes that the latest IPCC report will provide more evidence that land degradation will also exacerbate climate change and lead to an increase in the crisis.  Addressing land abuse can focus on intensive agriculture, which involves farming on as small a land as possible, allowing more natural land to absorb carbon dioxide, according to the BBC. In a moderately warm world, some aspects of the economy may improve slightly in the short term.  However, if the world does not reduce greenhouse gas emissions significantly and continuously, the planet is expected to continue to warm, causing significant net damage to the economy this century, especially as adaptation efforts are thwarted.  It is expected that the annual losses in some sectors of the economy will reach hundreds of billions of dollars by the end of the century, continuing to grow at the rate of past emissions. While some regions may see gains in productivity favoring expanded or alternative crops in the coming decades, overall, production of major crops is expected to decline due to higher temperatures, potentially altering water availability, soil erosion, and outbreaks of disease and pests.  Rising temperatures during the growing season are expected to be the biggest factor in the decline in agricultural productivity.  If the temperature at night exceeds 35 ° C, it will cause rice to be unable to pollinate; it will also aggravate the impact of diseases and pests, affecting the harvest of crops; high temperature and rain will make the soil unable to maintain nutrients, reduce crop yields and increase production costs.  The expected increase in extreme hot weather is expected to result in further heat stress for livestock, resulting in significant economic losses for producers.  Climate change is also likely to cause large-scale changes in the supply and prices of many agricultural products around the world, and the global supply and prices of agricultural products will also change dramatically.  These changes threaten future gains in commodity crop production and endanger rural livelihoods.  Agricultural production is an industry that is highly dependent on natural resources such as water, soil and biodiversity.  Climate change causes global temperature increases and uneven rainfall, disrupting crop growth, affecting the original habitats of ecosystems, and affecting the yield and quality of agricultural products, endangering food security and productivity, and causing loss of biodiversity.  There are many adaptation strategies to cope with climate variability, while reversing the adverse effects of change on agricultural production. The climate crisis has already been resolved. Does humanity need to do something about it?  And if you do, what?  A short article will not replace large-scale and detailed studies of specialists in a number of scientific disciplines - climatology, paleoclimatology, physics and chemistry of the atmosphere, geology, astronomy, biology, medicine, economics.  It formulates only a few basic theses on the main trends in the evolution of the global climate, forecasts of climatic changes, their consequences for humans.  First of all, those interested in the topic should not mix the problems of ecology (air pollution, water, soil in places of human life and work) and climate issues (the temperature of the planet's air, its humidity, the frequency and intensity of certain natural phenomena).  Environmental problems (primarily the production and disposal of garbage, emissions of hazardous substances, industrial and energy waste, emissions of gasoline engines, etc.) caused by human activities threaten the health and lives of millions of people, deserve the most serious attention and solutions.  Citizens who advocate for the solution of environmental problems are highly respected and deserve every support.  Climate change is largely caused not by human activities, but by natural factors, their impact on the health and lives of millions of people is minimal, and in recent decades, mostly positive; in addition, the degree of their impact on human life is constantly declining.  The struggle against climate change is as expedient as the struggle to change the motion of the planets or the intensity of the radiance of the sun, and persons depicting such a struggle join the ranks of the aggressive sects of climate alarmists and gretinists.  The topic of interest should also not be confused with climate and weather.  Climate is a long-term (according to the existing agreement between climatologists - at least three decades) weather regime.  Therefore, if you hear (read) statements about the need to combat climate change because, for example, there was no snow this year, or the last two summers were especially hot, or as a result of last year ’ s fires burned so many hectares of forest, then this is a clear confirmation that the person making such statements is either incompetent in climate and climate change issues, or deliberately misleading the public. Since a crisis in the most general sense is a radical change in the state of a phenomenon, a climate crisis can be called such a significant climate change, which would have the following characteristics: - it would be large-scale (for example, there was a significant increase in air temperature, radically different in its magnitude from traditional climate changes); - it would be very rapid (for example, the increase in air temperature occurred much faster than ever before); - it would have especially severe consequences for humans (for example, long - term increases in air temperature have led to increased mortality).  If none of these signs of a climate crisis is observed, then there is therefore no climate crisis itself, and the usual climate changes are taking place instead of the crisis.  The climate of planet Earth is constantly changing.  It has changed in the past, it has changed in the present, it will change in the future – as long as our planet exists.  Constant change is an inherent feature of the global climate.  There is no fundamental disagreement about the fact of climate change among scientists.  There is indeed a scientific consensus, but only on this issue: Earth ’ s climate change is and is happening all the time.  Attempts by climate alarmists and gretinists to spread the myth that their opponents deny the very fact of climate change are unscrupulous propaganda.  Differences between experts exist not on the fact of climate change, but on other issues.  In particular, there are disagreements about: — the ratio of current and historically observed levels of global temperature, — the direction of climate change, — the magnitude (scale) of climate change, — the speed of climate change, — the causes of climate change, — the predictions of climate change, — the effects of climate change on humans, — the optimal strategy for mankind ’ s response to climate change.  The correct answers to many of these questions depend crucially on the time horizon chosen — 40, 80, 1,000, 10,000, hundreds of thousands, or millions of years. The laws of climate change are currently completely unknown to mankind.  Historically, climate change has seen both long - term, relatively stable trends and cycles of varying durations and frequencies, as well as abrupt, crisis phenomena that radically changed the climate in a short time.  Over the past fifty million years, the global climate of the Earth has generally tended to cool down.  Over shorter periods of time (for example, in the last 800,000 years), climate change has been largely cyclical.  The time horizons of different climatic cycles are different - from the well-known annual cycle (winter - spring - summer - autumn) to cycles lasting 70-80 years, 1300 years, about 100 thousand years (Milankovitch cycles). In the history of the planet there were periods when the air temperature was lower than the current – in the early Permian period, in the Oligocene, during the periodic glaciations of the Pleistocene.  For most of the last half billion years, the air temperature on the surface of the Earth has been markedly higher than today, and for about half of this period it was about 10-15 ° C higher than today (that is, in the range of 25-30 ° C). About 10 thousand years ago, another sharp increase in temperature (about 10 ° C) began, thanks to which the colossal glaciers that occupied a significant part of the territory of Eurasia and North America melted.  This period, in which we were lucky to live, was called the climatic optimum of the Holocene.  Global warming of the climate has played a key role in mastering the secrets of agriculture and the transition of mankind to the civilizational stage of its development. Title: Reduce Global Warming by Modifying Food Production Methods
Content: In their new study, researchers from the University of Oxford found that modifying the way food is produced could be a good way to reduce global warming and climate change.  A new study shows that wind power and geothermal energy are not enough to keep the Earth cool.  Even if the energy transition takes place entirely in environmentally friendly ways, greenhouse gas emissions from the world ’ s food system will be exposed to heat.  In the new study, researchers from the University of Oxford suggest that to prevent climate change and extreme heat, all food production sectors must be rapidly and significantly modified.  In addition to replacing fossil fuels with environmentally friendly fuels, the food system also needs to change and reform.  Michael Clark and his colleagues believe that if things continue the same way, harmful emissions from agriculture will be released between 2020 and 2100.  Carbon dioxide is released as a result of many activities, including cutting down trees in tropical forests, using agricultural machinery, and using chemicals in agriculture.  The use of fertilizers can lead to the release of nitrous oxide, and cows also emit methane, which is a potent warming gas.  In this project, the researchers examined forests in the United States and applied standard hypotheses about how diets might improve economic conditions in communities.  As income increases, people tend to consume more meat, dairy, eggs and animal products.  The production of animal products has many negative effects on the climate and environment.  The researchers proposed an experiment in which all sources of greenhouse gas emissions were eliminated.  This test requires a complete modification of electric vehicles, buildings that draw their heat from geothermal sources, and so on.  Clark said such a situation would be really scary.  Researchers and food policy experts already know that food production plays a significant role in global warming, but adopting this proposed new strategy is far more rigorous and complex.  Clark said: “The good thing is that there ’ s a lot we can do to fix this problem, but it needs to be done a little bit of everything.  In the project, the researchers examined the impact of five important agricultural strategies, including rapidly strengthening land to reduce deforestation and changing diets with less animal products.  None of these strategies alone can do enough to reduce heat emissions, but advancing all of these strategies together could make it possible to achieve the ultimate goal.  End of message.

Title: Climate change and water scarcity are top priorities.
Content: Assistant Professor of Water Engineering at the Faculty of Agriculture of Shahrekord University said: “The main priority of the authorities should be water shortage and climate change, so that water factories are moved to the seaside and agriculture in areas that are facing water shortage is limited. ”  He said: “It ’ s been a long time, it ’ s been a long time, it ’ s been a long time, it ’ s been a long time.  “When we talk about climate change, we mean meteorological parameters that have been measured over long periods of time, and these changes manifest themselves in either natural or artificial forms, which are caused by humans.  Nasr Esfahani said: “Various factors such as sunspots, changes in the earth ’ s crust, changes in vegetation or the movement of continents, or changes in ocean temperature naturally cause climate change.  “What has happened in the past year is that humans have caused an imbalance in meteorological parameters due to excessive consumption of natural resources, including oil, gas and fossil fuels, and by destroying natural resources such as forests and expanding factories and cities.  The university professor pointed out that the country is climatally located in a dry region, saying: "We should not expect the climate to change from dry to wet, because this is a very wrong expectation that some in the society suggest this."  He said: "Climate change has become very clear in the last 40 years, so we have to adapt to this situation that has been fluctuating and know that drought or drought fluctuations are part of the nature of the region's climate."  Nasr Isfahani said: "In this situation, climate change is occurring and extreme phenomena such as severe droughts, drought, heat and cold are increasing, there is no alternative but to adapt to them, for example, agricultural products can be used to prevent frostbite, to use resistant products.  Regarding water resources, he said: “At the same time as the climate change, the consumption of water resources has greatly expanded, especially in the last 50 years, when agriculture has been the center of development in the country. ”  The university professor said: "If we examine the rainfall parameter in more detail, we see that the average rainfall has not changed, but the extremes have changed a lot and these changes are significant, on the other hand, the effective rainfall has not changed and the ineffective rainfall has increased, which means that there is a shortage of water resources."  He said: "What has been observed is that, contrary to the rainfall parameter, changes in the temperature parameter, especially the minimum temperature, are highly effective and the trend of increasing the minimum temperature is observed in many stations in the country."  Nasr Esfahani pointed out that in mountainous areas the precipitation has changed from solid to liquid state, adding: "When there is snow in the region, because the snow is slowly melting and sinking into underground sources, it feeds them, on the other hand, the occurrence of rain brings water runoff, which feeds surface water instead of feeding groundwater resources."  He added that excessive consumption of water resources, expansion of the area under cultivation, non-observance of the cultivation pattern and the use of traditional methods for irrigation have led to the reduction of groundwater.  Assistant Professor of Water Engineering at Shahrekord University emphasized: "The authorities were aware of the current situation, but they did not think that the effects of climate change would be egregious and misrepresented, and today we face a fundamental problem, for example, if there was a shortage of water, it was solved by harvesting from underground water resources and we assigned this problem to the future."  He continued: “We have reached a point where groundwater resources are not the answer to the shortage of water, and this problem has become such that measures must be taken.  Nasr Esfahani said that for short-term purposes, water resources have not been considered because steel and water mills have been built in the country, which if this decision process continues, despite the lack of water resources, will still be built in the future.  “We should not expect that one day our country will be as abundant as Europe, because the lack of rainfall in our region has been caused by the rotation of the earth and the circulation of the atmosphere, so in addition to adapting to climate change, if there is to be a cost to this, it should be done today and we should not postpone those costs to the future, because we may face more limitations in the future. ”  The university professor noted that the main priority of the authorities should be water scarcity and climate change, so that water factories are moved to the seaside and agriculture is limited in areas with water scarcity.  End of message.

Title: Land abuse contributes to climate change
Content: The land is often abused and contributes to the harm of climate change 2019-08-06 16: 42 Taiwan Awakening News reporter Zhuang Ruimeng / Taipei reported that the land has been used by humans to cultivate and lose its original function of absorbing carbon.  (Photo by M. Prinke on Flicker under Creative Commons license) Share Facebook Treating land better helps humanity fight climate change.  The UN Intergovernmental Panel of Experts on Climate Change, which is currently meeting, will present an updated report on the current state of human land use.  Experts pointed out that due to human behavior, land has changed from carbon capture to carbon release, threatening to exacerbate the power of climate change, and highlighting the importance of land use.  According to The Independent, global soils can currently absorb 1% of carbon, down from 7% in the past.  If the land is cultivated in a more sustainable way, carbon will be absorbed by the soil to become a carbon reservoir.  Currently, 1 / 3 of all pollution emissions come from land.  “If we take the severity of the climate problem seriously now, it will be worse if we don ’ t have land as a carbon reservoir, ” said Li Wen, a representative of the World Resources Institute. The scientists also pointed out that continued pressure on land, including the provision of food, wood and plant raw materials to meet increasing population needs, will make carbon reduction targets more difficult to achieve.  In addition, 33% of arable land has been used to grow crops that provide animal feed.  Professor Lixon of the University of Clanfield in the UK also believes that the latest IPCC report will provide more evidence that land degradation will also exacerbate climate change and lead to an increase in the crisis.  Addressing land abuse can focus on intensive agriculture, which involves farming on as small a land as possible, allowing more natural land to absorb carbon dioxide, according to the BBC.  Another option is to farm in a less dense and friendly climate.  Either way, however, the IPCC report will point out that poor farmers will be the group most affected by global warming.  Professor Berman, of the University of Oxford ’ s Institute of Environmental Change, said climate change had led to soil erosion in the south of the UK through more intense rainfall.  “Warmer temperatures and heavier rainfall will worsen soil erosion, soil compaction, loss of organic matter and biodiversity, and soil and rock flows, ” said Li Huicheng, chairman of the IPCC.“ I hope this report will serve to remind the world more about the threat that climate change poses to land. ”  [More details, see here]

passages.title: The End of Berlinale: Women ’ s Full Hands and Iranians ’ Empty Hands
passages.passage: The Berlin International Film Festival ended on Saturday, February 24 with a special ceremony.  The ceremony was attended by more than 1,600 guests at Berlin ’ s Berlinale Palace.  The Best Golden Bear Award went to the Romanian film “Don ’ t Touch Me ” by Adina Pintielli.  Iranian filmmakers returned home empty-handed this time.  In the main section of this year ’ s festival, 24 films were screened, of which 19 were competing for the Golden Bear and the Silver Bears of Berlinale.  This year ’ s jury consisted of German director and producer Tom Tikor, American critic Stephanie Zachark, Spanish film expert Chema Prado, American producer Adele Romanski, Japanese actress and musician Ryuichi Sakamoto, and Belgian actor Cecil de France.  “Don ’ t Touch Me ” co-directed by Germany, France, Romania, Bulgaria and the Czech Republic won the Berlinale Golden Bear.  The film also won the festival ’ s 50,000 Euro prize as the first film.  The Grand Jury Prize went to Polish film Mogue, and the Silver Bear went to American director Wes Anderson for his film Island of Dogs.  Other awards in this year ’ s main section were awarded in the following order: Silver Bear for Best Actor: Anthony Bajon for his performance in Praying from France.  Silver Bear for Best Actress: Anna Brown for her role in the film Heir Women from Paraguay.  (The film, directed by Marcelo Martisi, also received the Silver Bear Award for Best Film with a New Vision.)  Silver Bear for Best Screenplay: Alonso Virilassius and Manuel Alcala from Mexico for Museum Film.  Silver Bear for Outstanding Art Work: Elena Okinaya from Russia for the costume design of the Dolatov film.  The best short and documentary films in the Golden Bear category were given to the Rwandan and Swiss short film The Men Behind the Wall, directed by Samuel Eichmore, from Israel and the Silver Bear, and to the Rwandan and Swiss short film Imfura.  In the documentary category, Ruth Beckermann ’ s “Waltz Waldheim ” from Austria was selected as the best film of the year for the Berlinale.  The other Berlinale Awards are held annually in Berlinale, another section entitled Panorama.  In this section, awards are given to the best films by audience selection.  This year, the film "Profile", directed by Timur Bekmantov, and the documentary "Silence of Others", directed by Almodeena Karasedo, were awarded in the Panorama category.  The profile is a joint creation of the United States, Russia, Britain and Cyprus and the silence of others is a joint product of the United States and Spain.  The Crystal Bear received the adolescents section over the age of 14 from the Swiss feature film "Fortona" by Germinal Rao.  The film also won the 7,500 Euro International Jury Prize.  In this section, the film "Kim Hollikhanda" by Sara Voltmaier from the Netherlands was also awarded the Crystal Bear and the film Dressage by Pouya Badkoobeh was honored.  In the “Generation ” category for children ’ s films, this year the feature film“ Hand on Heart ” by Luke Picard from Canada and the short film “Guide to a 12-year-old Girl ” by Tilda Cobham Hervey from Australia received the Crystal Bears.  The empty hands of Iranians and the audacity of Leila Hatami all the Iranian artists present at the Berlin International Film Festival returned home empty-handed this year, and only the film “Dresaj ” directed by Pooya Badkoobeh was appreciated for the clever narrative of the story.  But the press conference of Mani Haghighi and Leila Hatami, the director and lead actress of the film "Pig", created controversy.  At the press conference, Leila Hatami lamented that peaceful protests in Iran are being violently suppressed, saying she suffered greatly from the issue.  In contrast, Mani Haghighi, while acknowledging that there is censorship in Iran and that artists are trying to circumvent this censorship in their own way, protested to journalists why they always ask political questions at press conferences when they reach Iranian artists instead of doing their work.  After the conference, Leila Hatami was severely criticized by the Fajr Film Festival officials and some regime figures on social media.  But Mani Haghighi supported Hatami in a video posted on YouTube and social media, saying: “Peaceful demonstrations are people ’ s natural right and they should not be repressed for it.  Laila Hatami ’ s discomfort was justified, and I understand that. ”

passages.title: Winners of the 2019 Berlin Festival are announced
passages.passage: According to the Mehr News Agency, the Berlin Film Festival recognized its winners an hour ago when it presented its main prize to the illegal representative of Iranian cinema.  Iranian cinema had four official representatives at the event, but the new film, Mohammad Rasoulof, which was produced in Iran without legal process and sent to the festival, was given special attention by the organizers of the event.  The Berlin Film Festival has previously paid more attention to the unofficial representatives of Iranian cinema and even anti-Iranian works.  According to Variety, the winners of the Silver and Gold Bears were announced on Saturday at the closing ceremony of the 70th Berlin Film Festival.  The International Competition Jury Awards were awarded: Golden Bear for Best Picture: Mohammad Rasoulof of The Great Jury Prize Silver Bear: “Never, Rarely, Sometimes, Always ” Eliza Hitman of USA Silver Bear Award Best Director: Hong Sang-soo for“ The Woman Who Escaped ” South Korea Silver Bear Award: Paula Bear Winner for “Ondyne ” Director Christian Petzold of Germany Award for Best Screenplay Winner Silver Bear: Elio Germano for“ Hidden ” Giorgio Dieretti of Italy Award for Best Screenplay Winner Silver Bear: Damiano and Fabio Dinochenzo for “Bad Stories ” Special Prize 70th Berlinale Silver Bear Winner:“ Eliminate Histori ” directed by Benoit Delpin and Gustave Croerne of France and Belgium Best Outstanding Artistic Achievement Silver Bear Winner: Jerogen Yorgis for Filming “Dao.Natasha ” by Ilya Kezhanovsky and Ekaterina Ortel (Germany) Best First Film:“ The Magrha ” by Camilo Risterpo Best Documentary Feature: “Exposure to the Radiation ” Directed by Rieti Pan Award Best Short Film Gold Bear:“ T ” by Keisha Ray Witherspoon Jury Award Winner Silver Bear Award Winner: "Filipino" by Rafael Manuel Uday Short Film Award: "Lucy the Genius" by Adrien Marizou Fipreschi Jury also won the award in the international competition section to "Ondin" directed by Christian Petzold.  The Panorama Award went to Bassam Tariq's "Joker Mongol" and won the award in the Forum section "Twentieth Century" directed by Matthew Rankin.  In the Panorama Audience category, Father, directed by Serdan Golabowicz, was selected as the winner of the Fiction Film Award.  In the same section, the second award was given to “Feel Not Hard ” directed by Faraz Shariat and the third award was given to“ Hope ” directed by Maria Sudal.  In the 2020 documentary section, the first prize was awarded to David France ’ s “Welcome to Chechnya ”, while the second prize was awarded to Susan Regina Moyers ’“ Saudi Escape ” and the third to “Little Girl ” by Sebastian Lifshitz of France.  In the jury section of the World Church, the international competition section award was given to “The Devil Does Not Exist ” by Mohammad Rasoulof and won the Panorama section“ Father ” by Serdan Golabovich from Serbia.  The film "Saudi Escape" by Swiss director Suzanne Regina Moyers was also praised.  Other winners this year: Children's Generation Awards (Kopelos) - Children's Bear Children's Jury Best Feature Film: Alexander Rockwell 's Something Sweet Special Commendation: John Sheedy' s Crystal Bear Best Short Film: Martina Matzkin 's Name Special Commendation: Amira Jahan' s Name Generation Children (Kopelos) - International Jury Awards - International Jury Awards Best Feature Film: “The Wolves ” directed by Samuel Kishi Leopo from Mexico Special Commendation:“ The Funny Ones ” directed by Mimona Dukura from France Special Commendation: “Mama Mama ” directed by Sol Berretto Picchon-Riviere from Argentina Best Short Film:“ In the Name of the Son ” directed by Martina Matzkin from Argentina Special Commendation: “Generation of Kites ” directed by Seyyed Hosseini in Iran The winner was Caro Alves de Souza of Brazil ’ s“ My Name is Baghdad, ” and a special tribute was given to Nebuchadnezzar Sova ’ s “A Voice in the Wind. ”  In this category, the award for the best short film went to Hamila Overdiri from Morocco and Mahyar Mandegar ’ s “Winged White Horse ” from Iran.  The closing ceremony of the 70th Berlin Film Festival began tonight at 17: 30 and the awards ceremony began at 19: 00 Berlin time.

Title: The End of Berlinale: Women ’ s Full Hands and Iranians ’ Empty Hands
Content: The Berlin International Film Festival ended on Saturday, February 24 with a special ceremony.  The ceremony was attended by more than 1,600 guests at Berlin ’ s Berlinale Palace.  The Best Golden Bear Award went to the Romanian film “Don ’ t Touch Me ” by Adina Pintielli.  Iranian filmmakers returned home empty-handed this time.  In the main section of this year ’ s festival, 24 films were screened, of which 19 were competing for the Golden Bear and the Silver Bears of Berlinale.  This year ’ s jury consisted of German director and producer Tom Tikor, American critic Stephanie Zachark, Spanish film expert Chema Prado, American producer Adele Romanski, Japanese actress and musician Ryuichi Sakamoto, and Belgian actor Cecil de France.  “Don ’ t Touch Me ” co-directed by Germany, France, Romania, Bulgaria and the Czech Republic won the Berlinale Golden Bear.  The film also won the festival ’ s 50,000 Euro prize as the first film.  The Grand Jury Prize went to Polish film Mogue, and the Silver Bear went to American director Wes Anderson for his film Island of Dogs.  Other awards in this year ’ s main section were awarded in the following order: Silver Bear for Best Actor: Anthony Bajon for his performance in Praying from France.  Silver Bear for Best Actress: Anna Brown for her role in the film Heir Women from Paraguay.  (The film, directed by Marcelo Martisi, also received the Silver Bear Award for Best Film with a New Vision.)  Silver Bear for Best Screenplay: Alonso Virilassius and Manuel Alcala from Mexico for Museum Film.  Silver Bear for Outstanding Art Work: Elena Okinaya from Russia for the costume design of the Dolatov film.  The best short and documentary films in the Golden Bear category were given to the Rwandan and Swiss short film The Men Behind the Wall, directed by Samuel Eichmore, from Israel and the Silver Bear, and to the Rwandan and Swiss short film Imfura.  In the documentary category, Ruth Beckermann ’ s “Waltz Waldheim ” from Austria was selected as the best film of the year for the Berlinale.  The other Berlinale Awards are held annually in Berlinale, another section entitled Panorama.  In this section, awards are given to the best films by audience selection.  This year, the film "Profile", directed by Timur Bekmantov, and the documentary "Silence of Others", directed by Almodeena Karasedo, were awarded in the Panorama category.  The profile is a joint creation of the United States, Russia, Britain and Cyprus and the silence of others is a joint product of the United States and Spain.  The Crystal Bear received the adolescents section over the age of 14 from the Swiss feature film "Fortona" by Germinal Rao.  The film also won the 7,500 Euro International Jury Prize.  In this section, the film "Kim Hollikhanda" by Sara Voltmaier from the Netherlands was also awarded the Crystal Bear and the film Dressage by Pouya Badkoobeh was honored.  In the “Generation ” category for children ’ s films, this year the feature film“ Hand on Heart ” by Luke Picard from Canada and the short film “Guide to a 12-year-old Girl ” by Tilda Cobham Hervey from Australia received the Crystal Bears.  The empty hands of Iranians and the audacity of Leila Hatami all the Iranian artists present at the Berlin International Film Festival returned home empty-handed this year, and only the film “Dresaj ” directed by Pooya Badkoobeh was appreciated for the clever narrative of the story.  But the press conference of Mani Haghighi and Leila Hatami, the director and lead actress of the film "Pig", created controversy.  At the press conference, Leila Hatami lamented that peaceful protests in Iran are being violently suppressed, saying she suffered greatly from the issue.  In contrast, Mani Haghighi, while acknowledging that there is censorship in Iran and that artists are trying to circumvent this censorship in their own way, protested to journalists why they always ask political questions at press conferences when they reach Iranian artists instead of doing their work.  After the conference, Leila Hatami was severely criticized by the Fajr Film Festival officials and some regime figures on social media.  But Mani Haghighi supported Hatami in a video posted on YouTube and social media, saying: “Peaceful demonstrations are people ’ s natural right and they should not be repressed for it.  Laila Hatami ’ s discomfort was justified, and I understand that. ”

The Panorama Award went to Bassam Tariq's "Joker Mongol" and won the award in the Forum section "Twentieth Century" directed by Matthew Rankin.  In the Panorama Audience category, Father, directed by Serdan Golabowicz, was selected as the winner of the Fiction Film Award.  In the same section, the second award was given to “Feel Not Hard ” directed by Faraz Shariat and the third award was given to“ Hope ” directed by Maria Sudal.  In the 2020 documentary section, the first prize was awarded to David France ’ s “Welcome to Chechnya ”, while the second prize was awarded to Susan Regina Moyers ’“ Saudi Escape ” and the third to “Little Girl ” by Sebastian Lifshitz of France.  In the jury section of the World Church, the international competition section award was given to “The Devil Does Not Exist ” by Mohammad Rasoulof and won the Panorama section“ Father ” by Serdan Golabovich from Serbia.  The film "Saudi Escape" by Swiss director Suzanne Regina Moyers was also praised.  Other winners this year: Children's Generation Awards (Kopelos) - Children's Bear Children's Jury Best Feature Film: Alexander Rockwell 's Something Sweet Special Commendation: John Sheedy' s Crystal Bear Best Short Film: Martina Matzkin 's Name Special Commendation: Amira Jahan' s Name Generation Children (Kopelos) - International Jury Awards - International Jury Awards Best Feature Film: “The Wolves ” directed by Samuel Kishi Leopo from Mexico Special Commendation:“ The Funny Ones ” directed by Mimona Dukura from France Special Commendation: “Mama Mama ” directed by Sol Berretto Picchon-Riviere from Argentina Best Short Film:“ In the Name of the Son ” directed by Martina Matzkin from Argentina Special Commendation: “Generation of Kites ” directed by Seyyed Hosseini in Iran The winner was Caro Alves de Souza of Brazil ’ s“ My Name is Baghdad, ” and a special tribute was given to Nebuchadnezzar Sova ’ s “A Voice in the Wind. ”  In this category, the award for the best short film went to Hamila Overdiri from Morocco and Mahyar Mandegar ’ s “Winged White Horse ” from Iran.  The closing ceremony of the 70th Berlin Film Festival began tonight at 17: 30 and the awards ceremony began at 19: 00 Berlin time.

Iranian cinema had four official representatives at the event, but the new film, Mohammad Rasoulof, which was produced in Iran without legal process and sent to the festival, was given special attention by the organizers of the event.  The Berlin Film Festival has previously paid more attention to the unofficial representatives of Iranian cinema and even anti-Iranian works.  According to Variety, the winners of the Silver and Gold Bears were announced on Saturday at the closing ceremony of the 70th Berlin Film Festival.  The International Competition Jury Awards were awarded: Golden Bear for Best Picture: Mohammad Rasoulof of The Great Jury Prize Silver Bear: “Never, Rarely, Sometimes, Always ” Eliza Hitman of USA Silver Bear Award Best Director: Hong Sang-soo for“ The Woman Who Escaped ” South Korea Silver Bear Award: Paula Bear Winner for “Ondyne ” Director Christian Petzold of Germany Award for Best Screenplay Winner Silver Bear: Elio Germano for“ Hidden ” Giorgio Dieretti of Italy Award for Best Screenplay Winner Silver Bear: Damiano and Fabio Dinochenzo for “Bad Stories ” Special Prize 70th Berlinale Silver Bear Winner:“ Eliminate Histori ” directed by Benoit Delpin and Gustave Croerne of France and Belgium Best Outstanding Artistic Achievement Silver Bear Winner: Jerogen Yorgis for Filming “Dao.Natasha ” by Ilya Kezhanovsky and Ekaterina Ortel (Germany) Best First Film:“ The Magrha ” by Camilo Risterpo Best Documentary Feature: “Exposure to the Radiation ” Directed by Rieti Pan Award Best Short Film Gold Bear:“ T ” by Keisha Ray Witherspoon Jury Award Winner Silver Bear Award Winner: "Filipino" by Rafael Manuel Uday Short Film Award: "Lucy the Genius" by Adrien Marizou Fipreschi Jury also won the award in the international competition section to "Ondin" directed by Christian Petzold.  The Panorama Award went to Bassam Tariq's "Joker Mongol" and won the award in the Forum section "Twentieth Century" directed by Matthew Rankin.  In the Panorama Audience category, Father, directed by Serdan Golabowicz, was selected as the winner of the Fiction Film Award.  In the same section, the second award was given to “Feel Not Hard ” directed by Faraz Shariat and the third award was given to“ Hope ” directed by Maria Sudal.  In the 2020 documentary section, the first prize was awarded to David France ’ s “Welcome to Chechnya ”, while the second prize was awarded to Susan Regina Moyers ’“ Saudi Escape ” and the third to “Little Girl ” by Sebastian Lifshitz of France.  In the jury section of the World Church, the international competition section award was given to “The Devil Does Not Exist ” by Mohammad Rasoulof and won the Panorama section“ Father ” by Serdan Golabovich from Serbia.  The film "Saudi Escape" by Swiss director Suzanne Regina Moyers was also praised.  Other winners this year: Children's Generation Awards (Kopelos) - Children's Bear Children's Jury Best Feature Film: Alexander Rockwell 's Something Sweet Special Commendation: John Sheedy' s Crystal Bear Best Short Film: Martina Matzkin 's Name Special Commendation: Amira Jahan' s Name Generation Children (Kopelos) - International Jury Awards - International Jury Awards Best Feature Film: “The Wolves ” directed by Samuel Kishi Leopo from Mexico Special Commendation:“ The Funny Ones ” directed by Mimona Dukura from France Special Commendation: “Mama Mama ” directed by Sol Berretto Picchon-Riviere from Argentina Best Short Film:“ In the Name of the Son ” directed by Martina Matzkin from Argentina Special Commendation: “Generation of Kites ” directed by Seyyed Hosseini in Iran The winner was Caro Alves de Souza of Brazil ’ s“ My Name is Baghdad, ” and a special tribute was given to Nebuchadnezzar Sova ’ s “A Voice in the Wind. ”  In this category, the award for the best short film went to Hamila Overdiri from Morocco and Mahyar Mandegar ’ s “Winged White Horse ” from Iran.  The closing ceremony of the 70th Berlin Film Festival began tonight at 17: 30 and the awards ceremony began at 19: 00 Berlin time.

background: I work for The United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR). I have been tasked to find ways to stop refugees from moving from France to England through the English Channel by small unsafe boats.
title: English Channel Refugees Drowning

passages.title: Four refugees, including two children, drowned in the English Channel.
passages.passage: Four asylum-seekers, including two children, drowned in the English Channel (Reuters) Photo source: A rescue operation has been going on for hours by French boats since French authorities announced the deaths of two children and a man and woman who were trying to cross the English Channel to reach Britain.  A boat carrying refugees has sunk across the English Channel between France and Britain.  The prosecutor of the French city of Dunkirk has opened an investigation into the cause of the sinking of the ship.  These people are said to be Iranian.  A massive rescue operation has been under way for hours, which crashed near the northern French city of Dunkirk.  According to French authorities, two children aged 5 and 8 and a man and woman died.  The other 14 were taken to hospitals in the port of Calais and the French city of Dunkirk.  The English Channel, between France and Britain, is one of the world ’ s busiest waterways, and it can be dangerous to cross by small vessels, especially in winter when the sea is stormy.  Another disaster came after the British Meteorological Office warned of bad weather and strong winds in the Channel region.  Natalie Alpeik, MP for the Dover region in the British Parliament, said: “It ’ s terrible that there ’ s been another disaster on the canal.  Human traffickers have no respect for human life: "A sailboat accidentally encountered a ship and alerted French authorities of the incident.  Four French ships, a Belgian helicopter and a French fishing vessel were involved in the rescue.  Since the beginning of the year, more than 7,400 asylum seekers have arrived in Britain by sea in small boats.  While there are still two months left until the end of 2020, that number is 1,825 more than in 2019.  The survivors were taken by helicopter to hospitals in the port of Calais and the northern French city of Dunkirk on Thursday, August 6, and a total of 235 migrants, including several pregnant women, crossed the English Channel from Europe to the southern coast of Britain.  This is the highest recorded number of illegal immigrants arriving in the region in a single day.  About ten days ago, Home Secretary Priti Patel announced the “most significant revision ” of the country ’ s asylum system in a decade.

passages.title: The UK is concerned about the increase in attempts to illegally cross the English Channel
passages.passage: The UK government intends to find the reasons for the sharp increase in attempts of migrants to cross the English Channel by boat from France to the UK.  Lodon intends to strengthen cooperation with France and the French coastal patrol services in order to make the illegal crossing of the English Channel “impossible ”.  Home Secretary Preeti Patel appointed on Sunday a special commissioner for countering attempts to illegally cross the English Channel, former naval officer Dan O'Maconey.  Dan O ’ Maconey will “work closely with the French ” and bear“ primary responsibility for the impassability of the strait for small ships, ” the Home Office said.  According to the BBC, about 300 boats have crossed the English Channel since the beginning of the year, and about four thousand migrants have landed on the English coast.  Recently, due to favorable weather conditions, the number of attempts to cross the border between France and the UK has increased significantly, AFP notes.  More than 500 migrants have crossed the English Channel from the French to the English coast in just the last three days.  France, for its part, says that from January to July 2020, the number of prevented English Channel crossings increased more than fivefold compared to the same period in 2019, and four times more boats and equipment were found in the dunes than last year.  Last month, a "Franco-British intelligence unit" was set up to deal with people smuggling migrants, the French Interior Ministry said.  Sunday ’ s Sunday Telegraph published an article in which it writes that France demanded from the UK the sum of 30 million pounds (33.2 million euros) to organize control all along the coast of the Channel.  The Sunday Telegraph, citing a source in the British Foreign Ministry, claims that the final decision by the British government has not yet been made.  The French Foreign Ministry has not yet commented on this information, saying only that “next week France and the UK will discuss the issue of strengthening the bilateral struggle against the illegal crossing of the English Channel. ”  British Immigration Minister Chris Philip is expected to visit France on Tuesday. passages.title: A repeat of the nightmare of 2015. Europe is facing a new migration crisis
passages.passage: https: / / ria.ru / 20210525 / migratsiya-1733716124.html A repeat of the nightmare of 2015.  Europe is facing a new migration crisis, a repeat of the nightmare of 2015.  Europe is waiting for a new migration crisis - RIA Novosti, 25.05.2021 A repeat of the nightmare of 2015.  Europe is once again on the brink of a migration crisis.  And this is not yet the summer, which traditionally accounts for the peak of the wave of illegal migration from countries...  RIA Novosti, 25.05.2021 2021-05-25T08: 00 2021-05-25T08: 00 2021-05-25T08: 02 migrants refugees europe authors / html / head / meta [@ name = 'og: title'] / @ content / html / head / meta [@ name = 'og: description'] / @ content https: / / cdn.com 24.img.ria.ru / images / 07e5 / 05 / 18 / 1733713287 _ 0: 153: 1920: 1233 _ 1920x0 _ 80 _ 0 _ 85ca65dc729db44d8073637ad5013c74.jpg Europe is again on the verge of a migration crisis.  And this is not yet the summer, which traditionally accounts for the peak of the wave of illegal migration from Asia and Africa.Now in the center of attention is Ceuta, a Spanish enclave in North Africa, where thousands of illegal refugees from Morocco rushed.  The refugee crisis in Ceuta and Melilla (another Spanish port in Africa) is largely the result of the artificial escalation of relations between Spain and Morocco.  According to many observers, Rabat decided to take revenge on Madrid for the assistance recently provided to the Polisario Front (which for many years has been fighting for the independence of Western Sahara from Morocco).  The revenge was the actual inaction of the border guards of this country, who turned a blind eye to the crowds of migrants breaking into Ceuta.  According to The Economist magazine, in this way King Mohammed VI of Morocco “made migration a weapon ” .But in fact, the sharp influx of refugees from Africa began not only in the Spanish enclaves.  Again, a series of flimsy ships illegally transporting Africans (mainly Libyans) from Tunisia to the Italian island of Lampedusa.  Last week, 1,200 people were transferred there during 12 hours of good weather alone.  And even despite the weather, accidents were recorded: 73 refugees from Bangladesh almost drowned trying to reach the cherished island.  How long it took, no one can say.  According to the Italian Interior Ministry, 4,290 migrants reached the country ’ s shores in the first three weeks of May.  While for the whole of May last year, their number was 1654 people.  The flow of illegal refugees is also increasing between the EU and Britain.  Since January, more than three thousand people have crossed the English Channel.  And over the same period last year, this figure was 1,400 refugees – more than double the growth.  Just the other day, the Belgian coast guard rescued a sinking ship on which 49 migrants, mostly Vietnamese, tried to cross the strait.  Based on the above facts and statistics, we can safely assume that the migration crisis will return to the European agenda in the foreseeable future.  However, the numbers are not as catastrophic as they were in 2015, when Europe was literally drowned by a flood of refugees.  And the increase compared to last year is easily explained by the fact that in 2020, many people in Asia and Africa gave up their intentions to go to pandemics in Europe.  In addition, the result of the shift of public attention from the problem of migration to the fight against the covid was a noticeable decrease in the ratings of a number of parties advocating strict measures to limit the influx of immigrants (in the Western media, these political organizations are usually indiscriminately called ultra-right, even despite the rather liberal economic program of many of them).  It is quite logical that now, with the rapid return of migration problems to the agenda, many publications have sounded the alarm in connection with the imminent growth of the popularity of these political forces.  Almost all analysts agree that the crisis around Ceuta, which has not descended from the front pages of the Spanish press for several days, will significantly strengthen the anti-Islamic party Vox (Voice).  Even before the current crisis, it actively dispersed the fears of the enclave residents in connection with the influx of poor Africans.  And in the end, it won the first place in the parliamentary elections of 2019, receiving more than 35 percent of the vote – and this is in a city where 40 percent of the population is Muslim.  It would be strange if the Vox party did not now take advantage of the crisis to increase its popularity in Ceuta.  For example, a local cell of the party is publicizing protests against the fact that African migrants entering the Spanish enclave receive coronavirus vaccinations, while Spanish citizens living there wait months for their turn.  This is confirmed by events in the regional parliament of Andalusia, where after the 2018 elections, for the first time in history, the People ’ s Party took the first place and was able to form a minority government.  Until last week, it relied solely on the informal support of Vox MPs.  However, on Thursday, they announced the termination of cooperation with the senior partner in connection with the fact that the authorities of the region agreed to accept 13 minor refugees who infiltrated Ceuta.  This could lead to the fall of the regional government and early elections.  That is why the People ’ s Party is forced to show more and more rigidity in the migration issue, causing panic in the European liberal media.Even more worrying in the mainstream is the electoral situation in Italy.  After the 2015 crisis, the League party, led by Matteo Salvini, has been the consistent leader of the polls there.  Having proved himself a tough fighter against illegal migration as the Minister of Internal Affairs, he increased the leadership of his party to record levels.  At the peak of popularity in the summer of 2019, the League ’ s figures were approaching 40 percent, which gave it hope even for the formation of its government.  Based on these calculations, Salvini provoked a government crisis in order to hold early elections, but was outplayed by opponents.  Since last year, there has been a drop in the ratings of this political force, whose supporters cannot forgive the support it expressed for the technocratic government of Mario Draghi.  Liberals can breathe freely.  But the fact is that the ratings of the League, which is still in the first place in the polls, are moving on opposite courses with the rapidly growing indicators of the even more right-wing and even more anti-migrant party “Brothers of Italy ”.  According to some polls, she already came in second place after the League, behind that couple of percent.  Three years ago, its ratings fluctuated around three to four percent, and now confidently approaching 20.  If elections were held now, these two forces, with the support of Silvio Berlusconi ’ s Forward Italy party, could well form a majority government.  They do not hide their ideological continuity from the far-right Italian social movement, which was created in 1946 by former supporters of Benito Mussolini.  This legacy is clearly indicated by the logo of the party, which includes the former symbol of ISD.The growth of the popularity of the "Brothers" will contribute to the charisma of the head of the party Georgia Meloni ("Sisters of Italy", as it was nicknamed by the press) - she last year surpassed in the approval ratings of the leader of the "League", becoming the second most popular politician in the country after the current prime minister.  There is no doubt that in the event of an aggravation of the migration crisis, the League and Brothers will be able to get additional votes to their already serious ratings.  Trends in the first months of the year show that the threat of the covid is no longer deterring refugees seeking to Europe.  And this means that the nightmare of 2015 may repeat itself — and the popularity of far-right, anti-migrant, anti-Islamic, Eurosceptic parties will again sharply rise.
