passages.title: Drowned refugees in the Channel are Iranians.
passages.passage: A woman and a man who died with their three children while trying to reach Britain are from the village of Glynne.  The website also published the names and photos of the deceased.  French authorities on Tuesday confirmed the capsizing of a small boat carrying asylum seekers and the death of four people on board in the English Channel.  The third child of the Kurdish family is missing.  A total of 27 people were on the way.  A number of survivors are being treated in the hospital.  The rescue operation involved several coast guard boats and a Belgian army helicopter.  British Prime Minister Boris Johnson offered his condolences to the survivors.  British Home Secretary Priti Patel expressed sympathy for the victims and said she was very sorry to hear the news.  Patel said the incident once again highlighted the dangers of crossing the canal.  He promised to do everything in his power to stop traffickers from exploiting refugees in need.  The English Channel (English Channel) is a canal in northern France and southern Britain that connects the Atlantic Ocean to the North Sea.  According to data from PA Media, more than 7,400 people reached the UK via the English Channel in small boats this year, nearly four times more than in 2019.  This year ’ s “record ” was set with the arrival of 416 refugees on September 2.  Official statistics show that from June 2019 to June 2020, more than 3,400 people who applied for asylum are under the age of 17.  Of these, nearly 2,800 were unaccompanied children.  The British government can return refugees arriving from France under the Dublin Accords.  According to the treaty, asylum seekers who have entered Europe are only allowed to apply for asylum at their place of entry on European soil.

passages.title: Thousands of refugees and asylum seekers are dying on their way to Europe.
passages.passage: The views are more of a point of the Mediterranean Sea.  Refugees from eastern Libya are trying to reach Europe.  Now, a report released by the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees speaks of the dangers elsewhere on the refugee route.  On Wednesday, July 29, Agence France-Presse published an article from Berlin on the new report of the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR).  According to the report, thousands of refugees die each year on their way from Africa to Europe.  The report said at least 1,750 people were killed on roads between African countries in the two years of 2018 and 2019 alone.  On the Mediterranean Sea route to Europe, an average of 72 refugees die each month.  This makes it “the deadliest refugee and refugee route in the world. ”  The report said there are many dangers lurking in the lives of refugees on other routes to the Mediterranean Sea.  For example, many refugees and war refugees die on their way from West to East Africa.  The UNHCR report goes on to point out that it is not possible to collect accurate statistics of victims in the mentioned routes.  These areas are occupied by human traffickers, making it impossible to obtain accurate statistics.  The rape and torture report of the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) is based on data from the Danish Refugee Council.  The Danish Refugee Council has launched an organisation called the Mixed-Migrations Centre (MMC).  According to the agency, 28% of the victims and deaths recorded in 2018 and 2019 were due to their passage through the Sahara Desert.  Many more refugees are losing their lives in southern Libya.  In addition, a number of refugees also die on their way from the Central African Republic and Mali to Libya.  Refugees who manage to cross these dangerous routes suffer from severe mental distress.  They have reported abuse, torture and rape in border areas and even in eastern Libya.  Hot oil and melted plastic are said to have been used to torture refugees.  Many refugees have also been sexually assaulted and raped.  The report said abuse and rape were not limited to human traffickers, and in many cases soldiers were involved in such violent behavior.  Join Deutsche Welle ’ s Instagram channel Filippo Grandi, the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees, said that for a long time this horrific abuse of refugees and asylum seekers has been ignored by international authorities.  He called for swift and decisive action by the international community to defend the lives of refugees.  Grandi has reiterated that Libya is not a safe country for refugees.  It should be noted that Libya has been witnessing a civil war since 2011.  Many parts of the country have fallen into chaos as a result of this war.

passages.title: Europe speaking. How dangerous is the new migration crisis?
passages.passage: The aggravation of the situation in the Middle East, caused by the murder of Iranian General Qassem Soleimani, forced the European Union to again talk about the possible admission of refugees.  Europe is still dealing with the migration crisis of 2015, even if it is not written daily in the media.  DELFI presents a short guide on how the situation with refugees is and whether the European Union is ready for a new wave of migrants.  What are we talking about?  Between 2015 and 2018, the number of migrants arriving in Europe fell sharply, from 1.8 million to 140,000.  Some European politicians hastened to call what was happening a “success story ”, attributing the decline in refugee activity to the migration agreements that Brussels had concluded with Turkey and North African countries.  However, as noted by public organizations, in reality, the migration crisis has not gone away – just the countries of Western Europe have noticeably tightened their “hospitality policy ”, which forces refugees to use more risky routes and means to move to Europe.  According to the EU delegation on border control in Libya, the death rate among migrants has increased significantly in recent years: if in 2017 there was one death for every 38 arrivals, in 2018 - one for every 14, and in the first quarter of 2019 - one for every three people who reached Europe alive.  A similar trend can be observed on the route between Spain and Morocco.  The UN refugee agency has estimated that in 2018, 138 thousand people arrived by sea to the shores of Italy, Greece, Spain, Cyprus and Malta, and more than 2,000 people drowned.  40% of those who arrived last year were women and children.  Most refugees are housed in temporary camps in the countries where their boats arrive.  Some try to later move to more prosperous Western countries (Germany, France, Belgium).  According to the European Commission, 580,000 people applied for asylum in the European Union in 2018.  Mostly they are citizens of Afghanistan, Iraq, Pakistan, Iran and Nigeria.  In 2018, compared with the previous year, the influx of refugees from Venezuela, Georgia, Turkey, Iran and Colombia increased.  Four out of five asylum seekers are under the age of 35, and one in three is a minor.  What does that mean?  For five years of the migration crisis, the European Union has not been able to agree on common rules for the reception and accommodation of refugees.  The countries of Eastern Europe and the Baltic States "wrapped up" the idea of quotas for the distribution of refugees (Poland, Hungary, the Czech Republic, Slovakia almost completely refused to accept migrants), the countries of Western Europe, in turn, under pressure from the public began to tighten the conditions for granting refugee status.  In 2018, 200,000 positive responses were received for 580,000 asylum applications.  At the same time, the number of migrants returned to their homeland has increased significantly.  For example, Germany last year deported 17,000 illegal immigrants, Greece in the fall announced plans to expel 10,000 people from the country.  The new president of the European Commission, Ursula von der Leyen, made it clear that the new asylum system in the EU “must include the search for new forms of solidarity and ensure that all member states make a meaningful contribution to supporting countries under the greatest pressure. ”  At the same time, it advocates strengthening humanitarian cooperation with third countries, that is, a policy of containing refugees in territories outside the European Union.  The most famous in this area is the agreement with Turkey: on May 20, 2016, a two-year agreement came into force, according to which Turkey had to close the way to the EU for refugees.  The agreement drew a barrage of criticism from human rights organizations (refugees are held in poor conditions, children are forced to work, there are reports that Turkish soldiers even shoot refugees at the border), and, according to many experts, failed to perform basic tasks.  Nevertheless, Brussels is ready to conclude a new deal with Ankara.  According to representatives of Croatia – this country took over the presidency of the EU Council from January 1, 2020 – this issue is on the list of priorities.  What do I care about that?  Despite the horror stories of nationalist politicians, the European migration crisis of 2015 practically did not affect Latvia.  According to the Foundation for Social Integration, over the past four years, more than 900 people have received asylum in our country, but two-thirds have already gone abroad.  Probably went to Germany.  The main reasons for leaving are low benefits, a cold climate, difficulties in finding a job, inflexible language policy, etc.  Latvia, like other countries in Eastern Europe, opposes mandatory quotas for the accommodation of refugees.  In 2015, at the height of the migration crisis, Latvia agreed to host 531 refugees from camps in Greece, Italy and Turkey in solidarity with other countries.  However, in the two years allotted for the fulfillment of the promise, only 346 people arrived in our country, most of whom left Latvia after that.  The aggravation of the crisis in the Middle East may require some new symbolic actions from the Latvian authorities, for example, to allow those people who are just waiting to receive refugee status to work.  It will be a great challenge if Latvia is flooded with refugees from Ukraine and other countries of the former Soviet Union.  But for now – due to the low standard of living and not the most attractive social security system – this is rather a hypothetical scenario.

passages.title: Joint Water Patrol with France: Six More Iranian Refugees Off British Coast
passages.passage: Photo copyright PA Image caption UK water patrols have taken many refugees from the water in recent days amid increasing numbers of migrants trying to reach Britain by water, and the country has agreed with France to further protect the border between the two countries.  A large number of these refugees are Iranian.  Sajid Javid, the British Home Secretary, returned to London in the middle of a family holiday and planned a joint Blue Patrol force with his French counterpart.  It was reported that on Sunday, at the same time as the minister ’ s efforts, six other Iranian men reached the beach near Dover.  The French say they stopped the influx of more refugees on Saturday.  Mr Javid has been accused by his rival party and even his own party of failing to act properly and should have dealt with the matter more harshly.  Javid eventually reached an agreement with French Interior Minister Christophe Castaner to become more active in the coming weeks.  LEWIS MORRIS Image caption Six Iranian men were taken from the water on Sunday The group was found in a boat where the two ministers agreed to deal with human traffickers, and another part involved informing refugees about the dangers of crossing the Channel in small boats.  The British Interior Ministry has given no further explanation in this regard.  More than 220 people have tried to reach the UK by boat in the past two months.  In addition to the Iranians, citizens of Afghanistan and Syria are also among the refugees.  Britain has five lifeboats, only one currently operating.  The other four are in the Mediterranean Sea and are helping with rescue operations there.  It is not known whether the other four boats will return to Britain.  Since 2017, about 2,200 people have taken refuge in the UK every month.  The increase in the number of Iranian refugees, according to the Financial Times, is the result of the worsening economic situation in the country.

passages.title: 39 'Iranian' refugees detained on Britain's southeast coast
passages.passage: Sean Gallup / Getty Images Image caption One of the boats normally used by asylum seekers to cross the Channel to the UK, four boats carrying 39 Iranian refugees were taken off Sunday, November 17, at separate events off Britain's southeast coast.  The British Interior Ministry confirmed that all of the asylum seekers identified themselves as “Iranian ”.  The first boat, which had nine people on board, took off at 4: 40 a.m. yesterday, while the second, with five people on board, reached the British coast at around 6 a.m.  According to the Coast Guard and Kent County Police, a boat with 11 people on board was seized at around 7 a.m. and a half hour later another boat with 14 people was taken off the coast of the UK.  As soon as they received a message of help from the boats, rescue helicopters, as well as rescue boats from the ports of Dover, Dunness and Hastings, as well as two coast guard vessels, took action to rescue the passengers.  A Home Office spokesman said: "Crossing the canal by these small boats is extremely dangerous.  For those who have gone through such a journey, their lives and their loved ones are at risk. ”  According to the British Home Office, over the past two years Iranian citizens have applied for asylum more than any other country in the UK.  In 2017, about 9% of all 26,350 asylum applications were submitted by Iranians.  In November last year there was a significant increase in the number of asylum seekers trying to cross the English Channel to Britain, with the Home Secretary calling the issue a "serious incident" and calling for the French government to work together to resolve the issue.  Due to the increasing number of migrants and asylum seekers arriving on the east coast of the UK via the sea and the English Channel, the British Coast Guard has announced an increase in staff.

passages.title: UN: EU to Blame for Deaths of Migrants in Mediterranean Sea
passages.passage: The United Nations has been implicated in the deaths of migrants in the Mediterranean because of its refusal to respond to calls for emergency relief, its refusal to meet humanitarian rescue efforts and its push to return them to Libya.  In its 37-page report, the UN said the number of migrant deaths this year on the sea route had so far reached 632.  The United Nations has described the incident as a “large-scale humanitarian tragedy. ”  Thousands of migrants and refugees, including from African countries, make long and risky voyages through Libya each year in hopes of getting to Europe and living a better life.  They often use small, inflatable boats to cross this dangerous path.  The report concluded that the lack of protection for migrants “is not a sad anomaly, but rather a consequence of the policies, decisions and actions of Libyan authorities, EU members, institutions and other actors.  The European Union has not only reduced the search and rescue operations of migrants in Mediterranean waters, but its governments have each hindered the rescue operations of humanitarian organizations with their own administrative and criminal proceedings.  Migrants told the UN Human Rights Office there were also efforts to "repatriate migrants at sea", which would return ships carrying migrants from international waters to Libya with the help of European helicopters.  The report is based on interviews with 80 migrants between January 2019 and December 2020.  According to them, some have faced interception operations by Libyan officials and their lives are in danger.  Some boats have been shot down, causing boats to capsize or forcing migrants to jump into the sea.  Most of the migrants returned to Libya face exploitation and ill-treatment.  Commenting on the report, UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Michelle Bachelet called for urgent reforms in the search and rescue policies and actions taken by Libya, the European Union and its member states to ensure that such policies and measures are complied with international law.  The real tragedy is that it is preventable to prevent the suffering and deaths of migrants on the current Mediterranean route.  The United Nations has called on European countries to use more effective and efficient mechanisms to address the wave of migrants and refugees.  The Guardian previously revealed that European countries used brutal methods to stop the passage of almost 40,000 refugees during the coronavirus epidemic, resulting in 2,000 deaths.

Title: Four refugees, including two children, drowned in the English Channel.
Content: Four asylum-seekers, including two children, drowned in the English Channel (Reuters) Photo source: A rescue operation has been going on for hours by French boats since French authorities announced the deaths of two children and a man and woman who were trying to cross the English Channel to reach Britain.  A boat carrying refugees has sunk across the English Channel between France and Britain.  The prosecutor of the French city of Dunkirk has opened an investigation into the cause of the sinking of the ship.  These people are said to be Iranian.  A massive rescue operation has been under way for hours, which crashed near the northern French city of Dunkirk.  According to French authorities, two children aged 5 and 8 and a man and woman died.  The other 14 were taken to hospitals in the port of Calais and the French city of Dunkirk.  The English Channel, between France and Britain, is one of the world ’ s busiest waterways, and it can be dangerous to cross by small vessels, especially in winter when the sea is stormy.  Another disaster came after the British Meteorological Office warned of bad weather and strong winds in the Channel region.  Natalie Alpeik, MP for the Dover region in the British Parliament, said: “It ’ s terrible that there ’ s been another disaster on the canal.  Human traffickers have no respect for human life: "A sailboat accidentally encountered a ship and alerted French authorities of the incident.  Four French ships, a Belgian helicopter and a French fishing vessel were involved in the rescue.  Since the beginning of the year, more than 7,400 asylum seekers have arrived in Britain by sea in small boats.  While there are still two months left until the end of 2020, that number is 1,825 more than in 2019.  The survivors were taken by helicopter to hospitals in the port of Calais and the northern French city of Dunkirk on Thursday, August 6, and a total of 235 migrants, including several pregnant women, crossed the English Channel from Europe to the southern coast of Britain.  This is the highest recorded number of illegal immigrants arriving in the region in a single day.  About ten days ago, Home Secretary Priti Patel announced the “most significant revision ” of the country ’ s asylum system in a decade.

Title: The UK is concerned about the increase in attempts to illegally cross the English Channel
Content: The UK government intends to find the reasons for the sharp increase in attempts of migrants to cross the English Channel by boat from France to the UK.  Lodon intends to strengthen cooperation with France and the French coastal patrol services in order to make the illegal crossing of the English Channel “impossible ”.  Home Secretary Preeti Patel appointed on Sunday a special commissioner for countering attempts to illegally cross the English Channel, former naval officer Dan O'Maconey.  Dan O ’ Maconey will “work closely with the French ” and bear“ primary responsibility for the impassability of the strait for small ships, ” the Home Office said.  According to the BBC, about 300 boats have crossed the English Channel since the beginning of the year, and about four thousand migrants have landed on the English coast.  Recently, due to favorable weather conditions, the number of attempts to cross the border between France and the UK has increased significantly, AFP notes.  More than 500 migrants have crossed the English Channel from the French to the English coast in just the last three days.  France, for its part, says that from January to July 2020, the number of prevented English Channel crossings increased more than fivefold compared to the same period in 2019, and four times more boats and equipment were found in the dunes than last year.  Last month, a "Franco-British intelligence unit" was set up to deal with people smuggling migrants, the French Interior Ministry said.  Sunday ’ s Sunday Telegraph published an article in which it writes that France demanded from the UK the sum of 30 million pounds (33.2 million euros) to organize control all along the coast of the Channel.  The Sunday Telegraph, citing a source in the British Foreign Ministry, claims that the final decision by the British government has not yet been made.  The French Foreign Ministry has not yet commented on this information, saying only that “next week France and the UK will discuss the issue of strengthening the bilateral struggle against the illegal crossing of the English Channel. ”  British Immigration Minister Chris Philip is expected to visit France on Tuesday. Europe is waiting for a new migration crisis - RIA Novosti, 25.05.2021 A repeat of the nightmare of 2015.  Europe is once again on the brink of a migration crisis. RIA Novosti, 25.05.2021 2021-05-25T08: 00 2021-05-25T08: 00 2021-05-25T08: 02 migrants refugees europe authors / html / head / meta [@ name = 'og: title'] / @ content / html / head / meta [@ name = 'og: description'] / @ content https: / / cdn.com 24.img.ria.ru / images / 07e5 / 05 / 18 / 1733713287 _ 0: 153: 1920: 1233 _ 1920x0 _ 80 _ 0 _ 85ca65dc729db44d8073637ad5013c74.jpg Europe is again on the verge of a migration crisis.  And this is not yet the summer, which traditionally accounts for the peak of the wave of illegal migration from Asia and Africa.Now in the center of attention is Ceuta, a Spanish enclave in North Africa, where thousands of illegal refugees from Morocco rushed.  The refugee crisis in Ceuta and Melilla (another Spanish port in Africa) is largely the result of the artificial escalation of relations between Spain and Morocco.  According to many observers, Rabat decided to take revenge on Madrid for the assistance recently provided to the Polisario Front (which for many years has been fighting for the independence of Western Sahara from Morocco).  The revenge was the actual inaction of the border guards of this country, who turned a blind eye to the crowds of migrants breaking into Ceuta.  According to The Economist magazine, in this way King Mohammed VI of Morocco “made migration a weapon ” .But in fact, the sharp influx of refugees from Africa began not only in the Spanish enclaves.  Again, a series of flimsy ships illegally transporting Africans (mainly Libyans) from Tunisia to the Italian island of Lampedusa.  Last week, 1,200 people were transferred there during 12 hours of good weather alone.  And even despite the weather, accidents were recorded: 73 refugees from Bangladesh almost drowned trying to reach the cherished island.  How long it took, no one can say.  According to the Italian Interior Ministry, 4,290 migrants reached the country ’ s shores in the first three weeks of May.  While for the whole of May last year, their number was 1654 people.  The flow of illegal refugees is also increasing between the EU and Britain.  Since January, more than three thousand people have crossed the English Channel.  And over the same period last year, this figure was 1,400 refugees – more than double the growth.  Just the other day, the Belgian coast guard rescued a sinking ship on which 49 migrants, mostly Vietnamese, tried to cross the strait.  Based on the above facts and statistics, we can safely assume that the migration crisis will return to the European agenda in the foreseeable future.  However, the numbers are not as catastrophic as they were in 2015, when Europe was literally drowned by a flood of refugees.  And the increase compared to last year is easily explained by the fact that in 2020, many people in Asia and Africa gave up their intentions to go to pandemics in Europe.  In addition, the result of the shift of public attention from the problem of migration to the fight against the covid was a noticeable decrease in the ratings of a number of parties advocating strict measures to limit the influx of immigrants (in the Western media, these political organizations are usually indiscriminately called ultra-right, even despite the rather liberal economic program of many of them).  It is quite logical that now, with the rapid return of migration problems to the agenda, many publications have sounded the alarm in connection with the imminent growth of the popularity of these political forces.  Almost all analysts agree that the crisis around Ceuta, which has not descended from the front pages of the Spanish press for several days, will significantly strengthen the anti-Islamic party Vox (Voice).  Even before the current crisis, it actively dispersed the fears of the enclave residents in connection with the influx of poor Africans.  And in the end, it won the first place in the parliamentary elections of 2019, receiving more than 35 percent of the vote – and this is in a city where 40 percent of the population is Muslim.  It would be strange if the Vox party did not now take advantage of the crisis to increase its popularity in Ceuta.  For example, a local cell of the party is publicizing protests against the fact that African migrants entering the Spanish enclave receive coronavirus vaccinations, while Spanish citizens living there wait months for their turn.  This is confirmed by events in the regional parliament of Andalusia, where after the 2018 elections, for the first time in history, the People ’ s Party took the first place and was able to form a minority government.  Until last week, it relied solely on the informal support of Vox MPs.  However, on Thursday, they announced the termination of cooperation with the senior partner in connection with the fact that the authorities of the region agreed to accept 13 minor refugees who infiltrated Ceuta.  This could lead to the fall of the regional government and early elections.  That is why the People ’ s Party is forced to show more and more rigidity in the migration issue, causing panic in the European liberal media.Even more worrying in the mainstream is the electoral situation in Italy.  After the 2015 crisis, the League party, led by Matteo Salvini, has been the consistent leader of the polls there.  Having proved himself a tough fighter against illegal migration as the Minister of Internal Affairs, he increased the leadership of his party to record levels.  At the peak of popularity in the summer of 2019, the League ’ s figures were approaching 40 percent, which gave it hope even for the formation of its government.  Based on these calculations, Salvini provoked a government crisis in order to hold early elections, but was outplayed by opponents.  Since last year, there has been a drop in the ratings of this political force, whose supporters cannot forgive the support it expressed for the technocratic government of Mario Draghi.  Liberals can breathe freely.  But the fact is that the ratings of the League, which is still in the first place in the polls, are moving on opposite courses with the rapidly growing indicators of the even more right-wing and even more anti-migrant party “Brothers of Italy ”.  According to some polls, she already came in second place after the League, behind that couple of percent.  Three years ago, its ratings fluctuated around three to four percent, and now confidently approaching 20.  If elections were held now, these two forces, with the support of Silvio Berlusconi ’ s Forward Italy party, could well form a majority government.  They do not hide their ideological continuity from the far-right Italian social movement, which was created in 1946 by former supporters of Benito Mussolini.  This legacy is clearly indicated by the logo of the party, which includes the former symbol of ISD.The growth of the popularity of the "Brothers" will contribute to the charisma of the head of the party Georgia Meloni ("Sisters of Italy", as it was nicknamed by the press) - she last year surpassed in the approval ratings of the leader of the "League", becoming the second most popular politician in the country after the current prime minister.  There is no doubt that in the event of an aggravation of the migration crisis, the League and Brothers will be able to get additional votes to their already serious ratings.  Trends in the first months of the year show that the threat of the covid is no longer deterring refugees seeking to Europe.  And this means that the nightmare of 2015 may repeat itself — and the popularity of far-right, anti-migrant, anti-Islamic, Eurosceptic parties will again sharply rise. Title: Thousands of refugees and asylum seekers are dying on their way to Europe.
Content: The views are more of a point of the Mediterranean Sea.  Refugees from eastern Libya are trying to reach Europe.  Now, a report released by the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees speaks of the dangers elsewhere on the refugee route.  On Wednesday, July 29, Agence France-Presse published an article from Berlin on the new report of the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR).  According to the report, thousands of refugees die each year on their way from Africa to Europe.  The report said at least 1,750 people were killed on roads between African countries in the two years of 2018 and 2019 alone.  On the Mediterranean Sea route to Europe, an average of 72 refugees die each month.  This makes it “the deadliest refugee and refugee route in the world. ”  The report said there are many dangers lurking in the lives of refugees on other routes to the Mediterranean Sea.  For example, many refugees and war refugees die on their way from West to East Africa.  The UNHCR report goes on to point out that it is not possible to collect accurate statistics of victims in the mentioned routes.  These areas are occupied by human traffickers, making it impossible to obtain accurate statistics.  The rape and torture report of the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) is based on data from the Danish Refugee Council.  The Danish Refugee Council has launched an organisation called the Mixed-Migrations Centre (MMC).  According to the agency, 28% of the victims and deaths recorded in 2018 and 2019 were due to their passage through the Sahara Desert.  Many more refugees are losing their lives in southern Libya.  In addition, a number of refugees also die on their way from the Central African Republic and Mali to Libya.  Refugees who manage to cross these dangerous routes suffer from severe mental distress.  They have reported abuse, torture and rape in border areas and even in eastern Libya.  Hot oil and melted plastic are said to have been used to torture refugees.  Many refugees have also been sexually assaulted and raped.  The report said abuse and rape were not limited to human traffickers, and in many cases soldiers were involved in such violent behavior.  Join Deutsche Welle ’ s Instagram channel Filippo Grandi, the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees, said that for a long time this horrific abuse of refugees and asylum seekers has been ignored by international authorities.  He called for swift and decisive action by the international community to defend the lives of refugees.  Grandi has reiterated that Libya is not a safe country for refugees.  It should be noted that Libya has been witnessing a civil war since 2011.  Many parts of the country have fallen into chaos as a result of this war.

Title: Europe speaking. How dangerous is the new migration crisis?
Content: The aggravation of the situation in the Middle East, caused by the murder of Iranian General Qassem Soleimani, forced the European Union to again talk about the possible admission of refugees.  Europe is still dealing with the migration crisis of 2015, even if it is not written daily in the media.  DELFI presents a short guide on how the situation with refugees is and whether the European Union is ready for a new wave of migrants.  What are we talking about?  Between 2015 and 2018, the number of migrants arriving in Europe fell sharply, from 1.8 million to 140,000.  Some European politicians hastened to call what was happening a “success story ”, attributing the decline in refugee activity to the migration agreements that Brussels had concluded with Turkey and North African countries.  However, as noted by public organizations, in reality, the migration crisis has not gone away – just the countries of Western Europe have noticeably tightened their “hospitality policy ”, which forces refugees to use more risky routes and means to move to Europe.  According to the EU delegation on border control in Libya, the death rate among migrants has increased significantly in recent years: if in 2017 there was one death for every 38 arrivals, in 2018 - one for every 14, and in the first quarter of 2019 - one for every three people who reached Europe alive.  A similar trend can be observed on the route between Spain and Morocco.  The UN refugee agency has estimated that in 2018, 138 thousand people arrived by sea to the shores of Italy, Greece, Spain, Cyprus and Malta, and more than 2,000 people drowned.  40% of those who arrived last year were women and children.  Most refugees are housed in temporary camps in the countries where their boats arrive.  Some try to later move to more prosperous Western countries (Germany, France, Belgium).  According to the European Commission, 580,000 people applied for asylum in the European Union in 2018.  Mostly they are citizens of Afghanistan, Iraq, Pakistan, Iran and Nigeria.  In 2018, compared with the previous year, the influx of refugees from Venezuela, Georgia, Turkey, Iran and Colombia increased.  Four out of five asylum seekers are under the age of 35, and one in three is a minor.  What does that mean?  For five years of the migration crisis, the European Union has not been able to agree on common rules for the reception and accommodation of refugees.  The countries of Eastern Europe and the Baltic States "wrapped up" the idea of quotas for the distribution of refugees (Poland, Hungary, the Czech Republic, Slovakia almost completely refused to accept migrants), the countries of Western Europe, in turn, under pressure from the public began to tighten the conditions for granting refugee status.  In 2018, 200,000 positive responses were received for 580,000 asylum applications.  At the same time, the number of migrants returned to their homeland has increased significantly.  For example, Germany last year deported 17,000 illegal immigrants, Greece in the fall announced plans to expel 10,000 people from the country.  The new president of the European Commission, Ursula von der Leyen, made it clear that the new asylum system in the EU “must include the search for new forms of solidarity and ensure that all member states make a meaningful contribution to supporting countries under the greatest pressure. ”  At the same time, it advocates strengthening humanitarian cooperation with third countries, that is, a policy of containing refugees in territories outside the European Union.  The most famous in this area is the agreement with Turkey: on May 20, 2016, a two-year agreement came into force, according to which Turkey had to close the way to the EU for refugees.  The agreement drew a barrage of criticism from human rights organizations (refugees are held in poor conditions, children are forced to work, there are reports that Turkish soldiers even shoot refugees at the border), and, according to many experts, failed to perform basic tasks.  Nevertheless, Brussels is ready to conclude a new deal with Ankara.  According to representatives of Croatia – this country took over the presidency of the EU Council from January 1, 2020 – this issue is on the list of priorities.  What do I care about that?  Despite the horror stories of nationalist politicians, the European migration crisis of 2015 practically did not affect Latvia.  According to the Foundation for Social Integration, over the past four years, more than 900 people have received asylum in our country, but two-thirds have already gone abroad.  Probably went to Germany.  The main reasons for leaving are low benefits, a cold climate, difficulties in finding a job, inflexible language policy, etc.  Latvia, like other countries in Eastern Europe, opposes mandatory quotas for the accommodation of refugees.  In 2015, at the height of the migration crisis, Latvia agreed to host 531 refugees from camps in Greece, Italy and Turkey in solidarity with other countries.  However, in the two years allotted for the fulfillment of the promise, only 346 people arrived in our country, most of whom left Latvia after that.  The aggravation of the crisis in the Middle East may require some new symbolic actions from the Latvian authorities, for example, to allow those people who are just waiting to receive refugee status to work.  It will be a great challenge if Latvia is flooded with refugees from Ukraine and other countries of the former Soviet Union.  But for now – due to the low standard of living and not the most attractive social security system – this is rather a hypothetical scenario.

Title: Joint Water Patrol with France: Six More Iranian Refugees Off British Coast
Content: Photo copyright PA Image caption UK water patrols have taken many refugees from the water in recent days amid increasing numbers of migrants trying to reach Britain by water, and the country has agreed with France to further protect the border between the two countries.  A large number of these refugees are Iranian.  Sajid Javid, the British Home Secretary, returned to London in the middle of a family holiday and planned a joint Blue Patrol force with his French counterpart. Europe is waiting for a new migration crisis - RIA Novosti, 25.05.2021 A repeat of the nightmare of 2015.  Europe is once again on the brink of a migration crisis. RIA Novosti, 25.05.2021 2021-05-25T08: 00 2021-05-25T08: 00 2021-05-25T08: 02 migrants refugees europe authors / html / head / meta [@ name = 'og: title'] / @ content / html / head / meta [@ name = 'og: description'] / @ content https: / / cdn.com 24.img.ria.ru / images / 07e5 / 05 / 18 / 1733713287 _ 0: 153: 1920: 1233 _ 1920x0 _ 80 _ 0 _ 85ca65dc729db44d8073637ad5013c74.jpg Europe is again on the verge of a migration crisis.  And this is not yet the summer, which traditionally accounts for the peak of the wave of illegal migration from Asia and Africa.Now in the center of attention is Ceuta, a Spanish enclave in North Africa, where thousands of illegal refugees from Morocco rushed.  The refugee crisis in Ceuta and Melilla (another Spanish port in Africa) is largely the result of the artificial escalation of relations between Spain and Morocco.  According to many observers, Rabat decided to take revenge on Madrid for the assistance recently provided to the Polisario Front (which for many years has been fighting for the independence of Western Sahara from Morocco).  The revenge was the actual inaction of the border guards of this country, who turned a blind eye to the crowds of migrants breaking into Ceuta.  According to The Economist magazine, in this way King Mohammed VI of Morocco “made migration a weapon ” .But in fact, the sharp influx of refugees from Africa began not only in the Spanish enclaves.  Again, a series of flimsy ships illegally transporting Africans (mainly Libyans) from Tunisia to the Italian island of Lampedusa.  Last week, 1,200 people were transferred there during 12 hours of good weather alone.  And even despite the weather, accidents were recorded: 73 refugees from Bangladesh almost drowned trying to reach the cherished island.  How long it took, no one can say.  According to the Italian Interior Ministry, 4,290 migrants reached the country ’ s shores in the first three weeks of May.  While for the whole of May last year, their number was 1654 people.  The flow of illegal refugees is also increasing between the EU and Britain.  Since January, more than three thousand people have crossed the English Channel.  And over the same period last year, this figure was 1,400 refugees – more than double the growth.  Just the other day, the Belgian coast guard rescued a sinking ship on which 49 migrants, mostly Vietnamese, tried to cross the strait.  Based on the above facts and statistics, we can safely assume that the migration crisis will return to the European agenda in the foreseeable future.  However, the numbers are not as catastrophic as they were in 2015, when Europe was literally drowned by a flood of refugees.  And the increase compared to last year is easily explained by the fact that in 2020, many people in Asia and Africa gave up their intentions to go to pandemics in Europe.  In addition, the result of the shift of public attention from the problem of migration to the fight against the covid was a noticeable decrease in the ratings of a number of parties advocating strict measures to limit the influx of immigrants (in the Western media, these political organizations are usually indiscriminately called ultra-right, even despite the rather liberal economic program of many of them).  It is quite logical that now, with the rapid return of migration problems to the agenda, many publications have sounded the alarm in connection with the imminent growth of the popularity of these political forces.  Almost all analysts agree that the crisis around Ceuta, which has not descended from the front pages of the Spanish press for several days, will significantly strengthen the anti-Islamic party Vox (Voice).  Even before the current crisis, it actively dispersed the fears of the enclave residents in connection with the influx of poor Africans.  And in the end, it won the first place in the parliamentary elections of 2019, receiving more than 35 percent of the vote – and this is in a city where 40 percent of the population is Muslim.  It would be strange if the Vox party did not now take advantage of the crisis to increase its popularity in Ceuta.  For example, a local cell of the party is publicizing protests against the fact that African migrants entering the Spanish enclave receive coronavirus vaccinations, while Spanish citizens living there wait months for their turn.  This is confirmed by events in the regional parliament of Andalusia, where after the 2018 elections, for the first time in history, the People ’ s Party took the first place and was able to form a minority government.  Until last week, it relied solely on the informal support of Vox MPs.  However, on Thursday, they announced the termination of cooperation with the senior partner in connection with the fact that the authorities of the region agreed to accept 13 minor refugees who infiltrated Ceuta.  This could lead to the fall of the regional government and early elections.  That is why the People ’ s Party is forced to show more and more rigidity in the migration issue, causing panic in the European liberal media.Even more worrying in the mainstream is the electoral situation in Italy.  After the 2015 crisis, the League party, led by Matteo Salvini, has been the consistent leader of the polls there.  Having proved himself a tough fighter against illegal migration as the Minister of Internal Affairs, he increased the leadership of his party to record levels.  At the peak of popularity in the summer of 2019, the League ’ s figures were approaching 40 percent, which gave it hope even for the formation of its government.  Based on these calculations, Salvini provoked a government crisis in order to hold early elections, but was outplayed by opponents.  Since last year, there has been a drop in the ratings of this political force, whose supporters cannot forgive the support it expressed for the technocratic government of Mario Draghi.  Liberals can breathe freely.  But the fact is that the ratings of the League, which is still in the first place in the polls, are moving on opposite courses with the rapidly growing indicators of the even more right-wing and even more anti-migrant party “Brothers of Italy ”.  According to some polls, she already came in second place after the League, behind that couple of percent.  Three years ago, its ratings fluctuated around three to four percent, and now confidently approaching 20.  If elections were held now, these two forces, with the support of Silvio Berlusconi ’ s Forward Italy party, could well form a majority government.  They do not hide their ideological continuity from the far-right Italian social movement, which was created in 1946 by former supporters of Benito Mussolini.  This legacy is clearly indicated by the logo of the party, which includes the former symbol of ISD.The growth of the popularity of the "Brothers" will contribute to the charisma of the head of the party Georgia Meloni ("Sisters of Italy", as it was nicknamed by the press) - she last year surpassed in the approval ratings of the leader of the "League", becoming the second most popular politician in the country after the current prime minister.  There is no doubt that in the event of an aggravation of the migration crisis, the League and Brothers will be able to get additional votes to their already serious ratings.  Trends in the first months of the year show that the threat of the covid is no longer deterring refugees seeking to Europe.  And this means that the nightmare of 2015 may repeat itself — and the popularity of far-right, anti-migrant, anti-Islamic, Eurosceptic parties will again sharply rise. Title: Europe speaking. How dangerous is the new migration crisis?
Content: The aggravation of the situation in the Middle East, caused by the murder of Iranian General Qassem Soleimani, forced the European Union to again talk about the possible admission of refugees.  Europe is still dealing with the migration crisis of 2015, even if it is not written daily in the media.  DELFI presents a short guide on how the situation with refugees is and whether the European Union is ready for a new wave of migrants.  What are we talking about?  Between 2015 and 2018, the number of migrants arriving in Europe fell sharply, from 1.8 million to 140,000.  Some European politicians hastened to call what was happening a “success story ”, attributing the decline in refugee activity to the migration agreements that Brussels had concluded with Turkey and North African countries.  However, as noted by public organizations, in reality, the migration crisis has not gone away – just the countries of Western Europe have noticeably tightened their “hospitality policy ”, which forces refugees to use more risky routes and means to move to Europe.  According to the EU delegation on border control in Libya, the death rate among migrants has increased significantly in recent years: if in 2017 there was one death for every 38 arrivals, in 2018 - one for every 14, and in the first quarter of 2019 - one for every three people who reached Europe alive.  A similar trend can be observed on the route between Spain and Morocco.  The UN refugee agency has estimated that in 2018, 138 thousand people arrived by sea to the shores of Italy, Greece, Spain, Cyprus and Malta, and more than 2,000 people drowned.  40% of those who arrived last year were women and children.  Most refugees are housed in temporary camps in the countries where their boats arrive.  Some try to later move to more prosperous Western countries (Germany, France, Belgium).  According to the European Commission, 580,000 people applied for asylum in the European Union in 2018.  Mostly they are citizens of Afghanistan, Iraq, Pakistan, Iran and Nigeria.  In 2018, compared with the previous year, the influx of refugees from Venezuela, Georgia, Turkey, Iran and Colombia increased.  Four out of five asylum seekers are under the age of 35, and one in three is a minor.  What does that mean?  For five years of the migration crisis, the European Union has not been able to agree on common rules for the reception and accommodation of refugees.  The countries of Eastern Europe and the Baltic States "wrapped up" the idea of quotas for the distribution of refugees (Poland, Hungary, the Czech Republic, Slovakia almost completely refused to accept migrants), the countries of Western Europe, in turn, under pressure from the public began to tighten the conditions for granting refugee status.  In 2018, 200,000 positive responses were received for 580,000 asylum applications.  At the same time, the number of migrants returned to their homeland has increased significantly.  For example, Germany last year deported 17,000 illegal immigrants, Greece in the fall announced plans to expel 10,000 people from the country.  The new president of the European Commission, Ursula von der Leyen, made it clear that the new asylum system in the EU “must include the search for new forms of solidarity and ensure that all member states make a meaningful contribution to supporting countries under the greatest pressure. ”  At the same time, it advocates strengthening humanitarian cooperation with third countries, that is, a policy of containing refugees in territories outside the European Union.  The most famous in this area is the agreement with Turkey: on May 20, 2016, a two-year agreement came into force, according to which Turkey had to close the way to the EU for refugees.  The agreement drew a barrage of criticism from human rights organizations (refugees are held in poor conditions, children are forced to work, there are reports that Turkish soldiers even shoot refugees at the border), and, according to many experts, failed to perform basic tasks.  Nevertheless, Brussels is ready to conclude a new deal with Ankara.  According to representatives of Croatia – this country took over the presidency of the EU Council from January 1, 2020 – this issue is on the list of priorities.  What do I care about that?  Despite the horror stories of nationalist politicians, the European migration crisis of 2015 practically did not affect Latvia.  According to the Foundation for Social Integration, over the past four years, more than 900 people have received asylum in our country, but two-thirds have already gone abroad.  Probably went to Germany.  The main reasons for leaving are low benefits, a cold climate, difficulties in finding a job, inflexible language policy, etc.  Latvia, like other countries in Eastern Europe, opposes mandatory quotas for the accommodation of refugees.  In 2015, at the height of the migration crisis, Latvia agreed to host 531 refugees from camps in Greece, Italy and Turkey in solidarity with other countries.  However, in the two years allotted for the fulfillment of the promise, only 346 people arrived in our country, most of whom left Latvia after that.  The aggravation of the crisis in the Middle East may require some new symbolic actions from the Latvian authorities, for example, to allow those people who are just waiting to receive refugee status to work.  It will be a great challenge if Latvia is flooded with refugees from Ukraine and other countries of the former Soviet Union.  But for now – due to the low standard of living and not the most attractive social security system – this is rather a hypothetical scenario.

passages.title: Stratolaunch, the largest aircraft to date, successfully passed one of the latest tests » DailyTechInfo
passages.passage: Over the weekend, the Stratolaunch, the world ’ s largest aircraft to date, successfully passed one of the final tests in preparation for the giant ’ s first attempt at takeoff.  We remind our readers that the purpose of the Stratolaunch project, founded by Paul Allen, is to create a space launch system capable of launching payloads weighing up to 230 tons into low Earth orbit using conventional runways, a giant aircraft and single-stage launch vehicles. It has a length of 72.5 meters and a wingspan of 116 meters.  The aircraft has two fuselages, in the right of which crew members are located, and the second fuselage serves as a place where navigation systems, flight systems and other aviation electronics are installed.  Both fuselages are connected by a reinforced wing, which serves as a mounting point for the rocket that will rise to the height of its launch.  During these tests, the suspension, brake system and a number of other related technologies were tested.  All these tests were carried out at low speed, despite the operation of all six Pratt and Whitney turbojet engines, the plane moved at a speed of no more than 45 kilometers per hour.The latest tests of the Stratolaunch aircraft were carried out on Saturday and Sunday in the traditional place, on the lanes and taxiways of the Mojave Air & Space Port in California.  This time the plane was allowed to accelerate to a speed of 75 kilometers per hour, a speed that is the limit at which this giant aircraft will have to start take-off in any case.  This, unfortunately, does not mean that the first attempt to take off the aircraft will be made in the near future.  According to the company ’ s plans, this moment should come only by the end of the current decade.

passages.title: World's Largest Aircraft Gets Ground Test at 74 km / h
passages.passage: Feb 27, 2018 14: 03 China Times News Yang Yulan has a wingspan of more than 117 meters, and the world ’ s largest aircraft with six engines is rapidly flying headfirst.  Recently, it has been seen moving rapidly at the Mojave Air and Space Port.  According to "The Drive" network reported on the 26th, now Stratolaunch Systems main sponsor Paul Allen took advantage of it before the first flight, released a wonderful picture of the roc rapid ground test.  Allen tweeted that it can reach a top speed of 46 miles per hour (74 km / h), which is quite fast for a big baby with a net weight of 226,800 kg, a maximum fuel load of 113,400 kg and an external weight of 250,000 kg.  Because in recent months, the Pentagon has sought to increase the flexibility and agility of its space capabilities, and has even been actively considering space as the next battleground, the tools to launch smaller satellites into orbit quickly and cheaply appear to be full of business opportunities.  (Stratolaunch Systems) To achieve this goal, the US Air Force ’ s 2019 budget for space “small launches ” lists a five-year plan with a budget of nearly US $200 million (nearly NT $6 billion), which will fund companies that can provide related services in the future.  U.S. Air Force Secretary Heather Wilson said the goal of the project is to develop a variety of launch capabilities to ensure access to space.  The world's largest aircraft, nicknamed Dapeng, can carry a 110-ton rocket from the ground to 35,000 feet (nearly 11,000 meters) in the stratosphere below the wings and in the middle of the fuselage, and then let the rocket ignite, launch, escape from the atmosphere, and then send satellites into low-Earth orbit.  Air-launched rockets have advantages and disadvantages compared to ground-launched rockets.  The advantage is that the air-launched rocket can avoid the dense atmosphere on the surface, greatly reducing the thrust / lift required for the rocket to enter the orbit, thus reducing the cost.  Overall, this launch method can quickly launch a launch object into space at a lower cost, without the need for complex launch site equipment.  In addition, the research of air-launched rocket technology has great military value.  The disadvantage of air-launched rockets is that during take-off, liftoff and flight, the rocket may be accidentally damaged, which increases the uncertainty of the launch.  (China Times Newsletter)

passages.title: The world ’ s largest aircraft can launch three rockets for the first time.
passages.passage: Stratolaunch Systems created the world ’ s largest aircraft and debuted on May 31 at the Mojave Space Station in California. (Photo / Stratolaunch Systems) The airborne giant has 28 wheels.  Stratolaunch Systems (Stratolaunch Systems), founded by Microsoft co-founder Paul Allen, announced on May 31 that the world ’ s largest aircraft will be launched for the first time at the Mojave Air and Space Port in California.  According to SPACENEWS and CNN, the huge object has a double body, a wingspan of more than 117 meters, a net weight of 226,800 kg, a maximum fuel load of 113,400 kg, and an external weight of 250,000 kg.  It has 28 wheels in addition to six engines used in the Boeing 747.  The company was originally set up in late 2011 to launch the mid-size SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket, but as the two companies parted ways a year later, Stratolaunch then signed a contract with Orbital Sciences Corp, now known as Orbital ATK, to launch the mid-size rocket.  However, due to the increasing need to launch small satellites, Stratolaunch is now focusing on providing related services.  Allen ’ s newly unveiled baby can launch up to three Pegasus XL small rockets with just one flight.  Stratosphere Launch Systems said in a statement that since this is the world ’ s first new aircraft, it is expected that the giant will fly as early as 2019 after thorough testing for the safety of the pilot and crew.  It will begin with a series of ground tests, including refueling tests, with six tanks on board. The refueling mechanism will be tested separately and whether oil leaks will occur.  Stratolaunch is working on technology to reduce launch costs, and its CEO, Jean Floyd, believes they have shown results.  He pointed out that Allen ’ s motivation for investing is not to make big money, but to change the human environment.  Stratolaunch ’ s world ’ s largest aircraft can launch three small rockets at a time. (Photo / Stratolaunch Systems) The world ’ s largest aircraft, nicknamed Roc, can carry a rocket weighing up to 110 tons to an altitude of nearly 11,000 meters in the stratosphere to launch the rocket. (Photo / Stratolaunch Systems) The aircraft can carry a 110-ton rocket from the ground to 35,000 feet (nearly 11,000 meters) in the stratosphere, and then fire the rocket, launch it out of the atmosphere, and then send satellites into low Earth orbit.  Air-launched rockets have advantages and disadvantages compared to ground-launched rockets.  The advantage is that the air-launched rocket can avoid the dense atmosphere on the surface, greatly reducing the thrust / lift required for the rocket to enter the orbit, thus reducing the cost.  Overall, this launch method can quickly launch a launch object into space at a lower cost, without the need for complex launch site equipment.  In addition, the research of air-launched rocket technology has great military value.  The disadvantage of air-launched rockets is that during take-off, liftoff and flight, the rocket may be accidentally damaged, which increases the uncertainty of the launch.  SpaceX founder Elon Musk believes that the advantages of an air-launched rocket are not enough to make up for its shortcomings. “From SpaceX ’ s point of view, to launch a rocket with a huge aircraft, or to increase the first stage capacity of the rocket by 5%? I will choose the latter. ”

passages.title: Pandora ’ s Box – In the United States for the first time rolled out of the hangar the largest aircraft in the world (PHOTOS, VIDEO)
passages.passage: May 31, 2017 in Mojave (California) took place the roll-out of the almost completed construction of the Stratolaunch Model 351 carrier aircraft (also sometimes referred to as "Roc", in fact, the official name has not yet been assigned) of the aerospace system "air launch" Stratolaunch, created by the American company Stratolaunch Systems (as part of Vulcan Aerospace Corporation). The BMPD blog.  Rolling out of the carrier aircraft Stratolaunch Model 351 aerospace system "air start" Stratolaunch American company Stratolaunch Systems.  Mojave (California), 31.05.2017 (c) Stratolaunch Systems The built twin-body Stratolaunch Model 351 aircraft is the largest aircraft in history, having a wingspan of 117 m and a length of 73 m. The maximum take-off weight should be 590 tons, with a suspended payload weight of 230 tons.  Thus, the Stratolaunch Model 351 aircraft in wingspan exceeds the former largest aircraft in the world, the Soviet An-225 "Mriya" (which has a wingspan of 88.4 m), although the An-225 retains an advantage in length (84 m) and maximum take-off weight (640 tons).  The Stratolaunch Model 351 aircraft is equipped with six twin-circuit Pratt & Whitney PW4056 turbojet engines with a thrust of 25 tons, removed from two decommissioned Boeing 747-400 aircraft.  The landing gear of the aircraft is 28-wheel, take-off distance with full load should be calculated to be 3800 m. The maximum range of the aircraft with full load will not exceed 3700 km.  The aircraft is designed to be used as a carrier for the aerospace system Stratolaunch, created by the American company Stratolaunch Systems, founded by co-founder Microsot Paul Allen and the famous aircraft designer Bert Rutan (who acted as the actual chief designer of the aircraft) (since 2015 Stratolaunch Systems is a subsidiary of the corporation created by the same Paul Allen Vulcan Aerospace).  The aircraft is designed to launch space launch vehicles using the "air launch" method, which will be carried out from an altitude of approximately 10,500 m. The launch vehicle should be suspended under the central part of the wing between the fuselages.  In the course of design and construction, the SpaceX Falcon 9 Air and Orbital ATK Pegasus II launch vehicles were successively replaced as payload options, and now only the long-known Orbital ATK Pegasus XL light launch vehicle used for “air launches ” from“ conventional ” aircraft in the United States since 1990 is considered as such (starting mass of 23.2 tons, payload mass load of 443 kg), and for which there was no need to create such a giant carrier - although the possibility of carrying and launching from it in one flight up to three Pegasus XL launch vehicles is claimed.  In light of this, the outlook for Stratolaunch is still uncertain.  In 2014, the notorious Sierra Nevada Corporation announced the development of a smaller version of the project of its lightweight manned shuttle Dream Chaser (previously rejected by NASA), which was to be launched using an unnamed launch vehicle developed by the Orbital ATK.  However, there is no information about the development of this project in relation to Stratolaunch.  During the launch vehicle roll-out ceremony on May 31, Stratolauch Systems CEO Joan Floyd said that the company would "actively explore a wide range of launch vehicles, allowing us to provide more flexibility for customers."  Rolling out of the carrier aircraft Stratolaunch Model 351 aerospace system "air start" Stratolaunch American company Stratolaunch Systems.  The Stratolaunch Model 351 was designed and built under the contract of Stratolaunch Systems by Scaled Composites, founded by Bert Rutan and now owned by Northrop Grumman Corporation.  The project was announced in December 2011.  The construction of the aircraft was carried out in a specially built for this purpose in 2012 in Mojave giant hangar.  The scheme of the intended use of the aircraft carrier Stratolaunch Model 351 of the aerospace system "air launch" Stratolaunch American company Stratolaunch Systems (c) Stratolaunch Systems The program is lagging behind in terms of about two years.  Currently, the beginning of flight tests of the carrier aircraft is scheduled for the end of 2017, and the first demonstration space launch from it - in 2019.  The start of commercial launches will be possible in this case from 2020. Title: The world ’ s largest aircraft can launch three rockets for the first time.

It has 28 wheels in addition to six engines used in the Boeing 747.  The company was originally set up in late 2011 to launch the mid-size SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket, but as the two companies parted ways a year later, Stratolaunch then signed a contract with Orbital Sciences Corp, now known as Orbital ATK, to launch the mid-size rocket. Allen ’ s newly unveiled baby can launch up to three Pegasus XL small rockets with just one flight. It will begin with a series of ground tests, including refueling tests, with six tanks on board. The refueling mechanism will be tested separately and whether oil leaks will occur. Air-launched rockets have advantages and disadvantages compared to ground-launched rockets.  The advantage is that the air-launched rocket can avoid the dense atmosphere on the surface, greatly reducing the thrust / lift required for the rocket to enter the orbit, thus reducing the cost.  Overall, this launch method can quickly launch a launch object into space at a lower cost, without the need for complex launch site equipment.  In addition, the research of air-launched rocket technology has great military value.  The disadvantage of air-launched rockets is that during take-off, liftoff and flight, the rocket may be accidentally damaged, which increases the uncertainty of the launch. (Reuters) - In a series of car accidents in the first stage of the Tour de France, a spectator approached the track with a sign, and one of the competitors, Tony Martin, crashed into the sign and overturned due to the very crowded track at the start. passages.title: Mass blockage at the cycling race "Tour de France" because of the antics of the cheerleader: the girl hit the racers with a poster and ran away
passages.passage: The girl showed the camera a poster with a joke inscription, knocked down the racers on the asphalt and fled from the scene.  45 km before the end of the first stage of the legendary cycling race "Tour de France" there was a massive blockage, as a result of which more than two dozen athletes were injured.  Almost half of the peloton fell, including the main favorites.  The culprit of the accident was a cheerleader who put up a poster with a joke inscription right in front of the riders.  Now she is wanted by the police, who asked witnesses for help through social networks.  The organizers of the race promised her legal proceedings.  "Allez Opi-Omi" The cheerleader intervened in the battle of the strongest riders of the world at the most famous stage race in history at the first stage from Brest to Landerno.  About 45 km before the finish, the girl in blue jeans and a bright yellow jacket jumped from the side of the road and put on camera in front of the athletes a poster with the inscription “Allez Opi-Omi ” (a joke and caressing appeal to grandparents in German, something like“ Go, old men ”).  Driving on the right side of the rider of the team “Jumbo Wisma ” German Tony Martin had no chance to dodge the collision with the poster and fell, which led to a major blockage.  Not escaped this and the main favorites: Slovenes Tadej Pogacar and Primož Roglic.  But they at least cost bruises and abrasions, but Spaniard Mark Soler of “Movistar ” broke the radial bones on both hands.  By some miracle, he reached the finish line, but he will not be able to continue the race.  Like the German Jascha Sutterlin.  Those who continued the Tour de France lost a lot of time.  “We had everything under control, I led the guys on the right side of the road, but crashed into a fan poster.  It all happened very quickly, all of a sudden, almost everyone was on the ground.  Many viewers behave respectfully, but in this case this was not the case, unfortunately.  I hope that there will be no consequences for the health of all the guys who fell into the rubble, ” said Tony Martin.  A year behind bars and a 15,000 euro fine The cheerleader, who became the culprit of the accident, quickly disappeared.  The Gendarmerie Landerno put her on the wanted list and asked for help from witnesses, posting a post on social media.  However, the comments are more negative towards the police than the desire to help find a negligent fan.  The organizers of the Tour de France have already promised that the culprit of the collision is awaiting trial.  “We must not allow a small number of hooligans to spoil the sporting event for participants and fans, ” said Pierre-Yves Tuo, deputy director of the race.  What threatens the offender?  While injured in the accident riders did not submit a statement to the police – a fine of 1500 euros.  But if Soler and Sutterlin write such a statement, the case will be reclassified.  Now the fan is accused that failure to comply with the required security measures led to harm to health.  In the case of a statement from the riders unknown until the violator faces a fine ten times more and up to a year in prison.  The organizers appealed to all fans with a request to observe security measures and even released a special video reminding how dangerous such clashes can be.  There are a lot of fans in the current Tour de France.  And almost no one follows the antiquated rules.  The organizers are ready to turn a blind eye to this, but when the physical safety of athletes is threatened, it is quite another matter.  The athletes themselves also urged fans to be more restrained in the display of emotions, although clashes with fans in cycling are quite regular.  But now it has crossed all boundaries.  “I hope Opi-Omi are proud of you, ” Belgian cyclist Jasper Stuyven wrote on Twitter.  It is wonderful to see that there are so many fans who love our sport and support us.  But please stay on the side of the road, not on the road! ”  The participants of the Tour de France quite cope with the organization of force majeure and without the participation of fans.  At the same first stage, about 8 km before the finish line, Briton Chris Froome forked to the side and organized another blockage, himself and being the main victim.  But serious injuries to athletes were avoided.  The leader in the overall stage race after two stages is the Dutchman Mathieu van der Poole from the Alpesin-Phoenix team.  Russian riders do not participate in the current Tour de France.

passages.title: Police are looking for the woman who caused the collision of cyclists during the Tour de France 2021
passages.passage: The woman held a cardboard poster and stood very close to the roadway.  Soon there was a column of cyclists, but the woman, apparently, did not notice.  German cyclist Tony Martin crashed into a poster, causing him to lose his balance and fall.  This created a domino effect, and several cyclists collided with each other, creating a rather serious collision.  As a result, several cyclists were injured, 21 of which required medical attention, and one, because of the injuries, had to be removed from the race.  French police say an investigation will be carried out and the woman is being actively sought.  Police also conducted interviews with eyewitnesses to find out where the woman might have gone.  The organizers of the event also said that the woman will be charged.  "We will bring charges against this woman so that the rest of the small population that acts so irresponsibly does not spoil the viewing and the competition for others," Tour de France spokesman Pierre Yves told AFP.

passages.passage: An accident in the Tour de France; police in pursuit of the 'reckless woman' 46 minutes ago Image source Gendarmerie du finistere Image caption Police are searching for a woman who caused a bicycle accident French police are searching for a woman whose carelessness made headlines during the Tour de France.  The spectator entered the path of the cyclists with a placard in his hand, and as a result, many athletes crashed and fell to the ground in the first round.  On Saturday, she leaned into the road in the speed section of the race in Brittany, France, holding a placard.  The first cyclist he encountered was German Tony Martin, followed by a significant number of athletes.  Police say they have filed a criminal case for the incident.  According to police, the charge is "deliberate violation of safety regulations and causing injuries that could prevent someone from working for up to three months."  The image of the incident has been widely circulated on social media.  A woman in a yellow coat with a sign in German that reads “Grandma and Grandpa. ”  The woman stands with her back to the group of cyclists and does not notice that they are approaching.  One of the injured cyclists was forced to retire from the Tour de France, and eight other cyclists were suspended by the official doctor.  Police said the woman fled the scene after the incident.  Police have asked witnesses to give their information to officers.  The vice president of the Tour de France also called for legal action against the woman, saying: “We will sue her for her very bad behavior.  We do this so that a small group of people can ’ t ruin a show that ’ s for everyone. ”  France has recently eased some of the restrictions imposed by the coronavirus outbreak, with a sizable population making its way to cyclists to watch races.  The Tour de France is an annual cycling race for men.  It is considered to be the most prestigious bicycle road race in the world.  France hosts the tournament, but sometimes competitions are held in the surrounding countries.

Title: Mass blockage at the cycling race "Tour de France" because of the antics of the cheerleader: the girl hit the racers with a poster and ran away
Content: The girl showed the camera a poster with a joke inscription, knocked down the racers on the asphalt and fled from the scene.  45 km before the end of the first stage of the legendary cycling race "Tour de France" there was a massive blockage, as a result of which more than two dozen athletes were injured.  Almost half of the peloton fell, including the main favorites.  The culprit of the accident was a cheerleader who put up a poster with a joke inscription right in front of the riders.  Now she is wanted by the police, who asked witnesses for help through social networks.  The organizers of the race promised her legal proceedings.  "Allez Opi-Omi" The cheerleader intervened in the battle of the strongest riders of the world at the most famous stage race in history at the first stage from Brest to Landerno.  About 45 km before the finish, the girl in blue jeans and a bright yellow jacket jumped from the side of the road and put on camera in front of the athletes a poster with the inscription “Allez Opi-Omi ” (a joke and caressing appeal to grandparents in German, something like“ Go, old men ”).  Driving on the right side of the rider of the team “Jumbo Wisma ” German Tony Martin had no chance to dodge the collision with the poster and fell, which led to a major blockage.  Not escaped this and the main favorites: Slovenes Tadej Pogacar and Primož Roglic.  But they at least cost bruises and abrasions, but Spaniard Mark Soler of “Movistar ” broke the radial bones on both hands.  By some miracle, he reached the finish line, but he will not be able to continue the race.  Like the German Jascha Sutterlin.  Those who continued the Tour de France lost a lot of time.  “We had everything under control, I led the guys on the right side of the road, but crashed into a fan poster.  It all happened very quickly, all of a sudden, almost everyone was on the ground.  Many viewers behave respectfully, but in this case this was not the case, unfortunately.  I hope that there will be no consequences for the health of all the guys who fell into the rubble, ” said Tony Martin.  A year behind bars and a 15,000 euro fine The cheerleader, who became the culprit of the accident, quickly disappeared.  The Gendarmerie Landerno put her on the wanted list and asked for help from witnesses, posting a post on social media.  However, the comments are more negative towards the police than the desire to help find a negligent fan.  The organizers of the Tour de France have already promised that the culprit of the collision is awaiting trial.  “We must not allow a small number of hooligans to spoil the sporting event for participants and fans, ” said Pierre-Yves Tuo, deputy director of the race.  What threatens the offender?  While injured in the accident riders did not submit a statement to the police – a fine of 1500 euros.  But if Soler and Sutterlin write such a statement, the case will be reclassified.  Now the fan is accused that failure to comply with the required security measures led to harm to health.  In the case of a statement from the riders unknown until the violator faces a fine ten times more and up to a year in prison.  The organizers appealed to all fans with a request to observe security measures and even released a special video reminding how dangerous such clashes can be.  There are a lot of fans in the current Tour de France.  And almost no one follows the antiquated rules.  The organizers are ready to turn a blind eye to this, but when the physical safety of athletes is threatened, it is quite another matter.  The athletes themselves also urged fans to be more restrained in the display of emotions, although clashes with fans in cycling are quite regular.  But now it has crossed all boundaries.  “I hope Opi-Omi are proud of you, ” Belgian cyclist Jasper Stuyven wrote on Twitter.  It is wonderful to see that there are so many fans who love our sport and support us.  But please stay on the side of the road, not on the road! ”  The participants of the Tour de France quite cope with the organization of force majeure and without the participation of fans.  At the same first stage, about 8 km before the finish line, Briton Chris Froome forked to the side and organized another blockage, himself and being the main victim.  But serious injuries to athletes were avoided.  The leader in the overall stage race after two stages is the Dutchman Mathieu van der Poole from the Alpesin-Phoenix team.  Russian riders do not participate in the current Tour de France.

Title: Police are looking for the woman who caused the collision of cyclists during the Tour de France 2021
Content: The woman held a cardboard poster and stood very close to the roadway.  Soon there was a column of cyclists, but the woman, apparently, did not notice.  German cyclist Tony Martin crashed into a poster, causing him to lose his balance and fall.  This created a domino effect, and several cyclists collided with each other, creating a rather serious collision.  As a result, several cyclists were injured, 21 of which required medical attention, and one, because of the injuries, had to be removed from the race.  French police say an investigation will be carried out and the woman is being actively sought.  Police also conducted interviews with eyewitnesses to find out where the woman might have gone.  The organizers of the event also said that the woman will be charged.  "We will bring charges against this woman so that the rest of the small population that acts so irresponsibly does not spoil the viewing and the competition for others," Tour de France spokesman Pierre Yves told AFP.
