passages.title: SpaceX successfully launches manned space capsule
passages.passage: On Saturday, space exploration technology company SpaceX launched its first crew Dragon, a critical flight to prove to NASA the safety of astronauts in future flights.  The mission, called Demo-1, was launched on a Falcon 9 rocket from the Kennedy Air Center in California.  This space capsule does not carry a human, but a model of an astronaut called Ripley, wearing sensors to measure various indicators of the human body in the space capsule.  This is the first of two SpaceX test flights under NASA ’ s Commercial Crew Program. Demo-2 will be the first to fly with a human pilot, scheduled for July of this year.  According to NASA ’ s plan, SpaceX will be the first company to send astronauts into space since 2011.  NASA Administrator Jim Bridenstine later stated that the successful launch marked a new chapter in American excellence, bringing us once again closer to carrying American astronauts from American soil on American rockets.  Since the retirement of the Space Shuttle in 2011, the United States has been unable to use its own rockets to transport astronauts to space on its own. NASA is working with private companies to develop the future of human spaceflight.  Currently, SpaceX and NASA have a contract value of $2.6 billion, and Boeing is $4.2 billion.

passages.title: NASA has agreed to reuse the Dragon capsule.
passages.passage: As part of its plans to send a man to the moon, NASA announced that it would re-use SpaceX ’ s Dragon capsule.  NASA has announced that it will allow SpaceX to re-use its Dragon capsule and Falcon 9 rocket in the near future.  The Dragon capsule recently sent two American astronauts to the International Space Station from the United States.  The launch was from NASA ’ s Kennedy Space Center (KSC) in Florida, which has been used for other missions, including Apollo.  The Demo-2 mission was a successful test flight.  In a statement, NASA said: “While this is not unexpected, it is an important step for NASA ’ s commercial manned programs that have led the United States to return to power and fly space from its soil. ”  According to NASA ’ s contract with SpaceX, the company has been allowed to reuse both its Falcon 9 and its Dragon.  The revised contract will allow SpaceX to carry out its second operational mission, known as PCM-2 or Crew-2.  The change is intended as part of a bilateral reform plan that formally extends the Demo-2 mission from two weeks to 119 days.  The Dragon capsule is said to be reused in 2021.  On SpaceX ’ s recent historic mission, Doug Harley and Bob Behenken were sent into orbit aboard the Dragon capsule.  About 19 hours later, the Crew Dragon capsule was automatically attached to the International Space Station to make the first successful journey to the orbital station from a US-based space station since the space shuttle's retirement in 2011.  End of message.

passages.title: Tomorrow SpaceX will test the emergency rescue system of the Crew Dragon spacecraft in flight. This is the last major test before the first operational flight with astronauts on board
passages.passage: Tomorrow, January 18, SpaceX intends to make the final major test of Crew Dragon ahead of the long-awaited Demo-2 mission with the first operational flight of a crewed spacecraft to the ISS.  We are talking about those additional tests of the emergency rescue system (SAS) with the shooting of the capsule during the flight.  Of course, the launch will be broadcast online, and those who want to watch the broadcast will find it below in this note.  The carrier rocket itself with the ship is already installed at the site of the SLC-40 complex at Cape Canaveral and is waiting for the countdown; a suitable launch window for the launch of the rocket opens on January 18 at 15: 00 Kyiv time.  SpaceX will have four hours to conduct the launch; assess the weather conditions as favorable and state that the probability of a successful launch is 90%.  Falcon 9 and Crew Dragon went vertical and the crew access arm was extended last night ahead of tomorrow's in-flight demonstration of the spacecraft's launch escape system.  The four-hour launch window opens at 8: 00 a.m.  EST, 13: 00 UTC → https: / / t.co / gtC39uBC7z pic.twitter.com / dS6R3hCgZi — SpaceX (@ SpaceX) January 17, 2020 These tests are not a mandatory part of NASA ’ s Crew Dragon certification program, but SpaceX on its own initiative intends to conduct them to demonstrate the reliability of the SAS and even donate one Falcon 9 rockets - for the purity of the experiment with simulated accident, it is likely to be destroyed during the flight, and the capsule soon after firing parachutes and splashdown in the ocean.  The animation for tomorrow ’ s launch can be seen below.  @ SpaceX's uncrewed in-flight abort test is targeted for 8am ET on Jan. 18.  This test will show that the # CrewDragon can protect astronauts even in the unlikely event of an emergency during launch.  Currently, weather is 90% GO for the demonstration.  https: / / t.co / PgHZol6PQA pic.twitter.com / kWCq7IHiq1 — NASA Commercial Crew (@ Commercial _ Crew) January 15, 2020 Recall that the Crew Dragon ship is equipped with two types of propulsion systems (low and high pressure).  The first with sixteen Draco engines is designed for orbital maneuvers and orientation of the ship in space, and the second with eight SuperDraco engines is responsible for shooting and controlled landing of the rescue capsule in case of an emergency.  The first Pad Abort Test simulated a rocket crash before launch and shot off the capsule from the launch pad SpaceX held back in 2015, and at the end of the year passed static tests of the emergency rescue system Crew Dragon in a new configuration with rupture diaphragm valves in the pressurization tubes instead of titanium valves.  The improvement should prevent the very possibility of a repeat of the scenario that led to the crash in April.  Also not so long ago, in preparation for the Demo-2 mission, SpaceX successfully tested new parachutes for Crew Dragon.  A few weeks ago, Elon Musk shared a video with computer animation of the first manned flight of the Crew Dragon spacecraft to the ISS.  It is hardly worth saying how important for SpaceX and the entire world of cosmonautics is this launch, to which SpaceX has been going for eight long years.  Recall, Crew Dragon is being developed as part of NASA ’ s program to stimulate the development of private ships Commercial Crew Development to send American astronauts to the ISS and ensure independence in this matter from Russia.  After the closure of the Space Shuttle program in 2011, the only means of delivering crews to the International Space Station are the Russian Soyuz spacecraft.  It is noteworthy that on January 20, SpaceX plans to carry out the next launch of Falcon 9, sending into orbit another batch of 60 satellites as part of its own project of a global satellite Internet network of a new generation.  This year, SpaceX plans to begin providing communication services to its first customers, and full network deployment is scheduled for the mid-2020s.  In total, in 2020, SpaceX plans to make from 35 to 38 launches, of which at least 24 in the interests of the Starlink project.

passages.title: Roscosmos welcomed the launch of Crew Dragon
passages.passage: The launch of the manned spacecraft Crew Dragon opens a new stage in the world space program.  This statement was made by the Executive Director of the state Corporation “Roscosmos ” Sergey Krikalev.  “I would like to welcome our American colleagues.  [...] I am confident that the success of this mission will give us additional opportunities that will benefit the entire international program, "Krikalev said, a video posted on Roscosmos's Twitter account.  According to him, a new cycle of tests has begun - before the ship has already flown in an unmanned version, but today "an important and responsible option", when astronauts went into orbit.  "This opens a new stage in the manned program - the world manned program, the ISS program, where this ship flew, because we have new opportunities, new reserves," Krikalev said.  SpaceX launched the Demo-2 mission on its second attempt.  It became the first manned flight of a private spacecraft Crew Dragon, as well as the first orbital space flight launched from the United States since 2011.  The ship will take astronauts Bob Benken and Doug Hurley to the ISS.  The launch was an important event in the history of American astronautics.  The first reusable stage of the Falcon 9 rocket has already made a successful automatic landing on a floating platform in the Atlantic. passages.passage: Already this week, SpaceX ’ s Crew Dragon spacecraft will go to the ISS as part of the Demo-2 test mission.  The launch will mark the return of the United States to manned flights, which ended with the closure of the Space Shuttle program in 2011.  How the mission will take place and why it is important, we tell in our material.  Channel 24 closely followed the process of preparation for the manned launch of the manned spacecraft Crew Dragon.  We decided to collect all the details and interesting points in one article so that you could get acquainted with the key stages of the mission.  Do not miss the US returning to the ISS: SpaceX and NASA have revealed the details of the historic mission What is happening The United States of America is returning to manned flights to the ISS using its own ships.  Already this week, on May 27, the first ever manned launch of a spacecraft to the ISS, carried out by a private company SpaceX, will take place.  Crew Dragon will have two American astronauts on board.  After launch, the ship docks with the International Space Station at an altitude of 400 kilometers above the surface of the planet.  The astronauts will get to the station, where they will continue their mission, the duration of which is not yet known and will depend on a number of factors, both during the launch and during the flight of the ship until the moment of docking with the ISS.  Despite the fact that the flight is manned, and the mission of astronauts will take a lot of time on the ISS, it is still a test, so it is called Demo-2.  Previously, SpaceX has already tested the ship Crew Dragon, but this time the company will do it for the first time as part of a crewed mission.  The broadcast of the flight will take place on Techno 24.  So visit our website on May 27 at 23: 15.  The start is scheduled for 23: 30 in Kiev.  In addition, the broadcast will be available here: NASA TV: YouTube; SpaceX: YouTube link to the broadcast will be available before launch.  The fact is that the manned launch of Demo-2 will be the first such launch from American soil in almost a decade.  The last manned spacecraft to perform such a mission was the Space Shuttle Atlantis, which landed on July 21, 2011 as part of the STS-135 mission.  After that, the shuttles to the ISS no longer flew, and NASA was forced to buy seats for its astronauts on the Russian Soyuz, which cost the United States a considerable amount.  It is worth paying attention to the fact that after the American shuttles stopped flying, Russia constantly raised the price of seats for American astronauts and other partners on board the Soyuz spacecraft.  As of today, one seat on the Soyuz costs NASA $90 million (in 2010 it cost about $30 million).  The Alpha Centauri portal notes that given the approximate prices of Russian state launch contracts, it turns out that NASA pays the entire ship and the full cost of launching as part of the mission, paying only for one of its astronauts.  According to the report of NASA OIG on the audit of the manned flight program / The Alpha Centauri Here are more interesting facts about the ISS: how to create a research bastion of humanity in space Commercial Crew Program A year before the last flight of the shuttle, NASA initiated the launch of the manned flight program.  Even then, the search for a replacement for space shuttles began, the launches of which were quite expensive for the state.  Then came the idea, which at that time was revolutionary and even strange: the delivery of astronauts to the ISS should be engaged in private space companies.  NASA in this scenario took over the control of the design and preparation for the launch and the payment of seats for astronauts.  Space Shuttle Atlantis 30 minutes after landing in the last flight of the program Finally, in 2014, two companies were selected that will continue to prepare and present manned ships that will be able to carry out the mission.  These companies are Boeing and SpaceX.  As for the first company, the launch of the Boeing Starliner was unsuccessful, despite the fact that the ship landed successfully.  The company was unable to ensure the docking of the ship with the ISS due to a number of errors.  Now Boeing is engaged in fixing all the problems and preparing for a new test launch, but for their money.  Boeing Starliner, after landing SpaceX in March 2020, successfully launched Crew Dragon, which has passed a number of tests and landed proving its ability to ensure the delivery of astronauts to the ISS.  After additional tests and final preparations, the ship was prepared for an important event - a manned launch, which will take place on May 27, 2020.  Crew Crew Dragon To the ISS will go two NASA astronauts: Robert "Bob" Benken and Douglas "Doug" Gurley.  Both of them were test pilots and together in 2000 got to NASA as part of the 18th selection of astronauts.  Robert "Bob" Benken and Douglas "Dag" Gurley / NASA As for Robert Benken, during his time at NASA, he took part in two missions of the shuttle Endeavour: STS-123 (2008) and STS-130 (2010).  As part of these missions, Benken had three spacewalks.  Astronaut Robert Benken During the Demo-2 flight, Robert Benken will take command of the flight stages that will be coordinated by the mission control center.  Douglas Gurley also participated in two missions of the shuttle Endevour on missions STS-127 (2009) and STS-135 (2011).  In both missions, Gurley was a shuttle pilot, and STS-135 was the last mission to complete the space shuttle program.  During the Demo-2 flight, Douglas Hurley will be the commander of the ship and responsible for all procedures related to the launch and landing of the Crew Dragon spacecraft.  As already noted, the launch of the Crew Dragon is scheduled for May 27.  It is worth noting that the mission can still be postponed.  The reasons for this may be, as detected at the last moment technical problems or the weather, which should be favorable not only at the launch site, but also throughout the flight path of the Falcon 9 rocket.  Because in these places must pass the splashdown of the crew, if something went wrong at the time of launch or flight.  The ship Crew Dragon / SpaceX Now it is known that if the launch does not take place on May 27, then it can be postponed both on May 30 and on May 31.  If everything goes according to plan and the ship successfully enters orbit, it will spend about 19 hours there.  This is necessary for additional tests and maneuvers as part of the test – Crew Dragon can get to the ISS much faster.  In orbit, the astronauts will check the operation of all systems, switch to manual control, perform several maneuvers and eventually experience how comfortable Crew Dragon is for sleeping.  Docking with the IDA-2 node of the Harmony module on the ISS is scheduled for May 28 at about 15: 39 UTC (18: 39 Kyiv time).  Before that, the astronauts will approach the ISS and conduct several maneuvers near the station.  It is worth noting that the entire docking process with the ISS will take place automatically.  Astronauts will observe the process and will be able to intercept control in case of an emergency.  After the crew of Crew Dragon will get to the station, he will meet with members of the 63rd expedition - Chris Cassidy, Anatoly Ivanishin and Ivan Wagner.  As noted at the beginning of the material, the duration of stay of astronauts on the ISS is still unknown.  It will finally be determined during the flight, taking into account the state of the Crew Dragon ship and the readiness of the next Crew Dragon capsule, which is already designed for flight as part of the first full-fledged mission.  Let me remind you that despite the manned flight, this is still a test flight.  In addition, NASA expects to keep Demo-2 in orbit for as long as possible.  It is necessary for that.  after returning to finish the certification of the ship and begin preparations for the next mission.  In general, Demo-2 has every chance to stay in orbit for up to 120 days.  Rehearsal of the launch of Demo-2 / SpaceX Here it is worth noting that this limitation is due to the peculiarity of the design of the Crew Dragon.  In particular, it is said about solar panels, which gradually deteriorate during their stay in orbit due to the concentration of atomic oxygen.  The next Crew Dragon ships already have a protective coating of silicon dioxide, which will allow them to stay in orbit for all 210 days.  Whatever it was, and after the expiration of their stay on the ISS, the astronauts will return to the ship, undock and land in the waters of the Atlantic Ocean near the coast of Florida. Title: SpaceX successfully launches manned space capsule
Content: On Saturday, space exploration technology company SpaceX launched its first crew Dragon, a critical flight to prove to NASA the safety of astronauts in future flights.  The mission, called Demo-1, was launched on a Falcon 9 rocket from the Kennedy Air Center in California.  This space capsule does not carry a human, but a model of an astronaut called Ripley, wearing sensors to measure various indicators of the human body in the space capsule.  This is the first of two SpaceX test flights under NASA ’ s Commercial Crew Program. Demo-2 will be the first to fly with a human pilot, scheduled for July of this year.  According to NASA ’ s plan, SpaceX will be the first company to send astronauts into space since 2011.  NASA Administrator Jim Bridenstine later stated that the successful launch marked a new chapter in American excellence, bringing us once again closer to carrying American astronauts from American soil on American rockets.  Since the retirement of the Space Shuttle in 2011, the United States has been unable to use its own rockets to transport astronauts to space on its own. NASA is working with private companies to develop the future of human spaceflight.  Currently, SpaceX and NASA have a contract value of $2.6 billion, and Boeing is $4.2 billion.

Title: NASA has agreed to reuse the Dragon capsule.
Content: As part of its plans to send a man to the moon, NASA announced that it would re-use SpaceX ’ s Dragon capsule.  NASA has announced that it will allow SpaceX to re-use its Dragon capsule and Falcon 9 rocket in the near future.  The Dragon capsule recently sent two American astronauts to the International Space Station from the United States.  The launch was from NASA ’ s Kennedy Space Center (KSC) in Florida, which has been used for other missions, including Apollo.  The Demo-2 mission was a successful test flight.  In a statement, NASA said: “While this is not unexpected, it is an important step for NASA ’ s commercial manned programs that have led the United States to return to power and fly space from its soil. ”  According to NASA ’ s contract with SpaceX, the company has been allowed to reuse both its Falcon 9 and its Dragon.  The revised contract will allow SpaceX to carry out its second operational mission, known as PCM-2 or Crew-2.  The change is intended as part of a bilateral reform plan that formally extends the Demo-2 mission from two weeks to 119 days.  The Dragon capsule is said to be reused in 2021.  On SpaceX ’ s recent historic mission, Doug Harley and Bob Behenken were sent into orbit aboard the Dragon capsule.  About 19 hours later, the Crew Dragon capsule was automatically attached to the International Space Station to make the first successful journey to the orbital station from a US-based space station since the space shuttle's retirement in 2011.  End of message.

Title: The launch of the ship Crew Dragon – NASA flight: date, all that is known
Content: Already this week, SpaceX ’ s Crew Dragon spacecraft will go to the ISS as part of the Demo-2 test mission.  The launch will mark the return of the United States to manned flights, which ended with the closure of the Space Shuttle program in 2011.  How the mission will take place and why it is important, we tell in our material.  Channel 24 closely followed the process of preparation for the manned launch of the manned spacecraft Crew Dragon.  We decided to collect all the details and interesting points in one article so that you could get acquainted with the key stages of the mission.  Do not miss the US returning to the ISS: SpaceX and NASA have revealed the details of the historic mission What is happening The United States of America is returning to manned flights to the ISS using its own ships.  Already this week, on May 27, the first ever manned launch of a spacecraft to the ISS, carried out by a private company SpaceX, will take place.  Crew Dragon will have two American astronauts on board.  After launch, the ship docks with the International Space Station at an altitude of 400 kilometers above the surface of the planet.  The astronauts will get to the station, where they will continue their mission, the duration of which is not yet known and will depend on a number of factors, both during the launch and during the flight of the ship until the moment of docking with the ISS.  Despite the fact that the flight is manned, and the mission of astronauts will take a lot of time on the ISS, it is still a test, so it is called Demo-2.  Previously, SpaceX has already tested the ship Crew Dragon, but this time the company will do it for the first time as part of a crewed mission.  The broadcast of the flight will take place on Techno 24.  So visit our website on May 27 at 23: 15.  The start is scheduled for 23: 30 in Kiev.  In addition, the broadcast will be available here: NASA TV: YouTube; SpaceX: YouTube link to the broadcast will be available before launch.  The fact is that the manned launch of Demo-2 will be the first such launch from American soil in almost a decade.  The last manned spacecraft to perform such a mission was the Space Shuttle Atlantis, which landed on July 21, 2011 as part of the STS-135 mission.  After that, the shuttles to the ISS no longer flew, and NASA was forced to buy seats for its astronauts on the Russian Soyuz, which cost the United States a considerable amount.  It is worth paying attention to the fact that after the American shuttles stopped flying, Russia constantly raised the price of seats for American astronauts and other partners on board the Soyuz spacecraft.  As of today, one seat on the Soyuz costs NASA $90 million (in 2010 it cost about $30 million).  The Alpha Centauri portal notes that given the approximate prices of Russian state launch contracts, it turns out that NASA pays the entire ship and the full cost of launching as part of the mission, paying only for one of its astronauts.  According to the report of NASA OIG on the audit of the manned flight program / The Alpha Centauri Here are more interesting facts about the ISS: how to create a research bastion of humanity in space Commercial Crew Program A year before the last flight of the shuttle, NASA initiated the launch of the manned flight program.  Even then, the search for a replacement for space shuttles began, the launches of which were quite expensive for the state.  Then came the idea, which at that time was revolutionary and even strange: the delivery of astronauts to the ISS should be engaged in private space companies.  NASA in this scenario took over the control of the design and preparation for the launch and the payment of seats for astronauts.  Space Shuttle Atlantis 30 minutes after landing in the last flight of the program Finally, in 2014, two companies were selected that will continue to prepare and present manned ships that will be able to carry out the mission.  These companies are Boeing and SpaceX.  As for the first company, the launch of the Boeing Starliner was unsuccessful, despite the fact that the ship landed successfully.  The company was unable to ensure the docking of the ship with the ISS due to a number of errors.  Now Boeing is engaged in fixing all the problems and preparing for a new test launch, but for their money.  Boeing Starliner, after landing SpaceX in March 2020, successfully launched Crew Dragon, which has passed a number of tests and landed proving its ability to ensure the delivery of astronauts to the ISS.  After additional tests and final preparations, the ship was prepared for an important event - a manned launch, which will take place on May 27, 2020.  Crew Crew Dragon To the ISS will go two NASA astronauts: Robert "Bob" Benken and Douglas "Doug" Gurley.  Both of them were test pilots and together in 2000 got to NASA as part of the 18th selection of astronauts.  Robert "Bob" Benken and Douglas "Dag" Gurley / NASA As for Robert Benken, during his time at NASA, he took part in two missions of the shuttle Endeavour: STS-123 (2008) and STS-130 (2010).  As part of these missions, Benken had three spacewalks.  Astronaut Robert Benken During the Demo-2 flight, Robert Benken will take command of the flight stages that will be coordinated by the mission control center.  Douglas Gurley also participated in two missions of the shuttle Endevour on missions STS-127 (2009) and STS-135 (2011).  In both missions, Gurley was a shuttle pilot, and STS-135 was the last mission to complete the space shuttle program.  During the Demo-2 flight, Douglas Hurley will be the commander of the ship and responsible for all procedures related to the launch and landing of the Crew Dragon spacecraft.  As already noted, the launch of the Crew Dragon is scheduled for May 27.  It is worth noting that the mission can still be postponed.  The reasons for this may be, as detected at the last moment technical problems or the weather, which should be favorable not only at the launch site, but also throughout the flight path of the Falcon 9 rocket.  Because in these places must pass the splashdown of the crew, if something went wrong at the time of launch or flight.  The ship Crew Dragon / SpaceX Now it is known that if the launch does not take place on May 27, then it can be postponed both on May 30 and on May 31.  If everything goes according to plan and the ship successfully enters orbit, it will spend about 19 hours there.  This is necessary for additional tests and maneuvers as part of the test – Crew Dragon can get to the ISS much faster.  In orbit, the astronauts will check the operation of all systems, switch to manual control, perform several maneuvers and eventually experience how comfortable Crew Dragon is for sleeping.  Docking with the IDA-2 node of the Harmony module on the ISS is scheduled for May 28 at about 15: 39 UTC (18: 39 Kyiv time).  Before that, the astronauts will approach the ISS and conduct several maneuvers near the station.  It is worth noting that the entire docking process with the ISS will take place automatically.  Astronauts will observe the process and will be able to intercept control in case of an emergency.  After the crew of Crew Dragon will get to the station, he will meet with members of the 63rd expedition - Chris Cassidy, Anatoly Ivanishin and Ivan Wagner.  As noted at the beginning of the material, the duration of stay of astronauts on the ISS is still unknown.  It will finally be determined during the flight, taking into account the state of the Crew Dragon ship and the readiness of the next Crew Dragon capsule, which is already designed for flight as part of the first full-fledged mission.  Let me remind you that despite the manned flight, this is still a test flight.  In addition, NASA expects to keep Demo-2 in orbit for as long as possible.  It is necessary for that.  after returning to finish the certification of the ship and begin preparations for the next mission.  In general, Demo-2 has every chance to stay in orbit for up to 120 days.  Rehearsal of the launch of Demo-2 / SpaceX Here it is worth noting that this limitation is due to the peculiarity of the design of the Crew Dragon.  In particular, it is said about solar panels, which gradually deteriorate during their stay in orbit due to the concentration of atomic oxygen.  The next Crew Dragon ships already have a protective coating of silicon dioxide, which will allow them to stay in orbit for all 210 days.  Whatever it was, and after the expiration of their stay on the ISS, the astronauts will return to the ship, undock and land in the waters of the Atlantic Ocean near the coast of Florida.  There the crew of the ship and the capsule itself will pick up the ship SpaceX Navigator. Title: The launch of the ship Crew Dragon – NASA flight: date, all that is known
Content: Already this week, SpaceX ’ s Crew Dragon spacecraft will go to the ISS as part of the Demo-2 test mission.  The launch will mark the return of the United States to manned flights, which ended with the closure of the Space Shuttle program in 2011.  How the mission will take place and why it is important, we tell in our material.  Channel 24 closely followed the process of preparation for the manned launch of the manned spacecraft Crew Dragon.  We decided to collect all the details and interesting points in one article so that you could get acquainted with the key stages of the mission.  Do not miss the US returning to the ISS: SpaceX and NASA have revealed the details of the historic mission What is happening The United States of America is returning to manned flights to the ISS using its own ships.  Already this week, on May 27, the first ever manned launch of a spacecraft to the ISS, carried out by a private company SpaceX, will take place.  Crew Dragon will have two American astronauts on board.  After launch, the ship docks with the International Space Station at an altitude of 400 kilometers above the surface of the planet.  The astronauts will get to the station, where they will continue their mission, the duration of which is not yet known and will depend on a number of factors, both during the launch and during the flight of the ship until the moment of docking with the ISS.  Despite the fact that the flight is manned, and the mission of astronauts will take a lot of time on the ISS, it is still a test, so it is called Demo-2.  Previously, SpaceX has already tested the ship Crew Dragon, but this time the company will do it for the first time as part of a crewed mission.  The broadcast of the flight will take place on Techno 24.  So visit our website on May 27 at 23: 15.  The start is scheduled for 23: 30 in Kiev.  In addition, the broadcast will be available here: NASA TV: YouTube; SpaceX: YouTube link to the broadcast will be available before launch.  The fact is that the manned launch of Demo-2 will be the first such launch from American soil in almost a decade.  The last manned spacecraft to perform such a mission was the Space Shuttle Atlantis, which landed on July 21, 2011 as part of the STS-135 mission.  After that, the shuttles to the ISS no longer flew, and NASA was forced to buy seats for its astronauts on the Russian Soyuz, which cost the United States a considerable amount.  It is worth paying attention to the fact that after the American shuttles stopped flying, Russia constantly raised the price of seats for American astronauts and other partners on board the Soyuz spacecraft.  As of today, one seat on the Soyuz costs NASA $90 million (in 2010 it cost about $30 million).  The Alpha Centauri portal notes that given the approximate prices of Russian state launch contracts, it turns out that NASA pays the entire ship and the full cost of launching as part of the mission, paying only for one of its astronauts.  According to the report of NASA OIG on the audit of the manned flight program / The Alpha Centauri Here are more interesting facts about the ISS: how to create a research bastion of humanity in space Commercial Crew Program A year before the last flight of the shuttle, NASA initiated the launch of the manned flight program.  Even then, the search for a replacement for space shuttles began, the launches of which were quite expensive for the state.  Then came the idea, which at that time was revolutionary and even strange: the delivery of astronauts to the ISS should be engaged in private space companies.  NASA in this scenario took over the control of the design and preparation for the launch and the payment of seats for astronauts.  Space Shuttle Atlantis 30 minutes after landing in the last flight of the program Finally, in 2014, two companies were selected that will continue to prepare and present manned ships that will be able to carry out the mission.  These companies are Boeing and SpaceX.  As for the first company, the launch of the Boeing Starliner was unsuccessful, despite the fact that the ship landed successfully.  The company was unable to ensure the docking of the ship with the ISS due to a number of errors.  Now Boeing is engaged in fixing all the problems and preparing for a new test launch, but for their money.  Boeing Starliner, after landing SpaceX in March 2020, successfully launched Crew Dragon, which has passed a number of tests and landed proving its ability to ensure the delivery of astronauts to the ISS.  After additional tests and final preparations, the ship was prepared for an important event - a manned launch, which will take place on May 27, 2020.  Crew Crew Dragon To the ISS will go two NASA astronauts: Robert "Bob" Benken and Douglas "Doug" Gurley.  Both of them were test pilots and together in 2000 got to NASA as part of the 18th selection of astronauts.  Robert "Bob" Benken and Douglas "Dag" Gurley / NASA As for Robert Benken, during his time at NASA, he took part in two missions of the shuttle Endeavour: STS-123 (2008) and STS-130 (2010).  As part of these missions, Benken had three spacewalks.  Astronaut Robert Benken During the Demo-2 flight, Robert Benken will take command of the flight stages that will be coordinated by the mission control center.  Douglas Gurley also participated in two missions of the shuttle Endevour on missions STS-127 (2009) and STS-135 (2011).  In both missions, Gurley was a shuttle pilot, and STS-135 was the last mission to complete the space shuttle program.  During the Demo-2 flight, Douglas Hurley will be the commander of the ship and responsible for all procedures related to the launch and landing of the Crew Dragon spacecraft.  As already noted, the launch of the Crew Dragon is scheduled for May 27.  It is worth noting that the mission can still be postponed.  The reasons for this may be, as detected at the last moment technical problems or the weather, which should be favorable not only at the launch site, but also throughout the flight path of the Falcon 9 rocket.  Because in these places must pass the splashdown of the crew, if something went wrong at the time of launch or flight.  The ship Crew Dragon / SpaceX Now it is known that if the launch does not take place on May 27, then it can be postponed both on May 30 and on May 31.  If everything goes according to plan and the ship successfully enters orbit, it will spend about 19 hours there.  This is necessary for additional tests and maneuvers as part of the test – Crew Dragon can get to the ISS much faster.  In orbit, the astronauts will check the operation of all systems, switch to manual control, perform several maneuvers and eventually experience how comfortable Crew Dragon is for sleeping.  Docking with the IDA-2 node of the Harmony module on the ISS is scheduled for May 28 at about 15: 39 UTC (18: 39 Kyiv time).  Before that, the astronauts will approach the ISS and conduct several maneuvers near the station.  It is worth noting that the entire docking process with the ISS will take place automatically.  Astronauts will observe the process and will be able to intercept control in case of an emergency.  After the crew of Crew Dragon will get to the station, he will meet with members of the 63rd expedition - Chris Cassidy, Anatoly Ivanishin and Ivan Wagner.  As noted at the beginning of the material, the duration of stay of astronauts on the ISS is still unknown.  It will finally be determined during the flight, taking into account the state of the Crew Dragon ship and the readiness of the next Crew Dragon capsule, which is already designed for flight as part of the first full-fledged mission.  Let me remind you that despite the manned flight, this is still a test flight.  In addition, NASA expects to keep Demo-2 in orbit for as long as possible. In particular, it is said about solar panels, which gradually deteriorate during their stay in orbit due to the concentration of atomic oxygen.  The next Crew Dragon ships already have a protective coating of silicon dioxide, which will allow them to stay in orbit for all 210 days.  Whatever it was, and after the expiration of their stay on the ISS, the astronauts will return to the ship, undock and land in the waters of the Atlantic Ocean near the coast of Florida. passages.title: Ontario court: Iran ’ s shooting down of Ukrainian plane was ‘ intentional ’ and ‘ terrorist ’
passages.passage: One year and four months after the Iranian Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) shot down Ukraine International Airlines Flight 752, Ontario ’ s Supreme Court on Thursday, May 20, called the shooting down of Ukrainian aircraft by Iran an “intentional ” and a“ terrorist ” act.  Ontario Supreme Court Justice Edward Billubaba announced in a ruling Thursday, May 20, that the downing of the Ukrainian plane PS752 over Tehran was "deliberate" and "terrorist".  The Ontario Supreme Court ruled that “the plaintiffs in this case have proved that the downing of Flight 752 by Iran was a deliberate act of terrorism. ”  In his ruling, he also condemned the Iranian government to pay compensation to the families of the victims of the Ukrainian plane that was shot down by the Islamic Republic ’ s Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) defense over Tehran.  The Supreme Court of Ontario of Canada has issued a ruling in the case of four relatives of the passengers of the Ukrainian plane who are officials of the Islamic Republic of Iran.  Shahin Moghadam, Shakiba Faghaati ’ s wife and Rustin Moghadam ’ s father, Mehrzad Zarei, Arad Zarei ’ s father, Ali Gorji ’ s uncle, and another member of the families of the victims, who did not want to be named, are four plaintiffs in the case.  In their complaint to the Ontario Supreme Court, they named Ali Khamenei, the Supreme Leader of the Islamic Republic of Iran, and several top Revolutionary Guard commanders.  In a statement, the four lawyers, Mark and Jonah Arnold, described the Supreme Court ruling as “unprecedented. ”  They stressed that the sentence would have "a significant impact on the relatives of the victims who seek justice."  According to the two lawyers, four plaintiffs in the case have asked Iran for 1 million euros in compensation.  Ukraine International Airlines Flight PS752 was shot down on January 8, 2021 after two IRGC missiles were fired over Tehran.  All 176 people on board, dual Iranian-Canadian citizens as well as citizens of Afghanistan, Britain, Germany, Sweden and Ukraine, were killed in the crash.  The crash of Ukraine Airlines Flight 752 occurred just four hours before Iran attacked U.S. military bases in response to the killing of former Quds commander Qasem Soleimani in Iraq.  Canadian broadcaster CBC reported on Saturday, July 4, that it had obtained a 90-minute audio file.  According to the network, Tehran ’ s sky was open at the time of the shooting down of the Ukrainian plane so that the plan of the IRGC ’ s attack on US military bases in Iraq would not be revealed.  The Iranian authorities, after publishing evidence and documents by Canada, the United States, Australia and the United Kingdom, finally declared "human error" after three days of concealment.  One year and four months after the downing of Ukraine International Airlines Flight PS752 by the Islamic Republic of Iran ’ s Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), the families of the victims refuse to accept the claims of the Iranian authorities and call for the identification and prosecution of the perpetrators. passages.title: Canadian court: Iran ’ s downing of Ukraine Flight 752 was an act of terror – Radio France Internationale
passages.passage: OTTAWA (AFP) - A Canadian court today ruled that the shooting down of Ukrainian International Airlines flight PS752 by Iranian forces early last year was a deliberate "terrorist act" and that the decision will pave the way for possible compensation for the families of the victims.  On January 8, Ukraine International Airlines Flight PS752 crashed near Tehran, killing all 176 people on board, including 85 Canadian citizens and permanent residents.  Iran initially denied the Western accusations, but three days later admitted that the Iranian military shot down the other side "unintentionally".  The Ontario Superior Court of Justice in Canada said it had determined, after "weighing the odds," that the plane was hit by two missiles shortly after take-off in Tehran, as a result of a "deliberate" act.  Judge Edward Belobaba also ruled that “the plaintiff ’ s claim that the shooting down of Flight 752 was an act of terrorism. ”  The plaintiffs ’ lawyers called the ruling “unprecedented in Canadian law. ”  "This will have a significant impact on the immediate families of the victims seeking justice," they said in a statement.  The lawsuit, filed by the families of the four victims, seeks 1.5 billion Canadian dollars (about NT $35.3 billion).  They claim that Iran launched the missile attack in retaliation for the US killing of Qasem Soleimani, the commander of the Quds Force of the Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps, near Baghdad airport in Iraq, days before the crash.  A final report released in March by the Iran Civil Aviation Organisation said the missile attack and the "vigilant" response of ground forces were the result of high tensions between Iran and the United States at the time.  Eleven Ukrainian citizens were killed in the crash.  The Ukrainian side pointed out that behind the report there was a "ridiculous attempt to cover up the real cause", while Canada said the report contained "no strong facts or evidence" and promised to publish its findings soon.  Iran did not defend itself in court, but three days after the crash admitted that Iranian forces shot down the Boeing 737-800 bound for Kiev.  The court will then decide on the amount of compensation. © 2021 AFP

Title: Ontario court: Iran ’ s shooting down of Ukrainian plane was ‘ intentional ’ and ‘ terrorist ’
Content: One year and four months after the Iranian Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) shot down Ukraine International Airlines Flight 752, Ontario ’ s Supreme Court on Thursday, May 20, called the shooting down of Ukrainian aircraft by Iran an “intentional ” and a“ terrorist ” act.  Ontario Supreme Court Justice Edward Billubaba announced in a ruling Thursday, May 20, that the downing of the Ukrainian plane PS752 over Tehran was "deliberate" and "terrorist".  The Ontario Supreme Court ruled that “the plaintiffs in this case have proved that the downing of Flight 752 by Iran was a deliberate act of terrorism. ”  In his ruling, he also condemned the Iranian government to pay compensation to the families of the victims of the Ukrainian plane that was shot down by the Islamic Republic ’ s Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) defense over Tehran.  The Supreme Court of Ontario of Canada has issued a ruling in the case of four relatives of the passengers of the Ukrainian plane who are officials of the Islamic Republic of Iran.  Shahin Moghadam, Shakiba Faghaati ’ s wife and Rustin Moghadam ’ s father, Mehrzad Zarei, Arad Zarei ’ s father, Ali Gorji ’ s uncle, and another member of the families of the victims, who did not want to be named, are four plaintiffs in the case.  In their complaint to the Ontario Supreme Court, they named Ali Khamenei, the Supreme Leader of the Islamic Republic of Iran, and several top Revolutionary Guard commanders. Content: One year and four months after the Iranian Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) shot down Ukraine International Airlines Flight 752, Ontario ’ s Supreme Court on Thursday, May 20, called the shooting down of Ukrainian aircraft by Iran an “intentional ” and a“ terrorist ” act.  Ontario Supreme Court Justice Edward Billubaba announced in a ruling Thursday, May 20, that the downing of the Ukrainian plane PS752 over Tehran was "deliberate" and "terrorist".  The Ontario Supreme Court ruled that “the plaintiffs in this case have proved that the downing of Flight 752 by Iran was a deliberate act of terrorism. ”  In his ruling, he also condemned the Iranian government to pay compensation to the families of the victims of the Ukrainian plane that was shot down by the Islamic Republic ’ s Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) defense over Tehran.  The Supreme Court of Ontario of Canada has issued a ruling in the case of four relatives of the passengers of the Ukrainian plane who are officials of the Islamic Republic of Iran.  Shahin Moghadam, Shakiba Faghaati ’ s wife and Rustin Moghadam ’ s father, Mehrzad Zarei, Arad Zarei ’ s father, Ali Gorji ’ s uncle, and another member of the families of the victims, who did not want to be named, are four plaintiffs in the case.  In their complaint to the Ontario Supreme Court, they named Ali Khamenei, the Supreme Leader of the Islamic Republic of Iran, and several top Revolutionary Guard commanders.  In a statement, the four lawyers, Mark and Jonah Arnold, described the Supreme Court ruling as “unprecedented. ”  They stressed that the sentence would have "a significant impact on the relatives of the victims who seek justice."  According to the two lawyers, four plaintiffs in the case have asked Iran for 1 million euros in compensation.  Ukraine International Airlines Flight PS752 was shot down on January 8, 2021 after two IRGC missiles were fired over Tehran.  All 176 people on board, dual Iranian-Canadian citizens as well as citizens of Afghanistan, Britain, Germany, Sweden and Ukraine, were killed in the crash.  The crash of Ukraine Airlines Flight 752 occurred just four hours before Iran attacked U.S. military bases in response to the killing of former Quds commander Qasem Soleimani in Iraq.  Canadian broadcaster CBC reported on Saturday, July 4, that it had obtained a 90-minute audio file.  According to the network, Tehran ’ s sky was open at the time of the shooting down of the Ukrainian plane so that the plan of the IRGC ’ s attack on US military bases in Iraq would not be revealed.  The Iranian authorities, after publishing evidence and documents by Canada, the United States, Australia and the United Kingdom, finally declared "human error" after three days of concealment.  One year and four months after the downing of Ukraine International Airlines Flight PS752 by the Islamic Republic of Iran ’ s Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), the families of the victims refuse to accept the claims of the Iranian authorities and call for the identification and prosecution of the perpetrators. Title: Families of Ukrainian plane victims: Canadian report reveals Islamic Republic ’ s crimes, secrecy and lies
Content: Last year, a Ukrainian passenger plane, minutes after flying from Tehran airport, was hit by two IRGC air defense missiles, killing all 176 people on board. The Islamic Republic ’ s regime was obliged to clearly reveal the causes of the flight ’ s shooting down in a detailed report in cooperation with the affected countries.  The Islamic Republic has so far refused to do so.  Canada ’ s decision to conduct an investigation is an important step, but it is not enough and cannot come to a final conclusion on the events that took place on January 8.  The statement goes on to say that the report clearly states that the experts did not have access to witnesses and documents.  The Government of Canada should strive to bring those responsible to justice and bring justice to the victims and their families.  Even without access to much important information, the report demonstrates the Islamic Republic ’ s refusal to carry out its investigation and its insubordination to international law.  The Family Association of the Victims of the Ukrainian Airliner described the conclusions of Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau, who said in the report “a reference to the secrecy, lack of accountability, lack of cooperation and lack of transparency in the behavior of the Islamic Republic ” and continued:“ The urgent need to hold the highest officials of the Islamic Republic accountable is one of these. ”  The Canadian report contains several key points that clearly document the Islamic Republic ’ s crimes, secrecy and lies.  First, it rejects the Islamic Republic ’ s claim of “human error ” and considers it unreasonable and considers senior officials of the Islamic Republic to be the perpetrators.  Nor is it credible to claim that this crime was committed by a low-level operator who refused to perform his duties and was misjudged.  An operator who committed this crime without any connection to the military command center.  The report points to the possible involvement of senior military and other government officials in the shooting down of the flight.  The report said that although the firing of the missile may have been delegated to a low-level authority, "... the system operator may not fire without orders from the commander."  According to the Ukrainian Aircraft Victims Association, the Canadian report asserts that “there is no evidence of electronic warfare or interference in communications signals.  And this conclusion is in violation of the Islamic Republic ’ s claim that it interferes with the call of its operator and commander. ”  “It is important to note that Canada ’ s report concluded that the basis for this crime is found at the highest levels of strategic decision-making and national security of the Islamic Republic, and it is likely that the Supreme Leader of the Islamic Republic and the Supreme National Security Council made these decisions. ”  In response to the publication of the Canadian government ’ s investigation into the Ukrainian plane, Mohsen Baharvand, deputy foreign minister of the Islamic Republic of Iran, said: “As we can see, the Canadians have also confirmed that the shooting of the plane was not intentional. ”  Iran ’ s Deputy Foreign Minister added, “As is easily verifiable, in the technical comments we have officially received from Canada, there are no such general and unintelligible comments as they have just said. ”  Commenting on the Canadian prime minister ’ s threat to refer the case to the International Court of Justice, Baharvand said: “These premature statements are said more than they have a basis in the real world of the aviation industry because of the pressures that Canadian politicians themselves are the source of.  They expected to create a position for themselves in public opinion, which they could not. ”  The Canadian forensic team released its report on Flight PS752 after eight months of investigation, stressing that Iran had “failed ” to provide a“ credible explanation of how and why ” it shot down the passenger plane.  Canadian broadcaster CBC said there was no evidence in the country ’ s forensic investigation into the destruction of the Ukrainian plane, but that does not in any way diminish the Islamic Republic ’ s responsibility in this regard.  At the same time, the prime minister stressed that Canada is pursuing the case with all available options. Title: Canadian court: Iran ’ s downing of Ukraine Flight 752 was an act of terror – Radio France Internationale
Content: OTTAWA (AFP) - A Canadian court today ruled that the shooting down of Ukrainian International Airlines flight PS752 by Iranian forces early last year was a deliberate "terrorist act" and that the decision will pave the way for possible compensation for the families of the victims.  On January 8, Ukraine International Airlines Flight PS752 crashed near Tehran, killing all 176 people on board, including 85 Canadian citizens and permanent residents.  Iran initially denied the Western accusations, but three days later admitted that the Iranian military shot down the other side "unintentionally".  The Ontario Superior Court of Justice in Canada said it had determined, after "weighing the odds," that the plane was hit by two missiles shortly after take-off in Tehran, as a result of a "deliberate" act.  Judge Edward Belobaba also ruled that “the plaintiff ’ s claim that the shooting down of Flight 752 was an act of terrorism. ”  The plaintiffs ’ lawyers called the ruling “unprecedented in Canadian law. ”  "This will have a significant impact on the immediate families of the victims seeking justice," they said in a statement.  The lawsuit, filed by the families of the four victims, seeks 1.5 billion Canadian dollars (about NT $35.3 billion).  They claim that Iran launched the missile attack in retaliation for the US killing of Qasem Soleimani, the commander of the Quds Force of the Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps, near Baghdad airport in Iraq, days before the crash.  A final report released in March by the Iran Civil Aviation Organisation said the missile attack and the "vigilant" response of ground forces were the result of high tensions between Iran and the United States at the time.  Eleven Ukrainian citizens were killed in the crash.  The Ukrainian side pointed out that behind the report there was a "ridiculous attempt to cover up the real cause", while Canada said the report contained "no strong facts or evidence" and promised to publish its findings soon.  Iran did not defend itself in court, but three days after the crash admitted that Iranian forces shot down the Boeing 737-800 bound for Kiev.  The court will then decide on the amount of compensation. © 2021 AFP

Title: Ukraine Threatens Iran with International Court of Justice
Content: Ukraine may file a lawsuit with the International Court of Justice if negotiations with Iran over the downed Boeing 737-800 of Ukraine International Airlines (UIA) near Tehran are unsuccessful.  This was stated by Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs of Ukraine Yevgeny Yenin in an interview with Radio Liberty.  “If negotiations reach a deadlock, we will be forced to resort to international arbitration, in particular the International Court of Justice.  We are talking not only about Ukraine, but about a united front of the states of Canada, Great Britain, Sweden, Afghanistan and Ukraine, ” Yenin threatened.  He expressed hope that Iran will fulfill its international obligations and hand over the black boxes for their decoding.  Yenin stressed that there are not so many states in the world today that have the necessary software.  The diplomat said that the issue of conducting an examination in France has already been worked out.  In mid-February, Iranian Foreign Minister Mohammad Javad Zarif said that the country does not have the technical capabilities to decipher the black boxes.  Minval.az

Title: The crash of the MAU plane. Ukraine, Canada, Sweden and the UK put forward demands on Iran
Content: The crash of the MAU plane.  Ukraine, Canada, Sweden and the United Kingdom put forward demands to Iran “The actions and inaction of the Islamic Republic of Iran are a violation of international law.  Our statement notes that our states, their citizens and residents on board flight PS752 suffered substantial and irreparable damage as a result of the tragedy, and Iran must fulfill its obligations to ensure full reparation to the group of states.  The signatories demand that Iran acknowledge the wrongdoing and provide a full account of the circumstances that led to the downing of the plane.  Also, the foreign ministers of Ukraine, Canada, Sweden and the United Kingdom demand a public apology, the return of the missing and stolen personal belongings of the victims, assurances of the prevention of such actions in the future, ensuring the transparency of the criminal investigation, as well as fair compensation to the families of those killed in the accident, regardless of nationality.  “We call on Iran to cooperate in order to determine the date of the official start of negotiations on reparations, which we will conduct in good faith, ” the authors of the appeal added.  Context: A Boeing 737-800 passenger plane of Ukraine International Airlines flight PS752, which was en route from Tehran to Kiev, crashed on January 8, 2020 near the capital of Iran.  There were 167 passengers and nine crew members on board.  No one survived.  Among the dead were 11 citizens of Ukraine.  Most of the passengers were citizens of Iran and Canada.  Iranian authorities, initially claiming that the plane crashed due to a technical malfunction, on January 11, under pressure from Western leaders, admitted that flight PS752 was shot down by an Iranian missile by mistake.  Deputy Foreign Minister of Ukraine Yevgeny Yenin July 23 said that the decryption of the black boxes, which was completed in France, confirmed the illegal interference in the work of the passenger liner.  On August 23, the Civil Aviation Organization of Iran released a series of data obtained from the onboard voice recorder and flight data recorder of the UIA aircraft.  According to the records, the crew knew about the emergency situation and tried to control the plane to the last.  The New York Times reported that Iranian Foreign Minister Javad Zarif gave an interview to Iranian economist Said Leilaz in March 2020.  In it, he admitted that the Iranian military immediately learned that the plane “International airlines of Ukraine ” was shot down.  Iran on February 20, 2021 announced the completion of the investigation of the disaster.  The Iranian prosecutor ’ s office accuses 10 people of involvement in the crash, among them the top military commanders of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.  The Minister of foreign Affairs of Ukraine Dmitry Kuleba called the report of Iran biased and promised to continue to seek punishment of Iran for this crime.  Yenin said that Ukraine will demand from Iran to continue the investigation.  The court of the Canadian province of Ontario on May 20 recognized the crash of the UIA airline as a deliberate terrorist act.  Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Saeed Khatibzadeh said the court had no jurisdiction to decide on a claim for damages in the plane crash because it occurred outside of Canada.  The National Security and Defense Council of Ukraine is inclined to believe that the crash of the UIA plane in Iran was a terrorist attack.  Tehran insists on the version of the unintentional shooting down of the plane.

passages.title: Russian fishing boat detained by North Korea for 10 days and 17 crew released
passages.passage: SEOUL, July 28, 2019 (AFP) The Russian Embassy in North Korea said today that North Korea has released a Russian fishing boat detained for violating immigration regulations.  The South Korean side confirmed that the fishing boat had arrived in Sokcho this afternoon.  The Russian Embassy in North Korea said on Thursday that North Korea had detained a fishing boat carrying 15 Russian and two South Korean crew members for violating entry rules.  Russia said the ship did not violate any regulations.  The embassy said in a Facebook post that the two South Korean crew members had also been released, adding that the boat had left Wonsan, North Korea, last night.  "The vessel has separated from the Kwon San port terminal at 7.30 pm (yesterday) and is headed for Sokcho, South Korea, where the two South Korean crew members will disembark."  The embassy said it would continue to investigate the "circumstances" of the vessel's detention.  South Korea's Unification Ministry, which handles relations between the two Koreas, welcomed the "safe release" of the fishing vessel, saying it was "a positive move from a humanitarian point of view." As for the return of the crew to their homeland, there are obstacles.  The fact is that all official authorities in China, which are engaged in the registration of documents necessary for repatriation, are now on forced holidays at least until the 10th, and maybe longer, ” Anikin said. Title: The crew of the ship “Patriot ” can not return from China to Russia due to the situation with the coronavirus
Content: Repatriation of the crew of the vessel “Patriot ”, which is located in the Chinese port of Ningde, is delayed due to the forced extended holidays with the authorities in China, which are engaged in the registration of documents for sailors.  As told TASS Deputy Director of the ship-owner "Hudson" Oleg Anikin, now "Patriot" is in the port of Ningde, where he came for repair, sailors are provided with everything necessary.  “We managed to agree on work with the shipyard, but due to the outbreak of pneumonia from the coronavirus, representatives of the plant are not yet able to start repairing, they do not even say when it will be possible.  As for the return of the crew to their homeland, there are obstacles.  The fact is that all official authorities in China, which are engaged in the registration of documents necessary for repatriation, are now on forced holidays at least until the 10th, and maybe longer, ” Anikin said.  According to him, the company has a prospect in terms of providing contracts for the work of its ships, which will allow in February to start paying seafarers debts.  In this, Hudson is assisted by a special commission of the Russian government, which was created to solve the problems of entrepreneurs who fell under American sanctions.  Earlier, the chairman of the Far Eastern regional organization of the Russian Seamen ’ s Trade Union Nikolai Sukhanov said that the crew of the Patriot appealed to the trade union with a request to assist in returning to their homeland.  During the stoppage at the port, the sailors complained of irregular supplies and non-payment of wages.  According to the Far Eastern Transport Prosecutor ’ s Office, the amount of debt on the salary of 19 crew members is 1.6 million rubles for November, December 2019 and January 2020.  Recall that in 2018, the United States Department of the Treasury announced the expansion of sanctions lists on the DPRK, which included the Russian-based shipping company Hudson.  In particular, the list includes six ships under the Russian flag: “Patriot ”,“ Neptune ”, “Bogatyr ”,“ Bella ”, “Partizan ” and“ Sevastopol ”.  According to the US authorities, they are involved “in the transfer of oil products to ships flying the flag of the DPRK, as well as activities prohibited by the UN Security Council. ”  The report of the UN expert group on the situation with the DPRK, which was published on the organization ’ s website on March 12, 2019, said that the experts did not receive from the United States evidence of pumping oil products from the company ’ s ship “Patriot ” to two North Korean tankers in January 2018, but so far the company is not excluded from the sanctions list.  After multiple detentions of ships and refusals of the company ’ s partners from contracts (in Hudson, this is associated with sanctions), employees of the shipping company wrote an open letter to the leadership of Russia in May last year, in which they asked to provide the company with monetary assistance and give access to government contracts in order to prevent bankruptcy.

title: Japan's Restarting of Whale Hunting

passages.title: Common ships will spend 6 billion yen to build new whaling mother ship
passages.passage: News from Japan (Kyodo News Agency, May 11) In the context of the commercial whaling that has resumed in Japan after 31 years in 2019, President Hideki So, the only company to carry out offshore operations, held a press conference in Tokyo on the 10th, announcing plans to spend about 6 billion yen (about 350 million yuan) to build a new whaling ship.  The company is optimistic that the Japanese government will expand the fishing quota and target sea areas in the future, and renovate the old mother ship.  Originally, it was "always said that it would cost more than 10 billion yen" (in the words of the president), but the cost was reduced by reducing the speed of the current mother ship "Nisin Maru".  It is expected to be completed in March 2024.  The government currently restricts commercial whaling to the exclusive economic zone (EEZ) of Japan, which covers only three species of minke whales, Bryde whales and Sei whales.  The new mother ship was also designed to operate outside the EEZ in the future. It can also catch large fin whales and ensure that it has the ability to reach the Antarctic waters.  The construction fee will not rely on subsidies, but will be obtained through crowdfunding through loans and online fundraising.  The president said that in order to guarantee the repayment of funds, "we hope to increase the amount of fishing in 2024."  He also stressed that the expansion of the whale meat market will be driven by higher wholesale prices and increased imports.  Japan withdrew from the International Whaling Commission (IWC) at the end of June 2019 and stopped its previous investigation of whaling activities.

passages.title: Withdrawal from the "cultural imperialist" Whaling Commission, Japan's diplomacy turned to "Trumpism"?
passages.passage: On July 1, Japan officially re-opened the "tradition" of commercial whaling for 31 years. 9 days ago, the first batch of whalers returned to the port, bringing back a total of more than a dozen baleen whales large and small.  From Kushiro, Hokkaido, south to Shimonoseki, Yamaguchi Prefecture, the whaling craze that has not been seen for a long time, whales are slaughtered and sold in various markets, attracting many people to come and buy.  In the Kushiro market, people who have tried it have a feeling of nostalgia in addition to admiring the delicious food.  On December 26, 2018, Japan announced that it would withdraw from the International Whaling Commission (IWC) after six months, and decided to reopen the commercial whaling route, prompting criticism from many countries.  At that time, there was also a debate in Japan that the government's decision-making process was not transparent, and the idea of reviewing whether to hunt whales was also repeated and fell into heated discussion for a time.  Japan's Minister of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries, Takayama Yoshikawa, said that the resumption of whaling was the "sad wish of the people involved in the national whaling" and that although Japan withdrew from the International Whaling Commission, it still hoped that Japan would rejoin as an observer in the future to express its concern for the development of the international fishing industry.  According to Article 65 of the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS), the conservation and management of cetaceans is to be determined by "appropriate international authorities".  Originally, the International Whaling Commission was responsible for this task, after Japan's withdrawal, there will be a future Japanese whaling ship triggered by the international case may be against the court, Yoshikawa said only that "whether it will go to both sides of the complaint, but also depends on the policy judgment of various countries", now I am afraid it is too early to say.  The International Whaling Commission was established in 1946 to focus on whale conservation around the world. Japan has a long tradition of whaling since the Edo period and is the world ’ s largest consumer of whales. During the recovery period at the end of World War II, whales were once used as a source of protein for a nutritious lunch.  However, after 1970, the world's whale population significantly reduced, in order to protect the whale population, the IWC interrupted commercial whaling in 1982, and Japan finally complied with the agreement to stop commercial whaling in 1988.  However, although there is no commercial whaling, Japan continues to carry out whaling activities under the name of “survey whaling ”, but in fact, there is still a lot of whale meat coming into the market. Although the quota for survey whaling is strictly limited, it is judged that there are still many illegal sales of whale meat that are privately caught.  The taste of raw whale meat is slightly hard. It is a bit like horse meat, and the fiber is thick. It is usually eaten with ground ginger.  This time, the Japanese government has also stressed the use of a fairly high standard, from the IWC official calculation method of "no bad impact in 100 years" of the three categories of minke whales, sei whales and cloth whales.  Unlike survey whaling in the Antarctic Sea and the North Pacific, Japan has resumed commercial whaling only off the coast of Japan.  However, according to the International Convention on the Control of Whaling, signed in Washington in 1946, these three species are still listed as threatened with extinction, so the Japanese decision still attracts strong criticism from conservation groups and other foreign media.  Photo Credit: Reuters / Tachih Image Preserving Whale Culture?  Although Japan says that whaling is inherent in its traditional culture, the overall whaling market has declined significantly since it withdrew from commercial whaling in 1988, with 383 whales captured in 2018, 40% less than in 2017.  In addition to not eating whales, many young people do not know that this species has been their traditional culture.  The president of the Japan Small Whaling Association, Berryman, said: "The expansion of new routes and financial austerity, or continue to explore."  Young people do not understand whales, and in the future, they hope to at least let the local people in the fishing port experience whale cuisine again. "After 31 years of no whaling, Japan's whaling industry aging is also quite obvious, and the operators only spent a lot of time repairing their boats and whaling habitat, and they also privately told the Japanese media when they left the port:" It is a fact that they are intertwined with hope and uneasy. "In addition, because of the inability to hunt whales for the past 31 years, the Japanese government has allocated a fixed subsidy to whalers every day. Now that whaling resumes, it is like they can“ feed themselves ” and the subsidy is likely to be cut or even cancelled in 2020.  The Wall Street Journal also published an article saying that Japan's foreign policy in the future is likely to adopt a harder "Trump" line, one is to restart commercial whaling for 31 years, and the other is to directly impose semiconductor export restrictions on South Korea, the article said: "For some Japanese nationalists, after withdrawing from the IWC, which is a symbol of cultural imperialism in Europe and the United States, it is also about national independence. Say a good claim.  This use of trade as a bargaining chip in international politics is also Trump ’ s usual trick, and the newspaper said that Japan also responded to “Trump flow. ”  In addition, the Japanese government has also invested about 1.9 billion yen (about 544 million Taiwan dollars) in the resumption of whale hunting for fishing grounds and technical support for decomposition.  However, if the next 10 years still rely on government funds to continue to invest, it will still be difficult to become a self-supporting industry.  While the Japanese government is advocating the resumption of whaling, in addition to the pressure of international disapproval, what is more cruel is that the next generation has no special ideas about whaling or not.
