passages.title: 【 News Classroom 】 Despite global criticism, when did Japan restart commercial whaling after 32 years? ｜ Hong Kong 01 ｜ The World Says
passages.passage: Japan officially withdrew from the International Whaling Commission (IWC) on Sunday (June 30), after 32 years to restart commercial whaling.  A number of whalers were greeted by local residents and sailed out of the harbour.  Japan is one of the few countries that still hunt whales. Today, let ’ s introduce Japan ’ s whaling history, the reasons for restarting whaling and the current state of the whaling industry.  A number of whaling vessels are moored at the wharf in Kushiro City, Hokkaido, waiting to sail. (Reuters) ↓ ↓ For more photos of whaling, please click to enlarge: + 4 + 3 + 2 Japan Whaling History Japan has a long history of whaling, which began in prehistoric times.  The word "fish" in the Nara period "Manye Collection" is an ancient Japanese word for whaling.  In the Edo period, whaling gradually became an industry. In addition to being used for food, various parts of the whale were fully utilized, such as whale oil as a pesticide, bone nata as carving, and ambergris as a perfume.  After World War II, Japan ’ s whaling industry soared due to food shortages and foreign exchange earnings. In the 1950s, Japan became the world ’ s largest whaling nation, with domestic consumption peaking at 233,000 tons in 1962.  In 1982, the IWC passed the Convention on the Prohibition of Commercial Whaling. Japan initially objected, but after the objection was rejected in 1986, Japan finally promised to gradually ban commercial whaling, and commercial whaling ceased in 1988.  However, commercial whaling does not mean that whaling will no longer be done. In fact, Japan has set up a new category of "survey whaling" to continue whaling on the grounds of "scientific research".  According to the report of the Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries, the annual consumption of whale meat in Japan since the 1990s has been about 2,000 to 6,000 tons, and the latest figure in 2018 totals 3,000 tons.  Japan has a long history of whaling, which has become an industry as early as the Edo period. (Getty Images) Revitalizing the economy with the help of Whaling Japan ’ s Small Whaling Association President Yoshinori Abe called the news of the resumption of commercial whaling “a shock of joy and a sense of limitlessness. ” Prosperity again.  Some areas that used to make a living from whaling also hope to revitalize the economy by restarting whale hunting, such as the Amikawa area in the east of Miyagi Prefecture, which was the base of the whaling port of that year.  After extensive damage during the Great East Japan Earthquake, residents hope to revive the local economy by reviving the whaling industry. A museum dedicated to introducing whaling culture is planned for April 2020 to attract visitors.  Whale meat is quite nutritious and has become an important food item for the Japanese since the end of World War II. (Reuters) Whale meat is not expensive, but it should be noted that since the 1970s, whaling in Japan has declined year by year, and today whale meat is no longer a common dish in Japan.  Compared to the annual consumption of 6 million tons of pork and chicken, only 3,000 tons of whale meat is really insignificant.  And interestingly, whale meat has not become expensive due to reduced availability.  In the Tokyo market price in 2018, the price of "red meat level 1" whale meat used for sashimi is 1,600 yen (about HK $110) per kilogram, and the price of "umu" whale meat used for high-grade smoked is 3,000 yen (about HK $210) per kilogram.  In fact, the price of salmon to tuna is about the price, can not say how expensive.  This means that the actual market demand for whale meat is not high.  Therefore, public opinion in Japan is worried that in the reality of low supply and demand, even if the resumption of whaling, it will be difficult to let this already sunset industry "rise back to life", and the desire to revitalize the regional economy will be difficult to achieve.  Whale meat sashimi, but in fact, the price of whale meat is not particularly expensive due to the low supply and demand. (Reuters) Possible political reasons behind this.  Including Prime Minister Shinzo Abe, the constituency of the former president of the ruling Liberal Democratic Party ’ s faction, the “Chi Shih Association ”, is a land of whaling.  Therefore, there are allegations that the government is strongly promoting the resumption of whale hunting in order to continue to gain the support of local residents.  However, whether it is for cultural, industrial or political reasons, the low supply and demand of whale meat and the low price of whale meat can not be ignored, and Japan will face condemnation from international environmental groups.

passages.title: Japan resumes commercial whaling, drawing strong international opposition
passages.passage: Image copyright AFP / Getty Images Image caption Japanese officials say eating whale meat is part of Japanese culture.  The Japanese government announced its withdrawal from the International Whaling Commission (IWC) and will resume commercial whaling in July 2019.  Such a move would attract strong criticism from the international community.  Japanese officials say eating whale meat is part of Japanese culture.  For many years, Japan has been hunting whales and selling whale meat in the name of "scientific research", which has been condemned by animal advocates.  The International Whaling Commission (IWC) has banned commercial whaling since 1986 because some whale species are threatened with extinction.  Japan joined the Committee in 1951.  Although the Japanese government's announcement was expected, some animal protection groups warned that the move would have serious consequences, which means that Japan will be free to fish for minke whales and other species protected by the International Whaling Commission.  Image copyright AFP / Getty Images Image caption Whale meat made sushi is sold in Miyagi, Japan.  What does the Japanese government say?  Chief Cabinet Secretary Yoshihide Suga said commercial whaling would be limited to Japan ’ s territorial waters and economic zones in the future.  As a result, Japan will stop fishing in Antarctic waters and the southern hemisphere. Whale conservation groups have previously welcomed the move.  In a statement, the Japanese government said that the IWC focused only on the goal of protecting whale populations and failed to meet its other goal of supporting sustainable commercial whaling.  For hundreds of years, whale fishing has been practiced in some coastal areas of Japan.  After the end of World War II, Japanese people used whales as the main source of meat, and consumption of whale meat soared, but consumption has declined sharply in recent decades.  According to the Asahi Shimbun, whale meat accounts for only 0.1% of all meat sold in Japan.  Image copyright AFP Image caption For years, Japan has been hunting whales and selling whale meat in the name of "scientific research."  Australian Foreign Minister Marise Payne and Environment Minister Melissa Price said in a joint statement that they were “very disappointed ” by Japan ’ s decision.  "Australia remains firmly opposed to all forms of commercial and so-called 'scientific' whaling," the statement said.  Before Japan ’ s official announcement, Nicola Beynon, head of campaigns at Humane Society International in Australia, said Japan would “operate entirely outside the scope of international law. ”  "This is a step on the path of a pirate whaling nation," he said, adding that Japan's disdain for international rules is disturbing.  Greenpeace has urged the Japanese government to reconsider the decision, warning that it could draw criticism from Japan, the host of the G20 summit next June.  Sam Annesley, executive director of Greenpeace ’ s Japan office, said the Japanese government ’ s announcement at the end of the year was an obvious attempt to avoid international media attention, but the whole world understood the Japanese government ’ s intentions.  “Today ’ s decision is at odds with the behavior of the international community and, more importantly, with the need to protect the oceans and the future of these great creatures, ” Anisseri said.  What is the current moratorium on whaling?  In 1986, the members of the International Whaling Commission unanimously agreed to suspend whale fishing to restore whale populations.  At the time, the moratorium on whaling was seen by pro-whaling countries as temporary and would continue after a consensus on sustainable fishing quotas had been reached.  Image copyright Getty Images Image caption Commercial whaling has brought some whale species to the brink of extinction.  This, however, became a quasi-permanent ban.  Countries such as Japan, Norway and Iceland, which support whaling, believe that whaling is part of their culture and should continue in the context of sustainable development.  To this day, whale populations have been closely monitored, and many of these species are still endangered, but there are also species such as the minke whale, Japan's main catch, that are not endangered.  In September, Tokyo tried to get the International Whaling Commission to agree to the allocation of commercial fishing quotas, but the commission rejected the proposal.  Can Japan afford to retire?  Although Japan will withdraw from the International Whaling Commission, it will still be subject to certain international laws.  The United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) stipulates that countries should cooperate "through appropriate international organizations" to protect, manage and study whale conservation.  However, the Convention does not specify the name of a specific international organization.  If other countries were willing to cooperate, Japan could try to establish another international organization or join an existing organization like the North Atlantic Marine Mammal Commission (Nammco).  The Commission is smaller than the International Whaling Commission (IWC) and consists of Norway, Iceland, Greenland and the Faroe Islands.  Image copyright Getty Images Image caption Japan fishes hundreds of whales a year.  Didn't Japan hunt whales all the time? Yes.  Although Japan has been hunting whales for the past 30 years, it is all in the name of scientific projects and is an exception to the International Whaling Commission's ban.  Critics say the practice is effectively a cover for commercial whaling.  Japan ’ s approach means that whales caught are used for scientific research, while whale meat can later be used for consumption and trafficking.  Japan fishes about 200 to 1,200 whales a year.  Japan says it is investigating whale populations to determine if they are endangered.  Why was the International Whaling Commission unable to reach an agreement?  Japan has been trying to overturn the moratorium on whaling and is pushing hard for the Commission to reach an agreement on sustainable fishing quotas.  In September, Japan made its last attempt at the IWC summit in Brazil.  Japan has put forward a series of proposals, including the establishment of a sustainable whaling commission and the establishment of sustainable fishing quotas for "abundant whale populations / species".  The proposal was rejected by the committee.  Since then, there have been rumors that Japan would withdraw from the organization without being bound by the rules of the committee.

passages.title: Animal Husbandry in the World + Pictures
passages.passage: They send a boat to find whales and dolphins in front of them.  After finding a flock of animals, other boats make terrible noises and sound walls as they move.  Frightened whales and dolphins swim to the bay, after the animals are exhausted, spears are thrust into their bodies, and the entire sea turns red.  Images of the sea of blood and the slaughter of animals have been repeatedly published in the media.  Japan is one of the countries that, as a tradition, kill large numbers of whales and dolphins.  Although environmental groups have repeatedly protested the move, the country withdrew from the International Whaling Commission (IWC) last year and resumed whaling.  Japan has been whaling for centuries, and its meat has been used as a key source of protein in the post-World War II years when the country was in extreme poverty.  Japanese fishermen also killed more than 300 large finned whales in the Antarctic Ocean last year, including 122 pregnant whales.  The country says it hunts for scientific research, while critics argue that killing whales is for commercial use and Japan sells and uses them for food.  In 2014, the International Court of Justice ruled that Japan ’ s Antarctic whaling program was not for scientific and research purposes and therefore had to be stopped.  However, Japanese authorities claim that the scale of whaling off beaches for commercial purposes is very small compared to whaling in the northern ocean for scientific purposes.  Apart from Japan, many other countries offer different animal sacrifices each year.  The killing of cows after bullfights in Spain, animal sacrifices in Haiti, the killing of whales in Denmark, and the killing of cows and sheep in Nepal and Africa are still held around the world, and in some cases, people are injured or killed.  Photographs published by Alistair Ward, a 22-year-old student at the University of Cambridge, of whaling in Sandavago Bay have received a lot of media attention.  People from the Faroe Islands in Denmark kill whales every year, and this tradition has been going on for centuries.  The Faroe Islands lie in northern Europe between the Norwegian Sea and the North Atlantic Ocean and are made up of 18 small islands.  Whale meat and tallow are a source of food for the nearly 59,000 islanders who are said to be spending the winter there.  The hunters at this ceremony guide the whales to the bay with their oars, and when they get close enough, the killing begins.  Even children participate in the ceremony.  Residents of the area consider whaling a collective activity that everyone can participate in.  They say this is done under national regulations and laws, so that the whales suffer the least amount of pain and suffering.  Many Faroe Islanders believe whaling is not incompatible with the ecosystem, and they hunt 800 pilot whales each year out of the 100,000 whales that surround the island.  Images of this massacre on social media caused a lot of reactions, and some of them, in response to the reaction of European animal rights defenders to the slaughter of animals in East Asia and Africa, wrote sarcastically: “Because Europeans are blond and white, the name of this work is not barbarism and the supply of meat, but the religious slaughter of Muslims is barbaric! ”  The Gadhimai Festival is another event in which thousands of cows and sheep are sacrificed.  The ceremony takes place every five years over two days in Nepal and is inspired by a Hindu religion in the village of Baryapur, which believes that sacrificing to the goddess Gadhimai will capture the devil and bring them happiness.  What animal rights advocates have been protesting at the festival is an unusual form of victimization.  In this place, the cattle are gathered in a field, and they are slashed from the back of the neck.  Animal rights advocates call it the largest animal slaughterhouse in the world because of its remarkable violence.  In addition to the whaling, the Gadhimai festival in Japan has another 3,500-year-old ceremony that takes place in Taiji.  This event is known for the hunt of dolphins by the people of the world.  The people of this city have long been engaged in fishing and whale or dolphin hunting.  Despite opposition, Taijis continue to do so for their food, claiming it has long been a source of livelihood and a part of their cultural identity.  Taiji ’ s history shows the existence of 400-year-old whaling weapons.  The World Health Organization (WHO) studied dolphin meat and declared the amount of toxins and mercury in the meat to be very high, warning people that high levels of mercury in dolphin meat cause diseases such as cancer, infertility and suppression of the immune system.  However, traditional Taiji fishermen continue to slaughter the animal, and its products can be seen in the city ’ s stores.  The people of Taiji send a boat out to hunt for the dolphins in the first place.  After finding a flock of dolphins, the other boats are arranged in the shape of an English letter V, making terrifying sounds and sound walls as they move.  Scared dolphins swim to the bay.  Then other boats chase them to throw their frightened dolphins ashore and crash into the rocks.  After the dolphins are exhausted, the spears are thrust into the bodies of these animals and the entire sea turns red.  Among the wounded dolphins, the more beautiful ones are hunted for aquariums and circuses.  In Taiji, Haiti, there is also a ceremony in which animals are killed.  Voodoo believers gather in the country in April and declare their obedience to their gods by sacrificing animals, dancing and playing music.  After the sacrifice, they pour the warm blood of the animal into a container and drink it.  Those present in the ceremony, dressed in white, shed some of this blood on themselves, and while believing that they are under the control of the spirits, they jump into the water and continue to worship.  Wearing white clothes with blood symbolizes adherence to voodoo.  Followers of the cult have combined drum dancing as an African tradition with traditional elements of the Catholic religion.  Millions of Haitians believe in voodoo, and the government adopted it as an official religion in 1960.  But in 2012, the Haitian Senate and House of Representatives decried Voodoo as the official religion with a constitutional amendment approved by their president, a move that caused widespread discontent among Haitian followers.  In Spain, bullfighting is also one of the most popular entertainment in the world.  San Fermin in Spain attracts many tourists every year.  The celebration of the release and running of angry cows among the crowd through the narrow alleys lasts a few minutes, but the celebration lasts for hours.  Cows enter the stadium after passing through the city center to witness the matador battle with the bulls.  In the past, due to the narrow streets and the lack of possibility of passing the cart, ranchers had to drive the cows on a short path to the stadium.  Over time, young people started running in front of the cows to show their courage.  Those who run in front of cows traditionally wear white shirts and trousers and a red necktie around their necks.  Every year, the ceremony leaves a number of injured and even killed.  At the end of the festivities in Spain, bullfighters circle the animals and kill them with decorated spears and knives.  Due to opposition to the ceremony, bullfighting festivals were banned in some Spanish cities, including the Canary Islands.  It is not only in rituals that animals are abused and slaughtered, but also in pictures and videos of the slaughter of pregnant cows in France, sheep in Australian slaughterhouses, the killing of goats in Thailand, the slaughter of camels in Mauritania, and the cooking of live pigs in Europe. Japan has resumed commercial whaling after 32 years, citing the need to study whale migration routes, diet, and other factors related to marine mammals [55f03ae7-157e-4e63-a0df-4d6d9cb8de74]. 
The country's withdrawal from the International Whaling Commission (IWC) was announced in December 2018, and it officially re-opened the "tradition" of commercial whaling for 31 years on July 1, 2019 [28c4ff25-dd87-450d-95bc-84af873027be].

One of the main reasons for Japan's decision to resume whaling is the need to support the country's whaling industry, which has been aging and struggling financially [5d5792ec-8053-43ad-948c-2ca1de7d4ea8]. 
The Japanese government has allocated a fixed subsidy to whalers every day, which will likely be cut or even cancelled in 2020 [5d5792ec-8053-43ad-948c-2ca1de7d4ea8]. 
By resuming commercial whaling, the government hopes to guarantee the repayment of funds and ensure the long-term sustainability of the industry [5d5792ec-8053-43ad-948c-2ca1de7d4ea8].

Another reason for Japan's decision is the country's cultural heritage and traditional practice of whaling [56413e55-0f89-45e1-94f9-7626dd17cbe2]. 
Whaling has been an integral part of Japanese culture for centuries, with the country's whaling industry dating back to the Edo period [56413e55-0f89-45e1-94f9-7626dd17cbe2]. 
The Japanese government argues that eating whale meat is a national tradition and a way to preserve the country's cultural identity [950af4b0-1f67-4f91-b764-77d5b8b1621f].

The Japanese government has also pointed to the low supply and demand of whale meat as a reason for resuming commercial whaling [950af4b0-1f67-4f91-b764-77d5b8b1621f]. 
Despite the decline in demand, whale meat is not expensive due to reduced availability, and the price of whale meat is comparable to that of other meats [950af4b0-1f67-4f91-b764-77d5b8b1621f]. 
The government hopes that by resuming commercial whaling, the industry will be able to increase its production and meet the growing demand for whale meat [950af4b0-1f67-4f91-b764-77d5b8b1621f].

In addition, Japan's withdrawal from the IWC has allowed the country to resume whaling in its territorial waters and exclusive economic zone [527be2e4-188c-4b13-8679-3e24183d08a8]. 
The government has also established a new category of "survey whaling" to continue whaling on the grounds of "scientific research" [28c4ff25-dd87-450d-95bc-84af873027be]. 
This move has been met with criticism from environmental groups and other countries, which argue that Japan's actions are effectively a cover for commercial whaling [950af4b0-1f67-4f91-b764-77d5b8b1621f].

The Japanese government has also emphasized the importance of whaling in supporting the country's fishing industry [55f03ae7-157e-4e63-a0df-4d6d9cb8de74]. 
Whaling has been an important source of protein for Japanese people, particularly during times of food shortages and economic hardship [56413e55-0f89-45e1-94f9-7626dd17cbe2]. 
The government hopes that by resuming commercial whaling, the industry will be able to contribute to the country's economic growth and food security [55f03ae7-157e-4e63-a0df-4d6d9cb8de74].

Overall, Japan's decision to resume commercial whaling is a complex issue with multiple motivations and implications. 
While the country's cultural heritage and traditional practice of whaling are significant factors, the need to support the country's whaling industry and address the low supply and demand of whale meat are also important considerations [950af4b0-1f67-4f91-b764-77d5b8b1621f].

Whale hunting has brought some whale species to the brink of extinction [950af4b0-1f67-4f91-b764-77d5b8b1621f]. 
The International Whaling Commission (IWC) has banned commercial whaling since 1986 because some whale species are threatened with extinction [950af4b0-1f67-4f91-b764-77d5b8b1621f]. 
However, Japan has been hunting whales under the guise of scientific research, and the country's withdrawal from the IWC has allowed it to resume commercial whaling [950af4b0-1f67-4f91-b764-77d5b8b1621f].

In 2014, the International Court of Justice ruled that Japan's Antarctic whaling program was not for scientific and research purposes and therefore had to be stopped [14366427-1989-44bf-b090-2a60f2e838fa]. 
However, the Japanese government has argued that its whaling program is necessary for the country's food security and sustainable development [5d5792ec-8053-43ad-948c-2ca1de7d4ea8].

Whaling has been a contentious issue for many years, with both proponents and opponents presenting different arguments and evidence [950af4b0-1f67-4f91-b764-77d5b8b1621f]. 
The debate surrounding whaling is complex and multifaceted, involving issues of cultural heritage, food security, economic development, and environmental conservation [950af4b0-1f67-4f91-b764-77d5b8b1621f].

The resumption of commercial whaling by Japan has been met with criticism from many countries, including Australia, Brazil, and other IWC member countries [527be2e4-188c-4b13-8679-3e24183d08a8]. 
These countries argue that Japan's actions are unsustainable and will have negative impacts on whale populations and the environment [527be2e4-188c-4b13-8679-3e24183d08a8]. 
However, the Japanese government argues that its whaling program is necessary for the country's food security and sustainable development [5d5792ec-8053-43ad-948c-2ca1de7d4ea8].

Title: Common ships will spend 6 billion yen to build new whaling mother ship
Content: News from Japan (Kyodo News Agency, May 11) In the context of the commercial whaling that has resumed in Japan after 31 years in 2019, President Hideki So, the only company to carry out offshore operations, held a press conference in Tokyo on the 10th, announcing plans to spend about 6 billion yen (about 350 million yuan) to build a new whaling ship.  The company is optimistic that the Japanese government will expand the fishing quota and target sea areas in the future, and renovate the old mother ship.  Originally, it was "always said that it would cost more than 10 billion yen" (in the words of the president), but the cost was reduced by reducing the speed of the current mother ship "Nisin Maru".  It is expected to be completed in March 2024.  The government currently restricts commercial whaling to the exclusive economic zone (EEZ) of Japan, which covers only three species of minke whales, Bryde whales and Sei whales.  The new mother ship was also designed to operate outside the EEZ in the future. It can also catch large fin whales and ensure that it has the ability to reach the Antarctic waters.  The construction fee will not rely on subsidies, but will be obtained through crowdfunding through loans and online fundraising.  The president said that in order to guarantee the repayment of funds, "we hope to increase the amount of fishing in 2024."  He also stressed that the expansion of the whale meat market will be driven by higher wholesale prices and increased imports.  Japan withdrew from the International Whaling Commission (IWC) at the end of June 2019 and stopped its previous investigation of whaling activities.

Title: Withdrawal from the "cultural imperialist" Whaling Commission, Japan's diplomacy turned to "Trumpism"?
Content: On July 1, Japan officially re-opened the "tradition" of commercial whaling for 31 years. 9 days ago, the first batch of whalers returned to the port, bringing back a total of more than a dozen baleen whales large and small. On December 26, 2018, Japan announced that it would withdraw from the International Whaling Commission (IWC) after six months, and decided to reopen the commercial whaling route, prompting criticism from many countries. According to Article 65 of the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS), the conservation and management of cetaceans is to be determined by "appropriate international authorities".  Originally, the International Whaling Commission was responsible for this task, after Japan's withdrawal, there will be a future Japanese whaling ship triggered by the international case may be against the court, Yoshikawa said only that "whether it will go to both sides of the complaint, but also depends on the policy judgment of various countries", now I am afraid it is too early to say. Unlike survey whaling in the Antarctic Sea and the North Pacific, Japan has resumed commercial whaling only off the coast of Japan. Title: 【 News Classroom 】 Despite global criticism, when did Japan restart commercial whaling after 32 years? ｜ Hong Kong 01 ｜ The World Says
Content: Japan officially withdrew from the International Whaling Commission (IWC) on Sunday (June 30), after 32 years to restart commercial whaling.  A number of whalers were greeted by local residents and sailed out of the harbour.  Japan is one of the few countries that still hunt whales. Today, let ’ s introduce Japan ’ s whaling history, the reasons for restarting whaling and the current state of the whaling industry.  A number of whaling vessels are moored at the wharf in Kushiro City, Hokkaido, waiting to sail. (Reuters) ↓ ↓ For more photos of whaling, please click to enlarge: + 4 + 3 + 2 Japan Whaling History Japan has a long history of whaling, which began in prehistoric times.  The word "fish" in the Nara period "Manye Collection" is an ancient Japanese word for whaling.  In the Edo period, whaling gradually became an industry. In addition to being used for food, various parts of the whale were fully utilized, such as whale oil as a pesticide, bone nata as carving, and ambergris as a perfume.  After World War II, Japan ’ s whaling industry soared due to food shortages and foreign exchange earnings. In the 1950s, Japan became the world ’ s largest whaling nation, with domestic consumption peaking at 233,000 tons in 1962.  In 1982, the IWC passed the Convention on the Prohibition of Commercial Whaling. Japan initially objected, but after the objection was rejected in 1986, Japan finally promised to gradually ban commercial whaling, and commercial whaling ceased in 1988.  However, commercial whaling does not mean that whaling will no longer be done. In fact, Japan has set up a new category of "survey whaling" to continue whaling on the grounds of "scientific research".  According to the report of the Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries, the annual consumption of whale meat in Japan since the 1990s has been about 2,000 to 6,000 tons, and the latest figure in 2018 totals 3,000 tons.  Japan has a long history of whaling, which has become an industry as early as the Edo period. (Getty Images) Revitalizing the economy with the help of Whaling Japan ’ s Small Whaling Association President Yoshinori Abe called the news of the resumption of commercial whaling “a shock of joy and a sense of limitlessness. ” Prosperity again.  Some areas that used to make a living from whaling also hope to revitalize the economy by restarting whale hunting, such as the Amikawa area in the east of Miyagi Prefecture, which was the base of the whaling port of that year.  After extensive damage during the Great East Japan Earthquake, residents hope to revive the local economy by reviving the whaling industry. A museum dedicated to introducing whaling culture is planned for April 2020 to attract visitors.  Whale meat is quite nutritious and has become an important food item for the Japanese since the end of World War II. (Reuters) Whale meat is not expensive, but it should be noted that since the 1970s, whaling in Japan has declined year by year, and today whale meat is no longer a common dish in Japan.  Compared to the annual consumption of 6 million tons of pork and chicken, only 3,000 tons of whale meat is really insignificant.  And interestingly, whale meat has not become expensive due to reduced availability.  In the Tokyo market price in 2018, the price of "red meat level 1" whale meat used for sashimi is 1,600 yen (about HK $110) per kilogram, and the price of "umu" whale meat used for high-grade smoked is 3,000 yen (about HK $210) per kilogram.  In fact, the price of salmon to tuna is about the price, can not say how expensive.  This means that the actual market demand for whale meat is not high.  Therefore, public opinion in Japan is worried that in the reality of low supply and demand, even if the resumption of whaling, it will be difficult to let this already sunset industry "rise back to life", and the desire to revitalize the regional economy will be difficult to achieve.  Whale meat sashimi, but in fact, the price of whale meat is not particularly expensive due to the low supply and demand. (Reuters) Possible political reasons behind this.  Including Prime Minister Shinzo Abe, the constituency of the former president of the ruling Liberal Democratic Party ’ s faction, the “Chi Shih Association ”, is a land of whaling.  Therefore, there are allegations that the government is strongly promoting the resumption of whale hunting in order to continue to gain the support of local residents.  However, whether it is for cultural, industrial or political reasons, the low supply and demand of whale meat and the low price of whale meat can not be ignored, and Japan will face condemnation from international environmental groups.

Title: Japan resumes commercial whaling, drawing strong international opposition
Content: Image copyright AFP / Getty Images Image caption Japanese officials say eating whale meat is part of Japanese culture.  The Japanese government announced its withdrawal from the International Whaling Commission (IWC) and will resume commercial whaling in July 2019.  Such a move would attract strong criticism from the international community.  Japanese officials say eating whale meat is part of Japanese culture.  For many years, Japan has been hunting whales and selling whale meat in the name of "scientific research", which has been condemned by animal advocates.  The International Whaling Commission (IWC) has banned commercial whaling since 1986 because some whale species are threatened with extinction.  Japan joined the Committee in 1951.  Although the Japanese government's announcement was expected, some animal protection groups warned that the move would have serious consequences, which means that Japan will be free to fish for minke whales and other species protected by the International Whaling Commission.  Image copyright AFP / Getty Images Image caption Whale meat made sushi is sold in Miyagi, Japan.  What does the Japanese government say?  Chief Cabinet Secretary Yoshihide Suga said commercial whaling would be limited to Japan ’ s territorial waters and economic zones in the future.  As a result, Japan will stop fishing in Antarctic waters and the southern hemisphere. Whale conservation groups have previously welcomed the move.  In a statement, the Japanese government said that the IWC focused only on the goal of protecting whale populations and failed to meet its other goal of supporting sustainable commercial whaling.  For hundreds of years, whale fishing has been practiced in some coastal areas of Japan. Before Japan ’ s official announcement, Nicola Beynon, head of campaigns at Humane Society International in Australia, said Japan would “operate entirely outside the scope of international law. ”  "This is a step on the path of a pirate whaling nation," he said, adding that Japan's disdain for international rules is disturbing.  Greenpeace has urged the Japanese government to reconsider the decision, warning that it could draw criticism from Japan, the host of the G20 summit next June.  Sam Annesley, executive director of Greenpeace ’ s Japan office, said the Japanese government ’ s announcement at the end of the year was an obvious attempt to avoid international media attention, but the whole world understood the Japanese government ’ s intentions.  “Today ’ s decision is at odds with the behavior of the international community and, more importantly, with the need to protect the oceans and the future of these great creatures, ” Anisseri said.  What is the current moratorium on whaling?  In 1986, the members of the International Whaling Commission unanimously agreed to suspend whale fishing to restore whale populations.  At the time, the moratorium on whaling was seen by pro-whaling countries as temporary and would continue after a consensus on sustainable fishing quotas had been reached. Although Japan will withdraw from the International Whaling Commission, it will still be subject to certain international laws.  The United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) stipulates that countries should cooperate "through appropriate international organizations" to protect, manage and study whale conservation.  However, the Convention does not specify the name of a specific international organization.  If other countries were willing to cooperate, Japan could try to establish another international organization or join an existing organization like the North Atlantic Marine Mammal Commission (Nammco).  The Commission is smaller than the International Whaling Commission (IWC) and consists of Norway, Iceland, Greenland and the Faroe Islands.  Image copyright Getty Images Image caption Japan fishes hundreds of whales a year.  Didn't Japan hunt whales all the time? Yes.  Although Japan has been hunting whales for the past 30 years, it is all in the name of scientific projects and is an exception to the International Whaling Commission's ban.  Critics say the practice is effectively a cover for commercial whaling.  Japan ’ s approach means that whales caught are used for scientific research, while whale meat can later be used for consumption and trafficking.  Japan fishes about 200 to 1,200 whales a year.  Japan says it is investigating whale populations to determine if they are endangered.  Why was the International Whaling Commission unable to reach an agreement?  Japan has been trying to overturn the moratorium on whaling and is pushing hard for the Commission to reach an agreement on sustainable fishing quotas.  In September, Japan made its last attempt at the IWC summit in Brazil.  Japan has put forward a series of proposals, including the establishment of a sustainable whaling commission and the establishment of sustainable fishing quotas for "abundant whale populations / species". Apart from Japan, many other countries offer different animal sacrifices each year. To this day, whale populations have been closely monitored, and many of these species are still endangered, but there are also species such as the minke whale, Japan's main catch, that are not endangered.  In September, Tokyo tried to get the International Whaling Commission to agree to the allocation of commercial fishing quotas, but the commission rejected the proposal.  Can Japan afford to retire?  Although Japan will withdraw from the International Whaling Commission, it will still be subject to certain international laws.  The United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) stipulates that countries should cooperate "through appropriate international organizations" to protect, manage and study whale conservation.  However, the Convention does not specify the name of a specific international organization.  If other countries were willing to cooperate, Japan could try to establish another international organization or join an existing organization like the North Atlantic Marine Mammal Commission (Nammco).  The Commission is smaller than the International Whaling Commission (IWC) and consists of Norway, Iceland, Greenland and the Faroe Islands.  Image copyright Getty Images Image caption Japan fishes hundreds of whales a year.  Didn't Japan hunt whales all the time? Yes.  Although Japan has been hunting whales for the past 30 years, it is all in the name of scientific projects and is an exception to the International Whaling Commission's ban.  Critics say the practice is effectively a cover for commercial whaling.  Japan ’ s approach means that whales caught are used for scientific research, while whale meat can later be used for consumption and trafficking.  Japan fishes about 200 to 1,200 whales a year.  Japan says it is investigating whale populations to determine if they are endangered.  Why was the International Whaling Commission unable to reach an agreement?  Japan has been trying to overturn the moratorium on whaling and is pushing hard for the Commission to reach an agreement on sustainable fishing quotas.  In September, Japan made its last attempt at the IWC summit in Brazil.  Japan has put forward a series of proposals, including the establishment of a sustainable whaling commission and the establishment of sustainable fishing quotas for "abundant whale populations / species".  The proposal was rejected by the committee.  Since then, there have been rumors that Japan would withdraw from the organization without being bound by the rules of the committee.

Title: Animal Husbandry in the World + Pictures
Content: They send a boat to find whales and dolphins in front of them.  After finding a flock of animals, other boats make terrible noises and sound walls as they move.  Frightened whales and dolphins swim to the bay, after the animals are exhausted, spears are thrust into their bodies, and the entire sea turns red.  Images of the sea of blood and the slaughter of animals have been repeatedly published in the media.  Japan is one of the countries that, as a tradition, kill large numbers of whales and dolphins.  Although environmental groups have repeatedly protested the move, the country withdrew from the International Whaling Commission (IWC) last year and resumed whaling.  Japan has been whaling for centuries, and its meat has been used as a key source of protein in the post-World War II years when the country was in extreme poverty.  Japanese fishermen also killed more than 300 large finned whales in the Antarctic Ocean last year, including 122 pregnant whales.  The country says it hunts for scientific research, while critics argue that killing whales is for commercial use and Japan sells and uses them for food.  In 2014, the International Court of Justice ruled that Japan ’ s Antarctic whaling program was not for scientific and research purposes and therefore had to be stopped.  However, Japanese authorities claim that the scale of whaling off beaches for commercial purposes is very small compared to whaling in the northern ocean for scientific purposes.  Apart from Japan, many other countries offer different animal sacrifices each year.  The killing of cows after bullfights in Spain, animal sacrifices in Haiti, the killing of whales in Denmark, and the killing of cows and sheep in Nepal and Africa are still held around the world, and in some cases, people are injured or killed.  Photographs published by Alistair Ward, a 22-year-old student at the University of Cambridge, of whaling in Sandavago Bay have received a lot of media attention.  People from the Faroe Islands in Denmark kill whales every year, and this tradition has been going on for centuries.  The Faroe Islands lie in northern Europe between the Norwegian Sea and the North Atlantic Ocean and are made up of 18 small islands.  Whale meat and tallow are a source of food for the nearly 59,000 islanders who are said to be spending the winter there.  The hunters at this ceremony guide the whales to the bay with their oars, and when they get close enough, the killing begins.  Even children participate in the ceremony.  Residents of the area consider whaling a collective activity that everyone can participate in.  They say this is done under national regulations and laws, so that the whales suffer the least amount of pain and suffering.  Many Faroe Islanders believe whaling is not incompatible with the ecosystem, and they hunt 800 pilot whales each year out of the 100,000 whales that surround the island.  Images of this massacre on social media caused a lot of reactions, and some of them, in response to the reaction of European animal rights defenders to the slaughter of animals in East Asia and Africa, wrote sarcastically: “Because Europeans are blond and white, the name of this work is not barbarism and the supply of meat, but the religious slaughter of Muslims is barbaric! ”  The Gadhimai Festival is another event in which thousands of cows and sheep are sacrificed.  The ceremony takes place every five years over two days in Nepal and is inspired by a Hindu religion in the village of Baryapur, which believes that sacrificing to the goddess Gadhimai will capture the devil and bring them happiness.  What animal rights advocates have been protesting at the festival is an unusual form of victimization.  In this place, the cattle are gathered in a field, and they are slashed from the back of the neck.  Animal rights advocates call it the largest animal slaughterhouse in the world because of its remarkable violence.  In addition to the whaling, the Gadhimai festival in Japan has another 3,500-year-old ceremony that takes place in Taiji.  This event is known for the hunt of dolphins by the people of the world.  The people of this city have long been engaged in fishing and whale or dolphin hunting.  Despite opposition, Taijis continue to do so for their food, claiming it has long been a source of livelihood and a part of their cultural identity.  Taiji ’ s history shows the existence of 400-year-old whaling weapons.  The World Health Organization (WHO) studied dolphin meat and declared the amount of toxins and mercury in the meat to be very high, warning people that high levels of mercury in dolphin meat cause diseases such as cancer, infertility and suppression of the immune system.  However, traditional Taiji fishermen continue to slaughter the animal, and its products can be seen in the city ’ s stores.  The people of Taiji send a boat out to hunt for the dolphins in the first place.  After finding a flock of dolphins, the other boats are arranged in the shape of an English letter V, making terrifying sounds and sound walls as they move.  Scared dolphins swim to the bay.  Then other boats chase them to throw their frightened dolphins ashore and crash into the rocks.  After the dolphins are exhausted, the spears are thrust into the bodies of these animals and the entire sea turns red.  Among the wounded dolphins, the more beautiful ones are hunted for aquariums and circuses.  In Taiji, Haiti, there is also a ceremony in which animals are killed.  Voodoo believers gather in the country in April and declare their obedience to their gods by sacrificing animals, dancing and playing music.  After the sacrifice, they pour the warm blood of the animal into a container and drink it.  Those present in the ceremony, dressed in white, shed some of this blood on themselves, and while believing that they are under the control of the spirits, they jump into the water and continue to worship.  Wearing white clothes with blood symbolizes adherence to voodoo.  Followers of the cult have combined drum dancing as an African tradition with traditional elements of the Catholic religion.  Millions of Haitians believe in voodoo, and the government adopted it as an official religion in 1960.  But in 2012, the Haitian Senate and House of Representatives decried Voodoo as the official religion with a constitutional amendment approved by their president, a move that caused widespread discontent among Haitian followers.  In Spain, bullfighting is also one of the most popular entertainment in the world.  San Fermin in Spain attracts many tourists every year.  The celebration of the release and running of angry cows among the crowd through the narrow alleys lasts a few minutes, but the celebration lasts for hours.  Cows enter the stadium after passing through the city center to witness the matador battle with the bulls.  In the past, due to the narrow streets and the lack of possibility of passing the cart, ranchers had to drive the cows on a short path to the stadium.  Over time, young people started running in front of the cows to show their courage.  Those who run in front of cows traditionally wear white shirts and trousers and a red necktie around their necks.  Every year, the ceremony leaves a number of injured and even killed.  At the end of the festivities in Spain, bullfighters circle the animals and kill them with decorated spears and knives.  Due to opposition to the ceremony, bullfighting festivals were banned in some Spanish cities, including the Canary Islands.  It is not only in rituals that animals are abused and slaughtered, but also in pictures and videos of the slaughter of pregnant cows in France, sheep in Australian slaughterhouses, the killing of goats in Thailand, the slaughter of camels in Mauritania, and the cooking of live pigs in Europe. passages.passage: He said, “The works of a man who writes short and clear are like a beautiful iceberg, only an eighth of which is out of the water. ”  Ernest Hemingway was born in Oak Park, Illinois.  His father was a doctor and his mother was a piano teacher and very religious.  While her mother engaged her in church and hymns, her father took her fishing and taught her how to use guns.  At school, he was fascinated by his literary teacher: “I liked his look and his expression.  I felt that there was something in me that he said well in the form of literature and poetry that he read. ” His first writings were published in the school newspaper.  After high school, he reported for magazines.  She was 19 years old when she was injured as a volunteer in the First World War and spent a long time in hospital to remove 200 pieces of shrapnel from her body.  After returning from the war, he wrote in magazines.  At the age of 22, he moved to Paris as a reporter, married his colleague Hadley Richardson, and his wife set out for the Greco-Turkish War.  There, Hemingway found his former friend James Joyce, who inspired him to publish the story.  In Paris he achieved his own style: “The sayings must be said in the unspoken. ”  He writes with clear, short, adjective-free phrases and sentences that look like aphorisms, but fills the reader with a sense of empathy or aversion to his characters.  He was 53 years old when he published his most enduring work, The Old Man and the Sea, for which he received a Nobel Prize in Literature.  In addition to adventure, fishing, hunting, and weapons, he was also interested in cooking and bullfighting, and reflected these interests in his stories.  His hamburger recipe recently ended up at the John F. Kennedy Museum in Boston.  Hemingway ’ s adventures were not limited to war and travel to Africa, but also to unknown places and new situations, car and air accidents, malaria, skin cancer, pneumonia, hepatitis, multiple fractures and kidney problems.  He had a popular collection of weapons, and his death was shaped by one of them.  Ernest Hemingway committed suicide in Idaho at the age of 61.

I am not a literary critic.  Not a writer.  But it seems to me that at that time there was no writer who at least once did not experience the influence of the magical Hemingway dialogues. Of course, Hemingway himself has repeatedly turned to the work of great predecessors.  The famous novel "For Whom the Bell Tolls" is called a phrase written 350 years before it was borrowed from the largest poet and priest, a contemporary of Shakespeare John Donne. Hemingway was often accused of a rampant lifestyle.  Addicted to alcohol.  To the cruel spectacles (bullfighting).  Accused of cynicism, excessive irony.  Over time, it became clear that the writer, like Democritus, ironically and laughed not at life, but at its seriousness.  His tolerance for human vices — including his own — was philosophical. I thought it was fake.  The best place on earth recognized Cuba.  The last 20 years of his enchanting life, the writer spent in a small settlement of San Francisco de Paula, 20 kilometers from Havana. To accommodate all this, it was necessary to expand the area.  "I bought two rooms from the neighbors," Mrs. Mary told me, showing the apartment. "All you see is Ernest."  A few minutes before the farewell, Mary Hemingway took my notebook and scribbled out a few lines.  “It ’ s my shortest story, ” she said.  Shortly before our meeting, she completed the main work: a book about twenty years of living together with Hemingway.  The book "As it was" immediately became a bestseller. passages.title: 【 Green Bird Residence 】 Event Feature ： Chen Jung-bin / Impression of Paris in Hemingway 's Text
passages.passage: In the 1920s, the Treaty of Versailles proclaimed the end of World War I, Hitler in Europe joined the Nazi Party, and the Communist Party of China rose in the East.  And the United States introduced a national prohibition of alcohol, so a group of American "expats" came to Paris, free and exile in various cafes and bars. Hemingway also moved to the old city as a reporter in 1921, beginning his penniless, but indulgent days.  A hundred years later, Chen Jung-bin and the audience of the Blue Bird House look back at the impression of Paris that was reflected in Hemingway ’ s words.  The Old Man and the Sea was born on an alcohol-soaked beach in Cuba; The War Bell is an interview from the Spanish Civil War; The Dawn of Truth records the memories of a trip to Africa with his fourth wife, Mary, and Hemingway, born in Oak Park, Illinois, USA.  At the age of 21, he worked as a reporter for the Toronto Star in Canada, became a special correspondent in Europe the next year, and moved to Paris to spend his 20 generations, nearly a decade of his golden years.  Ernest Hemingway in World War I. When he first arrived in Paris, he stayed in a small hotel and wrote in the Toronto Star: “PARIS — Paris in the winter is rainy, cold, beautiful and cheap. ”  It is also noisy, jostling, crowded and cheap.  It is anything you want — and cheap. ” — Living on $1,000 a Year in Paris Describes the bankruptcy of Europe at the end of World War I, the relative advantage of the dollar, and the ability to spend a thousand dollars in Paris for a year.  Although this article is published in the newspaper, the writing and rhyme are poetic.  “We ate well and cheaply and drank well and cheaply and slept well and warm together and love each other. ”  After graduating from high school, Hemingway worked as a reporter for the Kansas City Star, and his entire writing career was inextricably linked to journalistic writing.  “From Hemingway ’ s early writings, the Kansas Star newspaper ’ s“ style sheet ” for the rookie reporter shaped his unique style of writing, and the rules in the guide were as many as 110, and the first paragraph was indeed Hemingway ’ s rule: write short sentences.  The first paragraph is shorter.  Write articles in vivid English.  The influence of the rookie reporter period on his career also corresponds to the iceberg theory he proposed in 1932: "Prose is like architecture, not interior decoration, and the Baroque era is over... If you have enough understanding of what you are describing and write well enough, even if you write only one-eighth of the text, you can let the reader fully grasp the scene, plot and character description that he wants to express." Hemingway often uses a concise style to bury clues in the details or background, so that it is connected with emotional intimacy.  Paris was not only the place where Hemingway worked as a journalist, but also the beginning of his literary career.  The first two books, Three Stories & Ten Poems, and a collection of short stories, in our time, were published here.  Ernest Hemingway wrote many notes about his life and literary work in the 1920s. Two boxes were left in the basement of the Ritz Hotel in Paris, and when he returned to Paris in 1957, he opened these dusty old memories, namely, "The Feast on the Move".  This prose memoir of Paris also later became a guide for people on their pilgrimage journey, following Hemingway for a drink, order a cup of coffee at the Lilac Café, borrow a book at Shakespeare ’ s Bookstore on the Rue d ’ Odeon, and then take a walk in Luxembourg Park.  “If you are lucky enough to have lived in Paris as a young man, then wherever you go for the rest of your life it stays with you, for Paris is a movable feast. ” — Ernest Hemingway A moving feast.  Shakespeare Bookstore (Photo / Courtesy of Blue Bird) Mr. Chen then pointed out on the map several places where Hemingway often stopped in Paris. First came to the Shakespeare Bookstore, which is also like a library, which can rent books at affordable prices, and also provides mail collection services, which is suitable for young and poor boy Hemingway.  The owner of the bookstore, Shelville Beach, is also an American, and in her autobiography, Shakespeare's Bookstore, there is a chapter entitled "The Best Customer Hemingway".  In his translation of the book, Mr. Chen found hundreds of references to Hemingway, and the description of his affinity showed their deep and warm friendship at the time.  At the end of World War II, Hemingway returns to Paris with the Americans and meets Chevelle again.  There are still a lot of gun battles in the theater street, and we ’ ve had enough.  One day a jeep pulled into the street and stopped at the door of my bookstore.  I heard a low voice shouting, “Chevy! ” and it spread all over the street.  Edhiena cried, "It's Hemingway! It's Hemingway!" I rushed downstairs and hit the oncoming Hemingway.  He picked me up in circles and kissed me, and the people at the window of the street cheered … He asked if there was anything else I could do, and I said if I could get rid of the Nazi snipers on the roof of the street, especially those on Edsieena ’ s roof.  He called his buddies out of their jeeps, took them all to the roof, and then came the last gunfight on Theater Street.  Hemingway got down with his men and drove off in the jeep — next, Hemingway said, to the wine cellar at the Ritz.  The Lilac Garden Cafe (Photo / Courtesy of the Blue Bird House) The Lilac Garden on the Boulevard Montparnasse is the place where the artistic and cultural trends of Paris in the 1920s met and collided, and where Fitzgerald, Zola, Cezanne and Picasso all stopped.  “I sat in the corner writing with my notebook, and the afternoon sun was on my shoulders.  The waiter took me a cup of hot cream coffee (café crème), and I drank half of it after cooling, and the other half was on the table while I was writing.  When I stopped writing, I really didn ’ t want to leave the river where the trout could be seen in the pool. ” — Chen Jung-bin, author of “Feast on the Move, ” mentioned this text, poetically describing the process of creating the novel“ Our Time ” in Lilac Garden, and the river where the trout can be seen is the title of the book, “The Big Twin Heart River. ”  A Good Café on the Place St.-Michel "A girl walks into a cafe and sits alone at a table by the window.  She was beautiful, and her face was as fresh as a new coin — if only coins could be minted with silky muscles and rain-washed skin.  Her hair was as dark as the wings of a raven, cut into a blade, and covered her face obliquely.  I stared at her, and she disturbed my thoughts and made me very excited.  I wanted to put her in my novel or something, but she was sitting where she could see the street and the entrance to the cafe, so I knew she was waiting for someone.  So I continued to write.  The story seemed to unfold automatically, and my pen managed to keep up with it.  I ordered another glass of St. James ’ s brandy.  Whenever I raised my head or sharpened the pencil with a sharpener, I would look at the girl and let the curly scraps fall into the saucer under the glass. "  "I see you, my beauty, now you belong to me, no matter who you are waiting for, and no matter whether I can see you again in the future," I thought.  You belong to me, and all Paris belongs to me, and I belong to this notebook and this pencil.  From this Paris memoir, Teacher Chen Jung-bin led us to read this famous article. passages.title: Hemingway's Myth
passages.passage: In 1953, Hemingway was sitting at a dinner table at his camp in Kenya, writing. (NARA, Photographer, Look Magazine) Anyone familiar with American literature and literary criticism should know the iceberg talk about literary creation.  The author of this statement is the famous American writer and Nobel Prize winner Ernest Hemingway.  The main point is that if a writer has a mind about what he wants to write, he can omit something he knows when he creates, and the reader will feel those omissions because the author is writing true.  It is like an iceberg that looks magnificent as it moves in the sea, but in fact only one-eighth of it is out of the water, and the invisible part is more and more real.  In the theory of ancient Chinese poetry creation, there is a saying of "artistic conception", emphasizing the scenes and emotions depicted through the works, stimulating the imagination of the readers, and leaving them a space for full reflection and play.  This is synonymous with the "iceberg theory", but Hemingway emphasized the authenticity of the work, aiming to criticize some writers who seemed to him to be quite incompetent, who simply "omitted something because they did not understand".  Hemingway ’ s “iceberg talk ” actually interprets his own creative style, which is to omit everything he thinks is optional in his writing, and to be as simple and implicit as possible.  This creative style of Hemingway is indeed unique and has had a profound impact, some even said: Hemingway with no one has the courage, "English attached to the literature of the hair cut clean." But what interests me is that he uses the "iceberg" as a metaphor.  This analogy is really good.  What people usually use as metaphors are some common things, such as peach blossoms in "face like peach blossoms" and torches in "eyes like torches". How many people have seen an iceberg?  Three years ago, I went to Alaska to visit, and all I saw was a large piece of ice floe on the sea surface, real sea icebergs, probably only in the South Pole and Arctic areas where ordinary people are difficult to set foot.  However, this parable is also very relevant and can make people understand God.  What you can read in a good work is certainly brilliant, like the magnificence of an iceberg above the surface of the water, but what it contains can be much wider and deeper than the literal meaning, like a much larger body of mountain undersea support.  Without the presence of seven eighths below, there is no beauty at the top.  In the book of Revelation, there is a great deal to be said about the use of metaphors.  He said that the metaphor contains two aspects that are opposite and complementary, and the things that are compared must be the same, otherwise they cannot be joined together; but at the same time, they must be different, otherwise they cannot be distinguished.  As for the interaction between the two, the greater the difference, the more the same thing will be baked; the more open it will be, the more unexpected it will be, the more novel the metaphor will be, and the better the effect will be.  According to the theory of Qian Zhongshu, Hemingway uses the iceberg as a metaphor, and the things that belong to it are "very divided", and it has indeed produced a surprising winning effect, so it is unforgettable.  There are many other examples of this in the metaphor Hemingway has used.  After Hemingway became famous, he often compared himself with other writers, and was quite conceited, many writers he could not see, and only Shakespeare and Tolstoy were really admired.  He did not know this, but used boxing as a metaphor.  He said that he did not want to play Dostoyevsky in the first game, because he knew that Dostoyevsky was almost as good as he was, so he chose to play with Turgenev first because he felt he could play with him.  Then try Maupassant again, although it is difficult, but also can beat him; as for Henry James, he said, "As soon as I catch me, I press him, and immediately give him a blow where he has no meat, so tell the referee to stop the game." Hemingway's words, you can see his confidence.  About him and Cervantes who is stronger, he has a different saying, he believes that 20 rounds of war, you can beat the other side of the fart, but also admitted that Mr. Cervantes is very shrewd, while playing and learning, maybe the second game he will lose to the other side.  In Hemingway ’ s eyes, Shakespeare is the champion who can ’ t beat.  And speaking of Tolstoy, whom he equally admired, he said something different.  He said that if he played six rounds with Tolstoy, the opponent would not want to hit him, but he would be beaten enough, but if he played 20 rounds with Tolstoy, he would be knocked off the ear.  He also said that if he could live to sixty, he might defeat Tolstoy.  I guess Hemingway is probably trying to say that some of his works can win Tolstoy, but in general, they can ’ t talk about each other, unless he can create more good works in the future (need to live longer).  What kind of metaphor is used is often related to the personality and creation style of the user.  Pushkin is an emotional romantic poet, in his short life, wrote many beautiful people's poems.  I noticed that Pushkin often compared his beloved poetry to a harp.  So I thought, it must be because this ancient instrument can play a very moving tune, like a poem to move the heart.  Then because of the occasional experience, I have a new feeling about it.  That time was a trip to the Rocky Mountains, staying at the Castle Hotel by Lake Louise.  In the afternoon, a woman dressed like a classical beauty in a long skirt played the harp in the hotel's glittering lobby. Some of the hotel's guests sat, some stood, and listened.  It was at this moment that I suddenly understood why Pushkin used the harp as a metaphor for poetry, because the scenes and atmosphere in the lobby were so romantic.  Unlike Hemingway, his work has created many images of tough men, and he himself loves tough and exciting activities such as bullfighting, horse racing, boxing and hunting, so it is not surprising that he uses boxing as a metaphor.  However, not all people can use the analogy of the things that are "very divided" as Mr. Qian Zhongshu said.  In other words, the winning or losing of a boxing match and the level of a writer were originally two things that could not be fought with eight poles, but Hemingway "closed" them.  The Nobel laureate often had this idea.  His son once copied Turgenev's work and wrote a novel, which Hemingway did not notice at first, and praised his son after reading it.  Of course, he found out later.  However, when someone asked if his son would write a novel, his father ’ s face smiled and replied, “Gregory (his son ’ s name) sometimes does a little lame proofreading. ” Hemingway said this, and the people on the side laughed heartily.  To call plagiarism “lame proofreading ” is not a metaphor, it is hard to say, but I really admire Hemingway ’ s mental flexibility and language wisdom.  Aristotle said, "Parables are the sign of genius." Hemingway was indeed a genius. (From India)

passages.title: Hemingway is 18.
passages.passage: July 24, 2018 04: 10 Hemingway of China Times has written a highly representative work of short stories.  Hemingway's 18-year old book cover. (The author provides) Hemingway's 18-year old has several major events: he decided not to go to college, worked as a reporter, six and a half months in the army, and was immediately injured.  His view of war changed after witnessing the First World War, and at the age of eighteen he was unable to define Hemingway ’ s life.  Hemingway studied a voluminous, visibly staged biography.  This new book, Hemingway ’ s Eighteen Years — A Key Year for American Legendary Writers, takes a different approach, focusing only on the age of eighteen.  The author of the new book has worked for the Kansas City Star for more than 40 years, making good use of the newspaper content of Hemingway during the service period of the newspaper, familiar with the old landscape of the city, and referring to the private letters between Hemingway and friends, showing the details and wisdom that have never been seen before.  The influence of a writer's actual life in a literary work is often difficult to determine.  In particular, the life experience of an individual year does not regulate the literary landscape of mass writers (such as Hemingway).  However, if the information is detailed and involves an important turning point in the planning of a writer's career, or it can be seen that it touches the nourishment of those literary youth to later literary works.  The relevant inference is reasonable, and there is no need to overestimate it, and a net will exhaust the entire literary life of the writer.  Hemingway was eighteen years old From July 21, 1917, until July 20, the following year, several important events of that year are worth mentioning: Hemingway decided not to go to college, left home to work as a reporter for the Kansas City Star, left the army six and a half months later, and was soon wounded in the Italian battlefield.  The family of six children, the cost is already considerable, coupled with the strong mother, want to buy a cottage on the lake in order to practice singing and painting, as far as the doctor father is concerned, the burden of two children going to college at the same time is still a bit heavy.  Her older sister Masilan was a year older, and she dropped out of primary school to study music for a year, so she graduated from the same high school as her younger brother.  In addition, at that time, the United States had announced that it would participate in the First World War, and Hemingway was determined to join the army.  The summer letters show that Hemingway has had various job opportunities, and he has been rather hesitant, but he has no sense of loss in the future.  One of the options was to be introduced by my uncle to the Kansas City Star as a reporter, but that vacancy would have to wait until the fall.  In high school, Hemingway read Shakespeare, wrote a diary, wrote short stories, voted, was interested in news writing, and once heard the retired magazine editor remind: "To learn to write, you have to write."  It happened to be working in the country to make a friend from Kansas City.  Finally, on October 15, he arrived in Kansas City, 500 miles from home, to take up his new job.  A wave of resignation offers new recruits, such as Hemingway, an opportunity to show off their skills.  The senior editor is happy to carry it forward.  The Star ’ s “News Writing Rules ” date back to 1915, and before Hemingway reported, they had changed from oral to internal guidelines.  A total of 110 requests.  Many of them are just common sense, such as: "Elimination of the word".  The opening lines were later distinguished by Hemingway's literary achievements: "In short sentences."  The first few paragraphs of the article are short.  In strong English.  Be positive, not negative.  "There are a lot of good writers among them.  For example, a murder news article mentions how Dostoyevsky, author of Crime and Punishment, understood criminal psychology.  Some commentators believe that the Star News experience makes up for the lack of a formal university education for this young man.  In November 1940, Hemingway and his third wife, Martha Galhoun, passed through Kansas City for an interview with The Star.  At the time, Hemingway's reputation was prominent, and his new book, War Clock, was well received.  Perhaps to be polite, or to be frank, he recalled that the Star ’ s guide to journalistic writing contributed to his clear, concise, and accurate writing style.  Hemingway told reporters: “These are the best writing rules I ’ ve learned.  I never forgot them.  No matter how talented you are, you can write well if you really feel, tell the truth, and follow those writing rules. ”  During Hemingway's time at the Star, Kansas City had a serious drug and alcohol problem.  He knew or heard of street fights, robberies, political squabbles, car accidents, murders, lack of coal in winter, and bad nightlife.  Hemingway has been fascinated with boxing since childhood, and wrote related stories in high school. At this time, he wrote professional boxing news in the Star newspaper, and later mentioned boxers repeatedly in the novel.  Ernest Hemingway was once expelled from the hospital by the management of the hospital, and was very pleased that his report forced the hospital to solve a number of problems.  The Star ’ s work environment is not perfect. While the Star occasionally talks about racial inequality, it doesn ’ t shy away from calling “nigger ” racially biased.  Hemingway blindly followed, the development of social consciousness is incomplete, from the Star newspaper news writing, and later novels and private letters, black people are not shy of the title.  Some of the rumors about Hemingway are not true.  In family letters and private letters to friends, he boasted that he was in love with a popular female star and that his marriage proposal was rejected because the other party did not want to be the widow of a fallen soldier.  Forty-eight years later, the actress was interviewed and said that she had never met Hemingway.  There is a biography of Hemingway saying that he bravely punched people in the restaurant to protect his friends.  Years later, a Star-Telegram colleague said Hemingway was not at the scene.  Hemingway had a weak eye and flat feet, and was unable to join the United States or Canadian forces as he wished.  It happened that colleague Ted Blumbac had been an ambulance driver in the French battlefield for more than five months, and the Star reported on the battlefield.  The newspaper clearly attached importance, listing the initials of the author.  Unless it is a famous writer (such as President Roosevelt, below), most Star articles do not list the author's name, and Hemingway's articles do not even have initials.  Brumbaker's eyes are not good, he was blinded by a single eye injury in college, and at this time easily convinced Hemingway to drive an ambulance to the front line in Italy.  But you have to pass the medical examination of the recruits.  Rumor has it that a friend secretly predicted Hemingway to cheat by memorizing the entire vision test answer.  One of his colleagues falsely testified that Hemingway was twenty-one years old and proficient in French and Italian.  Hemingway's enthusiasm for reporting to the army was quite simple.  Battlefield experience not only provides material for later novels, allowing him to experience a more mature concept of duty and honor, but also changes his vision of war: as the Battlefield Bell shows, abandoning romantic aspirations and replacing them with healthy disillusionment.  At the end of April, Blumbault left with Hemingway, arrived in New York City in mid-May, and then passed through France to Italy.  Hemingway's ambulance team picked up the wounded on the front line during the day.  Two volunteers per vehicle.  Historical records are not sure if he drove the car himself, and if so, how many times he drove it.  The Austrian and Italian forces faced off, separating the two armies on the Piave River. In mid-June, the Austrians failed to cross the river and the Italians captured hundreds of war criminals.  The ambulance team was idle for a while, and Hemingway was bored. In late June, he seized the opportunity to leave his current unit and transfer food to the front trenches.  Hemingway moved to the city of Fortholta, just twenty yards from the Piave River, and rode his bicycle to the Italian trenches every day.  Late at night on July 8, an Austrian bomb exploded three feet from Hemingway in a bomb shelter at the Forward Listening Station by the river.  An Italian soldier was killed and Hemingway wounded on the spot between the bomb site and Hemingway.  Blumbac visited the Red Cross Hospital in Milan and wrote to Hemingway ’ s family to report his injuries.  Later letters from Brumbach and Hemingway described how, after being wounded, a wounded Italian soldier had been moved to safety before he lost his sanity.
