passages.title: How to read Hemingway?
passages.passage: Ernest Hemingway, a Nobel laureate and one of the most important of the 20th century, was born on July 21, 1899 in Illinois and wrote seven novels, six collections of short stories and two nonfiction books during his lifetime.  On the occasion of the birth of this author, which coincided with the thirteenth of July, we have suggestions for better reading of the works of this author.  Hemingway ’ s work is fluid, simple, and clear, but for many readers of literature, it may be difficult to begin reading Hemingway ’ s books.  Why read Hemingway?  Ernest Hemingway is an influential writer in the history of literature and fiction, his works have repeatedly won the most prestigious international literary awards such as Nobel and Pulitzer, this author employed a different kind of narrative description and caused many writers after him to borrow his own literary style.  Hemingway has named his literary style the Iceberg Theory, in this way of writing, fictional events are narrated like an iceberg floating in water, only one-eighth of which is visible, and the author includes only the information that is essential in the process and omits the rest of the information.  This technique created a tremendous change in storytelling, especially the writing of short stories, and it was a development that freed the stories from conventional chatter.  Hemingway ’ s works are included in the list of books of the century, books to read before death, and the best fiction books in history, highlighting the importance of this author.  What do we need to know?  One of the topics that helps to better understand Ernest Hemingway ’ s work is getting to know his personal life.  Much of what we read in his books is what he has turned from his personal life into a story.  At the age of 19, he volunteered for the First World War but was not allowed to fight because of poor eyesight, but Hemingway insisted on serving as an ambulance driver for the Red Cross.  He was wounded several times during the Chang, but his most significant injury is when he was wounded by mortar shell fragments and spent a long time in the hospital, a novel about this part of Hemingway ’ s life and the war.  Even the character of Catherine Barkley in this book is based on the nurse Hemingway fell in love with.  Hemingway also participated in World War II as a war correspondent, and several short stories are the result of this era.  The sun continues to blow, the Great River or along the river to the trees, each of which is somehow tied to the World War, and their heroes are survivors of the war and have many memories of these days.  But Hemingway ’ s most important masterpiece is a relic of his childhood, Hemingway ’ s father had a great interest in fishing, and this hobby was passed on to Ernest, a point that can be clearly seen in the famous and widely read story of The Old Man and the Sea.  But before the Old Man and the Sea, Hemingway had written about having and not having a fishing boat captain.  Another important point to know before reading Hemingway ’ s works is his political approach, he has written a lot in opposition to fascism and against dictatorship, both as a journalist and as a writer, sometimes even changing from a journalist to a social-political activist, who is this point in The Bell for, or who is this death knell?  It is a story of an American soldier in the Spanish Civil War fighting alongside groups against General Franco, which Hemingway did.  Perhaps the other thing that matters is that during the World War, Hemingway led a French group against the Nazis that was tried after the war for armed acts but was never proven guilty.  The political and social history of the world in the years of Hemingway's life, his personal life, as well as the knowledge of his contemporaries, such as Scott Fitzgerald, with whom he has written, are points that contribute to the understanding of his works.  Getting to know Hemingway ’ s contemporary writers helps to better understand the difference between him and his contemporaries.  Is it a classic?  To read Hemingway ’ s work, we must note that he is not a classic writer in his different style, he did not deal with the long margins and descriptions of classical literature, and his long novels are not immune.  He was interested in shorthand and engaging the audience with fiction, which is a feature of modern literature.  In general, Hemingway ’ s works are innovative and even among modern works have their own creativity, but the value of this author ’ s work has always been compared to classical works, and even classical enthusiasts have not been able to be indifferent to it.  In these works we have a happy and well-spoken writer, a writer who was in middle age with young people and was even close friends with a group of hippies.  Hemingway is a realistic writer, but he has always tried to maintain his sense of humor.  Where do we start?  To read Hemingway ’ s works, the first and most important suggestion is The Old Man and the Sea.  The book, translated by Najaf Daryabandari, was published in 222 pages by Kharazmi Publications.  The next book, Farewell to Arms, is again translated by Najaf Daryabendari, published by Amir Kabir Publications in 343 pages.  These two books are always on the list of works to be read or masterpieces of the 20th century.  If you are interested in short stories, you can also read Men Without Women, a collection of stories that have been published in various magazines by the author.  This book has been translated by Asadollah Amraei for publication of Horizon in 222 pages.  Even if you are interested in writing, Hemingway can be a good teacher and read his series of talks and learn very precise points.  The book The Last Interview and Other Conversations of Ernest Hemingway with a translation by Houshang Jirani has been published in 88 pages by Cheshmeh Publishing.  The final chapter of many critics considered Ernest Hemingway to be the greatest writer of the 20th century.  His stories are an exploration of real human life, suffering and the meaning of life.  The portrayal of human inner feelings is the most important characteristic of this author, which makes his works a read for every reader.  Who was Ernest Hemingway?  Ernest Hemingway was born on July 21, 1899 in Oak Park, Illinois.  His father, Clarence, was a doctor and his mother, Grace, was a piano and singing teacher.  Ernest spent the summers with his family in northern Michigan, where he discovered his passion for fishing.  After finishing high school, he worked for a while in Kansas City as a reporter for the Star Chronicle in 1917.  During World War I, he volunteered to serve in the army, but poor eyesight prevented him from doing so, instead serving as an ambulance driver for the Red Cross near the Italian front.  On July 8, 1918, he was injured and spent months in the hospital.  In 1925, his first collection of short stories, in our time, was published, which spoke well of his particular style.  His memoirs from that period were published after his death in 1964 as The Variable Eid.  Ernest Hemingway was an adventurer for most of his life.  From being wounded in Italy by 200 pieces of Austrian shrapnel during World War I, to taking part in the frontlines of the Spanish Civil War or touring the African wilderness, to fishing and hunting wildlife and living in Cuba.  He finally said goodbye to life with his hunting rifle.

He told me this short story about the nature of the effects of the effects of Hemingway.  That his stories were the closest thing to reality, but he put pure reality into artistic form and made it a pure story.  That Hemingway ’ s work is easy to read while it is easy to read, but understanding its deep layers may not be as easy as it seems. Maryam Saheli, author and lecturer of the Anzali Thousand and One Nights Story Society and the host of the program, said: Ernest Miller Hemingway was a writer with many biological experiences. Unlike some great storytellers, who only a specific audience of fiction is willing to read their stories, Hemingway ’ s works are pleasant for a specific and general audience. Ernest Hemingway was a renowned American writer, born in Oak Park, Illinois, who is famous for his unique writing style characterized by polished and concise language.

Hemingway's writing style is often described as simple and clear, yet powerful and evocative. 
He believed that "the sayings must be said in the unspoken" [249f068a-f51d-45b1-85a5-fec8b8c7de32]. 
This philosophy is reflected in his writing, where he omits unnecessary words to convey a powerful message.

Hemingway's literary style is often compared to an iceberg, with only a small portion of the text visible above the surface [5f24ee94-9596-438b-ac27-b252fccf62e3]. 
This analogy was popularized by Hemingway himself, who said that "prose is like architecture, not interior decoration" [60159e17-f50a-427c-aee9-32ac141efd2a]. 
According to Hemingway, if a writer has a clear idea of what they want to convey, they can omit unnecessary details and still create a powerful impression on the reader.

Hemingway's writing style has been praised for its ability to convey complex emotions and ideas through simple, concise language. 
His use of short sentences and sparse descriptions creates a sense of intimacy and immediacy, drawing the reader into the world of the story [60159e17-f50a-427c-aee9-32ac141efd2a].

Many critics have praised Hemingway's writing style, saying that it is a hallmark of his unique literary voice. 
According to one critic, "Hemingway's writing is like a scalpel, cutting through the noise and getting to the heart of the matter" [5f24ee94-9596-438b-ac27-b252fccf62e3].

Despite the simplicity of his writing style, Hemingway's works are often complex and layered, with multiple themes and motifs woven throughout the text. 
His use of symbolism, imagery, and other literary devices adds depth and complexity to his writing, making it more than just a simple, straightforward narrative [60159e17-f50a-427c-aee9-32ac141efd2a].

Hemingway's writing style has also been influenced by his experiences as a journalist and war correspondent. 
His time in the trenches of World War I and the Spanish Civil War had a profound impact on his writing, shaping his views on war, humanity, and the nature of reality [4e834b0f-1217-47cf-9407-8ae45e74f7c7].

In conclusion, Ernest Hemingway's writing style is a unique and powerful blend of simplicity, clarity, and complexity. 
His use of concise language, sparse descriptions, and literary devices creates a sense of intimacy and immediacy, drawing the reader into the world of the story. 
Whether writing about war, humanity, or the natural world, Hemingway's writing style is a hallmark of his literary voice and a testament to his enduring legacy as one of the greatest writers of the 20th century [249f068a-f51d-45b1-85a5-fec8b8c7de32].

Hemingway's writing style is also characterized by its honesty and directness. 
He believed that "the only thing that interests anyone is how you get away with it" [4e834b0f-1217-47cf-9407-8ae45e74f7c7]. 
This philosophy is reflected in his writing, where he often presents a raw and unvarnished view of the world, without apology or pretension.

In addition to his writing style, Hemingway was also known for his love of nature and his desire to explore the natural world through his writing.

Hemingway's writing style is also characterized by its use of understatement and subtlety.

Title: The Creator of Short Expressions in Long Stories
Content: He said, “The works of a man who writes short and clear are like a beautiful iceberg, only an eighth of which is out of the water. ”  Ernest Hemingway was born in Oak Park, Illinois.  His father was a doctor and his mother was a piano teacher and very religious.  While her mother engaged her in church and hymns, her father took her fishing and taught her how to use guns.  At school, he was fascinated by his literary teacher: “I liked his look and his expression.  I felt that there was something in me that he said well in the form of literature and poetry that he read. ” His first writings were published in the school newspaper.  After high school, he reported for magazines.  She was 19 years old when she was injured as a volunteer in the First World War and spent a long time in hospital to remove 200 pieces of shrapnel from her body.  After returning from the war, he wrote in magazines.  At the age of 22, he moved to Paris as a reporter, married his colleague Hadley Richardson, and his wife set out for the Greco-Turkish War.  There, Hemingway found his former friend James Joyce, who inspired him to publish the story.  In Paris he achieved his own style: “The sayings must be said in the unspoken. ”  He writes with clear, short, adjective-free phrases and sentences that look like aphorisms, but fills the reader with a sense of empathy or aversion to his characters.  He was 53 years old when he published his most enduring work, The Old Man and the Sea, for which he received a Nobel Prize in Literature.  In addition to adventure, fishing, hunting, and weapons, he was also interested in cooking and bullfighting, and reflected these interests in his stories.  His hamburger recipe recently ended up at the John F. Kennedy Museum in Boston.  Hemingway ’ s adventures were not limited to war and travel to Africa, but also to unknown places and new situations, car and air accidents, malaria, skin cancer, pneumonia, hepatitis, multiple fractures and kidney problems.  He had a popular collection of weapons, and his death was shaped by one of them.  Ernest Hemingway committed suicide in Idaho at the age of 61.

The influence of the rookie reporter period on his career also corresponds to the iceberg theory he proposed in 1932: "Prose is like architecture, not interior decoration, and the Baroque era is over... If you have enough understanding of what you are describing and write well enough, even if you write only one-eighth of the text, you can let the reader fully grasp the scene, plot and character description that he wants to express." Hemingway often uses a concise style to bury clues in the details or background, so that it is connected with emotional intimacy.  Paris was not only the place where Hemingway worked as a journalist, but also the beginning of his literary career.  The first two books, Three Stories & Ten Poems, and a collection of short stories, in our time, were published here.  Ernest Hemingway wrote many notes about his life and literary work in the 1920s. Two boxes were left in the basement of the Ritz Hotel in Paris, and when he returned to Paris in 1957, he opened these dusty old memories, namely, "The Feast on the Move".  This prose memoir of Paris also later became a guide for people on their pilgrimage journey, following Hemingway for a drink, order a cup of coffee at the Lilac Café, borrow a book at Shakespeare ’ s Bookstore on the Rue d ’ Odeon, and then take a walk in Luxembourg Park.  “If you are lucky enough to have lived in Paris as a young man, then wherever you go for the rest of your life it stays with you, for Paris is a movable feast. ” — Ernest Hemingway A moving feast.  Shakespeare Bookstore (Photo / Courtesy of Blue Bird) Mr. Chen then pointed out on the map several places where Hemingway often stopped in Paris. First came to the Shakespeare Bookstore, which is also like a library, which can rent books at affordable prices, and also provides mail collection services, which is suitable for young and poor boy Hemingway.  The owner of the bookstore, Shelville Beach, is also an American, and in her autobiography, Shakespeare's Bookstore, there is a chapter entitled "The Best Customer Hemingway".  In his translation of the book, Mr. Chen found hundreds of references to Hemingway, and the description of his affinity showed their deep and warm friendship at the time.  At the end of World War II, Hemingway returns to Paris with the Americans and meets Chevelle again.  There are still a lot of gun battles in the theater street, and we ’ ve had enough.  One day a jeep pulled into the street and stopped at the door of my bookstore.  I heard a low voice shouting, “Chevy! ” and it spread all over the street.  Edhiena cried, "It's Hemingway! It's Hemingway!" I rushed downstairs and hit the oncoming Hemingway.  He picked me up in circles and kissed me, and the people at the window of the street cheered … He asked if there was anything else I could do, and I said if I could get rid of the Nazi snipers on the roof of the street, especially those on Edsieena ’ s roof.  He called his buddies out of their jeeps, took them all to the roof, and then came the last gunfight on Theater Street.  Hemingway got down with his men and drove off in the jeep — next, Hemingway said, to the wine cellar at the Ritz.  The Lilac Garden Cafe (Photo / Courtesy of the Blue Bird House) The Lilac Garden on the Boulevard Montparnasse is the place where the artistic and cultural trends of Paris in the 1920s met and collided, and where Fitzgerald, Zola, Cezanne and Picasso all stopped.  “I sat in the corner writing with my notebook, and the afternoon sun was on my shoulders.  The waiter took me a cup of hot cream coffee (café crème), and I drank half of it after cooling, and the other half was on the table while I was writing.  When I stopped writing, I really didn ’ t want to leave the river where the trout could be seen in the pool. ” — Chen Jung-bin, author of “Feast on the Move, ” mentioned this text, poetically describing the process of creating the novel“ Our Time ” in Lilac Garden, and the river where the trout can be seen is the title of the book, “The Big Twin Heart River. ”  A Good Café on the Place St.-Michel "A girl walks into a cafe and sits alone at a table by the window.  She was beautiful, and her face was as fresh as a new coin — if only coins could be minted with silky muscles and rain-washed skin.  Her hair was as dark as the wings of a raven, cut into a blade, and covered her face obliquely.  I stared at her, and she disturbed my thoughts and made me very excited.  I wanted to put her in my novel or something, but she was sitting where she could see the street and the entrance to the cafe, so I knew she was waiting for someone.  So I continued to write.  The story seemed to unfold automatically, and my pen managed to keep up with it.  I ordered another glass of St. James ’ s brandy.  Whenever I raised my head or sharpened the pencil with a sharpener, I would look at the girl and let the curly scraps fall into the saucer under the glass. "  "I see you, my beauty, now you belong to me, no matter who you are waiting for, and no matter whether I can see you again in the future," I thought.  You belong to me, and all Paris belongs to me, and I belong to this notebook and this pencil.  From this Paris memoir, Teacher Chen Jung-bin led us to read this famous article. Reading this text, we followed Hemingway ’ s eyes, met the girl who distracted him in a cafe next to the square, took control between the mind and the pen, and then sat in the whole Paris.  Hemingway and Fitzgerald Fitzgerald (Photo / Courtesy of Blue Bird) Hemingway and artists from all walks of life in Paris, and Fitzgerald also met here, they first met at Dingo American Bar, and each other's affirmation is extremely sincere.  Hemingway left such a comment on Fitzgerald in "The Moving Feast": After reading "The Tycoon", he felt that no matter what outrageous things Fitzgerald did, he had to treat it as if Fitzgerald was sick, and he had to try to help him from the standpoint of a friend, "because, if he could write such a book, he could write a better book." This is probably the biggest compliment Hemingway has ever given to any of his peers.  Fitzgerald also gave Hemingway "He's the real thing." Title: Hemingway and Liao Hui-ying
Content: Ken Burns ’ six-hour documentary film for Hemingway was shown on the public television network yesterday. Burns has a lot of good work, but this is only the second time the writer has been featured, 20 years since he last shot Mark Twain.  PBS broadcasts for three days.  Ernest Hemingway is a good subject, 61 years old American Nobel Prize-winning writer who committed suicide, life is big river and sea, married four times, went hunting down the sea to fish, the United States of the Great Depression, Europe in war, he has lived brilliantly, can be drunk in a small bar, but can write like a practice, the text is simple, you can not look through the dictionary, but like "war dream" At the end of ell To Arms, the author changed the volume 47 times.  Reading and reading are two different things.  Take the short article "Indian Camp" (Indian Camp) less than three pages, for example, born from Hemingway's childhood, the little boy Nick with the father of a rural doctor, in the middle of the night to the Indian camp, a woman has a difficult birth, the doctor uses a folding knife to cut the abdomen, the woman screams the child all the way to the floor, Nick side to help the father, and then everyone found that the woman's husband has been lying on the double bed, Knife kills itself.  Nick rowed home with his father in the morning light, asking big questions about life and death.  In the end, Hemingway wrote that Little Nick felt that he would never die.  All right, it's over. People familiar with Liao said that in fact, to show such a big wound to people to see, Liao Huiying is not prepared, almost to go up to see the script, but can not turn his face away, had to say the part with reservations.  Very ungrateful.  Look at Hemingway, also see his big man in the image of the unbearable, young in Italy injured not dead, a lifetime afraid to sleep alone.  The second wife is the best friend of the first wife, rich daughter, Hemingway eating soft rice, repeatedly deceiving the pillow people, his image is a pile of lies. Title: Hemingway's Myth
Content: In 1953, Hemingway was sitting at a dinner table at his camp in Kenya, writing. (NARA, Photographer, Look Magazine) Anyone familiar with American literature and literary criticism should know the iceberg talk about literary creation.  The author of this statement is the famous American writer and Nobel Prize winner Ernest Hemingway.  The main point is that if a writer has a mind about what he wants to write, he can omit something he knows when he creates, and the reader will feel those omissions because the author is writing true.  It is like an iceberg that looks magnificent as it moves in the sea, but in fact only one-eighth of it is out of the water, and the invisible part is more and more real.  In the theory of ancient Chinese poetry creation, there is a saying of "artistic conception", emphasizing the scenes and emotions depicted through the works, stimulating the imagination of the readers, and leaving them a space for full reflection and play.  This is synonymous with the "iceberg theory", but Hemingway emphasized the authenticity of the work, aiming to criticize some writers who seemed to him to be quite incompetent, who simply "omitted something because they did not understand".  Hemingway ’ s “iceberg talk ” actually interprets his own creative style, which is to omit everything he thinks is optional in his writing, and to be as simple and implicit as possible.  This creative style of Hemingway is indeed unique and has had a profound impact, some even said: Hemingway with no one has the courage, "English attached to the literature of the hair cut clean." But what interests me is that he uses the "iceberg" as a metaphor.  This analogy is really good.  What people usually use as metaphors are some common things, such as peach blossoms in "face like peach blossoms" and torches in "eyes like torches". How many people have seen an iceberg?  Three years ago, I went to Alaska to visit, and all I saw was a large piece of ice floe on the sea surface, real sea icebergs, probably only in the South Pole and Arctic areas where ordinary people are difficult to set foot.  However, this parable is also very relevant and can make people understand God.  What you can read in a good work is certainly brilliant, like the magnificence of an iceberg above the surface of the water, but what it contains can be much wider and deeper than the literal meaning, like a much larger body of mountain undersea support.  Without the presence of seven eighths below, there is no beauty at the top.  In the book of Revelation, there is a great deal to be said about the use of metaphors.  He said that the metaphor contains two aspects that are opposite and complementary, and the things that are compared must be the same, otherwise they cannot be joined together; but at the same time, they must be different, otherwise they cannot be distinguished.  As for the interaction between the two, the greater the difference, the more the same thing will be baked; the more open it will be, the more unexpected it will be, the more novel the metaphor will be, and the better the effect will be.  According to the theory of Qian Zhongshu, Hemingway uses the iceberg as a metaphor, and the things that belong to it are "very divided", and it has indeed produced a surprising winning effect, so it is unforgettable.  There are many other examples of this in the metaphor Hemingway has used.  After Hemingway became famous, he often compared himself with other writers, and was quite conceited, many writers he could not see, and only Shakespeare and Tolstoy were really admired.  He did not know this, but used boxing as a metaphor.  He said that he did not want to play Dostoyevsky in the first game, because he knew that Dostoyevsky was almost as good as he was, so he chose to play with Turgenev first because he felt he could play with him.  Then try Maupassant again, although it is difficult, but also can beat him; as for Henry James, he said, "As soon as I catch me, I press him, and immediately give him a blow where he has no meat, so tell the referee to stop the game." Hemingway's words, you can see his confidence.  About him and Cervantes who is stronger, he has a different saying, he believes that 20 rounds of war, you can beat the other side of the fart, but also admitted that Mr. Cervantes is very shrewd, while playing and learning, maybe the second game he will lose to the other side.  In Hemingway ’ s eyes, Shakespeare is the champion who can ’ t beat.  And speaking of Tolstoy, whom he equally admired, he said something different.  He said that if he played six rounds with Tolstoy, the opponent would not want to hit him, but he would be beaten enough, but if he played 20 rounds with Tolstoy, he would be knocked off the ear.  He also said that if he could live to sixty, he might defeat Tolstoy.  I guess Hemingway is probably trying to say that some of his works can win Tolstoy, but in general, they can ’ t talk about each other, unless he can create more good works in the future (need to live longer).  What kind of metaphor is used is often related to the personality and creation style of the user.  Pushkin is an emotional romantic poet, in his short life, wrote many beautiful people's poems.  I noticed that Pushkin often compared his beloved poetry to a harp.  So I thought, it must be because this ancient instrument can play a very moving tune, like a poem to move the heart.  Then because of the occasional experience, I have a new feeling about it.  That time was a trip to the Rocky Mountains, staying at the Castle Hotel by Lake Louise.  In the afternoon, a woman dressed like a classical beauty in a long skirt played the harp in the hotel's glittering lobby. Some of the hotel's guests sat, some stood, and listened.  It was at this moment that I suddenly understood why Pushkin used the harp as a metaphor for poetry, because the scenes and atmosphere in the lobby were so romantic.  Unlike Hemingway, his work has created many images of tough men, and he himself loves tough and exciting activities such as bullfighting, horse racing, boxing and hunting, so it is not surprising that he uses boxing as a metaphor.  However, not all people can use the analogy of the things that are "very divided" as Mr. Qian Zhongshu said.  In other words, the winning or losing of a boxing match and the level of a writer were originally two things that could not be fought with eight poles, but Hemingway "closed" them.  The Nobel laureate often had this idea.  His son once copied Turgenev's work and wrote a novel, which Hemingway did not notice at first, and praised his son after reading it.  Of course, he found out later.  However, when someone asked if his son would write a novel, his father ’ s face smiled and replied, “Gregory (his son ’ s name) sometimes does a little lame proofreading. ” Hemingway said this, and the people on the side laughed heartily.  To call plagiarism “lame proofreading ” is not a metaphor, it is hard to say, but I really admire Hemingway ’ s mental flexibility and language wisdom.  Aristotle said, "Parables are the sign of genius." Hemingway was indeed a genius. (From India)

Title: Hemingway is 18.
Content: July 24, 2018 04: 10 Hemingway of China Times has written a highly representative work of short stories.  Hemingway's 18-year old book cover. (The author provides) Hemingway's 18-year old has several major events: he decided not to go to college, worked as a reporter, six and a half months in the army, and was immediately injured.  His view of war changed after witnessing the First World War, and at the age of eighteen he was unable to define Hemingway ’ s life.  Hemingway studied a voluminous, visibly staged biography.  This new book, Hemingway ’ s Eighteen Years — A Key Year for American Legendary Writers, takes a different approach, focusing only on the age of eighteen.  The author of the new book has worked for the Kansas City Star for more than 40 years, making good use of the newspaper content of Hemingway during the service period of the newspaper, familiar with the old landscape of the city, and referring to the private letters between Hemingway and friends, showing the details and wisdom that have never been seen before.  The influence of a writer's actual life in a literary work is often difficult to determine.  In particular, the life experience of an individual year does not regulate the literary landscape of mass writers (such as Hemingway).  However, if the information is detailed and involves an important turning point in the planning of a writer's career, or it can be seen that it touches the nourishment of those literary youth to later literary works.  The relevant inference is reasonable, and there is no need to overestimate it, and a net will exhaust the entire literary life of the writer.  Hemingway was eighteen years old From July 21, 1917, until July 20, the following year, several important events of that year are worth mentioning: Hemingway decided not to go to college, left home to work as a reporter for the Kansas City Star, left the army six and a half months later, and was soon wounded in the Italian battlefield.  The family of six children, the cost is already considerable, coupled with the strong mother, want to buy a cottage on the lake in order to practice singing and painting, as far as the doctor father is concerned, the burden of two children going to college at the same time is still a bit heavy.  Her older sister Masilan was a year older, and she dropped out of primary school to study music for a year, so she graduated from the same high school as her younger brother.  In addition, at that time, the United States had announced that it would participate in the First World War, and Hemingway was determined to join the army.  The summer letters show that Hemingway has had various job opportunities, and he has been rather hesitant, but he has no sense of loss in the future.  One of the options was to be introduced by my uncle to the Kansas City Star as a reporter, but that vacancy would have to wait until the fall.  In high school, Hemingway read Shakespeare, wrote a diary, wrote short stories, voted, was interested in news writing, and once heard the retired magazine editor remind: "To learn to write, you have to write."  It happened to be working in the country to make a friend from Kansas City.  Finally, on October 15, he arrived in Kansas City, 500 miles from home, to take up his new job.  A wave of resignation offers new recruits, such as Hemingway, an opportunity to show off their skills.  The senior editor is happy to carry it forward.  The Star ’ s “News Writing Rules ” date back to 1915, and before Hemingway reported, they had changed from oral to internal guidelines.  A total of 110 requests.  Many of them are just common sense, such as: "Elimination of the word".  The opening lines were later distinguished by Hemingway's literary achievements: "In short sentences."  The first few paragraphs of the article are short.  In strong English.  Be positive, not negative.  "There are a lot of good writers among them.  For example, a murder news article mentions how Dostoyevsky, author of Crime and Punishment, understood criminal psychology.  Some commentators believe that the Star News experience makes up for the lack of a formal university education for this young man.  In November 1940, Hemingway and his third wife, Martha Galhoun, passed through Kansas City for an interview with The Star.  At the time, Hemingway's reputation was prominent, and his new book, War Clock, was well received.  Perhaps to be polite, or to be frank, he recalled that the Star ’ s guide to journalistic writing contributed to his clear, concise, and accurate writing style.  Hemingway told reporters: “These are the best writing rules I ’ ve learned.  I never forgot them.  No matter how talented you are, you can write well if you really feel, tell the truth, and follow those writing rules. ”  During Hemingway's time at the Star, Kansas City had a serious drug and alcohol problem.  He knew or heard of street fights, robberies, political squabbles, car accidents, murders, lack of coal in winter, and bad nightlife.  Hemingway has been fascinated with boxing since childhood, and wrote related stories in high school. At this time, he wrote professional boxing news in the Star newspaper, and later mentioned boxers repeatedly in the novel.  Ernest Hemingway was once expelled from the hospital by the management of the hospital, and was very pleased that his report forced the hospital to solve a number of problems.  The Star ’ s work environment is not perfect. While the Star occasionally talks about racial inequality, it doesn ’ t shy away from calling “nigger ” racially biased.  Hemingway blindly followed, the development of social consciousness is incomplete, from the Star newspaper news writing, and later novels and private letters, black people are not shy of the title.  Some of the rumors about Hemingway are not true.  In family letters and private letters to friends, he boasted that he was in love with a popular female star and that his marriage proposal was rejected because the other party did not want to be the widow of a fallen soldier.  Forty-eight years later, the actress was interviewed and said that she had never met Hemingway.  There is a biography of Hemingway saying that he bravely punched people in the restaurant to protect his friends.  Years later, a Star-Telegram colleague said Hemingway was not at the scene.  Hemingway had a weak eye and flat feet, and was unable to join the United States or Canadian forces as he wished.  It happened that colleague Ted Blumbac had been an ambulance driver in the French battlefield for more than five months, and the Star reported on the battlefield.  The newspaper clearly attached importance, listing the initials of the author.  Unless it is a famous writer (such as President Roosevelt, below), most Star articles do not list the author's name, and Hemingway's articles do not even have initials.  Brumbaker's eyes are not good, he was blinded by a single eye injury in college, and at this time easily convinced Hemingway to drive an ambulance to the front line in Italy.  But you have to pass the medical examination of the recruits.  Rumor has it that a friend secretly predicted Hemingway to cheat by memorizing the entire vision test answer.  One of his colleagues falsely testified that Hemingway was twenty-one years old and proficient in French and Italian.  Hemingway's enthusiasm for reporting to the army was quite simple.  Battlefield experience not only provides material for later novels, allowing him to experience a more mature concept of duty and honor, but also changes his vision of war: as the Battlefield Bell shows, abandoning romantic aspirations and replacing them with healthy disillusionment.  At the end of April, Blumbault left with Hemingway, arrived in New York City in mid-May, and then passed through France to Italy.  Hemingway's ambulance team picked up the wounded on the front line during the day.  Two volunteers per vehicle.  Historical records are not sure if he drove the car himself, and if so, how many times he drove it.  The Austrian and Italian forces faced off, separating the two armies on the Piave River. In mid-June, the Austrians failed to cross the river and the Italians captured hundreds of war criminals.  The ambulance team was idle for a while, and Hemingway was bored. In late June, he seized the opportunity to leave his current unit and transfer food to the front trenches.  Hemingway moved to the city of Fortholta, just twenty yards from the Piave River, and rode his bicycle to the Italian trenches every day.  Late at night on July 8, an Austrian bomb exploded three feet from Hemingway in a bomb shelter at the Forward Listening Station by the river.  An Italian soldier was killed and Hemingway wounded on the spot between the bomb site and Hemingway.  Blumbac visited the Red Cross Hospital in Milan and wrote to Hemingway ’ s family to report his injuries.  Later letters from Brumbach and Hemingway described how, after being wounded, a wounded Italian soldier had been moved to safety before he lost his sanity. Title: How to read Hemingway?
Content: Ernest Hemingway, a Nobel laureate and one of the most important of the 20th century, was born on July 21, 1899 in Illinois and wrote seven novels, six collections of short stories and two nonfiction books during his lifetime.  On the occasion of the birth of this author, which coincided with the thirteenth of July, we have suggestions for better reading of the works of this author.  Hemingway ’ s work is fluid, simple, and clear, but for many readers of literature, it may be difficult to begin reading Hemingway ’ s books.  Why read Hemingway?  Ernest Hemingway is an influential writer in the history of literature and fiction, his works have repeatedly won the most prestigious international literary awards such as Nobel and Pulitzer, this author employed a different kind of narrative description and caused many writers after him to borrow his own literary style.  Hemingway has named his literary style the Iceberg Theory, in this way of writing, fictional events are narrated like an iceberg floating in water, only one-eighth of which is visible, and the author includes only the information that is essential in the process and omits the rest of the information.  This technique created a tremendous change in storytelling, especially the writing of short stories, and it was a development that freed the stories from conventional chatter.  Hemingway ’ s works are included in the list of books of the century, books to read before death, and the best fiction books in history, highlighting the importance of this author.  What do we need to know?  One of the topics that helps to better understand Ernest Hemingway ’ s work is getting to know his personal life.  Much of what we read in his books is what he has turned from his personal life into a story.  At the age of 19, he volunteered for the First World War but was not allowed to fight because of poor eyesight, but Hemingway insisted on serving as an ambulance driver for the Red Cross.  He was wounded several times during the Chang, but his most significant injury is when he was wounded by mortar shell fragments and spent a long time in the hospital, a novel about this part of Hemingway ’ s life and the war.  Even the character of Catherine Barkley in this book is based on the nurse Hemingway fell in love with.  Hemingway also participated in World War II as a war correspondent, and several short stories are the result of this era.  The sun continues to blow, the Great River or along the river to the trees, each of which is somehow tied to the World War, and their heroes are survivors of the war and have many memories of these days.  But Hemingway ’ s most important masterpiece is a relic of his childhood, Hemingway ’ s father had a great interest in fishing, and this hobby was passed on to Ernest, a point that can be clearly seen in the famous and widely read story of The Old Man and the Sea.  But before the Old Man and the Sea, Hemingway had written about having and not having a fishing boat captain.  Another important point to know before reading Hemingway ’ s works is his political approach, he has written a lot in opposition to fascism and against dictatorship, both as a journalist and as a writer, sometimes even changing from a journalist to a social-political activist, who is this point in The Bell for, or who is this death knell?  It is a story of an American soldier in the Spanish Civil War fighting alongside groups against General Franco, which Hemingway did.  Perhaps the other thing that matters is that during the World War, Hemingway led a French group against the Nazis that was tried after the war for armed acts but was never proven guilty.  The political and social history of the world in the years of Hemingway's life, his personal life, as well as the knowledge of his contemporaries, such as Scott Fitzgerald, with whom he has written, are points that contribute to the understanding of his works.  Getting to know Hemingway ’ s contemporary writers helps to better understand the difference between him and his contemporaries.  Is it a classic?  To read Hemingway ’ s work, we must note that he is not a classic writer in his different style, he did not deal with the long margins and descriptions of classical literature, and his long novels are not immune.  He was interested in shorthand and engaging the audience with fiction, which is a feature of modern literature.  In general, Hemingway ’ s works are innovative and even among modern works have their own creativity, but the value of this author ’ s work has always been compared to classical works, and even classical enthusiasts have not been able to be indifferent to it.  In these works we have a happy and well-spoken writer, a writer who was in middle age with young people and was even close friends with a group of hippies.  Hemingway is a realistic writer, but he has always tried to maintain his sense of humor.  Where do we start?  To read Hemingway ’ s works, the first and most important suggestion is The Old Man and the Sea.  The book, translated by Najaf Daryabandari, was published in 222 pages by Kharazmi Publications.  The next book, Farewell to Arms, is again translated by Najaf Daryabendari, published by Amir Kabir Publications in 343 pages.  These two books are always on the list of works to be read or masterpieces of the 20th century.  If you are interested in short stories, you can also read Men Without Women, a collection of stories that have been published in various magazines by the author.  This book has been translated by Asadollah Amraei for publication of Horizon in 222 pages.  Even if you are interested in writing, Hemingway can be a good teacher and read his series of talks and learn very precise points.  The book The Last Interview and Other Conversations of Ernest Hemingway with a translation by Houshang Jirani has been published in 88 pages by Cheshmeh Publishing.  The final chapter of many critics considered Ernest Hemingway to be the greatest writer of the 20th century.  His stories are an exploration of real human life, suffering and the meaning of life.  The portrayal of human inner feelings is the most important characteristic of this author, which makes his works a read for every reader.  Who was Ernest Hemingway?  Ernest Hemingway was born on July 21, 1899 in Oak Park, Illinois.  His father, Clarence, was a doctor and his mother, Grace, was a piano and singing teacher.  Ernest spent the summers with his family in northern Michigan, where he discovered his passion for fishing.  After finishing high school, he worked for a while in Kansas City as a reporter for the Star Chronicle in 1917.  During World War I, he volunteered to serve in the army, but poor eyesight prevented him from doing so, instead serving as an ambulance driver for the Red Cross near the Italian front.  On July 8, 1918, he was injured and spent months in the hospital.  In 1925, his first collection of short stories, in our time, was published, which spoke well of his particular style.  His memoirs from that period were published after his death in 1964 as The Variable Eid.  Ernest Hemingway was an adventurer for most of his life.  From being wounded in Italy by 200 pieces of Austrian shrapnel during World War I, to taking part in the frontlines of the Spanish Civil War or touring the African wilderness, to fishing and hunting wildlife and living in Cuba.  He finally said goodbye to life with his hunting rifle.

Title: The Creator of Short Expressions in Long Stories
Content: He said, “The works of a man who writes short and clear are like a beautiful iceberg, only an eighth of which is out of the water. ”  Ernest Hemingway was born in Oak Park, Illinois.  His father was a doctor and his mother was a piano teacher and very religious.  While her mother engaged her in church and hymns, her father took her fishing and taught her how to use guns.  At school, he was fascinated by his literary teacher: “I liked his look and his expression.  I felt that there was something in me that he said well in the form of literature and poetry that he read. ” His first writings were published in the school newspaper.  After high school, he reported for magazines.  She was 19 years old when she was injured as a volunteer in the First World War and spent a long time in hospital to remove 200 pieces of shrapnel from her body.  After returning from the war, he wrote in magazines.  At the age of 22, he moved to Paris as a reporter, married his colleague Hadley Richardson, and his wife set out for the Greco-Turkish War.  There, Hemingway found his former friend James Joyce, who inspired him to publish the story.  In Paris he achieved his own style: “The sayings must be said in the unspoken. ”  He writes with clear, short, adjective-free phrases and sentences that look like aphorisms, but fills the reader with a sense of empathy or aversion to his characters.  He was 53 years old when he published his most enduring work, The Old Man and the Sea, for which he received a Nobel Prize in Literature.  In addition to adventure, fishing, hunting, and weapons, he was also interested in cooking and bullfighting, and reflected these interests in his stories.  His hamburger recipe recently ended up at the John F. Kennedy Museum in Boston.  Hemingway ’ s adventures were not limited to war and travel to Africa, but also to unknown places and new situations, car and air accidents, malaria, skin cancer, pneumonia, hepatitis, multiple fractures and kidney problems.  He had a popular collection of weapons, and his death was shaped by one of them.  Ernest Hemingway committed suicide in Idaho at the age of 61.

The influence of the rookie reporter period on his career also corresponds to the iceberg theory he proposed in 1932: "Prose is like architecture, not interior decoration, and the Baroque era is over... Paris was not only the place where Hemingway worked as a journalist, but also the beginning of his literary career. Title: Hemingway's Myth
Content: In 1953, Hemingway was sitting at a dinner table at his camp in Kenya, writing. (NARA, Photographer, Look Magazine) Anyone familiar with American literature and literary criticism should know the iceberg talk about literary creation.  The author of this statement is the famous American writer and Nobel Prize winner Ernest Hemingway.  The main point is that if a writer has a mind about what he wants to write, he can omit something he knows when he creates, and the reader will feel those omissions because the author is writing true.  It is like an iceberg that looks magnificent as it moves in the sea, but in fact only one-eighth of it is out of the water, and the invisible part is more and more real.  In the theory of ancient Chinese poetry creation, there is a saying of "artistic conception", emphasizing the scenes and emotions depicted through the works, stimulating the imagination of the readers, and leaving them a space for full reflection and play.  This is synonymous with the "iceberg theory", but Hemingway emphasized the authenticity of the work, aiming to criticize some writers who seemed to him to be quite incompetent, who simply "omitted something because they did not understand".  Hemingway ’ s “iceberg talk ” actually interprets his own creative style, which is to omit everything he thinks is optional in his writing, and to be as simple and implicit as possible.  This creative style of Hemingway is indeed unique and has had a profound impact, some even said: Hemingway with no one has the courage, "English attached to the literature of the hair cut clean." But what interests me is that he uses the "iceberg" as a metaphor.  This analogy is really good.  What people usually use as metaphors are some common things, such as peach blossoms in "face like peach blossoms" and torches in "eyes like torches". How many people have seen an iceberg?  Three years ago, I went to Alaska to visit, and all I saw was a large piece of ice floe on the sea surface, real sea icebergs, probably only in the South Pole and Arctic areas where ordinary people are difficult to set foot.  However, this parable is also very relevant and can make people understand God.  What you can read in a good work is certainly brilliant, like the magnificence of an iceberg above the surface of the water, but what it contains can be much wider and deeper than the literal meaning, like a much larger body of mountain undersea support.  Without the presence of seven eighths below, there is no beauty at the top.  In the book of Revelation, there is a great deal to be said about the use of metaphors.  He said that the metaphor contains two aspects that are opposite and complementary, and the things that are compared must be the same, otherwise they cannot be joined together; but at the same time, they must be different, otherwise they cannot be distinguished.  As for the interaction between the two, the greater the difference, the more the same thing will be baked; the more open it will be, the more unexpected it will be, the more novel the metaphor will be, and the better the effect will be.  According to the theory of Qian Zhongshu, Hemingway uses the iceberg as a metaphor, and the things that belong to it are "very divided", and it has indeed produced a surprising winning effect, so it is unforgettable.  There are many other examples of this in the metaphor Hemingway has used.  After Hemingway became famous, he often compared himself with other writers, and was quite conceited, many writers he could not see, and only Shakespeare and Tolstoy were really admired.  He did not know this, but used boxing as a metaphor.  He said that he did not want to play Dostoyevsky in the first game, because he knew that Dostoyevsky was almost as good as he was, so he chose to play with Turgenev first because he felt he could play with him.  Then try Maupassant again, although it is difficult, but also can beat him; as for Henry James, he said, "As soon as I catch me, I press him, and immediately give him a blow where he has no meat, so tell the referee to stop the game." Hemingway's words, you can see his confidence.  About him and Cervantes who is stronger, he has a different saying, he believes that 20 rounds of war, you can beat the other side of the fart, but also admitted that Mr. Cervantes is very shrewd, while playing and learning, maybe the second game he will lose to the other side.  In Hemingway ’ s eyes, Shakespeare is the champion who can ’ t beat.  And speaking of Tolstoy, whom he equally admired, he said something different.  He said that if he played six rounds with Tolstoy, the opponent would not want to hit him, but he would be beaten enough, but if he played 20 rounds with Tolstoy, he would be knocked off the ear.  He also said that if he could live to sixty, he might defeat Tolstoy.  I guess Hemingway is probably trying to say that some of his works can win Tolstoy, but in general, they can ’ t talk about each other, unless he can create more good works in the future (need to live longer).  What kind of metaphor is used is often related to the personality and creation style of the user.  Pushkin is an emotional romantic poet, in his short life, wrote many beautiful people's poems.  I noticed that Pushkin often compared his beloved poetry to a harp.  So I thought, it must be because this ancient instrument can play a very moving tune, like a poem to move the heart.  Then because of the occasional experience, I have a new feeling about it.  That time was a trip to the Rocky Mountains, staying at the Castle Hotel by Lake Louise.  In the afternoon, a woman dressed like a classical beauty in a long skirt played the harp in the hotel's glittering lobby. Some of the hotel's guests sat, some stood, and listened.  It was at this moment that I suddenly understood why Pushkin used the harp as a metaphor for poetry, because the scenes and atmosphere in the lobby were so romantic.  Unlike Hemingway, his work has created many images of tough men, and he himself loves tough and exciting activities such as bullfighting, horse racing, boxing and hunting, so it is not surprising that he uses boxing as a metaphor.  However, not all people can use the analogy of the things that are "very divided" as Mr. Qian Zhongshu said.  In other words, the winning or losing of a boxing match and the level of a writer were originally two things that could not be fought with eight poles, but Hemingway "closed" them.  The Nobel laureate often had this idea.  His son once copied Turgenev's work and wrote a novel, which Hemingway did not notice at first, and praised his son after reading it.  Of course, he found out later.  However, when someone asked if his son would write a novel, his father ’ s face smiled and replied, “Gregory (his son ’ s name) sometimes does a little lame proofreading. ” Hemingway said this, and the people on the side laughed heartily.  To call plagiarism “lame proofreading ” is not a metaphor, it is hard to say, but I really admire Hemingway ’ s mental flexibility and language wisdom.  Aristotle said, "Parables are the sign of genius." Hemingway was indeed a genius. (From India)

Title: Hemingway is 18.
Content: July 24, 2018 04: 10 Hemingway of China Times has written a highly representative work of short stories.  Hemingway's 18-year old book cover. (The author provides) Hemingway's 18-year old has several major events: he decided not to go to college, worked as a reporter, six and a half months in the army, and was immediately injured.  His view of war changed after witnessing the First World War, and at the age of eighteen he was unable to define Hemingway ’ s life.  Hemingway studied a voluminous, visibly staged biography.  This new book, Hemingway ’ s Eighteen Years — A Key Year for American Legendary Writers, takes a different approach, focusing only on the age of eighteen.  The author of the new book has worked for the Kansas City Star for more than 40 years, making good use of the newspaper content of Hemingway during the service period of the newspaper, familiar with the old landscape of the city, and referring to the private letters between Hemingway and friends, showing the details and wisdom that have never been seen before.  The influence of a writer's actual life in a literary work is often difficult to determine.  In particular, the life experience of an individual year does not regulate the literary landscape of mass writers (such as Hemingway).  However, if the information is detailed and involves an important turning point in the planning of a writer's career, or it can be seen that it touches the nourishment of those literary youth to later literary works.  The relevant inference is reasonable, and there is no need to overestimate it, and a net will exhaust the entire literary life of the writer.  Hemingway was eighteen years old From July 21, 1917, until July 20, the following year, several important events of that year are worth mentioning: Hemingway decided not to go to college, left home to work as a reporter for the Kansas City Star, left the army six and a half months later, and was soon wounded in the Italian battlefield.  The family of six children, the cost is already considerable, coupled with the strong mother, want to buy a cottage on the lake in order to practice singing and painting, as far as the doctor father is concerned, the burden of two children going to college at the same time is still a bit heavy.  Her older sister Masilan was a year older, and she dropped out of primary school to study music for a year, so she graduated from the same high school as her younger brother.  In addition, at that time, the United States had announced that it would participate in the First World War, and Hemingway was determined to join the army.  The summer letters show that Hemingway has had various job opportunities, and he has been rather hesitant, but he has no sense of loss in the future.  One of the options was to be introduced by my uncle to the Kansas City Star as a reporter, but that vacancy would have to wait until the fall.  In high school, Hemingway read Shakespeare, wrote a diary, wrote short stories, voted, was interested in news writing, and once heard the retired magazine editor remind: "To learn to write, you have to write."  It happened to be working in the country to make a friend from Kansas City.  Finally, on October 15, he arrived in Kansas City, 500 miles from home, to take up his new job.  A wave of resignation offers new recruits, such as Hemingway, an opportunity to show off their skills.  The senior editor is happy to carry it forward.  The Star ’ s “News Writing Rules ” date back to 1915, and before Hemingway reported, they had changed from oral to internal guidelines.  A total of 110 requests.  Many of them are just common sense, such as: "Elimination of the word".  The opening lines were later distinguished by Hemingway's literary achievements: "In short sentences."  The first few paragraphs of the article are short.  In strong English.  Be positive, not negative.  "There are a lot of good writers among them.  For example, a murder news article mentions how Dostoyevsky, author of Crime and Punishment, understood criminal psychology.  Some commentators believe that the Star News experience makes up for the lack of a formal university education for this young man.  In November 1940, Hemingway and his third wife, Martha Galhoun, passed through Kansas City for an interview with The Star.  At the time, Hemingway's reputation was prominent, and his new book, War Clock, was well received.  Perhaps to be polite, or to be frank, he recalled that the Star ’ s guide to journalistic writing contributed to his clear, concise, and accurate writing style.  Hemingway told reporters: “These are the best writing rules I ’ ve learned.  I never forgot them.  No matter how talented you are, you can write well if you really feel, tell the truth, and follow those writing rules. ”  During Hemingway's time at the Star, Kansas City had a serious drug and alcohol problem.  He knew or heard of street fights, robberies, political squabbles, car accidents, murders, lack of coal in winter, and bad nightlife.  Hemingway has been fascinated with boxing since childhood, and wrote related stories in high school. At this time, he wrote professional boxing news in the Star newspaper, and later mentioned boxers repeatedly in the novel.  Ernest Hemingway was once expelled from the hospital by the management of the hospital, and was very pleased that his report forced the hospital to solve a number of problems.  The Star ’ s work environment is not perfect. While the Star occasionally talks about racial inequality, it doesn ’ t shy away from calling “nigger ” racially biased.  Hemingway blindly followed, the development of social consciousness is incomplete, from the Star newspaper news writing, and later novels and private letters, black people are not shy of the title.  Some of the rumors about Hemingway are not true.  In family letters and private letters to friends, he boasted that he was in love with a popular female star and that his marriage proposal was rejected because the other party did not want to be the widow of a fallen soldier.  Forty-eight years later, the actress was interviewed and said that she had never met Hemingway.  There is a biography of Hemingway saying that he bravely punched people in the restaurant to protect his friends.  Years later, a Star-Telegram colleague said Hemingway was not at the scene.  Hemingway had a weak eye and flat feet, and was unable to join the United States or Canadian forces as he wished.  It happened that colleague Ted Blumbac had been an ambulance driver in the French battlefield for more than five months, and the Star reported on the battlefield.  The newspaper clearly attached importance, listing the initials of the author.  Unless it is a famous writer (such as President Roosevelt, below), most Star articles do not list the author's name, and Hemingway's articles do not even have initials.  Brumbaker's eyes are not good, he was blinded by a single eye injury in college, and at this time easily convinced Hemingway to drive an ambulance to the front line in Italy.  But you have to pass the medical examination of the recruits.  Rumor has it that a friend secretly predicted Hemingway to cheat by memorizing the entire vision test answer.  One of his colleagues falsely testified that Hemingway was twenty-one years old and proficient in French and Italian.  Hemingway's enthusiasm for reporting to the army was quite simple.  Battlefield experience not only provides material for later novels, allowing him to experience a more mature concept of duty and honor, but also changes his vision of war: as the Battlefield Bell shows, abandoning romantic aspirations and replacing them with healthy disillusionment.  At the end of April, Blumbault left with Hemingway, arrived in New York City in mid-May, and then passed through France to Italy.  Hemingway's ambulance team picked up the wounded on the front line during the day.  Two volunteers per vehicle.  Historical records are not sure if he drove the car himself, and if so, how many times he drove it.  The Austrian and Italian forces faced off, separating the two armies on the Piave River. In mid-June, the Austrians failed to cross the river and the Italians captured hundreds of war criminals.  The ambulance team was idle for a while, and Hemingway was bored. In late June, he seized the opportunity to leave his current unit and transfer food to the front trenches.  Hemingway moved to the city of Fortholta, just twenty yards from the Piave River, and rode his bicycle to the Italian trenches every day.  Late at night on July 8, an Austrian bomb exploded three feet from Hemingway in a bomb shelter at the Forward Listening Station by the river.  An Italian soldier was killed and Hemingway wounded on the spot between the bomb site and Hemingway.  Blumbac visited the Red Cross Hospital in Milan and wrote to Hemingway ’ s family to report his injuries. Title: How to read Hemingway?
Content: Ernest Hemingway, a Nobel laureate and one of the most important of the 20th century, was born on July 21, 1899 in Illinois and wrote seven novels, six collections of short stories and two nonfiction books during his lifetime.  On the occasion of the birth of this author, which coincided with the thirteenth of July, we have suggestions for better reading of the works of this author.  Hemingway ’ s work is fluid, simple, and clear, but for many readers of literature, it may be difficult to begin reading Hemingway ’ s books.  Why read Hemingway?  Ernest Hemingway is an influential writer in the history of literature and fiction, his works have repeatedly won the most prestigious international literary awards such as Nobel and Pulitzer, this author employed a different kind of narrative description and caused many writers after him to borrow his own literary style.  Hemingway has named his literary style the Iceberg Theory, in this way of writing, fictional events are narrated like an iceberg floating in water, only one-eighth of which is visible, and the author includes only the information that is essential in the process and omits the rest of the information.  This technique created a tremendous change in storytelling, especially the writing of short stories, and it was a development that freed the stories from conventional chatter.  Hemingway ’ s works are included in the list of books of the century, books to read before death, and the best fiction books in history, highlighting the importance of this author.  What do we need to know?  One of the topics that helps to better understand Ernest Hemingway ’ s work is getting to know his personal life.  Much of what we read in his books is what he has turned from his personal life into a story.  At the age of 19, he volunteered for the First World War but was not allowed to fight because of poor eyesight, but Hemingway insisted on serving as an ambulance driver for the Red Cross.  He was wounded several times during the Chang, but his most significant injury is when he was wounded by mortar shell fragments and spent a long time in the hospital, a novel about this part of Hemingway ’ s life and the war.  Even the character of Catherine Barkley in this book is based on the nurse Hemingway fell in love with.  Hemingway also participated in World War II as a war correspondent, and several short stories are the result of this era.  The sun continues to blow, the Great River or along the river to the trees, each of which is somehow tied to the World War, and their heroes are survivors of the war and have many memories of these days.  But Hemingway ’ s most important masterpiece is a relic of his childhood, Hemingway ’ s father had a great interest in fishing, and this hobby was passed on to Ernest, a point that can be clearly seen in the famous and widely read story of The Old Man and the Sea.  But before the Old Man and the Sea, Hemingway had written about having and not having a fishing boat captain.  Another important point to know before reading Hemingway ’ s works is his political approach, he has written a lot in opposition to fascism and against dictatorship, both as a journalist and as a writer, sometimes even changing from a journalist to a social-political activist, who is this point in The Bell for, or who is this death knell?  It is a story of an American soldier in the Spanish Civil War fighting alongside groups against General Franco, which Hemingway did.  Perhaps the other thing that matters is that during the World War, Hemingway led a French group against the Nazis that was tried after the war for armed acts but was never proven guilty.  The political and social history of the world in the years of Hemingway's life, his personal life, as well as the knowledge of his contemporaries, such as Scott Fitzgerald, with whom he has written, are points that contribute to the understanding of his works.  Getting to know Hemingway ’ s contemporary writers helps to better understand the difference between him and his contemporaries.  Is it a classic?  To read Hemingway ’ s work, we must note that he is not a classic writer in his different style, he did not deal with the long margins and descriptions of classical literature, and his long novels are not immune.  He was interested in shorthand and engaging the audience with fiction, which is a feature of modern literature.  In general, Hemingway ’ s works are innovative and even among modern works have their own creativity, but the value of this author ’ s work has always been compared to classical works, and even classical enthusiasts have not been able to be indifferent to it.  In these works we have a happy and well-spoken writer, a writer who was in middle age with young people and was even close friends with a group of hippies.  Hemingway is a realistic writer, but he has always tried to maintain his sense of humor.  Where do we start?  To read Hemingway ’ s works, the first and most important suggestion is The Old Man and the Sea.  The book, translated by Najaf Daryabandari, was published in 222 pages by Kharazmi Publications.  The next book, Farewell to Arms, is again translated by Najaf Daryabendari, published by Amir Kabir Publications in 343 pages.  These two books are always on the list of works to be read or masterpieces of the 20th century.  If you are interested in short stories, you can also read Men Without Women, a collection of stories that have been published in various magazines by the author.  This book has been translated by Asadollah Amraei for publication of Horizon in 222 pages.  Even if you are interested in writing, Hemingway can be a good teacher and read his series of talks and learn very precise points.  The book The Last Interview and Other Conversations of Ernest Hemingway with a translation by Houshang Jirani has been published in 88 pages by Cheshmeh Publishing.  The final chapter of many critics considered Ernest Hemingway to be the greatest writer of the 20th century.  His stories are an exploration of real human life, suffering and the meaning of life.  The portrayal of human inner feelings is the most important characteristic of this author, which makes his works a read for every reader.  Who was Ernest Hemingway?  Ernest Hemingway was born on July 21, 1899 in Oak Park, Illinois.  His father, Clarence, was a doctor and his mother, Grace, was a piano and singing teacher.  Ernest spent the summers with his family in northern Michigan, where he discovered his passion for fishing.  After finishing high school, he worked for a while in Kansas City as a reporter for the Star Chronicle in 1917.  During World War I, he volunteered to serve in the army, but poor eyesight prevented him from doing so, instead serving as an ambulance driver for the Red Cross near the Italian front.  On July 8, 1918, he was injured and spent months in the hospital.  In 1925, his first collection of short stories, in our time, was published, which spoke well of his particular style.  His memoirs from that period were published after his death in 1964 as The Variable Eid.  Ernest Hemingway was an adventurer for most of his life.  From being wounded in Italy by 200 pieces of Austrian shrapnel during World War I, to taking part in the frontlines of the Spanish Civil War or touring the African wilderness, to fishing and hunting wildlife and living in Cuba.  He finally said goodbye to life with his hunting rifle.
